R1083.decision_summary: R1083 §5.51 §5.45 §5.16 tabbed docking: add an ADDITIVE DockNode::Tabs { id, panels, active } tab-well variant (>=2 invariant + collapse-to-Leaf at 1 = no dual representation; existing Leaf/Split serde+matches stay byte-identical) with a stable well id mirroring Split's; new DockTopology::tabify(source,target,new_tabs_id) primitive (remove source, stack onto target: Leaf->2-tab well / existing well->append+activate); route DockDropZone::Center -> DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify through the intent_for_zone SSOT (supersedes the tab-less v1 Swap) so the already-wired R1081/R1082 pointer + invoke coordinators tabify live for free; remove/split/swap recursions + the validator made well-aware (new TopologyError TabsTooFew/ActiveOutOfRange/DuplicateTabsId); render the well as a view_tabs strip keyed on the well id above the active panel rendered header-suppressed (DockPanelStyle::show_header) so a drop resolves the active panel id (edge->split whole well, centre->tabify); view_tabs tag lifted &'static str -> impl Into<Cow> (2nd consumer). Click-to-switch-active / tab-reorder / untab-drag-out / dock-well tab a11y are DECLARED-DEFER (R1084+, each its own forcing consumer).
changes_bullets: Model: add DockNode::Tabs { id, panels: Vec<panel_id>, active } as an ADDITIVE variant (existing Leaf/Split serde + match arms + tests stay byte-identical) — the tab well. Invariants enforced by DockTopology::try_new: panels.len() >= 2 (a single-panel well is a Leaf, never a degenerate Tabs), active < panels.len(), every panel id + the well's own stable id unique-and-non-empty in the one topology id namespace. The well carries a stable id mirroring Split's stable-id rationale (binds the view_tabs strip tag + future per-well selection signal).

Counts/walks: collect_panel_ids descends a well (all panels, tab order); new panel_count() (Leaf=1 / Tabs=len / Split=sum) = panel_ids().len(); leaf_count counts a well as one pane slot; split_count unchanged (Tabs=0). DockNode::tabs() constructor + DockTopology::panel_count() delegator.

Validation: NodeKind::Tabs + insert_panel_id helper shared by the Leaf and Tabs arms (a panel id collides identically whether in a leaf or a well). New TopologyError: DuplicateTabsId, TabsTooFew, ActiveOutOfRange; well-id-vs-panel/split collision => IdCollision; panel-in-well duplicating a leaf => DuplicatePanelId.

Mutation: remove_leaf_rec well-aware — shrink a well, clamp active, collapse to Leaf at 1 panel (the canonical >=2 rule, no dual representation); split_leaf_rec well-aware — an edge drop onto a panel inside a well splits the WHOLE well (stays together as one Split child); swap_panel_ids_rec relabels panels inside wells; NEW DockTopology::tabify(source, target, new_tabs_id) = remove source then stack onto target (Leaf -> 2-tab well / existing well -> append + activate); source==target is a no-op.

Routing (SSOT): intent_for_zone Center => DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify (supersedes the tab-less v1 Swap; Swap stays a valid public mutation but no zone produces it). DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify { source, target } + source()/target()/apply() arms; apply()'s new_split_id generalized to new_id (split id OR fresh well id). DockReorganizer gains a tabs_seq counter + tabs_seq() accessor; apply_intent mints reorg-tabs-{seq} for Tabify (REORG_TABS_ID_PREFIX) and bumps only the counter the applied gesture drew from. The already-wired R1081/R1082 pointer + invoke coordinators tabify live for free (no new pointer wiring).

Render: view_dock_surface_node Tabs arm renders a view_tabs strip (keyed on the well id) above the active panel's content; the active panel uses view_dock_panel with the header suppressed (DockPanelStyle::show_header, default true) — the strip is the title row — keeping its drop_target root + content + drop overlay so a drop onto the well resolves the active panel id (edge => split the whole well, centre => tabify into it). Substrate lift: view_tabs tag generalized &'static str -> impl Into<Cow<'static, str>> (2nd consumer = dock wells with runtime-minted ids forces it; hello-tabs unchanged).

Invariants enforced by DockTopology::try_new: panels.len() >= 2 (a single-panel well is a Leaf, never a degenerate Tabs), active < panels.len(), every panel id + the well's own stable id unique-and-non-empty in the one topology id namespace. The well carries a stable id mirroring Split's stable-id rationale (binds the view_tabs strip tag + future per-well selection signal).

Counts/walks: collect_panel_ids descends a well (all panels, tab order); new panel_count() (Leaf=1 / Tabs=len / Split=sum) = panel_ids().len(); leaf_count counts a well as one pane slot; split_count unchanged (Tabs=0). DockNode::tabs() constructor + DockTopology::panel_count() delegator.

Validation: NodeKind::Tabs + insert_panel_id helper shared by the Leaf and Tabs arms (a panel id collides identically whether in a leaf or a well). New TopologyError: DuplicateTabsId, TabsTooFew, ActiveOutOfRange; well-id-vs-panel/split collision => IdCollision; panel-in-well duplicating a leaf => DuplicatePanelId.

Mutation: remove_leaf_rec well-aware — shrink a well, clamp active, collapse to Leaf at 1 panel (the canonical >=2 rule, no dual representation); split_leaf_rec well-aware — an edge drop onto a panel inside a well splits the WHOLE well (stays together as one Split child); swap_panel_ids_rec relabels panels inside wells; NEW DockTopology::tabify(source, target, new_tabs_id) = remove source then stack onto target (Leaf -> 2-tab well / existing well -> append + activate); source==target is a no-op.

DockReorganizeIntent::Tabify { source, target } + source()/target()/apply() arms; apply()'s new_split_id generalized to new_id (split id OR fresh well id). DockReorganizer gains a tabs_seq counter + tabs_seq() accessor; apply_intent mints reorg-tabs-{seq} for Tabify (REORG_TABS_ID_PREFIX) and bumps only the counter the applied gesture drew from. The already-wired R1081/R1082 pointer + invoke coordinators tabify live for free (no new pointer wiring).

R1084.decision_summary: R1084 §5.51 §5.45 §5.16 consumer-forced seam (sprag R68 / PR-29.1): make the dock reorganize coordinator TOTAL over Option<DockTopology> so a consumer whose dock SSOT is Rc<Signal<Option<DockTopology>>> (None = empty dock, all panes floating) hands its single topology signal directly to the coordinator — no mirror. DockReorganizer + DockReorganizeExternal::new now hold/take Rc<Signal<Option<DockTopology>>>; apply_intent on None is the IDENTITY no-op (Ok("empty surface — no-op"), the honest total definition — no source to drag, no target to drop — not defensive code), on Some the existing path setting Some(next); with_undo records SignalEdit<Option<DockTopology>>; query("topology") serialises None to JSON null. DockTopology's leaf>=1 invariant is untouched (absence is the Option, never a degenerate topology); the coordinator provably never emits Some->None (Swap/SplitInsert/Tabify all preserve panel count, remove-sole-leaf is RootRemoval error) so None is input-only and unreachable via a pointer drag. with_reorganizer/from_reorganizer signatures unchanged (Rc<DockReorganizer>); view_dock_surface kept &DockTopology (callers wrap the Option). Editor migrated to the Option surface (seeds Some, gates externals on if-let-Some, view matches Some/None). Rejected fork: parallel new_optional + internal TopologyHandle enum (zero churn but permanent two-path split + contradicts empty-is-universal). Deferred (handoff-optional): lift view_dock_surface to Option<&DockTopology> for an empty-dock paint SSOT. sprag consumes the seam in a separate sprag-native session.
changes_bullets: Consumer-forced seam (sprag R68 / PR-29.1 handoff): make the dock reorganize coordinator TOTAL over Option<DockTopology> so a consumer whose dock SSOT is Rc<Signal<Option<DockTopology>>> (None = empty dock = all panes floating; sprag's R60 1B-collapse) can hand its single topology signal directly to the coordinator — no second mirror signal.

Core: DockReorganizer holds Rc<Signal<Option<DockTopology>>> (was non-Option). new()/topology() take/return the Option signal. apply_intent: `let Some(current) = topology.get() else { record "empty surface — no-op"; return Ok(..) }` — the empty surface is the IDENTITY no-op (no source to drag, no target to drop), the honest total definition, not defensive code; on Some it is the existing path and sets Some(next). with_undo records SignalEdit<Option<DockTopology>> (next = Some). DockReorganizeExternal::new takes the Option signal; query("topology") serialises None -> JSON null (AI reads the empty dock as null, not a fabricated tree).

Why total not weakened-topology: DockTopology keeps its leaf>=1 invariant (try_new/panel_ids/walker/serde all stand on it); absence is modelled by the Option, never by a degenerate empty topology. The coordinator provably never emits Some->None: Swap/SplitInsert/Tabify all preserve panel count (moves), remove_leaf on the sole leaf is RootRemoval error not None — so None is input-only, and a pointer drag cannot even originate on an empty surface (only the invoke path reaches it, and it gets the no-op).

with_reorganizer / from_reorganizer signatures UNCHANGED (Rc<DockReorganizer>) — only the coordinator's internal cell type changed; the External wrappers are untouched, so sprag's per-panel registration is unaffected.

Editor migration (hello-dock-panels-editor): use_editor_topology -> Rc<Signal<Option<DockTopology>>>, seeds Some(build_editor_topology()); create_extra_externals gates the splitter+panel externals on `if let Some(topology)` (the reorganize+undo anchors register unconditionally — an AI can invoke-reorganize an empty dock = no-op); the view fn matches Some(t)=>view_dock_surface(&t,..) / None=>empty container. The editor seeds Some and never empties but shares the universal Option dock surface (the model it will need when Phase-D editor regions empty).

Design fork (rejected): a parallel new_optional + internal TopologyHandle enum keeps the editor/tests on non-Option (zero churn) but adds a permanent two-path split + two constructors and contradicts "empty is universal to the dock model"; per cost-no-object the mechanical test churn does not justify it. Also DEFERRED (handoff marked optional): lifting view_dock_surface to Option<&DockTopology> so the empty-dock paint is a dock SSOT — the editor + sprag handle None->empty inline for now; lift on a clean 2-consumer case.
WALKER UNCHANGED: view_dock_surface stays &DockTopology (the editor/sprag wrap the Option at the call site), so sprag's existing walker call is not forced to migrate.

Tests: 5 R1084 empty-surface tests (apply_intent None=no-op + no id mint + last_outcome; with_undo None records nothing; invoke reorganize None = Ok no-op; query topology = JSON null; Some path still reorganizes under the Option signal) + ~18 existing reorganize/tabify tests migrated to Some(..) signals + .unwrap() read-backs (Option==Option compares left as-is).

For a 2-panel well [b,c], an RPC reorganize{source:"c",target:"b",zone:Center} ran the remove+restack path: remove c -> [b] collapses to Leaf{b} -> re-promoted under a FRESH new_tabs_id, discarding the well id the binding's per-well state keys on. R1085.decision_summary: R1085 §5.51 §5.45 §5.16 tab-well navigation slice (a) — the AI-first activate_tab primary. R1083's DockNode::Tabs wells were create+observe-only; this makes them navigable by RPC/AI over the existing SSOT, in three layers. (1) DockTopology::set_active_tab(well_id, index): a pure topology primitive — NOT a move (no panel relocates, no id minted, only the well's active changes) — returning a new validated topology; set_active_in_well_rec rebuilds the matching well (mirrors activate_in_shared_well); a stale/wrong-kind id -> new TopologyError::TabsWellNotFound, an out-of-range index -> try_new's existing ActiveOutOfRange (the one validation gate, not re-checked in the primitive). (2) DockReorganizer: extracted apply_intent's last_outcome + undo-or-set tail into a private commit() funnel — now the sole-writer SSOT both gestures pass through (the R1082.1 invariant preserved, not broken by a second writer) — and activate_tab navigates over it: empty surface = identity no-op, rejection self-records 'rejected:', success commits, bumping neither split_seq nor tabs_seq (navigation mints no id). (3) DockReorganizeExternal: invoke('activate_tab',{well_id,index}) arm + ('activate_tab','json') schema entry + thin delegate — the third action shape beside drop/reorganize, discoverable so an AI switches tabs symbolically (no pixels), the §2 #2 RPC-as-primary-path contract. Scope is slice (a) only: pointer click-to-switch (R1086) + dock-well tab a11y (R1087) share this same coordinator and follow. 7587 pass / 0 fail; committed locally, NOT pushed.
changes_bullets: DockTopology::set_active_tab(well_id, index) + set_active_in_well_rec helper — the pure tab-well navigation primitive (NOT a move: no panel relocates, no id minted, only the well's `active` changes), returning a new validated topology. Mirrors activate_in_shared_well's rebuild.

New TopologyError::TabsWellNotFound(well_id) when the id names no DockNode::Tabs well (absent, or a Leaf panel / Split divider id); an out-of-range index surfaces as the existing ActiveOutOfRange from try_new (the one validation gate, not re-checked in the primitive).

DockReorganizer: extracted the last_outcome + undo-or-set tail of apply_intent into a private commit(next, summary) funnel — now the sole-writer SSOT both gestures pass through. New activate_tab(well_id, index) navigates over it: empty surface = identity no-op (Ok("empty surface — no-op")), rejection self-records "rejected: …", success commits; bumps neither split_seq nor tabs_seq (navigation mints no id).

DockReorganizeExternal: invoke("activate_tab", {well_id, index}) arm + ("activate_tab","json") schema entry + thin activate_tab delegate (mirrors apply_intent); invoke rustdoc documents the third action shape beside drop/reorganize. The AI-first primary — an agent switches tabs symbolically (no pixels), the §2 #2 RPC-as-primary-path contract.
Scope: slice (a) AI/RPC navigation only. Pointer click-to-switch (b) + dock-well tab a11y (c) are R1086/R1087, each sharing this same activate_tab coordinator.

Topology (set_active_tab): flips the visible tab / index==active is an accepted no-op / index past the well -> ActiveOutOfRange from try_new / unknown well id -> TabsWellNotFound / a Leaf panel id or Split divider id -> TabsWellNotFound (not mistaken for a well) / a well nested in a split flips while its sibling leaf + split id stay intact.

Coordinator + invoke (activate_tab): invoke flips active in the live signal and returns "activate w0#2" / last_outcome records the gesture for introspection / malformed payload (non-object, missing index, missing well_id) -> TypeMismatch / out-of-range or unknown well -> Rejected with the rejection self-recorded and the live topology untouched / empty surface -> Ok("empty surface — no-op") leaving the signal None / with_undo is reversible (undo restores the prior active tab, redo re-applies) / the schema advertises activate_tab.

R1086.decision_summary: R1086 §5.21 §5.16 PR-30 (sprag R68 consumer-forced seam): view_splitter's flex children could not set a main-axis min:0, so a panel whose content is larger than its ratio share clamped to content and overflowed — the sprag P2 drag-to-dock symptom (a vertical split put both panels at full window height, the second off the 600px window). Root cause (source-verified): LayoutStyle had no min_size field; flex_basis:0 (R684) alone is the incomplete half of the CSS proportional-flex idiom — without min-*:0 taffy's automatic flex minimum pins each item to its content's min-content size. Fix, audit-first over the existing flex_basis substrate: (1) LayoutStyle gains pub min_size: Size + with_min_size builder + Hash inclusion; default Size::auto() lowers to taffy min_size: Auto = the pre-R1086 automatic minimum, so every binding's layout AND the §5.16 paint-fragment cache key stay bit-identical. (2) to_taffy_style lowers min_size per axis via to_dimension (analogous to size); a SizeValue::Px(0) axis overrides the automatic minimum to zero so a flex child can shrink below its content. (3) view_splitter::apply_flex_main (threaded with orientation) zeroes the MAIN-axis min (Horizontal->width, Vertical->height) on its ratio children, cross axis left Auto so AlignItems::Stretch still fills it; the 7 Scene arms refactored through a set_flex_main helper so flex_basis:0 + flex_grow + min:0 are set uniformly. Verification: a layout.rs regression witness proves the bug (no min override -> 800px content clamp -> second panel off-screen at y>=600) AND the fix (min:0 -> 0.5 ratio = ~300 each, both on-screen); a view_splitter end-to-end forcing-consumer mirrors sprag's vertical_reorganize_keeps_both_panels_onscreen guard (both panels on-screen, handle keeps thickness, panels+handle fill the viewport). 7595 pass / 0 fail. sprag consumes in a sprag-native session (pin bump only, no sprag code change expected; R60 fill_definite Percent(100) is orthogonal to min:0). Committed locally, NOT pushed.

R1087.decision_summary: R1087 §5.16 §5.41 §2 #7 PR-31 foundation (sprag R68 handoff): the floating-panel-as-positioned-window substrate for dock tear-off. Architecture DECIDED = A — model the floating panel as a real window whose position is declared SSOT data, the drag writes that position to the signal, the shell reconciles; B/C (borderless follower / in-app ghost) are NOT forks but render fallbacks BELOW the contract (dual-representation + AI-invisible = the §2 #2/#7 smell A avoids). This round lands the de-risked, fallback-compatible substrate; the live drag-follow coordinator + libXtst set_outer_position-under-grab acceptance are R1088 (HW-gated). (1) WindowSpec gains pub position: Option<(i32,i32)> (logical px, the doc-predicted additive field) + with_position builder + #[serde(default)] (legacy Signal<Vec<WindowSpec>> JSON omitting it -> None, never a breaking serde change); default None = WM placement = byte-identical for every pre-R1087 binding. (2) resume_spec honours position at create via WindowAttributes::with_position. (3) reconcile_windows gains a move pass — a pure window_position_moves(old,new) diff (unit-testable, no event loop) + Window::set_outer_position apply — keeping reconcile TOTAL over the new field (the R1084 totality lesson: the id-keyed add/drop passes would otherwise silently swallow a same-id position change the top-level new==old guard already saw). (4) scene/windows read-only RPC (pinion_rpc::DeclaredWindow {id,title,position} via DispatchContext::with_declared_windows, resolved shell-side by declared_window_specs from windows_signal else the static windows(), gated on the method) makes the position observable as scene-as-data — the §2 #7 obligation for the new state and the exact justification for choosing A over the AI-invisible follower/ghost. Forcing consumer: hello-dock-panels tear-off pushes a positioned floating WindowSpec (per-panel cascade offset). Verified: 6 move-diff unit tests + 1 WindowSpec position serde/default test + 3 scene/windows handler tests + r1087 RPC demo (26 asserts) tearing off and reading positions back over scene/windows; cargo test --workspace green / clippy clean / fmt clean / validate-workspace T1=0. Honest: headless + unit only — live OS placement and drag-to-follow are R1088 (HW-gated); the foundation is architecture-A-correct AND follower-fallback-compatible, so it does not bet on the live grab-move. Committed locally, NOT pushed.
changes_bullets: WindowSpec gains `pub position: Option<(i32,i32)>` (logical-px outer position, the doc-predicted additive field on the #[non_exhaustive] struct) + a `with_position(x,y)` builder + `#[serde(default)]` so a Signal<Vec<WindowSpec>> value serialized before the field existed deserializes to None — additive, never a breaking change to the reactive primitive's serde shape. Default None = window-manager placement = byte-identical for every pre-R1087 binding.

resume_spec (AppShell) honours a declared position at window-create time via WindowAttributes::with_position (the non-cached creation path); the cached suspend/resume path is untouched (a window keeps its OS position across resume).

reconcile_windows gains a move pass: a pure window_position_moves(old,new) -> Vec<(id,(x,y))> diff (a same-id spec whose declared position changed, including None->Some first-placement; a Some->None drop-back is deliberately NOT a move since set_outer_position has no hand-back-to-WM form) + a Window::set_outer_position apply over the live WindowSlot. This keeps reconcile_windows TOTAL over the new field — without it the id-keyed add/drop passes silently swallow a same-id position change the top-level new==old guard already detected (the R1084 totality lesson).

scene/windows read-only RPC: pinion_rpc::DeclaredWindow {id,title,position} wire type + DispatchContext::with_declared_windows + handle_scene_windows (HandlerKind::Read; None -> DeclaredWindowsUnavailable, the PacingStateUnavailable honesty parity; empty Vec is a real value). Shell-side declared_window_specs() (sibling of declared_window_ids) maps each WindowSpec the binding declares — windows_signal when opted in, else the compile-time windows() list, so the read is honest for single-window bindings too — and is resolved only for the scene/windows method (every other dispatch pays nothing). Makes the position observable as scene-as-data (§2 #7) — the exact justification for choosing architecture A over the AI-invisible follower/ghost.

Forcing consumer: hello-dock-panels tear-off now pushes a positioned floating WindowSpec via floating_window_position (a per-panel cascade offset, base (120,90) + step*40) — the first with_position consumer, proving the binding -> windows_signal -> reconcile_windows -> real-window arc.
verification_bullets: 6 pure window_position_moves unit tests (no event loop): unchanged->no moves, same-id position change, None->Some first placement, add-with-position is NOT a move (resume_spec places it), Some->None drop-back is NOT a move, multiple simultaneous moves reported in new order.

1 WindowSpec serde test: with_position round-trips Some((x,y)); the default builder is None; legacy JSON omitting the position key deserializes to None via #[serde(default)] (derived by stripping the key from a current serialize, robust to SizeStrategy's JSON shape).
3 scene/windows handler tests: None -> DeclaredWindowsUnavailable; a declared set serializes id+title+position ([x,y] / null); an empty Vec is a real empty list distinct from the unavailable error.

Tear-off driven by the tear_off invoke toggle (gesture-free + deterministic; a drag-to-centre now hits PR-29's reorganize/Tabify zone), since R1087 verifies the POSITION the reducer writes, not the gesture.

R1087.1.decision_summary: R1087.1 §5.16 §5.41 §2 #7 PR-31 audit-clearance: user re-challenge (hack/smell 없이 교과서적? SSOT? 북극성?) → 3 independent read-only reviewers (textbook-craft / SSOT-architecture / north-star-AI-first; parallel = safe per no-parallel-tree-mutating-review-agents) + author grep/read. STRUCTURE SURVIVED: zero must-fix smells, zero hacks/stubs/partials, zero correctness bugs in the load-bearing window_position_moves diff. All three reviewers independently confirmed textbook: architecture A (declared position = SSOT data, shell reconciles; B/C below-the-contract) faithfully implemented with no fork; SSOT single-source, NO dual representation (the OS holds a position that can diverge, but that is "SSOT pushed to a sink", not a 2nd in-app representation); crate layering forced-correct (DeclaredWindow in pinion-rpc, the highest crate rpc can own, mapped shell-side — no cycle; matches the InputStateSnapshot/PacingState read-payload precedent inverted because WindowSpec lives HIGH); seam choice windows_signal-diff (NOT reconcile_frame) is correct (position is reactive Signal data, not off-thread producer state — the entry plan's reconcile_frame hypothesis correctly rejected in impl); declared_window_specs vs declared_window_ids deliberately diverge per consumer (specs falls back to static windows() so a single-window binding honestly reports "main"; ids returns empty because union_focusable_tags prepends DEFAULT_WINDOW separately — do NOT lift); the totality DIFF is correct + fully unit-tested; deferral honesty sound. Cleared the last non-textbook RESIDUE (the R1082.2 false-doc class): (1) the central declared-vs-actual honesty — scene/windows reports DECLARED position; pinion does not feed winit WindowEvent::Moved back into the signal, so a user native title-bar drag is invisible to the read; sharpened DeclaredWindow + handle_scene_windows + declared_window_specs + WindowSpec.position docs from "where the window sits" to "where it is DECLARED to sit (declared, not a live OS read-back)", and NAMED the Moved->signal feedback as the convergence requirement owed with the R1088 drag-follow (re-apply-on-resume + Moved-feedback are coupled — deferred together to avoid a half-fix that clobbers a user move in the no-feedback interim). (2) "reconcile_windows TOTAL over the field" over-claimed: the DIFF is total, the APPLY is best-effort (skips a Suspended(Some) window with no live arc -> reconciles on next create, a mobile-lifecycle gap deferred with mobile) — softened the wording precisely in the fn doc + move-pass comment. (3) "byte-identical" conflated placement with serde shape: #[serde(default)] carries no skip_serializing_if so every WindowSpec now emits an explicit "position":null — placement BEHAVIOUR is byte-identical, the serde SHAPE is additive; qualified the doc + moved the deliberate-non-skip rationale from the test comment to the field doc. NITs cleared: window_position_moves O(N^2) deliberately accepted (N=window count, tiny; commented vs the HashSet add/drop siblings); demo _wait_unlisted redundant "or None" dropped; legacy-JSON serde test gained assert_ne!(legacy,current) so a future field landing after position fails loudly instead of silently weakening the omitted-key coverage. DOC/TEST/DEMO-only — ZERO production logic change. 7605 pass / 0 fail; clippy --workspace --all-targets vello clean; fmt clean; validate-workspace T1=0; r1087 demo (26 asserts) re-run green. Committed locally, NOT pushed.
changes_bullets: 3 independent read-only reviewers (craft / SSOT / north-star, parallel-safe) + author grep/read audit; structure SURVIVED — zero must-fix smells/hacks/stubs, zero correctness bugs. Independently confirmed textbook: architecture A, SSOT single-source (no dual representation), crate layering (DeclaredWindow in pinion-rpc, no cycle), seam choice (windows_signal-diff NOT reconcile_frame), declared_specs/ids per-consumer divergence (do-not-lift), the totality diff, and deferral honesty.

Declared-vs-actual honesty (the central finding): sharpened DeclaredWindow + handle_scene_windows + declared_window_specs + WindowSpec.position docs from "where the window sits" to "where it is DECLARED to sit (declared, not a live OS read-back)". pinion has no WindowEvent::Moved -> windows_signal feedback, so a user native title-bar drag is invisible to scene/windows — NAMED as the convergence carry owed with the R1088 drag-follow.

"total" precision: window_position_moves doc + the move-pass comment now state the DIFF is total over the field, the APPLY is best-effort (skips a Suspended(Some) no-arc window -> reconciles on next create, a mobile-lifecycle gap deferred with mobile).

"byte-identical" precision: WindowSpec.position doc qualified (placement BEHAVIOUR byte-identical; serde SHAPE additive — #[serde(default)] emits an explicit "position":null); the deliberate no-skip_serializing_if rationale moved from the test comment onto the field doc so a future reader does not "fix" it.

NITs: window_position_moves O(N^2) commented as deliberately accepted (N tiny, vs the HashSet add/drop siblings); demo _wait_unlisted redundant "or None" dropped; legacy-JSON serde test gained assert_ne!(legacy,current) future-field-add guard.
verification_bullets: DOC/TEST/DEMO-only clearance — ZERO production logic change, so no behaviour delta (the move pass, resume_spec, scene/windows, and the field all behave exactly as in R1087; only docs/comments + one test guard + one demo no-op were touched).

Gates re-run green: pinion-shell lib 88 pass (the serde test now carries the assert_ne!(legacy,current) guard) + pinion-rpc 3 scene/windows handler tests pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello clean (-D pedantic); cargo fmt clean; mnemosyne validate-workspace T1=0.
r1087_dock_window_position.py demo (26 asserts) re-run green after the _wait_unlisted "or None" drop.

Honesty: the clearance ADDED no verification of live behaviour — live OS placement, the drag-follow, AND the now-named WindowEvent::Moved -> signal feedback all remain R1088 (HW-gated). The clearance only stopped the docs over-claiming (declared-as-if-actual; total-diff-as-if-total-apply; placement-byte-identical-as-if-serde-byte-identical).
carry_forward_bullets: R1088 (next) now owes THREE COUPLED live-window items, to land together because shell-initiated moves and OS-originated moves must not echo each other (designing them apart risks a half-fix that clobbers a user move in the no-feedback interim): (a) live set_outer_position-under-grab acceptance (libXtst native-pointer, HW-gated on a real-GPU host); (b) the drag-follow coordinator (header drag escaping all dock zones -> detach to a floating positioned window that follows the cursor, each move writing the position signal) + the AI reposition intervene (the write peer of this round's scene/windows read); (c) WindowEvent::Moved -> windows_signal feedback so a user native title-bar drag writes the position SSOT back (declared becomes just another writer = the architecture-A convergence ideal, declared===actual) + re-apply spec.position on the cached Suspended(Some) resume path (closing the move-pass apply gap).

Until (c) lands, scene/windows reports DECLARED position only; the DeclaredWindow naming + sharpened docs keep that honest. Do NOT later rename the wire to "the window position" or drop "Declared" without the Moved feedback loop.

Pre-existing (NOT R1087's burden — a separate future round): there is no RPC method-discovery endpoint, so scene/windows (like every method) is reachable only by an AI that already knows the literal string. A self-describing rpc/methods (or scene/capabilities) round would close this north-star gap for the WHOLE wire surface, not just windows.

R1092.decision_summary: Completed the scene/windows window-GEOMETRY introspection surface by adding a declared SIZE alongside R1087's declared position: an AI introspecting a multi-window / docked editor layout now reads not merely WHERE each declared window sits but HOW BIG it is declared to be. Sourced from the binding's SizeStrategy SSOT via a new SizeStrategy::declared_size() projection — Fixed/OpenResizable declare an exact open size, IntrinsicAfterFirstPaint declares null (its eventual size is the post-first-paint content bbox, known only as a transient min floor at declare time) — the same null-means-system-determined honesty position uses for a WM-placed window. AUDIT-FIRST PIVOT: the SEED named R1089/R1092 region work; param-schema (the named rpc/methods next slice) was audited and DEFERRED because param shapes live per-handler with no uniform source signature to cross-check (a drift-prone hand-curated registry or a ~73-handler struct-extraction campaign, no forcing consumer yet); window-size is the clean, buildable, headless-demoable AI-first slice that closes the R1087 position-only geometry debt before the next round pivots to the Phase B DCC campaign.
changes_bullets: SizeStrategy::declared_size(self) -> Option<(u32,u32)> added to pinion-shell as the SSOT for "did the binding declare an open size": Fixed{w,h}=>Some, OpenResizable{size,..}=>Some, IntrinsicAfterFirstPaint=>None. Deliberately DISTINCT from initial_logical_size (the literal creation pixels, which returns Intrinsic's min): declared_size answers "what size did the binding DECLARE", and an Intrinsic window declares none — reporting its transient min floor would mislead an AI into reading it as the final geometry.

R1092.1.decision_summary: LIVE VERIFICATION finding (0 LOC, no round): the R1088 carry "live OS Moved / set_outer_position-under-grab NOT verified headlessly (HW-gated)" is CLEARED for the platform-feasibility question it gated. On re-checking the actual environment (the dev box HAS a real :0 Xorg + gnome-shell/mutter + GPU + libXtst, contradicting the earlier "environment can't" framing), a throwaway ctypes(libX11/libXtst)+xwininfo probe drove the EXISTING scene/window_move over a real visible hello-dock-panels floating window and read the actual OS geometry. Result: mutter honors set_outer_position to the pixel, INCLUDING during an active pointer grab. Conclusion: live dock tear-off drag-follow is PLATFORM-FEASIBLE on mutter; no follower-window fallback needed; only the coordinator code + winit CursorMoved-during-grab delivery remain (buildable, R1080-R1085 pattern). No production code changed; the probe is a scratchpad throwaway (not committed).
changes_bullets: No production code change (0 LOC). This entry records a live-verification finding against the existing R1087/R1088 window-position substrate, run via a throwaway ctypes+xwininfo probe (scratchpad, not committed per the no-temp-test-files rule).
verification_bullets: Probe drove scene/window_move over a REAL visible hello-dock-panels floating window on :0 (Xorg + gnome-shell/mutter, real GPU, scale 1.0); OS geometry read via xwininfo. (1) Plain move: RPC-commanded logical delta == observed OS physical delta to the pixel ((520,260)=>(520,260)); constant +37px Y = gnome title-bar decoration, cancels in the delta. (2) Under an ACTIVE pointer grab, cross-checked two independent ways that AGREE pixel-exact: (2a) XGrabPointer active grab held by the probe -> commanded (510,290) == OS (510,290); (2b) real synthesized button-1 hold over the main window (winit implicit grab, zero physical motion -> no app-drag/WM-move trips) -> commanded (-260,-180) == OS (-260,-180). So a pointer grab does NOT block ConfigureWindow for a different window on this WM. R1093.decision_summary: Began the live dock tear-off coordinator (PR-31 Tier 3, the sprag-forced handoff) by landing its foundational seam: the §5.15 input-forwarding ENRICHMENT that hands a drag source the absolute window-logical cursor, and exposes the live drag cursor as scene-as-data. The handoff doc's gap #1 was "the absolute cursor never reaches the drag source" — drag_to forwards only the rect-relative DropPoint, which goes None the instant the cursor escapes every tagged region (exactly the tear-off case), so a follow-the-cursor coordinator had no pointer to read. R1092.1 already live-verified the platform half (mutter honors set_outer_position under an active grab), so this round builds the data half. AUDIT-FIRST SCOPE: correct cursor-anchored window PLACEMENT additionally needs the source-window outer position (gap (b), shell-owned) — a second seam — so this round is the clean, complete, headlessly-verifiable foundation (cursor forwarding + AI-introspectable drag cursor); the placement+follow coordinator consuming it is R1094.
changes_bullets: pinion-core External trait: additive drag_to_at(payload,over,cursor:(f64,f64)) + drag_release_at, defaults DELEGATE to the cursor-less drag_to/drag_release so every pre-R1093 source is bit-identical and no source receives both calls. §5.15 input-forwarding ENRICHED not broken (additive default-delegating method, not a breaking drag_to signature change); the begin_drag contract doc corrected to name drag_to_at/drag_release_at as the forward path.

pinion-runtime InputRouter: update_drag forwards drag_to_at(payload,over,(x,y)); the pointer_up release site forwards drag_release_at with the cursor from self.cursors (falls back to drag_release when no cursor recorded). The absolute cursor is forwarded EVEN when the resolved DropPoint is None (cursor off every tag) — the whole point.

pinion-widget-paint DockPanelExternal: new drag_cursor: Cell<Option<(f64,f64)>>; drag_to_at/drag_release_at record it then delegate to the existing drag_to/drag_release (escape/dock/snap-back logic unchanged); reset on begin_drag; persists post-release for observability. Exposed read-only as query("drag_cursor") = [x,y]/null (schema + query + intervene ReadOnly + Debug). drag_cursor_introspect helper sibling of drop_preview_introspect.

3rd-consumer self-grep: the _at seam has one forcing consumer (dock drag_cursor); file_browser/reorder use the cursor-less hooks unchanged via default delegation (no _at need yet). drop_preview_introspect + drag_cursor_introspect are NOT identical (Signal vs Cell) so no lift.

R1106.decision_summary: R1106 PR-31: editor zone-honoring cross-window redock — a floating panel returning into main RELOCATES at the dropped zone via DockReorganizer::apply_zone_redock (reusing the same-window intent_for_zone SSOT), the editor's distinguishing value over the flat consumer; re-scoped from design B (host-window threading) to A(ii) (binding gate + one reorganizer method).

examples/hello-dock-panels-editor: the tear_off_redock_at arm (window==MAIN) now reads target/x_rel/y_rel + calls apply_zone_redock to RELOCATE the placeholder leaf AT the dropped zone (Center=tabify / edge=split-insert), then removes the floating window — vs R1105's home-slot return. A(ii) keeps the single gate in the binding (already there R1105) + one clean reorganizer method (intent_for_zone stays private). A(ii) chosen.

R1108.decision_summary: PR-34 redock-totality DECLINED and the spike (4740ea62+58933736) reverted to e340d97b on framework-first grounds. Making SplitInsert and tabify total over source-presence overloads a move primitive to fabricate a panel, violating pinion's own AI-first name-reference invariant (a move verb referencing a panel by name must reject a bad or stale name, not materialise a ghost) and SRP; the unguarded drop verb proved the regression empirically. The consumer-forced premise was also stale: sprag adopted the R72 placeholder model (the leaf survives a float; sprag's own code states the placeholder model moots PINION-PR34), so no live consumer is leaf-removing and the materialise half served nobody. Strict restored -- both drop and reorganize reject an absent source uniformly, no per-verb guard, no new public surface. A future genuine leaf-removing consumer gets materialisation via a distinct explicitly-named redock primitive, never a move-verb overload.

R1137.decision_summary: R1137 floater redock UX v1 (foundation of the pro-tool redesign): (R1136) snap-back fix — a borderless floater's title-bar drag is a WINDOW MOVE, so a release NOT over another window's dock now leaves it FLOATING at its moved position (is_floater_window_move + end_window_move) instead of snapping the panel home; only a DOCKED panel's tear-off snaps back. (R1137) SCXML redock_armed — dock_panel.scxml gains a redock_armed state (floating SUB-mode = over a dock zone) + over_zone/leave_zone events, driven from the shell-resolved cross-window over during the window-move, so the chart makes over-a-zone=redock / elsewhere=stay EXPLICIT + introspectable (query lifecycle). (R1137) visible preview — CoreShell::cross_window_drop_from + shell apply_redock_drag_hint paint the resolved dock zone INTO the dragged floater (topmost, always visible) since the opaque floater occludes the target-window preview.
changes_bullets: Floater redock UX v1 — the gesture fix + SCXML reflection + a visible preview, the foundation of the pro-tool redesign the user requested.

R1136 — snap-back fix: a borderless floater's title-bar drag is a WINDOW MOVE (R1116); a release NOT over another window's dock now leaves it FLOATING at its moved position (is_floater_window_move + end_window_move) instead of snapping the panel back home. Only a DOCKED panel's tear-off still snaps back. drag_cancel of a floater move also stays floating.

R1137 — SCXML redock_armed: dock_panel.scxml gains a `redock_armed` state (a floating SUB-mode = the floater is over a dock zone) + over_zone/leave_zone events. The widget drives it from the shell-resolved cross-window over during the window-move (edge-triggered arm/disarm); is_floating() covers Floating|RedockArmed; settle_cross_window_redock drives `dropped`. The chart now makes "over a zone = will redock / elsewhere = stay" explicit + AI-introspectable (query lifecycle = RedockArmed/Floating). dropped still fires from floating too (the AI invoke / cursor-less path).

R1137 — visible preview: CoreShell::cross_window_drop_from (source-side peer of cross_window_drop_into) + shell apply_redock_drag_hint injects the resolved dock zone INTO the dragged floater (topmost, always visible) via the existing dock_drop_preview hook, since the opaque floater occludes the target-window preview.

carry_forward_bullets: This is FOUNDATION v1 of a multi-round pro-tool floater-redock campaign the user asked for; the design is now well-grounded by a survey of how pro tools work (Visual Studio/Qt Advanced Docking/Unreal Slate = guide-diamond, cursor-based, translucent drag; VS Code/Photoshop/IntelliJ = highlighted-region, cursor-based). REMAINING SLICES (all DESIGN-SETTLED, verified-slice them next, build verified-release each time):

1. VISIBLE DOCK-ZONE GUIDES on main (the pro pattern) — when a floater is over main, highlight main's panels' edge/center dock zones so the user SEES where to aim (the cursor-based trigger feels broken only because the zones are invisible today). The current on-floater hint is the interim; the guides are the real fix.

2. OCCLUSION — pro tools make the dragged window translucent/outline so the target preview shows. pinion has no window-alpha (codegen Vello surface alpha = VELLO-carry-territory, HW/compositor-dependent). Interim = the on-floater hint (this round). Proper = window transparency OR keep the on-floater guide.

drain_drag_for_window (Vello shell + TUI shell, §2 #6 dual) gates the leading press on phase.presses() and the trailing release on phase.releases(); the cursor march always runs — a Begin leaves the router drag session OPEN across RPC calls so a follow-up scene/snapshot sees the held mid-drag, Move re-aims, End settles. R1142.decision_summary: R1142 fix dock-zone guides staying on screen after a drag ends — repaint every guide-host window on drag-END so its guides strip. The R1141 guides show whenever ANOTHER window drags (independent of the cursor), but only the cursor's last preview target was repainted, so releasing while holding the floater left main's guides on a stale frame.
changes_bullets: mouse_released_for_window: when the release ends a drag (the session is still open at entry), repaint EVERY other declared window. The R1141 dock-zone guides show on a window whenever ANOTHER window drags (any_other_window_dragging), independent of the cursor; the existing cross_preview_target repaint only covers the cursor's LAST preview target, so releasing while the cursor sits on the dragged floater (the common case — you let go holding the floater, not over main) left main's guides on a STALE frame, never repainted. That is the "윤곽선이 계속 떠있어" bug.

Headlessly observable via the redraw flag (the [[shell-handler-mutates-visible-state-needs-explicit-redraw]] class — scene data already clears; the bug was the stale visible frame).

Drag-end is fixed here; drag-START show currently relies on the cursor crossing into the host during the drag (works for the toward-host gesture). If guides fail to APPEAR when the cursor never enters the host, add the symmetric repaint on session-open.

R1143.decision_summary: R1143 make the redock preview more forgiving — fall back to the dragged floater's BODY CENTRE when the cursor (the header grab point) is off a zone, so dragging the floater body over a slot previews it even when the header is still outside. A single interior point, not full window-overlap, so the cursor-based model + stay-floating semantics hold.
changes_bullets: resolve_cross_window_live: after the cursor-precise pass finds no zone, fall back to cross_window_drop_at at the dragged window's BODY CENTRE. The grab point rides the header (top / side), so the floater's right edge can enter a slot while a left-side grab is still outside it — the centre catches "the floater body is over the slot" so the preview shows without precise cursor aim.

A single interior point (the centre), NOT full window-overlap: window-overlap is ambiguous (a large host always geometrically contains a small floater, so plain overlap cannot tell "the floater docks into main" from "main contains the floater"), but the floater's centre is a specific point and main's centre is not over the floater, so the existing cursor-based resolution + the "source over its own dock = None" semantics hold. Reuses the same hit-test (no new geometry / no resolution-model change).
verification_bullets: shell r1143_floater_body_centre_over_a_zone_resolves_even_when_the_cursor_is_off_it: a header-edge cursor over no zone (asserted precondition) + the floater centre inside main's dock → resolve_cross_window_live returns main/main_dock (returns None without the fallback — non-tautological).
Existing resolve_cross_window_live tests unchanged: the cursor-precise pass still wins when it hits, and "main over its own dock = None" still holds (main's centre is not over the floater).

carry_forward_bullets: Covers cursor + body-centre. TRUE "slight corner overlap" (조금이라도 = even a tiny touch) would need size-gated bounds-overlap (sample the whole floater footprint, resolve only into LARGER host windows to keep direction unambiguous). R1144.decision_summary: R1144 fix the wgpu validation FREEZE on tear-off — the R1141 dock-zone guide gate ('any other window dragging') lit guides on the brand-new floater a tear-OUT creates and painted them on its churning surface, cascading validation errors that froze the window. Gate guides + their repaint on a SMALLER window dragging toward a LARGER host (a floater into main).
changes_bullets: apply_dock_zone_guides + the R1142 drag-end repaint now gate on a SMALLER window dragging toward a LARGER host (smaller_window_dragging — a window smaller by declared area has an active drag), not "any other window dragging". A tear-OUT makes MAIN (the largest window) the dragger, so no smaller window is dragging → no guides are lit on, and the floater is not repainted on release. The R1141 broad gate lit guides on the brand-new floater being torn off and painted them on its still-churning surface (a just-created / moving window) → a wgpu "surface acquisition failed: validation" / "Texture with '' label is invalid" cascade that FROZE the window. A dock-back (floater small -> main large) still lights main's guides — the correct direction (a floater docks into a larger host, never the reverse).
Removed the now-superseded CoreShell::any_other_window_dragging (the broad gate that was the footgun).
verification_bullets: Live RPC tear-off (lavapipe, visible_window): drag the outliner header out past the right edge → the editor stderr has 0 wgpu surface/validation error lines (was 91 in the frozen R1143 run).

The size gate (smaller-into-larger) is the floater<->host direction; two similar-sized floaters would show no guides between them (edge case, acceptable — dock setups have one large host). LESSON: an overlay gated on "any other window dragging" must exclude the brand-new follower a tear-out is creating (its surface churns); a direction/size gate does this AND is semantically correct.

R1145.decision_summary: R1145 add undock for tabbed panels — pull a panel out of its tab well back into a SPLIT sibling (the reverse of a centre tabify). A live user merged viewport+properties into tabs with no way to separate them (tabs were click-to-switch only). AI invoke('undock_tab', panel) + a human 'Undock tab' toolbar button; a docked result, no floating window.
changes_bullets: DockReorganizer::undock_tab(panel) — pull a tabbed panel OUT of its well and re-dock it as a SPLIT sibling (the reverse of a centre-zone tabify): find a well-sibling (DockTopology::tab_well_sibling) then dock_panel_at_zone(panel, sibling, right edge), which removes the panel from the well (a 2-tab well collapses back to the sibling leaf) and splits it in. A deliberately DOCKED result — no floating window — so it sidesteps the fragile live window-move entirely. undock_active_tab() targets the first well's active panel (the human button); has_tab_wells() gates the affordance.
DockTopology queries: tab_well_sibling (the undock split anchor) + first_tab_well_active_panel.

Human path: a "Undock tab" toolbar button (tag undock_tab_btn) that PAINTS only while something is tabbed (reactive has_tab_wells gate) and undocks the active tab. Both funnel through the shared reorganizer's one commit.

R1146.decision_summary: R1146 dock window-move redesign — the VS Code model: preview during the drag, real OS window only on RELEASE. The pre-R1146 floater drag was app-driven — it created + repositioned a real OS window on EVERY cursor move (the tear_off_follow / window_move flood), whose first move did an expensive GPU-surface init (the live FREEZE) and whose set_outer_position stream wedged the WM (the live HANG). The R1135-R1145 session review found the tail (R1141-R1145) was reactive symptom-patching over this one architectural root. The fix moves window mutation to release-only: during the drag only the lightweight preview shows (the shell drag-image ghost + dock-zone guides + redock hint, all router-driven), and the floating window is created / repositioned ONCE on release. This dissolves the freeze + hang and lets the R1143 center-fallback + R1144 size-gate band-aids be deleted (the right architecture does not need them).
changes_bullets: DockPanelExternal drag handlers (dock.rs): the window-mutating intents now fire on RELEASE ONLY, not per cursor move. drag_to_at no longer emits tear_off_follow (tear-off) or window_move (floater title-bar drag) on each move — it drives only the redock-armed lifecycle + the drop preview. The floating window is created once in drag_release's escape arm (existing) and a floater repositions once in drag_release_at's window-move arm via the single delta window_move_delta(None, cursor, press) = cursor - press (the origin term cancels since the window never moved mid-drag). The previews (R1113 drag-image ghost + R1141 dock-zone guides + R1137 redock hint) are all shell-driven from the router's live drag session, so they keep tracking the cursor with no real window.

Removed the now-dead prev_desktop Cell (it was the per-frame desktop anchor for the per-move feedback-stable delta; release-only has no feedback loop, so it is gone) — field + begin_drag/end_window_move/drag_cancel set sites + constructor.

Dock-zone guides gate (substrate.rs apply_dock_zone_guides): replaced the R1144 smaller_window_dragging size-gate with a plain any_window_dragging gate. The size-gate existed only to keep guides off a brand-new mid-drag floater whose surface was churning (the freeze); the redesign creates no window mid-drag, so the churn is gone and the broad gate is correct (it also lights a SAME-window tear-off's host, which the size gate could not) and safe (the floater is created only after the drag session closes, so it is never painted with guides while initialising). Deleted smaller_window_dragging + window_area helpers.

Drag-end repaint (substrate.rs mouse_released): reverted the R1144 larger-than-source narrowing to repaint EVERY other declared window on a drag-ending release, so their guides clear regardless of relative size.

Removed the R1143 body-centre fallback in resolve_cross_window_live: the floater is stationary during the drag now, so abs = source_pos + cursor_local is the true desktop pointer and the cursor-precise single point resolves cleanly (the pro-tool / VS Code model); the dual resolution-point heuristic would point at the wrong place with a stationary floater.

R1146.publishable_decision_summary: R1146 dock window-move redesign — the VS Code model: preview during the drag, real OS window only on RELEASE. The pre-R1146 floater drag was app-driven — it created + repositioned a real OS window on EVERY cursor move (the tear_off_follow / window_move flood), whose first move did an expensive GPU-surface init (the live FREEZE) and whose set_outer_position stream wedged the WM (the live HANG). The R1135-R1145 session review found the tail (R1141-R1145) was reactive symptom-patching over this one architectural root. The fix moves window mutation to release-only: during the drag only the lightweight preview shows (the shell drag-image ghost + dock-zone guides + redock hint, all router-driven), and the floating window is created / repositioned ONCE on release. This dissolves the freeze + hang and lets the R1143 center-fallback + R1144 size-gate band-aids be deleted (the right architecture does not need them).
publishable_changes_bullets: DockPanelExternal drag handlers (dock.rs): the window-mutating intents now fire on RELEASE ONLY, not per cursor move. drag_to_at no longer emits tear_off_follow (tear-off) or window_move (floater title-bar drag) on each move — it drives only the redock-armed lifecycle + the drop preview. The floating window is created once in drag_release's escape arm (existing) and a floater repositions once in drag_release_at's window-move arm via the single delta window_move_delta(None, cursor, press) = cursor - press (the origin term cancels since the window never moved mid-drag). The previews (R1113 drag-image ghost + R1141 dock-zone guides + R1137 redock hint) are all shell-driven from the router's live drag session, so they keep tracking the cursor with no real window.

Removed the now-dead prev_desktop Cell (it was the per-frame desktop anchor for the per-move feedback-stable delta; release-only has no feedback loop, so it is gone) — field + begin_drag/end_window_move/drag_cancel set sites + constructor.

Dock-zone guides gate (substrate.rs apply_dock_zone_guides): replaced the R1144 smaller_window_dragging size-gate with a plain any_window_dragging gate. The size-gate existed only to keep guides off a brand-new mid-drag floater whose surface was churning (the freeze); the redesign creates no window mid-drag, so the churn is gone and the broad gate is correct (it also lights a SAME-window tear-off's host, which the size gate could not) and safe (the floater is created only after the drag session closes, so it is never painted with guides while initialising). Deleted smaller_window_dragging + window_area helpers.

R1159.decision_summary: R1159 §5.51 — discrete-target drop-resolution SSOT (B model): resolve_drop -> Dock|OuterDock|Float with a banded dead-zone, so a tab tears off inside a maximized window; route the tab through it.
changes_bullets: Introduced the discrete-target drop-resolution model (B): a single resolve_drop(over, is_panel, tabbing) -> DropResolution{Dock|OuterDock|Float} SSOT replacing the scattered over.is_none() float decision.

Added a banded zone classifier (dock_drop_zone_banded) with a FLOAT dead-zone ring: edge bands split, the centre square tabifies, the ring between FLOATS. So a tab tears off INSIDE the window — the structural fix for "탭이 창 밖으로 안 빠져" (the continuous model could only float by leaving the window, impossible when maximized).
resolve_drop validates the target is a dockable panel (DockReorganizer::is_panel), so a release over a splitter/container floats instead of no-op'ing (the R1158 live bug).

Routed the TAB drag (preview + release) through resolve_drop; the preview is DERIVED from the resolver so preview == result. Extracted dock_panel_at_resolved_zone (apply-only) so the banded geometry applies without re-classifying via the legacy continuous one.

R1160.decision_summary: R1160 §5.16 — adopt tracing (level-gated PINION_LOG) as the permanent logging substrate for the dock-drag traces, and fix the tab float window POSITION (positioned tear_off_follow at the drop cursor, not a fixed slot).
changes_bullets: Adopted tracing + tracing-subscriber (env-filter) as the logging substrate instead of ad-hoc eprintln (use-substrate-not-hand-rolled). R1161.decision_summary: R1161 §5.51 — the tabbed well's active panel now fills its cell (flex_grow on the panel itself), fixing the short preview band (preview가 가운데 일부만).
changes_bullets: Fixed the tabbed well's active panel not filling its cell. The walker wrapped the active panel in a flex-grow CONTAINER that grew while the panel INSIDE stayed at its natural content height (~113px in a ~580px cell), so the panel + its drop-zone preview overlay were a short band with empty space below — the "preview가 가운데에서 일부만 나와" bug the user reported.

R1162.decision_summary: R1162 §5.51 — route the panel-header drag (preview + result) through the resolve_drop SSOT, so preview == result by construction (lying-preview bug fixed) + split is the default (banded centre); +SnapBack/source for self-drop.

R1170.decision_summary: R1170 §5.16 §5.39 — floating dock-panel window controls + per-window close seam (the user: 'why no minimize/maximize/exit on a torn-off panel like VS Code'). R1121 deferred per-window close (every close exited the app) + drew no controls on the borderless floater. R1170: (a) WidgetView::window_close_requested binding seam — a torn-off panel's close docks it BACK (drops its WindowSpec, the reconcile removes the OS window), only the primary window's close exits; the shell routes both the OS CloseRequested and the chrome close button through it. (b) WindowChromeStyle.controls_only — the shell injects only the min/max/close buttons (no grip, no title, no content inset), so the panel's own header stays the redock drag handle (a grip would OS-move and break redock; an inset would gap above the header). The editor's window_chrome(torn-X) returns controls_only; the main window keeps OS decorations. min/max are the shell's existing per-window set_minimized/set_maximized.

R1170.1.decision_summary: R1170.1 §5.16 — fix the controls-only chrome contrast (user: the buttons' colours are hard to distinguish). R1170 skipped the grip background entirely for controls-only, so the default light glyphs were drawn directly on the panel header (a light surface) = near-invisible. Fix: (a) draw a background behind ONLY the buttons cluster (not a full-width grip — still no OS-move stealing the redock drag), pointer-transparent so the tagged button hit boxes own the clicks; (b) run V::window_chrome inside the reactive owner (it was outside, so a binding could not read its theme) so the editor themes the cluster — SurfaceContainerHighest bg (a step up from the header's SurfaceContainerHigh) + OnSurface glyphs — and the controls read clearly + distinctly. Added WindowChromeStyle::with_glyph / with_bg builders.

R1171.decision_summary: R1171 §5.16 — controls-in-header redesign (the user caught the smell: 'having to dimension-match the chrome to the header is itself a wrong design'). R1170 rendered a torn-off panel's window controls as a SHELL chrome overlay sized to fixed pixels, which the binding had to manually match to the panel's own header (height, then colour) — two independent layers reconciled by hand, the reactive-patching smell. Root cause: the floater already has a title bar (its panel header = the redock drag handle), so a second shell chrome bar was redundant. R1171: the controls (min/max/close) are rendered IN the panel header via view_dock_panel_with_actions' header-trailing slot — one title bar, auto-sized by the layout (intrinsic glyph+padding, header-centred, no dimension match); text glyphs from glyph.rs (the widget-layer convention). Retired WindowChromeStyle.controls_only (the wrong shell-overlay middle-ground) + the editor window_chrome override + the shell inset/resize branches + the owner-wrap. KEPT the framework-correct part R1170 got right: the WidgetView::window_close_requested seam + the shell's tag routing (try_chrome_press) — the editor tags its header buttons with the re-exported chrome control tags so a press routes to set_minimized/set_maximized/window_close_requested.

R1172.decision_summary: R1172 §5.16 — per-panel MOVE / FLOAT policy: a lockable panel (the user asked for toolbar/status lock). pinion had only DockPanelStyle.drop_target (opt out of RECEIVING a dock); R1172 adds the move-OUT side on DockPanelExternal: with_movable(false) makes begin_drag return None (no drag session opens — the panel cannot be reordered, docked elsewhere, or torn off — a fixed toolbar / status bar, Qt ADS non-movable / VS Code locked), and with_floatable(false) makes a drag that escapes every dock zone SNAP BACK instead of floating (dock-only; the mid-drag detach is floatable-gated so no float ghost). Both are read-only §2 #7 introspection (query movable/floatable). The editor locks its toolbar (with_movable(false)).

R1173.decision_summary: R1173 §5.16 — per-panel style hook in the dock walker (resolves the R1172 carry). The walker view_dock_surface used m3_default for every leaf, so DockPanelStyle.show_header / drop_target could not be set per panel; R1173 adds view_dock_surface_styled(topology, content, split, drop_zone, panel_style, theme) with a per-panel customizer Fn(&str, DockPanelStyle) -> DockPanelStyle run on each LIVE leaf (placeholders keep m3_default). view_dock_surface delegates with the identity customizer (byte-identical). The editor composes its toolbar = HEADERLESS (show_header(false): the menu strip IS the content, no title-bar drag handle) + NON-RECEIVING (drop_target(false): no panel docks INTO it), combined with R1172 with_movable(false) — per-panel chrome (header / receiving / movable) is now freely composed across orthogonal axes.

R1178.decision_summary: R1178 §5.41 — solid Block Element geometric synthesis in the Vello grid arm (PR-40). paint_text_grid routed every cell through parley glyph shaping; a FULL BLOCK / half / quadrant glyph fits its cell loosely (the R1002 *_loose_for_mismatched_cell margin), so block art (terminal logos, progress bars) showed inter-cell gaps — the 'broken bars' a sprag-session live capture of the claude logo reported. block_element_rects now returns the cell-exact fill rectangles for the SOLID blocks (U+2580-2590, U+2594-259F; integer-snapped splits => seamless tiling) and pass 2 fills them in fg instead of shaping a glyph; the block cursor inverse-redraws the same geometry in bg. Shades (U+2591-2593, an alpha pattern) + box-drawing (U+2500-257F, line geometry) deliberately fall through to the glyph path as deferred (A-shade)/(B-box) slices. Vello-arm-local: data contract + TUI arm + §2 #6 cross-consistency untouched, so sprag change 0. No new spec round (purely additive within §5.41's already-ratified rasterise arm; breaks no §2/§3/§5.15 invariant).
changes_bullets: paint_adapter.rs: new block_element_rects(cluster, cx, cy, cell_w, cell_h) -> Option<([KurboRect;4], usize)> — pure, paint-local classifier returning the cell-exact fill rectangles for a SOLID Unicode Block Element (U+2580-2590, U+2594-259F): full / upper-lower-left-right halves / eighths / quadrant subsets (bitmask UL/UR/LL/LR). Split points integer-snapped so abutting fills share a crisp pixel edge and a row of full blocks tiles seamlessly.

paint_text_grid pass 2: branch on block_element_rects BEFORE has_glyph_cluster — a solid block fills its sub-rects in fg_brush instead of routing to draw_cell_glyph; shades (U+2591-2593) and box-drawing (U+2500-257F) return None and fall through to the glyph path unchanged.
paint_grid_cursor Block arm: inverse redraw now fills block geometry in the cell bg (mirrors the glyph inverse-redraw) so a block cursor reads through a block char.
Scope = (A-solid) ONLY. Shades (alpha pattern) and box-drawing (line geometry) are deferred follow-ups; multi-char clusters never qualify.
verification_bullets: 4 pure-geometry unit tests (CI, no GPU): full-block-fills-cell + adjacent-tiles-gap-free, halves cover exact fraction, quadrant combo emits meeting rects (UL/LL/LR), non-solid (text/shade/box/multi-char/empty) falls through to None.

GPU pixel guard r1178_block_element_full_block_tiles_without_gap (#[ignore]d, lavapipe): two adjacent U+2588 cells (10x30 producer-picked, the sprag case) render with ZERO background gap columns across the 2-cell row incl. the boundary seam. Discriminating: r1002_*_loose_for_mismatched_cell proves the prior glyph path left a right gutter on the same cell.
Full pinion-shell --lib --ignored GPU suite (16 tests, lavapipe) green incl. r993 cursor shapes, r995 GUI/TUI cross-consistency (§2 #6), r1013 wide-head draw-order — cursor-arm change non-regressing.

R1180.decision_summary: R1180 §5.41 — box-drawing (B-box) geometric synthesis, completing the block/box render family. box_drawing decomposes the full U+2500-257F block into a BoxGlyph: an arm-weight model (up/down/left/right in none/light/heavy/double + dashed) plus rounded-corner arcs and diagonals. box_arm_rects renders the arm family as integer-snapped filled rects (half-arms abut at centre; any double makes arms overshoot the centre so the rail box connects; doubles draw two rails; dashes split into 2/3/4 segments); rounded corners are a quarter quadratic-bezier stroke, diagonals corner-to-corner strokes. Wired as paint_cell_synthesis's 3rd branch (block -> shade -> box -> glyph). Honest limitation: mixed single/double junctions are approximate, pure-double boxes + straights + simple corners are clean. Vello-arm-local: data contract + TUI + sec2#6 untouched, sprag change 0. With R1178/R1179 the block/box art classes (U+2500-259F) are now fully geometric.
changes_bullets: box_drawing(c): the full U+2500-257F block as BoxGlyph — Arms{up,down,left,right,dash} (weight 0 none/1 light/2 heavy/3 double + dash 2/3/4), Arc{down,right} rounded corners, Diagonal{slash,backslash}. Canonical Unicode arm decomposition, 128-codepoint table.

box_arm_rects: each present arm runs edge->centre; abutting half-arms + integer-snapped bands keep adjacent cells gap-free; any double arm makes all arms overshoot the centre by the rail half-separation so the central rail box connects; double arms draw two parallel rails; dashed glyphs split into 2/3/4 segments.

paint_box_drawing: Arms as filled rects, rounded corners as a quarter quadratic-bezier stroke (quad through the sharp corner), diagonals as corner-to-corner Line strokes; line thickness from the smaller cell dim so weight reads equal H/V.
paint_cell_synthesis 3rd branch: lone_char(cluster).and_then(box_drawing) -> paint_box_drawing; block -> shade -> box -> glyph dispatch order. Block/box art now fully geometric.

R1181.decision_summary: R1181 §5.41 — textbook cleanup of the R1178-1180 block/box synthesis from an independent adversarial audit (no correctness bug; the arm table + quadrant bitmasks verified correct). Fixes the real structural/perf/SSOT smells: (1) synthesizable_char is now the single SSOT gate (lone codepoint in U+2500-259F) and all three classifiers take a char extracted once - killing the triplicated lone-char extraction and the &str/char signature mismatch; (2) box_arm_rects returns a stack [KurboRect;8]+count instead of a per-frame heap Vec, matching its block_element_rects sibling (8 = exact all-double max); (3) box_line_metrics computed once (dead recompute removed); (4) magic numbers (arc 0.4, dash 0.7 duty) lifted to named consts; (5) §2 #6 is now test-pinned for the synthesis class via a box cross in text_grid_consistency_buffer (was reasoned-only) - r995 GUI+TUI green. Remaining items (arc/diagonal sub-pixel AA at junctions; mixed single/double junction not pixel-canonical) are audit-judged acceptable, documented.
changes_bullets: synthesizable_char(cluster) -> Option<char>: ONE SSOT gate for "painted as geometry not a glyph" — lone codepoint in the contiguous U+2500-259F range (box + block + shade). Fast-rejects ordinary text/spaces with a single range check before any classifier.

All three classifiers now take char (not &str): removed the triplicated lone-char extraction; block_element_rects + box_drawing + shade_block_fraction dispatch a char from paint_cell_synthesis (extracted once). block_element_rects also takes cell:KurboRect (param-convention parity with the box fns).

box_arm_rects returns stack ([KurboRect;8], count) instead of a per-frame heap Vec, matching its block_element_rects sibling; 8 is the exact max (all-double ChevronCross = 2 rails x 4 arms). Removes allocator churn on box-heavy screens (the pro-tool-perf axis).
box_line_metrics computed once: removed the dead top-level recompute in paint_box_drawing (Arms uses box_arm_rects' own; only Arc/Diagonal need it).
Magic numbers -> named module consts: BOX_DASH_DUTY (0.7), BOX_ARC_RADIUS_FRACTION (0.4).

changes_bullets: examples/hello-node-editor: AutoPan Tickable + use_autopan register-once (the CaretBlink precedent) scrolls the world ScrollState toward the rim each frame while a live node drag hugs it; autopan_push gives the 0.12 rim margin a linear edge-saturating ramp at 900 world-px/s, node clamps at the world extent.

node_drag lifted RefCell -> Rc<RefCell> + a new autopan_cursor Cell (use_node_drag / use_autopan_cursor holders) give the tick one authoritative drag state; the follow_members node-follow kernel + the cursor_graph_at projection are the shared SSOT that pointer_move and the tick both run.

R1183.decision_summary: R1183 audit-clearance of R1182 auto-pan: fix the world-clamp frame-burn (Tickable is_at_rest contract), complete the inverse-projection SSOT, and co-locate the cursor probe inside NodeDragStart.
changes_bullets: SMELL-1 (Tickable contract): AutoPan::active() now gates on scroll headroom (new pure autopan_axis_can_move over ScrollState offset/max), so is_at_rest is true once the viewport can no longer scroll in the push direction - a node pinned at the world edge no longer spins the redraw loop. R1182 wrongly modeled auto-pan on the inherently-periodic CaretBlink; it is progress-bounded.

SMELL-2 (SSOT overclaim): the inverse projection canvas-px -> graph is now ONE primitive canvas_to_graph that cursor_graph_at, the coordinator's cursor_graph, set_zoom_anchored's anchor solve, and the viewport.{x,y} query all route through (was 3 hand-inlined copies of the same affine). The forward twin graph -> offset (wpx + apply_viewport anchor solve) is left as a pre-existing separate follow-up.

NIT-1: the auto-pan rim-probe cursor moved into NodeDragStart (co-located Cell) so its lifecycle tracks the drag by construction; removed the separate autopan_cursor holder + use_autopan_cursor hook + GraphServices field + reset_gesture clear (which had been cleared at only 1 of 3 node_drag=None sites - harmless but fragile).
verification_bullets: New unit tests: r1183_autopan_axis_can_move_headroom (boundary of the headroom predicate) + r1183_autopan_rests_at_clamp_and_in_dead_zone (builds an AutoPan; asserts at-rest at the +x world clamp AND for an unlatched dead-zone press, active with headroom - the two gates R1182 left untested). Demo gains the zoom!=1 1:1 ride invariant (37 assertions).
143 hello-node-editor tests + cargo test --workspace (198 result-ok, 0 failed) pass; clippy -D pedantic (pinion-runtime/vello) + rustfmt clean.
carry_forward_bullets: Forward viewport projection (graph -> offset: wpx + apply_viewport anchor solve, ~4 sites) is NOT consolidated - pre-existing, deserves its own Viewport-value-type round (not an R1182/R1183 regression).
Wire-connect auto-pan (begin_drag DnD path) + a router-level generic auto-pan lift remain deferred pending a genuine 2nd consumer (carried from R1182).

R1184.decision_summary: R1184 §5.49 §5.39 — scene/type {text, at|path}: a single RPC that types a whole string, fanning text into one DeferredInput::CharacterKey per Unicode scalar (atomic Press) via the scene/key character path. Pure-text scope (A); declined A.1 (\n->Enter / \t->Tab control-char mapping) and A.2 (whole-string modifiers) — \n is a literal scalar, a client submits via an explicit scene/key {Enter}, keeping the text vocabulary separate from the named-key vocabulary on the wire. Unroll-at-dispatch (NOT a DeferredInput::TypeText batch) is faithful to the real input stream: a physical keyboard has no type-a-whole-string event, so N independent keystrokes is exactly what real input produces; scene/drag differs (keeps its batch intact to the drain) because a drag holds correlated cross-event state (button held + R51.34 capture lock) across its moves. Consumer-forced by sprag R88 PR41; sprag change 0.
changes_bullets: scene/type {text, at|path} added to pinion-rpc: fans text out to one DeferredInput::CharacterKey per Unicode scalar (text.chars()), atomic KeyWireState::Press, reusing the scene/key character-key path (drain -> handle_character_key -> V::keybinding then apply_key). Zero new input pipeline; commit f4a2f771.

Pure-text scope (A) decided; A.1 (\n->Enter, \t->Tab control-char mapping) and A.2 (whole-string modifiers) declined. \n is a literal U+000A scalar, not an Enter edge; a client submits via an explicit scene/key {Enter} (7 RPC -> 2). Keeps the text vocabulary and the named-key vocabulary separate on the wire, mirroring scene/drag's separation from scene/click.

Unroll-at-dispatch (not a DeferredInput::TypeText batch variant) is faithful to the real input stream: a physical keyboard has no "type a whole string" event, so N independent CharacterKey entries is what a real keyboard produces; scene/drag differs (keeps DeferredInput::Drag intact to the drain) because a real drag carries correlated held-button state across moves.

RPC_METHODS catalog entry ("scene/type", MethodOcc::Read) — deferred input does not bump the OCC revision synchronously, matching scene/key; guarded by the catalog_matches_dispatch_match_arms cross-check. 7 dispatch tests incl. a non-tautological newline scope-lock (fails if \n->Enter is ever added).

R1185.decision_summary: R1185 §5.16 §5.35 — reconcile_externals re-projects declarative policy onto preserved live externals via a new default-no-op External::reconcile_from(fresh) seam. The R688 reconcile preserved the live node for every surviving tag (right for in-flight gesture state) but that also froze declarative policy — a DockPanelExternal movable/floatable lock the factory recomputes each reconcile — at first construction, so a 'last docked pane cannot tear off' lock never reached the live node (begin_drag stayed movable, so the sole docked pane still showed a drag chip + drop preview). The fix hands each surviving live handle its freshly-built descriptor on BOTH the steady-state and preserve-by-tag paths; DockPanelExternal::reconcile_from copies movable/floatable from fresh through the existing introspection query channel (no Any / no downcast; the default no-op keeps every other External byte-identical). Consumer API with_movable(bool) unchanged; consumer-forced by sprag PR-42, sprag change 0.
changes_bullets: External::reconcile_from(&mut self, fresh: &dyn External) added to pinion-core (default no-op): the R688 external-set reconcile hands each preserved live handle its freshly-built descriptor so a widget re-projects declarative-but-reactive policy while keeping its own in-flight gesture state. Default no-op keeps every existing External (and every pre-R1185 binding) byte-identical.

CoreShell::reconcile_externals now calls reconcile_from on every surviving tag on BOTH paths — the steady-state early-return (tag set unchanged) and the preserve-by-tag rebuild — so a per-panel flag the factory recomputes each reconcile is no longer frozen at first construction. Root cause of PR-42: the preserve-the-live-node contract (right for in-flight state) also froze declarative policy.

DockPanelExternal::reconcile_from copies movable/floatable from fresh through the existing introspection query channel (no Any / no downcast, no boilerplate on the other ~15 External impls). drop_target is already dynamic via the R1173 dock-surface style walker. Consumer API with_movable(bool) unchanged, so the sole docked pane locks live: begin_drag returns None, no drag chip / no drop preview.

Rejected reactive-Signal flag (B: leaks reactive plumbing into every flag + the consumer factory, changes the API, does not fix the class) and imperative set_movable (C: needs the Effect-driven intervene the reconcile rustdoc explicitly warns against). (A) fixes the class — any declarative-but-reactive policy on any External. Consumer-forced by sprag PR-42; sprag change 0.
