R1186.decision_summary: R1186 §5.16 §5.39 — decouple the client-side resize border from window_chrome via a new WidgetView::window_resizable hook (PR-43, sprag-forced). A controls-in-header floating window (window_chrome==None, its title bar is the R1171 dock header) stays resizable: pre-R1186 the resize border rode the chrome gate, so such a window had no resize. AUDIT reframed the handoff — controls-in-header was ALREADY shipped (R1171 + hello-dock-panels-editor prove a binding builds header-hosted min/max/close that route via try_chrome_press), so the sole pinion gap was the resize-chrome coupling. window_resizable defaults None = derive from chrome presence (byte-identical back-compat); Some(true) keeps the border on a chrome-less window; Some(false) drops it on a chromed one. Resize VARIANT: a chromed window keeps all eight regions (its chrome strip is layered on top and reclaims the north); a chrome-less window uses inject_resize_border_below_titlebar which OMITS the north edge + top corners so they cannot shadow the header close button (the header owns the top — move + controls — and cannot be layered over the border the way a chrome strip is). Chosen against literal 8-direction, which shadowed the close button at the corner users reach to close; below-titlebar is parity with the chromed case's functional resize + the codebase's own title-bar-owns-the-top CSD principle.
changes_bullets: WidgetView::window_resizable(window_id) -> Option<bool> added to pinion-shell (default None = derive from window_chrome presence, so every existing binding is byte-identical to pre-R1186). apply_resize_border is re-gated on it via a new chrome-independent resolve_window_spec (window_chrome_for now delegates to it), applied on BOTH the live paint and the pure introspection mirror (§2 #7). The "field on WindowChromeStyle" alternative cannot express this — a controls-in-header window has no chrome, so the hook is forced.

inject_resize_border_below_titlebar added to pinion-overlay (shared inject_resize_regions(include_top) helper): OMITS the north edge + the two top corners for a window whose title bar is a CONTENT dock header (window_chrome==None, R1171 controls-in-header) that owns the top (move handle + close button). A chromed window keeps all eight regions (its chrome strip is layered ON TOP and reclaims the north). Chrome-less resizable → below-titlebar; chromed → all-8.

Design decided AGAINST literal 8-direction: injecting the north regions on a chrome-less floater let the NE resize corner shadow the header close button at the very corner users reach to close (the header is content, so hit_test last-child-wins gives the resize overlay priority — the chrome case avoids it only by after-injection). Below-titlebar = parity with the chromed case's functional resize + the codebase's own "the top edge is owned by the title bar" CSD principle. A title-bar window is MOVED from its top, not resized.

AUDIT reframed the sprag PR-43 handoff: controls-in-header was ALREADY shipped (R1171 view_dock_panel_with_actions + pinion glyph::WINDOW_* + public WINDOW_CHROME_*_TAG + try_chrome_press tag-routing), demonstrated + tested by hello-dock-panels-editor, so a binding CAN build header-hosted controls that route. The sole pinion gap was the resize-chrome coupling. Editor floating windows now return window_resizable Some(true) = the forcing consumer.

R1187.decision_summary: R1187 §5.16 §5.39 — lift view_window_controls (the min/max/close controls-in-header builder) from hello-dock-panels-editor into pinion_widget_paint::dock as the composition SSOT (R1186 PR-43 follow-up; sprag is the 2nd consumer). The builder owns the visual composition — three Scene::Text glyph buttons (glyph::WINDOW_*) in a flex Row for the view_dock_panel_with_actions header_trailing slot — while a new WindowControlTags param carries the binding-supplied routing tags. Dep-graph constraint: pinion-widget-paint is backend-agnostic and does NOT depend on the GUI-overlay crate that owns the WINDOW_CHROME_*_TAG routing tags, so the tags are passed IN (the binding already imports the pinion-shell re-exports and try_chrome_press routes on them) rather than hardcoded — no new dependency edge, composition SSOT in the widget crate, routing wiring stays with the binding that owns the window lifecycle. The editor was refactored to delegate (its ~30-line local copy + the now-unused glyph import removed); the pre-existing r1171 test is unchanged and passes, so the lift is behaviour-preserving.

R1188.decision_summary: R1188 §5.16 §5.49 §5.39 — RPC scene/click now DRIVES the window controls (min/max/close), closing the R1121 'an AI observes AND DRIVES the controls' contract's drive half (PR-44, sprag-forced). Pre-R1188 the control-press routing (AppShell::try_chrome_press -> set_minimized / set_maximized / window_close_requested) existed only on the winit pointer path; the RPC DeferredInput::Click drain fell into widget routing, so a click on WINDOW_CHROME_*_TAG no-opped (chrome strip AND R1187 controls-in-header buttons alike). Fix = design (A) one routing SSOT: a shell-neutral WindowControl vocabulary + window_control_for_tag mapping in pinion-overlay (beside the tags); the headless ShellCore Click drain mirrors the winit interception (resolve hover -> on a discrete-control hit resolve the canonical spec via resolve_window_spec(scope) and QUEUE it, consuming the click) and AppShell drains that queue right after dispatch_rpc through the SAME apply_window_control arm the winit press uses. Grip/resize are NOT intercepted (pointer-session gestures; RPC peers scene/window_move / scene/resize). Secondary finding REFRAMED (doc-only): scene/locate + scene/bbox read the geometry-less R795 STATE scene, so their zero-rect / OutOfBounds answers are by-design for view-fn bindings (live AND headless), not a live-only mirror-viewport defect; documented, pointing to scene/layout / snapshot-from-paint for painted-frame geometry.
changes_bullets: WindowControl { Minimize, Maximize, Close } + window_control_for_tag added to pinion-overlay beside the WINDOW_CHROME_*_TAG constants (the detection SSOT; shell-neutral, no winit types). Grip / resize tags deliberately map to None: pointer-session gestures whose RPC peers are scene/window_move / scene/resize, not a click. Re-exported from pinion-overlay + pinion-shell roots.

ShellCore (headless): the DeferredInput::Click drain arm now mirrors the winit interception — after seeding the cursor it resolves the hover target, and on a discrete control-tag hit resolves the CANONICAL spec id via resolve_window_spec(scope) (drain signature window_id: &str -> scope: Option<&str>, the R1123.1 never-re-derive-from-the-DEFAULT_WINDOW-fallback rule) and queues (spec, control) on pending_window_controls, CONSUMING the click (widget press/release skipped — winit parity: try_chrome_press consumes the press; the winit trailing release is a no-op over a chrome tag, so router state is equivalent). take_pending_window_controls() drains.

R1189.decision_summary: R1189 §5.16 §5.39 — client-side resize-border HOVER cursor affordance (PR-45, sprag-forced). A borderless (CSD) window's resize border worked on press-drag but never set the mouse cursor to a resize shape on hover — pinion-shell never called winit Window::set_cursor (grep-confirmed 0). The OS gives a decorated window this for free over its frame; a borderless window has no frame, so the shell owns it. Fix: handle_cursor_moved, after cursor_moved_for_window re-resolves the hover target, maps a hover over a WINDOW_RESIZE_* region to the matching CursorIcon through the press-side chrome_action_for_tag tag->ResizeDirection SSOT + a new pure resize_cursor_for_action (N/S=NsResize, W/E=EwResize, NW/SE=NwseResize, NE/SW=NeswResize); a per-window min-change latch (WindowSlot::last_resize_cursor, mirroring last_commanded_position) commands winit set_cursor ONLY on change, so a window that never enters a resize region is never commanded a cursor (a decorated / non-resizable window's client area stays OS-managed). The hover cursor and a press both resolve through the ONE hover_target->chrome_action_for_tag chain, so the shown cursor axis can never diverge from the resize a press would trigger. Grip/control -> the default arrow (a title bar is dragged, not shown a move cursor). No new hit-test; headless/RPC unaffected (pure live winit affordance). Independent review found no confirmed bug; its two actionable items folded (a CursorLeft reset so a leave over an edge does not strand the OS cursor, and the latch decision extracted to a pure next_cursor_command with a transition test).
changes_bullets: resize_cursor_for_action(ChromeAction) -> Option<CursorIcon> added to pinion-shell/app.rs (pure, next to chrome_action_for_tag): maps the eight ResizeDirection the tag SSOT resolves to the four CSS-standard resize cursors (N/S=NsResize, W/E=EwResize, NW/SE=NwseResize, NE/SW=NeswResize); Move(grip)/Control -> None (a title bar keeps the default arrow, the GTK/Win11 caption convention). Read side of the same tag vocabulary the press side drives through drag_resize_window; unit-tested tag->cursor for all 8 regions + None for grip/close/minimize/widget.

handle_cursor_moved now reads the hover target the just-run cursor_moved_for_window re-resolved -> chrome_action_for_tag -> resize_cursor_for_action -> command_resize_cursor. NO new hit-test: the hover target is already computed (the press path reads the same). borderless CSD windows get the resize-cursor affordance the OS gives a decorated window over its frame for free.

Per-window min-change LATCH WindowSlot::last_resize_cursor (mirrors last_commanded_position): command_resize_cursor calls winit set_cursor ONLY when the desired icon differs from what is shown, so the per-CursorMoved cost is a hover read + an equality compare. A window that never enters a resize region keeps the latch None and is NEVER commanded a cursor (a decorated / non-resizable window's client area stays OS-managed). Leave/re-enter is correct WITHOUT a CursorLeft reset: the latch persists across leave, so re-entry over content fires the once-only Default reset via the Some->None transition (a leave-reset would instead skip that needed reset and strand a stale OS-remembered resize cursor).
verification_bullets: Unit tests (2, pure — no live winit): r1189_resize_hover_maps_each_region_to_its_cursor (tag->cursor for all 8 resize regions = the 4 CSS axes; grip/close/minimize/widget -> None) + r1189_cursor_latch_only_commands_on_change (the extracted next_cursor_command latch decision: enter->set, same->suppress, region->region->set-new, region->content/leave->Default-once, content->content->suppress). The set_cursor + slot mutation is thin winit glue (live-only, no headless winit); the two pure fns ARE the routing + latch contract, mirroring how chrome_action_for_tag is tested without a window.

Workspace 198 suites pass; existing r1121_chrome_action mapping tests unchanged; clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello clean (set_cursor(impl Into<Cursor>) is the non-deprecated winit 0.30 API); cargo fmt --check clean; doc-links resolve.

Independent adversarial review: no CONFIRMED bug (hover cursor + press action share the ONE hover_target->chrome_action_for_tag chain, so shown-cursor axis can never diverge from a press's resize; borrow/NLL sound; decorated/non-resizable windows never commanded a cursor via the None==None short-circuit; multi-window per-slot latch isolated; the R1186 below-titlebar floater's north-omission → no top cursor, W/E full-height edges correctly show EwResize matching the press-side resize there). Two PLAUSIBLE cosmetic edges + 1 nit ADDRESSED: (#1 CursorLeft left the OS cursor + latch stale on leave → now command_resize_cursor(window_id, None) resets both on the CursorLeft arm) + (nit: latch untestable → extracted pure next_cursor_command + test). (#2 suspend/resume + maximize-under-stationary-cursor: carry — practically unreachable, resize cursors are desktop-mouse while suspend/resume is mobile-lifecycle + resume_spec rebuilds the slot re-initing the latch; maximize-stationary self-heals on the next motion.)
carry_forward_bullets: sprag PR-45: change 0 — the border is already on (sprag R95 window_resizable Some(true)); the cursor follows on a pinion bump. Live-verify (:0) the 8 main-window edge cursors + the floater's side/bottom cursors with NO cursor on its header-owned top edge (R1186 north-omission consistency).
Grip -> Move cursor DELIBERATELY omitted (a title bar is dragged, not shown a move cursor — GTK/Win11/VS Code convention); revisit only if a consumer asks.

A future per-widget hover cursor (I-beam over text, pointer over buttons) would extend command_resize_cursor's `desired` resolution beyond the resize regions; the natural seam is a WidgetView::cursor_for_hover(tag) hook (handoff option B) — deferred as YAGNI until a real consumer, since resize cursors are universal and shell-owned.

The set_cursor + latch is thin winit glue (live-only, no headless winit); the pure resize_cursor_for_action mapping is the unit-testable contract, mirroring how chrome_action_for_tag is tested without a live window.

Review carry (practically unreachable, not fixed): (#2a) suspend/resume with a cached-window reuse could leave the OS cursor attribute stale vs the rebuilt slot's None latch — but resize cursors are desktop-mouse-only while suspend/resume is a mobile lifecycle (no cursor), and resume_spec rebuilds the slot (latch re-inits None); (#2b) an RPC/keyboard maximize under a stationary cursor over a resize edge strands the resize cursor until the next motion (border leaves the scene, no CursorMoved) — self-heals on move. Both need a non-pointer state change with a stationary cursor over a region; low severity, carry only.

R1193.decision_summary: R1193 per-window WindowState consolidation: ShellCore's 11 lockstep *_per_window HashMaps become one HashMap<String, WindowState>, so a window's teardown drops ONE entry (retires the R1123.1/R681 add-a-map-then-forget-to-clear leak class). Behavior-preserving; the audit's charter-accretion fix.
changes_bullets: pinion-shell substrate.rs: new WindowState struct (11 axes) + window_state / window_state_mut accessors replace 11 parallel *_per_window: HashMap<String,T> fields. Presence-meaningful axes are Option<T> (absent = never-set for THAT axis, distinct from a default value) so an entry created for one axis never reads as present for another; natural-default flags (redraw_requested / immediate_subtree / maximized) stay plain bool.

remove_window collapses 11 OR-ed .remove() calls into one window_states.remove(id).is_some() — the payoff: a new per-window axis is now a WindowState field cleared by the single removal, not another map a future round must remember to add to teardown (the exact leak class the old body's R1123.1/R681 comment documented).

presence-gated views (fragment_cache_stat_windows, union_focusable_tags) filter by the field's .is_some(), NOT all window_states keys; clear_target_fps_for_window prunes an emptied entry (WindowState::is_empty) so remove_window's return stays exact; take_pending_immediate_dt helper keeps compute_paint_scene_internal within the 100-line budget.
AppShell already consolidated its per-window state into WindowSlot; this makes ShellCore symmetric (the R1192-re-labeled risk-gated charter accretion, now paid).
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: 198 targets ok / 0 failed (7919 assertions), incl. all per-window families that exercise the presence semantics at risk: R683 remove-drain, R907 timing-entry-drop, R1123.1 maximized-leak, R25 focus-union, pacing/fps, immediate-mode.

3 new invariant tests pin the crux: per-axis presence isolation (a maximized-only window is excluded from the fragment-stats + focus-union window sets), remove_window drops every axis at once + reports carried state, clearing the sole axis prunes the entry.

Independent adversarial review (per-field presence-semantics lens): EXACTLY behavior-preserving, 0 defects across all 40 access sites + 7 hazard classes — verified reads never mint entries, both presence-gated views filter by field presence, all Option-vs-bool categorizations correct, remove_window / is_empty / consume paths byte-equivalent.
clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello + fmt clean; cargo doc: new WindowState intra-doc links resolve, no new broken links.
carry_forward_bullets: L2 residual (pre-R1193, unchanged): WindowPolicy is resolved twice per paint (apply_resize_border + window_chrome_for) — minor, resolve-once threading touches the hot paint path.

R1194.decision_summary: R1194 measured variable-height list virtualization: view_measured_list windows against a MeasuredHeights table that starts from an estimate and is refined each frame by a layout-pass harvest reading every rendered row's laid-out height, keeping the scroll anchored (no jump) as rows resolve estimate->measured — the render-then-measure round-trip the RowOffsets scope note reserved, closing the last deferred Model/View windowing mode.
changes_bullets: pinion-core virtual_list.rs: new MeasuredHeights (estimated fallback + sparse measured map -> RowOffsets), scroll_anchor / anchor_preserving_offset (the measured list no-jump correction), and a shared RowOffsets::row_at row-at-pixel kernel lifted from compute_visible_range_variable's window edges.

pinion-core measured_rows.rs: new MeasuredRowState (RefCell<MeasuredHeights> behind a generation Signal) + use_measured_rows Owner-cached hook + harvest(scroll, viewport_h, rows) that records heights, grows the bound, and anchor-corrects the offset; MEASURED_ROW_TAG_PREFIX / measured_row_tag / measured_row_index tag SSOT.
pinion-core scene.rs: ScrollNode gains an optional measured_rows: Option<Rc<MeasuredRowState>> field + with_measured_rows builder (peer of state; None for every ordinary scroll, a pure opt-in).

pinion-runtime layout.rs: new post-layout harvest_measured_rows reducer (sibling of update_scroll_state_bounds) collects each windowed row's laid-out rect.h by tag and feeds MeasuredRowState::harvest; folded into the frame dirty bit for the measure-then-settle warmup.
pinion-widget-paint virtual_list.rs: new view_measured_list assembly + measured_slot (width-fixed / height-auto so the harvest reads natural content height, tagged measured-row:<index>).

examples/hello-measured-list + tools/demos/r1194_measured_list.py: forcing consumer (120 rows of lines(i) fixed-height strips; queryable MeasuredListExternal exposing measured_count / total_height / is_fully_measured / exact_total).
CLAUDE.md: corrected the stale "tray 0%" tally (the SNI substrate + real D-Bus bridge shipped R949/R950; only the headless session-bus test-watcher harness is outstanding).
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: all targets ok, 0 failed; adds MeasuredHeights + scroll-anchor units, 8 MeasuredRowState units, 2 view_measured_list shape units, 4 hello-measured-list units, and the existing compute_visible_range_variable suite guards the row_at SSOT refactor.

tools/demos/r1194_measured_list.py PASS (>=30 assertions): boot window small; each rendered measured-row slot height == modeled height (the harvest read real content height, not the estimate); scrolling the whole list grows measured_count monotonically and converges total_height from the 5760 estimate baseline to the exact 7920 sum with is_fully_measured true; offset clamps to exact_total - viewport.

Anchor no-jump proven headlessly in MeasuredRowState::harvest units (real ScrollState + real offsets): 400px of growth in rows above the viewport moves the offset to keep the viewport-top row pinned; measuring at or below the anchor leaves the offset untouched.

use_measured_rows seeds item_count at first construction; a growable/streaming measured list syncs via MeasuredRowState::set_count from a reconcile_frame hook (not the view fn) — auto-sync stays a 2nd-consumer gate.

Anchor correction is proven at the substrate level and exercised end-to-end by the demo's full traversal; the isolated jump-scroll-then-up render-pixel path has no separate live witness (substrate-tested instead).

R1195.decision_summary: R1195 chrome window top-edge resize band: a chromed window's outermost RESIZE_EDGE_PX top edge is now a live NORTH resize band (VS Code / Win11 / GTK parity), lifted back on top of the chrome strip by the new overlay raise_top_resize_edge after apply_window_chrome. Corrects the pre-R1195 'top owned by the title bar' layering (the north band was dead under the strip); reuses R1189's hover-cursor mapping and R1122's press routing, so no new cursor or press wiring.
changes_bullets: pinion-overlay window_chrome.rs: new raise_top_resize_edge(scene, viewport) strips the north resize band inject_resize_border put UNDER the chrome strip and re-pushes it as the TOPMOST child, so the outermost RESIZE_EDGE_PX (6px) of a chromed title bar resize the window (even over the controls, as VS Code) — self-gating on the band's presence (no-op unless a resizable, non-maximized, chromed window), idempotent.
pinion-overlay highlight.rs: new has_top_level_tag(scene, tag) helper to gate the re-layer on the node's presence.

pinion-shell substrate.rs: apply_window_overlays calls raise_top_resize_edge after apply_window_chrome (shared by the live paint and the pure introspection mirror); corrected the apply_resize_border + inject_resize_border rustdoc that claimed the top edge was owned by the title bar.
examples/hello-window-chrome: doc note that the top edge now resizes the window (VS Code / Win11).
Renamed the shell test chrome_strip_wins_over_resize_border_at_the_top to top_edge_is_a_resize_band_over_strip and updated the reachability probes for the corrected behavior.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace 0-fail: 4 new pinion-overlay units (north band raised above the strip and topmost / idempotent second raise / no-op without a band [chrome-less + bare scene] / degenerate viewport no-op) + updated shell hit-test tests that drive the real router: the top 6px at (150,3) and over the close button at (394,3) resolve to WINDOW_RESIZE_NORTH_TAG, while the close button (394,16) and the move grip (150,16) are reachable below the band.

The live top-edge drag-resize is HW-gated (:0 / a real window), verified in the consumer session like R1189's hover cursor; the headless witness is the router hit-test resolution plus the unchanged R1189 chrome_action_for_tag(North) -> NsResize and R1122 drag_resize_window(North) paths, which now become reachable once the band is on top.
carry_forward_bullets: The two TOP corners (NW / NE) deliberately stay under the strip (diagonal resize from the top off), so the NE corner cannot shadow the close button a user reaches for (the R1186 concern); the top edge resizes vertically only.
The top RESIZE_EDGE_PX (6px) shadows the very top of the controls, exactly as VS Code: a control is clicked from a few px below its top edge. Standard and acceptable.

R1199.decision_summary: R1199 audit-clearance of R1194 (measured windowing) + R1196 (cursor seam): three independent adversarial audits + own grep found the shipped session code sound (no functional bugs, no §2 violations) but flagged real debt. This round clears the R1194/R1196 findings: cursor_hint_at now REUSES hit_test + lookup_path_ref (the resolve_hover_tag / resolve_drop_target_tag SSOT pattern) instead of re-descending the tree; MeasuredRowState::offsets memoizes the RowOffsets by generation (Rc, O(1) scroll frames — the R1194 doc claimed a cache that did not exist); the measured-row slot tag is scoped by the scroll tag (no §2#7 namespace collision for two lists); a compute_layout-driven runtime test now covers the taffy->rect.h->harvest round-trip the round lacked; a debug_assert fails fast on a measured_rows node wired without a ScrollState.
changes_bullets: pinion-core scene.rs: Scene::cursor_hint_at reimplemented to REUSE hit_test's single tree descent (walk the returned HitPath deepest-first via lookup_path_ref, first node with a cursor_hint) — retires the duplicate descent, matching the resolve_hover_tag / resolve_drop_target_tag sibling resolvers so hit_test is the descent SSOT.

pinion-core measured_rows.rs: MeasuredRowState memoizes the RowOffsets keyed by the generation Signal (new cached field; offsets() returns Rc<RowOffsets>); a plain scroll frame (which moves the offset Signal, not the generation) returns the cached Rc in O(1) — the R1194 doc claimed this cache but never implemented it, so a settled list re-walked the O(n) table every scroll frame.

pinion-core measured_rows.rs: measured_row_tag(scroll_tag, index) scopes the row-slot tag under the scroll's tag (<scroll_tag>/measured-row:<index>); measured_row_index parses either form — two measured lists in one window no longer collide in the flat scene/snapshot tag namespace (§2 #7). view_measured_list threads scroll.tag() through.

pinion-runtime layout.rs: new compute_layout-driven test drives the REAL layout pass over a measured-list scene and asserts the harvest read each row's taffy-laid-out rect.h into MeasuredRowState (the integration coverage R1194 lacked — its Rust tests fed heights directly, bypassing taffy) + a debug_assert fails fast on a measured_rows node wired without a ScrollState.

pinion-core style.rs: corrected the LayoutStyle.cursor doc — the resolved cursor is read via a shell-side accessor (ShellCore::cursor_hint), not an RPC method (R1196's phrasing oversold the introspection).

carry_forward_bullets: NEXT clearance round (R1200) = R1195-R1198 window-resize doc debt from the in-session R1197->R1198 churn: apply_resize_border rustdoc + inline comment still say "omits the top-right corner" (R1198 restored a small one); the top-clearance contract is overstated (a 28px header centering its controls gives ~2-4px, not >= RESIZE_EDGE_PX — functionally fine, the doc reasoning is wrong); inject_resize_border_below_titlebar is production-orphaned since R1197 + its doc misattributes the role content_header now fills; raise_top_resize_edge's "north band exists iff chromed" rationale is stale (R1197 added a 2nd producer, hence the AND-chrome gate); SIDE_BOTTOM_RESIZE_TAGS const doc is stale; and raise reconstructs the north-band rect byte-for-byte (latent geometry dup vs inject_resize_regions).

The two-cursor-producer deferral (node-hint + chrome-tag in handle_cursor_moved) is process-correct: the chrome cursor path is under active extension this session (R1195/97/98), so folding it into node-hints would refactor a just-touched path. The single-cursor-SSOT end-state (grow CursorHint to 4 variants, stamp the eight overlay resize-region boxes, retire resize_cursor_for_action) stays on the books as a follow-up round.

R1219.decision_summary: R1219 fixes a live-testing bug: the bottom of a window flickered during interactive resize because the newly-exposed region went unpainted through the OS modal resize loop.
changes_bullets: pinion-shell app.rs note_window_resized: paint the resized surface SYNCHRONOUSLY (call render_window in-band) instead of scheduling an async request_redraw. During an interactive OS resize the platform's modal resize loop withholds RedrawRequested until the drag ends, so the async path left the grown region unpainted for the whole drag -> a flash at the grow edge (bottom when growing vertically). Shell-global, so all windows/apps benefit.
render_window early-returns on a 0-size (minimize) window, so the unconditional synchronous call is safe; winit coalesces any residual redraw so there is no double paint.
Found by the user live-testing the todomvc example window on :0 (the 'show me a testable app' request).
verification_bullets: VISUAL (user-verified on :0, the only way to verify this HW/compositor-timing artifact -- headless cannot reproduce an interactive resize): user resized the live todomvc window and confirmed the bottom flicker is gone.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = exit 0; cargo test -p pinion-shell = pass; no test asserted request_redraw-on-resize (no regression).
Rebuilt binary confirmed to contain the fix (binary newer than the edit; rebuild a 0.16s no-op).
carry_forward_bullets: LESSON: interactive-resize flicker = the OS modal resize loop withholds RedrawRequested during the drag, so any async request_redraw-on-resize leaves the newly-exposed region unpainted until drag-end. Fix = synchronous paint in the Resized handler. Verification of such flicker is HW-gated (user's eyes on a real compositor); headless/RPC cannot reproduce an interactive resize.

Watch: synchronous paint-per-Resized could in theory add paints on a very fast drag (user asked to watch for stutter; none reported). If a future fast-drag stutter appears, throttle to ~one paint/frame while keeping the sync-in-band paint.
Live-testing an example (PINION_SCREENSHOT for in-chat stills + a visible window on :0 for hands-on) is a high-value way to surface real rendering bugs the headless gate never sees.

R1220.decision_summary: R1220 adds the node-graph pin-drop node-creation menu: drag a wire off an output pin, release on empty canvas, and a type-filtered menu of the kinds that output can feed opens at the drop point; picking one creates the node there AND auto-wires it from the source pin to its first compatible input as one undo step. The signature Unreal/Blender blueprint authoring gesture on the codebase's declared value-order #1 advanced DCC widget, with a full AI-first RPC surface + keyboard + a11y menu peer.
changes_bullets: hello-node-editor: the pin-drop node-creation menu (Phase-B DCC axis, the codebase's declared value-order #1 advanced widget). Drag a wire off an OUTPUT pin and release on empty canvas -> a type-filtered menu of the node kinds that output can feed opens at the drop point; pick one and it is created there AND auto-wired from the source pin to its first compatible input, as ONE undo step. Before R1220 a wire released in empty space just cancelled; the graph could only grow from the fixed palette, never contextually from a pin.

Coordinator (NodeGraphExternal): a shared use_pin_create() Signal<Option<PinCreate>> (from_node/from_port/at_graph/at_screen/filter/highlight); methods open_pin_create / set_pin_filter / move_pin_highlight (wrapping) / commit_pin_create_kind (mints node + auto-wire edge in ONE record_edit) / commit_pin_create_highlighted / cancel_pin_create; pure fns pin_create_candidates(from_ty, filter) (input-bearing kinds assignable from the source type, title-substring filter) and first_compatible_input(kind, from_ty).

Live gesture: drag_release, when a fresh connect (not a reconnect) lands on the empty canvas (over.tag == GRAPH_TAG, resolved past the pointer-transparent preview), opens the menu at the drop point projected through cursor_graph_at; a drop on a port still connects, a reconnect dropped in space still cancels.

GUI menu: view_pin_create_menu paints a floating, absolutely-positioned (screen-space, outside the world scroll) search-header + candidate cards (node_graph#create_<idx>), the roving item bordered with the Accent selected-node idiom; clicking a card commits through commit_pin_create_kind; a click outside (or on a node) dismisses, a press on the menu chrome (pin_menu sub) does not.

Keyboard: while the menu is open apply_key_graph is modal — a printable char / Backspace edits the filter, arrows rove, Enter commits the highlighted item, Escape cancels — all funnelled through the same invoke verbs the RPC path uses.

AI-first RPC surface: query pin_create (JSON: from_node/from_port/at{x,y graph}/filter/candidates[]/highlight, Null when closed) + verbs open_pin_create "<node>.<port>" / pin_create_filter / pin_create_highlight / commit_pin_create ("<kind>" or Null=highlighted, returns the new node id) / cancel_pin_create; split into invoke_pin_create to keep invoke under the line budget (the R948 invoke_layout precedent).

a11y: the open menu lowers to an AriaRole::Menu of MenuItems via the menu_item_nodes SSOT, each item byte-matching its painted create_<idx> card, linked as a child of the canvas group so it is reachable; highlighted row = the roving focused item.

Added graph_to_canvas: the exact inverse of canvas_to_graph (canvas = graph*zoom - offset), for placing the RPC-opened menu overlay (distinct from graph_anchor_offset, which solves the same affine for the pan offset).
verification_bullets: 9 new unit tests (r1220_*): type-filtered candidates + wire-target existence; graph_to_canvas round-trips canvas_to_graph; open->commit auto-wires in ONE undo step (undo removes both node and edge); empty-canvas drop opens the menu at the drop point; a port drop connects and a reconnect drop never opens the menu; filter narrows + highlight roves with wrap; cancel + click-away (empty canvas and node) close the menu; the full RPC surface (open/filter/commit-by-name/cancel + schema-declared); a non-candidate commit is rejected and the menu stays open.

RPC verify demo tools/demos/r1220_node_pin_drop_create.py = PASS (~44 assertions, above the R660 30 baseline): boot taxonomy; LIVE drag-to-empty-canvas opens the menu at the drop point with the floating menu + cards painted; RPC type-to-narrow filter; roving highlight with wrap; GUI COMMIT by clicking a card (auto-wire + one atomic undo); RPC commit by kind name; KEYBOARD type-to-filter + Enter commit and Escape cancel (proves the modal keyboard path end-to-end); a non-candidate kind rejected with the menu left open.

Gates: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = exit 0 (-D pedantic; invoke + access_node kept under the 100-line budget by splitting invoke_pin_create + pin_create_access_nodes); cargo test --workspace -j2 = 0 failed, exit 0; cargo test -p hello-node-editor = 153 passed.
carry_forward_bullets: 3b self-grep (below the mechanical-lift threshold of 3, honest carries): parse_create_sub mirrors parse_palette_sub (2 identical strip_prefix.parse sub-parsers; parse_node_sub is a similar-but-NodeId-wrapping third) and the create-menu card render mirrors the palette card render (2 consumers) — a parse_indexed_sub / clickable-card helper waits for a genuine 3rd consumer per abstraction-needs-second-consumer.

Node evaluation stays Phase-C (this is the authoring substrate, not the compute engine). Still-absent blueprint gestures for later depth rounds: comment/group frames, reroute nodes, cut-wire, and wire-connect (begin_drag path) auto-pan (node-drag auto-pan is done).

The RPC-opened menu places the node right-of-source (PIN_CREATE_GAP) rather than at a cursor; the live gesture uses the true drop point. Menu height is a fixed row-count estimate (a flex column clips an over-tall child) — a very tall candidate list would need scroll (not reachable with the 7-kind palette).

Coordinator (NodeGraphExternal): a shared use_pin_create() Signal<Option<PinCreate>> (from_node/from_port/at_graph/at_screen/filter/highlight); methods open_pin_create / set_pin_filter / move_pin_highlight (wrapping) / commit_pin_create_kind (mints node + auto-wire edge in ONE record_edit) / commit_pin_create_highlighted / cancel_pin_create; pure fns pin_create_candidates(from_ty, filter) (input-bearing kinds assignable from the source type, title-substring filter) and first_compatible_input(kind, from_ty).

Live gesture: drag_release, when a fresh connect (not a reconnect) lands on the empty canvas (over.tag == GRAPH_TAG, resolved past the pointer-transparent preview), opens the menu at the drop point projected through cursor_graph_at; a drop on a port still connects, a reconnect dropped in space still cancels.

GUI menu: view_pin_create_menu paints a floating, absolutely-positioned (screen-space, outside the world scroll) search-header + candidate cards (node_graph#create_<idx>), the roving item bordered with the Accent selected-node idiom; clicking a card commits through commit_pin_create_kind; a click outside (or on a node) dismisses, a press on the menu chrome (pin_menu sub) does not.

Keyboard: while the menu is open apply_key_graph is modal — a printable char / Backspace edits the filter, arrows rove, Enter commits the highlighted item, Escape cancels — all funnelled through the same invoke verbs the RPC path uses.

AI-first RPC surface: query pin_create (JSON: from_node/from_port/at{x,y graph}/filter/candidates[]/highlight, Null when closed) + verbs open_pin_create "<node>.<port>" / pin_create_filter / pin_create_highlight / commit_pin_create ("<kind>" or Null=highlighted, returns the new node id) / cancel_pin_create; split into invoke_pin_create to keep invoke under the line budget (the R948 invoke_layout precedent).

a11y: the open menu lowers to an AriaRole::Menu of MenuItems via the menu_item_nodes SSOT, each item byte-matching its painted create_<idx> card, linked as a child of the canvas group so it is reachable; highlighted row = the roving focused item.

Added graph_to_canvas: the exact inverse of canvas_to_graph (canvas = graph*zoom - offset), for placing the RPC-opened menu overlay (distinct from graph_anchor_offset, which solves the same affine for the pan offset).
publishable_verification_bullets: 9 new unit tests (r1220_*): type-filtered candidates + wire-target existence; graph_to_canvas round-trips canvas_to_graph; open->commit auto-wires in ONE undo step (undo removes both node and edge); empty-canvas drop opens the menu at the drop point; a port drop connects and a reconnect drop never opens the menu; filter narrows + highlight roves with wrap; cancel + click-away (empty canvas and node) close the menu; the full RPC surface (open/filter/commit-by-name/cancel + schema-declared); a non-candidate commit is rejected and the menu stays open.

RPC verify demo tools/demos/r1220_node_pin_drop_create.py = PASS (~44 assertions, above the R660 30 baseline): boot taxonomy; LIVE drag-to-empty-canvas opens the menu at the drop point with the floating menu + cards painted; RPC type-to-narrow filter; roving highlight with wrap; GUI COMMIT by clicking a card (auto-wire + one atomic undo); RPC commit by kind name; KEYBOARD type-to-filter + Enter commit and Escape cancel (proves the modal keyboard path end-to-end); a non-candidate kind rejected with the menu left open.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: 3b self-grep (below the mechanical-lift threshold of 3, honest carries): parse_create_sub mirrors parse_palette_sub (2 identical strip_prefix.parse sub-parsers; parse_node_sub is a similar-but-NodeId-wrapping third) and the create-menu card render mirrors the palette card render (2 consumers) — a parse_indexed_sub / clickable-card helper waits for a genuine 3rd consumer per abstraction-needs-second-consumer.

Node evaluation stays Phase-C (this is the authoring substrate, not the compute engine). Still-absent blueprint gestures for later depth rounds: comment/group frames, reroute nodes, cut-wire, and wire-connect (begin_drag path) auto-pan (node-drag auto-pan is done).

R1221.decision_summary: R1221 completes the multi-object inspector's documented GUI follow-up: the Details value cells are now inline-editable and write across the ENTIRE selection. A Bool cell click toggles the property (resolving a mixed Bool to uniform); an Int/Float cell gets +/- steppers that shift each selected object relatively (mix-preserving). GUI gestures + the toggle_property/step_property verbs funnel through the same write set_property/intervene value.<i> drives. The property-grid/inspector value-order gap the R1220 audit ranked #1.
changes_bullets: hello-inspector: the multi-object Details panel's inline EDIT gestures (Phase-B DCC axis, the property-grid/inspector value-order gap the R1220 audit ranked #1). R922 built the multi-object model (common-property derivation + "Multiple Values" mixed state + write-all edit) but edited only over RPC (intervene value.<i>); R1221 makes the value cells interactive and write across the ENTIRE selection.

Bool value cell = a click target (inspector#toggle<i>) that flips the property across all selected, RESOLVING a mixed Bool to a single uniform state (representative flipped, written to all via the existing set_property funnel).

Int/Float value cell = a [-] value [+] SPINBOX (inspector#dec<i>/inc<i>) that shifts each selected object RELATIVELY (new step_property: per-object value += dir, or dir*FLOAT_STEP for Float), so a mixed numeric stays mixed but moves together (PRESERVES per-object differences, unlike the Bool toggle which resolves to uniform).

AI-first RPC peers: invoke toggle_property <i> (flip a common Bool) + step_property "<i>,<dir>" (step a common numeric); the GUI clicks funnel through the SAME set_property / step_property the verbs use (invoke-funnel). value.<i> / mixed.<i> stay the read surface.

Layout fix: interactive value cells reserve a trailing RESET_GUTTER so a +/toggle click on a MODIFIED row lands on the cell, not the absolutely-positioned reset dot at the row edge (found while writing the demo: click(inc1) on a modified Layer hit inspector#reset1 -> reset-to-default instead of +1); read-only cells (Choice/Color/Text) keep the old layout (a click on them does nothing).

SSOT: 4th consumer (reset + toggle + inc + dec) of the send-key strip_prefix+parse wiring -> lifted prefixed_index(key, prefix); handle_send is now one prefix->action line per gesture (R727/R732 3rd-consumer mandate).

Only the shared actor base (Visible/Layer/Locked = Bool/Int) is ever common across a multi-selection, so Bool toggle + numeric steppers cover every common row; inline delegates for Choice/Color/Text across a selection remain the property-grid's, reusable when a shared such property arises.
verification_bullets: 8 new unit tests (r1221_*): toggle resolves a mixed Bool to uniform across every object (verified per-object via e.objects); step shifts each object relatively (mix preserved, 1/1/2 -> 2/2/3); an agreeing selection stays uniform after a step; the value-cell gestures route through the send wire (toggle<i>/inc<i>/dec<i>); toggle rejects a non-Bool + step rejects a non-numeric + out-of-range is a no-op; parse_step_spec + a malformed/typed-wrong verb arg is Rejected; the verbs are schema-declared; no-selection edits are no-ops.

RPC verify demo tools/demos/r1221_inspector_inline_edit.py = PASS (~35 assertions, above the R660 30 baseline): select_all common base; RPC toggle_property resolves a mixed Bool to uniform (write-all); RPC step_property shifts each relatively (mix preserved); GUI CLICK the painted Bool cell + the +/- steppers (paint->route path); an agreeing selection stays uniform after a step; rejects (non-Bool toggle, non-numeric step, malformed spec) + no-selection no-ops.

Gates: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = exit 0 (-D pedantic); cargo test --workspace -j2 = 0 failed; cargo test -p hello-inspector = 31 passed. The gutter-overlap bug (a real mis-click) was found by driving the actual GUI click over RPC, not by the unit tests (which drive the wire directly) -- an instance of verify-via-real-consumer.
carry_forward_bullets: The inspector has no UndoStack (pre-existing: reset + intervene edits are also non-undoable); the toggle/step gestures match that posture. A shared UndoStack across the multi-object write funnel is a separate axis (the property grid has one).

Per-control AT semantics: the toggle/stepper cells, like the R958 reset dot, are paint+RPC affordances with no per-control button/switch/spinbutton AccessNode -- the row's ListItem announces the value (common_value_label). A switch/spinbutton role per interactive cell is a shared a11y follow-up (reset shares the gap).

step_property multi-object semantic is RELATIVE (each += dir), preserving the mix; an ABSOLUTE "set all to N" (mixed -> uniform) numeric edit needs an inline text field (the property grid's delegate), the next inline-edit slice. Choice/Color inline delegates across a selection likewise wait for a shared such common property (never arises in the sample data).

R1222.decision_summary: R1222 adds cell-range COPY (as TSV) to the shared Table coordinator: Table::selected_tsv serializes the selected cell rectangle row-major (the Excel/Sheets clipboard form), exposed as the cell_selection_tsv query -- the AI-first 'copy the selection' read (an AI copies a range by reading it, no clipboard). hello-cell-select's Ctrl+C writes the same TSV to the platform clipboard (the human copy). Additive on the shared Table (every grid gains it); closes part of the R953 'range copy' deferral.
changes_bullets: pinion-core Table (shared grid coordinator): cell-range COPY as TSV. New Table::selected_tsv() serializes the cell_selection_bounds rectangle row-major (tab columns, newline rows, reading each cell()) -- the Excel/Sheets clipboard form; None when no range is selected. Additive: no behavior change to any existing path, so every grid built on Table gains it and no consumer needs a change.

TableExternal: a selected_tsv() delegate (the established cell_selection_bounds/cell_selection_count delegate pattern) + a "cell_selection_tsv" query arm (Text, or Null when empty) + the schema entry. This is the AI-first "copy the selection" read (§2 #2): an AI copies a range by READING it -- no pixels, no platform clipboard.

hello-cell-select: Ctrl/Cmd+C in apply_key reads cell_selection_tsv and writes it to the platform clipboard via use_app_clipboard (the human copy; the SAME TSV the query returns). Unhandled (falls through) when nothing is selected. New pinion-platform-clipboard dep.
Closes part of the R953 "range copy" deferral (hello-cell-select module doc); the R953 rectangle-selection substrate is reused unchanged.
verification_bullets: pinion-core unit tests (r1222_*): Table::selected_tsv serializes full-grid / single-row / single-column / single-cell rectangles row-major and returns None with no selection / after clear; the cell_selection_tsv query mirrors it over the wire (Text vs Null) and is schema-declared.
hello-cell-select unit test: Ctrl+C with NO selection is unhandled and touches no clipboard (the safe guard).

RPC verify demo tools/demos/r1222_cell_range_copy.py = PASS (~30 assertions): boot Null TSV; single cell; grown 2x2 rectangle (row-major); full row; full column; whole 6x4 grid; a lower-right sub-rectangle whose TSV matches the cell_selection bounds exactly (one source of truth); clear -> Null; re-select after clear. Drives select-cell/extend-cell and reads cell_selection_tsv -- a pure read, no clipboard side-effect.
Gates: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = exit 0; cargo test --workspace -j2 = 0 failed; cargo test -p pinion-core r1222 + -p hello-cell-select = pass.
carry_forward_bullets: HW-gated (not auto-tested): the human Ctrl+C system-clipboard write. Driving it in a test/demo would call arboard on a live display and CLOBBER / race the user's real clipboard (the test-real-clipboard-races-concurrent class), so only the deterministic payload (Table::selected_tsv + the cell_selection_tsv query) is auto-asserted; the final clipboard.copy() platform call is exercised in production, not in CI.

The full "block clipboard" (PASTE + fill-down + clear-range over EDITABLE cells) stays deferred: hello-cell-select is read-only (paste has nowhere to write) and the editable grid (hello-data-grid, 9200 lines) still has a single-cell model. Bringing the cell-range model into the editable grid + block paste/fill is the next, larger slice; R1222 delivers the copy (read) half safely.
selected_tsv lives on the shared Table (the right home -- every cell-range grid wants copy-as-TSV); it reuses cell_selection_bounds + cell() (no new selection state).

R1223.decision_summary: R1223 audit-clearance of the R1220-R1222 session (user cost-no-object textbook/SSOT audit; independent adversarial reviewers per round + own SSOT grep found real smells my post-round self-claims missed). Fixes: the write-all SSOT (set_property/step_property share one mutate_selected funnel + killed a silent-fallback arm; my R1221 3b grep had missed the 3rd inlined copy); the §2 #2 pin_create introspection-twin + modal-keyboard-trap on a deleted source; the modal filter modifier-leak; the Ctrl+C !alt_key chord guard; TSV delimiter sanitization on the shared Table; mixed-Bool resolves to checked (Qt/Unreal). The interactive-inspector keyboard+a11y gap is deferred to R1224 (additive capability, not a regression).
changes_bullets: Audit-clearance for R1220-R1222 (user cost-no-object textbook/SSOT audit; independent adversarial reviewers per round + own SSOT grep). Fixes real smells in EXISTING code; the interactive-inspector keyboard+a11y GAP is deferred to R1224 (additive capability, not a regression).

SSOT (R1221-F2 + own grep, the biggest): hello-inspector set_property (absolute) and step_property (relative) had INLINED the same "iterate selection -> find named prop -> mutate" loop (a 3rd copy after reset); the R1221 3b self-grep missed it (grepped the send-key prefix, not the write scaffold). Lifted one mutate_selected(name, |j,cur| Option<new>) funnel both use; reset_names_to_default stays a peer (restore-per-object-default atomic multi-name is a genuinely different op, not the scaffold). Killed step_property's silent `other => clone()` (reintroduced the R906 no-silent-fallback anti-pattern set_property documents) -> explicit None no-op.

§2 #2 (R1220-#2): pin_create_introspect now gates on source validity (pin_candidates None -> query returns Null), mirroring the paint + a11y menu. Fixes the introspection-twin violation + modal-keyboard-trap when the source node is deleted while the menu is open (open_pin_create -> delete_node left query reporting an open menu the user could not see + swallowed all shortcuts).

R1220-#1: pin_create_key now takes modifiers; a command/Alt chord (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+A) while the menu is open is swallowed as a modal no-op, no longer typed into the type-to-narrow filter (the modal path had dropped the command_key gate the idle path applies).
R1222-#1: hello-cell-select Ctrl+C chord adds !alt_key() (the canonical text_field chord decode) so AltGr+C (Ctrl+Alt on EU layouts) no longer misfires the copy + swallows the character.

R1222-#2/#5: Table::selected_tsv sanitizes embedded tab/newline in a cell to a space (tsv_sanitize) so the TSV block's row/column shape ALWAYS matches the selection rectangle on a general-purpose (free-text) grid; doc corrected (data-ordered, NOT the paint-under-sort — paint suppresses the overlay while sorted).

R1221-F4: a mixed Bool toggle resolves to true (checked) -- the Qt/Unreal indeterminate-checkbox convention, order-INDEPENDENT -- not the pre-R1223 !first_selected (which turned a mostly-on group off depending on object order). A uniform Bool still flips.
R1220-#4: the create-menu ▸ glyph is a named PIN_MENU_ARROW const, not inlined twice (non-ASCII-literal convention).
verification_bullets: New regression tests (each FAILS on the pre-R1223 code): hello-node-editor r1223_menu_command_chord_does_not_leak_into_filter (Ctrl+Z swallowed, filter unchanged; a plain char still filters) + r1223_menu_source_deleted_reads_closed_and_untraps_keyboard (delete source -> query pin_create = Null, Ctrl+A reaches select_all); pinion-core r1223_selected_tsv_sanitizes_embedded_delimiters (tab/newline cell -> space, 2x2 block shape preserved). Updated r1221 toggle test + demo for the mixed->checked convention.

Gates: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = exit 0; cargo test --workspace -j2 = 0 failed; hello-inspector 31 / hello-node-editor 155 / hello-cell-select 16 / pinion-core lib pass. Demos r1220/r1221/r1222 all re-run PASS after the fixes.

Honest record corrections: R1221 decision_summary said gestures "funnel through set_property" -- only toggle did; R1223's mutate_selected lift makes it true for both. R1222 "HW-gated" over-claimed -- the positive Ctrl+C path is CI-testable via InMemoryClipboard fallback; the real constraint is local-:0 clobber (the sanitize/return-logic is now unit-covered regardless).
carry_forward_bullets: DEFERRED to R1224 (real gap, additive capability, feature-sized -- NOT a regression, the cells were read-only pre-R1221): hello-inspector's interactive value cells (toggle/steppers) have NO keyboard path and NO per-control switch/spinbutton AccessNode -- mouse+RPC only. The reset dot (R958) shares the gap. Closing it needs a keyboard edit model the inspector does not yet have + a11y roles. Prioritized as the next slice.

Accepted minor (documented, not fixed): toggle_property rebuilds common() twice (trivial at 3 rows); step_property/set_property's `_ => None` unreachable arm is a safe no-op (not a debug_assert like set's Err -- symmetric-enough).

Future enhancement: Table::selected_tsv sanitizes delimiters (structure-preserving, lossy on delimiter content); full Excel-style TSV quoting (faithful content for a delimiter-bearing grid) is deferred until such a grid exists.
The two frozen changelog entries (R1221/R1222) keep their original text; this R1223 entry is the correction of record for the F5/HW-gated overstatements.

Fixes the introspection-twin violation + modal-keyboard-trap when the source node is deleted while the menu is open (open_pin_create -> delete_node left query reporting an open menu the user could not see + swallowed all shortcuts).

R1220-#1: pin_create_key now takes modifiers; a command/Alt chord (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+A) while the menu is open is swallowed as a modal no-op, no longer typed into the type-to-narrow filter (the modal path had dropped the command_key gate the idle path applies).
R1222-#1: hello-cell-select Ctrl+C chord adds !alt_key() (the canonical text_field chord decode) so AltGr+C (Ctrl+Alt on EU layouts) no longer misfires the copy + swallows the character.

R1222-#2/#5: Table::selected_tsv sanitizes embedded tab/newline in a cell to a space (tsv_sanitize) so the TSV block's row/column shape ALWAYS matches the selection rectangle on a general-purpose (free-text) grid; doc corrected (data-ordered, NOT the paint-under-sort — paint suppresses the overlay while sorted).

R1221-F4: a mixed Bool toggle resolves to true (checked) -- the Qt/Unreal indeterminate-checkbox convention, order-INDEPENDENT -- not the pre-R1223 !first_selected (which turned a mostly-on group off depending on object order). A uniform Bool still flips.
R1220-#4: the create-menu ▸ glyph is a named PIN_MENU_ARROW const, not inlined twice (non-ASCII-literal convention).
publishable_verification_bullets: New regression tests (each FAILS on the pre-R1223 code): hello-node-editor r1223_menu_command_chord_does_not_leak_into_filter (Ctrl+Z swallowed, filter unchanged; a plain char still filters) + r1223_menu_source_deleted_reads_closed_and_untraps_keyboard (delete source -> query pin_create = Null, Ctrl+A reaches select_all); pinion-core r1223_selected_tsv_sanitizes_embedded_delimiters (tab/newline cell -> space, 2x2 block shape preserved). Updated r1221 toggle test + demo for the mixed->checked convention.

Gates: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = exit 0; cargo test --workspace -j2 = 0 failed; hello-inspector 31 / hello-node-editor 155 / hello-cell-select 16 / pinion-core lib pass. Demos r1220/r1221/r1222 all re-run PASS after the fixes.

Honest record corrections: R1221 decision_summary said gestures "funnel through set_property" -- only toggle did; R1223's mutate_selected lift makes it true for both. R1222 "HW-gated" over-claimed -- the positive Ctrl+C path is CI-testable via InMemoryClipboard fallback; the real constraint is local-:0 clobber (the sanitize/return-logic is now unit-covered regardless).
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: DEFERRED to R1224 (real gap, additive capability, feature-sized -- NOT a regression, the cells were read-only pre-R1221): hello-inspector's interactive value cells (toggle/steppers) have NO keyboard path and NO per-control switch/spinbutton AccessNode -- mouse+RPC only. The reset dot (R958) shares the gap. Closing it needs a keyboard edit model the inspector does not yet have + a11y roles. Prioritized as the next slice.

Accepted minor (documented, not fixed): toggle_property rebuilds common() twice (trivial at 3 rows); step_property/set_property's `_ => None` unreachable arm is a safe no-op (not a debug_assert like set's Err -- symmetric-enough).

Future enhancement: Table::selected_tsv sanitizes delimiters (structure-preserving, lossy on delimiter content); full Excel-style TSV quoting (faithful content for a delimiter-bearing grid) is deferred until such a grid exists.
The two frozen changelog entries (R1221/R1222) keep their original text; this R1223 entry is the correction of record for the F5/HW-gated overstatements.

R1256.decision_summary: R1256 = independent-audit-clearance of R1255 (3 adversarial reviewers CONFIRMED 5 defects the self-report missed, 5th self-report-bias confirmation): reuse quantize_unit_byte (drop the 5th channel_u8 copy), expose node.<id>.op (the §2#7 AI-identity read the docstring promised), derive is_reroute from op + from_palette SSOT (kill two drift paths), coerce the default branch symmetrically. set_graph validation + cycle localization carried.
changes_bullets: SSOT: removed channel_u8 (a 5th hand-rolled copy of pinion-core quantize_unit_byte, the R628-lifted clamp-round-cast that concentrates the cast_possible_truncation/sign_loss allow); promoted quantize_unit_byte to pub + generic Into<f64> (zero caller edits, f32 widens losslessly) and reused it.

node.<id>.op (+ detail.op) read via NodeOp::name: the rename-stable compute identity the AI needs to tell same-signature ops apart (Add vs Multiply, Texture vs Color) — closes the §2 #7 hole that contradicted NodeOp's own "an AI enumeration agrees on what a node does" docstring.

is_reroute is now DERIVED from op == NodeOp::Reroute at the single GraphNode::new chokepoint (removed the loose add_reroute assignment that could drift op vs is_reroute); GraphNode::from_palette SSOT constructor routes default_nodes/add_node/commit_pin_create_kind so titles/ports/op cannot drift from PALETTE.
resolve_input coerces the pin-default branch symmetrically with the wired branch, so a mistyped default on a set_graph/loaded graph broadcasts instead of a silent null.

R1258.decision_summary: R1258 set_graph structural validation (trust-boundary hardening, discharges the R1256+R1257-carried gap): graph_invariants_hold validates an injected graph's ids/typed-edges/op-arity/defaults/output_const/single-wire before load_json installs it, so the §2#2 AI-first write path rejects a malformed blob LOUD (unchanged) instead of silently mis-evaluating. A live graph always round-trips (reroutes incl.). Reason-string + cycle-localization carried.
changes_bullets: graph_invariants_hold(nodes, edges): validates an injected/loaded graph upholds every structural invariant the interactive editor maintains — unique node/edge ids, per-node node_invariants_hold (is_reroute==op==Reroute / one typed pin default per input port / output_const present iff source and typed to output 0 / op matches its PALETTE port arity or the reroute 1-in-1-out same-type shape), and edges_invariants_hold (every edge between existing in-range type-assignable ports, at most one wire per input). palette_shape(op) reads the PALETTE SSOT.

load_json gates on graph_invariants_hold + id-counters-ahead-of-every-stored-id before apply_snapshot, so an untrusted set_graph blob (the §2 #2 AI-first WRITE path) that is ill-typed / wrong-arity / duplicate-id / mistyped-default is rejected LOUD (set_graph returns Rejected, graph unchanged) rather than silently mis-evaluated to the wrong value or a permanent null. Discharges the R1256+R1257-carried trust-boundary gap.
A serialized live graph always passes (round-trip is total, reroutes included); a self-loop is allowed (an eval-safe observable cycle, not silently wrong).

R1259.decision_summary: R1259 = session audit-clearance (user-requested 교과서적/SSOT/북극성 review; 3 independent reviewers). Fixed the CONFIRMED defects: doc overclaims (mechanism-shared/non_exhaustive-extensible corrected to single-consumer-prototype reality), a factually-wrong output_const serde doc, the frames-validation gap (load_json now gates frame ids/counter), and dropped the redundant STORED is_reroute field (derived from op). Architectural carries (crate-lift with trait-dispatch, §2#7 debugger completeness, value model) honestly documented, not overclaimed.
changes_bullets: Doc honesty (the core defect a 3-reviewer session audit flagged): corrected the PortType/NodeOp/module-header docstrings that overclaimed "the taxonomy is the consumer's, the mechanism is shared" and #[non_exhaustive] extensibility. Reality documented: the whole eval+validation mechanism is a single-consumer prototype trapped in this example binary (0 external consumers), NodeOp::evaluate is a closed match fused ONTO the taxonomy, #[non_exhaustive] is inert within its own module; the trait/registry-dispatched pinion-node-graph crate is a future redesign, not today's shape.

output_const serde doc corrected: the "no serde default -> fails deserialize -> fresh" claim was factually wrong (an Option<T> is implicitly serde-default-None, it does not error on a missing field). Documented that node_invariants_hold (R1258), not deserialize-failure, is the SSOT enforcing the source/output_const invariant, and that the three post-R1242 fields use three different serde-evolution styles.

Frames validation gap closed (R1258 validated nodes+edges but NOT the frames in the same blob): load_json now checks unique FrameIds + next_frame_id ahead of every stored frame id, so a malformed set_graph frame set no longer installs a duplicate-id / lagging-counter that would collide on the next add_frame.

is_reroute SSOT: dropped the redundant STORED is_reroute: bool field (it was always == op == NodeOp::Reroute, a two-representations-of-one-fact smell) and DERIVED it as a method from op. Backward-compatible: an old blob's now-unknown is_reroute key is ignored on load, op derives the truth. Removed the now-vacuous validator cross-check.

R1260.decision_summary: R1260 §2#7 node-graph DEBUGGER reads: query node.<id>.resolved_input.<port> (the value that actually flows in, coercion visible, null on cycle) + eval.cycle_nodes (localises which nodes are ON a cycle, not just whether one exists). Discharges the audit-flagged debugger-completeness carry; pure AI-introspection, no paint/framework change. The crate-lift is deliberately deferred (2nd-consumer-gated). Lifted the 3rd map_or-null site to cell_or_null.
changes_bullets: query node.<id>.resolved_input.<port> — the value that ACTUALLY resolves into an input port: a wired source's output COERCED to the port type (so the Float->Vector broadcast is visible), else the R899 pin default, null on a cycle upstream. The eval-internal resolve_input value surfaced as a debugger read (+ detail.resolved_input mirror), so debugging "why is this grey" no longer requires the AI to find the edge, read the source, and re-apply the coercion by hand.

query eval.cycle_nodes — the ids of the nodes ON a dependency cycle (not merely downstream), sorted CSV, so a null value points at the exact knot to break. eval.acyclic says WHETHER a cycle exists; this LOCALISES it. A node is on a cycle iff reachable from itself along the input<-source edges (self-loop counts); the seen set excludes downstream-of-cycle nodes.

SSOT (mandatory 3b lift): the value / resolved_input / eval.output reads shared a .map_or(Null, to_introspect) mapping — a 3rd consumer crossed the rule-of-three threshold at R1260, lifted to cell_or_null().
verification_bullets: Discharges the §2#7 debugger-completeness carry the R1256/R1258/R1259 audits flagged (per-input resolved reads + cycle-localization). The crate-lift the R1259 audit named is deliberately NOT done — it is 2nd-consumer-gated (premature-abstraction otherwise); this round is pure AI-introspection reads, no paint, no framework change, no architectural churn.

R1261.decision_summary: R1261 measure-first pro-tool-perf: drop the node-graph paint's O(nodes*edges) node<->edge cross-scans to O((n+e)logn) by precomputing the wired-input map (view_node_cards) and a node-by-id index (view_edges) once per paint. Byte-identical scene output (all tests+demos pass unchanged), asymptotically justified by the large-graph editor use case. Viewport-culling the card build carried (repaint-model-dependent, needs a frame-timing profile).
changes_bullets: view_node_cards precomputes the wired-input port sets ONCE from the edge list (a per-node BTreeMap lookup) instead of rescanning every edge per node — the per-node O(edges) scan was O(nodes*edges) across the paint.

view_edges indexes the nodes by id ONCE (BTreeMap<NodeId,&GraphNode>) so each edge's two endpoint lookups are O(log n), not the linear node_ref scan edge_endpoints runs per call — view_edges was O(edges*nodes). edge_endpoints stays for the non-paint callers where a per-call O(n) is not a per-frame cost.

Net: the node-graph paint's node<->edge cross-references drop from O(nodes*edges) to O((n+e)*log n), the frame-build cost the self-hosted editor needs bounded for large graphs. The scene output is byte-identical (a pure algorithmic refactor).
verification_bullets: Measure-first pro-tool-perf (the lowest-completion buildable Phase-B axis; Model/View is concluded, node crate-lift is 2nd-consumer-gated). Un-blocked, correctness-preserving: an asymptotic O(nodes*edges)->O((n+e)logn) fix justified by the large-graph use case, NOT a speculative micro-opt. Viewport-culling the card BUILD was deliberately NOT done — the ScrollNode already clips off-screen cards at render, so culling is repaint-model-dependent and would need real frame-timing evidence (GPU harness) to justify; carried honestly.

R1263.decision_summary: R1263 PR-47 (sprag-forced consumer seam; reviewed 6/6 code claims against HEAD, then built on user directive). Decouples the RPC transport from stdin/stdout via a winit-free injection seam so an execution-independent, runtime-toggleable RPC endpoint is possible. New pinion-rpc transport.rs: RpcReply (one-shot FnOnce response sink), RpcFrame{request,reply}, trait RpcIngress: Send+Sync -- winit-free so ONE seam serves both GUI and TUI (a raw EventLoopProxy seam is un-implementable for the TUI backend, §2 #6). AppEvent::RpcRequest now carries RpcFrame; AppShell::dispatch_rpc routes the response through frame.reply, and the stdin reader supplies a stdout reply so stdin->stdout is byte-identical. ShellConfig + run_with_config expose an on_rpc_ingress hook; run/run_with_handlers become thin wrappers. New crate pinion-rpc-transport ships a reusable UnixSocketTransport + TransportControl -- runtime on/off falls out of the consumer owning the transport lifetime, with no framework-side toggle (the (A)-over-(B) design proven). TUI migrated to the same RpcFrame seam, collapsing the per-backend stderr hardcode into a per-frame reply. Breaks no §2 invariant (additive seam, not a spec round).
changes_bullets: pinion-rpc: new transport.rs seam -- RpcReply(Box<dyn FnOnce(String)+Send>, manual Debug so AppEvent keeps its derive), RpcFrame{request,reply}, trait RpcIngress: Send+Sync. The dispatch core (dispatch_rpc_scoped -> Option<String>) was already transport-agnostic; the coupling was only the stdin read + stdout/stderr write, now lifted behind this seam.

pinion-shell: AppEvent::RpcRequest(String) -> RpcRequest(RpcFrame); ProxyRpcIngress wraps EventLoopProxy (Send+Sync, no Mutex needed); AppShell::dispatch_rpc consumes the frame and sends the response through frame.reply -- the stdin reader attaches stdout_reply() so the stdin->stdout path is byte-identical. Added ShellConfig{handlers,on_ingress} + run_with_config + ShellConfig::on_rpc_ingress; run/run_with_handlers delegate.

New crate pinion-rpc-transport (deps: pinion-rpc only): UnixSocketTransport::serve(path,ingress) -> TransportControl. Per-connection reader builds RpcFrame(reply -> per-conn writer channel) and submits; a dedicated writer thread serializes responses. TransportControl set_enabled/enable/disable (runtime on/off = refuse-service while bound), path(), shutdown()/Drop unbind + unlink. Non-blocking listener + 50ms accept poll (control-plane, not hot path).

pinion-tui: RPC channel migrated Sender<String> -> Sender<RpcFrame>; stdin reader attaches stderr_reply(); drain routes via frame.reply. The per-backend stderr response wire is no longer hardcoded in the drain -- it is chosen per frame by the reply.
verification_bullets: pinion-rpc-transport: 5 integration tests ZERO-FLAKE x3 runs -- roundtrip; two-connection response correlation (no cross-talk); notification-produces-no-response; disabled endpoint refuses new connections then re-enable serves; drop unbinds the socket path.
Regression 0: pinion-shell dispatch_core 148 + unit 154, pinion-tui rpc_ingress 18 + unit 90, pinion-rpc 886 all pass. Both new doctests (ShellConfig::on_rpc_ingress, transport crate) compile.

Workspace clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello CLEAN (every example + crate). Reviewed first: the R1200-pinned handoff's 6/6 code claims (stdin reader unconditional/private, stdout write in the AppShell wrapper, transport-agnostic core, EventLoopProxy owner-internal, no alt transport) verified against HEAD before building.
carry_forward_bullets: Runnable GUI example mounting the socket (heavy pinion-forge scaffolding) + its lavapipe e2e is the only path not covered by an automated test: the full socket -> ProxyRpcIngress -> winit -> dispatch -> reply -> socket composition (each piece is verified; the winit-forward hop is a 1-line send_event). Consumer-gated, deferred.

TUI socket-mount hook (TuiRpcIngress + TuiConfig) deferred -- no TUI consumer yet, so it would be dead code / violate the 2nd-consumer gate. Note: std::sync::mpsc::Sender is !Sync, so a TuiRpcIngress needs a Mutex wrap.

sprag consumes run_with_config().on_rpc_ingress(|i| UnixSocketTransport::serve(path, i)) + owns the on/off policy (env/signal) in a sprag-native session; the pinion side (this round) is complete. Cross-repo rule: not edited from here.
Viewport card-culling still carried (R1261, needs a frame-timing profile / GPU harness).

R1265.decision_summary: R1265 §5.40 — grouped data-grid flatten O(rows*groups) -> O(rows*log groups): the R1261 precompute-an-index-once perf lesson applied to hello-data-grid. group_of linear-scanned the label table per source row (O(groups)) and group_rows calls it once per row, so grouping by a high-cardinality column made the per-frame flatten quadratic in the row count (the grid's 10k-row target). Precompute a label->id index once (group_index_of) -> O(log groups) per row; dedup group_table via a BTreeSet seen-guard -> O(rows*log groups). Byte-identical scene output (a pure algorithmic refactor, asymptotic-and-strictly-better, so it qualifies without a profiler per the R1261 rule).
changes_bullets: hello-data-grid: group_table dedups through a BTreeSet seen-guard instead of the O(groups) labels.contains scan, so it is O(rows * log groups) with a byte-identical source-order first-appearance label list; this fixes the O(rows * groups) cost at all 7 group_table call sites

hello-data-grid: group_of now reads a label -> id index (new group_index_of, the inverse of group_table) in O(log groups), replacing the O(groups) table.iter().position scan; group_rows calls it once per source row, so the grouped flatten drops from O(rows * groups) to O(rows * log groups) per paint (grouping by a high-cardinality column was quadratic in the row count on the grid's 10k-row target)
hello-data-grid: visible_rows builds the label -> id index ONCE per grouped paint (group_index_of) and hands it to the per-row group_of closure; BTreeMap added to the std::collections import
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace -j2 = 8145 passed / 0 failed (hello-data-grid 127, +2 new r1265_*: the grouped flatten scales to n=300 distinct-key rows with exactly n headers + n data and no drop/dup, and group_of via group_index_of is byte-identical to the old table.iter().position scan for every row including out-of-order repeats and the group-0 fallback). clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello (-D pedantic) + cargo doc --workspace --document-private-items green.

Output-preservation is proven by the untouched suite: ALL r892_* editable-grouping tests + the r845/r846 read-only grouped grids (which share the pinion-core group_rows SSOT, unmodified) pass — a changed group flatten would fail them.

r1265_data_grid_group_scale.py 34 assertions PASS (release binary): grow to 40 distinct-Asset rows via one paste, group by Asset => 40 one-member groups / 80 visible rows / correct header-data interleave across the range / collapse + collapse_all + expand_all track exactly / ungroup returns the flat 40-row view. Regression demos PASS: r892 (editable grouping), r845 / r846 (read-only grouped), r983, r1237 / r1244 (paste auto-grow), r837. validate-workspace T1 orphan=0.
carry_forward_bullets: (1) view still calls group_table twice per grouped frame (once inside visible_rows, once at line 4366 for the header labels) — now 2x O(rows * log groups), a CONSTANT factor, not asymptotic; by the R1261 rule (constant-factor + tradeoff = measure-first) it is left alone. Folding them would change visible_rows' signature to also return the label table; deferred until a profiler shows it matters.

(2) The other 5 group_table sites (group_count via .len(), single-label .get()) each rebuild the whole label table for one lookup — O(rows * log groups) each, but called per-query / per-a11y, not per-frame-per-row, so none is quadratic. A shared per-frame group-index memo (the pattern grid_sort's OrderMemo uses to recompute the order only on a config-key change) is the next step ONLY if a profile shows these per-query rebuilds hurt.

(3) The audit that surfaced this (an independent read-only sweep) found the pinion-core Model/View proxy family already clean (memoized order, BTreeSet selection, windowed a11y) and only this one example-level asymptotic hot-path — so R1265 is a single, bounded, output-preserving win, not a campaign.

R1360.4.decision_summary: R1360.4: build(rect) was a landmine — one body, two placement policies, and auto-height chrome
changes_bullets: build(rect) was CONDITIONALLY correct — it baked rect's origin into every child under an unplaced root, so it only landed right beneath a root at the window origin
Now: one private build_body(size) emits the local body; build(rect) places it with absolute(rect), build_fill(size) with fill_parent(). Same signatures, no landmine, correct under ANY parent
Kills the post-hoc mutation: build_fill used to call build then overwrite the root's layout through an `if let` that silently no-ops if build ever returns another variant (R832 class)
Chrome rows are auto-height: a definite width + auto height routes them through the text measure, so the title wraps and the flex slot absorbs it
verification_bullets: Pixel-identity oracle: hello_chart_r1354.py asserts window-absolute pixels and passes unchanged — build(rect)'s consumers see no difference
r1360_chart_layout_native.py (real scene/resize) + hello-chart-fill's 5 tests + pinion-chart's 48 all green

The r1358 test was rewritten to the new model rather than renumbered: it now pins BOTH contracts (commands local to their path rect; the ROOT carries the placement) and would fail if a child carried rect's origin again
Chrome reflow verified live at 300x260: the title wraps to 2 lines and the slot shrinks to 280x175 — no clip, no overflow
carry_forward_bullets: Two reviewers disagreed here: SSOT called the 2-entry-point split correct composition; architecture called it a frozen dishonest contract. Both were right about different halves — the split is fine, the CONTRACT was the landmine, so the fix is the shared body + placement policies (the architecture reviewer's own MED-1), not a signature change
Size::fill() is still hand-rolled: 11 sites spell out with_width(Percent(100)) across shell/chart/examples. A pinion-core Size::fill() is the lift, deferred as its own round
Legend/tick-label overflow below a tight slot is DOCUMENTED, not clamped — it predates R1360 and the margins normally absorb it, but a docked narrow chart would paint over its neighbour

R1361.decision_summary: R1361: hello-frame-profiler becomes pinion-chart's real forcing consumer — the use_frame_timings seam + a live frame-time chart, which immediately exposed that render_us measures vsync back-pressure
changes_bullets: use_frame_timings: the view-fn read seam for the profiler. The stats live on ShellCore and a pure sync view fn had NO way to reach them, so a frame-time chart was structurally impossible, not merely absent

FrameTimingStats::samples(): the per-frame history. snapshot() folds to min/mean/max and DESTROYS shape — a steady 8ms window and an alternating 1ms/15ms one report identical aggregates; only the series tells them apart

The seam is deliberately NOT a Signal — the one non-reactive member of the use_* family. Signal::set dirties the subscribed owner and the shell bridges dirty->request_redraw; timings differ every frame by construction so the equality-skip can never fire, and publish->dirty->redraw->paint->publish would spin an idle window at 100% CPU. A measurement of painting must not drive painting
FrameTimingsView carries samples + the SAME snapshot scene/frame_timings returns, so HUD and AI client cannot drift on mean/fps/jank; one jank_budget_us_for_window source feeds both

publish_frame_timings is demand-gated (no holder => no work) and DEFAULT_WINDOW-only, inheriting the R1006 rule: the holder is one per-owner slot, so a secondary window would clobber the primary's history

The budget line is conditional on budget_us being Some, drawn as a 2-point Series::with_color — no new chart API, no magic 16.7ms. An unpaced window HAS no deadline, so a hardcoded rule would assert one that does not exist

Window was SizeStrategy::Fixed (the derive default; the binding declared only initial_size) — the SEED's dockable+resizable claim was FALSE. Now OpenResizable, with the chart in a flex_grow slot sized by its siblings
verification_bullets: 3 gates green: cargo test --workspace (222 suites ok, 0 failed) + clippy -D pedantic + cargo doc
r907_frame_profiler.py PASS unchanged — the Toggle stays the manual driver, so nothing declares a startup fps target and r925's section-A unpaced contract is untouched

r1361_view_charts_the_seam_not_a_synthetic_series: two different published histories must yield different painted geometry — a canned series paints identically for both
Chart tracks a FLEX slot, not just a window, closing R1360's declared dock/flex-placement gap: the root is strictly shorter than the window because the chrome takes its share first
r925 baseline re-run under git stash on clean f13e5f6c: also FAILS => the failure is pre-existing, not this round's regression

r925_frame_budget.py fails LOCALLY — pre-existing (verified by stashing to clean main). Same ~1s acquire root cause. Its section B compares a 1_000_000us budget against wgpu's ~1s acquire timeout — the same number — so it is a coin flip (baseline failed E, this run failed B). CI globs every demo under Xvfb and main is green there, so it is environment-shaped; the flaky-at-the-boundary assertion is real regardless
