R1366.8.1.decision_summary: R1366.8.1 audit-clearance §5.22 §5.16 §5.23: the cost-no-object 'textbook?' audit of R1366.3-.8 found SSOT clean and the verdicts correct, but the generated provider_slot_tests! macro is TAUTOLOGICAL (its ptr_eq and its assertion both derive from scope(), so a wrong verdict flips both and still passes — R1366.1's 'passes both readings = 0 discrimination' recurring inside the campaign that learned it), the two per_scope slots had NO real oracle, and the frame_timings demand-gate reached around the type via .key(). This round clears the fixable: ProviderSlot::get() lands (no more .key() reach-around); value-based non-inheritance oracles for viewport_size + frame_timings, PROVEN to discriminate by flipping the verdict to inherited (both FAIL); and the macro doc says plainly it is a wiring-consistency guard, not a verdict discriminator. Un-clearable residue (frozen R1366.7 hash, cache_inherited-pub footgun, north-star hygiene) registered as debt.
changes_bullets: `provider_slot.rs`: `ProviderSlot::get(&owner) -> Option<Rc<V>>` lands — the missing GET-ONLY leg (this owner, no walk, never creates). Completes the API (declare / resolve / resolve_current / get / provide / seed_root). The frame_timings demand-gate now models THROUGH the type instead of reaching around it via `.key()` + raw `Owner::cache_get_by_str`.

`provider_slot.rs` macro doc: an added "What this does NOT verify" section states plainly the generated `provider_slot_tests!` is NOT a verdict discriminator — both the `ptr_eq` outcome and the assertion branch derive from `self.scope` (resolve picks cache_inherited/cache from scope; the match picks assert-same/assert-not-same from scope), so flipping the verdict flips BOTH and it still passes. It catches a broken cache_inherited/cache + a forgotten test, not a WRONG verdict. The real discriminator is the slot's own value-based binding-path test.

`viewport.rs` + `frame_timing.rs`: value-based non-inheritance oracles (`r1366_8_1_a_child_scope_does_not_inherit_...`) for the two `per_scope` slots — seed root with a distinct value (viewport (1920,1080) / a 42000us frame), assert a child scope reads its OWN default (viewport (0,0) / an empty view). These DISCRIMINATE (proven by flipping the verdict, see verification); the 6 inherited slots already had binding-path oracles, so now EVERY migrated slot has a real oracle, not just the tautological macro.

`substrate.rs` publish_frame_timings + `dispatch_core.rs` test: rewired from `FRAME_TIMINGS.key()` + `cache_get_by_str::<FrameTimingsHolder>` to `FRAME_TIMINGS.get(owner)`. The FRAME_TIMINGS static doc's stale "uses .key() directly" prose is corrected to "through ProviderSlot::get" — the exact prose-drift-on-migration the audit flagged, caught by a path-based grep BEFORE shipping.

Registered as debt in [[debt-r1366-audit-findings]] (NOT clearable here): R1366.7's FROZEN changelog cites pre-fmt hash `4736d984` + "fmt clean" while committed is `b5af21b1` (a frozen-ledger SSOT violation the design cannot amend in place); `Owner::cache_inherited`/`cache` stay `pub` until scene_revision + waiter_registry migrate (footgun, tail-cleanup at R1366.9/.10); the frozen R1366.3-.8 changelogs' OVERCLAIM of the macro as a verdict discriminator cannot be amended; and the honest note that the 6-round campaign is substrate hygiene, not Phase B feature progress.
verification_bullets: All four CI gates on the literal `.github/workflows/ci.yml` commands, bracketed by code diff hash `6356fa631dc7daecbbe98aa5e1c34c43`. fmt --check verified clean BEFORE the hash — the R1366.7 fmt-after-hash slip was NOT repeated (the doc-link fix + all edits preceded the hash; nothing edited after).

★DISCRIMINATION PROVEN (the R1366.1 lesson: a test that passes under both the true AND false reading proves nothing — check it discriminates): temporarily flipped `VIEWPORT_SIZE` and `FRAME_TIMINGS` from `per_scope` to `inherited` and ran ONLY the new oracle each time — both FAILED ("a child scope inherited the primary's viewport" / "...the root's frame history"). Reverted both to `per_scope` (grep-confirmed: both back to `ProviderSlot::per_scope`, no sed corruption). The tautological generated macro, by contrast, passes under BOTH verdicts — which is exactly why these value-based oracles were needed.

`cargo test --workspace` — 0 failed. New: `r1366_8_1_a_child_scope_does_not_inherit_the_primary_viewport`, `r1366_8_1_a_child_scope_does_not_inherit_the_roots_frame_timings`. The ProviderSlot unit tests + the frame_timings demand-gate / no-dirty / secondary-window-no-clobber tests all pass through the new `get()`.
`cargo build --workspace --all-targets` — Finished (examples + integration tests; caught nothing new, all `.key()`/`cache_get_by_str` consumers rewired to `get()`).
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` — clean.

`cargo doc --workspace --document-private-items --no-deps --features pinion-runtime/vello` — clean AFTER fixing a bare `[resolve]` intra-doc link in the crate-root macro doc (`resolve` is not in scope at the `#[macro_export]` site) — a real find the `-D warnings` doc gate caught; made prose.

Audit-clearance round (visible-deliverable exemption): no new demo; the deliverable is the discriminating per_scope oracles + the completed get-only API. The independent 3-reviewer could not run (2 agents died on ECONNRESET infra), so this was a deliberate self-audit applying correctness/SSOT/structure lenses adversarially, incl. flipping verdicts to prove discrimination.
carry_forward_bullets: The un-clearable audit residue stays registered in [[debt-r1366-audit-findings]]: R1366.7's frozen changelog (pre-fmt hash `4736d984` + false "fmt clean"); the frozen R1366.3-.8 changelogs' overclaim of the macro as a verdict discriminator; the `Owner::cache_inherited`/`cache`-stay-`pub` footgun (closes when the last two slots migrate); and the north-star note (6-round campaign = substrate hygiene, not Phase B feature progress).

The generated `provider_slot_tests!` macro STAYS (now honestly documented): it is a wiring-consistency guard (verifies resolve behaves per the declared scope) + a non-forgettable-existence device, NOT a verdict discriminator. It is not removed because it still guards a broken cache_inherited/cache and a forgotten test; the value-based binding-path oracle is what discriminates a wrong verdict.

`ProviderSlot::get()` now has ONE consumer (frame_timings publish). If a 2nd get-only demand-gate never appears it is still justified as the API's completeness leg (declare/resolve/get/provide/seed_root), not speculation — it removed a live abstraction leak.

NEXT = R1366.9 / R1366.10 = `scene_revision` / `waiter_registry` (the last two; pinion-shell/rpc-homed bare Arcs, seed_root shape). On completion: `cache_inherited` -> `pub(crate)`, the owner.rs markdown slot table dies wholesale, and the cache/cache_inherited footgun closes — the campaign ends. THEN return to Phase B feature work (DCC widgets / Model-View at scale); do not extend the plumbing campaign indefinitely.
Method: when infra allows, re-run the independent read-only 3-reviewer on THIS clearance too (the 2 that would have reviewed R1366.3-.8 died on ECONNRESET).

`resolve_scene_revision` / `resolve_waiter_registry` survive as thin `Arc::clone(&SLOT.resolve(owner))` wrappers, NOT cosmetic delegates: `resolve` returns the cache's `Rc<Arc<V>>` and callers need the inner `Arc<V>` — the boot wake observer moves it into a `Send` closure, and the outer `Rc` is `!Send`. `use_scene_revision` (the `pub` producer hook) unchanged. Module doc rewritten for the fully-migrated state, with no `Owner::cache_inherited` intra-doc link (prose "the slot's `Inherited` parent walk"), so R1366.10's `pub(crate)` demotion never has to touch this file.

R1371.decision_summary: R1371 §5.16: consume the sce statechart markers (landed R1370) to CLEAR SCE-002. Two new proc-macro derives in pinion-derive — WidgetStateName + WidgetEventName (mirror WidgetTag) — reconstruct the a11y/RPC-introspect name mappings from the enum's own tokens plus the sce structural markers: WidgetStateName::from_name_or_default falls through to Self::default() (the #[default]-marked SCXML initial state), WidgetEventName::from_name admits only variants in the sce-emitted EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS assoc const (rejecting internal <raise> events = the RPC forgeability boundary). build.rs injects them via compile_scxml_with_derives (state_extras += pinion_derive::WidgetStateName, event_extras += pinion_derive::WidgetEventName); pinion-core normal-deps pinion-derive (dev-dep cycle only) + adds extern crate self as pinion_core so the derive-emitted ::pinion_core::Widget*Name resolves internally. Retires the per-widget macro_rules re-enumeration: 22 invocation blocks across 11 widgets + the 2 macro_rules defs deleted (net -96 LOC). Behavior-preserving (verified per widget: #[default]==old default, EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS==old external set). Full RFC loop (handoff -> sce 9ec9ad906 -> R1370 bump -> this) closes SCE-002.
changes_bullets: `pinion-derive/src/lib.rs` (+136): two new derives mirroring `WidgetTag` — `#[proc_macro_derive(WidgetStateName)]` + `#[proc_macro_derive(WidgetEventName)]` (unit-variant guard, `split_for_impl`, emit absolute `::pinion_core::` trait paths). `WidgetStateName::from_name_or_default` falls through to `Self::default()`; `WidgetEventName::from_name` parses to a candidate then admits it only if `Self::EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS.contains(&candidate)`.

`pinion-core/Cargo.toml`: add `pinion-derive` as a normal `[dependencies]` (pinion-derive dev-deps pinion-core, so no build cycle — the serde/serde_derive shape). `build.rs`: inject `pinion_derive::WidgetStateName` into `state_extras` + `pinion_derive::WidgetEventName` into `event_extras` of `compile_scxml_with_derives`. `lib.rs`: add `extern crate self as pinion_core;` so the derive-emitted `::pinion_core::Widget*Name` path resolves INSIDE pinion-core (the generated enums compile here).

Deleted: the two `#[macro_export] macro_rules!` (`widget_state_name!`, `widget_event_name!`) in `widget_core.rs` (the traits stay); 22 macro-invocation blocks across the 11 widgets (button/toggle/checkbox/disclosure/radio/listbox_item/slider/color_area/scrollbar/text_field/dock_panel); the dangling doc-link references in `input.rs` + `examples/figma-button-m3`. Net -96 LOC.
verification_bullets: Injection confirmed on the actual generated code: `{widget}_sm.rs` enums now carry `#[derive(.., pinion_derive::WidgetStateName)]` / `#[derive(.., pinion_derive::WidgetEventName)]`.

`cargo build --workspace` green; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` clean (independent re-run); `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `cargo test --workspace -j2 --features pinion-runtime/vello` = 8676 passed / 0 failed (implementing agent), independently re-confirmed: `pinion-core` 2617 pass / 0 fail + every `pinion-derive` test binary 0-fail.

Behavior-preservation checked per widget: the `#[default]` variant == the old hand `default =` (all `Idle` except `dock_panel = Docked`); `EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS` == the old `external = [..]` set (pointer / keyboard / enable-disable; `*Activate` raises + `Null` excluded). `as_name` is total over all variants either way. R1372.decision_summary: R1372 §5.38: the editable data grid gets cell-range COPY, closing the copy/paste asymmetry R1237 left (a block PASTE existed, no copy). A rectangular cell selection — the spreadsheet / Qt SelectItems model the Table widget got in R952 — over the bespoke DataGridExternal: a SOURCE-keyed cell_anchor Signal (the cursor's peer), the selected rectangle derived as the bbox of the anchor's + cursor's CURRENT visible positions, so it is always one contiguous, paintable screen block under any sort / filter / group (an off-view endpoint collapses to the lone cursor) — unlike the Table widget's data-indexed rectangle that scatters under a sort. copy serializes the selection to the SAME TSV a paste consumes, so a copy round-trips through a paste. The wire mirrors the cross-grid cell-selection vocabulary the Table widget / hello-cell-select speak (invoke select-cell / extend-cell / clear-cell-selection / copy; query cell_selection / cell_selection_count / cell_selection_tsv), so an AI drives copy identically on every grid. Keyboard: Shift+arrow / Home / End extend, a plain nav key collapses, Escape clears, Ctrl/Cmd+C copies to the platform clipboard through the same copy funnel. Two substrate reuses at the 2nd consumer: the pure TSV rectangle codec Table::selected_tsv had is lifted to pinion_core::widgets::table::rows_to_tsv (Table refactored to call it, R1222/R1223 tests the regression guard); and the R952 table.rs parse_row_col wire-arg parser is made pub + reused rather than re-copied. The R952 GridCell.selected a11y axis (left None here) now carries per-cell aria-selected in the flat grid.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/table.rs`: new `pub fn rows_to_tsv(&[Vec<String>]) -> String` — the shared clipboard-copy TSV codec (row-major, tab columns, newline rows, each cell `tsv_sanitize`d), lifting the pure core of `Table::selected_tsv` at its 2nd consumer (`Table::selected_tsv` refactored to build its data-ordered rectangle then call it — R1222/R1223 tests unchanged = the refactor's regression guard). `parse_row_col` (the R952 `select-cell`/`extend-cell` wire-arg parser) made `pub` so the bespoke grid reuses the one SSOT instead of a divergent copy. +1 `rows_to_tsv` codec unit test.

`examples/hello-data-grid/src/main.rs`: cell-range selection + copy on the bespoke `DataGridExternal`. `use_cell_anchor` Signal + `cell_anchor` field (the cursor's SOURCE-keyed peer); free fn `cell_selection_bounds(visible, anchor, cursor_row, cursor_col)` (projects the SOURCE endpoints to a normalized VISIBLE-position rectangle; off-view endpoint -> None = collapse); coordinator `select_cell`/`extend_cell`/`clear_cell_selection`/`cell_selection`/`cell_selection_count`/`selected_tsv`/`copy_tsv`/`query_cell_selection`. RPC: invoke `select-cell`/`extend-cell`/`clear-cell-selection`/`copy` + query `cell_selection`/`cell_selection_count`/`cell_selection_tsv` + 3 schema fields (the cross-grid cell-selection wire the Table widget / hello-cell-select speak). Keyboard: `maintain_cell_selection` (Shift+arrow/Home/End extend, plain nav collapse, Escape clear) + `copy_selection_to_clipboard` (Ctrl/Cmd+C via the `copy` funnel -> `use_app_clipboard`), both split out for the line ceiling. Paint: per-cell `cell_fill` (focus highlight > Accent selection wash > transparent); `view_cell` takes the precomputed `fill` (arg count -1) and the view threads the visible-position rectangle -> per-row col range. a11y: the R952 `GridCell.selected` (left `None` here) now carries per-cell `aria-selected` in the flat grid. `pinion-platform-clipboard` dep + `use_app_clipboard` import. 8 unit tests (bounds projection, parse guard, fill precedence, RPC select/extend/clear/reads, copy range-then-lone-cell, keyboard extend/collapse/escape, a11y aria-selected, scene-data wash guard).

`tools/demos/r1372_data_grid_copy.py`: 35-assertion RPC demo — select/extend -> the rectangle + count + TSV; `copy` == `cell_selection_tsv` and the lone-cell fallback; a copy->paste ROUND-TRIP via the same TSV string; out-of-range/malformed guards; the selection + copy following an active sort (VISIBLE order, not source).
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green. `hello-data-grid` = 135 (127 prior + 8 R1372); `pinion-core` table tests green incl. the new `rows_to_tsv` codec test and the R1222/R1223 `selected_tsv` regression (the lift's guard).

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`: clean (`-D pedantic`); the two dispatch fns kept under the 100-line ceiling by the helper splits (`query_cell_selection`, `maintain_cell_selection`, `copy_selection_to_clipboard`) and `view_cell` under the 7-arg ceiling by taking the precomputed `fill`.

`tools/demos/r1372_data_grid_copy.py`: PASS (35 assertion-class; ZERO-FLAKE; `PINION_HIDDEN_WINDOW`, no window flicker). Covers select/extend/copy, copy==tsv + lone-cell, the copy->paste round-trip, guards, and visible-order-under-sort.

Selection WASH guarded at the scene-data level (§2 #7), not a GPU screenshot: a flat cell background is fully determined by `view` threading selection -> `cell_fill`, so the test asserts the painted cell container's fill (selected-non-focused -> non-transparent wash, unselected -> transparent) — deterministic + CI-safe, no pixels.

3b self-grep: the `rows_to_tsv` lift leaves 0 TSV-rectangle-join duplicates outside table.rs; `parse_row_col` is now reused from table.rs (was a 2nd independent copy of the same wire-arg parser = a divergence risk removed); `cell_selection_bounds`/`selected_tsv` legitimately DIVERGE from the Table widget's (Table = data-indexed coords, this bespoke grid = visible-position projection, so its rectangle is always contiguous/paintable and needs no overlay-omit-under-sort); `use_app_clipboard` is an established substrate (10th consumer).
`mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace`: T1 orphan total=0 (new +0), style reject=0 (baseline unchanged).
carry_forward_bullets: Grouped-mode a11y `aria-selected` is a bounded substrate follow-up: the FLAT grid now emits per-cell `aria-selected`, but the grouped treegrid goes through `pinion_a11y::grouped_grid_access_nodes` whose `GroupedGridSelection` is ROW-level only (`Display` / `Single`) — no cell-range variant. The selection WASH already paints in grouped mode (source-row membership, mode-independent); only the grouped AT `aria-selected` is omitted. Wiring it = a new `GroupedGridSelection` cell-range variant on the a11y crate (in-repo substrate extension), deferred to keep this round scoped.

OS-clipboard READ (Ctrl+V pulling from another app) stays the R1237 deferral: `paste` takes its TSV as an RPC arg (AI-first primary); a Ctrl+V that reads the OS clipboard would funnel to `paste` (HW-gated). Copy WRITES the OS clipboard (`use_app_clipboard`), so the human-side copy is complete; the deterministic AI peer is `query cell_selection_tsv` / `invoke copy`.

Copy is structure-preserving, not content-faithful: an embedded tab/newline in a Text cell becomes a space (`tsv_sanitize`, the R1223 tradeoff so the block shape always matches the rectangle). Full Excel-style quoting is a later enhancement only if a delimiter-bearing grid needs it.

select-cell/extend-cell take SOURCE coords (matching `focused_row` + Table's data-coord contract); `cell_selection` READS visible-position bounds (the rectangle is defined over the view, like `source_at.<pos>`). An AI extending by visual position resolves `source_at.<pos>` first — the grid's existing source/visible split (paste is visible-ordered, `value.<r>.<c>` is source), documented on both wires.

Next: Phase B feature return — more DCC depth (the inspector's RPC-only edit gap = inline delegates; node-eval GUI), or Model-View slice ⑥ (text-reflow virtualization) if a real consumer appears. Standing debts unchanged: (R1364) quit-veto forcing consumer; demo-sweep-push gating.

R1372.1.decision_summary: R1372.1 §5.40: clear the R1372 grouped-mode a11y carry — the flat editable grid announced per-cell aria-selected but the grouped treegrid did not, because pinion_a11y::grouped_grid_access_nodes has only a ROW-level selection axis (GroupedGridSelection = Display | Single, no cell-range variant). Rather than generalize the shared a11y substrate for this one consumer (premature — there is no 2nd grouped cell-select consumer), the CONSUMER stamps the cell-range aria-selected onto the emitted gridcells after the fact, exactly the emit_reset_affordances augmentation pattern used two lines above it. Both grid modes now announce the cell selection to AT identically. In-repo debt cleared inline the round it surfaced, not carried (only external / vendor deps justify a carry).
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-data-grid/src/main.rs`: new `stamp_cell_selection(&mut [AccessNode], visible_sources, focus)` — post-stamps per-cell `aria-selected` onto the grouped treegrid's emitted gridcells from the `cell_selection_bounds` membership over the grouped visible DATA order (`Some(in_range)` when a range is active, `None` = omit otherwise, matching the flat grid's `GridCell.selected` semantics). Called in the grouped a11y branch right after `emit_reset_affordances` — the consumer augments the substrate's output rather than change it. +1 test: a grouped treegrid's gridcells carry `aria-selected` for a range that spans a group boundary.
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green; `hello-data-grid` = 136 (135 from R1372 + 1 grouped-a11y test).

carry_forward_bullets: Bool/Choice copy->paste round-trip is a PASTE-domain follow-up, not a copy gap: copy exports every column's display faithfully; paste-back is text/int/float/colour only because paste's `CellKind::parse` is the inline-editor-commit path (Bool toggles / Choice popup-selects, both correctly non-text there) AND `CellKind::Choice` is a unit kind carrying no option list (options live on the value, so paste cannot map a label -> index). True symmetry needs a deserialize-from-display path + a kind-with-options decision — a paste round, deferred (documented + tested as export-only).

Framework gap (upstream-ish): `pinion_core::external::SchemaField` has no prose-description slot, so a per-field caveat (e.g. hello-data-grid `cell_selection` reads VISIBLE positions while `select-cell` writes SOURCE) cannot live in the machine-readable `$schema` an AI introspects — it lives only in the query doc. An RFC to add a `description` to `SchemaField` would let the coordinate-space (and every wire caveat) be self-describing. Not fixed here (touches the introspect substrate + every consumer's schema).

The a11y post-stamp O(rows*cols*nodes) scan (`stamp_cell_selection`, mirroring `emit_reset_affordances`) is a pre-existing family pattern, not a regression; a `tag -> &mut node` map would make both O(nodes + cells) — a follow-up for the whole a11y-augment family if a large grouped grid needs it.

R1373.decision_summary: R1373 §5.38 §5.40 §5.27: the multi-object inspector Details panel gains the DCC numeric drag-scrub — press-and-drag a common Int/Float row to shift it across the whole selection relative to each object's own value (mix-preserving), riding the already-lifted DragCalibration substrate (R935 caller-owns application; not re-lifted). Name-keyed target (stable property name + per-object base snapshot, re-resolved by name not the selection-derived row index) closes the R1372.2-class stale-index hazard a mid-drag RPC select would trip; the pre-commit 3-reviewer adversarial audit caught the draft's FALSE 'stable under the capture lock' invariant. Plus: a leaked-arm defense (a non-scrub press abandons an armed scrub, killing the RPC-unpaired-PointerDown phantom-scrub path), DETAIL_TAG SSOT reuse (no redundant tag twin), and intervene honesty (scrubbing + the query-only peers return ReadOnly not UnknownPath via read_only_or_unknown). Hand-written impl External (the macro cannot express pointer capture); capture is per-External so an object-row press-drag now selects the press row (disclosed + tested).
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-inspector/src/main.rs`: the multi-object Details panel gains the iconic DCC **numeric drag-scrub** — press-and-drag a common `Int` / `Float` row to shift it across the WHOLE selection RELATIVE to each object's own value (mix-preserving; the continuous peer of the R1221 steppers). Rides the already-lifted `DragCalibration<CellKind>` substrate (R935: the per-widget scrub glue is divergent, the substrate is not re-lifted); the multi-object base snapshot is `ScrubTarget { name, bases }`, the new dimension the single-source property-grid / data-grid scrubs lack.

**Name-keyed target (R1372.2-class robustness)**: the scrub snapshots the STABLE property NAME + per-object bases at its first move and re-resolves later moves by name, NEVER the selection-derived row index — a mid-drag RPC `select` can reorder `common_properties` (the capture lock is pointer-routing only, so RPC is reachable between moves), and re-deriving through a stale index is the R1372.2 hazard. The property-grid stable-`ValueRef` discipline. (Caught by the pre-commit correctness reviewer: my draft re-derived through `drag.row` under a FALSE "stable under the capture lock" comment.)

**Leaked-arm defense**: a pointer press/release on any NON-scrub affordance abandons an armed scrub, defending the desync where an RPC `send "typein<i>:PointerDown"` with no paired release leaks `scrub_armed` and a later real press would seed a PHANTOM scrub off it (the router dispatches the send-wire `PointerDown` before it forwards the initial capture move, so the clear wins).

**Capture**: the `impl External` is hand-written (the `query_proxy_external_impl!` config-holder macro cannot express `wants_pointer_capture` / `capture_normalize` / `pointer_move` — the property-grid / data-grid precedent). `capture_normalize` names `DETAIL_TAG` (the Details panel, a fixed `DETAIL_PANEL_W`-wide basis). Capture is per-External so it also spans the object listbox: an object-row press-drag-release now selects the PRESS row (was the release-hover row) — disclosed on `wants_pointer_capture` + tested.

**SSOT**: reuse the pre-existing `DETAIL_TAG` (the a11y group tag) for the view + `capture_normalize` instead of a redundant `DETAIL_PANEL_TAG` twin (moved `DETAIL_TAG` up to the tag-const block; one tag = view + a11y node + scrub basis cannot drift). The `SCRUB_FLOAT_PER_PX` / `SCRUB_INT_PX_PER_STEP` sensitivities are kept per-example (NOT lifted despite the 3rd identical copy): the `DragCalibration` contract ratifies value application as caller-owned (R935), so a DCC panel is free to tune its own feel — the docstring's over-claim of cross-widget uniformity is corrected to "convention, not a lifted SSOT".

**Honesty**: `intervene scrubbing` (and the pre-existing query-only peers `editing` / `edit_text` / `prop_cursor` / `any_modified` + the invoke verbs) now returns `ReadOnly` via the `read_only_or_unknown` SSOT, not `UnknownPath` — an agent that can `query` a field must not be told it does not exist (§2 #7).

`tools/demos/r1373_inspector_scrub.py`: >=34-assertion RPC demo driving scrub via the deterministic `scene/drag` RPC (single float/int + multi-object mix-preserving verified per object + isolation + click-not-scrub + non-numeric-drag-toggles + double-click-still-edits).

+14 unit tests (multi-object mix-preserve, absolute-from-base, int whole-unit steps, dead zone, un-armed no-op, arms-only-numeric, scrubbing query/schema, send-wire+pointer_move, leaked-arm abandonment, intervene-ReadOnly, object-row press-drag selects press row).
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green, 8705 tests, 0 failed. `hello-inspector` = 78 (67 prior + 11 R1373).
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`: clean (`-D pedantic`).
`cargo fmt --all --check`: clean. `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean.
`tools/demos/r1373_inspector_scrub.py`: PASS (~34 assertions; ZERO-FLAKE, PINION_HIDDEN_WINDOW). The multi-object case F re-selects each object and asserts Layer 1+k / 1+k / 2+k (mix preserved).

**Capture regression gate**: all 9 pre-existing inspector demos (r909/r910/r922/r958/r1221/r1224/r1225/r1249/r1251) PASS — enabling `wants_pointer_capture` did not regress any click path (select / stepper / toggle / cycle / type-in / colour / keyboard / a11y / reset).

**Independent 3-reviewer adversarial audit ran BEFORE commit** (correctness / SSOT-DRY / hacks-smells lenses, read-only). It found no reachable MUST-FIX but one R1372.2-class latent hazard (a stale `drag.row` re-derived after a mid-drag selection change under a FALSE invariant comment) + SSOT/honesty should-fixes; every finding is remediated in this same round (name-keyed target, leaked-arm defense, `DETAIL_TAG` reuse, `intervene` ReadOnly, capture disclosure+test, docstring honesty, tightened test tolerance).
carry_forward_bullets: Choice dropdown popup + Colour swatch popup delegates remain the documented GUI follow-up (both a floating overlay — NOT a lifted substrate, unlike `DragCalibration` — so a popup round may itself surface a popup-infra lift question; deferred honestly, those kinds keep their click-cycle / hex type-in + `intervene value.<i>`).

The scrub sensitivities are 3 identical copies across property-grid / data-grid / inspector, deliberately NOT lifted (the `DragCalibration` contract ratifies caller-owned value application). If a future round wants enforced uniformity, that is a deliberate design-change (a shared `pinion_core::input` default next to `DRAG_CLICK_THRESHOLD_PX`), not a bundled cleanup.

A capture-scrub `impl External` variant macro could collapse the truly-identical skeleton + `pointer_move`, but the case is weak (backends diverge, data-grid carries an extra `begin_drag`) and R935 counsels against chasing it — a NIT future carry, not a defect.

R1374.decision_summary: R1374 §5.16 §5.7 §5.38: pinion-chart gains a categorical BarChart (vertical bars, value y-axis, per-bar colour, build/build_fill layout-native), forced by a frame-time DISTRIBUTION histogram in hello-frame-profiler (bins the rolling window's total_us; over-budget bins in the jank colour = the R925 classification made visual, the distribution the R1361 timeline cannot show). To share code the leaf draw primitives + plot_rect margin math were lifted pub(crate) out of line.rs into draw.rs, step_of into ticks::tick_step, and ChartStyle/Margin into a neutral style.rs (byte-identical lifts, no behaviour change). A pre-commit 3-reviewer adversarial audit found no reachable correctness MUST-FIX but one honesty MUST-FIX (lib.rs listed 'bar' as Not-yet while shipping it) + SHOULD-FIXes (a gate-invisible tick_decimals doc-comment mangling from the tick_step insert, the plot_rect SSOT lift, a y-label tag alignment ylabel->label.y, the ChartStyle home move, a dead-palette fix color(0)->color(i), a pinned-domain bar-overflow clamp, a missing wire colour test, a min-window-height fix); all remediated in-round before commit.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/bar.rs` (NEW): a categorical `BarChart` — vertical bars, a value y-axis (nice ticks + gridlines + labels), per-category x labels, per-bar colour override, tagged `chart.bar.{i}` / `chart.label.y.{k}` / `chart.axis.*` for §2 #7. `build` (pinned) + `build_fill` (layout-native) mirror `LineChart`. It shares the crate's scale / ticks / palette / draw core rather than re-deriving it (the "same core" the crate anticipated for a 2nd chart type).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/draw.rs` (NEW): the leaf retained-`Scene` draw primitives (`box_node` / `stroke_path` / `area_path` / `label_node` / `absolute` / `fill_parent` / `bbox_of` / `to_f32` / `to_u32`) + the `plot_rect(rect, margin)` margin→pixel geometry, lifted `pub(crate)` out of `line.rs` so `line` + `bar` share ONE definition (a bar IS a `box_node`, an axis a `stroke_path`). Byte-identical lift, no behaviour change (audit-verified line-for-line).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/style.rs` (NEW): `ChartStyle` + `Margin` relocated out of `line.rs` — at two chart types, `crate::line::ChartStyle` read as "bar borrows line's style"; a neutral home fixes the SSOT. `ticks::tick_step` = the lifted `line::step_of` (de-duped for both builders).

`examples/hello-frame-profiler/src/main.rs`: a frame-time **distribution histogram** panel below the R1361 timeline — `histogram_bars` bins the rolling window's `total_us` into `HIST_BINS` ms buckets (one `BarChart`), over-budget bins in the error (jank) colour = the R925 over-budget classification made visual (the timeline's horizontal budget line re-encoded as a colour boundary). The distribution answers "how OFTEN does each duration band happen", which the time-series cannot. Its own `HIST_TAG` measured-rect seam (two `build_fill` charts coexist).

`tools/demos/r1374_frame_profiler_histogram.py` (NEW): >=30-assertion RPC demo — the panel renders one bar per bin + axes (a distinct panel below the timeline), bars share the baseline, laid out left-to-right, a real distribution (modal bin tall), layout-native (a real `scene/resize` re-spans the bars), and the over-budget colour classification reaches the wire (under a 1s budget every bar carries the one under-budget fill, read from the snapshot `style.fill`).
+10 unit tests (bar geometry / per-bar colour / non-finite omit / build_fill sentinel / pinned domain / tag prefix; histogram binning + over-budget colour + empty-window + paint-cycle two-seam).

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`: clean (`-D pedantic`). `cargo fmt --all --check` + `cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean.
`tools/demos/r1374_frame_profiler_histogram.py`: PASS (~37 assertions incl. the wire colour check; ZERO-FLAKE, PINION_HIDDEN_WINDOW).

**Regression gate**: `r907_frame_profiler` / `r925_frame_budget` (profiler) + `hello_chart_r1354` / `r1360_chart_layout_native` (line chart, exercises the `draw.rs` + `ChartStyle`-move refactor) all PASS unchanged.

**Independent 3-reviewer adversarial audit ran BEFORE commit** (correctness / SSOT-DRY / hacks-smells, read-only). NO reachable MUST-FIX correctness bug (the refactor is behaviour-preserving line-for-line; bar geometry / binning / two-seam coexistence all traced sound). Every finding remediated in-round: the MUST-FIX honesty lie (lib.rs listed "bar" as "Not yet" while shipping it), a gate-invisible doc-comment mangling (`tick_step` split `tick_decimals`'s doc), the `plot_rect` SSOT lift, the y-label tag alignment (`ylabel`->`label.y`), the `ChartStyle` home move, the dead-palette fix (`color(0)`->`color(i)`), the pinned-domain bar-overflow clamp, the wire colour-test gap, and the min-window-height fix (both panels survive).
`mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace`: T1 orphan total=0 (new +0), style reject=0.
carry_forward_bullets: The mid-level chart ASSEMBLY (horizontal gridlines / the two axes / the y-tick-label loop) is near-identical between `line.rs` and `bar.rs` and is deliberately NOT lifted: an axis-furniture API fitted to only line + bar risks being wrong for a 3rd chart type (scatter / donut). Lift when the 3rd consumer shows the right shape (the leaf primitives + `plot_rect` WERE lifted; the assembly is the judgment-call deferral). Same for the byte-identical `build`/`build_fill` wrappers — a shared `ChartCanvas` trait would force consumers to import a trait to call `build`, a worse public API, so they stay inherent (2 copies, defer to 3rd).

`ChartStyle` still carries line-only knobs (`series_width` / `area_alpha` / `crosshair` / `marker_radius` / `tooltip_*` / `x_ticks`); splitting a shared `AxisStyle` core from per-chart extras is deferred until a 3rd chart type shows which knobs are truly common (YAGNI on a 2-consumer split). `BAR_GAP_FRAC` stays a bar.rs const until then.

The over-budget histogram colouring is bin-granular (a bin straddling the budget is coloured under); the exact per-frame jank count stays truthful in the status line. A future finer classification (split a straddling bin) is possible but the status line already carries the precise count.
Remaining pinion-chart chart types (donut / treemap / scatter) + interactions (legend-toggle / cross-filter / y-rescale-on-zoom) stay follow-up slices on the shared core (crate scope doc).

R1375.decision_summary: R1375 §5.16 §5.7 §5.40: pinion_chart::BarChart gains a scrub inspect overlay (a highlight ring on the focused bar + a value tooltip), the bar-chart twin of the line chart's R1355 inspector and its 2nd consumer. The tooltip callout (rounded box + header + colour-per-row) is lifted pub(crate) into draw.rs, consumed byte-identically by both line + bar; BarChart build_body is refactored onto a geom() SSOT so the drawn bar and the highlight ring share ONE definition. Forced by hello-frame-profiler: the R1374 distribution histogram becomes press-drag scrubbable (a SliderExternal in the extra_externals slot + a transparent capture surface), and the per-bin readout reaches a11y describedby the tooltip region, computed against the SAME live measured size the paint uses (access_node runs in root_owner.run so use_pane_viewport_size resolves identically) — closing the R1355 'values dropped at the a11y boundary' class for a build_fill chart. A pre-commit 3-reviewer adversarial audit (correctness / SSOT / honesty, read-only) found NO reachable correctness MUST-FIX (hit-test, geom SSOT, callout byte-identity, and the a11y/paint parity traced sound incl. the access_node-before-frame-record shell ordering), one SSOT SHOULD-FIX (a hand-rolled read_toggle now reuses the substrate toggle_group::read_toggle) and two honesty MUST-FIX (a #[widget] doc still claimed a derived WidgetA11y the a11y_manual opt-out removed; a stale view-fn (ToggleState, bool) signature doc), all remediated in-round before commit.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/bar.rs`: `BarChart` gains a scrub `inspect(Option<f32>)` overlay — a categorical slot hit-test (`resolve_focus`: fraction across the chart -> the evenly-spaced slot under it, the bar-chart analogue of the line chart's nearest-numeric-point), a highlight RING framing the focused bar (`outline_box` = a transparent-fill box with an Outside-placed crosshair-colour border), and a value tooltip, plus `inspect_readout` for a11y. `build_body` is refactored onto a `geom()` + `bar_slot_center_and_rect` SSOT so the DRAWN bar and the ring read ONE geometry and cannot drift. New tags `chart.inspect.highlight` / `.tooltip` / `.header` / `.value` (singular, one per categorical slot, vs line's per-series `.value.{i}`); a non-finite bar shows no ring but a tooltip with an em-dash value.

`crates/pinion-chart/src/draw.rs`: the tooltip `callout` (a rounded box + a header line + one colour-per-row value line, placed right of the anchor and flipped LEFT on overflow) + `rounded_box_node` + `CalloutRow` + `TOOLTIP_WIDTH` lifted `pub(crate)`, consumed by BOTH `line` + `bar`. The line chart's tooltip output is byte-identical (its inspect tests + `hello_chart_r1354` demo unchanged).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/line.rs`: `inspect_tooltip` refactored to assemble the header + rows and call the shared `callout` (was ~40 lines of bespoke box placement); every tag / position / colour preserved (the mechanical geometry moved to `draw.rs`, the per-series row CONTENT stayed).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/lib.rs` + `bar.rs` module doc: the Scope + Introspection docs record the R1375 bar inspect as SHIPPED (not "Not yet") and list the four inspect tags with their correct cardinality.

`examples/hello-frame-profiler/src/main.rs`: the R1374 distribution histogram becomes press-drag SCRUBBABLE — a `SliderExternal` in the `extra_externals` slot (`hist_scrub`) + a transparent capture surface sized to the measured panel drive `BarChart::inspect`. State grows to `(ToggleState, bool, f32)`; `read_state` reads BOTH externals by tag (the Toggle via the substrate `toggle_group::read_toggle`, the scrub via `read_scrub`). `a11y_manual` + a hand-written `WidgetA11y`: the repaint Switch (reproducing the derived form) + the scrub Slider `describedby` the histogram inspect region, the readout computed against the LIVE measured size (`access_node` runs in `root_owner.run`, so `use_pane_viewport_size(HIST_TAG)` resolves to the same size the paint used).

`tools/demos/r1375_histogram_hover.py` (NEW): >=30-assertion RPC demo — the boot scrub paints the overlay, the ring frames a REAL bar (geom SSOT: ring.rect in the bar-rect set), driving the scrub over `scene/intervene` moves the ring strictly right, bin 0 (fraction 0.0) reads "0" (its 0ms lower edge), and the right-edge tooltip flips LEFT of its bar and stays in-window.

+7 bar unit tests (no-overlay default / overlay tags / slot hit-test / ring==bar rect / readout parity + tooltip agreement / non-finite em-dash + no ring / right-edge flip) + 1 profiler test (histogram scrub overlay + a11y readout reaches the described region).
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green, 0 failed. `pinion-chart` = 62 (55 prior + 7 bar inspect); `hello-frame-profiler` = 14 (13 prior + 1 scrub overlay/a11y).

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`: clean (`-D pedantic`). `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean (the gate that catches doc mangling — both honesty doc MUST-FIX cleared before this ran).
`tools/demos/r1375_histogram_hover.py`: PASS (ZERO-FLAKE, `PINION_HIDDEN_WINDOW`; every wait polls the profiler frame_count, never wall-clock).
Regression gate: `r907_frame_profiler` / `r925_frame_budget` / `r1374_frame_profiler_histogram` (profiler) all PASS unchanged after the state-tuple growth + capture surface + a11y_manual switch.

Independent 3-reviewer adversarial audit ran BEFORE commit (correctness / SSOT-DRY / honesty-doc, read-only): NO reachable correctness MUST-FIX — the correctness reviewer traced the fraction->slot hit-test (no edge off-by-one), the `geom()` SSOT (behaviour-identical to the pre-R1375 inline bar layout), the `callout` byte-identity for line, the ring==bar-rect equality, and the a11y/paint parity, INCLUDING verifying in app.rs that `access_node` runs BEFORE `record_frame_timing` so the a11y readout reads the SAME timings snapshot the paint did (no R1355-class divergence for a `build_fill` chart). Every finding remediated in-round: the SSOT SHOULD-FIX (a hand-rolled `read_toggle` -> the substrate `toggle_group::read_toggle`, dropping the now-unused `IntrospectValue` import) and both honesty MUST-FIX (the `#[widget]` doc still claimed a derived `WidgetA11y` the `a11y_manual` opt-out removed; a stale `view-fn (ToggleState, bool)` signature doc), plus SHOULD-FIX tidy-ups (the "Two nodes" a11y count -> three-when-focused; the demo's flip claim tightened to prove the tooltip sits LEFT of its bar, not merely in-bounds).
`mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace`: T1 orphan total=0 (new +0), style reject=0.
carry_forward_bullets: The scrub-inspector demo boilerplate (a transparent tagged capture surface hosting a `SliderExternal` + a read-fraction-by-tag helper) now has a 2nd consumer (hello-chart's line scrub + this histogram scrub), but the two DIFFER (hello-chart pins a `build` chart to a window rect; the profiler sizes a `build_fill` chart to the measured seam), so it stays a documented lift candidate deferred to a 3rd identical consumer (the mechanical-vs-opinionated 3b rule). `read_scrub` likewise re-derives the "read a 1-D fraction by tag" idiom; the lift target is a `pinion_core` slider-value-by-tag helper mirroring `toggle_group::read_toggle`, when a 3rd core-only consumer appears — NOT before (the existing `read_slider_state` lives in `pinion-widget-paint`, a dep `pinion-chart` deliberately avoids, and returns a different shape).

The manual `WidgetA11y` reproduces the derived Switch `AccessState` verbatim just to APPEND one sibling node (the scrub Slider). This reproduce-to-append need now recurs across ~4 `a11y_manual` bindings = the signal for a `pinion-derive` a11y-augment/append hook (keep the derived node, add siblings); there is no such hook today (only full `a11y_manual` opt-out). A derive-macro enhancement, out of scope for a chart round — noted as derive debt.

The bar chart's mid-level axis furniture (gridlines / axes / y-tick-label loop) stays un-lifted vs `line.rs` (the R1374 deferral held): the R1375 `callout` lift is MECHANICAL (byte-identical box geometry for both), the axis furniture is OPINIONATED (an API fitted to only line+bar risks being wrong for scatter/donut) — lift at the 3rd chart type. `outline_box` (the highlight ring) is kept LOCAL to `bar.rs` at its 1 consumer; the existing ring helpers (`pinion-overlay`/`pinion-widget-paint`) live in crates `pinion-chart` does not depend on.

Remaining pinion-chart interactions (legend-toggle / cross-filter / y-rescale-on-zoom) + types (donut / scatter / treemap) stay follow-up slices on the shared core (see [[debt-dataviz-dashboard-substrate]]).

R1377.decision_summary: R1377 §5.16 §5.7 §5.40: pinion_chart gains ScatterChart — the crate's THIRD cartesian chart (numeric x AND y), plotting each series as filled circle point marks with the R1355 scrub inspect (a crosshair, a stroked ring per series' nearest point, a value tooltip, an a11y readout). Being the third axis-based chart is what forced the substrate lifts R1376 named to land at their consumer count: the axis furniture (gridlines/axes/y-tick-labels) factored out of line+bar into draw.rs (line+bar+scatter now CALL it); the legend inner loop (line+donut+scatter) lifted to draw::legend_row; and the cubic-Bezier arc unified — line's former private circle re-expressed through the donut's arc_beziers (circle_commands = arc(0..TAU) closed), so the crate has ONE circle. Also lifted at 2 consumers (line+scatter, the crate's 2nd-consumer practice): plot::CartesianPlot / resolve_focus / axis_ticks / domain_from_ticks and series::nearest_point_in / in_domain. Forced by a new hello-scatter binding: two sample series with a press-drag scrub whose 1-D fraction maps through the plot to a data x, the readout reaching a11y describedby the tooltip region. A pre-commit 3-reviewer adversarial audit (correctness/geometry, doc-honesty, substrate-reuse) verified the refactor byte-identical for every moved helper and the arc unification numerically exact (TAU == 4*FRAC_PI_2 in f32 -> exactly 4 segments), found NO premature lift, and caught+remediated in-round one correctness edge case (a pinned-y-domain scrub could ring a point clipped from view -> scatter now filters hits to the y-domain for its ring/tooltip/readout) plus a batch of R1374-class doc-honesty errors (bar/donut/lib/scatter docs still claiming the axis-furniture lift was deferred / mis-attributing which charts call the shared legend+circle helpers; stale consumer counts).
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/scatter.rs` (NEW): `ScatterChart` — the crate's THIRD cartesian chart (numeric x AND y). One filled `Scene::Path` circle per finite, in-domain point (`chart.point.{i}.{j}`), palette-coloured per series; a scrub `inspect(Option<f32>)` overlay (a crosshair at the scrubbed x, a stroked ring per series' nearest point, a `callout` value tooltip, an `inspect_readout` a11y string). Reuses `Series` / `DataPoint` (the line chart's data model). `build` / `build_fill` mirror the line chart's R1360.4 placement contract.

`crates/pinion-chart/src/plot.rs` (NEW): `CartesianPlot::resolve` + `resolve_focus` + `axis_ticks` + `domain_from_ticks` — the numeric-x/-y plot substrate, lifted out of `line.rs`'s private `Plot` so the line and scatter charts share ONE resolver rather than scatter "borrowing line's Plot".

R1378.decision_summary: R1378 §5.38 §5.50 §5.53: an anchored-overlay vertical-flip positioner lifts to pinion_widget_paint::anchor::flip_y — the drop-below-or-flip-above decision (an anchor span + a panel height + a viewport height + a preferred side -> a y; flush against the preferred side, flipping only when it overflows AND the opposite side fits, else keeping the preferred side) that THREE consumers had independently re-derived: the tooltip anchor_position, the property-grid popup_origin, and the data-grid popup_anchor — a Rule-of-Three the popup surface's module doc had earmarked as a deferred 2nd-binding lift. The tooltip's vertical half now CALLS flip_y (verbatim extraction — its 13 flip/clamp tests unchanged) with the cross-axis clamp left inline (single consumer, deferred with a note); both grids' inline flips route through it. Forced and demonstrated by a NEW 4th consumer: hello-combobox's trigger relocated low so opening below overflows the window bottom, and its dropdown now FLIPS ABOVE via flip_y (bottom flush at the trigger top). An audit-first pre-round census corrected a wrong initial premise (the popup infra was NOT absent — popup_surface/menu/context-menu/listbox already exist) and, crucially, caught the third (data-grid) copy the SEED plan had missed, turning a barely-met 2nd-consumer gate into a full Rule-of-Three. A doc-honesty sweep cleared stale 'deferred lift' claims (popup.rs, tooltip.rs) and inline-flip descriptions (both grids), the R1374-class discipline.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/anchor.rs` (NEW): `AnchorSide { Above, Below }` + `flip_y(anchor_y, anchor_h, panel_h, viewport_h, prefer) -> u32` — the anchored-overlay vertical positioner. Places a panel flush against the preferred side, flipping to the opposite side only when the preferred side overflows the viewport AND the opposite side fits (a flip never trades a partial overflow for a fully-clipped panel); keeps the preferred side when neither fits. Pure geometry, no paint/theme. 9 unit tests (below/above with room, flip both directions, neither-fits keeps-preferred each way, above-flip saturates at 0, and two grid-shaped cases pinned byte-identical against the old hand-rolled flip).

`crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/tooltip.rs`: `anchor_position`'s vertical half now calls `anchor::flip_y` (verbatim extraction — its 13 flip/clamp tests pass unchanged). The horizontal cross-axis left-clamp stays inline (a single-consumer concern, deferred with a note per `[[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]]`). Module doc updated: the positioner is no longer "inline first consumer".

`crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/popup.rs`: module doc corrected — the earmarked "reusable anchored-overlay positioning helper ... lifts when a 2nd binding needs it" deferral now records the R1378 lift to `anchor::flip_y` (the 2nd/3rd-consumer gate was already met by the grids).

`examples/hello-property-grid/src/main.rs`: `popup_origin`'s inline drop-below-or-flip-above replaced by `flip_y(row_top, ROW_H, panel_h, WIN_H - PANEL_PAD, Below)`; the fn now owns only the grid row -> anchor-y arithmetic. Doc de-staled (delegates to the shared positioner). 81 tests green.

`examples/hello-data-grid/src/main.rs`: `popup_anchor`'s i32 grid-local flip routed through `flip_y(grid_row_top, ROW_H, panel_h, GRID_VIEWPORT_H, Below)` (grid_row_top > 0 by the on-screen guard, so the u32 conversion is safe). Doc de-staled. 143 tests green.

`examples/hello-combobox/src/main.rs` (the forcing/4th consumer): the trigger relocated low (`TRIGGER_Y` 110 -> 280) so opening below would overflow the window bottom; the panel's `y` is now `flip_y(TRIGGER_Y, TRIGGER_H, panel_h, WIN_H, Below)` -> the dropdown FLIPS ABOVE, its bottom flush at the trigger top. `const PANEL_Y` removed (now open-time computed). New `r1378_dropdown_flips_above_the_low_trigger` unit test guards the premise (a future edit raising the trigger fails it) + the flip. 18 tests green.

`tools/demos/r714_combobox.py`: 3 flip assertions added (panel top ABOVE the trigger top, panel bottom flush == trigger top, whole panel inside the viewport bottom), off the paint snapshot's `abs_rects_of`. Doc updated (glyph flip vs panel flip disambiguated). 37 assertions total.

Popup panel LAYOUT (anchor x, size, flex direction, padding) stays per-callsite by design — only the surface skin (`popup_surface`, R870) and now the vertical flip (`flip_y`, R1378) are shared; the anchor-x math genuinely diverges (grid value-column vs combobox trigger vs scrolled grid-local).

`flip_y` degenerate "neither side fits" branch keeps the preferred side (tooltip semantics), whereas the old grids' hand-rolled flip flipped unconditionally — divergent ONLY for a viewport shorter than the panel, unreachable for the grids' short popups (pinned by two byte-identical tests); the primitive's keep-preferred is the more-correct native behaviour.

Standing defers unchanged: numeric-x chart presentation lift (tooltip-row/readout/x-label) awaits a 3rd identical-format consumer; 2-D geometric hover needs a 2-D pointer external; quit-veto forcing consumer `[[debt-r1364-quit-split-clearance]]`; the demo-sweep push gap (`[[r1322-r1323-dock-gesture-regressions]]`) is still not push-gated (pre-push runs unit+clippy+doc, not the demo sweep).

R1379.decision_summary: R1379 §5.38 §5.40: pinion_chart::Series gains a visible flag — a hidden series drops only its own geometry (the line chart's area + polyline, the scatter chart's point marks) while KEEPING its palette index, its legend slot, and (because data_bounds still measures it) the auto-domain, so toggling a series never re-colours or re-indexes the others and never rescales the axes: a series toggled back on lands on exactly the same grid. The shared scrub focus resolver (plot::resolve_focus) skips hidden series too, so a scrub never rings or reports a point whose geometry was dropped (the R1377 visible_hits class, applied at the focus source; behaviour-preserving for every existing all-visible consumer). Forced and demonstrated by a NEW hello-series-toggle binding: a bar of three toggle chips — each a series-coloured swatch + name, so the chips ARE the legend — shows / hides its series over a LineChart whose own internal legend is off; a further consumer of the toggle_group toggle-button-group substrate (with hello-segmented-multi, hello-filter-chip, hello-frame-profiler). The R1379 entry audit scoped and deferred two larger directions as genuine design forks that change ratified behaviour: the inspector Choice dropdown would replace the established R1225 click-to-cycle gesture, and a click-the-chart's-own-legend toggle needs the chart-owned legend to expose input hit geometry it does not have yet (this round drives visibility from an external toggle bar instead). A self-grep caught + fixed a doc-honesty slip (the demo first claimed 3rd consumer of toggle_group when it is the 4th).
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/series.rs`: `Series` gains a `visible: bool` (default `true`) + `with_visible(bool)` builder. Doc records the model: a hidden series keeps its palette index, its legend slot, and — because `data_bounds` still measures it — the auto-domain, so hiding never re-colours / re-indexes the others or rescales the axes (a returning series lands on the same grid).
`crates/pinion-chart/src/line.rs`: `series_layer` skips a `!visible` series (no area, no polyline); the palette index `i` is preserved so the visible series never shift colour.
`crates/pinion-chart/src/scatter.rs`: `point_marks` skips a `!visible` series (no marks); index preserved likewise.

`crates/pinion-chart/src/plot.rs`: `resolve_focus` skips hidden series so a scrub never rings / reports a point whose geometry was dropped (the R1377 `visible_hits` class, applied at the shared focus source; behaviour-preserving for every existing all-visible consumer). New `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: two visible / one visible (index preserved) / all hidden (no focus).

`examples/hello-series-toggle/` (NEW binding — Cargo.toml / build.rs / app.pinion.xml / src/main.rs): the forcing consumer. A bar of three toggle chips — each a series-coloured swatch + name, so the chips ARE the legend — shows / hides its series over a `LineChart` (`ChartStyle { legend: false }`, the chips replace the internal legend). A further consumer of the `toggle_group` toggle-button-group substrate (with hello-segmented-multi, hello-filter-chip, hello-frame-profiler): N independent `ToggleExternal`s, each its own Tab stop, `read_toggle` / `boot_toggle` / `extra_toggles` / `apply_key` shared verbatim, `toggle_button_group_nodes` for the `group` + `button[aria-pressed]` a11y. 5 unit tests (all-visible draws 3 polylines / toggle one off hides only it / all-hidden draws none / boot all on / a11y one pressed button per series).

`tools/demos/r1379_series_toggle.py` (NEW): >=30-assertion RPC demo — boot draws all three `chart.series.{i}` polylines with all chips on; a `scene/click` (and a keyboard Space / Enter) on a chip drops ONLY that series' polyline while its siblings and its own chip stay; a second toggle round trip and arrow-roved focus confirm independence; an unknown introspect path is rejected.
`Cargo.toml`: register `examples/hello-series-toggle` as a workspace member.

`tools/demos/r1379_series_toggle.py`: PASS end-to-end (1.99s) — a click / Space / Enter on a series chip hides exactly that series' polyline (verified over `scene/snapshot`) while the others and the chip persist, and toggling back restores it on the same grid.

The forcing consumer reuses `toggle_group` rather than re-deriving a toggle group. Until then this round drives visibility from an external toggle bar (the chips), and the chart's internal legend stays off. A companion "muted hidden legend entry" rendering on `legend_row` waits on that same legend-interactivity work.

Donut / bar series (slice) visibility is not wired — the line + scatter cartesian charts share `Series`; the donut's `Slice` toggle carries a divergent semantic (hiding a slice re-normalises the part-of-whole), so it is its own future round, not a mechanical extension.

No rescale-on-toggle by design: `data_bounds` measures every series regardless of visibility, so the axes stay fixed when a series is hidden (predictable dashboard behaviour). An opt-in "rescale to visible series" is a possible follow-up.

Two larger dataviz / DCC directions the R1379 entry audit scoped but deferred as genuine design forks (each changes ratified behaviour): the inspector `Choice` cell dropdown would replace the established R1225 click-to-cycle gesture; a chart legend-interaction API is the click-the-legend prerequisite above. Standing defers unchanged: quit-veto forcing consumer, demo-sweep push gap.

R1380.decision_summary: R1380 §5.38 §5.39: LineChart::interactive_legend gives the chart-owned legend the input hit geometry it lacked (the R1379 follow-up it named). Each legend entry becomes a focusable, hit-testable Container tagged with the caller's tag, whose only children are an untagged swatch + label — the toggle_group chip structure, chart-authored — so the router's deepest-tagged-ancestor hit-test resolves a click anywhere on it to that tag; a hidden series' entry renders muted (grey swatch + dimmed label) while keeping its palette index + slot. The chart stays a pure scene producer: it emits the tagged, focusable entries; the caller owns the tag namespace and binds the ToggleExternals, so the legend drives Series::visible without the chart importing any widget. Forced and demonstrated by a NEW hello-legend-toggle binding: the chart draws its own legend and each entry IS the toggle surface (no separate chip bar), a 5th consumer of the toggle_group substrate reused verbatim. This CLEARS the R1379 deferrals (click-the-legend + muted hidden entry). Interactive-legend stays line-only (single consumer, not lifted to shared draw.rs); a self-grep caught + fixed a doc-honesty slip (the Cargo.toml first claimed 4th consumer of toggle_group when it is the 5th).
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/line.rs`: `LineChart` gains `legend_tags: Option<Vec<String>>` + an `interactive_legend(tags)` builder. `legend()` branches: when interactive it emits `interactive_legend_entries` (one focusable, hit-testable `Container` per series, tagged with the caller's `tags[i]`, whose only children are an untagged swatch + label — the chip structure, chart-authored — so the router's deepest-tagged-ancestor hit-test resolves a click anywhere on it to `tags[i]`); otherwise it calls the shared static `draw::legend_row` unchanged (byte-identical for donut / scatter / non-interactive line). A hidden series' entry greys its swatch to the muted `style.label` colour and dims its label (the "this line is off" affordance) while keeping the palette index + slot. Three new unit tests: entries are focusable + tagged with the caller namespace (and the static per-part `chart.legend.{i}.swatch/.label` tags are absent in interactive mode); a hidden entry greys while the sibling keeps its series colour; the default legend stays static + unfocusable.

`examples/hello-legend-toggle/` (NEW binding — Cargo.toml / build.rs / app.pinion.xml / src/main.rs): the forcing consumer. The chart draws its OWN legend (`ChartStyle { legend: true }`, `interactive_legend`), and each entry IS the toggle surface — no separate chip bar. The caller passes `LEGEND_TAGS` to the chart AND binds N `ToggleExternal`s to the same tags, so a click on entry `i` routes to toggle `i` which gates `Series::visible`. A further (5th) consumer of the `toggle_group` toggle-button-group substrate (with hello-segmented-multi, hello-filter-chip, hello-frame-profiler, hello-series-toggle): `boot_toggle` / `extra_toggles` / `read_toggle` / `apply_key` shared verbatim, `toggle_button_group_nodes` for the virtual `group` + `button[aria-pressed]` a11y (no consumer-drawn row — the chart owns the legend paint). 6 unit tests.

`tools/demos/r1380_legend_toggle.py` (NEW): >=30-assertion RPC demo. Boot draws all three `chart.series.{i}` polylines with all entries on; a COORDINATE `scene/click` at a legend entry's rect centre (exercising the real geometric hit-test the chart now exposes) drops ONLY that series' polyline while siblings + other toggles persist; a round trip restores it on the same grid; keyboard Space / Enter toggles only the focused entry and Arrow roves focus. A BOUNDED-hit-region check clicks the plot body (not on any entry) and asserts nothing toggles — proving the hit geometry is the legend, not the whole chart. An unknown introspect path is rejected.
`Cargo.toml`: register `examples/hello-legend-toggle` as a workspace member.
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green, 0 failed. `pinion-chart` = 91 (+3 interactive-legend tests); `hello-legend-toggle` = 6.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`: clean (`-D pedantic`; clippy caught `LegendState::visibility(&self)` — the state is under the copy-by-ref threshold once R1379's `focused` field is dropped — fixed to by-value in round). `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` + `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.

`tools/demos/r1380_legend_toggle.py`: PASS end-to-end (1.94s) — a coordinate click at a legend entry's centre hides exactly that series' polyline (verified over `scene/snapshot`) while siblings persist and toggle back restores it; a plot-body click toggles nothing (hit region bounded to the legend); keyboard + roving focus confirmed.

Self-grep (3b mandate): interactive-legend has exactly ONE consumer (line.rs) — NOT lifted to shared `draw.rs` per abstraction-needs-a-2nd-consumer (donut / scatter keep the static `legend_row`; lift when a 2nd chart needs an interactive legend). The `start_x + i*LEGEND_SLOT` per-entry stride is at 2 sites (static `legend_row`, interactive path), both trivially over the shared `LEGEND_SLOT` const (the SSOT magic number) — below the Rule-of-Three lift. The demo reuses `toggle_group` verbatim (its 5th consumer) rather than re-deriving a toggle group. Self-grep also CAUGHT + fixed a doc-honesty slip: the Cargo.toml description first claimed "4th consumer" of toggle_group when it is the 5th.

carry_forward_bullets: R1380 CLEARS the R1379 carry "click-the-chart's-own-legend to toggle a series is deferred" and its companion "muted hidden legend entry rendering waits on legend-interactivity work": both land here (`LineChart::interactive_legend` + the muted hidden entry).

The interactive legend does not show per-entry hover / pressed micro-states (the chart takes `Series::visible`, not the `ToggleState`): the entry reflects on/off via the muted swatch + the shell-injected focus ring, but a press-highlight skin like the chip's is not wired. A chart legend is a compact swatch+label, not a full button skin, so this is a deliberate MVP simplification, not a regression; wiring `ToggleState` through would be a follow-up if a consumer needs the press feedback.

Interactive legend is line-only: scatter / donut still emit the static `legend_row`. When a 2nd chart needs a clickable legend, lift `interactive_legend_entries` (and the `start_x + i*LEGEND_SLOT` entry-geometry it shares with `legend_row`) into `draw.rs` — deferred now (single consumer, abstraction-needs-a-2nd-consumer).

Donut / bar slice visibility still unwired (a slice toggle re-normalises the part-of-whole — its own future round). No rescale-on-toggle by design (`data_bounds` measures every series). Standing defers unchanged: quit-veto forcing consumer, demo-sweep push gap.

R1381.decision_summary: R1381 §5.38: LineChart::rescale_to_visible is the opt-in that lets hiding the dominant series rescale the axes to the survivors — the interactive-dashboard behaviour the R1379/R1380 stable-grid default deliberately withholds. It is a single bool threaded from the LineChart builder (default false) through CartesianPlot::resolve into a new series::visible_data_bounds (bounds over only the visible series), which shares one bounds_of scan with data_bounds so the addition removed a duplicate scan rather than adding one. R1382.decision_summary: R1382 §5.16: Treemap is pinion-chart's SECOND part-of-whole form, area-encoded rather than the donut's angular — a treemap TILES its whole frame with value-sized rectangles, legible for far more items than a donut's thin sectors (the asset-browser / disk-usage shape). The distinctive new machinery is the SQUARIFIED layout (Bruls-Huizing-van Wijk 2000): squarify packs tiles into rows along the frame's shorter side, extending a row while the next tile lowers its worst aspect ratio (max(w2.rmax/s2, s2/(w2.rmin))) and starting a fresh row against the remaining sub-frame otherwise, so every tile stays near-square rather than the long slivers a naive slice-and-dice produces (a unit test asserts aspect < 5 for 8 varied tiles). Tiles lay out largest-first, so chart.tile.{i} is RANK by value. In-tile labels are contrast-aware (near-white / near-black by WCAG relative luminance in LINEAR light, the 0.179 white/black equal-contrast crossover) so they read on both light and dark palette entries, gated on a tile-width minimum. Scrub inspect mirrors the donut exactly — a captured 1-D fraction scrubs the tiles, rings the focused one with the lifted outline_box, and shows value + percent share through the shared callout, the readout reaching a11y. outline_box (the rect-highlight ring) is LIFTED from bar.rs to draw.rs at this 2nd consumer, joining the crate's other shared draw leaves; percent_text is duplicated (donut + treemap = 2) and deferred to a 3rd part-of-whole chart per the rule-of-three. A doc-honesty pass on lib.rs recorded R1379-R1381 (series visibility / interactive legend / rescale-to-visible) as shipped — the crate Scope doc had missed them and still listed 'Not yet: legend-toggle'. Forced by a NEW hello-treemap binding: a squarified asset-size treemap driven through the real windowed shell + a >=30-assertion RPC demo that reads the tiles as tagged boxes partitioning the frame and proves the ring frames EXACTLY the scrubbed tile over the wire. Phase B dataviz #1 (charting substrate) depth, not catalog regression.

Tiles are laid largest-first, so `chart.tile.{i}` is RANK by value. `contrast_text` picks near-white / near-black in-tile labels by WCAG relative luminance in LINEAR light (threshold 0.179, the white/black equal-contrast crossover) so labels read on both light and dark palette entries; a label is emitted only when the tile clears a width gate. R1383.decision_summary: R1383 §5.38 §5.52: a layered (Sugiyama) auto-layout for the node graph — the AI-first peer of an editor's arrange / tidy command (Unreal Blueprint / Blender / Substance). A NEW pure layered_layout(nodes, edges, origin) arranges the graph into left-to-right columns so data flows forward, with a crossing-reduced vertical order inside each column: three deterministic phases — forward-DFS cycle breaking (back-edges dropped so any cyclic graph gets an acyclic base), longest-path Kahn layering, and barycenter crossing-reduction sweeps — each id-ordered, integer-keyed, reading only the node set + heights + edges (never positions), so identical input yields an identical layout and a second pass is idempotent. NodeGraphExternal::auto_layout tidies the WHOLE graph (no selection) in ONE undo step through the shared apply_node_moves SSOT, wired as invoke auto_layout (the align/distribute precedent). Closes the dataviz debt #3 'automatic graph layout ABSENT' — a self-grep confirmed no prior layout algorithm existed to reuse, and the existing DFS cycle helpers are divergent domain logic (backward->bool vs forward->back-edge-index-set), not a mechanical duplication warranting a lift. Coordinate assignment is ordered-stack-per-column + vertical centring (not a straight-edge solver) and long edges are not dummy-split — documented simplifications. Forced and demonstrated by hello-node-editor's auto_layout verb + a NEW ~60-assertion RPC demo that tidies a scrambled graph and a widened 3-column graph over the wire.
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-node-editor/src/main.rs`: a NEW pure `layered_layout(nodes, edges, origin) -> BTreeMap<NodeId,(x,y)>` (Sugiyama layered graph drawing) plus five id-ordered helpers it composes — `layout_successors` (edge-index-tagged adjacency), `layout_back_edges` (iterative forward-DFS cycle breaking: an edge into an on-stack node is a back-edge, dropped), `layout_assign_layers` (longest-path layering by Kahn topo order, smallest id first), `layout_neighbours` (undirected adjacency), and `layout_reduce_crossings` (LAYOUT_SWEEPS=4 alternating barycenter sweeps, exact-rational integer keys, id tie-break). It reads only the node set + `GraphNode::height` + edges — never the stored x/y — so identical input yields an identical layout (deterministic, idempotent once applied). Long edges are not dummy-split (documented). Constants LAYER_GAP=60 / LAYOUT_ROW_GAP=24 / LAYOUT_SWEEPS=4.

`examples/hello-node-editor/src/main.rs`: a NEW `NodeGraphExternal::auto_layout()` — tidies the WHOLE graph (no selection) into left-to-right columns in ONE discrete undo step through the shared `apply_node_moves` SSOT (align / distribute / nudge peer), anchored at the graph's current bounding-box top-left. A no-op `false` on <2 nodes or when nothing moves (idempotent). Wired as the AI-first `invoke auto_layout` verb (SchemaField + invoke_layout arm, the align/distribute precedent) and documented in the module header. Comment frames are left in place (the align/distribute nodes-only contract).

`examples/hello-node-editor/src/tests.rs`: 10 NEW tests — 8 pure `layered_layout` (linear chain forward columns, diamond fan-out no-overlap, every-edge-flows-forward, no pairwise card overlap, deterministic + position-independent, cycle-does-not-hang + spine-forward, isolated node = layer-0 source, barycenter reduces a crossing) + 2 coordinator `auto_layout` (scrambled graph tidies in one undo step + undo/redo round-trip; idempotent second pass moves nothing).

`tools/demos/r1383_node_auto_layout.py` (NEW forcing consumer, ~60 assertions over real windowed RPC): (A) boot taxonomy; (B) a reversed/scrambled seed graph tidies so the two sources share the layer-0 column, each consumer one column right (pitch NODE_W+LAYER_GAP=190), stacked sources non-overlapping; (C) idempotent second pass = Bool false, positions unchanged; (D) one-undo-step + undo restores all four scrambled positions + redo re-applies; (E) grows an Add consumer + fresh Texture source via add_node/add_edge -> a THREE-node layer-0 column (pairwise non-overlapping) + a two-node consumer column, every old and new edge flowing forward.
verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green, 0 failed across every crate. hello-node-editor = 254 passed (the 10 new R1383 tests among them, run before and after `cargo fmt`).

`cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean (private-item intra-doc links resolve). `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.

`tools/demos/r1383_node_auto_layout.py`: PASS end-to-end (3.26s) over real windowed RPC — forward-flow columns, shared source column, no-overlap, idempotency, one-undo-step + undo/redo, and a widened 3-node-column graph, all read back over `query node.<id>.{x,y}` (scene-as-data, §2 #7) and driven over the §5.12 plane (§2 #2).

R1384.decision_summary: R1384 §5.38 §5.39: the chart family's first cross-filter — a selection in one widget filters another. BarChart::select(active_mask) mutes the bars outside the active category set (their fill drops to a low alpha) while the selected bars stay full; BarChart::selectable(tags) overlays one transparent, focusable, caller-tagged hit region per bar spanning its whole slot column, so a coordinate click in a category's column routes through the real geometric hit-test to that category's toggle — the interactive-legend chip mechanism (R1380) applied to the bars themselves. The new example hello-cross-filter wires the SAME active mask to two purposes: it emphasises the bars AND filters a companion line chart to the selected categories (via Series::visible), so a click in the selector reshapes the dependent view — the dashboard interaction the chart family (line/bar/donut/scatter/treemap, R1354-R1382) was building toward. An empty selection is no filter = all data (the crossfilter convention). The selection state is the 6th consumer of the toggle_group substrate (verbatim reuse: N independent ToggleExternals, per-bar Tab stop, aria-pressed buttons, keyboard model). Closes the categorical-selection leg of the dataviz cross-filter debt; a numeric brush-range cross-filter and arbitrary chart-to-chart linking remain.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/bar.rs`: NEW `BarChart::select(active: Vec<bool>)` — with a NON-empty active mask every bar OUTSIDE the set renders muted (its `chart.bar.{i}` fill drops to a low alpha, MUTED_ALPHA=0x4D) while the selected bars stay full; an empty / all-`false` mask is "no filter" and leaves every bar full (the crossfilter convention that no selection = all data). And `BarChart::selectable(tags: Vec<String>)` — overlays ONE transparent, focusable, caller-tagged hit region per bar spanning its whole slot COLUMN, emitted last so the geometric hit-test resolves a click anywhere in a category's column to that bar's tag (the `interactive_legend` chip mechanism, R1380, now applied to the bars themselves). Both are pure render/emit; the caller owns the selection state and the cross-widget link. `is_active` helper. 5 new tests (mute vs full, empty + all-false = no mute, focusable tagged regions, tag-count under + over bounds).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/lib.rs`: scope doc records R1384 as the crate's FIRST cross-filter surface (select + selectable + the wired example); the "Not yet" line narrowed to a numeric BRUSH-range cross-filter and linking two arbitrary chart types.

`examples/hello-cross-filter/` (NEW forcing consumer): a SELECTOR bar chart of per-category totals (`selectable` + `select`) linked to a DEPENDENT line chart of per-category timelines. The one active-category mask serves both purposes — it mutes the unselected bars AND filters the timelines (through `Series::visible`), so a click in the selector reshapes the dependent view. 6th consumer of the `toggle_group` substrate (verbatim `boot_toggle` / `extra_toggles` / `read_toggle` / `apply_key`) + `toggle_button_group_nodes` a11y (one aria-pressed button per category). 8 tests.

`tools/demos/r1384_cross_filter.py` (NEW, >=30 assertions over real windowed RPC): boot no-filter taxonomy; a COORDINATE click in a bar's column drives BOTH widgets (the timeline filters to the selected category AND the other bars mute — `style.fill.a` drops); a filter is a SET (multi-select keeps every selected timeline); deselect round-trips undisturbed; keyboard (each column a Tab stop, Space toggles only the focused category, Arrow roves focus); BOUNDED / cross-widget (a click in the dependent timeline area toggles nothing — the hit surface is the selector, not the window); negative introspect path rejected.

COORDINATE clicks in a bar's column drive BOTH widgets, read back over `scene/snapshot` — `style.fill.a` proves the bar mute (255 -> low), `chart.series.{i}` presence proves the timeline filter (§2 #7 scene-as-data, driven over the §5.12 plane, §2 #2). Covers boot no-filter, single + multi (set) selection, deselect round-trips, keyboard (Tab / Space / Arrow), a BOUNDED cross-widget check (a click in the dependent timeline toggles nothing), and a negative path.

R1385.decision_summary: R1385 §5.7 §5.16 §5.40: the sparkline — a compact, axis-less trend line (pinion-chart) for inline display in a table cell or a KPI stat tile, the glanceable counterpart to the full LineChart. Sparkline::new(Vec<f64>) (x = the implicit index) reuses the crate's LinearScale + retained draw core (stroke_path / area_path / marker_node / box_node) VERBATIM but drops all the furniture (axes, ticks, gridlines, legend) and adds inline affordances a full chart lacks: an optional faint area fill, an end-cap dot marking the latest value (accent colour, drawn last), and optional min/max reference dots (subdued axis tone). A single value draws a lone dot; a flat series centres. Being a distinct chart TYPE (like treemap/donut/scatter), not a LineChart mode. Forced by the new display-only example hello-stat-tiles (PR-51 no-primary-surface, the hello-chart-fill mould) — a KPI row where each tile composes a card + metric name + value + a period-over-period delta coloured by SIGN (rise green, fall red — the semantic colours the dashboard brief keeps distinct from any brand accent) + a trend sparkline; it is the FIRST scene to compose several sparklines, so each takes a distinct spark_{i} tag prefix (the documented row-collision guard). Closes the dataviz debt #7 stat-tile / sparkline gap. Verified by an >=30-assertion RPC demo reading every value, delta text, semantic delta colour, and sparkline mark back as scene data (§2 #7).
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/sparkline.rs` (NEW): the `Sparkline` builder over a bare `Vec<f64>` (x = the implicit index) — the compact, axis-less counterpart to `LineChart`. `build` / `build_fill` (the R1360 layout-native contract), an optional faint area fill, an end-cap dot marking the LATEST value (accent colour, drawn last), and optional min / max reference dots (subdued axis tone). A single value draws a lone dot (not a line); a flat / all-equal series centres vertically rather than dividing by zero. Reuses the crate's `LinearScale` + retained `draw` core (`stroke_path` / `area_path` / `marker_node` / `box_node`) verbatim, dropping ALL the furniture (axes, ticks, gridlines, legend).
