R1386.decision_summary: R1386 §5.12 §5.18 §5.34: scene/snapshot path errors teach the valid form, and the whole PathError family surfaces its concrete reason (sprag PINION-PR66 consumer-forced seam). R-66.1: SnapshotError::UnsupportedPath goes from a payload-free unit variant to {raw_path, scene_tail}, so the RPC error data echoes the offending input and names the valid form (empty or /window[<id>], no scene tail) in the same register as the sibling params.from error — recovery from the message alone (§2 #7 scene-as-data extends to the error surface). R-66.2: the Path(_) => "Path" collapse that discarded PathError's reason is replaced by a PathError::wire_tag() SSOT (MalformedPrefix / EmptyWindowId / UnknownWindow — machine-matchable, matching the codebase's own error-data tag philosophy). An independent read-only 3-reviewer audit found the collapse was a CLASS defect at 12 error surfaces, not the 1 sprag reported; wire_tag is applied uniformly across all 12 (10 dispatch mappers + simulate + the preview set_signal hand-rolled tag). Behaviour, wire shape, syntax, and control flow are unchanged — only the failure response's data string becomes informative.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-rpc/src/path.rs`: add `PathError::wire_tag()` SSOT — the concrete machine-matchable reason tag (`MalformedPrefix` / `EmptyWindowId` / `UnknownWindow`) per the codebase's own error-`data` tag philosophy (see `preview::ApplyError::ApplyRejected`) + a distinctness unit test.

`crates/pinion-rpc/src/snapshot.rs` (R-66.1): `SnapshotError::UnsupportedPath` unit variant -> struct `{raw_path, scene_tail}` (drops `Copy`); `snapshot()` populates both fields; enum doc rewritten; 2 tests (no-prefix raw==tail, window-prefixed tail isolated).

`crates/pinion-rpc/src/dispatch.rs` (R-66.1 + R-66.2): `snapshot_error_to_rpc` emits a prose message teaching the valid form + echoing the input for `UnsupportedPath`, and `wire_tag()` for `Path`; the same `wire_tag()` applied to 9 sibling `Path(_) => "Path"` mappers (rewind/dry_run/wait_for/screenshot/bbox/layout_query/invoke/intervene/query) + `simulate_error_to_rpc` (the audit-found 11th site).

`crates/pinion-rpc/src/preview/kinds.rs`: `rewind_error_tag` (the `set_signal` apply surface) forwards `wire_tag()` instead of its hand-rolled blanket `"Path"` (the audit-found 12th site) + a test over `apply_set_signal`.

`crates/pinion-rpc/src/dispatch_tests.rs`: the query path-error assertion `"Path"` -> `"MalformedPrefix"`; +5 tests (snapshot `/` prose, window-prefixed tail echo, unknown-window reason, `from` no-regression, `simulate` class-fix proof).

R1387.decision_summary: R1387 §5.18 §5.12 §5.34: clear the R1386 carry — PathError::UnknownWindow now carries the offending window-id and echoes it on the wire (UnknownWindow: "nope"), so an AI agent sees WHICH window it mistyped instead of a bare, identical tag. () (forward peer of window_from_name — parallel root: one name per region in document order; flat root: the sole root) + App::window_names(). PathError::UnknownWindow(String) reshaped to {requested, valid: Vec<&static str>}; resolve() fills valid=App::window_names() on the failure branch only (no cost on success); wire_tag() formats UnknownWindow: "nope" (valid: main), still a machine-matchable prefix. An agent that mistypes /window[dahsboard] now sees which id was rejected AND that main would have worked. Data-only wire change (JSON-RPC code -32602 / control flow unchanged). R1389.decision_summary: R1389 §5.16 §5.7 §5.40: pinion-chart gains its first NON-value form — Timeline: labelled time Spans grouped into horizontal Lanes over a shared numeric time ruler, with a draggable playhead scrubber whose readout names the span under it per lane (a11y-mirrored via describedby_region, the R1355 parity). The track view an editor sequencer / capture-replay tool needs — gap #4 of the dataviz dashboard audit [[debt-dataviz-dashboard-substrate]]. It REUSES the crate's scale/ticks/palette/draw core wholesale (a span IS a box_node, the ruler a stroke_path, the readout the shared callout; redefines no leaf) — the 3rd+ consumer of that furniture, not a re-derive. build/build_fill layout-native pair like the charts. Forcing consumer examples/hello-timeline is a FLAME of the profiler's real streaming data (use_frame_timings, the seam hello-frame-profiler reads): the four disjoint render sub-phases (build/encode/acquire/render) abut end-to-end from each frame's cumulative-time offset, one lane per phase — measured, not synthetic. Audit-first found the debt note's 'retrofit the profiler into a live chart' directive already done at R1361; picked the genuinely-absent gap #4 instead. 15 crate tests + 8 consumer tests + r1389_frame_timeline.py (>=30 assertions, structural invariants on non-deterministic data over real windowed RPC).
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/timeline.rs`: NEW module — the crate's first non-value form. `Span{start,end,label,color?}` / `Lane{name,spans}` / `Timeline` builder. `build(rect)` + `build_fill(size)` layout-native pair (the R1360 contract), `with_x_domain` (brush-zoom / scrubbed-window) / `with_palette` / `with_tag_prefix` / `playhead(Option<f32>)`, and `playhead_readout()` for a11y parity. Tags: `timeline.{bg, axis.x (top ruler), axis.y (gutter edge), grid.x.N, tick.N, rule.N, lane.i.label, lane.i.span.j, playhead, playhead.tooltip/header/value.i}`. 15 unit tests.

REUSE, not re-derive: the time axis is `LinearScale`, the ruler `nice_ticks`/`tick_step`/`format_axis_tick`, every leaf a `crate::draw` primitive (`box_node`/`stroke_path`/`gridlines`/`label_node`/`callout`/`plot_rect`/`fill_parent`/`absolute`) — grep confirms it redefines none. The 3rd+ consumer of that shared furniture, so no lift owed (R727/R732).
`crates/pinion-chart/src/lib.rs`: `mod timeline` + `pub use timeline::{Lane, Span, Timeline}`; the `# Scope` doc gains the Timeline paragraph (first non-value / time form).

`examples/hello-timeline/` (NEW crate, registered in root `Cargo.toml` members): the forcing consumer — a FLAME of the profiler's real streaming data (`use_frame_timings`, R1361, the seam `hello-frame-profiler` reads). 4 phase lanes (build/encode/acquire/render) laid end-to-end from each frame's cumulative-time offset; a `SliderExternal` playhead scrub over a transparent capture surface (the `hello-scatter` idiom); manual a11y — the scrub Slider `describedby` the playhead readout region (the R1355 tooltip↔screen-reader parity). Pinned `build` (the `build_fill` seam is already proven by the profiler). 8 tests.

`tools/demos/r1389_frame_timeline.py`: the RPC verify (>=30 assertions) — the ruler + lane labels exist before any frame flows; driving real frames fills each phase lane with stacked, accumulating span boxes; the playhead overlay reads back as tagged data; and driving the playhead over `scene/intervene` moves its line right and changes its time header. Structural invariants only (the data is measured, not reproducible).
verification_bullets: `cargo test -p pinion-chart` (timeline module): 15 passed, 0 failed. `cargo test -p hello-timeline`: 8 passed, 0 failed. Full `cargo test --workspace -j2`: green.
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`: clean (`-D pedantic`; 3m08s cold).

`cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean (`-D warnings`) — one private-intra-doc-link caught locally (`playhead_readout` -> `active_at`) and fixed to a plain code span before commit, saving a hook round-trip [[cargo-doc-not-in-commit-gate]].
`cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.

`tools/demos/r1389_frame_timeline.py`: PASS (~4.3s, >=30 assertions) over real windowed RPC — the ruler + lane labels are present before any frame flows; driving real frames fills each of the 4 phase lanes with stacked, accumulating span boxes (`lane.0` above `lane.3`); the playhead overlay reads back as tagged data; and driving the playhead over `scene/intervene` moves its line right and changes its time header. All structural invariants (the data is measured, not reproducible run to run).

3rd-consumer self-grep (R727/R732 obligation): grep confirms the timeline redefines NO draw/scale helper — it is the 3rd+ consumer of `crate::draw` (`box_node`/`stroke_path`/`callout`/`label_node`/`gridlines`/`plot_rect`/`fill_parent`/`absolute`) and of `LinearScale`/`nice_ticks`/`tick_step`/`format_axis_tick`, reusing them. No mechanical triple-duplication introduced; no lift owed.

Audit-first (`[[verify-seed-claims-audit-first]]`): the debt note's bottom directive — "retrofit `hello-frame-profiler` into a live frame-time chart" — was verified ALREADY DONE at R1361 (+ histogram R1374, scrub R1375); that paragraph is stale. Picked the genuinely-absent gap #4 (timeline / playhead) instead.
carry_forward_bullets: The flame consumer's playhead reads AT MOST ONE lane at a given wall-clock (the four render phases are SEQUENTIAL within a frame, so only one is active at any instant) — HONEST, not a defect: it is the true reading of a single-threaded render loop ("at t, the loop was in frame N's acquire phase"). The substrate itself supports many-lanes-active: `active_at` collects every lane whose span contains the time; a future capture-replay / concurrent-lane consumer exercises that path.
Inclusive-endpoint semantics: at a phase boundary (one lane's span end == the next lane's span start) BOTH lanes report active. Honest at the seam; documented via `Span::contains`.

The consumer uses the PINNED `Timeline::build` (like `hello-scatter`), not the layout-native `build_fill` — the `build_fill` measured-rect seam is already proven by `hello-frame-profiler` / `hello-chart-fill`, so a const rect keeps the a11y-readout parity a one-liner. A DOCKED / resizable timeline consumer (build_fill) is a follow-up; the substrate ships both entry points.

§2 #6 (GUI/TUI dual) does not hold for the timeline, same as every chart: the ruler / gridlines / playhead are `Scene::Path` (not TUI-rendered); only the span boxes + text labels survive on TUI. Stated in the crate-level "Known limitations", not left silent.
`layered_layout`-style crate-lift NOT triggered: the timeline reuses the shared draw/scale core rather than adding a new duplicated helper (3rd-consumer self-grep clean).

Remaining Phase B dataviz gaps `[[debt-dataviz-dashboard-substrate]]` for future rounds: force-directed graph layout (#3, R1383 shipped layered only), numeric BRUSH-range cross-filter (#1, R1384 shipped categorical only), live-streaming chart feed (RepaintSink ready), hex/byte-dump viewer (#7, small `Scene::TextGrid` consumer), and dock/tab placement of `build_fill` charts (unproven — no dock-side `use_pane_viewport_size` consumer yet). Next round continues this roadmap.

R1390.decision_summary: R1390 §5.38 §5.52: a force-directed (Fruchterman-Reingold spring-electrical) organic auto-layout for the node graph — the AI-first peer of a pro editor's 'organic' arrange mode (yEd organic / Graphviz neato / Gephi ForceAtlas), the second layout mode beside R1383's layered 'tidy'. A NEW pure force_directed_layout(nodes, edges, origin) relaxes the graph into a compact symmetric cluster: every node repels every other by an inverse-distance electrical force (k^2/d), every edge springs its endpoints together (d^2/k), summed per step and moved at most a linearly-cooling temperature over a fixed FORCE_ITERS=200 iterations — annealed to a low-energy rest state. Deterministic (ZERO-FLAKE) like layered_layout: it reads only the node set + edges (never positions), seeds from a fixed grid in id order (no trigonometry, so the arithmetic is + - * / sqrt only and bit-identical across platforms), id-ordered accumulation with integer tie-breaks, so identical input yields an identical layout and a second pass is idempotent; the relaxed cloud is translated so its bbox top-left sits at origin. NodeGraphExternal::force_layout relaxes the WHOLE graph (no selection) in ONE undo step through the shared apply_node_moves SSOT, wired as invoke force_layout (the auto_layout precedent). Advances dataviz debt #3 'automatic graph layout' from layered-only to layered+organic — a self-grep confirmed no prior force-directed / spring code existed. The auto_layout/force_layout apply-skeleton is a 2-site mechanical duplication (deferred; a 3rd layout mode triggers the lift), and both layout functions stay example-local (1 graph consumer). Forced by hello-node-editor's force_layout verb + a NEW ~40-assertion RPC demo.
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-node-editor/src/main.rs`: a NEW pure `force_directed_layout(nodes, edges, origin) -> BTreeMap<NodeId,(x,y)>` (Fruchterman-Reingold spring-electrical) plus two helpers — `force_unit` (unit vector + floored distance, deterministic ±x fallback by id order when two nodes coincide, so no divide-by-zero) and `force_grid_cols` (ceil(sqrt(n)) grid-seed column count). Every node repels every other (k²/d), every edge springs its endpoints together (d²/k), summed per step and moved at most a linearly-cooling temperature over FORCE_ITERS=200 iterations. It reads only the node set + edges — never the stored x/y — grid-seeded in id order (no trigonometry, arithmetic is + − × ÷ √ only so it is bit-identical across platforms), id-ordered accumulation, so identical input yields an identical layout (deterministic, idempotent once applied). The relaxed cloud is translated so its bbox top-left sits at `origin`, then rounded via the existing `round_i32`. Constants FORCE_ITERS=200 / FORCE_K=190.0 (= NODE_W 130 + LAYER_GAP 60) / FORCE_EPS=1.0.

`examples/hello-node-editor/src/main.rs`: a NEW `NodeGraphExternal::force_layout()` — relaxes the WHOLE graph (no selection) into an organic cluster in ONE discrete undo step through the shared `apply_node_moves` SSOT (the R1383 `auto_layout` precedent, mirrored exactly), anchored at the graph's current bounding-box top-left. A no-op `false` on <2 nodes or when nothing moves (idempotent). Wired as the AI-first `invoke force_layout` verb (SchemaField + the `invoke_layout` arm beside `auto_layout`) and documented in the module header as the organic counterpart to the layered tidy.

`examples/hello-node-editor/src/tests.rs`: 9 NEW tests — 6 pure `force_directed_layout` (every node placed + bbox anchored at origin, deterministic + position-independent [reads only structure], an edge pulls its endpoints tighter than an isolated node, repulsion keeps every pair from coinciding, a 3-cycle terminates and places every node, force-vs-layered yield distinct arrangements) + 3 coordinator (scrambled graph relaxes in one undo step + undo restores; idempotent second pass moves nothing; `force_layout` dispatches via `invoke` and is schema-declared).

`tools/demos/r1390_node_force_layout.py` (NEW forcing consumer, 31 static assertions, ~40+ at runtime, over real windowed RPC): (A) boot taxonomy; (B) a scrambled seed graph relaxes so the two directly-wired pairs (0-2, 2-3) end tighter than the two-hop pair (0..3) and no two nodes coincide; (C) idempotent second pass = Bool false, positions unchanged; (D) one-undo-step + undo restores all four scrambled positions + redo re-applies; (E) position-independence — relaxing from two different scrambled bounding boxes yields the SAME anchor-free node-to-node offsets; (F) coexists with the layered mode — auto_layout re-columns (sources share layer-0), then force_layout returns to the same organic shape, proving the two modes are independent and each deterministic-from-structure.

R1391.decision_summary: R1391 §5.16 §5.7: the numeric BRUSH-range cross-filter — the continuous-range twin of R1384's categorical bar cross-filter. A NEW ScatterChart::select_x_range(Option<(f64,f64)>) mutes every point mark whose x falls OUTSIDE [lo,hi] (dimmed to the shared MUTED_ALPHA, but still DRAWN as context, unlike a pinned domain which drops out-of-domain points); None = no filter (every point full, the crossfilter convention that no selection = all data). MUTED_ALPHA was LIFTED from bar.rs to draw.rs at its 2nd consumer (the TOOLTIP_WIDTH precedent), so the categorical (bar) and numeric (scatter) cross-filter forms dim to the identical strength. examples/hello-scatter wires it CROSS-WIDGET: an overview brush strip (a RangeSliderExternal sibling in the R1249 extra_externals slot, tag scatter_brush, the hello-chart idiom) whose selected x-window drives the scatter's select_x_range — a numeric brush in one widget dims the corresponding points in another. Forced by hello-scatter + a NEW ~38-assertion RPC demo that drives the brush low/high over scene/intervene and reads each point's style.fill.a back over scene/snapshot, proving the filter mutes, keeps points DRAWN (not dropped), reverses on the opposite half, and resets. Advances dataviz debt #1: the numeric cross-filter leg lands; arbitrary chart-to-chart linking + a y-rescale-to-brush remain. The brush-external consumer wiring is now a 2-site dup (hello-chart + hello-scatter), deferred to a 3rd consumer per R732.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/draw.rs`: LIFTED `MUTED_ALPHA` (0x4D) here as a `pub(crate) const` — the cross-filter mute strength, previously a private const in `bar.rs`, now shared by the categorical `BarChart::select` (R1384) and the numeric `ScatterChart::select_x_range` (R1391) so the two forms dim identically. Lifted at the 2nd consumer, the `TOOLTIP_WIDTH` precedent (a shared semantic constant, not a code-pattern dup).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/scatter.rs`: a NEW `ScatterChart::select_x_range(Option<(f64,f64)>)` cross-filter (+ `select_x_range` field, `new()` init, and an `is_muted(px)` helper). With `Some((lo,hi))` every point whose x is OUTSIDE `[lo,hi]` (inclusive) renders muted (its fill dimmed to `MUTED_ALPHA`) while in-range points stay full; the muted points are still DRAWN (unlike a pinned domain, which drops out-of-domain points), so they stay on screen as context. `None` = no filter. The numeric-range, mark-level twin of `BarChart::select`. 3 new tests (mute-outside-and-keep-drawn, none=all-full, boundary-inclusive).
`crates/pinion-chart/src/bar.rs`: `MUTED_ALPHA` now imported from `crate::draw` (the local const + its doc removed); no behaviour change.

`crates/pinion-chart/src/lib.rs`: the Shipped scope now records the R1391 numeric cross-filter leg; the "Not yet" note drops the numeric-brush item (landed) and keeps arbitrary chart-to-chart linking + the y-rescale-to-brush.

`examples/hello-scatter/src/main.rs`: the forcing consumer — a NEW overview brush STRIP (a `RangeSliderExternal` sibling in the R1249 `extra_externals` slot, tag `scatter_brush`, the `hello-chart` idiom) whose selected x-window drives the scatter's `select_x_range`, so a numeric brush in one widget mutes the point marks in another (CROSS-widget). Adds `brush_extras` / `read_brush` / `x_extent` (the `data_bounds` SSOT) / `brush_domain` / `brush_strip`; the widget state grows to `(SliderState, f32, f32, f32)` (scrub + brush low/high) with `extra_externals = brush_extras`; the a11y `access_node` gains a brush `AccessNode` (Slider role + `AccessValue::Text` x-window, the `hello-chart` parity); `CHART_RECT` shrank to make room for the strip. 3 new tests (mute-out-of-range-but-keep-drawn, full-brush=no-filter, brush-strip-present-and-announced); the existing R1377 scrub tests + demo re-verified.

`tools/demos/r1391_brush_filter.py` (NEW forcing consumer, ~38 assertions over real windowed RPC): (A) boot = 16 points all full + brush strip present + full window; (B) brush the lower half (`intervene /scatter_brush/external/high`) mutes the high-x points (each point's `style.fill.a` drops) while all 16 stay DRAWN (mute != drop); (C) brush the upper half REVERSES the filter; (D) reset to full span returns every point to full — the whole round-trip driven over `scene/intervene` and read back over `scene/snapshot` (§2 #7, §2 #2).

R1391.publishable_decision_summary: R1391 §5.16 §5.7: the numeric BRUSH-range cross-filter — the continuous-range twin of R1384's categorical bar cross-filter. A NEW ScatterChart::select_x_range(Option<(f64,f64)>) mutes every point mark whose x falls OUTSIDE [lo,hi] (dimmed to the shared MUTED_ALPHA, but still DRAWN as context, unlike a pinned domain which drops out-of-domain points); None = no filter (every point full, the crossfilter convention that no selection = all data). MUTED_ALPHA was LIFTED from bar.rs to draw.rs at its 2nd consumer (the TOOLTIP_WIDTH precedent), so the categorical (bar) and numeric (scatter) cross-filter forms dim to the identical strength. examples/hello-scatter wires it CROSS-WIDGET: an overview brush strip (a RangeSliderExternal sibling in the R1249 extra_externals slot, tag scatter_brush, the hello-chart idiom) whose selected x-window drives the scatter's select_x_range — a numeric brush in one widget dims the corresponding points in another. Forced by hello-scatter + a NEW ~38-assertion RPC demo that drives the brush low/high over scene/intervene and reads each point's style.fill.a back over scene/snapshot, proving the filter mutes, keeps points DRAWN (not dropped), reverses on the opposite half, and resets. Advances dataviz debt #1: the numeric cross-filter leg lands; arbitrary chart-to-chart linking + a y-rescale-to-brush remain. The brush-external consumer wiring is now a 2-site dup (hello-chart + hello-scatter), deferred to a 3rd consumer per R732.

Lifted at the 2nd consumer, the `TOOLTIP_WIDTH` precedent (a shared semantic constant, not a code-pattern dup).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/scatter.rs`: a NEW `ScatterChart::select_x_range(Option<(f64,f64)>)` cross-filter (+ `select_x_range` field, `new()` init, and an `is_muted(px)` helper). With `Some((lo,hi))` every point whose x is OUTSIDE `[lo,hi]` (inclusive) renders muted (its fill dimmed to `MUTED_ALPHA`) while in-range points stay full; the muted points are still DRAWN (unlike a pinned domain, which drops out-of-domain points), so they stay on screen as context. `None` = no filter. R1392.decision_summary: R1392 §5.38 §5.39: the ARBITRARY chart-to-chart cross-filter — a chart type OTHER than the two existing selectors (bar-click R1384, brush R1391) drives a filter on a DIFFERENT chart type. A NEW ScatterChart::interactive_legend(tags) makes the scatter's own legend a cross-filter SELECTOR (focusable, caller-tagged entries, the R1380 chip mechanism), and the interactive-legend chip emission was LIFTED from line.rs's interactive_legend_entries to a shared draw::interactive_legend_row at its 2nd consumer (line + scatter now emit one identical interactive legend). Forcing consumer examples/hello-linked-legend: a scatter (interactive-legend selector) + a companion line chart (pure target), sharing ONE toggle_group visibility state — clicking a scatter legend entry hides that series in BOTH charts (a selection in one widget reshapes a DIFFERENT chart type). Distinct tag prefixes (scatter./line.) keep the two charts' nodes apart; the line has no legend of its own, so no LEGEND_TAG is claimed twice (one selector, one target). 3 crate tests + 5 consumer tests + a 32-assertion RPC demo; the R1380 line-legend demo re-verified (the lift is behaviour-identical). Advances dataviz debt #1: the arbitrary-chart-to-chart leg lands; a numeric cross-TYPE cross-filter and the y-rescale-to-brush leg remain.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/draw.rs`: a NEW shared `interactive_legend_row(entries: &[(Color, String, bool)], tags, start_x, row_y, style)` — the INTERACTIVE (focusable, caller-tagged, hit-testable) legend, the clickable twin of the static `legend_row`. LIFTED from `line.rs`'s `interactive_legend_entries` at its 2nd consumer (line + scatter), so both charts emit one identical chart-owned interactive legend (a `Container([swatch, label])` per series, tagged with the caller's `tags[i]`, greyed + dimmed when the series is hidden) rather than each re-deriving the R1380 chip geometry.

`crates/pinion-chart/src/line.rs`: `interactive_legend_entries` now maps its series to `(color, name, visible)` and delegates to `crate::draw::interactive_legend_row` (behaviour-identical); the now-unused legend-chip imports (`BoxNode` / `TextNode` / `AlignItems` / `BoxStyle` / `FlexDirection` / `LayoutStyle` / `Size` / `TextStyle` / `LEGEND_SLOT`) were dropped.

`crates/pinion-chart/src/scatter.rs`: a NEW `ScatterChart::interactive_legend(tags)` (+ `legend_tags` field, `new()` init) — makes the scatter's own legend a cross-filter SELECTOR (the scatter counterpart of `LineChart::interactive_legend`, sharing the lifted helper). `legend()` now branches: interactive tagged entries when opted in, else the static row. 3 new tests (focusable tagged entries + no static row when interactive; static row otherwise; a hidden series keeps its interactive entry).

`examples/hello-linked-legend/` (NEW example — Cargo.toml + build.rs + app.pinion.xml + src/main.rs, workspace member added): the forcing consumer. A SCATTER with an interactive legend (the selector, tag prefix `scatter.`) + a companion LINE chart (a pure target, tag prefix `line.`, no legend of its own so no duplicate LEGEND_TAG), sharing ONE `toggle_group` per-series visibility state (the 6th+ consumer of `toggle_group`, verbatim `boot_toggle` / `extra_toggles` / `read_toggle` / `apply_key` / `toggle_button_group_nodes`). Clicking a scatter legend entry hides that series in BOTH charts — a selection in one widget reshaping a DIFFERENT chart type. 5 tests.

`tools/demos/r1392_linked_legend.py` (NEW forcing consumer, 32 static assertions over real windowed RPC): (A) boot = both charts full (3 `scatter.point.{i}.*` + 3 `line.series.{i}`) + 3 focusable `legend_{i}` entries, all toggles ON; (B) a coordinate-click on scatter legend entry 1 hides series 1 in BOTH the scatter AND the line, the other two surviving in both; (C) click ON again returns it to both; (D) entry 0 off is independent; (E) keyboard — each entry is a Tab stop, Space toggles only the focused series, in both charts.

R1393.decision_summary: R1393 §5.7 §5.12 PINION-PR67: the RPC ingress gains connection identity + lifecycle so a stateful ingress can keep per-connection state crash-safely (the sprag detach-on-destroy no-detached / list-clients consumer-forced seam). R-67.1: every RpcFrame now carries a ConnId — a process-unique, opaque, monotonic lifecycle token (a fresh 64-bit counter via ConnId::allocate) the transport stamps on each frame — so a stateful ingress (one dispatch owner serving many connections) attributes a frame to its originating connection; RpcFrame::new takes the conn, and both stdin transports stamp their single stable id. R-67.2: RpcIngress gains on_connect/on_disconnect default-no-op hooks; the Unix-socket transport allocates a ConnId per accepted connection, fires on_connect before the reader loop, and fires on_disconnect when the reader loop ends however the client dies (EOF/reset/crash) — the crash-safe cleanup edge, before the writer teardown so it fires within a bounded time, and after every submit for that conn (the documented happens-before). Request/response semantics and wire form are unchanged (no server-push, no auth — ConnId is a lifecycle token, not identity); existing consumers (GUI ProxyRpcIngress, TUI stdin drain, the roundtrip Echo/Silent ingresses) keep the default no-op hooks and compile unchanged. Proven by two new pinion-rpc-transport integration tests (one connection's ordered connect/frames/disconnect on one id; two concurrent connections get distinct ids and closing one fires only that one's disconnect) and a new reference consumer example hello-conn-lifecycle + r1393 demo that drives real AF_UNIX socket connect/disconnect and reads the crash-safe "N connections attached" count + live ids back as scene-as-data over a second (stdin) transport.

R1395.decision_summary: R1395 §5.16 §5.7: numeric DIFFERENT-geometry cross-filter — the completing leg of the cross-filter matrix after categorical bar-click (R1384), numeric same-type scatter (R1391) + line (R1394), and arbitrary legend (R1392). A single numeric x-window brush now cross-filters TWO UNLIKE GEOMETRIES at once: a ScatterChart mutes its out-of-window points (R1391) and a BarChart histogram mutes the BINS whose numeric [lo,hi) extent falls outside the window (BarChart::select_x_range, new in R1395 — a numeric brush over a categorical bar layout). Bar gains an optional Bar::bin (Option<(f64,f64)>) + with_bin(lo,hi): a bar declaring a bin [blo,bhi) mutes to MUTED_ALPHA when the bin does not overlap the window (blo>=hi || bhi<=lo); a binless bar is never x-muted, a full-span window is a natural no-op, and muted bars stay DRAWN as context — the same shape as the scatter's per-point is_muted. It is orthogonal to the categorical select (R1384): either dims a bar (AND-of-inclusions crossfilter semantics). The forcing consumer examples/hello-histogram-brush drives ONE x-window brush (the 4th consumer of the R1394 pinion_chart::Brush substrate — a CALL to the SSOT, no new lift) that cross-filters a ScatterChart (top) and a BarChart histogram (bottom), re-prefixed scatter.*/hist.* so tags never collide; both share x-axis [0,12] with a point at bucket centre k+0.5 and its bin [k,k+1), so an integer-edged window classifies a point and its bin identically. A ~50-assertion RPC demo drives the brush over scene/intervene and reads both panels' style.fill.a back over scene/snapshot, asserting per-bucket that the bin and point carry the SAME alpha (§2 #7, §2 #2). R1396.decision_summary: R1396 §5.16 §5.49 §5.51: dock-placed chart PROVEN + narrow-pane clamp. examples/hello-dock-chart is the forcing consumer the pinion-chart debt note called for — a LineChart::build_fill inside a view_dock_surface pane, keyed on use_pane_viewport_size of a tag nested two containers deep (the dock's splitter container -> the panel's #content wrapper -> the chart root). The shell's post-layout publish_pane_viewports walks the laid-out scene for that tag through the dock containers and writes its measured rect, so the docked chart re-scales on a window scene/resize AND on a splitter scene/drag (the dock-native resize the window path cannot exercise), clearing the 'dock/tab placement is UNPROVEN — do not assert it' flag for DOCK placement. It also forces R1396's narrow-pane containment clamp: a window absorbs a chart's legend + last-tick overhang in its own padding, a dock pane paints it over the neighbour. draw.rs gains centered_label_x (clamps a centred tick label inside the chart — line/scatter/timeline, the 3-consumer lift) and legend_fit (shrinks the legend slot from LEGEND_SLOT toward LEGEND_MIN_SLOT, then drops the tail into a tagged +N marker, .legend.overflow, when even the minimum will not fit); label_node now emits TextOverflow::Clip so a squeezed label scissors instead of bleeding. A 40-assertion RPC demo drives both resize paths and asserts the legend collapses to +N while every x-tick label's right edge stays inside the chart, over scene/snapshot (§2 #2, §2 #7). Wide charts are byte-unchanged (the clamp only moves a label that would overhang; the legend still seats every entry at the preferred slot when it fits).
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-dock-chart/` (NEW forcing consumer): a `pinion-chart` `LineChart::build_fill` lives inside a `view_dock_surface` dock pane (left leaf `chart-pane`), keyed on `use_pane_viewport_size(CHART_TAG)` where `CHART_TAG` is nested two containers deep (the dock's splitter container -> the panel's `{panel}#content` wrapper -> the chart root). R1397.decision_summary: R1397 §5.16 §5.7: the chart y-axis auto-fits the brushed x-window. LineChart::rescale_y_to_x_window(true) makes an auto y-domain measure only the points whose x falls inside the resolved x-domain, so pairing it with a brush that with_x_domain-zooms the chart lets the y-axis zoom in on just that window's values — the canonical "auto-scale Y to the visible X range" of a monitoring chart (an oscilloscope zoom). It is the orthogonal twin of R1381's rescale_to_visible (which picks which SERIES the axes measure): this windows the y-fit to the visible X-RANGE. The two rescale opt-ins are bundled into a named-field pinion-chart plot::Rescale so the two booleans can never be swapped at a resolve() call site (the R832-class silent-swap the crate has been bitten by). series::bounds_in_x_window is the new auto-y-fit source (bounds_of gained an x-window filter, shared with data_bounds / visible_data_bounds). examples/hello-autoscale-y is the forcing consumer: one signal — a large startup transient (x=2, y=5000) over a long steady state of small ripples — charted with the brush as its PRIMARY external (the manual hello-range-slider shape, so no fifth copy of the scrub wiring); brushing past the transient re-domains x AND fits the y-axis to the window, so ripples that were a flat line at the bottom expand to fill the plot and the y-tick labels fall from thousands to tens. A 32-assertion RPC demo drives the brush over /external/low|high and reads the rescale back as data over scene/snapshot (§2 #2, §2 #7).
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-chart/src/series.rs`: `bounds_of` gains an `Option<(f64,f64)>` x-window filter (points outside it are skipped); NEW `pub bounds_in_x_window(series, window) -> Option<Bounds>` measures the y-extent over the in-window points (the auto-y-fit source), sharing the one scan with `data_bounds` / `visible_data_bounds` (both now pass `None`). `None` when the window holds no point (the caller keeps the full-data y). 3 new tests (windowed y fits the ripples off the transient / order-agnostic + inclusive / empty-window `None`).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/plot.rs`: NEW `pub(crate) Rescale { to_visible, y_to_x_window }` (`Default` = both false) bundles the two orthogonal auto-domain opt-ins into named fields, so `CartesianPlot::resolve` takes one `Rescale` instead of two positional bools (the R832-class swap guard). `resolve` settles the x-domain FIRST, then — when `y_to_x_window` and y is auto — fits `raw_y` to `bounds_in_x_window(series, dom_x)`; a pinned `y_domain` still wins, an empty window falls back to the full bounds. 1 new test (fit snaps y to the window / full-width window is a no-op / empty window keeps full-data y / pinned y wins).

`crates/pinion-chart/src/line.rs`: NEW `LineChart::rescale_y_to_x_window(bool)` builder + field; a private `rescale()` bundles the two flags into a `Rescale` for the two `resolve()` call sites (`build_body` + `inspect_readout`) so they resolve identical domains.

R1397.publishable_decision_summary: R1397 §5.16 §5.7: the chart y-axis auto-fits the brushed x-window. LineChart::rescale_y_to_x_window(true) makes an auto y-domain measure only the points whose x falls inside the resolved x-domain, so pairing it with a brush that with_x_domain-zooms the chart lets the y-axis zoom in on just that window's values — the canonical "auto-scale Y to the visible X range" of a monitoring chart (an oscilloscope zoom). It is the orthogonal twin of R1381's rescale_to_visible (which picks which SERIES the axes measure): this windows the y-fit to the visible X-RANGE. The two rescale opt-ins are bundled into a named-field pinion-chart plot::Rescale so the two booleans can never be swapped at a resolve() call site (the R832-class silent-swap the crate has been bitten by). series::bounds_in_x_window is the new auto-y-fit source (bounds_of gained an x-window filter, shared with data_bounds / visible_data_bounds). examples/hello-autoscale-y is the forcing consumer: one signal — a large startup transient (x=2, y=5000) over a long steady state of small ripples — charted with the brush as its PRIMARY external (the manual hello-range-slider shape, so no fifth copy of the scrub wiring); brushing past the transient re-domains x AND fits the y-axis to the window, so ripples that were a flat line at the bottom expand to fill the plot and the y-tick labels fall from thousands to tens. A 32-assertion RPC demo drives the brush over /external/low|high and reads the rescale back as data over scene/snapshot (§2 #2, §2 #7).

R1399.decision_summary: R1399 §5.41 §5.16 §5.12: the terminal cell underline gains a STYLE axis and a COLOUR (sprag PINION-PR68 consumer-forced seam). CellAttrs.underline is no longer a bool but the closed ECMA-48 SGR 4:x UnderlineStyle enum (none/single/double/curly/dotted/dashed — the axis the R974.1 forward-compat hedge named), and TermCell gains an orthogonal underline_color: Option<TermColor> (SGR 58 set / 59 reset; None tracks the foreground, Some is explicit). The forcing case is an editor's LSP diagnostics — a red-curly error vs a blue-dotted spellcheck — which without this flatten to one indistinguishable rule. Vello paints all five styles (double=a second rule, curly=a quadratic-bezier undercurl, dotted/dashed=explicit short segments) in the resolved underline colour; the ratatui TUI collapses every style to its one UNDERLINED modifier plus 0.29 underline_color (best approximation). scene/snapshot reports attrs.underline as a self-describing string discriminator (mirroring the cursor shape) and a run-level underline_color resolved like fg/bg, so an AI client discovers the SGR 4:x axis from a snapshot (§2 #7). R1400.decision_summary: R1400 §5.41 §5.16 §5.12: a hex/byte-dump viewer over Scene::TextGrid — the classic offset|hex|ascii dump — with a byte-range Brush that highlights a selected field across BOTH the hex column and the ascii gutter at once. A byte appears in two disjoint cell regions of one grid (its two hex digits + its one ascii char), so field selection must light both together or read as two unrelated smears; a primary Brush (R1394, this being its fifth consumer) over the byte offsets [0,N] paints an rgb background on every selected byte's two hex cells AND its one ascii cell, leaving the rest default — the cross-filter matrix (R1384-R1398) extended to a NEW hex geometry, the field selection a protocol inspector (Wireshark, a dlt trace) or a hex editor draws. Pure composition of the existing cell model (no framework seam forced — none was missing): the second real Scene::TextGrid data consumer after hello-grid-pointer (R1008). The highlight is cell background so scene/snapshot grid_rows reports it as data (no OCR), and the primary HexDumpOracle (/external/*) exposes byte_count/bytes_per_row/row_count/total_cols + invoke oracles hex_cell/ascii_cell/byte_window so the byte<->cell mapping is read, not guessed. Closes dataviz gap #7.
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-hex-dump` (NEW): a hex/byte-dump viewer over `Scene::TextGrid` — a fixed 128-byte buffer rendered as the classic offset|hex|ascii dump (8 rows x 78 cols at the 8x16 CellMetric::DEFAULT), the second real cell-projection consumer after `hello-grid-pointer`. `hex_dump_buffer` composes the offset column, `8 + 8` hex pairs (a group gap splits the two halves), and an ascii gutter (each non-printable byte shown as `.` in a muted tint) from `TermCell`s; nothing new in the framework — pure composition of the existing cell model + Brush.

The novel capability: a two-region LINKED highlight. A byte appears in two disjoint cell regions (its two hex digits + its one ascii char), so selecting a field must light BOTH. A primary `Brush` (R1394) over the byte offsets `[0, N]` is the fifth consumer of that substrate; its window `[lo, hi)` (via `selected_bytes`, the round's SSOT) paints an `rgb` background on every selected byte's two hex cells AND its one ascii cell, leaving the rest `default` — the cross-filter matrix (R1384-R1398) extended to a NEW hex geometry, the field selection a protocol inspector (Wireshark / a `dlt` trace) or a hex editor draws.

`HexDumpOracle` (primary external, `/external/*`): the layout as introspectable data so the byte<->cell mapping is read, not guessed — `query` byte_count / bytes_per_row / row_count / total_cols, and invoke oracles `hex_cell` / `ascii_cell` (byte index -> `"col,row"`, or `"none"` past the buffer) + `byte_window` (`"low,high"` fractions -> `"lo,hi"` byte range, the same `selected_bytes` SSOT the view paints from). The brush is the sibling extra (`create_extra_externals`, tag `hex_brush`), drag- and RPC-driven, seeded at boot to the payload field (bytes 8..24) so the linked highlight shows before any drag.

`tools/demos/r1400_hex_dump.py` (NEW, 60+ assertions > R660 baseline): reads the highlight from `scene/snapshot from=paint` `grid_rows` (a selected cell's run carries an `rgb` `bg`) and asserts two invariants — global (the count of rgb-background cells is exactly `3 * (hi - lo)`, two hex + one ascii per byte, nothing else tinted) and per-byte via the oracle (a sampled byte's `hex_cell` AND `ascii_cell` BOTH resolve rgb when selected, both default otherwise — proving the SAME byte is lit in both regions, not a neighbour). Drives windows over RPC (`/hex_brush/external/{low,high}`): the length field spanning the group gap, a window crossing a row boundary, the full buffer, and a last-row interior window.
`Cargo.toml`: registers the `examples/hello-hex-dump` workspace member.

The 12 new `hello-hex-dump` unit tests cover the column layout (`hex_col`/`ascii_col` two 8-byte groups + gutter bars), the sample header, the buffer dims, offset/hex/ascii rendering, the non-printable `.` substitution, the two-region linked highlight (both hex cells + the ascii cell tinted, bytes outside default), the `selected_bytes` SSOT (full/half/boot/reversed), and the oracle mappings + read-only guards.

`HexDumpOracle` (primary external, `/external/*`): the layout as introspectable data so the byte<->cell mapping is read, not guessed — `query` byte_count / bytes_per_row / row_count / total_cols, and invoke oracles `hex_cell` / `ascii_cell` (byte index -> `"col,row"`, or `"none"` past the buffer) + `byte_window` (`"low,high"` fractions -> `"lo,hi"` byte range, the same `selected_bytes` SSOT the view paints from). The brush is the sibling extra (`create_extra_externals`, tag `hex_brush`), drag- and RPC-driven, seeded at boot to the payload field (bytes 8..24) so the linked highlight shows before any drag.

R1402.decision_summary: R1402 §5.41 §5.49 §5.12: R1401's single-byte click cursor generalises into a press-drag byte-range SELECTION — the hex-editor's select-bytes gesture, of which a plain click is now the collapsed single-byte case (R1401 subsumed, no regression). A press latches an anchor byte, each drag move extends the focus, and the range [start, end) reverse-videos (R974) while the focus byte rings with a GridCursor (R975). Two orthogonal channels ride each byte's cells: the R1400 brush fills the background, the selection reverse-videos. HexDumpOracle owns the selection: wants_pointer_capture keeps forwarding pointer_move under the held drag, and the router delivers PointerDown/PointerUp via invoke(send) — the first example consumer of the R884 press/release channel outside the SCXML widget catalogue (proven by the r1402 second-drag-starts-fresh assertion: a missed PointerDown would extend the first). An AI client selects with no pixel via invoke select_range 'start,end' and reads it back at selection_start/end/len/hex; selection_hex (the bytes a hex editor copies) is cross-checked against the hex the grid paints, so the readout and the paint can never diverge. Reuses the R1008 CellMetric::px_to_cell substrate (second consumer, from R1401).
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-hex-dump/src/main.rs`: R1401's single-byte click cursor GENERALISES into a press-drag byte-range SELECTION — the hex-editor's select-bytes gesture, of which a plain click is now the collapsed single-byte case (R1401 subsumed, no regression). Two orthogonal visual channels ride each byte's cells: the R1400 brush fills the background, the R1402 selection reverse-videos (R974 `reverse` attr, painted by R991) — a byte can be in both (the two selections are independent gestures: the minimap field vs the direct byte selection).

`Selection { start, end, focus }` (NEW) is the drag range `[start, end)` with the drag's live end at `focus` (the byte the `GridCursor` rings). `HexDumpOracle` becomes stateful over `selection: Option<(anchor, focus)>` + `pending_anchor`: `wants_pointer_capture` keeps forwarding `pointer_move` under the held drag, and the router delivers `PointerDown` / `PointerUp` via `invoke("send", ...)` — a `PointerDown` latches a fresh anchor for the next move, so a press starts a new selection and each subsequent move extends the focus (a non-byte cell deselects a fresh press but is ignored mid-drag, so dragging over the gutter never collapses the range). This is the R1008 `CellMetric::px_to_cell` substrate's continued reuse (second consumer, from R1401) plus the R884 `invoke("send")` press/release channel's first example consumer outside the SCXML widget catalogue.

Oracle surface: query gains `selection_start` / `selection_end` / `selection_len` / `selection_hex` (the selected bytes as a lowercase hex string — what a hex editor copies); `cursor_byte` / `cursor_value` / `cursor_cell` now report the FOCUS byte. Intervene `cursor_byte` sets a collapsed selection (R1401 compat). Invoke gains `select_range "start,end"` (the AI-first no-pixel range write, `InvokeError::Rejected` on an empty / out-of-range range) and `send` (handling the router's PointerDown/Up/Leave/Cancel). R1403.decision_summary: R1403 §5.41 §5.12: the terminal cell gains an OSC-8 hyperlink target (sprag PINION-PR69 consumer-forced seam). TermCell gains hyperlink: Option<HyperlinkId> — an index into a NEW per-GridBuffer interning table (Vec<Hyperlink> where Hyperlink { uri, id }), the OSC-8 analogue of how TermColor::Indexed references a Palette, so a link spanning hundreds of cells stores its URI once (R-69.2) rather than cloning it per cell. The optional OSC-8 id is the grouping key: two NON-adjacent runs sharing an id are ONE logical link — a link split across a soft-wrap, or repeated — which pure position-based highlighting cannot express (R-69.3.b). The forcing case is a compiler / ls --hyperlink / doc renderer emitting clickable file/URL links a real terminal turns into underline + hover + click-to-open; termwiz already parses OSC 8 fully (SetHyperlink -> Hyperlink { uri, params }) but the cell model had nowhere to keep it — the same "cell model cannot hold what the VT parser already parsed" class as PR68, and the exact field the R974.1 #[non_exhaustive] hedge named. scene/snapshot resolves each run's index through the buffer table (a paint-time readback, like colour resolution) and reports a hyperlink object ({uri, id} or null); the index joins the run-coalescing key so a link boundary splits a run and same-index adjacent cells coalesce, and an AI client discovers the OSC-8 axis and recognises two runs as one link by a shared id from a snapshot alone (§2 #7). Delivered as the pinion-side cell DATA MODEL + $schema discoverability ONLY (R-69.1 + R-69.2); the live hover-highlight of the id-group + click -> URI activation (R-69.3.a/c) is the next slice on the hex-dump-oracle pattern, and sprag adapts in its own native round. Additive and backward-compatible: #[serde(default)] on both TermCell.hyperlink and GridBuffer.hyperlinks keeps the readback compatible, and the validating deserialize rejects an out-of-range cell index (fail-fast, mirroring the existing cell-count invariant). No new Vello/TUI paint this round — the link affordance reuses the R1399 underline attr a producer sets on linked cells.

NEW `TermCell.hyperlink: Option<HyperlinkId>` (`#[serde(default)]`, the R974.1 hedge's named example) + `with_hyperlink` builder; `blank`/`new` default it to `None` and `trailer()` inherits the head's link (a wide link glyph is one target). NEW `GridBuffer.hyperlinks: Vec<Hyperlink>` interning table (`#[serde(default)]`) + `with_hyperlinks` builder + `hyperlink(id)` accessor (the OSC-8 `Palette::indexed`). The validating `TryFrom<GridBufferWire>` gains a fail-fast guard: every cell's hyperlink index must address the table (so a resolved lookup never dangles), mirroring the cell-count invariant. The bool-free wire change is intended — sprag constructs `GridBuffer` in Rust (path-dep), not over serde, so there is no persisted-payload break; `#[serde(default)]` on both `TermCell.hyperlink` and `GridBuffer.hyperlinks` keeps the readback additive.

R1404.decision_summary: R1404 §5.16 §5.22: a producer-supplied in-memory image source for Scene::Image (sprag PINION-PR70 consumer-forced seam). Before R1404 an ImageNode.source was a filesystem path only (ImageCache::resolve -> std::fs::read), so a producer that decoded an image at runtime — a terminal's Kitty-graphics / sixel raster, an app-generated bitmap — had no way to hand pinion those pixels, and the VT parser's already-fully-parsed Sixel / KittyImage escapes were dropped for want of a render path. R1404 adds MemoryImageStore: a producer-registered, mutable, Send+Sync store (Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String,ImageData>>>) with insert(key,&DecodedImage) / remove / contains / len, exposed as an inherited ProviderSlot (IMAGE_STORE) the shell seeds at root and a producer resolves through use_image_store. ImageCache gains with_store + a memory://<key> resolve arm that reads the store FRESH each frame (NOT the decode-once entries map — the store is mutable, so a re-register / remove is visible on the next paint, the Kitty animation / retransmit / delete a terminal image needs). The store is an Arc handle, not a cache field, because the painter rebuilds its cache freely (fresh per headless call, per-window live) so a registration must outlive any one cache — the WINDOW_CONTROL_SINK / WAITER_REGISTRY idiom, the binding-registered store the PR asked for. It is seeded in ShellCore::new_with_seed beside the other root-DRIVEN slots so ShellCore::new alone (the PINION_SCREENSHOT headless path) is wired too; every WindowSlot::build and try_headless_screenshot builds its cache off the seeded store, so a memory:// source paints GPU-backed and headless alike (the headless-render-valid north-star). Delivered as the pinion-side SEAM only: a pinion example (hello-memory-image) proves it, an RPC demo (37 assertions) + an #[ignore]d lavapipe pixel guard verify it; the sprag-side vertical (sixel / Kitty payload decode, placement model, Container[TextGrid, Image] compositing) is a large sprag-native effort registered as sprag debt, per cross-repo discipline. Additive and backward-compatible: ImageCache::new (no store) resolves only filesystem sources and a memory:// source there paints nothing (graceful); https:// stays the one un-wired Scene::Image scheme.
changes_bullets: `pinion-runtime/src/image_cache.rs`: NEW `MemoryImageStore` — a producer-registered, mutable, `Send + Sync` in-memory image store (`Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, ImageData>>>`) with `insert(key, &DecodedImage)` / `remove` / `contains` / `len` / `is_empty` and a `pub(crate) get`; poisoned locks recover (no panic in the paint path). NEW `MEMORY_SCHEME` const (`"memory://"`). `ImageCache` gains an optional `store` + `with_store` ctor; `resolve` intercepts a `memory://<key>` source and reads it from the store FRESH each frame (NOT the decode-once `entries` map — the store is mutable), returning `None` gracefully when absent or storeless. NEW `IMAGE_STORE: ProviderSlot<MemoryImageStore>` (`inherited`, `provider_slot_tests!` verdict) + `use_image_store` / `resolve_image_store` hooks. `insert_decoded` doc corrected (the `memory://` path is now the store).

`pinion-runtime/src/core_shell.rs`: `new_with_seed` (and thus `ShellCore::new`) seeds `IMAGE_STORE.seed_root(root_owner)` beside the other root-DRIVEN slots (`LOCAL_TASK_PUMP` / pane registry) — vello-gated with the module — so a `create_external` registration and the per-window cache land on the ONE store, and the `PINION_SCREENSHOT` headless path is seeded too.

`pinion-runtime/src/lib.rs`: re-export `MEMORY_SCHEME` / `MemoryImageStore` / `resolve_image_store` / `use_image_store` (vello-gated) and `DecodedImage` (ungated, the store's `insert` param type — the `LayoutCache` rationale) at the crate root.

`pinion-shell/src/app.rs`: `WindowSlot::build` takes a `MemoryImageStore` and builds its `ImageCache::with_store`; both resume call sites resolve it off `root_owner`. The `PINION_SCREENSHOT` `try_headless_screenshot` builds its cache off the seeded store too (headless render valid).

`examples/hello-memory-image` (NEW): a `MemoryImageOracle` (primary external) resolves `use_image_store()`, registers a procedurally-generated four-quadrant RGBA image (no file) under `memory://tile`, and swaps / removes / restores it via `invoke send` / `intervene variant|present`; the view emits `Scene::Image { source: "memory://tile" }`. Introspects `image_source` / `variant` / `present` / `registered` / `width` / `height`.

`pinion-shell/src/headless_screenshot.rs`: NEW `#[ignore]d` lavapipe pixel guard `r1404_memory_scheme_image_paints_and_mutates` — a `memory://` image floods the rect, a re-register shows the new pixels, a remove paints the base (the GPU witness the `gpu-tests` CI job runs).

`tools/demos/r1404_memory_image.py` (NEW, 30+ assertions): the scene declares `source: "memory://tile"` and the node STAYS put across every mutation (only the pixels move, invisible to a snapshot); the oracle reports the store state a snapshot cannot; `invoke send swap/remove/restore` and `intervene variant/present` drive it, read back at `variant` / `present` / `registered`.

R1405.decision_summary: R1405 §5.41 §5.35: OSC-8 hyperlink hover / click interaction over a Scene::TextGrid (sprag PINION-PR71, the R-69.3 layer on the R1403 hyperlink data model). Before R1405 a TextGrid drew its OSC-8 links as plain styled text: no hover affordance, no id-group highlight, no click activation, and no way for a widget to even know WHICH cell a plain hover was over (the router forwards intra-widget position only under a capture-lock, not on free hover). R1405 adds the seam that closes all three (R-71.1/.2/.3), reusing the R1403 data + the hex-dump oracle pattern. Framework additions (minimal): (1) CursorHint::Pointer — the pointing-hand affordance a node declares via LayoutStyle::with_cursor, forcing the shell's exhaustive cursor_icon_for_hint to map it to winit CursorIcon::Pointer (the R1190 cross-crate exhaustiveness); (2) External::wants_hover_move (default false) — opt into pointer_move on a plain hover, the wants_pointer_capture sibling, so the router forwards each hover move's widget-relative position (cached per-pointer on the Enter as hover_wants_move, forwarded after refresh_hover so moves WITHIN one target are forwarded too, where refresh_hover early-returns); (3) GridBuffer::cell_hyperlink(col,row) — the cell -> index -> table pointer-hit resolution in one step (the R972-deferred convenience the click round now consumes). The hover highlight + cursor are producer RE-PROJECTION, not framework TextGrid paint: the hello-hyperlink HyperlinkOracle tracks the hovered cell (frac_to_px -> px_to_cell -> cell_hyperlink) and the view reverse-videos the hovered link's whole id-group (a wrap-split link lights on both rows, the grouping a position-based highlight cannot express) + sets the grid node's CursorHint::Pointer while a link is hovered; a click (the R1401 press channel) or invoke activate records the activated URI, which the consumer (sprag) opens — pinion owns the affordance + the hit/activation seam, not the opening. Two R727 3rd-consumer lifts fell out: CellMetric::frac_to_px (three grid-pointer examples' byte-identical private copy) and widget_flag/widget_flag_walk (three identical capture/cancel/hover-move scene walks). Purely additive: wants_hover_move defaults false so the capture-only forwarding is byte-unchanged, and a widget that never opts in pays only the Enter/Leave it already got.

R1406.decision_summary: R1406 §5.35: a LineChart inspector crosshair that follows the BARE hover (no button), the 2nd consumer of the R1405 External::wants_hover_move seam (the first is R1405's HyperlinkOracle, a TextGrid cell highlighter). Proves the hover-move seam serves a structurally-unrelated consumer with ZERO framework change — the strongest form of abstraction-needs-second-consumer. Before R1405 a chart got a continuous pointer position only under pointer capture (a button-held drag), so hello-chart's scrub inspector fakes the crosshair with a captured SliderExternal. R1406 adds hello-crosshair: a CrosshairExternal opts into wants_hover_move but NOT wants_pointer_capture, so a plain hover forwards its widget-relative x fraction; the view feeds it to LineChart::inspect, and the crosshair / per-series markers / value tooltip track the cursor with no press. Hovering off the plot fires Leave (the router boundary send), which clears the fraction so the crosshair is alive only over the plot. All example-level — the R1405 seam is the only framework machinery needed. Also corrects hello-chart's now-false header comment (it claimed pinion cannot forward a free-hover position — true pre-R1405, false since) and cross-references the hover variant.
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-crosshair` (NEW): a `CrosshairExternal` (primary external) opts into `External::wants_hover_move` but NOT `wants_pointer_capture` — a plain hover forwards its widget-relative x fraction, which `pointer_move` stores; a `send` PointerLeave/PointerCancel (the router boundary) clears it. The view feeds the fraction to `LineChart::inspect`, so the crosshair / per-series markers / value tooltip track the BARE hover with no press. Introspects `x_frac` (0.0..=1.0 or Null, writable — the AI-first no-pixel drive) + the derived read-only `has_crosshair`.

`examples/hello-chart/src/main.rs`: header comment corrected. Its "pinion forwards a continuous pointer position only under capture; free hover gives no position" claim was true pre-R1405 and FALSE since `wants_hover_move`; the comment now states both gestures are capture drags on purpose (the scrub value persists on release + answers ARIA-slider keys, which a transient hover position does not) and cross-references `hello-crosshair` for the bare-hover variant. Doc-only, no behaviour change.
`Cargo.toml`: register `examples/hello-crosshair` as a workspace member.

R1407.decision_summary: R1407 §5.35 §5.22: lift the duplicated Ctrl/Cmd+C copy-chord into pinion_core::external::selection_copy_payload (a pure fn: AltGr-safe chord-decode + &self query -> Option<String>, the payload a copy would write), and add hello-hex-dump as its third consumer (copy the R1402 byte selection as hex). R1408.decision_summary: R1408 §5.41: a sequential-magnitude heatmap over Scene::TextGrid with a bare-hover cell inspector (hello-heatmap), and the CellMetric::frac_to_cell lift its hover forced. A 12x8 intensity matrix renders as squarish colour cells (a single-hue surface->accent sequential ramp + a per-cell value label in a COMPUTED max-WCAG-contrast ink + a legend strip). A BARE hover (wants_hover_move, NOT capture — the 3rd consumer of that seam) reveals the cell under the pointer: pointer_move turns the router rect fraction into a cell via the lifted frac_to_cell, cell_at_char maps it to a data cell, which reverse-videos and is read by the oracle; a PointerLeave clears it. frac_to_cell = px_to_cell(frac_to_px(x,W), frac_to_px(y,H)), the composite hex-dump + hyperlink reconstructed by hand (both migrated; heatmap = the 3rd consumer that forced the lift, the composite twin of the R1405 frac_to_px lift). hello-grid-pointer keeps its own frac_to_px + a clamping cell_at_px shared with a px press handler (a divergent shape, not migrated). Three independent read-only reviewers audited pre-commit; reviewer 3 caught a real contrast bug (a fixed light/dark ink threshold picked the lower-contrast ink on the surface->accent ramp + a false doc claim), fixed with a computed WCAG contrast choice + corrected docs.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-core/src/cell_metric.rs: NEW CellMetric::frac_to_cell(self, x_rel, y_rel, rect_w, rect_h) -> (u16, u16) = self.px_to_cell(frac_to_px(x_rel, rect_w), frac_to_px(y_rel, rect_h)) — the rect-fraction -> cell hit-test the frac_to_px doc already named, lifted (R727 3rd-consumer, the composite twin of the R1405 frac_to_px lift). + a test that it composes the two steps for every fraction + concrete corners.

examples/hello-hex-dump + hello-hyperlink: migrated their by-hand frac_to_px + px_to_cell pointer_move onto frac_to_cell (behaviour byte-unchanged; the r1400-1402 / r1405 demos PASS). hello-grid-pointer is NOT migrated on purpose: its frac_to_px feeds a strict-hit cell_at_px that CLAMPS to (cols,rows) and is shared with a pixel-based press handler — a divergent shape, documented in the frac_to_cell doc.

examples/hello-heatmap (NEW): a 12x8 intensity matrix over Scene::TextGrid; each data cell fills 6x3 char cells with a sequential surface->accent ramp (Color::lerp, linear space) + a centred value label (identity never colour-alone) + a legend strip. A BARE hover (wants_hover_move, NOT capture) -> frac_to_cell -> cell_at_char -> the hovered data cell reverse-videos; a PointerLeave clears it. The HeatmapOracle introspects rows/cols/max_value/hovered_row/col/value + value_at (whole matrix) + hovered_cell (no-pixel intervene). The 3rd consumer of both wants_hover_move and frac_to_cell.
Cargo.toml: register examples/hello-heatmap as a workspace member.

R1409.decision_summary: R1409 §5.51 §5.49: a chart in a dock TAB well — hello-tabbed-chart proves a pinion-chart LineChart::build_fill lives as one tab of a DockNode::Tabs well, the case R1396 left UNEXERCISED (do not assert). A Tabs well is NOT byte-identical to a Leaf: the walker renders ONLY its active panel, header-suppressed, below a fixed tab strip, so an inactive chart tab is absent from the scene entirely. Two proofs: (1) while the chart tab is active, a window resize AND a splitter drag re-scale the chart through the tab well (the R1396 measured-rect seam, one wrapper deeper; a narrow well still collapses its legend to a +N marker); (2) switching to a sibling tab removes the chart tag from the scene, and re-activating it makes the chart reappear and re-measure — if the well was resized while the chart was hidden, the reappeared chart rebuilds from the NOW-narrow pane, not the stale wide size, caught within the activation frame by the shell publish->dirty->same-frame re-pass. The tab well also announces itself (§2 #7 WAI-ARIA tablist via dock_tablist_access_nodes). NO framework code changed: the seam already handles the tab-well case, so the round proves the hypothesis without touching the walker.
changes_bullets: examples/hello-tabbed-chart (NEW): a pinion-chart LineChart::build_fill lives as one tab of a DockNode::Tabs well (chart tab + notes tab) beside a readout Leaf, split by a SplitterExternal. A DockReorganizer + TabWellExternal drive tab switching through the topology-owned active-tab SSOT (no shadow index). The chart reads its measured cell via use_pane_viewport_size(CHART_TAG), so a window resize, a splitter drag, AND a tab re-activation all re-scale it. WidgetA11y::access_node emits the well WAI-ARIA tablist/tab/tabpanel via dock_tablist_access_nodes (2nd example consumer after hello-dock-panels-editor). PR-51 display-only, no primary surface. 6 unit tests, incl. the DISCRIMINATING stale-catch-up test: it asserts the reappeared narrow chart x-tick labels stay CONTAINED in its rect (fails iff the internal geometry rebuilt from the stale wide size) — not a vacuous root-width check.

The reducer's three arms (tear_off toggle / tear_off_follow ensure / tear_off_redock remove) float + dock the chart via BOTH the AI invoke("tear_off") and a live header drag; when floated the main dock drops the chart to a view_floating_placeholder so CHART_TAG is drawn in exactly one window per frame (the R1021.1 precondition). NO framework behaviour changed — the R1021 per-window publish and the R1396 build_fill pattern compose; the round is a consumer proof. It ALSO lands two R727 3rd-consumer lifts the new consumer forced: the windows-topology mutation shell (toggle/remove over a Signal<Vec<WindowSpec>>) to pinion-shell beside window_exists (migrating hello-dock-panels + hello-dock-panels-editor), and the chart-demo count_indexed_tags counter to rpc_verify (migrating r1396 + r1409). A pre-commit 3-reviewer audit fixed a repeat of the R1409 vacuous-test trap (the headline test keyed on the fill-parent root rect) by asserting the (cw,ch)-driven internal geometry instead.

R1411.decision_summary: R1411 §5.51 §5.52 §5.49: a palette card is now a DRAG SOURCE — dragging a node kind from the hello-node-editor palette onto the canvas INSTANTIATES that node AT THE DROP POINT (the Unreal/Blender toolbox-to-graph object-creation gesture), the highest-value editor interaction the node-graph substrate still lacked. Before R1411 the palette was click-only (R849: add at a fixed spawn point) and begin_drag armed only wire drags off a pin — the palette cards were not drag sources at all. The gesture reuses two already-built substrates with ZERO new framework code: the R742/R1093 drag session (the source resolves the drop under the absolute cursor) and the R1113 drag-image follower (the translucent chip that surfaces the drag payload's Text value as its label, so a palette drag carrying the node TITLE gets a Scalar/Lerp follower for free). It coexists with click-to-add-at-spawn: the router's !became_drag gate (input.rs) makes the drop-commit and the trailing click mutually exclusive, so there is no double-add. It also extracts add_node_at(kind, x, y), the position SSOT shared by add_node (spawn cascade) and the drop. An audit-first entry REFUTED all three stale SEED R1411 candidates and five stale debt-dataviz absent gaps before building.
changes_bullets: examples/hello-node-editor/src/main.rs: a palette card is now a DRAG SOURCE. PendingPress::Palette is Palette(usize) carrying the pressed PALETTE index; begin_drag gains a palette arm returning DragPayload{kind:"palette-node", value:Text(title)} (the title is the R1113 drag-image follower chip label the shell surfaces automatically, no wire preview); drag_release gains a palette branch that, on a release over GRAPH_TAG, projects the drop fraction to graph coords (the R1220 cursor_graph_at) and instantiates via add_node_at. add_node is refactored to extract add_node_at(kind, x, y) — the position SSOT shared by the spawn add (its fan-out cascade reads next_node_id via a peek so the values are bit-identical) and the drop. A PALETTE_DRAG_KIND const distinguishes the palette drag from the "node-edge" wire drag; click-to-add-at-spawn (pointer_up) is untouched.

R1412.decision_summary: R1412 §5.49 §5.16 §5.51: a named dock-layout PRESET manager (examples/hello-dock-presets) — apply a built-in named layout, save the current layout under a name, delete one — and the forcing consumer of a NEW framework seam. Auditing DockTopology serde revealed Deserialize was derive-only, so it BYPASSED the try_new validation gate: a persisted/wire topology with a duplicate panel id or non-finite ratio could reconstruct an INVALID DockTopology, the exact state the private root field promises cannot exist. R1412 makes DockTopology::Deserialize a hand-written impl routing the parsed tree through try_new, so a corrupt blob is a deserialize ERROR, not a silently-invalid value. The preset manager persists presets as serialized DockTopology blobs and deserializes on apply, exercising and PROVING the seam end-to-end: the corrupt-witness preset (a duplicate panel id) is REJECTED, the live topology unchanged. Serialize stays a derive.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/dock.rs: DockTopology::Deserialize is now a hand-written impl (was a derive) that deserializes the root DockNode then routes it through DockTopology::try_new, mapping a TopologyError to serde::de::Error::custom. So a persisted/wire topology is validated (unique panel/split/tabs ids, canonical wells, finite ratios) exactly as a constructed one — the private-field "cannot be broken from outside the module" invariant now holds across the serde boundary. Serialize stays a derive (writing out is always sound). 3 new tests: a valid topology round-trips; a duplicate-panel-id blob and a duplicate-split-id blob are deserialize ERRORS (built by serializing a raw unvalidated DockNode tree into the {"root":...} wire shape). 718/718 green.

R1413.decision_summary: R1413 §5.28 §5.16 §5.7: a media transport (play/pause/stop) over the R1389 pinion-chart Timeline with a LIVE auto-advancing now-playhead (dashboard-substrate gap #4). The playhead is TransportClock, an example-local §5.28 Tickable registered via Owner::register_animation_once (the theme-fade / caret-blink / IndeterminateSweep substrate), advancing a 0..=1 Signal LINEARLY while playing (constant speed, not a spring) with is_at_rest=(status!=Playing) so the existing frame loop is the clock — no thread, no RepaintSink poke. Because the driver is the §5.28 one, the R724 scene/tick RPC frame-steps it DETERMINISTICALLY, so a wall-clock transport is CI-testable without racing real frames: Play advances, Pause freezes (the at-rest gate stops all ticks), Stop rewinds, the end clamps at 100% + auto-pauses, Play-at-the-end replays. Timeline's 2nd consumer; the transport state machine stays example-local (1st consumer).
changes_bullets: examples/hello-transport (NEW, + Cargo.toml workspace member): a media transport (play/pause/stop) over the R1389 pinion-chart Timeline, with a LIVE auto-advancing now-playhead. The playhead is driven by TransportClock, an example-local §5.28 Tickable holding a Signal<f32> position (0..=1) + a Cell<TransportStatus{Stopped,Playing,Paused}>, registered via Owner::register_animation_once (the theme-fade / caret-blink / IndeterminateSweep substrate — its 7th consumer, the 2nd example-local Tickable after hello-node-editor's AutoPan). tick(dt) advances position LINEARLY by dt/DURATION while Playing (constant speed — a spring would decelerate into the end); is_at_rest = (status != Playing), so the backend requests frames only while playing — no thread, no RepaintSink poke, the existing frame loop is the clock. Reaching 1.0 clamps + auto-pauses at the end; Play from the end rewinds first (replay); Stop rewinds to 0. 13 unit tests.

Owner-scoping (the hello-progress pattern): the clock is resolved-or-registered in the pure view via use_transport_clock (idempotent), so it lives on the ticked window owner and its position Signal auto-subscribes the paint; the reducer maps a play/pause/stop button click straight onto the clock (the reducer shares the owner, as hello-live-chart's reducer reaches its cached producer). Three M3 buttons: Play is the primary external, Pause+Stop are extra externals. Timeline's 2nd consumer (after hello-timeline).

tools/demos/r1413_transport.py (NEW, 36 assertions): drives the transport over RPC and frame-steps it DETERMINISTICALLY with the R724 scene/tick method — Play then scene/tick advances the playhead pixel rightward (monotonic, within the plot, the status names the clip under it); Pause then scene/tick leaves the pixel FROZEN (the at-rest gate proven); Play resumes past the frozen spot; Stop rewinds to 0; a tick past the 12s duration clamps at 100% and auto-Pauses; Play at the end replays. Exact values are asserted only in at-rest states (Stopped 0%, Paused frozen, ended 100%) where no real frame tick can confound them (the r726 indeterminate-sweep discipline).

R1416.decision_summary: R1416 §5.35 §5.15 §5.7: deliver the raw multi-button pointer stream (the sprag PR-72 pointer-capture gap). The default pipeline routes only the LEFT button to a widget and drives right/middle presses as GUI defaults (context menu / PRIMARY paste / pan), so a widget that IS the pointer authority for its region (a terminal pane forwarding xterm mouse reports, a game viewport) could not see right/middle buttons, the right RELEASE edge, or press-time modifiers. R1416 adds an additive External opt-in: wants_raw_pointer_buttons + the typed raw_pointer_button(RawPointerButton{button,edge,modifiers}) method. A raw sink receives every left/middle/right press+release with the held modifiers on both edges and the button identified, while every non-raw widget keeps the standard per-button GUI semantics unchanged (the non-capture invariant, the W3C listener-opts-out-of-default model). Native winit input and a new single-edge scene/pointer_button RPC share one pointer_button_for_window seam, so an injected edge is indistinguishable from a physical one.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-core/src/input.rs: added the raw-pointer vocabulary the External sees — PointerButton (Left/Middle/Right, the full W3C PointerEvent set with lower-case as_wire_name/from_wire_name), PointerEdge (Down/Up), and the RawPointerButton { button, edge, modifiers } carrier (a cross-crate struct literal like DragUpdate/DropPoint, NOT non_exhaustive). Position is deliberately off the carrier (the widget correlates it via pointer_move); both edges carry modifiers, closing the press-edge-drops-modifiers gap.

crates/pinion-core/src/external.rs: two additive External methods — wants_raw_pointer_buttons() (opt-in, default false) and raw_pointer_button(RawPointerButton) (typed delivery, default no-op). A widget that opts in trades the legacy PointerDown/PointerUp send wire and the GUI defaults (context menu / paste / pan) for the raw multi-button edges; every non-opting widget is unaffected (the non-capture invariant).

R1417.decision_summary: R1417 §5.35 §5.15: lift the transparent capture-surface idiom into pinion_core::capture_surface. R1415's mandatory 3rd-consumer self-grep surfaced a hand-rolled idiom — a transparent, geometrically pointer-opaque Scene::Box laid out over an absolute rect and carrying a tag, the invisible interaction layer a pointer routes through to reach the External under that tag — copied across the interaction examples (~8 at R1415, grown by R1416). The audit found it fully uniform: every copy byte-identical but for (tag, rect, focusable). A wholesale lift is therefore warranted (not premature per [[edit-machinery-crate-lift-is-audited-premature]]): one capture_surface(tag, rect, focusable) constructor in pinion-core (a byte-identity unit test pins it) + all 11 consumers migrated. The 11th (hello-frame-profiler) was NOT in R1415's named list; grepping ALL sites rather than trusting the list is what found it.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-core/src/scene.rs: new pub fn capture_surface(tag, rect, focusable) -> Scene — a transparent, geometrically pointer-opaque Scene::Box laid out over rect (absolute position + px size) and carrying tag: the one home for the "invisible interaction layer over content" idiom (a chart plot, a scrub track, a terminal pane). Transparent so content shows through; opaque to the alpha-independent hit-test so the router targets it; focusable marks a Tab stop for widgets whose keyboard interaction needs focus (the scrub bar). 1 unit test proves it BYTE-IDENTICAL (Debug-form) to the hand-rolled BoxNode form for focusable=false (incl. the omitted-with_focusable default), focusable=false-explicit, and focusable=true.

examples (11 migrated to capture_surface, hand-rolled idiom removed): hello-crosshair / -timeline / -scatter / -donut / -treemap / -chart / -histogram-brush / -linked-brush / -frame-profiler (chart hover/scrub surfaces, focusable=false) + hello-scrubber (focusable=true, track inflated 12px vertically, Rect::new inline) + hello-raw-pointer (the R1416 pane sink, focusable=false). hello-frame-profiler was NOT in the R1415 carry's named list — the mandatory 3rd-consumer grep (all sites, not the prior list) found it as the 11th. Each drops now-unused BoxNode/Color imports; hello-scatter's test module keeps a scoped Color import.

R1418.decision_summary: R1418 §5.35 §5.15: give the raw pointer sink Qt QMouseEvent parity — the implicit mouse grab + the held-button set — applying the 2026-07-23 directive to use Qt as the reference and stop deferring Qt-present features by YAGNI. R1416 delivered the raw button EDGES but a raw sink bypasses pointer_down, so it never engaged the capture machinery and lost the release of any press-drag that strayed off its rect: a DOWN with no matching UP, the stuck button PR-72 explicitly named (and PR-72 framed the sink as a capturing External). R1418 adds the framework's implicit mouse grab (Qt grabMouse / DOM implicit pointer capture): a raw sink's first press pins its tag, routing every later button edge and cursor move to it regardless of location until the last held button lifts. It also adds PointerButtons, the Qt buttons() / DOM MouseEvent.buttons held-button set carried on RawPointerButton, so a chord (press left then right reports left+right) or a motion-with-buttons is expressible where the single changed button cannot. Both are ALSO driven no-pixel over scene/pointer_button and queryable as scene data (last_buttons) — the AI-first bar that makes it superior to Qt, not just at parity.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-runtime/src/input.rs: the R1418 IMPLICIT MOUSE GRAB (Qt grabMouse / Win32 SetCapture / DOM implicit pointer capture) for a raw sink. A raw sink bypasses pointer_down, so it never engaged captured_targets and would lose the release of a press-drag that strayed off its rect (a DOWN with no UP = the "stuck button" PR-72 named). New per-pointer raw_grabs map: a raw sink's first press pins its tag, routing every later button edge AND cursor_moved position to it regardless of cursor location, releasing only when the last held button lifts. gesture_pins_hover + pointer_cancel now include the grab. deliver_raw_pointer_button rewritten around the grab; cursor_moved gains a raw-grab move-forward branch. 3 new grab tests (cross-boundary release pairing / multi-button chord holds until last up / a lone release opens no grab).

crates/pinion-core/src/input.rs: PointerButtons — the Qt QMouseEvent::buttons() / DOM MouseEvent.buttons held-button SET (u8 bitmask over left/middle/right; empty/is_empty/contains/with/without + as_wire_token/from_wire_token "lmr", the R773 encode-inverse-decode pair). RawPointerButton gains a `buttons` field (the set held AFTER this edge: a press includes the pressed button, a release excludes it — DOM/Qt convention), so a chord or motion-with-buttons is expressible where the single changed `button` cannot. 1 unit test (set ops + wire round-trip).

examples/hello-raw-pointer: the sink stores + exposes the held set — ButtonReport gains buttons; a new `last_buttons` introspect field (lmr token) so an AI client reads WHICH buttons are down. +1 unit test.

tools/demos/r1416_raw_pointer.py: two new sections — (1) the grab pairs a release that lands OUTSIDE the pane (no stuck button); (2) the held set tracks a chord (left down -> "l", right down while left held -> "lr", left up -> "r", right up -> ""). The grab surfaced unbalanced press sequences the pre-R1418 demo had (a held button correctly grabs the pointer and suppresses leave — Qt discipline); every press is now balanced by a release.

Both built, both ALSO driven no-pixel over RPC + queryable as scene data (the "superior to Qt" AI-first bar).
