carry_forward_bullets: Directive recorded (durable, [[qt-parity-over-yagni]]): from now on ignore YAGNI, use Qt as the reference, implement what Qt has (do not defer as "no consumer yet"), aim to be at minimum superior to Qt (pinion's edge = §2 #7 scene-as-data + §2 #2 RPC-primary AI-first introspection on top of Qt behavior). This overrides YAGNI / [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]] for BUILDING Qt-present capabilities; the latter still governs INTERNAL helper-lift decisions.

Honest correction: R1416 deferred the implicit grab + buttons() as "no consumer / speculative". That was wrong — both are universal Qt primitives (grabMouse / QMouseEvent::buttons()) the actual consumer (sprag's pane, cross-pane drag) needs, and PR-72 explicitly framed the sink as a capturing External and named the stuck-button failure the grab prevents. Built in R1418.

Grab discipline is now load-bearing: a raw sink press that is never released keeps the pointer grabbed (Qt behavior). scene/click{right} is a press-edge one-shot (GUI context-menu arc, no release), so on a raw sink it opens a grab a caller must balance with an explicit right-up; native right-click balances itself (winit sends Right/Released -> the R1416 right-release arm). The demo balances every press.

Next Qt-parity candidates for the pointer axis (build, do not defer): double-click synthesis (QApplication::doubleClickInterval / MouseButtonDblClick) — the router already times the LEFT double-click (last_press); extend it to the raw stream as a click-count on RawPointerButton. Then broader QMouseEvent parity is essentially complete for the raw sink.

R1419.decision_summary: R1419 §5.39 §5.16: add the OS-window-focus reactive paint-path read (PINION-PR73). pinion_core::window_focus_state::os_focused_window() is the peer of focus_state::focused() on the OS-focus axis — the binding-wide window IDENTITY (Option<String>, not a bool), published by pinion-shell's one set_os_focused_window funnel (both note_os_focus and the window-destruction reconcile route through it) so a paint path can dim on blur / re-arm on refocus. Also lands the missing drive peer scene/window_focus {focused} — the winit Focused simulator for the os_focused_window READ leg of scene/input_state, so an AI drives OS-focus-reactive display headlessly. hello-window-focus is the first consumer.
changes_bullets: pinion_core::window_focus_state::os_focused_window() -> Option<String>: the paint-path reactive read of which OS window holds OS keyboard focus, the peer of focus_state::focused() on the OS-focus axis, carrying the window IDENTITY (not a bool) so a multi-window/tear-off binding compares against its own window id.
Owner gains an os_focused_window mirror field threaded tree-wide by new_child exactly like focused_tag (one shell-owned binding-wide fact); os_focused_window_signal() accessor.

pinion-shell ShellCore::set_os_focused_window funnel: both writers of os_focused_window (note_os_focus and the window-destruction reconcile) route through it, publishing the R1419 mirror alongside the existing key-dispatch gate (one SSOT, self-healing).

scene/window_focus {focused: bool} drive method (MethodOcc::Read, out-of-band like focus/set): the missing drive peer of the os_focused_window READ leg of scene/input_state, simulating a winit Focused edge for the {window} scope so an AI can exercise OS-focus-reactive display headlessly. Deferred-apply pattern survives the dispatch borrow split; R889 unknown-window gate reused.
hello-window-focus example: view reads os_focused_window() and dims the panel + re-renders a status label on OS focus/blur.
verification_bullets: pinion-core: 7 window_focus_state unit tests (no-scope None, publish read-back, per-binding isolation, tree-shared child scope, reactive re-run on focus AND blur, equality-skip). Full suite 2657 green.

pinion-rpc: 4 scene/window_focus dispatch tests (true drives+echoes result, false blurs+null, missing focused -> -32602, no-gate reject) + catalog_matches_dispatch_match_arms + occ_is_honest cross-checks green (919).
pinion-shell: dispatch_core r1419 integration test drives note_os_focus + secondary window, asserts the paint-path mirror equals the key-dispatch gate leg and carries the window identity; 180 green.
hello-window-focus: 2 example tests (view reflects focus/blur edges, status_text spelling); binary boots + responds over RPC.

r1419_window_focus.py demo: 38 assertions PASS (discovery, boot None, focus/blur drive echoes result, reactive view re-render, idempotent re-focus, side-effect-free read, invalid-params + unknown-window rejection, real window still drives after bogus traffic).
Gates: clippy -D pedantic clean (4 crates), cargo doc --document-private-items clean, mnemosyne validate-workspace T1=0.
carry_forward_bullets: scene/window_focus drives note_os_focus's concern only (the OS-focus gate + R1419 mirror); it deliberately does NOT trigger the FocusManager save/restore or held-key clear that the winit Focused arm also performs (those are the widget-focus axis, already RPC-drivable via focus/set / focus/clear). A fuller "simulate the whole Focused edge" verb would need &mut self across the dispatch borrow split (early-return, not a closure) — deferred until a consumer needs the combined semantics.

Multi-window per-window reflection is proven by unit/shell tests (tree-shared identity read); the shipped example is single-window. A multi-OS-window example dimming only its blurred window is a future demo, not a gap.

R1420.decision_summary: R1420 §5.39 §5.16: complete scene/window_focus to a FULL winit WindowEvent::Focused simulation, removing the R1419 deferral ([[qt-parity-over-yagni]]). The R1419 drive replayed only note_os_focus (OS-focus gate + paint-path mirror); it now also replays window_focused/window_blurred, so a driven blur saves the focused widget for restore AND clears the held-key chord (no stranded chord across an alt-tab) and a driven refocus restores it — byte-for-byte the AppShell winit Focused arm, matching a physical OS blur/refocus and Qt window deactivation.
changes_bullets: pinion-shell: the scene/window_focus deferred-apply now replays the shell's OWN winit WindowEvent::Focused arm byte-for-byte — note_os_focus (gate + R1419 mirror) THEN window_focused()/window_blurred(), not the R1419 gate/mirror-only stub.

Effect: a driven blur snapshots the focused widget for restore AND clears the held-key chord cache (no stranded chord across an alt-tab); a driven refocus restores the saved widget. Matches a physical OS blur/refocus and Qt window deactivation/reactivation.
dispatch.rs field + handler docs updated to describe the full OS-focus-edge simulation.
demo r1419_window_focus.py: +4 assertions (K) — arm a Space chord while focused, drive a blur, observe held_keys cleared over RPC (proves window_blurred fires, not just note_os_focus).
verification_bullets: r1419_window_focus.py: 42 assertions PASS (was 38) — new section K drives a full blur and asserts the held-key chord is cleared, the direct observable of window_blurred replaying over RPC.
pinion-shell 180 + dispatch_core r1419 + pinion-rpc r1419 (4) green; clippy -D pedantic clean; cargo doc --document-private-items clean.
window_focused restore fires symmetrically through the same call site; FocusManager save/restore has its own unit tests (pinion-runtime focus.rs).
carry_forward_bullets: none — R1420 clears the R1419 deferral (scene/window_focus is now a full winit Focused-edge simulation, not gate/mirror only). R1421.decision_summary: R1421 §5.39 §5.16: ship hello-window-focus-multi — two OS windows each dimming ONLY on its own blur, the concrete proof that the R1419 paint-path OS-focus read is a window IDENTITY (os_focused_window() == Some(window_id)) not a binding-wide bool. Each view_for_window reads the one binding-wide mirror and compares against its own id; a demo drives scene/window_focus per window and reads each window's paint separately, showing the roles swap on one mirror. Closes the R1419 'multi-window demo is future' note ([[qt-parity-over-yagni]] — Qt apps dim per-window).
changes_bullets: New example hello-window-focus-multi: TWO OS windows (main + inspector) sharing one binding, each view_for_window reads the binding-wide os_focused_window() mirror and compares it against ITS OWN window id (== Some(window_id)) — so each window dims only when its own window is blurred.

This is the concrete demonstration of the R1419 design-review call: the paint-path OS-focus read is a window IDENTITY (Option<String>), not a binding-wide bool — a bool read could not tell two windows apart. Manual WidgetView (windows() + view_for_window), since the #[widget] macro has no multi-window override.

Demo r1419_window_focus_multi.py: 34 assertions PASS — focus main → only inspector dims; focus inspector → the roles swap on the same mirror; whole-app blur → both dim; the gate leg agrees with each window's painted label; unknown-window drive rejected. Reads each window's paint via snapshot(window="…").
verification_bullets: hello-window-focus-multi: 2 unit tests (per-window dimming swaps as OS focus moves main<->inspector<->none; main carries the Button primary, inspector is display-only). green.
r1419_window_focus_multi.py: 34 assertions PASS over RPC (per-window identity dimming, gate/label agreement, blur-both, unknown-window rejection).

R1422.decision_summary: R1422 §5.35 §5.15: synthesise a double-click on the raw multi-button pointer stream — the Qt MouseButtonDblClick / DOM MouseEvent.detail verb the R1416/R1418 raw sink (External::wants_raw_pointer_buttons) still lacked. RawPointerButton gains click_count: the router's deliver_raw_pointer_button reports 2 on a press that repeats the same button at the same spot within the double-click window (else 1), echoes that count onto the matching release, and caps at 2 (no rolling triple). The per-(pointer,button) raw_click_marks tracker is keyed by button (the Qt per-button rule) and REUSES the DOUBLE_CLICK_TIME_MS + DOUBLE_CLICK_DIST_PX thresholds of the send-wire DoubleClick path so the two double-click rules cannot drift. Synthesis lives in the one deliver_raw_pointer_button seam both native winit MouseInput and scene/pointer_button cross; hello-raw-pointer exposes it as last_clicks + a x2 readout badge.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: RawPointerButton gains click_count: u8 (the Qt MouseButtonDblClick / DOM MouseEvent.detail peer); PointerButton derives Hash so it keys the router's per-button raw double-click tracker.

pinion-runtime: deliver_raw_pointer_button synthesises click_count via raw_click_for + commit_raw_click_mark over a per-(pointer,button) raw_click_marks map; a press reports 2 on a same-button same-spot repeat inside the window (else 1), a release echoes the press count, capped at 2 (no rolling triple); the mark commits only on delivery so a non-sink edge cannot poison the next real press.
raw_click_marks reuses DOUBLE_CLICK_TIME_MS + DOUBLE_CLICK_DIST_PX (the send-wire DoubleClick thresholds) so the two double-click rules cannot drift (one vocabulary).

hello-raw-pointer: records and exposes click_count as last_clicks (read-only int) and badges a synthesised double as a x2 readout; the double is drivable over the wire via scene/double_click, already routed through the raw seam at R1416.
verification_bullets: pinion-runtime: 4 new router tests — a same-spot second press is 2 and its release echoes 2; a strayed second press stays 1; per-button independence (a left double leaves a right press 1); a third press resets to 1 (no rolling triple). runtime 534 green.
pinion-core 2657 green; hello-raw-pointer 12 unit tests green (last_clicks exposure + x2 badge; a single click is not badged).

r1422_double_click.py: 36 verifications PASS over RPC — a deterministic double via scene/double_click reads last_clicks == 2 plus a x2 readout badge; the fresh-button, no-triple, and strayed-press negatives read 1; arm_double plants a position-mismatched mark so each double is deterministic (the router double-click cycle persists across the sink clear, as Qt's does).
clippy -D pedantic clean; cargo doc --document-private-items clean; mnemosyne T1=0.
carry_forward_bullets: none — the raw double-click was the last unimplemented QMouseEvent verb on the R1416/R1418 raw-pointer line; the send-wire DoubleClick and the raw click_count now share one threshold vocabulary. The router's per-button double-click mark persisting across the sink clear is Qt-correct (not a debt); the demo primes each double via arm_double.

R1423.decision_summary: R1423 §5.35 §5.15: add pointer PRESSURE to the raw pointer surface — the W3C PointerEvent.pressure / Qt QTabletEvent::pressure() axis a mouse lacks but a pen / touch has, the one QMouseEvent-adjacent verb the R1416/R1418/R1422 raw sink still missed. External::pointer_pressure forwards a normalised 0..1 force alongside each pointer_move (pressure travels with position, the W3C pointermove model) and on a standalone change; the router holds it per-pointer (set from the platform pen force winit Touch::force, or the scene/pointer_pressure RPC — positionless / out-of-band like scene/modifiers, delivered to the surface at once). hello-raw-pointer paints a pressure-reactive ink dot (diameter = 6 + pressure*44 px), the DCC ink-brush vignette, fully drivable and introspectable headless (§2 #2, no tablet required).
changes_bullets: pinion-core: External::pointer_pressure(f32) hook — the W3C PointerEvent.pressure / Qt QTabletEvent::pressure() peer, forwarded alongside pointer_move (pressure travels with position); default no-op, a mouse reports 0.

pinion-runtime: Touch gains force: Option<f32> (winit Touch::force source); InputRouter holds a per-pointer pressure, forwards it in forward_pointer_move (id param added), and splits note_pointer_pressure (store, for the pen bridge) vs set_pointer_pressure (store + immediate deliver to the move-target, for the RPC path).
pinion-rpc: scene/pointer_pressure {value} — a positionless out-of-band DeferredInput::PointerPressure (the scene/modifiers shape); a non-numeric value rejects, the router clamps.
pinion-shell: the winit Touch boundary reads force (Force::normalized); the deferred-input drain routes PointerPressure through CoreShell::set_pointer_pressure_for_window.

hello-raw-pointer: reads pressure (pointer_pressure hook, `pressure` introspect + readout) and paints a pressure-reactive ink dot whose diameter scales with force (6 + pressure*44 px) — the DCC ink-brush vignette.
verification_bullets: pinion-runtime: 2 router tests (a noted pressure rides a forwarded hover move; set_pointer_pressure delivers immediately and clamps out-of-range input). runtime 437 green.
pinion-rpc: 2 dispatch tests (a numeric value enqueues PointerPressure; a missing / non-numeric value rejects with invalid_params, enqueuing nothing). rpc 921 green.

hello-raw-pointer: 3 unit tests (pressure stored / exposed / clamped and read-only; the ink dot appears only under force and grows with it; the readout names the pressure). example 15 green; core 2657 / shell 180 green.

r1423_pressure.py: 37 verifications PASS over RPC — a driven force delivers and paints the ink mark, the mark scales with force / vanishes at zero / clamps at 1.0 / rides a move / drops off-pane; the wire rejects a bad value.
clippy -D pedantic clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo doc --document-private-items clean; mnemosyne T1=0.
carry_forward_bullets: The native pen / touch force source (winit Touch::force) is wired but hardware-gated: a tablet / touchscreen exercises it natively, while the AI-first scene/pointer_pressure path is fully verified headless (§2 #2) — the standard hardware carry, like the Mac / Win native surfaces.

Tilt / altitude (Qt QTabletEvent xTilt / yTilt) is a distinct follow-up axis, gated on winit exposing only Force::Calibrated::altitude_angle (partial, no azimuth); pressure is the single high-value force axis this round.

R1425.decision_summary: R1425 §5.41: add the DECSCUSR blink-vs-steady mode to the cell-native TextGrid cursor — GridCursor::blink: bool (+ with_blink), the flag the CursorShape rustdoc named 'a separate concern not folded into the shape' and the GridCursor forward-compat hedge foreshadowed. blink is the DECSCUSR mode (blinking vs steady variant) the producer reports (R969), a first-class fact distinct from visible (DECTCEM show/hide) and from the render-time blink phase (R974.1 dual-fact). The phase is a paint-time renderer concern owned by the last renderer in the chain — the way every real terminal keeps the blink timer in the widget, not the PTY app — and is NEVER folded into visible, because folding it would conflate 'app hid the cursor' with 'blink off-phase' so a projection consumer or scene/snapshot could no longer read the two apart (§2 #7). Reported as data on both the GridCursor and the RPC snapshot; a two-reviewer independent design audit (architecture + terminal-correctness lenses) settled the data model against a phase-in-visible alternative. The paint-time phase animation is the deferred renderer-owned slice, following the axis build discipline (the R993 Vello paint followed the R975 cursor data model), mirroring the CaretBlink primitive pinion already ships for its own carets.

R1426.decision_summary: R1426 §5.41: land the render-time cursor blink PHASE animation the R1425 blink MODE drives — a GridCursor in the blinking DECSCUSR mode alternates ON/OFF at the 530 ms CaretBlink half-period in BOTH backends, while a steady cursor stays drawn. The phase is a renderer-owned, paint-time concern kept strictly downstream of both the state-scene and the paint-scene, so it never folds into GridCursor::visible (DECTCEM) or the scene/snapshot (§2 #7): "app hid the cursor" and "blink off-phase" stay distinguishable to a projection consumer. Every real terminal keeps the blink timer in the widget, not the PTY app — pinion mirrors that with one free-running per-window clock (the CaretBlink primitive it already ships for its own carets, its second consumer; NO reset-on-activity, because a terminal cursor blinks independently of typing), armed only while a visible blinking cursor is on screen so an idle window releases the frame loop. The cross-backend draw gate is one SSOT predicate, GridCursor::shown_this_phase(blink_on) = visible && (!blink || blink_on), called by the Vello overlay and the pinion-tui inverted-cell painter alike so the two can never drift. A two-reviewer independent design audit (architecture + terminal-correctness lenses) settled the design before code: per-window clock (not a single global — a secondary-window blink would otherwise freeze), the phase read UNTRACKED at pixel-paint (not folded into the scene), determinism via forcing the steady ON phase on the headless/produce/test paint paths (only the live surface animates), and focus-gating DEFERRED (a filled solid block when unfocused is behaviourally wrong — real terminals show a hollow box + stop-blink; shipping the wrong half is worse than none). The TUI keeps R1424's painted-cell model (host hardware cursor stays hidden), so this is pinion's painted-cell projection blink, not a delegation to the host terminal's settings-driven blink.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: GridCursor::shown_this_phase(blink_on) — the cross-backend draw gate SSOT (visible && (!blink || blink_on)); a steady cursor ignores the phase, a blinking cursor draws only on the visible half, a hidden cursor never draws. Scene::has_visible_blinking_grid_cursor() — a read-only recursive walk (mirrors is_cacheable_for_paint) the shell reads once per paint to decide whether to arm the blink clock.

pinion-runtime: paint_adapter threads a cursor_blink_on: bool through the cached walker (to_vello_cached_with_text_engine / _inner / paint_text_grid / paint_grid_cursor); the thin to_vello_cached forwards the steady default (true) so its ~30 call sites are untouched; the uncached reference walker always paints steady. paint_grid_cursor now gates via shown_this_phase, never touching the visible (DECTCEM) check. CoreShell::arm_grid_cursor_blink(&self, window_id, &Scene) registers/enables (or idles) a per-window CaretBlink clock keyed __grid_cursor_blink__ on the window owner (a child of root_owner, so tick_animations_for_window advances it and the any_animation_active cascade arms the repaint); CoreShell::grid_cursor_blink_on reads the phase gate (!enabled || visible) untracked.

pinion-tui: to_buffer_with_cursor_phase(scene, buf, on) threads the phase through to_buffer_inner / paint_container / paint_text_grid_inner; the thin to_buffer forwards true; the cursor-inversion guard uses shown_this_phase, so on the off-phase the inverted cell is not painted and the plain cell shows.

pinion-shell: compute_paint_scene_internal (live only, never the pure mirror) arms the clock from the freshly-produced paint scene before the any_animation_active gate; the live winit paint (app.rs) threads grid_cursor_blink_on, the headless/produce path forces the steady ON phase for deterministic screenshots; a substrate grid_cursor_blink_on passthrough.

carry_forward_bullets: Focus-gating is DEFERRED to its own round (the R1427 candidate): a terminal cursor should stop blinking AND render a hollow/outline box when the window loses focus (xterm/VTE/alacritty/kitty), plus likely a new introspectable active/inactive fact so an AI reads the unfocused state as data. Shipping only the easy half ("steady solid block when unfocused") is behaviourally wrong (it misreads as active), so R1426 ships pure free-running blink (matching xterm-when-enabled / Windows Terminal, both free-run) with the has_blink arming gate as the idle-power release.

The off-phase is not screenshot-able by design: the headless/produce/screenshot paint path forces the steady ON phase so a golden capture never flakes on the wall-clock phase. The off-phase gating is proven by the pinion-tui buffer test (pixel-equivalent) + the shown_this_phase SSOT unit test; a live-pixel off-phase guard would need to drive the live winit clock deterministically (a CI/GPU concern, not added).

The TUI keeps R1424's painted-cell software blink (host hardware cursor hidden). A host-hardware-cursor delegation arm (crossterm SetCursorStyle blinking/steady + DECTCEM + OSC-12, respecting the user's terminal blink prefs) stays deferred because it cannot recolour the native cursor and would regress the R1424 TUI OSC-12 inverted cell.

Preserve the TextGrid-uncacheable invariant (Scene::is_cacheable_for_paint → TextGrid false): the paint-walk phase argument is cache-safe only because the grid subtree is re-walked every frame. If TextGrid ever gains a paint cache, the phase must enter its paint_hash or the cursor freezes.

SGR-5 CELL-text blink in the Vello backend (CellAttrs::blink) stays a separate remaining slice, a different axis from this DECSCUSR cursor blink; the new per-window clock is a natural future substrate/second consumer for it.

pinion-runtime: paint_adapter threads a cursor_blink_on: bool through the cached walker (to_vello_cached_with_text_engine / _inner / paint_text_grid / paint_grid_cursor); the thin to_vello_cached forwards the steady default (true) so its ~30 call sites are untouched; the uncached reference walker always paints steady. paint_grid_cursor now gates via shown_this_phase, never touching the visible (DECTCEM) check. CoreShell::arm_grid_cursor_blink(&self, window_id, &Scene) registers/enables (or idles) a per-window CaretBlink clock keyed __grid_cursor_blink__ on the window owner (a child of root_owner, so tick_animations_for_window advances it and the any_animation_active cascade arms the repaint); CoreShell::grid_cursor_blink_on reads the phase gate (!enabled || visible) untracked.

pinion-tui: to_buffer_with_cursor_phase(scene, buf, on) threads the phase through to_buffer_inner / paint_container / paint_text_grid_inner; the thin to_buffer forwards true; the cursor-inversion guard uses shown_this_phase, so on the off-phase the inverted cell is not painted and the plain cell shows.

pinion-shell: compute_paint_scene_internal (live only, never the pure mirror) arms the clock from the freshly-produced paint scene before the any_animation_active gate; the live winit paint (app.rs) threads grid_cursor_blink_on, the headless/produce path forces the steady ON phase for deterministic screenshots; a substrate grid_cursor_blink_on passthrough.

pinion-tui shell: compute_paint_scene arms the clock (single DEFAULT_WINDOW, free-running — no OS focus signal), commit_paint threads grid_cursor_blink_on into to_buffer_with_cursor_phase; the run loop's any_animation_active poll advances the phase.
publishable_verification_bullets: pinion-core: 2 tests — shown_this_phase gates only a blinking cursor on the phase (steady/hidden unaffected; DECTCEM dominates), and has_visible_blinking_grid_cursor detects the arming condition (visible+blink true; steady/hidden false; recurses through Container/Scroll). core 2663 green.

pinion-runtime: 1 test — arm_grid_cursor_blink drives the phase and gate end-to-end: arming enables the clock (never at rest → window keeps painting), tick_animations_for_window flips grid_cursor_blink_on every half-period, re-arming does NOT reset the phase (free-run), a steady-only scene disarms it (steady gate + window idles). runtime 537 green.

pinion-tui: 1 test — the blink phase gates the inverted cursor cell (reversed on ON, plain on OFF; the non-cursor cell identical across phases; a steady cursor reversed on both; the two-arg to_buffer paints steady ON). The ratatui cell IS the pixel, so this is the pixel-equivalent off-phase proof.

r1426_textgrid_cursor_blink_phase.py: ~52 verifications PASS over RPC — the headline §2 #7 invariant is that advancing the blink clock via scene/tick (8 half-period steps + a 5 s step) leaves every scene/snapshot byte-stable (blink=true, visible=true), so the phase is observable only in pixels; the closed cursor wire keys carry no phase field; the steady sibling / R1424 OSC-12 colour / default cursors / R973 colours / R1403 hyperlink all regress clean.
Regression demos PASS: r975 / r1424 / r1425 (TextGrid cursor) + r977 (alt-screen) + r1400-r1402 (hex viewer).
Workspace: cargo check --workspace --all-targets green; clippy -D pedantic clean (changed crates); cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo doc --document-private-items -D warnings clean; mnemosyne T1=0.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: Focus-gating is DEFERRED to its own round (the R1427 candidate): a terminal cursor should stop blinking AND render a hollow/outline box when the window loses focus (xterm/VTE/alacritty/kitty), plus likely a new introspectable active/inactive fact so an AI reads the unfocused state as data. Shipping only the easy half ("steady solid block when unfocused") is behaviourally wrong (it misreads as active), so R1426 ships pure free-running blink (matching xterm-when-enabled / Windows Terminal, both free-run) with the has_blink arming gate as the idle-power release.

The off-phase is not screenshot-able by design: the headless/produce/screenshot paint path forces the steady ON phase so a golden capture never flakes on the wall-clock phase. The off-phase gating is proven by the pinion-tui buffer test (pixel-equivalent) + the shown_this_phase SSOT unit test; a live-pixel off-phase guard would need to drive the live winit clock deterministically (a CI/GPU concern, not added).

The TUI keeps R1424's painted-cell software blink (host hardware cursor hidden). A host-hardware-cursor delegation arm (crossterm SetCursorStyle blinking/steady + DECTCEM + OSC-12, respecting the user's terminal blink prefs) stays deferred because it cannot recolour the native cursor and would regress the R1424 TUI OSC-12 inverted cell.

Preserve the TextGrid-uncacheable invariant (Scene::is_cacheable_for_paint → TextGrid false): the paint-walk phase argument is cache-safe only because the grid subtree is re-walked every frame. If TextGrid ever gains a paint cache, the phase must enter its paint_hash or the cursor freezes.

SGR-5 CELL-text blink in the Vello backend (CellAttrs::blink) stays a separate remaining slice, a different axis from this DECSCUSR cursor blink; the new per-window clock is a natural future substrate/second consumer for it.

R1427.decision_summary: R1427 §5.41 §5.39: gate the terminal-cursor render on OS focus — an unfocused window draws its cursor as a HOLLOW outline box (overriding the shape) and stops blinking, the universal unfocused-terminal indicator (xterm / VTE / alacritty / kitty / Windows Terminal / iTerm2). paint_grid_cursor gains a cursor_focused flag threaded like R1426's cursor_blink_on; false strokes the hollow box (checked after shown_this_phase so a hidden cursor is never resurrected), true keeps the filled render. Stop-blink gates CoreShell::arm_grid_cursor_blink on focus so an unfocused window disables its clock (grid_cursor_blink_on then returns the steady ON phase) and idles. BOTH the hollow flag and the stop-blink arm read ONE fails-open predicate (is_key_dispatch_window), so they can never disagree (a design review caught that a mismatch — stop-blink fails OPEN, hollow fails CLOSED — would render a self-contradictory blinking-hollow cursor on unknown focus); the winit Focused arm requests a repaint on both edges so the transition lands on the next frame. Focus is a paint concern, never folded into the scene (§2 #7 — OS focus is already data via scene/input_state); focus-hollow is orthogonal to blink (a steady cursor goes hollow too). GUI-only: the TUI has no OS-window focus (it does not track host-terminal focus), so it passes focused=true and is unchanged — the host-terminal-focus TUI arm is a deferred follow-up, like R1426's TUI deferrals. This is the focus slice R1426 deferred (shipping the wrong half — a solid block when unfocused — is worse than none).
changes_bullets: pinion-runtime: paint_grid_cursor gains cursor_focused: bool — an unfocused window (false) draws a visible cursor as a HOLLOW outline box (span_w for wide cells, inset by half the stroke) overriding the shape, checked AFTER shown_this_phase so a hidden / off-phase cursor is never resurrected; focused (true) keeps the filled block / bar / underline. Threaded (like R1426 cursor_blink_on) through to_vello_cached_with_text_engine -> the cached walker -> paint_text_grid; the uncached / thin / headless entries force the focused default (true). Never stored in the scene (paint-time, so scene/snapshot stays stable, §2 #7).

pinion-runtime: CoreShell::arm_grid_cursor_blink gains a focused param — the blink clock enables ONLY when the window is focused AND carries a visible blinking cursor; an unfocused window disables its clock so grid_cursor_blink_on returns the steady ON phase (the cursor stops blinking on blur, as every real terminal does) and the window idles. The focus verdict is decided at the call site, so the TUI passes true and is unchanged.

pinion-shell: the live winit paint reads cursor_focused = is_key_dispatch_window(window) (the fails-open OS-focus predicate — unknown focus renders filled) and threads it into to_vello; a ShellCore::arm_grid_cursor_blink wrapper reads the SAME predicate for the stop-blink arm, so the hollow-render and stop-blink facts can never disagree (no blinking-hollow contradiction). The winit Focused arm requests a repaint on BOTH edges, so the fill/hollow + blink/steady transition lands on the next frame (an unfocused window otherwise idles and would latch the stale frame).

pinion-tui: the TUI arm passes focused = true — the TUI has no OS-window-focus concept (it does not track host-terminal focus) and is single-window, so its cursor stays filled + free-running, unchanged; hollow-on-blur is GUI-only (like multi-window), with the host-terminal-focus TUI arm a deferred follow-up.

hello-window-focus-multi: each window also carries a blinking block cursor grid (focus_cursor_grid); the shell paints it filled + blinking on the focused window and hollow + steady on the unfocused one, demonstrating the focus-gated cursor beside the R1419 per-window dimming.
verification_bullets: pinion-runtime: 1 test — an unfocused arm (focused=false) never enables the clock, so a blinking cursor is steady-ON and the window idles; refocus re-arms and the phase animates a half-period later; blur freezes it steady again. runtime 538 green.

pinion-shell: headless GPU pixel guard r1427_unfocused_text_grid_cursor_is_hollow (lavapipe) — the same block cursor renders a FILLED interior (cursor colour) when focused and a HOLLOW interior (cell background) plus an outline stroke when unfocused; the r1424 cursor-colour guard still passes (the focused / filled path is byte-unchanged). shell 180 green + guards.
hello-window-focus-multi: 1 test — both windows carry the identical blinking block cursor mode regardless of OS focus (focus is not scene data). example 3 green.

r1427_cursor_focus.py: 34 verifications PASS over RPC — the cursor snapshot is byte-identical across every focus configuration (focus never folds into the cursor, §2 #7; an AI reads hollow by correlating os_focused_window from scene/input_state), while the R1419 per-window dimming labels still track focus; the r1419 regression demo PASS.

clippy -D pedantic clean (a too_many_lines in compute_paint_scene_internal was fixed by lifting the focus-gated arm to a one-line ShellCore::arm_grid_cursor_blink wrapper); cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo doc --document-private-items clean (RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings); mnemosyne T1=0.
carry_forward_bullets: TUI host-terminal-focus (crossterm DECSET 1004 FocusGained / FocusLost + a character-cell hollow representation) stays a deferred follow-up — the TUI paints its own inverted cell (not the host hardware cursor), so hollow-on-blur is not free, and a 1px outline inside one text cell is genuinely hard; consistent with R1426's TUI deferrals. OS-focus stays GUI-only this round (like multi-window).

Introspection ergonomic (R1428 candidate, from the design review): a derived, non-stored window_focused: bool at the per-window scene/snapshot ENVELOPE (computed at serialize time from the os_focused_window SSOT, NOT on the GridCursor node) so an AI reads the cursor's hollow state from ONE RPC instead of correlating scene/snapshot with scene/input_state. Deferred because handle_scene_snapshot does not thread the window id + os_focused_window today; the data is already reachable (not a §2 #7 gap), so this is ergonomics — an explicit follow-up, not a closed decision.

The Vello paint walk now threads TWO cursor paint flags (cursor_blink_on R1426 + cursor_focused R1427) as bare bools; a THIRD would justify lifting them to a CursorPaintFlags struct. No lift yet (2 flags, the bare-bool style matches R1426; a swap is caught by the focus / blink tests + the GPU guard).

A two-reviewer + one-reviewer independent design audit shaped this round: hollow-box overrides shape (universal across xterm / VTE / alacritty / kitty / Windows Terminal / iTerm2), focus-hollow is orthogonal to blink (a steady cursor goes hollow too), and the biggest risk it caught — a focus-predicate mismatch (stop-blink fails OPEN, hollow fails CLOSED, giving a self-contradictory blinking-hollow cursor on unknown focus) — is closed by routing BOTH through one fails-open is_key_dispatch_window, plus a request_redraw on both focus edges.

R1428.decision_summary: R1428 §5.49 §5.39 §5.16 §5.41: expose a derived, non-stored per-window focused: bool on scene/input_state's key_dispatch, so an AI reads a terminal window's cursor filled-vs-hollow state (R1427) in ONE call instead of correlating a snapshot with a client-side compare of os_focused_window against a hard-coded window id. This is the R1427 review's introspection follow-up realized on the category-correct axis: auditing the snapshot path showed scene/snapshot returns a BARE node (no envelope), so wrapping it is a breaking wire change across every consumer and folding focus onto the node is the exact category error R1427 itself flagged. The input/focus axis already carries the os_focused_window SSOT, so focused joins it there. focused is the SAME fails-open predicate (is_key_dispatch_window) that gates key admission AND the R1427 cursor render: true when this window holds OS focus OR when no window's focus is known (the gate fails open) so the cursor renders filled, false when another window is focused so it renders hollow. The raw SSOT stays exposed beside it (both are one value projected, no drift). Derived per dispatch {window} scope in the shell's window_scoped_rpc_reads which already owns the resolved wid; the bare global builder is byte-unchanged for its many callers. GUI-only: the TUI leaves the whole key_dispatch axis None (single OS window), so hollow-on-blur stays GUI-only exactly like R1427.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: KeyDispatchFocus gains focused: bool — the fails-open per-window focus verdict, derived at snapshot time from os_focused_window and never stored (Default = false). It is the global os_focused_window fact PROJECTED onto a dispatch's {window} scope through the gate, distinct from the raw SSOT which stays on the same object.

pinion-shell: ShellCore::key_dispatch_focus_for_window(window_id) projects the global key_dispatch_focus() plus focused = is_key_dispatch_window(window_id) — the SAME fails-open predicate the R1427 cursor paint and key admission read. window_scoped_rpc_reads calls it with the already-resolved wid; the bare key_dispatch_focus() sets focused=false and is byte-unchanged for its global-fact callers (the R1074 tests).

pinion-rpc: handle_scene_input_state renders "focused": kd.focused in the key_dispatch object beside os_focused_window + key_press_owners, so an AI reads the exact bit predicting a window's cursor (true=filled, false=hollow) in ONE scene/input_state {window} call.

tools/demos: r1428_input_state_focused.py (36 assertions) proves per-window focused over RPC on hello-window-focus-multi; r885_input_state.py + r1419_window_focus.py updated for the new third leg in the key_dispatch key set (R47-class self-grep found both).
verification_bullets: pinion-core: input tests — the KeyDispatchFocus default reads focused=false; carries_dispatch_focus round-trips focused=true for a scope on the focused pane. core 2663 green.

pinion-rpc: r1428_scene_input_state_focused_is_a_derived_per_window_verdict — an unfocused scope (os_focused_window names another window) reads focused=false while the raw SSOT stays beside it; the fails-open case (os_focused_window null) reads focused=true, matching the R1427 filled cursor. rpc 924 green.

pinion-shell: r1428_key_dispatch_focus_for_window_derives_the_per_window_verdict — boot fails open (both windows true); focus main -> main true / inspector false (per-window identity, not a shared bool); the roles swap on one SSOT; app blur -> both true again; and focused == is_key_dispatch_window for both windows (one predicate, so introspection cannot drift from the render). shell 159 green.

The snapshot-envelope idea is therefore CLOSED (not deferred): the category-correct home is the axis that already owns the os_focused_window SSOT.

R1430.decision_summary: R1430 §5.35 §5.15 §5.49: complete the Qt QTabletEvent SCALAR axis set on the raw pointer surface — twist (W3C PointerEvent.twist / Qt rotation(), the barrel rotation), tangential pressure (W3C tangentialPressure / Qt tangentialPressure(), the airbrush finger wheel), and hover height (Qt z(), no W3C peer) — on top of R1423 pressure + R1429 tilt. Each is a positionless out-of-band axis driven by its own scene/pointer_* RPC (§2 #2, the AI-first primary path); winit 0.30 exposes NONE of them, so the RPC is the sole driver and every axis is exercisable headless with no tablet. Because pressure + tilt made pointer-axis storage a 2nd+ consumer, this round LIFTS the shared plumbing rather than copy-pasting a fifth time (three-site-internal-duplication-substrate-lift): the router's two per-axis HashMaps become ONE PointerAxisValues bundle forwarded WHOLE (forward_to) on every move, and the R1423/R1429 target-resolution copies fold into resolve_axis_target + deliver_axes. The External keeps per-axis hooks and the RPC keeps per-axis methods (self-describing for AI clients); only the internal duplication is removed. Both backends deliver the 3 new axes through the one set_pointer_*_for_window seam (§2 #6 parity), the TUI via a try_drain_pointer_axis dispatcher that routes all five axes off the main match. hello-raw-pointer paints each: twist orbits an orientation dot around the pen tip, tangential fills a finger-wheel bar, height shrinks the pen-tip marker; the r1430_tablet_axes.py demo drives all three over the wire. This answers the user's qt-parity-over-yagni directive to reach beyond Qt with nothing deferred: the scalar axes are done, leaving only the discrete pointerType classifier (R1431).

R1431.decision_summary: R1431 §5.35 §5.15 §5.49: add pointerType — the DEVICE that produced the pointer stream (W3C PointerEvent.pointerType / Qt QTabletEvent::pointerType()) — as the last member of Qt QTabletEvent, COMPLETING the tablet-event parity begun with pressure (R1423), tilt (R1429), and twist/tangential/height (R1430). PointerKind is a closed enum Mouse/Pen/Eraser/Touch (wire mouse/pen/eraser/touch, Default Mouse) in pinion-core; the Eraser variant keeps the stylus eraser end distinct — a Qt distinction W3C folds into pen — so an eraser-aware surface flips a paint canvas to erase without a device query. Unlike the five scalar axes, pointerType is a discrete classifier, but it rides the SAME PointerAxisValues bundle (a 6th field forwarded by forward_to) and the SAME set_pointer_*_for_window / try_drain_pointer_axis seams, so it needed no new plumbing — the R1430 lift already generalised the storage/forward/target-resolution. The RPC is scene/pointer_type {type: string}, which decodes via PointerKind::from_wire_name and rejects an unknown/missing/non-string device so a typo surfaces at the call. winit does not classify the device, so the RPC is the sole driver (§2 #2): a headless AI client presents as a pen or eraser with no tablet. hello-raw-pointer colours the pen-tip marker by device (accent pen / error-tone eraser / muted touch / on-surface mouse) and badges the readout; the pointer_type introspect field exposes it (§2 #7). This answers the user's qt-parity-over-yagni directive in full: the QTabletEvent surface is now implemented beyond Qt (every axis RPC-drivable + introspectable headless) with nothing deferred; the only unmodelled members are device-identity metadata (uniqueId / pointingDevice registry), not per-event axes a widget reacts to.

R1432.decision_summary: R1432 §5.35 §5.15 §5.49: open the native-gesture axis (Qt QNativeGestureEvent) after the QTabletEvent campaign closed at R1431, with its first member — a two-finger trackpad PINCH (magnify). External::pinch_gesture forwards the W3C wheel-with-Ctrl / macOS magnify: / Qt ZoomNativeGesture peer: a cursor-anchored incremental magnification bracketed by a GesturePhase arc (Begin/Update/End/Cancel). It rides the wheel hook's shape, not the tablet pointer-axis bundle — a gesture is a transient event delivered to the widget under the cursor (offer_pinch_to_external mirrors offer_wheel_to_external minus the Scene::Scroll fallback, since a native gesture has no default scroll action), not persistent per-pointer state. The RPC scene/pinch_gesture {at|path, magnification, phase} is the AI-first driver: winit 0.30 fires WindowEvent::PinchGesture only on macOS/iOS, so a headless client zooms a viewport with no trackpad (§2#2), and reads the scale back through introspect (§2#7). The GesturePhase is the point — the demo viewport accumulates magnification across Begin..End and DISCARDS the in-flight zoom on Cancel, reverting to the scale captured at Begin, exactly as a preview drops when the fingers lift without committing. Both GUI (winit source) and TUI (RPC-only) drains funnel through one ShellCore::pinch_gesture seam so a pinch-reactive External sees identical delivery (§2#6).

R1433.decision_summary: R1433 §5.35 §5.15 §5.49: continue the native-gesture axis (Qt QNativeGestureEvent) opened at R1432 with its second member — a two-finger trackpad ROTATION (twist). External::rotation_gesture forwards the Qt RotateNativeGesture / macOS rotation / winit RotationGesture peer: a cursor-anchored incremental rotation in DEGREES (positive = counter-clockwise, winit's sign convention) bracketed by the SAME GesturePhase arc pinch introduced (Begin/Update/End/Cancel). It rides the pinch shape, not the tablet pointer-axis bundle — a gesture is a transient event to the widget under the cursor, not persistent per-pointer state. Because the third native-input offer (wheel/pinch/rotation) would have been a third verbatim copy of the resolve-and-normalise scaffold, that boilerplate is lifted to offer_to_hovered_external with the per-gesture payload left in each caller's closure (the three-site internal-duplication substrate lift). The RPC scene/rotation_gesture {at|path, rotation, phase} is the AI-first driver: winit fires WindowEvent::RotationGesture only on macOS/iOS, so a headless client rotates a gizmo with no trackpad (§2#2) and reads the angle back through introspect (§2#7). The demo gizmo accumulates angle across Begin..End and DISCARDS the in-flight rotation on Cancel, reverting to the angle captured at Begin, exactly as a preview drops when the fingers lift without committing — a needle tip orbits the hub so the paint tracks the angle field. Both GUI (winit source) and TUI (RPC-only, via the try_drain_native_gesture sub-dispatcher) drains funnel through one ShellCore::rotation_gesture seam so a rotation-reactive External sees identical delivery on both backends (§2#6).

R1434.decision_summary: R1434 §5.35 §5.15 §5.49: continue the native-gesture axis (Qt QNativeGestureEvent) with its THIRD member — an N-finger trackpad PAN. External::pan_gesture forwards the Qt PanNativeGesture / winit PanGesture peer: a cursor-anchored incremental TWO-AXIS delta in LOGICAL PIXELS, bracketed by the same GesturePhase arc pinch introduced. It is the first gesture whose payload is not a single scalar, which is what actually tests R1433's offer_to_hovered_external closure-payload lift instead of merely re-using it, and the first that needs the window scale factor (winit reports the delta in physical pixels, so the shell converts at the boundary through the shared winit_pointer_to_logical, exactly as the pixel wheel and CursorMoved do). The delta keeps the platform's own sign: a native pan is direct manipulation — the content follows the fingers — so unlike the W3C-signed wheel it is never flipped. The R1433 carry's flagged name collision is paid off here rather than worked around: the private drag-latch struct PanGesture becomes DragPan and the pub predicate pan_gesture_in_flight becomes drag_pan_in_flight, because a held-button drag that pans is not a gesture in the native-gesture vocabulary — the same line Qt draws between QPanGesture and Qt::PanNativeGesture — so the platform-canonical name goes to the new axis and the implementation detail takes the precise one. Two more third-copy scaffolds are lifted on the way (the router's cursor/paint/hover guard preamble into hovered_gesture_target, the RPC phase decode into parse_gesture_phase), and the too_many_lines regression the new winit arm caused is fixed by extracting all three gesture arms into try_forward_native_gesture — the shell mirror of the TUI's try_drain_native_gesture — never by an allow. The RPC scene/pan_gesture {at|path, delta_x, delta_y, phase} is the AI-first driver: winit fires PanGesture only on iOS, the narrowest native source of the three gestures, so a headless client slides a map with no trackpad (§2#2) and reads the offset back through introspect (§2#7). The demo viewport accumulates the offset across Begin..End, saturates at a content bound, and DISCARDS the in-flight pan on Cancel; both GUI and TUI drains funnel through one ShellCore::pan_gesture seam so a pan-reactive External sees identical delivery on both backends (§2#6).

R1435.decision_summary: R1435 §5.35 §5.15 §5.49: CLOSE the native-gesture axis (Qt QNativeGestureEvent) with its fourth and last member — SMART-ZOOM, the two-finger double tap. External::smart_zoom_gesture forwards the Qt SmartZoomNativeGesture / macOS smartMagnifyWithEvent: / winit DoubleTapGesture peer, and it is the member shaped unlike the other three: NO GesturePhase and NO payload, because the platform reports one completed toggle. There is no arc to bracket, nothing to accumulate, and nothing a Cancel could discard — so the round's design question was what the gesture actually carries, and the answer is the anchor. That is not a leftover: the anchor SELECTS the object to fit, which is the entire meaning of 'smart' zoom, so a widget that ignores it has implemented a plain zoom toggle instead. The wire follows: scene/smart_zoom_gesture takes {at|path} and nothing else, and a stray phase key is IGNORED rather than rejected, because validating a lifecycle would advertise an arc this gesture does not have (a test pins the ignore so it reads as a decision). The naming takes Qt's semantic name over winit's input-shaped one on purpose — pinion already has scene/double_click (R663), a mouse-button event with a click count, and this is a buttonless trackpad gesture that must not be confused with it on the wire. The round is also where R1434's lifts pay for themselves: the fourth gesture entered the shell through ONE arm of try_forward_native_gesture instead of growing window_event, reused hovered_gesture_target unchanged, and made offer_to_hovered_external's closure span its full payload range (2D delta at one end, nothing at all at the other). It equally confirms R1434's audited decision NOT to collapse the per-gesture vertical slice behind a payload enum: the last member would not have fitted one. The demo toggles a three-block document page between fit-to-page and zoom-to-block, where the same block again restores but a DIFFERENT block re-targets while staying zoomed — the behaviour that separates a smart zoom from a binary in/out.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: External::smart_zoom_gesture(x_rel, y_rel, modifiers) -> bool default-false hook. R1436.decision_summary: R1436 §5.35 §5.49: give pinion-chart its CONTINUOUS colour scale — the sequential + diverging half of the dataviz palette item, the categorical half having landed at R1354. Where a categorical palette answers 'which series', a ColorScale answers 'how big' (sequential) or 'how far, and which way, from a meaningful zero' (diverging), which is the encoding a heatmap, a severity grid or a correlation matrix needs. The round's substance is the diverging contract: map_diverging normalises each wing on its OWN width so the data's neutral lands exactly on the ramp's centre stop, because real deviation data is asymmetric — the demo's -14..+32 matrix through a linear map would paint zero a third of the way up and a genuinely positive deviation would read as on-target. That is not argued in prose: the oracle publishes both the diverging colour and the linear one for the same cell, so the failure is observable over the wire. Interpolation goes through Color::lerp, i.e. linear light, and the module also takes in the WCAG trio (relative_luminance / contrast_ratio / readable_ink) LIFTED out of hello-heatmap, which had hand-rolled correct code in the wrong home — including a private sRGB EOTF duplicating core's. hello-heatmap is refitted behaviour-preserving (same colours, all nine tests unchanged and green) and a new hello-deviation-grid exercises the other kind on the other render path (diverging over vector Scene::Box vs sequential over Scene::TextGrid). Legibility is treated as verifiable data rather than decoration: every label is inked with the per-cell contrast winner, the grid publishes min_contrast, and the demo script RECOMPUTES WCAG independently in Python to cross-validate the crate's arithmetic. That measurement changed the design — the conventional near-black ink cleared the floor by 0.0005 on the vermillion end, so the demo pins pure black and asserts the margin. The round also carries an audit finding: the debt note's 'free-hover tooltip still absent, build hit-bands' item is STALE (the wants_hover_move seam landed R1405 with four consumers, hello-crosshair being the chart tooltip itself), so that workaround must not be built.
changes_bullets: pinion-chart: a new `color_scale` module — `ColorScale`, the CONTINUOUS peer of the categorical palette. `sequential(stops)` / `diverging(low, mid, high)` constructors plus two defaults: `viridis()` (a ten-stop sampling of matplotlib's perceptually-uniform, colour-blind-safe map, documented as the approximation it is) and `blue_orange()` (built FROM the Okabe-Ito hues the crate already ships, so its two colour systems agree and the ramp is colour-blind-safe by construction). `sample(t)` interpolates piecewise through `Color::lerp`, i.e. in LINEAR LIGHT, so a ramp does not darken through its middle.

pinion-chart: `map(value, min, max)` (linear) and `map_diverging(value, low, neutral, high)` — the latter normalises each wing on its OWN width so the data's neutral lands exactly on the ramp's centre stop even for an asymmetric domain. That is the whole contract of a diverging scale: through a linear map, data running -14..+32 would paint zero a third of the way up and a positive deviation would read as on-target. Both are total functions: out-of-domain clamps, a degenerate domain maps to the low end, NaN reads as the low end, and a scale built with too few stops falls back rather than panicking.

pinion-chart: the WCAG contrast trio `relative_luminance` / `contrast_ratio` / `readable_ink`, LIFTED from `hello-heatmap` (correct code in the wrong home) and rebuilt on `Color::to_linear` — the example carried its own private sRGB EOTF, a pure duplicate of core's. `readable_ink` picks the higher-contrast of two candidate inks per background, computed rather than thresholded.

examples/hello-heatmap: refitted onto the crate — its local ramp, its private EOTF and its own luminance/contrast pair deleted. Behaviour-preserving on purpose (same theme-derived `surface -> accent` colours, all nine existing tests unchanged and green): what moved is the machinery, not the taste.

examples/hello-deviation-grid: the NEW second consumer, exercising the OTHER kind on the OTHER render path — a diverging scale over a 6x10 deviation-from-baseline matrix painted as vector `Scene::Box` cells (the heatmap is sequential over `Scene::TextGrid`). The oracle publishes `color_at` AND `linear_color_at` for the same cell, so the linear map's failure at zero is observable over the wire rather than asserted in prose, plus `min_contrast` (the worst WCAG ratio over the grid) as a machine-checkable accessibility claim.

examples/hello-deviation-grid: the label inks are PINNED, not theme-derived — a theme ink is chosen against the app surface, not against the ramp cell it sits on, so a dark theme's pale ink over the light neutral would be unreadable, and the published contrast would describe numbers no viewer sees. The dark ink is pure black because the measurement demanded it: the conventional near-black `#1a1a1a` computes to 4.5005:1 on the vermillion end, clearing the WCAG floor by five ten-thousandths; black takes the same cell to 5.4:1.
verification_bullets: pinion-chart: 10 new `color_scale` tests — every stop reproduced EXACTLY at its own fraction; out-of-range and NaN clamp; a degenerate scale never panics; the linear map ranks and clamps outliers, and its black-to-white midpoint is LIGHT (the linear-light interpolation proven, since a naive byte lerp would give 128); a degenerate or inverted domain maps to the low end; the diverging map anchors zero on the neutral for the asymmetric -2..+8 domain WITH the counter-assertion that the linear map does not, plus equal saturation at the half-way point of each unequal wing; a one-sided domain is tolerated; viridis lightness increases monotonically (the property that makes it a legitimate sequential map); WCAG luminance/contrast match the published anchors (black 0.0, white 1.0, ratio 21.0, symmetric, identical = 1.0); and `readable_ink` clears 4.5:1 at all 21 sampled steps of the viridis ramp. 190 crate tests green.

examples/hello-heatmap: all 9 pre-existing tests green UNCHANGED after the refit (the ramp monotonicity and ink-choice tests now measure with the crate's helpers), and `r1408_heatmap.py` re-run PASS over RPC — the behaviour-preserving claim is tested, not asserted.

examples/hello-deviation-grid: 7 unit tests — the matrix spans both wings and crosses zero; a zero cell IS the neutral while the linear map's is not; each wing normalises on its own width; every cell clears WCAG 4.5 AND (a second assertion) clears it with margin, so a future ramp tweak cannot silently land back on the 4.5005 edge; the oracle publishes the model; the cell oracles answer and reject out-of-range / malformed / wrong-TYPE args as `Rejected` vs `TypeMismatch` (the two failure kinds told apart); cells are tagged and laid out without overlap inside the window.

r1436_deviation_grid.py PASS over RPC (55+ assertions): the domain is published and asymmetric; every on-target cell in the zero row paints the neutral; the linear map does NOT (the counter-proof, with an explicit "if these matched the demo would prove nothing"); the coldest cell is blue and the hottest warm, judged at the EXTREMES because a cell just past the baseline is legitimately near-neutral; a mild deviation sits between the neutral and the extreme; the worst-cell contrast clears 4.5 with margin; and — the strongest leg — WCAG is RECOMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY in Python (sRGB EOTF + BT.709 + the (L+0.05) ratio) and cross-validated against the crate's figures to within 0.01, with the chosen ink verified to beat the other candidate, so a bug in the Rust implementation cannot hide behind a test that calls it. Plus the paint agreeing with the model (cell rects, gaps, in-window), the readout naming the domain shape, four malformed cell args rejected, a read-only intervene rejected, and recovery after the rejects.

clippy -D pedantic clean on the three touched crates, every lint fixed AT THE SOURCE rather than allowed: the `usize -> f32/f64/i64/u32` casts became `From` conversions off `u32` extents, `!(max > min)` became an explicit NaN-aware predicate, `min`/`mid` became `low`/`neutral` (too-similar bindings), and the heatmap's now-test-only WCAG imports moved into its test module. fmt --all --check; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items --features pinion-runtime/vello exit 0; validate-workspace T1=0.
carry_forward_bullets: This clears the second half of the dataviz debt item #2 (the categorical palette landed R1354; sequential + diverging were what remained). The debt note's SSOT should now record #2 as done and — the audit finding below — stop describing three other items as absent.

AUDIT FINDING, recorded because the note asked for it: entering this round, `debt-dataviz-dashboard-substrate` listed a free-hover (no-button) chart tooltip as STILL ABSENT and proposed hit-bands as the workaround for a framework that "delivers only which TAG is hovered". Both halves are STALE: `External::wants_hover_move` landed at R1405 and already has four consumers (`hello-crosshair` R1406 is precisely the chart hover tooltip, plus hello-hyperlink / hello-heatmap / hello-raw-pointer). The hit-band workaround must NOT be built. The note's own advice — re-verify before building — is what caught it, for the second round running.

What remains in the dataviz list after this round: #3's force-directed LIVE auto-relaying topology view and a Brandes-Kopf straight-edge solver (the layered and force layouts themselves are built and example-local); user-facing data INPUT (chart data is still programmatic); and the `Brush` `Rescale`/`window_domain` sub-lifts, still waiting on a 3rd consumer.

`ColorScale` is NOT wired into any chart TYPE yet — no `ScatterChart::color_by` / treemap-fill-by-value. That is the natural third consumer and the point at which a value-encoded legend (a ramp strip with ticks) would be forced; deliberately not built speculatively here.

The crate now carries two colour systems (categorical + continuous) that agree by construction: `blue_orange` is built from the Okabe-Ito constants the categorical palette ships. If a future round adds more diverging defaults, they should keep that provenance rather than importing an unrelated published ramp.
`readable_ink` takes exactly two candidates. A consumer wanting N candidates or a WCAG AA/AAA threshold gate would force a richer API; two is what both consumers need today.

R1437.decision_summary: R1437 §5.15 §5.16: give the three OS file-drag/drop WidgetView hooks the window they fired on. The information was never missing — winit delivers the event per window, the RPC frame carries {window}, and the shell already used that id to pick which window to repaint — but run_file_hook consumed it for the redraw and handed the binding only the path, so the identity died one call short of the code that needed it. Every other window-scoped hook on the trait (view_for_window, access_node_for_window, window_close_requested, window_policy) already leads with window_id; these three were the outliers, which makes this a parity fix rather than a new capability. It matters because 'the drop target is the window' is only a contract if the binding can tell the windows apart: a multi-window binding could previously only guess, and the natural guess — route to the focused pane — mis-aims exactly when it matters, since X11 / Wayland DND does not focus a window before delivering the drop, so a file dropped on an unfocused torn-off panel lands in the focused one. The substrate threads the id THROUGH run_file_hook rather than letting each entry point capture it, so the window the binding routes on and the window the shell repaints are the same value by construction. Coordinates remain absent: winit 0.30's DroppedFile carries a path and nothing else, so the window is the finest target the platform offers, and the hook doc says so rather than implying a sub-widget hit-test is coming.
changes_bullets: pinion-shell WidgetView: on_file_hover / on_file_hover_cancel / on_file_drop now take window_id as their LEAD argument, matching view_for_window and access_node_for_window. Breaking for overriders only — all three keep their false default, so the census (cargo build --workspace --all-targets, the whole 20-crate / 115-example tree) rebuilt with exactly one binding touched.

pinion-shell substrate: run_file_hook's hook parameter became FnOnce(&str, &State) -> bool and the funnel passes window_id IN, instead of each file_*_for_window closure capturing it. A future entry point therefore cannot hand the hook one window and redraw another — the divergence is unrepresentable rather than merely untested. file_hover_cancel_for_window drops its closure entirely: the cancel hook's signature IS the hook shape (no path, no position — the OS reports neither on cancel).

pinion-rpc: the shared file-event handler doc now states the wire scoping — params.window picks the window the drop is ON (absent = primary), and since R1437 that id reaches the binding rather than only the repaint. The RPC leg needed no code change: window scoping was already there, which is precisely the shape of the gap.

examples/hello-filedrop: upgraded from one window to two PEER windows (main = Inbox, archive), each owning its own hover flag and path list keyed by window id through Owner::cache — Cow<'static, str> takes the runtime key, so no Box::leak. Peers, not a dialog and its parent: a mis-routed drop is only observable when the OTHER list is the one that must stay empty. view_for_window and access_node_for_window are overridden per window so paint and the AT tree read the same per-window state.
verification_bullets: Census, not grep: cargo build --workspace --all-targets exit 0 (15m55s, every crate and example compiled against the new signatures) — the authoritative answer to "who else overrides these hooks", and it said only hello-filedrop.

hello-filedrop 6 unit tests green, three of them new and about routing rather than mechanics: a drop addressed to the archive lands there AND the peer list stays empty; hover/cancel are window-scoped (cancelling one window leaves the other lit); and paint + AT agree per window (the archive paints its path and counts 1 while the inbox counts 0, and the AT name reports the hovered window's own state). The pre-existing R770 tests survive unchanged apart from the new lead argument.

r1437_filedrop_window.py PASS over RPC, 60 assertions across 10 phases: both windows declared and independently idle at boot; a drop lands in the window it names and NOT in the peer, in both directions; three follow-up drops addressed to the archive never drift (the tear-off case a focus fallback fails); hover lights only the addressed zone and cancel clears only the named one; a drag crossing windows leaves exactly one zone lit and drops where it ended; a frame with NO window param still addresses the primary, so the pre-R1437 wire shape is unchanged; unicode and space-bearing paths ride the routed path; and a final ledger asserts no path appears in both windows, each list in arrival order.

COUNTERFACTUAL, because a passing demo proves nothing on its own: with on_file_drop reverted to ignore its window argument and route everything to main — the pre-R1437 behaviour — the demo FAILS at phase 2 (the archive never receives the drop addressed to it). Restored, it passes again. r770_filedrop.py also re-run PASS, so the single-window arc including its live-pixel screenshot leg is unregressed.

R1438.decision_summary: R1438 §5.35 §5.49: teach a chart to encode MAGNITUDE in colour, and give it the legend that requires. Every chart in this crate until now colours by series identity — a categorical palette answering 'which one is this', a nominal channel where rank means nothing. A ColorScale answers 'how much is this', and R1436 built one without wiring it to any chart type, deliberately leaving the third consumer to force what the encoding actually needs. It needed two things. First a third data channel: DataPoint gains an optional value, carried ON the point rather than in a parallel index-keyed table (the Qt QXYSeries::setPointConfiguration shape), so a magnitude cannot fall out of step with the sample it describes. Second, and the real content of the round, a legend of a different KIND: a swatch row asserts that a colour names a series, which stops being true the moment colour means magnitude, so ScatterChart::color_by replaces the row with a colour bar. The bar is built from ColorScale::stop_offsets — where each stop sits along the DOMAIN under the live encoding — not from the scale's own even spacing, because for a diverging encoding over an asymmetric domain those are different numbers. That difference is the whole point: with the demo's -6..+18 deviation domain the target sits a quarter along the bar, and a bar that re-spaced the scale's stops evenly would misreport exactly the case map_diverging exists to fix. None of this is argued in prose. The oracle publishes color_at beside linear_color_at so the two maps' disagreement at the target is readable on the wire, and the strip's gradient stops ride in the scene as data, so an AI verifies a mark's fill against the published ramp without sampling a pixel — where a pixel-only colour-scale widget leaves it to the eye.
changes_bullets: pinion-chart `DataPoint` gains `value: Option<f64>` — the third data channel — plus a `with_value` builder. `DataPoint::new` keeps its two arguments, so all 107 existing construction sites are untouched (a census found zero literal struct constructions). The magnitude rides ON the point rather than in a parallel index-keyed side table, which is the Qt `QXYSeries::setPointConfiguration` shape: with no second array there is nothing to fall out of step.

pinion-chart `ScatterChart::color_by(scale)` / `color_by_diverging(scale, neutral)` / `with_color_domain(lo, hi)` — mark colour resolves from the point's value through `ColorScale` instead of from the series palette. The domain is measured by the new `value_bounds` (exported beside `data_bounds`) unless pinned. A point with no value keeps its series colour: the encoding covers the points that carry the channel and invents no magnitude for those that do not.

pinion-chart `ColorScale::stop_offsets(domain, neutral)` — the ramp as `(domain_fraction, colour)` pairs. For a sequential encoding these are the scale's own even spacing; for a diverging one the centre stop moves to the neutral's fraction of the domain and each wing spreads over its own side, mirroring `map_diverging`'s independent normalisation. This is what a colour bar must be built from, and it is exact rather than sampled: colour is piecewise-linear between stops, so a gradient with these offsets reproduces the mapping.

pinion-chart `draw::color_bar` — the value-encoding legend, the peer of `legend_row` and seated in the same top band. A gradient strip (`chart.colorbar.strip`) plus domain ticks (`chart.colorbar.tick.{k}`), with a third tick at the neutral for a diverging encoding. A value encoding REPLACES the categorical swatch row rather than adding to it: showing both would assert that colour means series identity and magnitude at once.

examples/hello-value-scatter: the consumer. Three probes over a latency/throughput plane, each sample carrying its deviation from target, over a deliberately ASYMMETRIC domain (-6..+18) so the diverging contract is observable. The encoding is switchable live over `scene/intervene`, and the oracle publishes `color_at` alongside `linear_color_at` so the two maps' disagreement at the target is readable on the wire. The External and the view share ONE reactive holder rather than each keeping a copy.
verification_bullets: pinion-chart 199 tests green (+9). The load-bearing one asserts that a diverging ramp over -2..+8 seats its centre stop at 0.2 — the neutral's fraction — and carries its own counterfactual: the same scale's sequential placement puts it at 0.5, so the assertion discriminates. A symmetric domain test pins the boundary case where the two placements coincide, so the diverging arm is not merely "always different". Every offset is cross-checked against the map it describes (the colour at each offset's value IS that stop's colour), which is what makes the legend and the marks one encoding rather than two agreeing by luck.

pinion-chart scatter tests: colour ranks value not series (two marks of one series differ; equal values across different series agree); a valueless point keeps its series colour WITH the counter-assertion that a valued point in the same series does move; the colour bar replaces the swatch row and both vanish under `legend = false`; and `color_by` over data with no third channel draws no bar at all.

examples/hello-value-scatter 5 unit tests: every sample carries the channel and the set spans both wings plus exact zeros; the domain is asymmetric by construction (the overshoot wing is 3x the shortfall wing, so the target sits at 0.25); the diverging and linear maps DISAGREE at the target; the bar reports the active encoding (0.25 diverging vs 0.50 sequential); and switching encodings moves the on-target mark while leaving the domain ENDS put — the ends being shared by both maps, which stops the first assertion passing for the wrong reason.

r1438_value_scatter.py PASS over RPC, 51 assertions across 10 phases: the asymmetric domain and its 0.25 neutral offset; the colour bar present with a real gradient and a non-zero rect (a zero-height strip would satisfy every stop assertion while being invisible); NO categorical swatches; the strip's middle stop at 0.25 read straight out of the paint scene; the two maps disagreeing at the target but agreeing at both domain ends; the on-target mark painted exactly the bar's neutral colour; equal values in different series sharing a colour; the live switch to sequential re-spacing the bar to 0.50 and dropping the neutral tick; the switch back; and typed rejections (OutOfRange for an unknown mode, ReadOnly for a derived projection, InterveneTypeMismatch for a wrong-typed value, plus rejected out-of-range and unparseable oracle arguments) followed by a working query.

COUNTERFACTUAL over the wire: with `stop_offsets` forced to even spacing for the diverging case, the demo FAILS at phase 3 reporting 0.5 where 0.25 was required; restored, it passes. Chart-consumer regressions re-run PASS: r1436_deviation_grid, r1377_scatter_scrub, r1408_heatmap.

Gates: cargo build --workspace --all-targets exit 0 (the census that also proves the `DataPoint` field is non-breaking); clippy -D pedantic clean on both touched packages with every lint fixed at the source (a doc-markdown item backticked, a nested tuple type named `Sample`, the view-fn `&Frame` allow that mirrors the trait signature); fmt --all; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items exit 0 after demoting two pub-doc links into private items and EXPORTING `value_bounds`, which the doc gate correctly flagged as the honest fix; validate-workspace T1=0.
carry_forward_bullets: This is the third consumer R1436's carry predicted for `ColorScale`, and it forced exactly what that carry said it would: a value-encoding legend. The bar now exists as a shared `draw` primitive beside `legend_row`, so a second chart type (treemap fill-by-value, a heatmap chart type) inherits it rather than re-deriving one.

`color_by` is scatter-only for now. The obvious next consumers are a treemap whose fill encodes a metric separate from its area, and a line chart whose marks encode a per-sample magnitude; neither is built speculatively, and the bar is placed where they would reach for it.

A point that carries no third channel keeps its series colour, which is a defensible default but a MIXED encoding when a chart has some of each. A dedicated "no value" ink would be the alternative; no consumer needs it yet, and the current behaviour is at least the pre-encoding one rather than an invention.

The colour bar seats itself in the legend band and spans the plot width. A vertical bar (the more common orientation for a tall colour scale, and what `QCPColorScale` defaults to) is not built: the horizontal form is what fits the existing legend slot, and a second orientation should be forced by a consumer whose layout needs it rather than added for symmetry.

`stop_offsets` describes a piecewise-linear ramp exactly. A future non-linear scale (log, quantile, or a perceptual re-spacing) would need the bar to sample the mapping instead of placing stops, and that is the round where the two would stop coinciding.

The load-bearing one asserts that a diverging ramp over -2..+8 seats its centre stop at 0.2 — the neutral's fraction — and carries its own counterfactual: the same scale's sequential placement puts it at 0.5, so the assertion discriminates. A symmetric domain test pins the boundary case where the two placements coincide, so the diverging arm is not merely "always different". Every offset is cross-checked against the map it describes (the colour at each offset's value IS that stop's colour), which is what makes the legend and the marks one encoding rather than two agreeing by luck.

pinion-chart scatter tests: colour ranks value not series (two marks of one series differ; equal values across different series agree); a valueless point keeps its series colour WITH the counter-assertion that a valued point in the same series does move; the colour bar replaces the swatch row and both vanish under `legend = false`; and `color_by` over data with no third channel draws no bar at all.

examples/hello-value-scatter 5 unit tests: every sample carries the channel and the set spans both wings plus exact zeros; the domain is asymmetric by construction (the overshoot wing is 3x the shortfall wing, so the target sits at 0.25); the diverging and linear maps DISAGREE at the target; the bar reports the active encoding (0.25 diverging vs 0.50 sequential); and switching encodings moves the on-target mark while leaving the domain ENDS put — the ends being shared by both maps, which stops the first assertion passing for the wrong reason.

r1438_value_scatter.py PASS over RPC, 51 assertions across 10 phases: the asymmetric domain and its 0.25 neutral offset; the colour bar present with a real gradient and a non-zero rect (a zero-height strip would satisfy every stop assertion while being invisible); NO categorical swatches; the strip's middle stop at 0.25 read straight out of the paint scene; the two maps disagreeing at the target but agreeing at both domain ends; the on-target mark painted exactly the bar's neutral colour; equal values in different series sharing a colour; the live switch to sequential re-spacing the bar to 0.50 and dropping the neutral tick; the switch back; and typed rejections (OutOfRange for an unknown mode, ReadOnly for a derived projection, InterveneTypeMismatch for a wrong-typed value, plus rejected out-of-range and unparseable oracle arguments) followed by a working query.

COUNTERFACTUAL over the wire: with `stop_offsets` forced to even spacing for the diverging case, the demo FAILS at phase 3 reporting 0.5 where 0.25 was required; restored, it passes. Chart-consumer regressions re-run PASS: r1436_deviation_grid, r1377_scatter_scrub, r1408_heatmap.

Gates: cargo build --workspace --all-targets exit 0 (the census that also proves the `DataPoint` field is non-breaking); clippy -D pedantic clean on both touched packages with every lint fixed at the source (a doc-markdown item backticked, a nested tuple type named `Sample`, the view-fn `&Frame` allow that mirrors the trait signature); fmt --all; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items exit 0 after demoting two pub-doc links into private items and EXPORTING `value_bounds`, which the doc gate correctly flagged as the honest fix; validate-workspace T1=0.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: This is the third consumer R1436's carry predicted for `ColorScale`, and it forced exactly what that carry said it would: a value-encoding legend. The bar now exists as a shared `draw` primitive beside `legend_row`, so a second chart type (treemap fill-by-value, a heatmap chart type) inherits it rather than re-deriving one.

`color_by` is scatter-only for now. The obvious next consumers are a treemap whose fill encodes a metric separate from its area, and a line chart whose marks encode a per-sample magnitude; neither is built speculatively, and the bar is placed where they would reach for it.

A point that carries no third channel keeps its series colour, which is a defensible default but a MIXED encoding when a chart has some of each. A dedicated "no value" ink would be the alternative; no consumer needs it yet, and the current behaviour is at least the pre-encoding one rather than an invention.

The colour bar seats itself in the legend band and spans the plot width. A vertical bar (the more common orientation for a tall colour scale, and what `QCPColorScale` defaults to) is not built: the horizontal form is what fits the existing legend slot, and a second orientation should be forced by a consumer whose layout needs it rather than added for symmetry.
