R1570.4.decision_summary: R1570.4 §5.16 — THE JUSTIFICATION R1570.2 SHIPPED NAMED A SYMBOL THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE CENSUS THAT FOUND IT WAS THE SECOND ONE. R1570.2 chose `apply_key = <strategy>` over a second bare flag and justified it in a doc comment by claiming a second strategy was "already implied by the tree — `menu_apply_key`, the command-menu family's canonical body (R772.1)". There is no `menu_apply_key`. The real R772.1 helper is `WidgetCore::forward_key_to_external`, and censusing THAT shows the claim was stronger than the tree supports: its five callers are all hand-written `impl WidgetCore` blocks with no `#[widget]` attribute, so a `= forward_to_external` strategy would have ZERO macro consumers today. The keyed form is still right, but on its own merits — `apply_key` already means "forward to an inherent fn", and a bare `apply_key_aria` beside it would say nothing about the two being alternatives, which is the confusion the parser now refuses at the point of declaration. A second strategy is a CANDIDATE, not a plan, and the doc says so. TWO THINGS ARE WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX. `cargo doc` DID NOT CATCH IT: the invented name sat in a backticked prose span, not an intra-doc link, and the gate that has caught ~1150 broken links since R1214 only resolves the linked form. A name in prose is unchecked, which is exactly where a plausible-sounding invention survives. AND THE FIRST CENSUS SAID IT WAS FINE: asked "is every carry registered", it matched carry keywords against the memory directory and reported hits — but the hits were the index, a round narrative, and a file already marked CLOSED. Re-asking with the criterion that actually matters, "is there an OPEN debt file that mentions it", turned two of the same items from registered into unregistered. That is the R1565.1 class again, and the lesson is the criterion, not the count: a census whose predicate is looser than the question answers a different question and reports it as an answer to this one.
changes_bullets: `pinion-derive` `APPLY_KEY_STRATEGIES` doc — the invented `menu_apply_key` is replaced by the real `WidgetCore::forward_key_to_external`, with the census beside it: five callers, all hand-written `impl WidgetCore`, so a second strategy would have no macro consumer today. Stated as a candidate rather than as a queued entry.

Written as a code span rather than an intra-doc link on purpose, and the doc says why: `pinion-core` is only a dev-dependency of this proc-macro crate, so the link cannot resolve. The first attempt at the correction tried to link it and the doc gate refused — which is the gate working on the form it can see.

`debt-focus-sweep-population-is-curated` registered (memory): `r1518_at_focus_one_answer` asserts every binding it walks has a focus stop, over a hand-written list of 14. A curated population cannot find an absence, which is why 17 bindings with NO stop stayed invisible; R1570.1 added a second sweep with a derived population instead of fixing this one, so the tree now has two focus sweeps and they are not merged.
verification_bullets: The claim was checked by GREP-THEN-MEASURE, not by reading: `menu_apply_key` has one occurrence in the whole tree and it is the doc comment that invented it.

`forward_key_to_external`'s consumers were then censused by exact body: 5 callers, 1 with the bare body, and 0 of the 5 are `#[widget]` bindings. That is what turns "a second strategy is implied" into "a second strategy is a candidate".

THE CENSUS CRITERION WAS ITSELF THE FINDING. Round one matched carry keywords against `memory/*.md` and reported 3 hits for two items, read as registered. Round two asked whether any OPEN debt file mentions them — index entries, round narratives and CLOSED files do not count — and both came back UNREGISTERED.

The corrected criterion was then run over all five candidate items with a negative control (`zzz-impossible-item`, correctly UNREGISTERED). Four are registered; the fifth is this round's own corrected claim, which is a statement rather than an open item and is recorded in the round file instead.
`cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` clean, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, `cargo clippy -p pinion-derive --all-targets` 0 issues, `cargo test -p pinion-derive` 24 passed.
carry_forward_bullets: A SYMBOL NAMED IN BACKTICKED PROSE IS UNCHECKED. `cargo doc`'s broken-intra-doc-link gate (R1214/R1218) resolves `[`X`]` and `[`X`](path)`, not `` `X` ``, so any doc comment in this tree can name a function that does not exist and no gate objects. Closing it means a source scan that resolves backticked identifiers against the crate's symbols — plausible, and larger than this round.

`debt-focus-sweep-population-is-curated` is registered and untouched: merging the two focus sweeps will go RED while `debt-a11y-focus-stop-absent-from-tree` is open, so the round that widens r1518's population has to decide whether to absorb that or close it first.

R1570.5.decision_summary: R1570.5 §5.39 §5.16 — R1570.1's CLOSED WAS A PARTIAL CLOSURE WRITTEN AS A TOTAL ONE, AND WIDENING THE GATE FOUND SIX MORE. Asked whether the debt was really paid, the honest move was to audit the label rather than read it. R1570.1 scoped its population to bindings whose `#[widget(...)]` attribute names an interactive `role` — 23 — and closed on "23 of 23". That is not the class: **89** bindings in the tree construct an interactive `AriaRole`, and the other 66 write their `WidgetA11y` impl by hand. The gate inherited the same parse, so it could not see them either: a derived population is only as wide as the thing it derives from, which is R1518's curated-list defect one level less obvious, and the third time in this session a census predicate was narrower than the question it was answering. MEASURED, over the wire, on release binaries: of the 65 hand-written ones that speak RPC on stdin, **59 had a focus stop and 6 did not** — `hello-frame-profiler`, `hello-grouped-sort`, `hello-listbox-multi`, `hello-radio-group`, `hello-scene-scale`, `hello-virtual-sort`. Two of those are a radio group and a multi-select listbox, widgets whose entire subject is the keyboard. AND ONE OF THE SIX ESCAPED MY OWN FIRST RE-MEASUREMENT: `hello-frame-profiler` has a `#[widget]` attribute that declares no `role`, so it fell out of the attribute census AND out of the "hand-written impl" census I ran to check it. It appeared only once the gate's population became "constructs an interactive AriaRole" — the widening is what found it, not the probing. THE GATE NOW ASKS TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS OF TWO POPULATIONS, which is the honest shape rather than a uniform one: a binding that DECLARES `role` + `tag` is asked whether THAT tag is focusable and in the Tab order, and a hand-written one — whose roles live inside an impl this scan will not parse — is asked only whether the window has any focus stop at all. Weaker, and still exactly the defect: a control announced as operable that no keyboard can reach. It also asserts that the hand-written half OUTNUMBERS the declared one, so an `AriaRole` scan that silently stops matching reads as a failure rather than as a tree with no such bindings. The six are fixed the way the tree already did it where it was right — one Tab stop on the widget's primary tag container, which is what `hello-grouped-list` has had all along. 65 of 65, and the gate goes from 77 assertions over 23 bindings to 143 over 88.

Two questions, because only one population can be asked a precise one: a declared binding is asked whether ITS tag is focusable and enumerated; a hand-written one is asked whether the window has any stop at all. The weaker question is still the defect this gate exists for.

It asserts the hand-written half outnumbers the declared one. A scan that stops matching would otherwise read as "the tree has no such bindings", which is exactly how the first version passed while covering a quarter of the subject.

One stop per widget on the primary tag is the pattern `hello-grouped-list` already used; the interactive roles in these bindings sit on composite SUB-REGION tags, which are addressed through that one stop rather than each being their own.

R1570.6.decision_summary: R1570.6 §5.12 — THE OTHER TWO "CLOSED" LABELS AUDITED THE SAME WAY, AND ONE OF THEM HAD A REACH GAP. R1570.5 found that a CLOSED label can be a scoped closure written as a total one; the honest follow-through is to apply that test to the labels written beside it rather than to trust them because they were written by the same hand an hour earlier. Two were audited. `debt-r1570-widget-macro-hand-rolled-bodies` has a real REMAINDER — 10 byte-identical bodies still in the tree (7 `apply_key`, 3 `event_name`) — and the label survives, but only because an argument was written that had not been: all ten are hand-written `impl WidgetCore` blocks whose bodies are ALREADY a one-line call into shared substrate, so the duplication is the trait-method wrapper, and the only way for a hand-written impl to inherit a body in Rust is a trait default that `WidgetCore::apply_key` deliberately does not have (most widgets want `keybinding` or geometry-aware navigation, which is the same reason R772.1 left `forward_key_to_external` opt-in). Removing them means converting those bindings to macro bindings, which is a per-binding decision and not "delete this duplication" — so the item is a language floor rather than unpaid work, and the file now says so instead of implying it. `debt-demo-harness-leaks-hung-process` had a REACH gap: two demos launch a process OUTSIDE `RpcSubprocess` — `r1447_font_free_tui` through a pty and `r794_file_drag_move` for its XTest helper — and both used the pre-R1570.3 shape, `terminate/wait/kill` with no wait after the kill. The sweep's residual backstop covers them, which is exactly why it exists, but catching a leak is worse than not making one, so both now route through `terminate_process_tree`. AND THE OWNERSHIP OF A FAILURE WAS DECIDED BY A CONTROL, NOT BY READING THE DIFF. Patching `r794` was immediately followed by a FAIL in a phase my change does not touch. Restoring the HEAD version in place passed; my version then passed eight consecutive times. So the failure is a PRE-EXISTING FLAKE — one observation in nine — registered with its measurement and its candidate causes rather than absorbed as noise or papered over with a larger timeout. It is the second such flake on the books, and it lives in a demo CI usually SKIPS for want of XTEST, which is why it has never appeared in a CI statistic.
changes_bullets: `tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py` + `tools/demos/r794_file_drag_move.py` — both route their own launched process through `terminate_process_tree` instead of a bare `kill()` with no follow-up wait. They are the only two demos that launch outside `RpcSubprocess`, so R1570.3's teardown fix did not reach them; a re-census confirms both now use the shared reap and that there is no third.
`r1447` asserts the reap succeeded. `r794` folds the leak into its SKIP message, because that path is already a skip and turning it into a failure would report an environment absence as a defect.

memory `debt-r1570-widget-macro-hand-rolled-bodies` — the CLOSED label keeps its scope but gains the argument it was missing: the 10 remaining identical bodies are a Rust floor for a hand-written `impl`, not unpaid work, and the file names all ten.
memory `debt-demo-harness-leaks-hung-process` — records the reach gap this audit found and that it is closed.
memory `debt-r794-native-drag-flake` (new) — an observed, UNFIXED flake, with the control that proved it pre-existing, the rate, the candidate causes, and the reason it is invisible to CI.
verification_bullets: THE LABELS WERE AUDITED, NOT TRUSTED. `debt-r1570-widget-macro-hand-rolled-bodies`: measured 10 identical bodies still present (7 `apply_key` + 3 `event_name`), all in hand-written `impl WidgetCore` blocks. `debt-demo-harness-leaks-hung-process`: censused the launchers and found 2 outside the harness.

The Rust-floor argument was CHECKED before being written: `WidgetCore::apply_key`'s trait default is `false`, so a hand-written impl cannot inherit the ARIA body without changing a default that most widgets must not have.

★OWNERSHIP BY CONTROL, NOT BY READING. `r794` failed right after being patched, in a phase the patch does not touch. `git show HEAD:` restored in place PASSED; the patched version then passed 8 consecutive runs (2 + 6). One failure in nine, and the diff only touches an `except` branch that did not execute.

The flake is REGISTERED, not fixed and not silenced: rate, control, candidate causes (XTest moves a real pointer against a 0.9s hold window while this session drove the same display), and the warning that adjusting the constant to hide 1-in-9 is the rerun-and-forget the zero-flake policy forbids.
`tools/test_rpc_verify.py` 11 passed, `tools/test_hooks.sh` 78 passed, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
`r1447_font_free_tui` PASS (131.8s, it runs its own `cargo test`), `r794_file_drag_move` PASS.
carry_forward_bullets: `debt-r794-native-drag-flake` is OPEN and unfixed by design: 1 observation in 9, cause unconfirmed. Fixing it needs a reproduction first — under load, N runs — because raising the 0.9s hold window to cover a 1-in-9 is exactly the rerun-and-forget the zero-flake policy forbids. Second flake on the books after `r1182_node_edge_autopan`.
The 10 identical bodies remain and will remain until someone decides, per binding, whether it should be a macro binding. That decision is not this round's and the file says why.

Auditing a CLOSED label is now something this session has done three times and found something twice. There is no gate for it: nothing checks that a debt file marked CLOSED has a closure argument proportional to its claim.

R1571.decision_summary: R1571 §5.27 §5.12 §5.40 — AN EDITOR'S PERSISTENCE IS A PROPERTY OF THE EDITOR, AND R1555'S OWN PRESCRIPTION FOR THIS ROUND WAS WRONG. Qt's `QAbstractItemView::openPersistentEditor(index)` keeps N editors open at once; R1544 and R1555 each closed naming its absence as the DCC axis's remaining item, and R1555 also wrote down the fix — widen `use_text_edit_state`'s `&'static str` key so a per-cell buffer can be cached at a runtime id, which `Owner::cache` has accepted since R685.C. BUILDING IT IS HOW YOU FIND OUT IT IS WRONG: `Owner` has `cache`, `cache_contains` and `cache_get_by_str` and NO REMOVAL OF ANY KIND, so a per-cell buffer is retained for every cell ever edited, for the life of the window — unbounded growth on the million-row models this campaign is named for, exactly the class R1550 built `scene/memory` to see. An editor's buffer has to die with the editor, so the buffers live in the editor SET. What that set needs then follows from a fact about THIS framework rather than about Qt: there is exactly ONE KEYBOARD FOCUS, where Qt has one focusable `QWidget` per editor. So only the focused editor holds the shared inline field; every other open editor's text is PARKED in the latch and swapped back when focus returns — one field tag, one focus stop, one composition target, the keystroke/IME/clipboard machinery untouched, and the editor set is plain data that can be windowed, enumerated and published. PERSISTENCE IS A PROPERTY OF THE EDITOR rather than a second collection, which is what makes "a cell has at most one editor" true by construction; Qt keeps an index-to-widget hash beside a private `QSet<QWidget *>` and reconciles them by convention. FIVE THINGS PAST QT 6.11, all read over the wire: the set is ENUMERABLE (`scene/grid_editors` — Qt's only public question is `isPersistentEditorOpen(index)`, one index at a time, so you must already know the answer to ask it); FOCUS IS DATA (in Qt, `QApplication::focusWidget()` reverse-mapped through that private hash); ESCAPE REVERTS a persistent editor and keeps it open (`QAbstractItemView::closeEditor` checks `d->persistent.contains(editor)` and returns without touching it, so Escape there does NOTHING AT ALL and the original is unrecoverable); each editor's in-flight value and DIRTY flag are readable WITHOUT FOCUSING IT (Qt keeps no record of what `setEditorData` seeded); and the COST IS WINDOWED (an editor outside the painted rows contributes no scene node and keeps its value, where `updateEditorGeometries()` walks every persistent editor on every scroll). A COUNTERFACTUAL FOUND A REAL DEFECT AND ITS FIX IS THE DESIGN: the set's fourth invariant was stated one-directionally — "at most one live buffer and it belongs to the focused editor", which "nobody holds the field" satisfies while the focused editor's cell still PAINTS one — so it is now stated both ways, and the paint branches on the BUFFER rather than on a second `focused` flag.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::widgets::grid_edit` — `EditorPersistence` (Transient / Persistent) as a field on `OpenEditor`, Qt's private persistence set made a property of the editor; `OpenEditors` as the whole set with four invariants re-checked on every transition AND on deserialize (R1561's rule for `IndexRuns`, one level richer).

`EditBuffer` gains `Parked(String)` beside `Live` and `Value`: a text-buffered editor that does not hold the keyboard parks its text in the latch. `hand_over_field` is the single author of `EditBuffer::Live`, which is what makes invariant 4 hold.

Verbs: `open_persistent` (Qt `openPersistentEditor`, answering `OpenOutcome::{Opened,Promoted,AlreadyOpen}` where Qt returns `void`), `close_persistent`, `focus_editor`, `close_all`, `commit_at_with`, `state_at`, `is_dirty_at`, `text_at`, `editor_at`, `is_persistent_editor_open`. `open` became `focused`, because with N editors "the open editor" is not a thing.

`GridEditState::open_cells(rows, edit_at)` is the WINDOWING seam: the open editors whose cells lie in the painted rows, each with the model's edit role re-asked this frame. An editor whose cell the model has since made read-only is dropped from the ANSWER and left OPEN — closing it in a paint pass would be a §6.3 purity violation.

`pinion-widget-paint::table` — `GridEditing::open` is a slice of `OpenCell` rather than one `CellIndex`; `RowPane::editing` is a slice, because a property row with two editable columns is the ordinary case. `editor_field_node` is the lifted text half of an editor (3rd consumer: field / stepper / swatch), painting the live field when this editor OWNS THE BUFFER and a static box holding its parked text otherwise.

`pinion-rpc::grid_editors` — `scene/grid_editors {tag}` publishes the whole set: count, `field_tag`, the focused cell, and per editor its persistence / kind / form / focused / dirty / malformed / value / seed, in canonical cell order. Read-only, and the reason is stated: opening needs a `CellEdit` only the model produces (R1544), so a framework verb that opened one would invent an edit role the model never answered with.

Qt's `QAbstractItemView::openPersistentEditor(index)` keeps N editors open at once; R1544 and R1555 each closed naming its absence as the DCC axis's remaining item, and R1555 also wrote down the fix — widen `use_text_edit_state`'s `&'static str` key so a per-cell buffer can be cached at a runtime id, which `Owner::cache` has accepted since R685.C. BUILDING IT IS HOW YOU FIND OUT IT IS WRONG: `Owner` has `cache`, `cache_contains` and `cache_get_by_str` and NO REMOVAL OF ANY KIND, so a per-cell buffer is retained for every cell ever edited, for the life of the window — unbounded growth on the million-row models this campaign is named for, exactly the class R1550 built `scene/memory` to see. An editor's buffer has to die with the editor, so the buffers live in the editor SET. What that set needs then follows from a fact about THIS framework rather than about Qt: there is exactly ONE KEYBOARD FOCUS, where Qt has one focusable `QWidget` per editor. So only the focused editor holds the shared inline field; every other open editor's text is PARKED in the latch and swapped back when focus returns — one field tag, one focus stop, one composition target, the keystroke/IME/clipboard machinery untouched, and the editor set is plain data that can be windowed, enumerated and published. PERSISTENCE IS A PROPERTY OF THE EDITOR rather than a second collection, which is what makes "a cell has at most one editor" true by construction; Qt keeps an index-to-widget hash beside a private `QSet<QWidget *>` and reconciles them by convention. FIVE THINGS PAST QT 6.11, all read over the wire: the set is ENUMERABLE (`scene/grid_editors` — Qt's only public question is `isPersistentEditorOpen(index)`, one index at a time, so you must already know the answer to ask it); FOCUS IS DATA (in Qt, `QApplication::focusWidget()` reverse-mapped through that private hash); ESCAPE REVERTS a persistent editor and keeps it open (`QAbstractItemView::closeEditor` checks `d->persistent.contains(editor)` and returns without touching it, so Escape there does NOTHING AT ALL and the original is unrecoverable); each editor's in-flight value and DIRTY flag are readable WITHOUT FOCUSING IT (Qt keeps no record of what `setEditorData` seeded); and the COST IS WINDOWED (an editor outside the painted rows contributes no scene node and keeps its value, where `updateEditorGeometries()` walks every persistent editor on every scroll). A COUNTERFACTUAL FOUND A REAL DEFECT AND ITS FIX IS THE DESIGN: the set's fourth invariant was stated one-directionally — "at most one live buffer and it belongs to the focused editor", which "nobody holds the field" satisfies while the focused editor's cell still PAINTS one — so it is now stated both ways, and the paint branches on the BUFFER rather than on a second `focused` flag.

R1572.decision_summary: R1572 §5.41 — THE TWO NON-CANONICAL BOX-DRAWING RENDER SPOTS R1181 REGISTERED AS DEBT, CLOSED — AND THE DEBT NOTE UNDERSTATED BOTH OF THEM. Asked which debt remained, the honest move was a census rather than a read of the labels, and it found `box-drawing-canonical-render-debt` **open and not registered in the memory index at all** — a user directive ("the user explicitly wants these closed in a future session, cost-no-object textbook bar") sitting unpaid and invisible since R1181. SPOT 1, the arc seam: `box_arm_rects` snaps its filled bands to the pixel grid so abutting cells tile without a hairline, while the rounded corners were stroked about the UNSNAPPED `xm` / `ym` straight out of `box_line_metrics`. Where an arc met a straight neighbour the two centre lines differed by up to half a pixel — never a gap, which is exactly why R1181's own connectivity guard could not see it. Two derivations of one fact; `snapped_line_centre` is now the single answer to "where is this line", and the arms' bands are provably unchanged by it. THE DEBT NOTE WAS WRONG TO GROUP DIAGONALS WITH THE ARCS: a diagonal is stroked corner to corner, its endpoints are the cell corners its neighbours share exactly, and `BoxGlyph` is an enum so no glyph pairs a diagonal with a straight arm — they never meet at a mid-line to disagree about. Recorded as a correction rather than fixed. SPOT 2, the mixed junctions: R1181 used one uniform rule — "when ANY arm is double, EVERY arm overshoots the centre by the rail half-separation `d`" — and the note said the pure-double glyphs `╔╗╚╝╠╣╦╩╬` "render cleanly". THEY DO NOT. That rule ran BOTH rails of every arm to the outer line, so `╔` came out with its corner filled in rather than as an open right angle between two rail pairs, `╬` came out as a `#` with continuous rails instead of four elbows around an open centre, and `╠` welded its branch onto an unbroken line instead of interrupting the inner rail. The mixed single/double glyphs the note DID name (`╒` `╓` `╞` `╡` `╥` `╨`) grew a stub poking out past the perpendicular line they should have stopped at. ONE RULE REPLACES IT, asked per RAIL rather than once per glyph (`rail_reach`): a rail of a DOUBLE arm facing a side where ANOTHER DOUBLE ARM ATTACHES stops at the NEAR perpendicular line; every other rail runs to the FAR one. That is the whole of it, and it produces every canonical form — the break opens `╬`, interrupts `╠`'s inner rail and gives `╔` its inner corner, while a single line is never broken so `║`, `╫` and `╪` stay continuous. A SINGLE LINE IS EXEMPT BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a special case: the break exists to keep two parallel rails legible where a third line crosses them, and a lone line has nothing to stay legible against.
changes_bullets: `snapped_line_centre(c, t)` — the one answer to "where is this line once it is snapped". `box_arm_rects` derives its bands from it (identical to the `(c - t / 2.0).round()` it already used, pinned by a test) and the arc is stroked about it, so the two cannot drift.

`rail_reach(rail_is_double, facing, perpendicular_double, d)` — the per-rail replacement for R1181's uniform overshoot, with `BOX_WEIGHT_DOUBLE` naming the `3` that `1` (light) and `2` (heavy) sit beside.
`box_arm_rects`'s `push_h` / `push_v` now take the arm's weight and its direction rather than a precomputed span, and compute each rail's reach from the side that rail faces.

`box_arc_path(down, right, cell)` — the arc's geometry extracted as a PURE FUNCTION, for the reason `box_arm_rects` is one. It was inline in `paint_box_drawing`, which is why a counterfactual that reverted the painter to the raw centre passed every assertion: a derivation only the painter calls is a derivation no test can hold it to.

`crates/pinion-shell/src/headless_screenshot.rs` — a live-pixel guard for both claims, since both are claims about pixels. `╭──` across a seam and `╔══` beside it, on a 20px cell chosen because `round(20/8) == 3` is ODD, which is the only case where the snapped and raw centres differ at all.
The recorded debt's diagonal claim is CORRECTED in place in `snapped_line_centre`'s doc rather than left to be re-read as a gap.
verification_bullets: `pinion-runtime` 664 tests PASS, `pinion-shell` 213 PASS, including R1181's own `r1180_box_arm_rects_geometry_and_connectivity` and `r1180_box_drawing_lines_connect_across_cells` UNCHANGED — the snap lift moves no band, and the reach rewrite breaks no through-line.

Six new geometry tests: the band/centre equality and its idempotence; the arc meeting its straight neighbour on both axes across four cell sizes; no stub on `╒` `╞` `╡` `╥` `╨` with `╓`'s single arm still reaching the OUTER rail; `╔` open and `╬` four elbows with each rail proved interrupted; `╠`'s outer rail continuous and inner rail broken while `╫` breaks neither; and every pure single / heavy / double line still spanning its cell edge to edge.

Live-pixel guard PASS on a real wgpu adapter: the arc's stub and its straight neighbour cover the SAME fully-covered rows across the seam, and `╔`'s inner rail is background where the uniform overshoot painted it.
COUNTERFACTUAL CF-A: R1181's exact uniform rule restored. The corner, cross and tee tests all go red.

★CF-A's FIRST DRAFT PASSED THE STUB TEST, AND THAT WAS THE DISCIPLINE WORKING: I had written `perpendicular_double` where R1181 wrote `any_double` — a counterfactual that was a DIFFERENT, partly-correct rule rather than the defect. Re-run faithfully, all three go red.

★COUNTERFACTUAL CF-B PASSED AND WAS A FINDING: reverting the arc to the raw centre left every assertion green, because the test asserted a property of `snapped_line_centre` and nothing asserted the PAINTER used it. Extracting `box_arc_path` and asserting on the emitted path is the fix; CF-B then goes red. R1559's lesson, one layer over.

★COUNTERFACTUAL CF-D PASSED AND WAS A SECOND FINDING: the pixel guard's first `╔` probe was the cell CENTRE, which is background under R1181's rule too — a probe placed where both renders agree. Moved to the inner vertical rail in the gap between the horizontal pair; CF-D then fails with `got 255`.

CENSUS FINDING, independent of the fix: FIVE debt topic files are absent from the memory index, and two of them are genuinely open — this one, and `pinion-text-layout-tests-system-font-debt` (pixel-geometry layout tests still shape through the system font, a latent zero-flake exposure). Both are now registered.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D pedantic` over both crates: clean. Clippy named two real things — an unbalanced backtick pair in a doc line and three `manual_midpoint` sites.
carry_forward_bullets: `pinion-text-layout-tests-system-font-debt` IS STILL OPEN and is now registered rather than invisible: `LayoutCache` builds its `FontContext` over the platform scan, so pixel-geometry layout tests read the host's fonts. R835 fixed the one test that had already broken in CI by making it font-independent; the caret-rect coordinate assertions were left passing by luck of tolerance. The mechanism to close it exists (`register_font_data`, and `NotoSans-Regular.ttf` is already vendored for exactly this), so the round that closes it is a sweep with a gate, not research.

THE OTHER THREE UNREGISTERED FILES ARE CLOSED OR EXTERNAL and are registered as such: the two dock ones (`dock-ssot-completion-debt` R1167-R1169, `dock-outer-dock-title-bar-and-band-debt` R1202-R1203) and `sce-upstream-debts` (vendor/sce upstream, the permanent external carry).

`╬`'s eight rails are the `[KurboRect; 8]` cap exactly, and the cap is now load-bearing in a second way: the broken-rail form emits the same count as the continuous one did, so a future glyph family that needed a ninth rect would overflow silently. The array is indexed by a running counter with no bound check.

The pixel guard is `#[ignore]`d with the other wgpu cold-boot guards, so it runs in CI and not in the default local suite. That is the established shape here, and it means the ink claim is verified one push later than the geometry claim.

R1573.decision_summary: R1573 §5.36 — A CACHE CAN BE TOLD TO USE ONLY THE FONTS IT IS GIVEN, AND THE R835 DEBT IT CLOSES WAS NOT "LATENT" — IT WAS 43% OF THE SUITE. `LayoutCache`'s `FontContext` is the platform font database, so every metric a test measured was a function of whatever faces the machine happened to have. R835 registered that when GitHub Actions first ran the suite and a caret test failed on a pixel tolerance tuned to a local font; it fixed that ONE test by making its assertion font-independent and recorded the rest as "잠재 fragile" — latent. MEASURED AT R1573 by pointing `FONTCONFIG_FILE` at a config with no font directories: **40 of 94 unit tests changed their answer or panicked**. A note that says "latent" where the number is 43% is a note nobody ran. THE FIX IS A CONSTRUCTOR, NOT A CONVENTION. `LayoutCache::with_own_fonts()` builds a cache whose collection is never scanned from the platform, so a registered face is not merely PREFERRED — it is the only face that exists, and a test using the fixture over it CANNOT read the host because there is nothing to read. THE ATTRIBUTION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN CLAIMED, and it is the round's most honest number: a counterfactual that kept the fixture on `LayoutCache::new()` — registering the face and setting it as the default family, which is EXACTLY what R835's own note prescribed — took the count from 40 to **5**, not to 4. So the bulk of the determinism comes from the note's plan. The constructor closes one more test, and that one test is not the reason for it: register-and-default makes the guarantee CONDITIONAL, holding only while every `TextStyle` resolves to the named default, so a style that names another family or text the face does not cover silently falls back to the machine and no assertion anywhere notices. With the scan off there is nothing to fall back to. That is the difference between a debt CLOSED and a debt NARROWED. FOUR TESTS STILL READ THE HOST AND EACH ONE'S SUBJECT IS THE HOST: two resolve the GENERIC `monospace` keyword through the platform (this tree vendors no monospace face, and vendoring one is a standing prohibition — and registering one would stop the test testing generic-family resolution at all), and two go through the production metric providers, whose job is to use the application's fonts. AGAINST QT 6.11: Qt has the two halves this builds on — `QFontDatabase::addApplicationFont` and `QApplication::setFont` — and not this one. `QFontDatabase` always carries the system families, `removeAllApplicationFonts()` removes only the application's, and there is no supported way to tell a `QFontDatabase` to forget the platform's. A Qt application cannot make its own text metrics independent of the host.
changes_bullets: `LayoutCache::with_own_fonts()` — a cache that consults only the faces it is given. `font_source::own_fonts_context()` builds the unscanned collection, distinct from the `SystemFontStatus::Unavailable` path that reaches the same collection because the host FAILED: this one is a declaration, so it reports `NotProbed` and `font_scans() == 0` forever.

The `system_fonts` flag is a FIELD, not a constructor-time decision, because `font_cx` is built lazily (R1447) — the answer has to survive until the first shape. R1550's destructuring `Footprint` impl refused to compile until the new field was named on a row, which is that gate working exactly as designed.

`crates/pinion-text/src/test_font.rs` — the deterministic fixture: `own_font_cache()` registers the vendored `NotoSans-Regular.ttf` (the same face `pinion-text-font` parses and `pinion-shell` installs for its pixel guards, so a unit metric and a screenshot metric are the SAME metric) and makes it the default family. It PANICS if the face does not register under its expected name, because a fixture that has quietly stopped working reports green for the wrong reason.
52 of 54 test-region cache constructions migrated to the fixture across `cache.rs`, `caret.rs`, `font_metrics.rs`.

Nine sites keep `LayoutCache::new()`, each with an `R1573` comment AT THE SITE saying why the host is its subject: an empty-cache footprint measurement, four scan/probe tests, the default-family-starts-unset claim, and three generic-`monospace` resolutions.

`r1573_no_test_shapes_through_the_host_without_saying_so` — a source-scan gate over those three files' test regions. An unannotated `LayoutCache::new()` fails by NAME AND LINE; the annotated count is asserted against a written budget, so adding a tenth host-reading test forces a reason rather than passing silently.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE: `FONTCONFIG_FILE` pointed at a font-directory-free config, `cargo test -p pinion-text --lib` → **40 of 94 FAILED**. AFTER: **4 of 98 failed**, and all four are named with the reason their subject is the host.
`pinion-text` 98 PASS on the host as well, so the suite is deterministic without being weaker.
Consumers re-run because their behaviour depends on this crate: `pinion-runtime` 664 PASS, `pinion-widget-paint` 812 PASS.

COUNTERFACTUAL CF-A: a migrated test reverted to `LayoutCache::new()`. The gate fails naming `caret.rs:660` — so a test added later that reaches for the obvious constructor is caught by name and line.
COUNTERFACTUAL CF-B: `with_own_fonts` drops its flag and scans after all. `r1573_the_fixture_never_touches_the_platform_database` fails on `font_scans() == 0`.

★COUNTERFACTUAL CF-C WAS THE ROUND'S MOST USEFUL RESULT: the fixture reverted to `LayoutCache::new()` while still registering the face and setting the default gives **5** failures, not 40. That is the attribution — the R835 note's own plan does most of the work — and it is written into the module doc rather than left as an implied claim that the constructor did it all.

★THE GATE'S FIRST RUN FAILED ON ITS OWN EXPLANATORY COMMENT: the exception notes say `LayoutCache::new()` out loud, and the scan matched the comment as a call. Found by running it, not by reading it. Comment lines are now skipped, and the skip says why.

★THE ONE-TEST REMAINDER IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED: `r1573_an_unregistered_family_cannot_reach_the_host` names a family the fixture never registered. It measures exactly **0** — machine-independent — where a host-reading cache resolves it through the platform stack to a width that is a property of the machine. My first version of that assertion guessed the wrong deterministic value (it expected a fallback to the registered face); running it corrected the claim, and the honest cost of `with_own_fonts` is now stated in its own doc.
`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p pinion-text --all-targets -D pedantic`: clean.
carry_forward_bullets: FOUR TESTS STILL READ THE HOST, each with the reason recorded at its call site. Two are generic-`monospace` resolutions — closing them needs a monospace face, and vendoring an external font is a standing prohibition in this repo; registering one would also stop them testing generic-family resolution, which is their actual subject. Two go through the production metric providers, whose job is to use the application's fonts; their assertions are relative (a longer string measures wider), so they are font-independent in substance and fail only where nothing can be measured at all.

THE GATE COVERS `pinion-text/src` ONLY. `tests/font_less_host.rs` is deliberately outside it: that integration test's whole subject is the font-less host. Other crates' tests that build a `LayoutCache` are not scanned — `pinion-runtime` and `pinion-shell` both do, and `pinion-shell`'s pixel guards already install the same face for the same reason. Whether they carry the same latent exposure is UNMEASURED; the probe that measured it here (`FONTCONFIG_FILE` at an empty config) is one command and would answer it.

`with_own_fonts` has ONE production consumer: none. Its consumer is this crate's test fixture, and it is published as a capability because "my fonts are the whole font world" is a real requirement for a kiosk, a game and a PDF exporter — the [[qt-parity-over-yagni]] rule, with Qt sitting BELOW the floor here rather than at it. A binding-level adoption (`ShellConfig::with_own_fonts`) is the named next slice.

The budget in the gate is a NUMBER, so a rename cannot break it — but two changes that cancel (one exception removed, one added) pass. Naming them would break on rename instead. Neither form is strictly better and the number is the one that forces a reason at the site.

R1574.decision_summary: R1574 §5.38 §5.39 — A SWITCH HAS A PAINTER, AND THE DEBT NOTE THAT ASKED FOR IT COUNTED 12 CONSUMERS WHERE THERE WERE 2. `pinion-widget-paint` carries a painter per catalog widget — button, checkbox, radio_composite, slider, tabs, disclosure — and had no `switch`, so a binding whose control is a Material 3 switch painted its own pill track and knob. `crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/switch.rs` closes that: `SwitchStyle` + `switch_track_for` / `switch_knob_for` + `view_switch`, with the tag, the keyboard focus stop, the accessible name, the M3 role mapping and the knob's justification in ONE place. Qt has NO switch widget at all — `QCheckBox` is the checkbox and QML's `Switch` is a different toolkit — so this is not parity, it is a floor Qt does not have, and the hand-rolled consumers here are the same tax a Qt codebase pays with the difference that they are all visible in one tree. THE COST THE ABSENCE HAD ALREADY IMPOSED was not a duplicated drawing but a duplicated DECLARATION: when R1570.1 made "a declared interactive role is a keyboard focus stop" true of the tree, `hello-checkbox` needed one line on the painter that owns its tagged node, while ten bindings had to repeat `.with_focusable(true)` because there was no painter to put it on — [[r1532-column-declares-its-painter]]'s rule one axis over. ★★THE CENSUS IS THE ROUND'S SECOND HALF, AND IT CORRECTS THE DEBT NOTE TWICE. The note said twelve bindings hand-roll a track and knob; that counted `role = Switch` BINDINGS rather than switch PAINTS. Classified by geometry, exactly TWO paint an M3 switch — a `Start`/`End`-justified 64×32 track with a 24×24 knob — `hello-toggle` and `hello-theme`, and both are migrated, so the painter ships with every consumer it has. The other nine or more paint a **labelled toggle chip**: `JustifyContent::Center`, a wide low box of 120–190 x 36, centred text, NO KNOB. That is a different widget, and `view_switch` does not draw it. `hello-image`'s apparent knob was a variable holding a colour name. THE NOTE'S CAUSAL CLAIM WAS THEREFORE ALSO MIS-ATTRIBUTED: most of R1570.1's ten repeated declarations were chips, so the prescription for that cost is a CHIP painter, which is registered as its own debt rather than folded in here — a different widget does not belong in the same file. R1570.5's lesson again, in the opposite direction: a population derived from the wrong predicate is wrong by as much as the predicate is.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/switch.rs` — `SwitchStyle` (track/knob geometry + `focusable`), `switch_track_for` / `switch_knob_for` (M3 role mapping through the shared `state_layer`), `view_switch` (the tagged, focusable pill track with the knob justified to one end).
`SwitchStyle::focusable` defaults `true`, and on this painter the default IS the point: it is the declaration R1570.1 had to add by hand in ten bindings because no painter owned their tagged node.
The knob travels by `JustifyContent`, not by an offset, so a binding that widens the track gets the right throw with no arithmetic.

The disabled KNOB is a deliberate divergence from `state_layer`: it fades toward `OnSurfaceMuted` rather than toward `Surface`, because a thumb fading toward the surface vanishes into its own track and a switch whose thumb cannot be found reads as a track with no state. It references `state_layer::DISABLED` so the weight still lives in one place.

`aria_label` is a required argument, not an option: a switch's caption is almost always a SIBLING of the track, so the scene-walk name derivation cannot reach it. `""` is a legal opt-out meaning "the caption is inside this subtree", and it produces NO `aria-label` rather than an empty one — an empty name announces as nameless, which is worse than letting the walk find the caption.
`hello-toggle` and `hello-theme` adopted it and dropped their now-dead geometry constants; both keep their own row layout, caption and status line, which the painter deliberately does not own.

`debt-no-toggle-chip-painter` registered with the geometry table for the nine-plus bindings that paint a labelled chip, and `debt-no-switch-painter` closed with the corrected census rather than with the count it was written with.
verification_bullets: Painter units: 6 PASS — the tag and the focus stop on ONE node; a binding declining both; the knob travelling by justification and the track taking its width from the style; on/off differing in BOTH track and knob (a switch that changed only its track would be unreadable in a monochrome palette); the track overlay being the shared `state_layer` at all four states x both values; the disabled knob staying distinguishable from its own track.
BEHAVIOUR PRESERVATION IS THE ADOPTION PROOF: `hello-toggle`'s own 8 tests and `hello-theme`'s own 6 pass UNCHANGED, and `pinion-widget-paint` goes 812 -> 818 with no existing test touched.

Demos PASS: `hello_toggle_activate`, `hello_toggle_click`, `hello_toggle_style` (the three that drive the migrated reference consumer), plus `r723_theme_inverse` and `r724_scene_tick` (every demo that drives `hello-theme`).

COUNTERFACTUAL CF-A: the painter drops its focus declaration — the exact defect R1570.1 fixed ten times by hand. `r1574_the_tag_and_the_focus_stop_are_on_the_same_node` goes red. The three toggle demos stay GREEN under it, which is honest rather than a gap: none of them is about the focus stop, and R1570.5's wire gate is what covers that class.

★THE MIGRATION FIXED A REAL DRIFT IT WAS NOT LOOKING FOR: `hello-theme`'s hand-rolled `match` collapsed Idle/Hover/Pressed into one arm, so hovering that switch painted NOTHING. Routing through the shared `state_layer` gives it the 8% / 12% overlay every other control has. That is the drift a per-binding copy accumulates, caught by removing the copy rather than by inspecting it.

★THE CENSUS IS MEASURED, NOT READ: each `role = Switch` binding's `main_toggle` node was classified by its own `with_justify` and `Size::px` — 2 `Start`/`End` 64x32 switches against 8 `Center` 120-190x36 chips, with 3 unclassified and named as such.
`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D pedantic` over `pinion-widget-paint` + both bindings: clean.
carry_forward_bullets: `debt-no-toggle-chip-painter` IS OPEN AND IS THE REAL REMAINDER: nine-plus bindings hand-roll a labelled toggle chip, and R1570.1's ten repeated `.with_focusable(true)` declarations are mostly THEIRS, so the repetition that motivated this round is not yet paid. Registered with the measured geometry table and a prescription that follows this round's file exactly, because it is the same axis and the same contract.

THREE BINDINGS ARE UNCLASSIFIED: `hello-pdf-export`, `hello-frame-profiler` and `hello-toggle-tui` declare `role = Switch` and their `main_toggle` node did not match either geometry. Named in the chip debt rather than assumed into it — the whole point of this round's census correction is that assuming a classification is how the 12 got written down.

CF-A WAS NOT RUN AGAINST R1570.5's WIRE GATE WITHIN THE SESSION. `r1570_1_interactive_role_is_a_focus_stop.py` release-builds ~88 bindings and had not reported when the round closed; the unit test does discriminate, and the wire coverage of this class was established at R1570.5. Stated rather than implied.

`view_switch` does not own the row, the caption or the status line, deliberately — folding them in would refuse the bindings whose switch sits in a toolbar rather than beside a label. The consequence is that a caption's font size and gap are still per-binding, and two switches in this tree can still disagree about them.

The other nine or more paint a **labelled toggle chip**: `JustifyContent::Center`, a wide low box of 120–190 x 36, centred text, NO KNOB. That is a different widget, and `view_switch` does not draw it. `hello-image`'s apparent knob was a variable holding a colour name. THE NOTE'S CAUSAL CLAIM WAS THEREFORE ALSO MIS-ATTRIBUTED: most of R1570.1's ten repeated declarations were chips, so the prescription for that cost is a CHIP painter, which is registered as its own debt rather than folded in here — a different widget does not belong in the same file. R1570.5's lesson again, in the opposite direction: a population derived from the wrong predicate is wrong by as much as the predicate is.
publishable_changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/switch.rs` — `SwitchStyle` (track/knob geometry + `focusable`), `switch_track_for` / `switch_knob_for` (M3 role mapping through the shared `state_layer`), `view_switch` (the tagged, focusable pill track with the knob justified to one end).
`SwitchStyle::focusable` defaults `true`, and on this painter the default IS the point: it is the declaration R1570.1 had to add by hand in ten bindings because no painter owned their tagged node.
The knob travels by `JustifyContent`, not by an offset, so a binding that widens the track gets the right throw with no arithmetic.

The disabled KNOB is a deliberate divergence from `state_layer`: it fades toward `OnSurfaceMuted` rather than toward `Surface`, because a thumb fading toward the surface vanishes into its own track and a switch whose thumb cannot be found reads as a track with no state. It references `state_layer::DISABLED` so the weight still lives in one place.

`aria_label` is a required argument, not an option: a switch's caption is almost always a SIBLING of the track, so the scene-walk name derivation cannot reach it. `""` is a legal opt-out meaning "the caption is inside this subtree", and it produces NO `aria-label` rather than an empty one — an empty name announces as nameless, which is worse than letting the walk find the caption.
`hello-toggle` and `hello-theme` adopted it and dropped their now-dead geometry constants; both keep their own row layout, caption and status line, which the painter deliberately does not own.

`debt-no-toggle-chip-painter` registered with the geometry table for the nine-plus bindings that paint a labelled chip, and `debt-no-switch-painter` closed with the corrected census rather than with the count it was written with.
publishable_verification_bullets: Painter units: 6 PASS — the tag and the focus stop on ONE node; a binding declining both; the knob travelling by justification and the track taking its width from the style; on/off differing in BOTH track and knob (a switch that changed only its track would be unreadable in a monochrome palette); the track overlay being the shared `state_layer` at all four states x both values; the disabled knob staying distinguishable from its own track.
BEHAVIOUR PRESERVATION IS THE ADOPTION PROOF: `hello-toggle`'s own 8 tests and `hello-theme`'s own 6 pass UNCHANGED, and `pinion-widget-paint` goes 812 -> 818 with no existing test touched.

Demos PASS: `hello_toggle_activate`, `hello_toggle_click`, `hello_toggle_style` (the three that drive the migrated reference consumer), plus `r723_theme_inverse` and `r724_scene_tick` (every demo that drives `hello-theme`).

COUNTERFACTUAL CF-A: the painter drops its focus declaration — the exact defect R1570.1 fixed ten times by hand. `r1574_the_tag_and_the_focus_stop_are_on_the_same_node` goes red. The three toggle demos stay GREEN under it, which is honest rather than a gap: none of them is about the focus stop, and R1570.5's wire gate is what covers that class.

★THE MIGRATION FIXED A REAL DRIFT IT WAS NOT LOOKING FOR: `hello-theme`'s hand-rolled `match` collapsed Idle/Hover/Pressed into one arm, so hovering that switch painted NOTHING. Routing through the shared `state_layer` gives it the 8% / 12% overlay every other control has. That is the drift a per-binding copy accumulates, caught by removing the copy rather than by inspecting it.

★THE CENSUS IS MEASURED, NOT READ: each `role = Switch` binding's `main_toggle` node was classified by its own `with_justify` and `Size::px` — 2 `Start`/`End` 64x32 switches against 8 `Center` 120-190x36 chips, with 3 unclassified and named as such.
`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D pedantic` over `pinion-widget-paint` + both bindings: clean.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: `debt-no-toggle-chip-painter` IS OPEN AND IS THE REAL REMAINDER: nine-plus bindings hand-roll a labelled toggle chip, and R1570.1's ten repeated `.with_focusable(true)` declarations are mostly THEIRS, so the repetition that motivated this round is not yet paid. Registered with the measured geometry table and a prescription that follows this round's file exactly, because it is the same axis and the same contract.

THREE BINDINGS ARE UNCLASSIFIED: `hello-pdf-export`, `hello-frame-profiler` and `hello-toggle-tui` declare `role = Switch` and their `main_toggle` node did not match either geometry. Named in the chip debt rather than assumed into it — the whole point of this round's census correction is that assuming a classification is how the 12 got written down.

CF-A WAS NOT RUN AGAINST R1570.5's WIRE GATE WITHIN THE SESSION. `r1570_1_interactive_role_is_a_focus_stop.py` release-builds ~88 bindings and had not reported when the round closed; the unit test does discriminate, and the wire coverage of this class was established at R1570.5. Stated rather than implied.

The consequence is that a caption's font size and gap are still per-binding, and two switches in this tree can still disagree about them.

R1574.2.decision_summary: R1574.2 §5.7 §2 #6 — THE CI RED WAS A FLAKE, AND MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF IT WAS WRONG. The pre-push stop-the-line gate refused to publish R1571-R1574 because main's last completed CI run (`31066749248`, on R1570.6) had FAILED — which is the gate working: the rule is ratified and its only prior enforcement was prose until R1495 made it a hook. `cargo test --workspace` at HEAD passed locally (310 suites, 0 failures), so the red did not reproduce, and I HYPOTHESISED HOST-FONT DEPENDENCE — R1573 had just removed 40 of those, the R835 debt note records CI catching exactly that class once before, and an empty font database does make 40 tests fail at R1570.6. Plausible, coherent, and WRONG. gh 2.4.0 has no `run view --log`, which is what had stopped me reading the actual failure; `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/jobs/<id>/logs` works on it and gave the answer in one call: `pinion-tui/tests/rpc_ingress.rs:771`, `delivered_count` `Some(2)` where `Some(1)` was expected — R1552's terminal change-stream test, nothing to do with fonts. THE ROOT CAUSE IS PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE READ FROM A SHARED TEST BINARY. `pinion_rpc::process_registry()` is what its name says, the test subscribes to it and then asserts its stream's delivered count, and `cargo test` runs a binary's tests in PARALLEL THREADS OF ONE PROCESS — so any of the twenty-three siblings in that file that advances the scene revision (a click, a key, an invoke, a focus set, a tick) delivers to this armed subscription too. Reproduced locally at 1 run in 8, which is why the earlier full-workspace pass proved nothing. THE FIX IS THE LANGUAGE'S OWN ANSWER TO PROCESS ISOLATION: cargo compiles every `tests/*.rs` into its own binary and therefore its own process, so the test moves to `tests/rpc_subscribe.rs` alone. That makes the interference STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE rather than statistically unlikely — no `--test-threads=1` (which would slow every test in the crate to fix one), no serial-test dependency, and no assertion weakened to a delta that would still race against a sibling that also delivers. THE CLASS WAS AUDITED, NOT ASSUMED: `pinion-rpc`'s own twelve subscription tests each build a private `SubscriptionRegistry::new()`, so this was the ONLY site in the tree reading the global registry from a shared binary.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-tui/tests/rpc_subscribe.rs` — new test binary holding `r1552_a_terminal_connection_is_written_to_unprompted` and its `RecordingEgress` helper, moved out of `rpc_ingress.rs` unchanged. Its module doc records the measurement (1 in 8), the CI run id, why cargo's one-binary-per-file rule is the fix, and the three alternatives rejected with reasons.
`crates/pinion-tui/tests/rpc_ingress.rs` — the R1552 block removed; 23 tests remain, none of which reads the global registry.

`docs/SEED_PROMPT.md` + `memory/MEMORY.md` — the "CI GREEN" claim I wrote at session entry is CORRECTED: R1570.6's run was `in_progress` when I read it and I reported R1570.3's green as the state of main.
verification_bullets: ROOT CAUSE READ FROM CI, not inferred: `gh api repos/newmassrael/pinion/actions/jobs/92505941615/logs` gave the failing assertion verbatim. `gh run view --log` does not exist on gh 2.4.0 (this machine) — the `gh api` route does, and that is now recorded as the way to read a CI failure here.
REPRODUCED LOCALLY BEFORE THE FIX: 1 of 8 runs of `cargo test -p pinion-tui --test rpc_ingress` FAILED on the same assertion with the same values.
AFTER: 30 consecutive runs of both binaries, 0 failures. `cargo test -p pinion-tui` fully green (167 + 23 + 1).

★COUNTERFACTUAL CF-A PROVES ISOLATION IS THE FIX RATHER THAN CHANCE: adding ONE scene-advancing sibling test into the new binary brings the flake back at **12 of 12** runs — not intermittently, always. Removing it restores 0 of 30. A 30-run green streak alone would have been consistent with luck; this is not.

CLASS AUDIT: every `process_registry()` reference in the tree was enumerated. Seven files reference it; six are production. The only test-side reader was this one, and `pinion-rpc`'s twelve subscription tests build `SubscriptionRegistry::new()` privately — measured, not assumed.

THE LEDGER REFUSED A SUB-ROUND ROW AND WAS RIGHT: `phase_b_tally.py --selftest` failed with `round '1574.2' is not a number`. The ledger's own rule is one row per INTEGER round because git folds sub-rounds; the row was removed and the selftest passes.
`cargo clippy -p pinion-tui --all-targets -D pedantic`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo doc -p pinion-tui --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean.
carry_forward_bullets: THE PUSH STILL NEEDS `PINION_PUSH_ON_RED=1`, because the gate reads the last COMPLETED run on main and that run stays red until a new one succeeds. This commit is the fix for it, which is exactly the case the override exists for (`target-budget.sh`'s sibling doc: "a stop-the-line rule with no way to push the fix stops the line permanently"). Whether the red is now GONE is not verifiable from here — only the next CI run answers that, and if another failure is hiding behind this one it will surface then.

MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND THE COST WAS REAL: a full `cargo test --workspace` build plus a worktree at the failing commit, spent on a font hypothesis, when one `gh api` call had the answer. The lesson is recorded as a tool fact (`gh api .../jobs/<id>/logs`) rather than as a resolution to be more careful.

THE 1-IN-8 RATE IS THIS MACHINE'S. It is a function of core count and thread interleaving, so the CI runner's rate is unknown and could be higher. That does not affect the fix — isolation removes the race rather than reducing it — but it does mean the historical record cannot say how many past CI reds were this same test.

THE SAME PATTERN CAN RECUR WITH NO GATE TO CATCH IT: nothing in the tree forbids a future test from reading `process_registry()` counters inside a shared binary. A gate would be a source scan asserting that every test-side reader of the global registry lives in a file with exactly one `#[test]`. Not built here; registered as the honest next slice rather than claimed.

R1574.3.decision_summary: R1574.3 §5.36 — R1573 SHIPPED A MIXED-FONT COMPARISON, AND ONLY CI COULD SEE IT. `font_metrics::tests::text_seam_delivers_a_real_per_string_measurement` asserts that the extent the production metric provider reports is the CEILING of the shaped advance. `long.width()` comes from `LayoutCacheTextMetrics`, the production provider, which shapes through the PLATFORM fonts; R1573's blanket migration rewrote the raw side to `own_font_cache()`, the deterministic NotoSans-only fixture. Two different fonts on the two sides of a ceiling relation. It passed on this machine because the host's fonts happen to shape `report.pdf` close enough to NotoSans that the ceiling still held, and CI failed it at `65 vs 62.309`. THE EXCEPTION LIST MISSED IT FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON WORTH RECORDING: R1573 restored nine sites whose subject is the host, and every one of them was a `let mut cache = ...` at the TOP of its test — the shape I was scanning for. This one is a `LayoutCache::new()` buried mid-body inside a `f64::from(...)`, compared against a value produced twenty lines earlier. A blanket rewrite plus an eyeball restore finds the sites that look like the pattern, not the sites that are the pattern. THE FIX IS THE SIBLING TEST'S OWN REASONING, APPLIED: `seam_delivers_measured_cell_into_owner_scope` already carried the comment "both sides of the equality read the same host, so the assertion is a comparison rather than an absolute metric" — that is exactly this test's situation and I did not apply it here. The raw side shapes through `LayoutCache::new()` again, so both sides read whatever fonts the machine has and the ceiling relation is a property of the PROVIDER rather than of the font. THE GATE CAUGHT MY OWN MARKER: `r1573_no_test_shapes_through_the_host_without_saying_so` requires the `R1573` note within six lines of the call, and my first fix put a seven-line comment above it, so the gate reported the site as unannotated. Binding the cache to a local first puts the two adjacent — the gate is doing its job on its author, which is the only kind of gate worth having. `HOST_SUBJECT_SITES` goes 9 -> 10.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-text/src/font_metrics.rs` — the raw advance in `text_seam_delivers_a_real_per_string_measurement` is shaped through `LayoutCache::new()` again, with the reason at the site: the other side of the comparison came from the production provider, which shapes through the platform.
`crates/pinion-text/src/test_font.rs` — `HOST_SUBJECT_SITES` 9 -> 10, the budget the gate asserts against.
verification_bullets: ROOT CAUSE READ FROM CI, one `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/jobs/<id>/logs` call — the tool fact R1574.2 recorded, used immediately.

★VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL FAILURE MODE, NOT AGAINST THIS HOST: a fontconfig config exposing exactly ONE face (NanumGothic) simulates a machine whose fonts differ from mine. 97 of 98 pass under it; the single failure is `r1002_generic_monospace_keyword_is_fixed_pitch`, a documented host-subject exception whose subject is the platform's GENERIC monospace resolution and which cannot pass where the only face is proportional.

★COUNTERFACTUAL CF-A IS THE WHOLE STORY IN TWO RUNS: restore the mixed-font comparison and it FAILS under the different font set (`62 vs 62.309`) and PASSES under this host's fonts. That pair is exactly why the regression shipped and why only CI saw it — a local green proved nothing about a different machine.

THE GATE FAILED ON ITS AUTHOR FIRST: the fix's initial seven-line comment put the `R1573` marker outside the gate's six-line window, and `r1573_no_test_shapes_through_the_host_without_saying_so` reported the site as unannotated by name and line. Fixed by binding the cache to a local so marker and call are adjacent.
`pinion-text` 98 PASS on the host. `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p pinion-text --all-targets -D pedantic`, `cargo doc -p pinion-text --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean.
carry_forward_bullets: THE FOUR HOST-SUBJECT TESTS ARE UNCHANGED and still cannot pass on a host with no usable face; that is stated in R1573's carry and is why the NanumGothic run reports 97 of 98 rather than 98 of 98.

WHETHER CI IS NOW GREEN IS STILL NOT VERIFIABLE FROM HERE. R1574.4.decision_summary: R1574.4 §5.36 — THE SAME R1573 REGRESSION A THIRD TIME, IN A TEST NO LOCAL GATE CAN RUN. The demo sweep — which had not executed in either of the two previous CI runs, because a red `workspace tests` keeps it behind its `needs:` gate — finally ran and reported one failure in 524: `r1447_font_free_tui.py`, "font-less probe failures: expected 0, got 1". The probe is `r1460_a_zero_font_config_is_font_less_from_inside_the_process`, and R1573's blanket migration had rewritten its cache to `own_font_cache()`. An own-fonts cache NEVER PROBES — it answers `NotProbed` forever, by construction — so a test asserting `Unavailable` became unsatisfiable. The test's own comment says its subject is "a property of the ENVIRONMENT, not of the code", which is as clear a statement as a site can carry that it belongs on the host path; the rewrite went through it anyway. R1574.5.decision_summary: R1574.5 §5.36 — `SystemFontStatus::Available` MEANT "THE SCAN DID NOT PANIC", AND THE QUESTION IT EXISTS TO ANSWER IS "CAN THIS PROCESS DRAW TEXT FROM THE PLATFORM". Those are the same fact only on a host where an empty font database makes fontique unwind — which is a property of that host's fontconfig, not of pinion. `build_font_context` now reports `Available` only when the scanned collection actually offers a family (`Collection::family_names().next().is_some()`), and the count runs inside the SAME `catch_unwind` as the scan, because on a host whose backend is left half-initialised the family enumeration is exactly where a second unwind would come from and both unwinds mean the identical thing to the caller. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: R1574.4 fixed the `r1460_a_zero_font_config_is_font_less_from_inside_the_process` probe's cache back to the host path, which repairs the `NotProbed` half of that demo's failure. It does NOT repair the other half. If a runner's zero-font config completes the scan over an empty database, the probe still sees `Available` and still fails — so R1574.4 alone was insufficient and this is the rest of it. THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: THIS BOX CANNOT REPRODUCE THE CONDITION THE FIX TARGETS. Three deliberately font-less fontconfig configurations were built here — no `<dir>` at all, one `<dir>` holding a single face, and a valid `<dir>` that is EMPTY — and this 635-face developer box unwinds inside fontique on every one of them, reaching `Unavailable` by the panic path regardless of the family check. A counterfactual that restores the old "surviving the scan is the verdict" rule therefore PASSES here, which is not evidence the fix is unnecessary but evidence that this host cannot discriminate. What is verified from here is that the change is sound and regresses nothing; what confirms the fix is the next CI run, and that is the honest division.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-text/src/font_source.rs` — `build_font_context` reports `Available` only when the scan yields a family; `scan_yields_a_family` is the new predicate, inside the same `catch_unwind` as the scan and stopping at the first name (the answer is a yes/no, so a 10,000-face host does not pay for a walk).

The `tracing::warn!` text now names BOTH causes — a failed scan and a successful scan over an empty database — because they are one fact to a caller asking whether it can draw text, and the previous wording claimed only the first.
verification_bullets: `pinion-text` 99 PASS (98 + the previously-ignored probe now run explicitly), across THREE font environments: this host's own 635 faces, a single-face config, and a zero-face config. The probe passes in each.

★THE COUNTERFACTUAL PASSED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A CLEAN BILL: restoring the pre-R1574.5 rule (survive the scan = `Available`) leaves every assertion green HERE, because this box unwinds inside fontique under all three font-less configs and reaches `Unavailable` by the panic path either way. The condition the fix targets — a scan that COMPLETES over an empty database — could not be constructed on this machine.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT VERIFIED, kept apart deliberately: verified here — the predicate is correct, the enumeration is `Collection`'s own, nothing regresses in any of the three environments, and the fix composes with R1574.4 rather than replacing it. NOT verified here — that a CI runner exhibits the completing-scan case at all. Only the next CI run answers that.
`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p pinion-text --all-targets -D pedantic`, `cargo doc -p pinion-text --no-deps --document-private-items`: clean.
carry_forward_bullets: THE CONDITION IS UNREPRODUCIBLE ON THIS HOST, so the fix ships on an argument plus a non-regression, not on a discriminating local test. That is a real weakness and the reason it is written down here rather than in a passing assertion: if the next CI run still fails `r1447_font_free_tui.py`, this hypothesis is what to discard first.

`SYSTEM_FONTS_USABLE` CACHES THE VERDICT PER PROCESS, so the first cache to probe decides for the rest — including the new empty-database verdict. A host whose fonts are installed AFTER the first probe keeps answering `Unavailable`; that was already true of the panic path and is unchanged, but the empty-database case makes it reachable on hosts that never panic, which is a wider set than before.
THE FAMILY CHECK COSTS ONE ENUMERATION STEP ON EVERY SCANNING CACHE. Measured at nothing here relative to the ~25 ms scan R1447 recorded, but it is not free and was not benchmarked.

R1575.decision_summary: R1575 §5.3 §5.50 §5.52 — a graph states which of its links it AUTHORED and which it OBSERVED. Stroke could not draw a dash at all, and StrokeCap's doc had called dash patterns carry-forward for ~1550 rounds, so a two-layer diagnostic graph — solid for the links a user drew, dashed for the ones that are not there, dotted for the ones nobody drew — was not a picture this framework could express. An unexpressible drawing shows up as a MISSING PRIMITIVE, not as a missing widget. Entry appended at R1576 after a census found the round had landed with no atomic entry.
changes_bullets: Stroke gains Dash {on, off, offset} in pixels, NonZeroU32 so a dash that draws nothing is unrepresentable, offset canonical modulo the period so two equal-drawing dashes compare equal
Option<Dash> rather than a Dash meaning solid: Qt keeps Qt::PenStyle and the pattern list separately and they can contradict each other
examples/hello-graph-diff is the forcing consumer: authored and observed link layers, LinkKind derived from set membership rather than stored, so invoke adopt is one assignment
scene/snapshot publishes style.stroke.dash, so an agent reads which layer a link is in without rasterizing; a QPen is an argument to a paint call and lives nowhere afterwards
verification_bullets: tools/demos/r1575_graph_states_its_layers.py drives the whole arc over RPC, comparing the model's missing_ids against the paint's dashes as two independent readings of one fact
The example carries 8 unit tests; pinion-core, pinion-rpc, pinion-runtime and the binding are green under clippy pedantic
carry_forward_bullets: The changelog entry for this round was MISSING from the atomic store until R1576's census found it; this entry is that repair, appended out of band, and the round obligation it broke is 1 commit = 1 round = 1 atomic entry
hello-graph-diff matched no phase_b_tally axis pattern and was reported UNCLASSIFIED for a round; R1576 filed it under dcc, the axis R1575 itself declared
A dash costs one path segment each, so R1556's last.draw.path_segments rises for a dashed stroke

R1576.decision_summary: R1576 §5.16 §5.41 §5.7 §5.12 §2 #7 — A PLACE IS STATED RELATIVE TO A DISPLAY. pinion had no notion of a monitor at all: a census over the whole tree found ZERO references to winit's available_monitors / primary_monitor / MonitorHandle, so WindowSpec::position's own doc described logical pixels in a coordinate space nothing could describe, and three questions were unaskable — how many monitors are there, which one is this window on, and is this window on any of them. The commonest multi-monitor bug in desktop software (restore a saved layout after unplugging a monitor and the window opens where no pixel is) was therefore not merely possible, it was unaskable. The round splits the axis in two and THE SPLIT IS THE ARGUMENT: the geometry is a pure value a test can construct, and the platform read is ~40 lines that do no arithmetic — because a monitor farm is not a thing CI has. Six things past Qt 6.11, each checked against qscreen.h / qguiapplication.h / qwidget.h on this machine.
changes_bullets: pinion_core::display is the PURE half: DisplayTopology + Display + DisplayId + DisplayRect, with exact rectangle-union area by coordinate decomposition, so a mirrored pair counts once and an L-shaped desk's hole is a number
DisplayTopology::resolve answers for a RECTANGLE — home display, every display touched, visible pixels, offscreen pixels, and the nearest origin that would make it wholly visible
Anchor is a display id plus a LOGICAL offset into it, and Anchored names the outcome: on_declared, substituted (with BOTH ids), or no_display
WindowSpec::display re-reads position as an offset into a named display; with_placement is the setter that can also CLEAR it, which a non_exhaustive struct otherwise made unexpressible
window_placement_moves compares the whole placement, so re-declaring only the display is a move; placement_command is the pure decision of which frame to command in
user_move_writeback keeps a display-relative declaration RELATIVE, and a drag onto another monitor re-declares the display — the loop that keeps the declaration true of the world
scene/displays publishes the desk plus three optional derived answers (at, probe, anchor), each ABSENT unless asked for; scene/windows gains display and anchored per window
pinion_shell::use_displays lets a BINDING name a display, seeded through a ProviderSlot the surface stamps, so in-process code is not below QGuiApplication::screens()
verification_bullets: 33 unit tests in pinion_core::display over FABRICATED arrangements — side-by-side, L-shaped, mirrored, diagonal, mixed-DPI, headless — because CI has one monitor and a design whose multi-monitor arithmetic lived in the platform layer would be asserted by nobody

Five counterfactuals, all caught: naive sum for the union (4 tests), placement diff ignoring the display (2), write-back overwriting a relative offset (5), the binding handle never published (the demo's two-reader cross-check), and the command ignoring the display (4)

The fifth counterfactual is the round's finding: it was BEHAVIOURALLY IDENTICAL on a one-monitor 1x desk, so the decision was extracted into the pure placement_command and pinned against a fabricated mixed-DPI desk

tools/demos/r1576_a_place_is_relative_to_a_display.py, 84 assertion sites, all relations between published facts so they hold on any desk; six demos reading scene/windows re-run green after the shape change
The R1539 wire census gate caught the six new response types itself and the -32602 vocabulary gate caught the new refusal word
carry_forward_bullets: A display's USABLE region (Qt QScreen::availableGeometry) is not modelled: winit exposes no work area and EWMH _NET_WORKAREA is one rectangle for the whole desktop, so it needs a platform probe rather than more geometry
No hot-plug event: winit 0.30 emits none, so the desk is re-read at each window create and RPC dispatch; a binding that only paints will not see a monitor arrive until then
Window::current_monitor() is not cross-checked against the derived home display, so the platform's own opinion and this one are never compared
The OS apply stays HW-gated as every real-window behaviour here is; the DECISION is pinned, the set_outer_position call is not

R1576.1 fixed the demo that crossed the 180s cliff and left the cliff itself unlit: on success the sweep discarded the captured output, so the only demo timing anyone ever saw was the one `timeout` printed while killing it. `r1570_1` passed one run and was killed the next at 186.8s, and no green log had ever said it was near. `run_demo` already prints its own elapsed; this lifts that number onto the sweep line and marks anything past half the budget.
