R1577.decision_summary: R1577 §5.38 §5.52 §5.7 §5.12 §2 #7 — A NODE CAN BE A GRAPH, AND THE FRAMEWORK OWNS IT. The single largest capability a node editor has — wrap a selection in a re-usable node — was inexpressible here, because the whole node model lived inside a 9,075-line example as a flat Vec<GraphNode> plus a Vec<Edge>, and a flat vector cannot hold a node that is a graph. The user directive is the round's frame: pinion must not re-implement Blender, it must PROVIDE THE API a Blender-class node system is composed from. So the mechanism moves into two crates and the taxonomy stays with the application. pinion_graph::group is the pure arithmetic (a selection's boundary, the interface derived from it, the legality of the collapse, nesting acyclicity); pinion-node-graph is the typed model built on it (trees, sockets, links, group definitions and instances, the edit path, and a memoised evaluator that descends into groups). hello-node-groups is the proof: 1,092 lines against 9,075, and the difference is not features but the model, the invariants, the groups and the evaluator, none of which it contains. It also HAS groups, which the older example does not.
changes_bullets: pinion_graph::group derives a selection's boundary as pure arithmetic over 0..n: Boundary::derive answers the interface plus a four-way partition of the caller's links, and Nesting::cycle answers whether a definition may be placed in another

An interface socket is ONE VALUE CROSSING THE BOUNDARY, identified by its PRODUCER — one rule covering both directions, where Blender reaches the same two behaviours through two independent booleans whose struct defaults are the opposite of what its own group-make passes

A collapse is refused by REACHABILITY and the walk is reported; Blender tests a one-hop approximation, so a two-hop bypass is accepted there and the cycle is found later by a pass that flags links rather than by anything that could refuse

pinion-node-graph: NodeKind is the whole of what an application supplies (a socket type, a value, port lists, evaluate); NodeBody owns the three structural kinds, so groups cannot be forgotten or got wrong

Document::connect checks socket existence, type agreement, one-link-per-input and acyclicity, and NAMES which failed, including the path a refused wire would have closed and the link a replacement displaced

Document::group / ungroup / instantiate, with the interface derived from the crossings and each port named from its INTERNAL end; expose / unexpose maintain the links inside the definition AND at every instance
The evaluator's memo is keyed by INSTANCE, not by node, so two instances of one definition fed differently do not share a value; evaluating inside a definition uses the interface's own port defaults
EditPath is the breadcrumb, with prune for when the document changes underneath it; Document::validate is the standing check for documents that arrived from a file or a peer

hello-node-groups composes all of it: five material ops, a paint, and an RPC surface publishing the definition library, the derived interface, the edit path, any node's value, and the TEXT of the last refusal
verification_bullets: 51 unit tests in pinion_graph::group and 39 in pinion-node-graph, every one a hand-written document — no renderer, no window, no pointer

Six counterfactuals, all caught: memo keyed by node rather than instance (2 tests), interface keyed by the consumer end (5 + 19), the reachability refusal removed (4 + 1), mutating before validating (1), a partial ungroup rewiring (1), and the edit path left unpruned (the demo)

The pinion-graph suite carries Blender's own one-hop rule as a helper so the divergence is ASSERTED rather than described, and it earned its keep at once by catching that very assertion written the wrong way round
tools/demos/r1577_a_node_can_be_a_graph.py, 59 assertion sites over the live wire, PASS in 19.3s

The demo found a real API gap while being written: ungroup could only act on the tree the view was inside, so the situation an edit path exists to survive was unreachable; the verb is now addressed by tree and node
A round-trip test asserts DeserializeOwned at the type level, which caught a taxonomy carrying a borrowed field being only Deserialize<'static> — invisible until something asks for the owned form
The tally reported the new binding UNCLASSIFIED at the push that added it and it was registered inline, the same census finding R1576 cleared for hello-graph-diff
carry_forward_bullets: hello-node-editor is NOT migrated onto the substrate: it has 9,042 lines of tests against its own model, and moving it is per-binding domain work rather than seam work — the substrate's first consumer is a new binding, which is what production-level-from-first-consumer asks for

The Blender census names eleven gaps and this round closes the largest one; copy/paste, duplicate, collapse/mute/hide, the richer selection vocabulary, link mute and detach, insert_offset, find, resize, view_selected and swap remain, and they are the campaign's scope rather than this round's carry

Execution semantics are untouched and no reference census can see them: evaluate(inputs) -> outputs is pure dataflow, so control flow, side effects, iteration and time are still inexpressible; that axis is UE Blueprint's, not Blender's

An unconnected socket on a selected node is not exposed, deliberately: Blender special-cases a single-node selection to expose the whole signature and its own source marks that inconsistency with a TODO
Group nodes are not laid out by pinion-graph's Sugiyama pass, so a collapsed selection keeps its authored positions rather than being re-placed
The tally did not demand a re-judgment (rd 4 -> 5 = +25%, exactly the band edge), so the DCC completion stays at 97% and this round's advance is absorbed at the next one

R1578.decision_summary: R1578 §5.38 §5.52 §5.7 §5.12 §2 #7 — A FRAGMENT OF A GRAPH IS A VALUE. Copy, paste and duplicate look like three editor gestures and are one question: can a piece of a node graph be lifted out and stand on its own? A selection is not a list of nodes — it is nodes, the links BETWEEN them, the links that CROSS its edge, and, when one of those nodes is a group instance, the whole transitive closure of definitions it depends on; lift only the nodes and a pasted group instance points at nothing. So Fragment carries a whole Document, which is not a convenience but what makes it ANSWERABLE — how many nodes, which definitions came with them, which wires were severed, whether it satisfies the invariants, what it evaluates to, and how many bytes it serializes to, all without pasting. Blender's clipboard is a .blend file written to the temp directory, so a paste is the only thing that can be done with it. Document::extract and Document::insert are the whole substrate; clipboard copy, clipboard paste, duplicate, duplicate-keep-inputs and duplicate-linked are call sites of them, which is four of the eleven gaps the Blender census names closed by one concept rather than four verbs.
changes_bullets: pinion_graph::group splits Boundary::derive into a CUT and a collapse: a cut always succeeds because severing a crossing cannot create a cycle, while a collapse routes every crossing through one new vertex and can be refused. R1577 fused the two questions, which is right for a collapse and wrong for every other consumer of the partition

Fragment carries a Document — root holds the copied nodes, the definitions hold the transitive closure they instance — plus the boundary it was cut from, in the same producer-keyed form a derived group interface uses, because it is the same fact
Document::extract lifts a selection out without touching the document; Document::insert puts one anywhere; Document::duplicate is the two in one call, and DuplicateError says which half refused

Crossings::KeepInbound restores the severed inputs, and the asymmetry with the outputs is DERIVED rather than a missing boolean: an output may feed many consumers so an inbound crossing costs the original nothing, while an input takes at most one link so an outbound one would steal the original's connection — so the outbound crossings are published instead

Definitions::Share matches a carried definition against the destination's by CONTENT and re-uses it, so pasting a group twice leaves one definition and three instances; Definitions::Fork is the deep copy, and both are arguments rather than a user preference

A recursion is refused by walking the containment relation as it WOULD stand, one prospective edge at a time, so the edge that closes the cycle is the one named — and every check runs before the first mutation, so a refused insertion leaves the document untouched
The crossings are resolved in the PLAN, against the tree before any copy exists: an address resolved after the copies are placed can find a copy where its own producer used to be

hello-node-groups gains copy / paste / duplicate and four read slots — clipboard, clipboard_severed, clipboard_bytes, last_insert — supplying only where the value is kept and how the two policy arms are spelled on the wire
verification_bullets: 27 new unit tests in pinion-node-graph (68 total) and 3 in pinion_graph::group (54 total), every one a hand-written document — no renderer, no window, no pointer

Eight counterfactuals, ALL caught with zero coverage gaps: the cut reverted to a derive, the crossings resolved after placement, the closure reduced to the direct definitions, the definition matched by NAME as Blender matches it, the recursion check dropped, the type check dropped, the interface-node guard dropped, and the fragment positions left absolute
tools/demos/r1578_a_fragment_is_a_value.py, 76 assertion sites over the live wire, PASS in 1.9s

A test written to check the REPORTING of an unrestorable crossing caught a real defect instead: pasting into an emptier tree gave the copy the id its own producer used to have, and the re-attachment wired the copy to itself. The resolution moved into the plan

Blender measured at 8cf5059963d69eebca8f4e092dc7040ce515e8d3 rather than described: node_copy_local copies a link only when both ends are selected and records the rest nowhere; NODE_OT_clipboard_paste declares one property, offset, so keep_inputs exists on duplicate alone; BKE_main_merge keys candidates on the datablock name and are_ids_from_different_mains_matching returns true on the name alone for two local IDs; node_copy_local reports a node it cannot place, skips it and its links, and finishes

The counterfactual driver asserts its own anchor appears exactly once, which caught a vacuous counterfactual — and its first version died between applying a patch and restoring, leaving the tree mutated, the exact residue failure R1557 recorded. The restore is now in a finally and hash-checked
carry_forward_bullets: group_insert and group_separate are still absent: moving a node ACROSS a definition boundary re-derives the interfaces at both ends, which extract plus insert do not do, and it is the next slice on this axis

The Blender census names eleven gaps; R1577 closed one and R1578 closes four more, leaving collapse/mute/hide, the richer selection vocabulary, link mute and detach, insert_offset, find, resize, view_selected and swap as campaign scope rather than this round's carry

A fragment names the outside end of a crossing by socket ADDRESS, which is exact going back into the tree it came from and a guess anywhere else; the guess is type-checked and every outcome reported, and carrying a stronger producer identity is the honest next step if a consumer needs one

The definition match is conservative by construction: two definitions identical up to a renumbering of their nodes are reported as different and a duplicate is added. The other error would silently rebind an instance to a graph that computes something else, which is what matching by name does
Execution semantics are still inexpressible and no reference census can see it, because Blender is pure dataflow too — that axis is UE Blueprint's
hello-node-editor still holds its own node model, which R1577 registered as debt-two-node-graph-models and this round does not change

The definition match is conservative by construction: two definitions identical up to a renumbering of their nodes are reported as different and a duplicate is added. The other error would silently rebind an instance to a graph that computes something else, which is what matching by name does
Execution semantics are still inexpressible and no reference census can see it, because Blender is pure dataflow too — that axis is UE Blueprint's
hello-node-editor still holds its own node model, which R1577 registered as debt-two-node-graph-models and this round does not change

R1579.decision_summary: R1579 §5.16 — A RUN'S ABSENCE AND A RUN'S SUCCESS ARE DIFFERENT FACTS. R1495 made stop-the-line a gate instead of a sentence, and it reads the branch's last COMPLETED run — which silently assumes the last thing CI judged is the thing you are building on. Measured here on 2026-08-06 it was not: ae377e0c was pushed at 21:38:23Z and `actions/runs?head_sha=` answered 0, still 0 forty-five minutes later; a8249cd7 was pushed at 21:41:16Z, answered 0 at 21:45, and got a push-event run created at 22:11:17Z — half an hour after the push that caused it. The gate read the previous commit's green and said nothing, which is the R1470 shape one level up: not a check that reports red, a check that stopped happening. check_base_ci_coverage asks the second question — does the commit being pushed ONTO have a run of its own — and says so when it does not. It reports rather than refuses, and the measurement is what decided that: a pending run is a normal state, so refusing would stop the line with no move available, and this file's own rule is that "cannot verify" must not become "cannot publish". What was wrong was the silence. The round also corrects the debt census: three files carried `status: open` while their own bodies said CLOSED.
changes_bullets: ci_run_count_for_sha asks GitHub how many workflow runs a commit has, through `gh api --jq` because the plain-text `gh run list` has no SHA column at all — the question cannot be put to the listing this file already parses

check_base_ci_coverage reports whether the base has a run of its own, names the consequence when it does not (the verdict above is about an earlier commit), and hands over the command that schedules one now

A scheduling grace distinguishes "not yet" from "not coming", because two pushes seconds apart legitimately leave the first without a run and crying wolf there trains the reader to ignore the notice that matters
An answer that is not a run of digits becomes `unknown` rather than a count, so a gh replying with usage text or an error object cannot be read as "has runs"
pre-push passes the remote sha git already feeds it on stdin, so the base being checked is the one being pushed onto rather than a guess

CENSUS CORRECTION: debt-r1366-provider-slot-type, debt-r1366-audit-findings and debt-r1456-modal-handoff-residue all carried `status: open` while their bodies said CAMPAIGN COMPLETE, cleared, or reassigned. R1574.1 made the census a field lookup; a field lookup is only as true as the field
verification_bullets: 25 new assertions in tools/test_hooks.sh (91 total), which pre-push runs before trusting the libraries they cover

Six counterfactuals, all caught with zero coverage gaps: the probe always claiming a run, the grace removed, the grace swallowing an unknown age, the notice no longer relating the verdict to the base, a non-count read as a count, and the check refusing instead of reporting

The counterfactual driver reported six gaps on its first run and the code was correct: its FAIL detector required whitespace after FAIL where the harness prints a colon. It now cross-checks its own detector against the suite's summary line and refuses to report at all if the two disagree
The gate was run against the live GitHub API for both real commits, not only against the stub

THE CLAIM WAS CORRECTED BY RE-MEASURING: the first reading was "GitHub scheduled no run", and half an hour later a push-event run existed for one of the two commits. A lag is not a failure, so the wording no longer says GitHub scheduled none, and the notice states only what stays true either way — this base has no run of its own
A test written in this round was vacuous and was caught before it landed: it claimed to check a non-numeric answer and fed the stub a number, so it asserted the stub rather than the code
carry_forward_bullets: Whether GitHub schedules a run at all is outside this repository; the gate can observe the fact and cannot cause it, which is why it reports

The grace is 180 seconds against a measured 30-minute lag, so the notice will fire while a run is legitimately pending. That is deliberate — the fact it states (the verdict above is about an earlier commit) is true whether the run is late or absent
21 debt files remain open after the census correction, and clearing them is the campaign this round opens rather than finishes

R1580.decision_summary: R1580 §5.16 — THE HARNESS EVERY DEMO RIDES IS TESTED PAST ITS TEARDOWN. R1570.3 put tests on tools/rpc_verify.py for the first time and covered exactly one function, terminate_process_tree, because that is where that round was bitten. The argument it made — this code drives every demo in the repository and nothing verifies it — applies unchanged to the rest of the file, and the rest of the file is what every demo calls on every line. wait_until in particular is where the zero-flake policy is actually enforced: it is the thing that replaced a fixed sleep with an observation, so a defect in it turns into flake spread across two hundred demos rather than one failing test. This round takes the file from 6 cases and 11 assertions to 22 and 50, still under a second, still inside pre-push, and still without launching a single process: request runs against a fake pipe, wait_until against a deterministic predicate, and the scene readers against literal dicts. Two of the eight counterfactuals found defects in the harness itself rather than confirming its behaviour.
changes_bullets: request is covered where it is hardest: it answers the frame carrying its own id and skips others, and it KEEPS a server-initiated notification rather than discarding it -- the property R1552 recorded as the reason the wire form is a notification and not a second response

wait_until evaluates its predicate BEFORE consulting the deadline, so a condition already true never fails on a zero budget; a loop written the other way makes every demo's first check load-dependent, and that is now an assertion rather than a reading
The timeout message is pinned to carry the description, the last value seen and the budget spent -- the three things that make a timed-out demo diagnosable without a rerun

find_by_tag is pinned to descend Container.children and Scroll.content and NOT a Text's content, which is a string; access_node_by_tag is pinned as a flat scan, because an access tree nests by tag reference rather than by containment

key's argument rules are asserted, including R882.1's positionless release, and the boot gate is asserted to read PINION_ASSUME_BUILT's VALUE rather than its presence -- the R1333 defect where setting 0 disabled the rebuild
A case that RAISES is now that case's failure rather than a dead suite, and every verdict carries the name of the case it came from, so a failure and an exception are reported in one vocabulary
The case list is DERIVED from the module rather than hand-written, and a scan that finds nothing reports itself broken instead of clean
verification_bullets: 22 cases / 50 assertions, 0.95s, run by pre-push before it trusts the demos

Eight counterfactuals, all caught with zero coverage gaps: notifications discarded, any id answering, the deadline consulted before the predicate, the last value dropped from the message, a Scroll no longer descended, the boot gate presence-checking, key accepting an empty name, and assert_eq dropping its label

TWO of those counterfactuals found harness defects rather than confirming behaviour. Making wait_until check its deadline first did not turn the file red, it turned it SILENT -- the exception escaped and took the summary line and the other twenty-one verdicts with it. And the case list was a hand-written tuple, the same shape debt-focus-sweep-population-is-curated names one file over: a case added and not registered is not a failure, it is a non-existence

The counterfactual driver cross-checks its own detector against the suite's summary and refuses to report if the two disagree, which is what caught the raising-case gap instead of reporting it as a coverage hole
carry_forward_bullets: The population fix here is local to this suite; debt-focus-sweep-population-is-curated is the same shape in tools/demos and is still open

The tests are unit-shaped by construction, so the boot path that actually launches a binary -- boot_grace, the first-paint wait, the boot_timeout handshake -- is still exercised only by the demos themselves

R1581.decision_summary: R1581 §5.40 §5.39 §2 #7 — A KEYBOARD FOCUS STOP IS A NODE IN THE AT TREE. R1518 made the accessibility focus flag something the assembler stamps, which killed two whole classes of defect, and it named a residue it could not close with a stamp: focus targets that name a tag no node in that tree carries. AccessTreeBuilder folds such a target onto the window root, so a screen-reader user who Tabs to that control is told they are on the window — the R1329/PR-53 failure shape, on controls nobody had checked. This round closes it, and correcting the note was as much of the work as fixing the code. The note listed eight bindings; walking them found eleven stops across nine. Two of its entries were false positives and both for one reason: their node lives in a window the wire cannot ask about. Three of the six it filed as "the tree exists, the stop is missing" had no tree at all. And settings-panel's exemption read "AT-invisible for v1, real ARIA wiring carries to R668" — R668 is nine hundred rounds past, and the one control that panel is navigated by was the one control a screen-reader user could not hear.
changes_bullets: Eight bindings gained the nodes their focus stops needed: three readouts as a status with the sentence they paint, four buttons named by the label they paint, and settings-panel's section rail as a navigation landmark through the same builder every other rail in the tree uses

Every announced name comes from the SAME derivation as the pixels -- the three readouts share one readout_body_text between the paint and the node, the dock buttons read the button's own label, the rail goes through navigation_link_nodes -- so spoken and drawn cannot become two sentences

hello-dock-panels generalised inspector_host_window into panel_host_window at its second consumer, so the viewport button's node lands in the window that paints it by the same rule the inspector tree does

hello-window-refocus's nodes are emitted per window because its stops are split across two, which is what R813 built access_node_for_window for; the note it replaces argued that being readable over RPC was enough, and being readable over RPC and being reachable by a screen reader are different facts

An existing test was rewritten rather than adjusted: r813_inspector_at_nodes_emit_for_host_window_only pinned nodes[0].role, so adding a second node broke it without breaking anything it claims. It is now predicate-shaped and additionally asserts that floating the viewport moves its button
A new debt is registered rather than worked around: scene/access takes no window and rejects the window[id]/ prefix, so a multi-window binding's AT tree cannot be verified over the wire at all
verification_bullets: tools/demos/r1581_a_focus_stop_is_a_node.py, 25 assertion sites over 14 focus stops in seven bindings, PASS in 18.8s
Five counterfactuals, all caught with zero coverage gaps: each binding's new node removed, and one announcing a different sentence from the one it paints

THE FIRST COUNTERFACTUAL RUN PROVED NOTHING: four of the five failed to COMPILE, so rustc caught them and the demo was never asked. The driver now raises on a build failure instead of reporting it as a result, and the five were rewritten to build

The demo's own first draft reported a defect that was not there: it asserted the AT tree against stops[-1], and a walk that stops on a repeat has already moved focus PAST its last recorded stop. walk_stops now returns where focus came to rest, and the exclusion cases steer focus onto the stop under test

Two stops remain unverifiable over the wire and are pinned in Rust instead -- hello-multi-window's assertion has existed since R813, hello-window-refocus's was added here -- and the demo states the exclusion rather than skipping it, so if scene/access ever becomes window-routable the demo fails and says the premise changed
Every touched binding's own test suite is green, including the rewritten R813 one
carry_forward_bullets: The census covered the bindings the note named, not the tree: a full sweep needs every example built and is what debt-focus-sweep-population-is-curated is about. R1581 removed that debt's stated blocker and did not close it
settings-panel's DETAIL pane widgets are still absent from the AT surface; the old note meant that wiring, and it is a different axis from "a focus stop is reachable"
scene/access is not window-routable, registered as debt-scene-access-is-not-window-routable; until it is, a multi-window AT tree is checkable only from Rust

R1582.decision_summary: R1582 §5.16 — WHICH PACKAGES A CHANGE CAN BREAK IS A COMPUTATION, NOT A THING TO REMEMBER. The standing local rule is "test the crates this round touched", and the defect lives in the reading: touched means the crates whose BEHAVIOUR changed, consumers included. R1497 tested pinion-runtime and broke pinion-shell; R1499 wrote the lesson down; R1511 then retired a focus ring in pinion-widget-paint, ran the three crates it had edited, and committed examples/hello-dialog asserting that very ring. Every gate was green because clippy --all-targets COMPILES a test and does not run it. A lesson recorded twice and re-broken twice is a computation nobody had written. tools/blast_radius.py is that computation and it found a live instance the moment it existed: R1578 edited pinion-graph and tested three of the five packages in its radius. The gate runs the radius when it is affordable and reports it with its command when it is not, and where that line falls was measured rather than chosen.
changes_bullets: tools/blast_radius.py answers, from cargo metadata, the packages that own a change plus every workspace package depending on them transitively; dev-dependencies count, because a change that breaks only a consumer's test harness still breaks that consumer's tests
The nested-package rule is explicit: the LONGEST matching directory wins, so a package inside another package's directory is attributed to itself
.githooks/lib/consumer-tests.sh runs that radius in pre-commit and again in pre-push, the second warm, so an amend or a --no-verify commit cannot publish what pre-commit would have refused

The cap is stated in packages and justified in time: cargo metadata is 0.2s, a warm eight-package run 1.4s, and a real cold five-package radius 9.7s, so linking is the cost and it scales with the radius. At roughly two seconds of link per consumer, twelve is under half a minute -- smaller than the clippy the hook already pays for. pinion-core's radius is 237 packages and belongs to CI
Over the cap the radius is REPORTED with its cargo test line rather than dropped, because a check that goes quiet is the failure this whole file exists to prevent
PINION_SKIP_CONSUMER_TESTS=1 is the escape, armed by that exact value only, and it announces itself
pre-push runs blast_radius.py --selftest, the shape R1522 fixed for the tally: a gate whose own arithmetic nothing verifies
verification_bullets: 16 new assertions in tools/test_hooks.sh (106 total) plus 10 in the radius tool's own selftest, which runs against a SYNTHETIC workspace so its assertions state the graph they are about instead of inheriting today's tree

Eight counterfactuals, all caught with zero coverage gaps: a failing consumer no longer refusing, the over-cap radius going quiet, the cap off by one, a failed computation read as an empty radius, the skip flag armed by any value, the radius stopping at direct consumers, dev-dependencies dropped, and the shortest directory prefix winning

THE TOOL FOUND A LIVE MISS ON ITS FIRST RUN: R1578's radius is five packages and that round tested three. Running the two it missed found them green -- which is luck, and the point is that nothing had said so

A stub written for these tests hijacked python3 for the whole suite and turned the tally's own cases red; the stub is now scoped to the subshell that uses it, which is the same trap stub_gh was written to avoid one level out
carry_forward_bullets: The second axis of this debt is untouched and stays open in the same file: an #[ignore]d test is run by no local gate either, and 40 of the 47 in this tree need a real GPU, so "always run --ignored" is the wrong prescription
The cap means a core-crate change is still reported rather than covered locally; that is the deliberate boundary with CI, not an omission

R1583.decision_summary: R1583 §5.40 §5.12 §2 #7 — THE ACCESS WIRE REPORTS THE FOCUS THIS WINDOW RESOLVES. R1581 registered a debt saying scene/access cannot be asked about a window. That was false and this round found it out before working on it: the scope is params.window, which Request::window_scope reads, not the window[id]/ method PREFIX that addresses paths inside query and invoke. One failed spelling had been read as an absent capability. But a real defect was in that place, and it is the one the false debt was standing in front of: the shell's focus target is GLOBAL — one tag across every window — and AccessTreeBuilder::build folds a tag its node set lacks onto the window root, while access_to_json republished the global tag into every window's reply. Measured on hello-window-refocus with focus on edit_title, the notes window's reply named edit_title, and that window's real AccessKit TreeUpdate carries ROOT_NODE_ID. A surface whose whole purpose is to answer "what does a screen reader on this window see" was answering with something that window's screen reader does not see.
changes_bullets: access_to_json applies the same existence filter AccessTreeBuilder::build applies, so the wire reports what the AccessKit tree carries rather than being a second description free to disagree with the first

The fold is NAMED rather than performed silently: the reply keeps the global tag and adds how this window resolved it, so "where is focus" and "what does this window's AT see" are both still answerable. Collapsing to null would have answered the second by destroying the first
R947.1's active-descendant filter is mirrored too — a roving cursor scrolled out of the realized set is not advertised as a node this frame does not contain

r1581_a_focus_stop_is_a_node.py's two EXCLUSIONS became assertions: the node is in the window that paints it, and the window that does not paint it resolves the same tag to its own root. That demo had written down the condition under which its exclusion should go, and this is it

THE DEBT THIS CLOSES WAS ITSELF WRONG, and the correction is the round's first finding: a single failed call had been recorded as an absent capability. The second spelling was never tried

R1584.decision_summary: R1584 §5.38 §5.52 §2 #7 — A GROUP BOUNDARY IS A PARTITION, AND THE PARTITION MOVES. group CREATES a partition (these nodes inside, the rest outside, the interface derived from what crosses) and ungroup destroys one; neither can MOVE one, and moving one is what an editor does all day. group_insert and group_separate are the two directions of a single operation: a pair (host tree, instance node) names one boundary, a selection names the nodes changing sides, and the interface is re-derived from the partition that results. Re-deriving is the whole job, and it is where Blender stops: measured at 8cf50599, node_group_separate_selected copies the selected nodes into the parent tree, deletes them from the group for the Move arm, and touches the interface not at all — so the group keeps sockets that reach nothing, the separated nodes arrive wired only to each other, and the value that used to flow through them is gone. Here the graph goes on computing what it computed, asserted as a VALUE in both directions rather than as a structure.
changes_bullets: Document::group_insert and Document::group_separate, built on one derivation each: inward the partition is the selection plus the instance, so every check a collapse runs applies unchanged because it IS a collapse of a set that already has one member; outward it is the nodes staying behind MINUS the interface nodes, which is the same statement about the other side of the same partition

An interface edit is a script rather than an append: ports whose inside end the move leaves unwired are removed (descending, so no surviving index moves under a later removal), new crossings are appended, and a value that already crosses at this instance re-uses its port instead of gaining a second

Sharing::Shared or Fork is an argument at the call, and Repartitioned reports what the caller cannot see: other_instances counts the instances an edit to a shared definition dragged along, and severed names every link that died anywhere, each with the tree it was in

Document::unexpose now answers Vec<DroppedLink> rather than Vec<Link>: a link id is unique within one tree and meaningless outside it, and the links worth reporting are exactly the ones in trees the caller was not editing

Numbering lifted to its own module at its third and fourth consumers (group collapse, fragment cut, both boundary moves), and lifting it found a shared defect: both copies indexed the node map directly, so a document holding a link that names a missing node — which validate exists to report and nothing stops a deserialized document from holding — PANICKED. It is now a refusal that names the link, in all three error types

hello-node-groups gains group_insert / group_separate / fork and a last_move readout, supplying only WHERE the boundary is: pointed at inward, and the edit path's own last step outward, which is where Blender reads it from too (snode->edittree against ED_node_tree_get(snode, 1))

Every refusal the example makes now reaches last_refusal: the substrate's arrived through edit which records them, while the application's own — a malformed argument, a boundary that is not there — reached the error frame and nothing else, so the readout could show one kind and not the other
verification_bullets: pinion-node-graph 84 unit tests (18 new for R1584) + 1 doctest, clippy -D pedantic clean, cargo doc clean; hello-node-groups builds and its 6 tests pass. Blast radius computed rather than remembered (R1582): cargo test -p hello-node-groups -p pinion-node-graph
tools/demos/r1584_the_boundary_is_a_partition.py — 8 phases, 78 assertions, PASS in 2.6s over the live RPC wire against the release binary

The claim is asserted as a VALUE, not a shape: the group's output is read before and after every move, the in-and-back-out round trip is byte-identical, and the premise is pinned to a concrete colour first so the comparison cannot pass by both sides being nothing

Blender's rule is held as a TEST HELPER and the divergence asserted rather than described: blender_separate reproduces node_group_separate_selected over this crate's types and the same fixture, and the sink it leaves receives NOTHING where ours receives the value; blender_insert_port_count reproduces build_node_set_interface's socket walk and answers 3 where the derivation answers 1

TWO WERE INITIALLY MISSED AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S FINDING: the demo separated a source node with no inputs, so neither the reconnection path nor the dying-input path ran, and the headline claim was untested until a phase was added where values cross BOTH ways

A boundary round trip preserves the graph's meaning and NOT the port order, found by the demo contradicting its own expectation. It is forced rather than sloppy: other instances address ports by index, so restoring a removed port to its old position would silently rewire every one of them
carry_forward_bullets: hello-node-editor still holds its own Vec<GraphNode> model, so the tree has two node-graph models (registered debt debt-two-node-graph-models). This round widened the crate side of that gap

Execution semantics — control flow, side effects, iteration, time — stay inexpressible in evaluate(inputs) -> outputs, and no census against Blender can find that because Blender is pure dataflow too; UE Blueprint is the only reference and its source is account-gated

R1585.decision_summary: R1585 §5.18 §5.7 §2 #7 — A METHOD SAYS HOW A WINDOW IS NAMED TO IT. Two spellings name a window to this dispatcher and they mean different things: params.window is the dispatch SCOPE (whose state answers, type-checked and gated against the live window set before routing) and /window[id]/ is a prefix on a scene PATH (which subtree it runs through). Which method takes which was published nowhere, and the cost is on the record rather than hypothetical: R1581 tried window[main]/scene/access, met a bare -32601 Method not found, and registered a debt saying scene/access could not be asked about a window — it could, and R1583 measured it and withdrew the debt a day later. This round closes the gap from both ends. rpc/methods now carries a per-method window class beside occ, plus a WINDOW_DOC legend on the wire for the same reason OCC_DOC is there; and the unknown-method arm READS that catalog, so the exact call that produced the false debt is now answered with the method meant, the window named, and the spelling that works. The correction is derived, so a method added tomorrow is corrected with no edit here and a name that is not a method after stripping gets no invented advice.
changes_bullets: MethodWindow (scope | path) as a third column of RPC_METHODS, published per entry by rpc/methods, with WINDOW_DOC as its legend — a closed two-word vocabulary an agent can match on rather than prose it must read

dispatch_parsed's unknown-method arm calls unknown_method_error, which strips a window prefix off the method NAME and, when the remainder is in the catalog, names it and the params.window spelling. Derived from RPC_METHODS, never guessed

wait_for_error_to_rpc carries the CAUSE instead of the wrapper: wait_for reaches its path through query, so a malformed prefix arrived as Query(Path(EmptyWindowId)) and went out as the bare word "Query" — the transport's classification published in place of the fact observed, the class R1565 named one method over. The same failure now yields the same published word through scene/query and scene/waitFor
WaitForError::Path removed with its From impl: nothing could produce it, and its presence was why the wrapper's own name reached the wire
wire_census gains MethodWindow and the two new fields, so the R1539 source-parse gate keeps describing the response truly — it caught this shape change itself
verification_bullets: pinion-rpc 1148 unit tests (3 new for R1585) + 4 integration, clippy -D pedantic clean, cargo doc clean; pinion-shell / pinion-tui / pinion-cli / pinion-rpc-transport green. The blast radius is 210 packages, over the R1582 cap, so the tool reported the command and CI covers the rest
tools/demos/r1585_a_method_says_how_a_window_is_named.py — 7 phases, 30 assertions, PASS in 2.4s over the live wire

THE COLUMN IS PROVEN, NOT PARSED. r1585_the_window_column_is_what_the_methods_actually_do probes every catalogued method with /window[]/anything — a well-formed PATH and a malformed WINDOW — and asserts the published class equals whether the method answers with the published EmptyWindowId word. Non-vacuity is asserted: a probe that reached nothing would agree with an all-scope catalog for the wrong reason

A SOURCE CENSUS CANNOT ANSWER THIS, measured rather than assumed: a call graph keyed by bare function name merges four different fn parse (displays.rs, draw_profile.rs twice, font.rs) and credits font/parse and scene/displays with reading a window prefix neither sees. Qualifying the call to path::resolve removed one false positive and not those two

The probe's first draft under-reported by SEVEN methods, each because it rejected an unrelated argument before ever looking at its path — and each named the argument in its refusal, so the probe was completed by reading what it was told. scene/simulate carries its path inside a step; scene/waitFor could not be reached at all until the wrapper defect above was fixed

A substring match on the reply body reported rpc/errors as path-addressed — it answers with the whole error vocabulary, EmptyWindowId included. Tightened to the error.data SLOT (R1560's boundary-less census trap, met head on)
7 counterfactuals, all caught, each reverted from a hash-verified copy in finally with build failures raised as errors rather than counted as catches (R1581)
carry_forward_bullets: The window column says whether a method's PATH takes a prefix; it does not say whether a method's ANSWER varies by scope, because that is applied by the embedder (pinion-shell / pinion-tui) before dispatch and cannot be observed from inside pinion-rpc. WINDOW_DOC states the universal instead of implying a per-method fact the surface has not established

rpc/methods still publishes no per-method param schema, so an agent learns a method exists and how a window is named to it, and not how to call it. R1539's withheld method-to-type binding is the same gap from the other side
Of the two window spellings, only the path one is now discoverable per method; a client that wants to know which methods CHANGE their answer under a scope must still try it

R1585.1.decision_summary: R1585.1 §5.18 §5.7 — THE PROBE'S OWN POPULATION IS GATED, AND TWO RE-JUDGMENTS THE TALLY DEMANDED. Asked whether every new debt had been registered, the audit found three things and this closes them. (1) R1585's window-column probe supplied eleven param names chosen by watching methods refuse; a census of `params.get("...")` across the crate found THIRTY, and two of the nineteen missing are path-shaped — `signal_path` and `target_path`. A method reading its path from one of those would answer the probe with a param error, be observed as not path-addressed, and be published as `scope` while taking a window prefix: the curated-population defect, inside the gate built to prevent one. (2) R1584's round-trip port-order limit was stated in its demo and nowhere a consumer of the crate would read it. (3) R1584 read the tally while its own round was still DECLARED AHEAD, saw +17%, and deferred — the reading R1550 recorded as the one to distrust, because the ledger counts rounds git HAS. Both axes were STALE at the push gate; both are re-judged here.
changes_bullets: probe_params() is derived from PROBE_PARAM_NAMES, and r1585_1_the_probe_supplies_every_param_the_surface_reads asserts that list covers every params.get("<name>") in the crate, so a new param name fails the test instead of silently narrowing the probe. The census pattern is unambiguous, unlike the call-graph census this gate replaced
The wider probe leaves all twelve classifications unchanged, which is the useful outcome: the published column was right, and nothing had guaranteed it would stay right

partition.rs states the round-trip limit in its module docs: a boundary round trip keeps what the graph computes and NOT the port order, because ports are addressed by index and other instances are wired by it, so restoring a port to its old position would silently rewire every one of them
Advanced DCC re-judged 95 -> 96 and §7 API 62 -> 65, both demanded by tools/phase_b_tally.py, with the leverage order changing: DCC goes from first (100) to joint-last (80)
verification_bullets: pinion-rpc 1149 unit tests + 4 integration, pinion-node-graph 84 + 1 doctest, clippy -D pedantic clean, cargo doc clean

The new gate is asserted non-vacuous twice: it fails if it reads fewer than 20 source files, and again if the census finds fewer than 25 param names — a pattern that drifted would otherwise report an empty difference and pass
tools/phase_b_tally.py --selftest PASS, and the report carries no STALE axis after both re-judgments

R1586.decision_summary: R1586 §5.38 §5.52 §2 #7 — A NODE SAYS HOW IT TAKES PART, AND ONLY ONE OF THOSE FACTS IS THE GRAPH'S MEANING. Taking a stage OUT of a pipeline is half of what a node editor does, and this crate could not do it at all: a node computed or it did not exist. R1586 adds bypass — the node stops computing and the values at its inputs pass through it — with the routing DERIVED rather than authored, and applies the same derivation to the structure as dissolve and detach, so what a preview shows and what a delete leaves behind cannot disagree. Blender unifies those two as well and says so in its own operator description ("Remove nodes and reconnect nodes as if deletion was muted"), so the unification is parity; what is chosen differently is the rule underneath, what is reported when it cannot be applied, and where the facts live. The rule is one sentence — a bypassed node is the IDENTITY as far as its signature allows: output n takes input n when their types agree, else the lowest-indexed input of the right type, else nothing. It is a function of the signature alone. Blender scores every input against every output through a static socket-type table (get_internal_link_type_priority) and breaks ties by whether the input happens to be WIRED, so unplugging one port there changes which value leaves by a different port of the same node. Three more divergences, each measured against ~/blender-ref at 8cf50599: an output no input can feed is NAMED (Blender produces no internal link and node_internal_relink then deletes the downstream wire with node_remove_link, returning void); the derivation is READ rather than materialised into node runtime internal_links behind a tree-update pass whose job is to notice the stored copy has gone stale; and a muted LINK is a different word from a bypassed NODE because they are opposite behaviours — a muted link stops a value, a bypassed node passes one through — where Blender spells both "mute" (NODE_LINK_MUTED, NODE_MUTED). The fifth is where the facts live: Appearance is a separate TYPE holding what a node looks like, and Blender keeps NODE_COLLAPSED, NODE_PREVIEW, NODE_SELECT and NODE_MUTED in one flag integer, so nothing in its model says which of those bits its evaluator may read. This closes two of the six Blender census gaps R1584 left — the collapse/hide/mute family and the link-manipulation family — leaving four.
changes_bullets: Node::bypassed and Link::muted as separate fields with separate words, plus Appearance (collapsed, hide_unused_ports, show_options, show_preview, width) as a distinct TYPE the evaluator never reads. Appearance lives in the document for the reason x and y do: a group collapse and a paste move nodes between trees, so a side table keyed by NodeId would attach one node's looks to another's

Document::passthrough derives the routing and publishes what it cannot route: dropped_outputs (an output no input can feed) and unreached_inputs (an input reaching no output), beside the routes themselves and an is_identity predicate

Document::dissolve and Document::detach apply that derivation to the structure — Blender's delete_reconnect and links_detach / move_detach_links — reporting bridged, severed and removed. No bridge can close a cycle or displace a link, both by construction, and both asserted

push_link gained a muted argument so the COMPILER enumerates every link-moving derivation and each one decides. The rule is uniform: a derived link inherits the mutedness of the link that fed its consumer, OR-ed across any two links it joins. That is a crossing's per-consumer half in a collapse, the join in an inline, the recorded crossing in a paste, and the carried and takeover paths in a boundary move

Node::adopt_from is the one place a node is copied without being moved (paste, inline), and it DESTRUCTURES its source so a field added to Node fails to compile until someone says whether a copy carries it. Before this round both sites copied the label and nothing else — complete at the time, and silently incomplete the moment a field arrived, because the compiler sees struct literals and not hand-rolled copies
Document::visible_ports is the derivation only the document can make: hide_unused_ports is unanswerable without knowing what is wired. A muted link still counts as wired
Severed carries the crossing consumers that were muted at the cut, so re-attaching an inbound crossing puts back a wire that stops the value rather than one that carries it

hello-node-groups drives all of it over the wire (bypass, mute_link, dissolve, detach, collapse, hide_ports; passthrough, visible_ports, looks, bypassed, muted_links, last_rewire) and PAINTS it: a bypassed node draws its routes across its card, a muted wire is dashed, a collapsed node draws only what visible_ports says

R1587.decision_summary: R1587 §5.38 §5.52 §2 #7 — A PORT SAYS WHETHER A VALUE PASSES THROUGH IT. R1586 left a debt of its own making: the bypass routing was uniform over the signature and a taxonomy had no way to say it wanted a different one. That note prescribed the fix, and the census run to carry it out showed the prescription wrong in both directions — which is the round. Measured at ~/blender-ref 8cf50599: the per-port form the note called "the one actually used" (no_mute_links) is declared by NO node type in Blender's tree, only read; the per-node C callback it called speculative (internally_linked_input) is registered by ELEVEN. And yet the answer is still the per-port form, for a reason the note did not have: those eleven callbacks compute exactly three things between them — the identity matched by name (7, under the comment "Internal links should always map corresponding input and output sockets"), the identity matched by index (1), and "skip the leading control input" (3) — and this crate's default already produces every one of them. Blender needs a per-node callback to express the IDENTITY, because its default is a static socket-type priority table with a wired tie-break. Ours is the identity, so a per-node hook has nothing left to say. What is left over is exclusion, in exactly two shapes: a control input that happens to share the data type it selects between (Switch<Bool>, where the bare identity passes the SWITCH through), and an output whose value means nothing while the node is not computing (node_geo_menu_switch answers nullptr for every output after its first). Both are one declaration on the port, read from both ends. Eleven C callbacks in the reference reduce to one declaration here.
changes_bullets: Port::passthrough (default true) with the Port::no_passthrough builder, read from both ends: an excluded INPUT is never a source for any output, an excluded OUTPUT receives nothing and is reported among Passthrough::dropped_outputs. One declaration, because a pass-through has two ends

Document::passthrough honours it at BOTH steps of the derivation — the identity preference and the lowest-of-the-right-type fallback — so an exclusion cannot be defeated by falling through, and dissolve and detach inherit it because they read the same derivation
serde default = "yes" so a document written before this round still loads with its ports on the path; the pre-R1587 wire form is asserted to parse

hello-node-groups gains Op::Cap, the forcing consumer: Ceiling and Amount are both amounts, so the bare identity would pass the CEILING through, and Clipped is a derived value that means nothing while the node is bypassed. Both sides of the declaration in one node

node_ports publishes the declaration beside each port (name:type(off)), so an agent reads what was DECLARED next to what passthrough DERIVED. Blender's no_mute_links lives in a private socket declaration and is readable from no API
the yes() serde helper moved to model.rs and is shared with Appearance rather than being written twice

tools/demos/r1586_bypass_is_the_identity.py gains phase H2 — 93 assertions total, PASS in 2.2s. One demo because it is one subject

THE CENSUS IS A TABLE THE TESTS ASSERT AGAINST, not a paragraph. BLENDER_HOOKS holds all eleven implementors with the shape each computes, and our derivation is asserted to answer what each callback answers. The PAIRING is checked and not just output 0, because two of the three shapes agree on output 0 and a rule sending every output to input 0 would pass otherwise. The census's own arithmetic is asserted too — eleven rows, 3/1/7 by shape

7 crate counterfactuals and 4 demo counterfactuals, all caught, each reverted from a hash-verified copy in finally. One demo counterfactual did not compile on its first draft and was rewritten to compile before being counted, since a counterfactual rustc rejects has zero discriminating power

The two residues are each pinned by a test that FAILS without the declaration: the control-input case asserts the bare identity picks the control first, then that the declaration leaves the first data input; the excluded-output case asserts it is reported as dropped, in the same slot an output no input could feed uses

The census is the argument that nothing needs to: all eleven of Blender's callbacks are reproduced by the default plus exclusion. If a case ever appears that exclusion cannot express, it will appear as a taxonomy declaring ports it does not want in an order it does not want, and the honest fix then is a routing hook rather than more flags

Blender's seven "corresponding socket" callbacks match by NAME; this crate matches by index and the two agree only because a node that pairs its sockets declares them in one order. Name matching is deliberately NOT adopted: Port::name's own doc says a name is not an identity, and routing by it would make it one

The declaration is part of the signature the taxonomy supplies, so it cannot vary per NODE — two instances of one kind always agree about which ports are on the path. Blender's is per socket instance and so could differ; no use of that was found in its tree
Op::Cap is the only consumer in the workspace; hello-node-editor's own taxonomy is untouched, which is the per-binding domain work [[debt-two-node-graph-models]] already names

R1588.decision_summary: R1588 §5.39 §5.40 §2 #7 — THE TWO FOCUS SWEEPS CENSUS ONE POPULATION. R1518's sweep asserted something strong about every binding it walked, and walked a hand-written list of fourteen composite names. A curated population cannot find an absence: a binding with zero focus stops is simply never walked, which is how debt-interactive-role-without-focus-stop stayed invisible in seventeen bindings for some fifty rounds. R1570.1 did not fix that list — it added a SECOND sweep whose population is derived — so the tree carried one curated sweep and one derived one, asking different questions of different sets, and which gate saw a binding depended on who last edited a list. tools/binding_focus.py is the merge: the derivation lives in one module, both demos import it, and it has its own tests, in pre-push, because a population that has quietly narrowed makes every sweep resting on it pass while covering less. R1518 goes from 14 bindings to the derived 92 and from 164 assertions to 509. The widened census answers the question the debt registered and could not measure: ZERO new focus-stop absences. The five observations it did surface are all bearers in ANOTHER window — which this axis could not previously tell apart from a real absence, and can now because R1583 published `resolved`, making this the first gate to read it. So the debt file's own warning that widening would produce multi-window false positives was correct, and the round that would have paid it had already been done.
changes_bullets: tools/binding_focus.py — the population derivation, moved out of r1570.1 and shared: Population with its two halves (attribute-declared, which can be asked about a named tag; and AriaRole-constructed, which can only be asked whether the window has any stop) plus both kinds of exclusion carried rather than dropped, since a population that reports only what it kept cannot be audited

tools/test_binding_focus.py — 271 checks on the derivation itself, run by pre-push. Non-vacuity of both halves, the R1570.5 invariant that the hand-written half outnumbers the declared one, disjointness, every exclusion real and absent from the walk, and every walked name a directory that exists

r1518's WALKED is the derived population, and the sweep ASSERTS it is: a counterfactual replacing it with a two-name list passed in seven seconds, because removing a curated list is not the same as removing the ability to have one. A floor on the size catches a narrowing that a re-derivation would not
check() splits the two causes of an absent bearer using R1583's `resolved`, and asserts the wire always answers HOW it resolved — a fold is a statement, not the absence of one

the walk is bounded twice: the ring closes rather than running to a fixed count, and how far a binding is walked follows what it declares. A focus move costs ~1s (the pre-existing R1561 stall), so a fixed four over 92 bindings was 310s against a 180s budget
binding_focus.build_command() derives the cargo line the demos' docstrings used to spell out by hand, and the tests assert it names exactly the population
verification_bullets: r1518 PASS: 509 assertions over 92 focus stops in 92 bindings, 29s warm and 138s cold against the sweep's 180s budget. r1570.1 PASS unchanged through the shared derivation (147 assertions, 50.5s), which is the proof the lift was faithful

5 counterfactuals, all caught after two were not. CF-1 (the population falls back to a curated list) PASSED at first — the sharpest possible result, since that is the very defect this round removes, and it is what forced the identity assertion. CF-5 (the build line pinned to one package) PASSED because nothing read it, and forced the test that does

Every example binary in the tree was built 08-06 21:28-21:34 and R1583 landed 08-07 08:46, so a PINION_ASSUME_BUILT=1 run over 92 bindings was comparing binaries from two different commits — the first assertion to read a field R1583 added failed on a binding whose binary simply predated it, and the earlier PASS was measuring history. The population was rebuilt (9m40s) before any result was believed

The ~1s per-move cost was isolated rather than reasoned about: timing each method separately showed focus/get, scene/access and focus/next all at 0.000s except one 0.999s stall, which is the pre-existing R1561 finding and not a regression from the rebuild

R1589.decision_summary: R1589 §5.38 §5.52 §2 #7 — A NODE CAN BELONG TO A FRAME, AND BELONGING IS A FOREST. A node editor has two kinds of containment and they are not the same kind: a GROUP contains a graph (its members are in another tree, they compute, the boundary is a signature — R1577), and a FRAME contains a region of CANVAS (its members stay where they are, they compute exactly as before, and the boundary means nothing to the evaluator). The crate had no concept of the second at all, which is the largest of the eleven gaps the R1577 Blender census names — eight operators, re-measured 2026-08-07 as the heaviest of the five remaining clusters. NodeBody::Frame is a structural body this crate owns (like Group and Interface, so an application cannot forget it or get it wrong) with an EMPTY signature, so nothing links to it and evaluation never reaches it; Node::parent is the relation, a within-tree reference exactly like a Link's sockets. Read across a tree that relation is a FOREST, and that is the whole subject: a container must be a frame, and nothing may contain itself. Blender declares the same bNode *parent and states BOTH rules as BLI_assert inside node_attach_node, compiled out of the build it ships — and its own NODE_OT_parent_set calls node_detach_node FIRST, so by the time the second assert runs the chain it would have walked is already cleared and the guard cannot fire even in a debug build. Nothing there then terminates: node_is_parent_and_child and get_sorted_node_parents both walk parent to nullptr. ONE DERIVATION, NOT ONE PER GESTURE: every gesture over the forest asks which members of a selection are not inside another member of it, so Document::outermost is that question and enframe, unframe and translate are its call sites. Blender computes it twice as node_join_attach_recursive and node_detach_recursive — two recursive functions over two structs with identical fields, NodeJoinState and NodeDetachstate, both {bool done; bool descendent;} — and a third time in the transform code.
changes_bullets: NodeBody::Frame + Node::parent: canvas containment as a forest, refused when it would not be one, with the chain named
Document::outermost is the one derivation enframe / unframe / translate all act on; Blender writes it three times
set_parent / enframe / unframe / translate / ancestry / members / contents / common_frame; ParentError names which rule broke
remove_node answers Removed{links, adopted}: a deleted frame hands its members to the frame ABOVE, not to the canvas
Orphaned reports every containment an edit could not carry — extract, insert, group, ungroup, group_insert, group_separate
insert puts a copy back inside its original's frame when the fragment is going home, and only then — an id is not a name
validate gains DanglingParent / ParentNotAFrame / ContainmentCycle; every forest walk terminates on a broken document
FIX: partition::move_nodes copied the label alone, so a node crossing a group boundary lost its bypass and its looks
hello-node-groups draws a fence at an extent derived from its contents, and frames / unframe / reparent / nudge over RPC
verification_bullets: 17 counterfactuals, each reverted with hash verification: all CAUGHT. Two were INVALID (did not compile — R1581's class) and were rewritten to compile; ONE PASSED and that is a finding — CF-9 gave a frame its TREE's interface ports and the first draft of the signature test still passed, because it asserted in the ROOT tree whose interface is empty, so the counterfactual and the truth produced identical answers. The test now asserts inside a definition that HAS an interface. R1586's lesson, one round on: do not assert an invariant where discrimination is zero.

Crate: 137 tests (23 new) + the doc-test. Each past-Blender claim holds BLENDER'S OWN RULE as a test helper and asserts the divergence, rather than describing it — blender_is_parent_and_child reproduced with its detach-first ordering, node_unlink_attached's outright clear, node_copy_local's silent detach, and node_group.cc's flattening loop.

Demo: tools/demos/r1589_a_frame_is_a_forest.py, 14 phases over the live wire — the forest enumerated, the two refusals driven, one-level unframing, a frame's DERIVED extent read out of the PAINT scene and asserted to contain and to travel with its cards, a duplicate re-entering its fence, a collapse leaving its instance in the pipeline, an inline putting the definition's own frames back, a dissolve handing members up, and a paste into another tree refusing to join a frame by number — with the destination made to actually HOLD a frame at that number so the check discriminates. Four counterfactuals run against the DEMO after a release rebuild: all CAUGHT.

A tautological assertion was found in the demo's own draft and removed: "a node outside the fence did not move" compared one live read with another live read. It now compares against a rect captured before the drag.

Blast radius (tools/blast_radius.py) = pinion-node-graph + hello-node-groups. The group verb's reply gained a field, which broke r1577 / r1578 / r1584 — caught by running them, fixed, and all five node-graph demos pass.

Gates: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D pedantic on both packages, cargo doc --document-private-items, validate-workspace. Clippy's line caps forced four extraction points that are better code: copy_selection_into, reframe_copies, move_selection_into, inline_body, forest_violations.
carry_forward_bullets: A frame's EXTENT is derived by the application, not the crate: it needs card geometry a model crate deliberately does not have. hello-node-groups derives it; a second consumer would decide whether a `Extent` trait belongs in the crate.

NODE_OT_join_named and NODE_OT_join_nodes are macro/UI compositions of enframe plus a rename and are not separate model operations; translate_attach and detach_translate_attach are transform macros whose model halves are translate + set_parent. The eight-operator cluster is closed at the model layer, and the gesture layer is the application's.

hello-node-editor still holds its own graph model (debt-two-node-graph-models) and now also its own frames, so the tree has two frame implementations as well as two node models. Unchanged by this round and registered.

NODE_FRAME's own looks — Blender's NodeFrame{flag: SHRINK|RESIZEABLE, label_size} — are not in Appearance. shrink is what decides whether a frame's box hugs its contents or is user-sized, and a user-sized one needs a height, which Appearance deliberately has only a width for (a node's height is a function of its ports; a frame's is not). That asymmetry is the open question, not the field.

Of the eleven gaps the R1577 census names, item 12 (frame/parent) is closed here. Items 5 (selection vocabulary), 7 (insert_offset), 8 (find_node) and 10 (view_selected) remain open; 9 (resize) and 11 (swap_node / node_copy_color) remain half-done.

R1590.decision_summary: R1590 §5.38 §5.52 §2 #3 §2 #7 — A SELECTION GROWS BY ASKING THE GRAPH A QUESTION. The selection itself is deliberately not in the model — R1586 put it outside the document because two people looking at one graph have two selections and one document — so what belongs here is the other half: given these nodes, which others are the ones you mean? Blender spells that as six operators; four of them are questions about the GRAPH and are now Document::grow, and two are questions about the CANVAS and are measured out (see the carry). Every one of them is a PURE QUERY: Blender's set the SELECT bit on bNode and carry OPTYPE_UNDO, because there the selection lives in the document, so "what would this select?" cannot be asked without selecting it and every answer costs an undo step. Here the answer is a value and the guarantee is the signature — grow takes &self, held as a compile-time witness rather than as an assertion, because an edit that happened to change nothing would satisfy any runtime comparison. THE LARGEST DIFFERENCE IS THAT THE REACH IS A PARAMETER: node_select_linked_to walks output_socket->directly_linked_sockets() — ONE HOP — and so does linked_from, so the question a person actually has (what depends on this?) is answered by pressing the key until the picture stops changing, with nothing telling you when that has happened. Reach::Transitive is that question asked once, and Grown::added empty is the signal a mutating operator cannot give. TWO RELATIONS, ONE READING OF THE REACH: links are one relation and R1589's containment is the other, so the four relational arms are the two directions of each and Reach means the same thing in all four. They cannot collide — a frame has no ports, so no link ever reaches one, and containment only ever relates a frame to its members. Three more divergences, each asserted against Blender's own rule held as a test helper: two instances of DIFFERENT definitions are not one kind (every group node there is type_legacy == NODE_GROUP, so grouping by type sweeps in instances of unrelated definitions, while an instance's signature IS its definition's interface); an affix that is not there offers NO CRITERION (node_select_grouped_name substitutes the whole name for a missing suffix, conflating "no suffix" with "the suffix is the entire name"); and the affix is read off the name that is PAINTED (Blender groups on bNode::name, the datablock id its own node header does not draw). R1591.decision_summary: R1591 §5.32 §2 #2 §2 #7 — A REGION OF THE PAINTED SURFACE IS A VALUE. Selecting by dragging a shape over what is drawn is one gesture every canvas has: a node editor's marquee and lasso, a timeline's range, a chart's brush, a diagram editor's rubber band. The framework had exactly ONE of the shapes — Scene::hit_test_region takes a rectangle — and exactly ONE of the two things you can mean by "covered": touches. R1590 measured the absence from the other end, against Blender's NODE_OT_select_circle and NODE_OT_select_lasso, and recorded that those are not node-graph capabilities at all: they test a region against node->runtime->draw_bounds, the DRAWN rectangle, which is a question for the layer that knows what was painted where. This round is that layer answering it, and the proof is a composition — a node editor's lasso select is scene/locate_region plus the application's own tag mapping, with no node-graph code involved. pinion_core::region holds Region (Rect / Circle / Lasso) and RegionFit (Intersects / Contains), in integer arithmetic on purpose, because a selection is a question about which PIXELS a shape covers and floating point would make the answer depend on rounding at exactly the edge a user notices. Scene::hit_test_shape is the general form and hit_test_region is now its rectangle-and-touching case: the walk prunes and translates by the region's BOUNDING RECT exactly as it always did and decides whether to REPORT a node by the precise shape, which is what makes a rectangular query answer byte-for-byte what it answered before, and it is why the descent is gated on the bounds rather than on the fit — a child can be contained by a region its parent only touches. Five things past Qt 6.11, measured against qgraphicsview.h / qgraphicsscene.h / qnamespace.h on this machine: three shapes are ONE method where Qt has three items() overloads and Blender three operators; the fit is a per-QUERY argument where QGraphicsView::rubberBandSelectionMode is a VIEW property, so two selections in one view cannot mean different things and nothing records which mode a given selection used; the outcome REPEATS the question, so an answer is interpretable on its own; a degenerate shape is NAMED where items(QPolygonF, ..) answers with the same empty QList an empty surface gets; and the whole thing is askable from OUTSIDE THE PROCESS, which a QPainterPath — an opaque mutable object that can only be built in-process — cannot be. Qt's four ItemSelectionMode arms collapse to two here, and that is a fact about this framework rather than an omission: a scene node's extent IS a Rect, every hit test in the tree including the pointer's is rectangular, so shape and bounding rect are the same thing.
changes_bullets: pinion_core::region: Region (Rect / Circle / Lasso), RegionFit, RegionError, integer geometry, even-odd for a lasso
Scene::hit_test_shape is the general form; hit_test_region is its rectangle-and-touching case, unchanged for every caller
Region::covers_at applies a signed offset, so the precise test runs in the frame the caller drew in across a Scroll
scene/locate_region gains shape / fit / from, the last being the two-scene basis scene/snapshot already uses
LocateRegionOutcome repeats the shape and the fit, and now derives Serialize so the wire census can check it
locate_region the function is retired: locate_shape is the one derivation and the wrapper had no caller left
FIX: the R1585.1 param census was a raw substring scan, so every params.get rustfmt had broken across lines was invisible
verification_bullets: 15 counterfactuals, each reverted with hash verification. THREE did not do what they were named for on the first pass, and each is a finding. CF-3 deleted the lasso Contains crossing guard and was NOT caught: the concave fixture had a rect whose corners were in the bite, so four-corners-inside already refused it and the guard changed nothing. The fixture it needs is a rect whose four corners land in the C's ARMS while it still spans the bite; that rect is now in the test, with each corner asserted inside first so the fixture cannot silently stop discriminating. CF-4 disabled a clause by operator precedence and turned off the corners clause instead of the vertices clause it was named for. CF-9 deleted the collinear branch of segments_cross and was not caught — and the measurement is the answer: that branch CANNOT change what Region::covers answers, because a point where a lasso edge overlaps a rect's corner-cycle segment lies on that rect, so the corner or vertex clause has already fired. It is kept, because segments_cross is a general predicate whose contract includes the case, and it is now tested DIRECTLY, since a test that cannot fail is not a test.
pinion-core: 3130 tests (17 new). pinion-rpc: 1150 plus the four wire-census gates. Every Blender and Qt claim was measured against the headers and the sources on this machine rather than recalled.

Demo: tools/demos/r1591_a_region_is_a_value.py, 8 phases over the live wire against hello-node-groups' real painted canvas: the rectangle form answers what it always answered whether or not the new params are named; the fit changes the answer for the same rectangle; a disc and a triangular lasso are driven; the lasso is shown to select STRICTLY fewer cards than its own bounding rectangle, with the near card in and the far one past the hypotenuse and the triangle sized from the painted geometry so a layout change cannot make it pass by accident; four refusals are driven; and the state tree is shown to answer nothing for the same rectangle the paint frame answers, which is why `from` had to exist.

The R1585.1 fix is itself measured: with the census normalised, it found eight param names the probe had never supplied — delta, key, magnification, points, rotation, tilt_x, tilt_y, with_origin — plus `from`, which scene/snapshot and scene/drag both read. 22% of the surface's param names were invisible to a gate built to prevent a curated population.

Two contracts changed deliberately and both are visible: a zero-area region is now refused by scene/locate_region rather than answered with an empty list, and the outcome carries two more keys. The second is inside the wire census now; the first went red in this crate's own tests, which is where a contract change should surface.
carry_forward_bullets: The region is tested against a node's RECT, which is what every hit test in this tree does. A PathNode's actual outline is not consulted, so Qt's ItemShape / ItemBoundingRect distinction has nothing to bite on here; if a future round makes the pointer honour real outlines, this is the second place that decision lands.

scene/locate and scene/bbox still answer against the state tree only. `from` was added to locate_region because a region select is meaningless without geometry; the same argument applies to the other two and is not made here.
A lasso arrives as a polygon and is treated as closed. A stroke with width — a brush select — is a different primitive and is not this.

The R1585.1 probe still classifies by FIRST refusal (debt-probe-classifies-by-first-refusal), so a method refusing on a param's VALUE before reaching its path is still unreachable. This round supplied legal values for the eleven params it touched, which narrows that debt without closing it: `from` means an enum to scene/snapshot and a POINT to scene/drag, so no single bag can satisfy both.

Params read through a closure with a variable key (scene/locate_region's own w and h) remain invisible to the census, which matches on a literal. Recorded rather than fixed: a census that follows a binding is a parser, and this one is a scan.
