R1633.decision_summary: an axis says which labels it dropped: `pinion_chart::fit` -- `Along` / `Room` / `Fitted` / `FitRule`, the one derivation that decides which tick labels are drawn, and the three derivations that publish what it cost. THE GAP WAS IN THE ANALYZER SPEC AND NOT IN THE CENSUS. Plane C requires "high-density label overlap avoidance"; R1568 recorded it; R1622's re-audit passed over it; and it survived as prose inside `debt-dataviz-dashboard-substrate`'s table with no file of its own, so the standard `grep 'status: open'` census could not see it. It was found by the user asking whether the analyzer work was finished -- the fourth repeat of "knowing is not registering" -- and the audit row that said "only the 3D surface remains" was corrected in the same pass. THE TWO REFERENCES DO DIFFERENT THINGS AND NEITHER IS ENOUGH, both measured from source rather than remembered. The toolkit draws every label and hides the colliders, but only on its VERTICAL axis: `verticalaxis.cpp` keeps a running edge and hides anything reaching past it, while `horizontalaxis.cpp` hides a colliding label ONLY when its text has already been elided down to the ellipsis -- so on the axis where the problem actually bites, an ordinary overlapping label is drawn anyway. Its newer graphs module has no overlap pass at all: one text item per category, elided to its own slot, every one visible. The DCC does the better thing and a different one -- it measures the label at each end of the range, adds six pixels, and hands that to the grid-step chooser as a minimum spacing, so nothing is ever PLACED too close and no label is ever dropped. That only works on an axis with a ladder to climb, and its editors have no categorical axis. SO THIS DOES BOTH, CHOSEN BY WHAT THE AXIS IS, because the two kinds genuinely differ: a ladder axis (linear / log / time) COARSENS -- the tick target is lowered until the labels clear, so the axis has fewer ticks and NO label is dropped -- and a category axis STRIDES, because its ticks are its slots and its slots are the data. The ticks and the labels are separate answers for that reason: `Fitted::ticks` is every tick (the grid) and `Fitted::labelled` is the subset that gets a name, since thinning the grid with the labels would take away the slot separators a category axis is read by. MEASURED, NOT MODELLED -- the round's own correction. The first draft modelled a label's width as its character count times a widest-character advance, which is exact for tabular digits and an over-estimate for text; that made this the ONE axis where the work was worse than both references, since both measure the laid-out string. The user asked whether the demo-host question was really the long-term-correct one, and it was not: the real item was this. pinion-core already had the seam -- R1453 §5.36 `TextMetrics` / `measured_text_extent`, whose own module doc names "multiply a character count by a monospace cell" as the upper bound it exists to retire -- so `Along::extent_px` now measures the real face THROUGH THE STYLE THE LABEL IS ABOUT TO BE PAINTED IN, and the model is the declared headless fallback where no provider is seeded. No new dependency, no purity break, no build-entry signature change, and the runtime already seeds `LayoutCacheTextMetrics` at boot. A test seeds a provider that deliberately DISAGREES with the model and asserts the two fits differ, which is the only way that claim is checkable. PAST BOTH REFERENCES IN FOUR PLACES: the report reaches the scene (`label_fit` always, `labels_omitted` only when a label really was left off, `label_crowding` as a PIXEL measurement when even the coarsest answer fails) where both references are silent; both ends of a stride are pinned where a greedy first-wins scan loses whichever it reaches last; the fallback is DECLARED where a missing measurement elsewhere is a silent zero; and one value (`Along`) is the whole difference between the axes the toolkit implements twice with different behaviour. FOUR SITES WERE REACHING PAST `axis_ticks`: bar, boxplot and the candlestick's ordinal arm each drew one category label per slot in their own loops, and bar called `nice_ticks` directly for its value axis. The first three were found by a derivation test that PASSED VACUOUSLY -- it asserted an omission count on a chart whose category axis never went through the fit -- which is the same class as R1632's two passing counterfactuals. AND NO EXAMPLE IN THE TREE HAD EVER HAD MORE CATEGORIES THAN ROOM, which is why a defect this visible survived from R1374: every category axis in the tree carried twelve short names. `hello-category-axis`, the forcing consumer for the category axis, gains a dense thirty-endpoint list, because a forcing consumer that only exercises the easy arity is not forcing the axis.

R1634.decision_summary: a chart is a table to a reader who does not read pixels: `pinion_a11y::chart` projects a chart as `table` / `row` / `columnheader` / `rowheader` / `cell`, and `BarChart::access_table` / `ScatterChart::access_table` answer it -- so what was ONE `AccessNode` carrying whatever string the inspect readout happened to build is now a structure a screen reader navigates. THE REFERENCES HAVE NOTHING HERE, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the toolkit's three charting modules at 6.11 -- its 2D charts, the newer graphs module replacing them, and the 3D data visualisation one -- contain no accessibility integration at all between them, not one call into the platform layer the rest of that toolkit is wired through, and a chart view there reaches the platform as a single scroll-area object. The DCC and the engine have no charting. So for once there was no floor to clear and the shape had to be ARGUED. It is a TABLE for three reasons: that is what a chart's data is (points down, series across); WAI-ARIA has no chart role and its graphics module's roles are dropped by the platform bridges, so a role nothing maps announces nothing; and `table`/`row`/`cell` are already in this crate's vocabulary, already lowered by the tree builder, and already navigable with commands users know. Rows are points and columns are series because a chart usually has many points and few series -- that keeps the COLUMN count small, which is what a table reader moves across, and makes reading down a column reading one series in order. THE HEADLINE IS THE CONTRAST WITH R1633. That round thins axis labels when there are more of them than room; this one names every row from the DATA, and the demo asserts both numbers in the same frame: 8 labels painted, 30 rows announced. Thinning is a fact about pixels and a reader who is not reading pixels is not subject to it -- the two reports are consistent rather than in conflict, because `labels_omitted` says what the PICTURE left off and the table says what the DATA has. HOW MANY NODES was the question the debt file said had to be settled first, and its own answer -- that ten thousand marks would collapse the tree -- was an untested guess, so it is not designed around. The bound is the chart's own window and nothing else: `aria-rowcount` and `aria-setsize` state the full extent while the present rows are what was drawn, which is exactly the model `virtual_list` established for a windowed list, and the tree's standing rule is that the AT tree exposes what the paint exposes. A cell carries its series name WITH its value, because a number announced alone has no subject and a reader crossing a row of four series must hear which one each figure belongs to; and it resolves its bounds to the MARK it was drawn as, so a touch explorer or a magnifier lands on the bar rather than on the chart. A datum drawn inside a shared path -- a line chart's samples -- carries no tag rather than borrowing one, which is stated as the reason line charts are not among the two consumers here. The assembler sits in `pinion-a11y` beside `grid` and `virtual_list` because that is where a11y topology lives in this tree, not because two consumers had duplicated it; bar and scatter are its first two, and scatter is there specifically because a single-series bar chart cannot exercise the column axis at all.

R1634.1.decision_summary: the half of R1634's carry that was never a carry: `BoxPlotChart::access_table` and `CandlestickChart::access_table`. R1634 registered `debt-a-line-chart-has-no-per-sample-mark` and wrote inside it that boxplot and candlestick "have no structural obstacle" -- and then deferred them anyway. A carry whose own file says there is nothing in the way is not a carry; the standing rule is that the only legitimate one is an external dependency. The user asked why it was not paid immediately, which is the correct question, and this is the payment. AND THE PAYMENT VALIDATED THE ABSTRACTION, which is the part worth recording rather than the discipline. Both new consumers have columns that are NOT SERIES: a box plot's are the five landmarks a summary is made of and a candlestick's are open / high / low / close. `ChartColumn` was named and documented for a series because its only two consumers were a single-series bar chart and a multi-series scatter, and one of those exercises no column axis at all. So the definition is now what it should always have been -- a column is WHAT THE CHART CARRIES PER POINT -- and the doc says so with the three cases beside it. Deferring would have left that abstraction resting on one consumer with one column. TWO FINDINGS FELL OUT. First, the wire spelling and the announced word are different audiences: `SummaryPosition::name` answers `lower_extreme` for a client that matches on it and the new `label` answers "lower whisker" for a person who hears it, because running the wire spelling through a screen reader has it say an underscore -- the same split R1628 drew between a measurement's shape and a scene's. Second, and this one is about truth rather than phrasing: the word is WHISKER and not MINIMUM, because a distribution with outliers has values below its whisker, so announcing it as the minimum states something false to exactly the reader who cannot check it against the picture. `Distribution::positions` / `at` are lifted to mirror `Candle::positions` / `at` -- the argument is symmetry with an existing type rather than a count of copies, and `off_scale` becomes a call site of the pair instead of re-listing the five landmarks itself.

R1635.decision_summary: the SCE pin moves and the gate can see it. `vendor/sce` goes 287 commits forward to `8597e6929a`, and the `[workspace.dependencies]` revs move with it in the same commit, which is the dual-pin discipline the workspace manifest states: the built SCE and the vendored checkout must not drift, because the C++ side and the canon sync track the submodule while cargo builds from the rev. AND THE BUMP EXPOSED A GATE DEFECT, which is the half worth recording. `tools/blast_radius.py` -- the tool R1582 built so a round computes which packages a change can break instead of remembering the rule, and which the standing verification instruction now names by hand -- reported a radius of **ZERO** for this change. Its `owning_packages` maps a changed path to the member package whose DIRECTORY contains it, and the workspace root `Cargo.toml`, the lockfile and `vendor/` sit under no member at all. Its docstring said so approvingly: a path under no package "cannot break a cargo test". That is true of `tools/` and `docs/` and false of exactly these three, since the root manifest holds the `rev` half the tree links against, the lockfile is the resolved answer to it, and `vendor/` is the checkout those pins name. A gate that answers "nothing is affected" to the change class with the WIDEST reach is worse than having no gate, because the zero reads as a clean bill rather than as an absence -- the same failure shape R1495 recorded for a check that silently stopped happening. The fix is a named `WORKSPACE_WIDE` set and an `is_workspace_wide` predicate, with the root manifest and lockfile matched EXACTLY so a member's own `crates/x/Cargo.toml` still owns only that member: widening everything would be the same uselessness as zero with the opposite sign, and there is a selftest case for that direction too. R1636.decision_summary: a field that outlived its reason, deleted. `ChartStyle::label_advance_px` went in with R1633 as the number the label fit modelled a width from, back when that model was the fit's primary answer. By the time R1633 landed the primary answer was `pinion_core::measured_text_extent` -- the user's question in that round is what moved it -- and the field was only what a headless caller falls back to. It kept the shape of the design it no longer served, and that cost something measurable: TEN examples set `label_size_px` through `..ChartStyle::default()`, which leaves the advance at the default's, so every one of them fits 12-to-14-pixel labels against an advance derived from 11. Meanwhile NOTHING in the tree ever set the field -- the consumer it existed for never arrived -- and `with_label_size`, the builder added specifically to keep the pair from drifting, had no callers either. So the fix is not a gate on the pair but the removal of the pair: the fallback is derived from the label size and the two cannot disagree. A consumer that really has measured its face states that the way every measurement in this framework is stated, by seeding a `TextMetrics` provider, which the fit consults first anyway. HOW IT WAS FOUND MATTERS AS MUCH AS WHAT IT WAS. The user asked whether every new debt from this session had been registered in memory. The honest answer was no; the audit that followed turned up this one, and the right response was not to register it but to delete the thing. The general form: **a field whose only reason was to let a consumer override a default is a liability the moment the default stops being the primary answer**, and the way to notice is to count who sets it -- zero setters and ten silent mismatches is not a feature with no consumer, it is a defect with ten. AND ONE COUNTERFACTUAL PASSES, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: widening the three-fifths ratio to four-fifths breaks no test. That is structural rather than a hole. The constant is consulted ONLY when nothing can measure, so any assertion about how close it sits to a real advance would need the measurement whose absence is the sole condition for reaching it. What can be pinned is pinned -- that the fallback follows the label size, and that a seeded provider wins over it whatever it says -- and the reason the rest cannot is written where the constant is.

R1637.decision_summary: a call must be declared first: the transport asks the declaration BEFORE it dispatches, on both channels, so a name absent from $schema is absent from the wire. THE DEBT THIS CLOSES HAD HALF ITS DIAGNOSIS WRONG, and establishing that was the round's first act. R1632 recorded that an External's declared action list "does not reach the wire at all", measured against rpc/methods and scene/snapshot. Both measurements are true and the conclusion is false: the list has been on the wire since R825 as the reserved $schema introspect PATH, not a scene/* method, so a census run on one axis reported absence about a thing living on another -- our own surface, and the same class as debt-blender-census-by-field-name. What was actually missing was the ORDER of two questions. The transport dispatched first and consulted the declaration only to explain a refusal, which left the dangerous direction -- implemented, never declared -- working perfectly and unobservable: R1631's arrange verb was callable and undiscoverable for a full round with cargo test, clippy, the demo and the push gate all green, because none of them had two lists to compare. THIS IS THE REFERENCE'S FLOOR, PROVED BY COMPILING IT rather than by reading about it. A toolkit 6.4.2 class carrying one slots: method and one plain one, driven through the toolkit's meta-object: invokeMethod ran the declared name and answered true, refused the undeclared one with false and indexOfMethod() == -1 and did not run it; its 6.11.1 source still emits the same "No such method" from the meta-object's own translation unit. The toolkit reaches the guarantee by codegen because its declarations generate its dispatch; pinion reaches it by gate because its surfaces are hand-written -- and gets one report out of that the meta-object cannot express, DeclaredButUnhandled (the surface published a name and did not answer it), split out of UnknownInvokePath so an agent that read the schema and an agent that guessed are no longer told the same word. TURNING THE ORDER AROUND MADE THE TREE SAY WHERE IT WAS WRONG, which is the answer the debt file said could not come from source text. 123 undeclared or mis-declared actions: 56 never declared, and 67 declared as READ slots while dispatched as verbs, so $schema said "query me" about names only invoke answers. pinion-audio's two Externals had their ENTIRE invoke surface undeclared while the type doc described all ten verbs in prose. Two more on the read channel, one of them pinion_widget_paint::dock's lifecycle, whose own doc calls it "surfaced as scene-as-data via query(lifecycle) (2 #7)". FIVE NAMES CARRIED BOTH CHANNELS AT ONE ADDRESS (bump, boost, restamp, dense, focus_region) and a schema field holds one channel, so whichever was declared hid the other; split into a tally and a verb, which is what the reference does too -- a property and its setX() live in different meta-object namespaces. Three surfaces hand-copied an upstream declaration and moved to SchemaField::concat; hello-tab-reorder's copy had already lost send and demoted move and grab_cancel to reads. THE SOURCE CENSUS FAILED THREE TIMES and each miss is recorded with what caught it: it read only the first match; then missed tuple-pattern arms, found by a DEMO dying rather than by a test; then missed if path == "...". The method that worked was to over-report every string literal in an invoke body and classify by hand. The general lesson is larger than the tool: A WIRE GATE RETIRES THE CENSUS, because an undeclared action now dies in its own demo, so the answer to the census-over-text class is sometimes to move the invariant to a runtime boundary rather than to write a better parser. EIGHT COUNTERFACTUALS, 8/8 CAUGHT -- after the first run of CF-7 PASSED and was a finding: nothing anywhere asserted that a declared read reaches the wire, because every lifecycle assertion in the tree calls the trait directly and never passes the transport. The test written to close that found three more mis-declarations in dock on its first run. Its first oracle had to be replaced: "every declared read answers" reported fourteen text_field paths that answer None because the widget is UNBOUND, which is a fixture that cannot discriminate rather than a finding; asking the surface's own dispatch instead needs no binding and is exact.

R1638.decision_summary: an action says what it takes, and the declaration is enough to call it. R1637 made the declared surface the callable surface and left the other half of the contract unsaid: `$schema` published a verb's name, its channel and its return tag, and nothing about the argument -- 45 of 45 actions on one surface, measured over the wire. So an agent could DISCOVER a verb and still had to read pinion's source to USE it. THE ROUND STARTS FROM BEING BEHIND THE REFERENCE, which is rare enough here to say plainly: a meta-method publishes each parameter's name and type, and that list is generated from the signature so it cannot drift from what the method accepts. SILENCE IS AN ARM, AND THAT IS THE CENTRAL DECISION. 487 actions are declared across this tree and the overwhelming majority take an argument nothing describes; making an empty `args` mean "takes nothing" would have converted every one of them into an affirmative false statement, which is the error direction R1602 records as the expensive one -- a wrong `have` inflates silently, a wrong `absent` self-corrects the moment somebody reaches for it. `ArgForm::Undeclared` therefore publishes NO `args` key at all, and `Nullary` publishes an empty list, so a client can tell "has not said" from "takes nothing". The reference cannot represent the first state: a generated parameter list is always a claim. It is a state a hand-written declaration very much has, and pretending otherwise is what R1637 spent a round undoing on the neighbouring axis. PAST THE REFERENCE IN TWO PLACES. An argument says where its values COME FROM rather than only its type -- `OneOf` for a closed vocabulary, `ValuesOf` for a live path on the same surface -- where a meta-method gives a type name and constrains only enum-typed parameters, through its meta-enum. And `optional` marks the segments a delimited payload may elide, under the invariant that they must be a SUFFIX, which is forced by the only form that can elide anything: a delimited payload drops trailing segments, so a gap in the middle is unrepresentable. EVERY CLOSED VOCABULARY IS PROJECTED FROM ITS DEFINITION rather than written out. `Axis::WIRE_NAMES`, `Edge::WIRE_NAMES`, `ArrangePass::WIRE_NAMES` and `VoicePolicy::WIRE_NAMES` are const-evaluated from each type's own `ALL` through its own `name()` / `as_wire()`, and `ALL`'s length is the `VariantCensus` arm count -- so a new variant is a BUILD failure rather than a vocabulary quietly one short on the wire. That projection is what makes a literal domain defensible at all, and the `ArgDomain` doc now draws the line the old text did not have to: a bound derived from the MODEL is live and must never be a literal, while a verb vocabulary is a fact about the CODE and moves in the same commit as the schema. A hand-written `OneOf` would be exactly the disconnected census R1630 exists to end. ARRANGEPASS IS THE CRATE LIFT THIS FORCED. R1639.decision_summary: a widget publishes the events it accepts, so a client never has to guess one. R1638 gave an action an argument grammar and applied it where the grammar belonged to a crate. It could not describe the COMMONEST action in the tree: eleven widgets spell `send` as one statechart event name, and the set of legal names is per widget and existed only as a runtime `Vec` -- reachable when a refusal was being worded, and nowhere a schema could point at. So the vocabulary was discoverable ONLY BY GETTING IT WRONG. R1564 made that refusal name the accepted set, which is a good refusal and a poor contract: it asks an agent to make a call it expects to fail before it can make one it expects to succeed. A TRAIT METHOD CANNOT BE CONST ON STABLE, and that is why this needed the derive rather than a helper function. An argument's declared domain is a `&'static [&'static str]` evaluated at compile time; `as_name` is a trait method. So `#[derive(WidgetEventName)]` now emits the arms TWICE -- once as the trait's `as_name`, once as an inherent `const fn wire_name` -- which is duplication a generator performs and an author never sees, and folds `DRIVABLE_NAMES` out of `EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS`, the const the statechart codegen already emits and `from_name` already gates on. The set a client reads, the set a refusal advertises, and the set the parser admits are now ONE LIST BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by care. INTERNAL EVENTS STAY UNFORGEABLE, and that is precisely what makes publishing the set safe. The projection is over the DRIVABLE const rather than the variant list, so a chart-raised `ButtonActivate` is absent from the published vocabulary and refused on the wire. A reader who assumed every event of the machine was callable would have been wrong, and both halves are asserted -- in the crate and again over RPC. THE SIX DUAL-GRAMMAR SURFACES WERE DECIDED RATHER THAN LEFT ALONE. `datepicker`, `disclosure_group`, `listbox`, `radio_group`, `table` and `text_field` decode a composite payload AND fall back to a bare event name, so they accept either, and `ArgForm` has no union arm. It deliberately gains none here: a declaration states what a client SHOULD send, and a shorthand a surface also happens to accept is a convenience rather than a contract -- so the composite form is declared, because that is the one that stays true if the shorthand is ever retired. It is the same call `pinion_audio::play` made for its bare-string form, and the union question is left where it belongs, in the debt that owns the collision. A CONSTRUCTOR COULD NOT BE WRITTEN, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED RATHER THAN REDISCOVERED. `SchemaField::send_event(returns, names)` was drafted and removed: a `const fn` cannot build the `&'static [SchemaArg]` a field needs out of its own parameter, because a function argument is not subject to rvalue static promotion. The helper therefore sits at the ARGUMENT level (`SchemaArg::event`) and each call site writes the one-element slice inside a `const` block, which is where the promotion is legal. That reasoning is in the doc so the next round does not re-derive it and reach the same dead end. A CATALOG WALK NOW REFUSES A SILENT `send` -- and refuses an EMPTY vocabulary too, which is the shape a widget whose chart drives nothing externally would publish. It found the two dual-grammar surfaces inside the catalog on its first run, which is how those six came to be decided in this round rather than deferred with the rest of the collision.

R1640.decision_summary: the catalog walk is every widget surface, and its escape hatch is not free. R1637 built a walk that compares a surface's declaration against what it dispatches, R1638 and R1639 added two more checks to it, and all three ran against the nineteen widget externals whose constructors happen to take no arguments -- out of thirty-nine. THE DENOMINATOR WAS STATED NOWHERE, which is exactly what made the gap invisible: the walk built what was easy to build, passed, and read as coverage. Among the twenty nobody had ever checked were `TableExternal`, `ListBoxExternal`, `RadioGroupExternal` and `ToolbarExternal` -- four large surfaces that carry the composite send wire. Widening the catalog to all thirty-nine found a real mis-declared channel in the first run: `ColumnResizeExternal`'s `send` was declared a READ slot and has always been dispatched through `split_send_payload`. That is the same hit rate this walk had on its very first run, when it found three in dock. THE ORACLE HAD A HOLE, AND A NEGATIVE CONTROL IS WHAT CLOSED IT. The channel check asked whether a surface's `invoke` answers a declared read with anything other than `UnknownPath` -- and a surface that declines EVERY name with one stated sentence answers that way for names it has never heard of. `ButtonStateSnapshot` and `ToggleStateSnapshot` refuse uniformly ("this surface is a read-only copy; drive the live button external instead"), and three of their declared reads came back as mis-declared channels on the first widened run. The walk now probes an invented name FIRST and compares shapes: a surface that answers a name it does not know the same way it answers a declared one is telling us nothing about either. Three false positives out, one true positive left. A FUZZY COMPARISON INSIDE A COMPLETENESS GATE IS ITS OWN FAILURE MODE. The first draft matched a snake_case catalog label against the type name by lowercasing and dropping underscores, and four entries that WERE in the catalog came back unaccounted (`row_dissect` against `RowDissectionExternal`). The catalog's labels are now the type names themselves and the comparison is an exact set difference -- a completeness gate that reports its own spelling as a gap is worse than no gate, because the noise trains a reader to widen the matcher rather than to look. AND THE ESCAPE HATCH IS NOT FREE, which a counterfactual had to teach: adding a reason-less exclusion PASSED against the first draft, making the gate's own opt-out the cheapest way through it. An exclusion must now carry a reason of real length AND name a type that is actually present in the source, so a stale exclusion cannot quietly shrink the denominator either. THE SOURCE SCAN FOLLOWS R1605 RATHER THAN COUNTING. Rust cannot enumerate a trait's impls at runtime, so the denominator has to come from the text -- and this session has burned three times on text censuses that read a doc comment, a tuple pattern, and only the first match of a body. So the scan does not produce a number: it collects names, and every name must be in the catalog or in the stated exclusions. A mis-parse therefore surfaces as an unaccounted NAME that a reader can act on, rather than as a total that happens to agree.

R1641.decision_summary: a number and its unit sit on one line. A field report from a repo that git-rev-pins pinion ported a production design system to an all-Korean product UI and reported three gaps; two of them were mis-scoped here before the reference was read, and the correction is the round. LETTER SPACING was filed as a precision bug -- four of its five tracking values (-1.5 / -0.5 / -0.3 / +1.5 px) were unrepresentable in a whole-px i32 -- and the obvious repair, f32, is wrong: TextStyle derives Eq + Hash and that participates in the 5.16 paint-fragment cache key. But precision was only the symptom. The reference font carries SpacingType { PercentageSpacing, AbsoluteSpacing }, so spacing specifiable RELATIVE TO THE FONT is the existence floor, and the field is now LetterSpacing { Normal, PxX100, EmX1000 } -- the same either-or shape LineHeight already had one type above it. BASELINE ALIGNMENT looks like a missing enum arm and is not: taffy types its measure callback with no channel for a baseline, so a measured leaf's synthesized baseline IS its bottom edge and mapping to TaffyAlign::Baseline would have published a variant identical to End. Measured, not read -- the naive mapping leaves the pair 10px apart at exactly End's offset. The shift is computed BEFORE layout and injected as taffy margin, so the row's height is the layout engine's answer about the shifted children. WHITESPACE was one symptom with two causes: the trailing half reproduces (the intrinsic measure is parley's width(), which excludes trailing whitespace) and the leading half does not. A fix aimed at full_width() would have closed one of two things filed as one.

R1641.publishable_decision_summary: a number and its unit sit on one line. A field report from a repo that git-rev-pins pinion ported a production design system to an all-Korean product UI and reported three gaps; two of them were mis-scoped here before the reference was read, and the correction is the round. LETTER SPACING was filed as a precision bug -- four of its five tracking values (-1.5 / -0.5 / -0.3 / +1.5 px) were unrepresentable in a whole-px i32 -- and the obvious repair, f32, is wrong: TextStyle derives Eq + Hash and that participates in the 5.16 paint-fragment cache key. But precision was only the symptom. The reference font carries SpacingType { PercentageSpacing, AbsoluteSpacing }, so spacing specifiable RELATIVE TO THE FONT is the existence floor, and the field is now LetterSpacing { Normal, PxX100, EmX1000 } -- the same either-or shape LineHeight already had one type above it. BASELINE ALIGNMENT looks like a missing enum arm and is not: taffy types its measure callback with no channel for a baseline, so a measured leaf's synthesized baseline IS its bottom edge and mapping to TaffyAlign::Baseline would have published a variant identical to End. Measured, not read -- the naive mapping leaves the pair 10px apart at exactly End's offset. The shift is computed BEFORE layout and injected as taffy margin, so the row's height is the layout engine's answer about the shifted children. WHITESPACE was one symptom with two causes: the trailing half reproduces (the intrinsic measure is parley's width(), which excludes trailing whitespace) and the leading half does not. A fix aimed at full_width() would have closed one of two things filed as one.

R1641.1.decision_summary: R1641's own entry carries another project's names, and this is the correction the ledger admits. The reference-name ratchet excludes docs/.atomic/ with a stated reason -- the ledger is frozen by construction, so occurrences already in it are unreachable -- and that exclusion ends with the sentence NEW ENTRIES ARE THE ROUND'S OWN RESPONSIBILITY. R1641 wrote header paths and a product name into its verification bullets anyway, and found out only when the ratchet failed on the source files, which it does gate. The ledger is append-only, so the remedy is an append rather than an amend: the capability statements R1641 should have written are restated here, and the fact that its entry does not is recorded rather than left for a later reader to notice. WHAT THE REFERENCE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, in capability terms: its alignment set carries baseline as a first-class flag, so baseline alignment is an existence floor rather than a preference; its font takes a spacing MODE beside the spacing value -- a percentage of each glyph's own natural advance, or an absolute length -- so font-relative tracking is likewise a floor; its font also has word spacing, which pinion has none of; and its text line publishes BOTH the width excluding trailing whitespace and the advance including it, where pinion picks one internally and reports neither. Those four statements are the evidence R1641's decisions rest on, and none of them needs a name to be checkable.

R1641.5.decision_summary: the five debts R1641 registered, paid. WORD SPACING: TextStyle::word_spacing exists and reaches the shaper. The design question the debt file left open was reuse-or-duplicate; the answer is a SHARED type -- LetterSpacing renamed TextSpacing, both fields carrying it, the FIELD naming which gap and the type naming only the policy, so one resolve stays the one place "what an em means here" is decided. ADVANCE-RELATIVE TRACKING: closed as a DECISION, after correcting the debt file's own diagnosis -- it said the shaper could not express it, and it can (per-range spacing plus readable per-cluster advances, so shape twice and it is exact). Declined rather than blocked, for reasons now in the type doc: the floor is that spacing be specifiable relative to the FONT and the em form is that; no design medium expresses the advance-proportional form; and the cost is two shaping passes plus a style range per cluster, living outside the type the cache key is built from. THE EXCLUDED ADVANCE IS READABLE: TextNode::advance_px and LayoutNode.advance_px carry the width INCLUDING trailing whitespace where the rect excludes it, published as two widths rather than a delta so a client need not reason about a sign. BASELINE SYNTHESIS: a child with no baseline of its own now gets one at its bottom MARGIN edge, narrowing the no-op case to a row with fewer than two children. The two-pass shape was predicted; what was not is WHAT forces the second pass -- a text baseline is a function of font metrics and is knowable before layout, only a synthesized one is not -- so an all-text row still settles in one layout. Paying it broke one of R1641's own tests, which is the right way for a documented boundary to move. THE SHARED VOLUME: the push gate reports the build-cache volume's free space and TIGHTENS this project's budget under pressure, which is the case that actually happened mid-round: nothing was wrong per project and the build died because the shared image was full.

R1641.6.decision_summary: the red on main, paid off as its own round. The push gate refused to publish onto a base whose last completed CI run had failed, which is the stop-the-line rule doing exactly what R1495 built it for -- and the run it named was R1640's, red on one test in one example. THE FAILURE IS DETERMINISTIC AND REPRODUCED LOCALLY ON THE FIRST TRY, so it is not a flake and was not treated as one: `hello-answer-origin::r1482_every_declared_slot_answers` panicked on `model/bump`. THE TEST'S ORACLE WAS THE THING THAT WENT STALE, not the surface. Before R1637 a schema field was a read path and nothing else, so "declared" and "queryable" were one word and the test walked every field through `query`. R1637 split the five names that carried BOTH channels at one address -- bump, boost, restamp, dense, focus_region -- into a tally that is read and a verb that is called, and `SchemaChannel::Invoke`'s own doc states the consequence in one sentence: "probing it with `query` is expected to answer nothing". So the surface became correct and the assertion became wrong, which is the direction that reads as a regression and is not one. BOTH HALVES ARE NOW ASSERTED, not just the half that broke: a Read field must answer, and an Invoke field must NOT -- because an action that is still readable means the address is carrying two channels and the split did not actually happen. The walk also refuses an unhandled channel rather than skipping it, since `SchemaChannel` is non_exhaustive and a silently skipped arm is how a walk stops covering its population (R1640's lesson, one round old). Non-vacuity is asserted per surface: each of the three declares at least one read AND at least one action, so a surface that lost its actions cannot make this pass by having nothing to check. THE BLAST RADIUS WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: two other sites walk `schema().fields` into `query`, and both were already channel-aware -- `virtual_select` matches on `field.channel` and `dock` only tests membership -- which is why CI reported exactly one failure and why fixing one instance here is not leaving siblings behind.

R1641.7.decision_summary: declared tracking is not the self-hosted arm's to paint. Found by an audit rather than a test, and the reason it was invisible is the finding: `self_hosted_text_eligible` is an SSOT that DECLINES any leaf whose declared style the arm cannot reproduce -- a background declines (R1546), a text-indent declines (R1551), each with a clause and a comment saying that serving it would paint something the scene does not declare. Letter spacing had no clause from R47.5, and word spacing arrived at R1641.3 with the same hole, so a leaf declaring tracking was measured and painted at the font's NATURAL advances while the scene said otherwise. IT HID BECAUSE BOTH ARMS IGNORE THE SAME FIELD: the measure reports a box at the natural advances and the paint draws at the natural advances, so they register exactly with each other -- the "measure and paint cannot drift" contract this module is built around was satisfied the whole time, and the text was still wrong. Two arms consistent with one another is not the same as either being right, and only a third reference (the scene's own declaration) can tell them apart. THE TEST CAUGHT ITS AUTHOR on the first run: the clause was drafted as `matches!(spacing, Normal)` while the comment beside it argued that an explicitly-zero tracking should stay eligible because it renders identically, and the assertion written from the comment failed against the code. The comment's argument was the right one, so the clause now keys on the RESOLVED amount -- `PxX100(0)` and `EmX1000(0)` are callers who asked for no tracking and get exactly that. THE BLAST RADIUS OF THE CLASS WAS CHECKED, not assumed: the TUI ignores tracking too and cannot do otherwise (a cell grid has no sub-cell advance), but unlike this arm it has nowhere to decline TO, so it is registered as its own question -- what a backend does with a declaration it cannot honour -- rather than folded in here.

R1642.decision_summary: a conditional argument declares its cases. R1638 declared arrange's third segment as one slot -- string, domain open, optional -- which is the only sentence a flat positional argument list can produce about a segment that is a closed edge vocabulary after align, an integer after stack, and ABSENT after distribute and straighten. THE DECLARATION WAS NOT SILENT, IT WAS WRONG: measured over the wire before the fix, it admits nine calls, the dispatcher refuses three of them (align:horizontal with the segment elided, align:horizontal:17, stack:horizontal:start) and ACCEPTS AND SILENTLY IGNORES a fourth (distribute:horizontal:start). Silence would have been honest; that carried a schema's authority while being false, the wrong-have direction Round 1602 records as the expensive one. item was the case a flat list cannot fix at any price -- add:in:1, remove:in:0 and move:in:2:0 are three different ARITIES -- and it published no args at all. THE CASE TABLE HANGS OFF THE DISCRIMINANT, for Round 1593's reason restated: which values may I pass and what does that value then require are ONE fact, and a declaration that splits them lets them drift, exactly as link legality and link conversion became one declaration so that may-I-draw-this and what-arrives-if-I-do could not disagree. PAST THE REFERENCE, AND THE REFERENCE PROVES ITS OWN CEILING: a meta-method's parameter list is generated from one C++ signature, so a conditional argument there has to become SEPARATE METHODS, which is what the toolkit does and what Round 1631 folded into parameters; its one concession is the Cloned attribute, the synthetic shorter overloads a default argument generates, which enumerates arities and cannot say two of them belong to different values of one parameter. A client there discovers seven unrelated verb names; here it discovers two verbs and seven cases, which is the same information plus the fact that they are two operations. THE TABLE IS PROJECTED AND THE PROJECTION IS GATED AT COMPILE TIME: ArrangePass::tail and the new ItemEdit::tail answer what a verb reads after its shared segments, each tail answers required, the case arrays are const loops over ALL, and because pinion-node-graph is pure data and must not depend on the framework to name a SchemaArg, the argument's name and vocabulary are spelled at the declaration while a const assertion (ArgCase::adds) holds the pair to the model's facts -- swapping which tail may be elided is now error E0080 by name rather than a schema that lies. THE RULE IS ONE DEFINITION WITH THREE CALLERS: SchemaField::conditional_defect refuses two discriminants, an optional discriminant, a shadowed argument name, an expansion that puts an optional before a required, and a nested case table, the last forbidden not because the append rule breaks down but because an unexercised wire shape is a claim no client has been held to. THE GATE STATES ITS DENOMINATOR: no pinion-core widget declares a case table, so the workspace walk asserts the INHABITANT COUNT IS ZERO rather than reporting no defects over an empty population, which is Round 1640's finding applied to the gate written the round after it. R1642.1.decision_summary: the census R1642 demanded, run, and the two false names it found. R1642 registered a debt saying an argument's DOMAIN still cannot depend on a sibling argument, and wrote that the census had not been run. The standing rule is that an un-run census is not a legal carry, so it was run in the same session, over the wire: the three surfaces that declare arguments publish 36 of them, 19 are open, and SIBLING DEPENDENCE IS EXACTLY ONE SITE -- item's index and its per-case peer to. That number is the finding, and it argues AGAINST the branch the debt file listed first: parameterising a domain path would make the schema a small grammar for a single consumer, so the measurement supplies the reason to wait for a second one rather than a preference. What the census DID find is a defect one crate over, and it is the same failure R1642 had just removed from arrange: set_attenuation declared two names the surface does not read. model was published and never read, because there is exactly one distance model and Attenuation has no field for it; reference was the wrong spelling of reference_distance, so a client that followed the declaration had its value silently dropped and the mirror's kept. Accepted and silently ignored, on the one surface an agent is told to trust. The gate is a negative control the declaration never had: every declared name is driven and the READ must move, so a name that reaches nothing cannot survive here, and it fails before the fix by naming both wrong spellings.

R1643.decision_summary: the declaration gate reaches every surface, and the six-round-old red it left is paid. CI had failed on every push since R1640, the sweep named nine demos, and all nine reproduce locally and deterministically, so none is a flake. Every one is R1637's declaration gate firing on a surface no local gate can see, in three kinds. ClickRouter::click was declared with SchemaField::new -- a READ -- from R683.C, while invoke is the only thing that answers it and query returns None, so the declaration was wrong in BOTH directions at once; three demos refused with PathIsAReadSlot. hello-node-flow declared twenty-one reads and ZERO actions while its dispatcher takes ten verbs, the pinion-audio shape R1637 found, in an example R1637's source census could not reach because the binding landed at R1599/R1600 and that census was a hand classification of invoke-body string literals; two demos refused with UnknownInvokePath. Four demos over hello-answer-origin walk every declared slot through query, which R1637 made false for an action. THE FOURTH KIND IS THE SHARPEST AND IT IS ABOUT ABSTRACTION, NOT COVERAGE: that walker exists FIVE times, and R1641.6 repaired the fifth copy -- a Rust unit test -- while its own blast-radius note read the two sibling UNIT walks and not these four. The shared definition was not missing either: assert_declared_channels_are_true has been in the harness since R1566, seventy-seven rounds, used by exactly one demo. So the duplication was not for want of an abstraction but for want of a POINTER to one, and what this round adds is the small piece those four walks each need -- a declared_read_paths filter -- rather than a whole-surface assertion they would have to be rewritten around. WIDENING PARTIALLY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASS: the first wiring routed two of the three channel checks at both catalogs and the third still iterated one, and the third was precisely the check whose oracle catches ClickRouter. The counterfactual meant to prove the widening PASSED instead, which is the finding. THE WIDENED WALK THEN FOUND A REAL MIS-DECLARATION ON ITS FIRST RUN: SplitterExternal's send is also declared READ and also dispatched by invoke, the same hit rate the walk had on dock (three on its first run) and on the thirty-nine-widget widening (one). Repaying it published PointerWireEvent's ALL and WIRE_NAMES, projected from the enum, because that surface accepts exactly the five names its parser admits and had no way to say so -- and a fourth hand-written copy of the arm list, in the test that checks the round trip, went with it. AND THE RATCHET ITSELF HAS A HOLE: variant_census(all) holds ALL's LENGTH to the arm count and cannot see an arm written TWICE. Replacing one arm with a duplicate of another keeps the length right, publishes one name twice, loses the other entirely, and left the whole suite green -- including the round-trip test written this round, because walking ALL and asking that each published name parses back to its own arm is satisfied by the duplicate. R1630 had recorded the argument that closes it (total plus surjective plus equal cardinality implies injective) and the test had only the third term; a distinct-set check supplies the second. Registered as a general debt, because every ALL in this tree has the same hole and this round closed one.

R1644.decision_summary: a run can be stopped, stepped and watched. R1599 gave the graph an execution order and R1600 gave it registers and a clock, and both answer in one gulp: a run derives a whole order, a tick moves every register at one instant, and NEITHER CAN BE INTERRUPTED. So the two questions a person actually asks of a graph that misbehaves -- stop before this node, and what is this port holding -- had no mechanism at all, and nothing observed run or tick from outside. THE DESIGN IS ONE SENTENCE: A BREAKPOINT CANNOT CHANGE THE RUN. The debugger suspends nothing; it computes the whole run once, WITHOUT REFERENCE TO ANY BREAKPOINT, and then moves about inside it, so the property is structural rather than promised. It is bought by R1600's decision that state is a delay and nothing else, which makes a run a pure function of the document and the registers -- and nothing weaker would do, because a debugger that halts a running machine observes a DIFFERENT execution from the one the program has without it, and reverse stepping then has to replay recorded frames. That is exactly why the reference's tree debugger has CurrentValues and SavedValues as two commands over two data sources; here they are one object, and the proof asserts it: the readings are identical at two positions while the trace prefix is not. FIVE STEPPING COMMANDS ARE TWO WORDS. Direction times Stride is six, and STRIDES is that product computed at compile time -- the array's length is the product rather than a literal and the fill is positional, so an arm added to either vocabulary and forgotten leaves a cell unfilled, which is a const panic. The sixth cell, stepping back OUT, is not a feature added on top but the one the reference's naming left unwritten. This is R1643's hole closed by construction rather than by a length check. OUT IS THE ONE STRIDE THAT DOES NOT INVERT, and that is the operation rather than a defect: leaving a frame is precisely forgetting which frame you were in, and at the outermost one there is none to return into. Asserted over every position and every stride, with into an exact bijection, over inverting whenever it stayed inside its frame, and all three bracketing -- so the non-inversion is recorded by name and a later round will not read it as a bug. AN OCCURRENCE IS PART OF THE ADDRESS. A node site and a port site each carry Any or one named instance, so stop the second time through this subgraph is a thing to say; the reference cannot express it at all, because it expands a macro into a copy per use before anything runs. A MARK THAT COULD NEVER FIRE IS REFUSED, and the check hangs off the document for the reason forcing a register does (R1601.1): only the document knows the node is there, that a run can reach it (a node with no control port is PULLED, never run), that a group instance takes no turn of its own, and that a port carries a value rather than control. A silently inert mark reads as a mark that never fired. AND A MARK THAT OUTLIVES WHAT IT MARKED IS NAMED, NOT DROPPED, with the reason on the same channel -- a document is editable while it is being debugged, and a debugger that silently forgets the place a person marked is worse than one that says the mark no longer holds. The reference asks that question one breakpoint at a time and answers bool. A READING IS PER OCCURRENCE RATHER THAN PER STEP, and that is a consequence rather than a simplification: a port's value is a pure function of the document and the registers, so within one run it cannot differ between two moments, and what it does differ between is instances -- which is the axis whose absence forces the reference's watch surface to depend on a currently selected debug object. Each reading reports whether that occurrence RAN, because a value off the trace (a pure node, pulled) and a value the run never reached look alike and are not.
changes_bullets: Add `pinion-node-graph::debug` — the mechanism for stopping a run, stepping it, and reading what it holds. `Breakpoints` (armed sites plus an enabled flag), `Watches`, `Session` (position + marks + watches, serializable together), `Timeline`, `Paused`, `Landing`, and the address types `NodeSite` / `PortSite` / `Occurrence`.

The design decision: A BREAKPOINT CANNOT CHANGE THE RUN. `Document::timeline` computes the whole run through `run_on` with no reference to any breakpoint, and every debugger command is arithmetic over that timeline. The property is structural rather than promised, and it is bought by R1600's "state is a delay and nothing else", which makes a run a pure function of the document and the registers.

`Command::STRIDES` is `Direction::ALL` x `Stride::ALL` computed at compile time: the array's length is the product rather than a literal and the fill is positional, so an arm added to either vocabulary and forgotten leaves an unfilled cell, which is a const panic. The reference names five stepping commands; the sixth cell — stepping back OUT — is the one its naming left unwritten.

Both address types carry an `Occurrence` (`Any` or `At(Instance)`), so a mark can be narrowed to one instance of a shared definition. Both are checked at the document rather than trusted, for the reason `Document::force` is (R1601.1): only the document knows the node exists, that a run can reach it (a node with no control port is pulled, never run) and that a port carries a value.

`Document::stale_breakpoints` / `stale_watches` report every mark the document no longer supports AND WHY, rather than dropping it; `Document::occurrences` enumerates every instance chain landing in a tree.
Publish `Document::tree_of` (a `Step`'s instance+node pair is not an address until it resolves) and add `Instance::from_wire`, the inverse of the `Display` a trace row already prints.

Add a const gate in `model.rs` asserting no `Side` wire name is a prefix of another's — the property `PortSite::from_wire` depends on, checked where the vocabulary lives rather than inside each parse.

R1644.1.decision_summary: the write channel is probed, and the probe overturned the round's own debt note. R1644 registered a debt saying every surface hand-writes its read paths a second time as an `intervene` match arm and nothing checks that list, so a read declared in $schema and missing from the arm would answer "no such path". A COUNTERFACTUAL SAID OTHERWISE, TWICE. Removing a path from `hello-node-flow`'s arm is not observable, because `intervene.rs` derives `ReadOnly` for any declared SCALAR the impl declines; and breaking that derivation is not observable either, because the arm answers first. The refusal has TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES AND EITHER ALONE SUFFICES, which is a defensible design and an unguarded one, and the debt was withdrawn and re-registered as what it actually is. THE ASSERTION THAT GUESS WOULD HAVE PRODUCED WAS THEREFORE NOT WRITTEN: for a scalar it is structurally unfailable, and an assertion that cannot fail reads as coverage -- R1628's lesson, applied to a check this round was two lines from shipping. What ships is the reachable part: the value is not taken, and the negative control. BOTH OF THOSE FIRED FOR REAL. The first draft read the field type as `ty`, the name on the Rust struct, where the WIRE spells it `type` -- so every probe fell through to an integer and `hello-data-grid`'s writable `focused_row` TOOK it, which is the gate mutating what it inspects. That is the same failure class as reading a census by one spelling of a field name, committed here against our own wire. And the first run of the probe reported `hello-text-field`'s `mode` as answering a type refusal rather than ReadOnly, which is not a defect but the standing debt showing through: a declared read is not necessarily read-ONLY and SchemaChannel has no word for writable, so the check is written to what the declaration can express. THE GATE SCOPING WAS AGAIN PART OF THE COUNTERFACTUAL, as R1643 recorded: three properties, three gates. The denominator case is caught by this round's own demo, the ill-typed-write case only by a demo that walks a surface with a writable slot, and the negative control only by a surface edited to refuse everything by habit -- a case authored against the demo's own binding rather than by disabling the assertion, because disabling a control on a correct surface changes nothing and PASSES.
changes_bullets: `assert_declared_channels_are_true` probes the WRITE channel of every declared read, which its own docstring had deferred with a reason that covers `invoke` and does not cover `intervene`: writing to a declared read is refused by definition and changes nothing, so the stated danger — a gate that changes what it inspects — does not apply to it. One sentence bundling two directions deferred the safe one along with the unsafe one.

The probe sends a value of the WRONG declared type, so a writable slot refuses on the type and a read-only one on the channel and neither takes it, plus a negative control (an invented path must be refused as unknown) for R1640's reason: a surface that refuses everything by habit satisfies any refusal check.

`hello-node-flow`'s demo now runs the channel walk over its own surface and asserts the counts, so R1644's ten new reads and fourteen new actions are held to their declarations rather than merely declared.

`UNKNOWN_INTERVENE_PATH` names the two spellings a missing write path answers by (`UnknownIntervenePath` from the framework's dispatch, `UnknownPath` from an `External`), instead of matching them at each site.
verification_bullets: 5 counterfactuals, 3 CAUGHT and 2 PASSED — and both PASSED cases are the finding above, not an omission: they are what proved the read-only refusal has two independent sources, so no single-point break in it is observable and the assertion the debt note called for cannot be written.

CF-C (the walk visits only the easy half) caught by this round's demo; CF-D (the field-type key read from the Rust struct rather than the wire, so the probe is taken) caught by r1566's demo, which walks a surface with a writable int slot; CF-E (a surface refusing every name by habit) caught by this round's demo after being authored against the binding rather than against the assertion.

R1644.2.decision_summary: the fourth cell, and the row the push gate refused. Two channels and two directions is a 2x2, and the walk R1644.1 widened checked THREE of its cells: a read answers a query, an invoke path refuses one as PathIsAnAction, and a read does not take an ill-typed write. Writing to a declared ACTION was the cell nobody asked, and it is as cheap and as safe as the others -- measured before turning it on: all four of hello-node-flow's probed actions refuse before dispatch and the session's position is unmoved afterwards, so nothing fires. A counterfactual confirms it discriminates: telling a client that an action is a read-only slot is caught. AND THE PUSH GATE FOUND A DEFECT THIS SESSION HAD COMMITTED. `docs/phase-b-rounds.tsv` keys by INTEGER round on purpose -- its own tool says a round occasionally lands as R1481 and R1481.1 and is one round either way -- so the `1644.1` row R1644.1 appended is malformed, and `phase_b_tally.py --selftest` raised on it inside `tools/test_hooks.sh`, which `pre-push` runs before trusting its own libraries. The row is folded into R1644's, whose note is free text, so nothing is lost. What IS lost is the axis: R1644 advanced `dcc` and R1644.1 advanced `api`, and a sub-round has nowhere to say that -- which is the R1526 blindness this ledger exists to remove, reappearing one level down. Registered rather than fixed here, because the fix is a change to how the ledger keys and that is the tally's model, not this round's.

R1645.decision_summary: a drawing says how sure it is. The analyzer spec's graph plane is explicit that its canvas has TWO layers -- solid for what a user drew, dotted for what a source reported -- and that the DIFFERENCE between them is the feature's core product. R1575 built that and could not use this crate for it: there was nowhere in the model to put a reported link, so the binding kept two Vec of name pairs of its own, 801 lines, and an application wanting the capability had to copy the example, which is a fork. AN OBSERVATION IS NOT IN THE GRAPH -- IT IS A REPORT ABOUT ONE. So it lives beside a tree's links rather than in them, and no derivation in this crate walks it. That is structural rather than disciplined, and it is the same placement R1644 chose for breakpoints: a layer TAG on Link would have put reported edges inside the structure every derivation reads, where only care keeps them out. Asserted both ways -- adding four reports leaves evaluate, validate, cycle_nodes, the link count and the data path identical, and on the wire a completely different set of reports leaves the drawn links byte-identical. OBSERVATION IS ADMITTED WHERE AUTHORING IS REFUSED, and that asymmetry is the design. connect refuses a wire that closes a value cycle, over-subscribes an input or crosses incompatible types; THE WORLD IS UNDER NO SUCH OBLIGATION, and a tool that declined to record what it saw because its model forbids it would be a tool lying about the capture. So observe checks only that the report is about this graph -- both sockets resolve, and they point the way the report says traffic went -- and a report written backwards is a DIFFERENT refusal from a port that is not there, because which way traffic went is the content of the report. Where the asymmetry shows up is adopt, which runs the authoring rules and NAMES the refusal: "this exists out there and your drawing cannot express it" is a finding, and the binding's old assignment of one set to the other could not produce it, because nothing in a set of name pairs knows what a cycle is. A DRAWING KNOWN TO BE INCOMPLETE SAYS SO. The spec records a lab's hard-won lesson -- a static rule said a path was blocked and the real system disagreed, because links had appeared that nobody drew -- so reachability answers carry a Standing, and it is Partial when auto-discovery is on OR WHEN ANYTHING HAS DRIFTED. The second is the stronger condition and it is DERIVED rather than switched: one reported link nobody drew is proof the drawing is not the whole topology, whatever the switch says. And because both graphs are in the model the answer is about both, so the disagreement -- drawn says no, observed says yes -- is one read rather than an inference. Judgement::certain() returns the answer ONLY when the standing is certain, which is the shape that makes the distinction hard to ignore: a caller who wants a bare bool must say what it should mean when the drawing is known to be partial.
changes_bullets: Add `pinion-node-graph::observed` — `Observation`, `LinkLayer`, `Layers`, `Discovery`, `Standing`, `Judgement`, `Reachability`, `ObserveError`, `AdoptError`, and the `Document` verbs `observe` / `unobserve` / `clear_observations` / `observations` / `layers` / `link_layer` / `adopt` / `standing` / `reaches` / `discovery` / `set_discovery`.

The reported links are a `BTreeSet<Observation>` on the `Document`, deliberately NOT in `Tree::links`, reached only through five crate-private accessors in `model.rs`. Both new fields carry serde defaults, so a document written before this round loads.
`LinkLayer` is derived from the two layers on every read and stored nowhere — the derivation `hello-graph-diff` established at R1575, lifted whole.

`hello-graph-diff` now DEPENDS on the crate instead of copying it: its two `Vec<Link>` become one `Document<Named>`, its own `LinkKind` becomes `LinkLayer`, and its `adopt` becomes `Document::adopt` per reported link plus a retraction of what was drawn and never seen — so the authoring rules apply where before there was an assignment.

Its wire gains `standing`, `certain`, `discovery` (the one writable slot, the determinism switch) and `reaches <from>,<to>`, and an `impossible` scenario whose report closes a cycle, which is what makes the refusal reachable at all.

R1646.decision_summary: the analysis-tool axis gets a meter, and it says the framework owes ten of sixty-seven. The user asked whether a lot still does not work, and the honest first answer was that I COULD NOT SAY WITH CONFIDENCE. The node-graph axis has had a meter since R1601 -- a tool, a pin, one verdict per reference operator, a number cargo test re-derives. The analysis-tool axis had a prose table in a session note, and prose drifts: measured twice in this session alone, it called the charting remainder "3D only" while a label-thinning gap sat inside it, and it listed the two-layer link diff as closed when what existed was the PAINT and the model lived in an example that did not depend on the crate at all. Both are exactly the failure the other census exists to prevent, and the capability list itself had asked for the fix in writing -- "split the axes and BUILD A METER and you can answer yes or no per axis with a number; the meter's numbers must sum" -- which nobody had built. FIVE VERDICTS RATHER THAN TWO, because a framework census answering only yes/no lies in both directions: most of a tool like this is neither present nor missing IN THE FRAMEWORK, it is the application's own subject matter over substrate that is present. So `have` / `gap` / `app` / `outside` / and `unmeasured`, which is the point of the whole file: a row nobody has looked at is invisible in a prose summary and is a row here, because the silent error direction is the expensive one (R1602). THE FIRST RUN OWED SIXTEEN, HALF OF THEM ONLY BECAUSE NOBODY HAD CHECKED. Measuring those eight turned five into facts the tree already had -- named layout presets round-trip and the tile grid's own test is named for it, tooltips are a widget that distinguishes hovered from focused from dismissed, the transport carries stopped/playing/paused with a playhead -- and TWO INTO REAL FINDINGS. There is no property grid in any crate: it exists only in two examples, so the node inspector this capability list puts in its must-have tier is an example an application copies, which is the same shape R1645 closed one round earlier. And no keyframe or scrub-editing timeline exists at all, so a scenario that kills a node at a given time has no authoring surface. WHAT THE METER PROVES IS COMPLETENESS AND NOT TRUTH, and it says so in the same breath: four of twenty-four `have` verdicts name a proof and the other twenty are claims, reported on every run rather than left to be assumed. That is the reference census's own asymmetry, arriving on a second axis.
changes_bullets: Add `tools/analyzer_census.py` and `docs/analyzer-census.json` — 67 capability rows across three planes and three tiers, each with a verdict from a closed five-word set, a `have` naming what covers it, and an optional `proven_by` in the reference census's format.

The tool validates completeness only: unique ids, ids agreeing with their plane, known plane / tier / verdict, a `have` that names its cover, an owed verdict that does NOT name a proof, and a tally that sums to the row count. `--selftest` exercises every one of those rules, `--check-pin` is the hook's form.
`.githooks/pre-push` runs both before the reference census, for the same reason that one is gated: the judgement is committed here and the judgement is what rots.

Every capability row is phrased as a property of the tool CLASS — a capture and decode viewer, a node authoring and execution lab, a widget dashboard — at the level the public tools in each family describe themselves. No product, domain, protocol or customer appears, and none may.

R1647.decision_summary: stop-the-line: R1645 changed a persisted shape and did not say so. Adding the reported-link layer and the discovery switch to a Document changed what every saved graph looks like, because hello-node-editor's persisted type IS one -- `type Graph = Document<MaterialOp>` -- and the R1599 shape gate caught it in CI. Reproduced locally and deterministically, so it is not a flake. THE DECISION THE GATE FORCED IS THE INTERESTING PART AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. R1600 drew a line: what the graph IS goes in the file, what it is DOING does not, which is why a Machine's registers live beside the document rather than inside it. A reported link could be argued onto either side of that line -- it is evidence about the world at a moment, which sounds like doing rather than being. It is SAVED, because the entire value of a two-layer view is comparing a drawing against what was seen, and a difference that evaporates when the file closes makes that a live-session-only feature. The residue that buys is stated rather than hidden: an observation carries no time, so a reopened file shows last week's drift exactly as it shows this minute's. Old blobs still LOAD, because both fields carry serde(default), so this is a shape change rather than a compatibility break and the version number is what says which. AND THE GATE'S OWN MESSAGE CANNOT BE FOLLOWED LITERALLY, which cost one round trip: it prints "bump to N and append (N, <digest>)", but that digest was taken over a sample carrying the OLD version number, so bumping changes it. Bump first, read the digest the gate prints on the SECOND run. Written into the comment beside the ledger, because the next person to add a field will hit it too. THE CONSUMER GATE DID NOT FAIL -- IT PREDICTED THIS EXACTLY. R1645's own pre-commit printed "251 package(s) can be affected -- over the local cap of 12, so CI covers them" and then printed the command, hello-node-editor included. The cap is stated design and agrees with the standing rule against local full sweeps. What is worth registering is the RADIUS: 251 is the whole workspace for a change whose crate reports no direct dependents, and the likeliest cause is that R1645 also edited a Cargo.toml -- so the act of making an example USE a crate is what turns off the gate that would catch the consequence, and that is precisely the edit this campaign keeps making. Registered with its diagnosis marked unverified, because a debt note written without a test is a guess.
changes_bullets: `hello-node-editor`: `PERSISTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` 9 -> 10 and the shape ledger gains `(10, 0x9fed_b236_9417_723a)`, which is R1645's consequence declared rather than discovered by a user with an old file.

The comment beside the constant records WHY the reported layer is saved rather than held beside the document like a `Machine`, and what that costs: an observation carries no time, so a reopened file cannot say how old its drift is.
It also records that the gate's instruction cannot be followed literally — the digest it prints is taken before the bump it asks for, so it moves when you bump.

R1648.decision_summary: An `app` verdict is a claim about COMPOSITION, so a composite proves it: the analysis-tool dashboard shell is assembled as one binary, and the card it is made of becomes a framework vocabulary. R1646's meter classifies 26 of 67 capabilities as `app` -- the substrate is here, the domain logic is the application's -- and nobody had ever assembled one, so the largest bin was also the least reviewed. The census gains `assembled_by` beside `proven_by`, the two are mutually exclusive by verdict (a `have` is proven by a test, an `app` by an assembly, and a row carrying the other kind claims evidence its verdict cannot produce), every path an assembly names must exist on disk, and the report says 3 of 23 rather than assuming. THE ASSEMBLY MOVED THREE ROWS THE OTHER WAY: loading/empty/error, no-permission and encrypted-link were `app` on the grounds that a per-widget state machine is a design this axis had not asked for, but the capability list asks for all five in writing and they are ONE mechanism. `pinion_core::widgets::card` is that mechanism: `CardState` is six arms and `Remedy` is what a person can do about each, DERIVED rather than decided per card kind. The pair that justifies six arms rather than one Error is denied/opaque -- both render as "no content" and they are opposite, so a shell with one arm offers "request access" on a link no permission can open; `remedy` returns Option so no-problem, a-remedy, and a-needed-remedy-that-does-not-exist are three answers. Measured on the toolkit at 6.11: NO content-state concept exists on any panel or view class and its item views have no placeholder at all. ONE CARD OFFERS TEAR-OFF AND MAXIMISE, which the toolkit cannot express -- floating lives on its dock widget and maximising on its MDI child, and no class has both. `CardChrome` is a set in one canonical layout order and it is ENFORCED ON THE WIRE: an affordance a card does not offer is refused by name, because hiding a button leaves an agent able to do what the screen says is impossible. `TileGrid::maximize` hands back `Maximized`, which IS the previous arrangement, as a #[must_use] value -- there is no copy on the side for a second maximise to clobber or a preset load to drop. AND THE SHELL IS OPERATED BY HAND: a real press and a scripted one reach ONE set of handlers, controls fire on release over the same target, a cancel drops the latch without performing it, and the painter and the hit test read ONE geometry. The demo sweeps the window in both directions to keep that true, and the second direction -- every painted control must be pressable at the centre of the rectangle it was painted in -- was missing until a counterfactual proved it, whereupon it immediately found that this file painted every card's contents at TWICE their intended offset, because children of an absolutely-positioned container are placed relative to IT.

R1649.decision_summary: The reference tool is the specification for a shell, not a data point -- so where R1648's own design disagreed with it, R1648's design loses. Directive received mid-round: match the reference's UI and its behaviours (dock, undock, widget placement). Read from its screenshots and its layout constants, restated domain-neutral -- twelve columns, a 174px row, a 16px gutter, and its dark and light token sets mapped onto this framework's theme roles, because a tool looked at for hours in a dim room has a palette that is a decision rather than a default. FIVE THINGS CHANGED AND EACH IS A DIFFERENT CLAIM FROM THE ONE R1648 PROVED: a THREE-COLUMN shell -- icon rail, a sub-header carrying the layout preset and the two board verbs, canvas, and a widget PALETTE the board is populated from -- rather than a board with a strip; a card is ADDED rather than seeded, so what is on the board is a decision somebody made and the count in two places has to agree; a drag PREVIEWS where it will land rather than displacing cards live, because the reference commits on release and a board reflowing under the finger makes the preview a lie about where the card goes; LAYOUT-EDIT MODE puts per-card size steppers on the cards, so a board is rearranged with no pointer drag at all; and DETACH REMOVES THE CARD FROM THE BOARD, with re-dock appending at the bottom. That last one REVERSES R1648, which is the part worth recording: R1648 kept the tile in place and argued that a temporary gesture should not reflow a layout. The reference does remove it, so a detach IS a layout edit there, and a round that kept its own argument would have been defending a design decision against the thing the axis is measured by. WHAT THE ROUND ACTUALLY LEARNED IS ABOUT ITS OWN BLIND SPOT. Two real defects shipped and both were found by counterfactuals rather than by the demo: a `TextNode` carries a rect but WITHOUT A LAYOUT STYLE IT IS LAID OUT IN FLOW, so every card painted its title, its code badge and its description stacked down the left edge -- and nothing in a 118-assertion demo noticed, because every assertion read tags, texts, and the rects of tagged CONTAINERS, and a text run carries no tag. R1648's double-offset bug was the same blind spot one level up. The fix is not a bigger demo but a DIFFERENT KIND of assertion: the demo now checks that a card's title sits beside its drag grip and its description past its code badge, which is a placement that flow cannot produce.

Twelve widget kinds as a CATALOGUE with code, label, domain-neutral description, colour and default cell size; three placed. Card ids are `<kind>#<n>` so a kind can be placed twice and its definition is recoverable without a side table. Painted icons rather than font glyphs (a glyph this project does not ship is a box, and a box is not an icon).

carry_forward_bullets: ONE structural difference is NOT closed and is registered rather than hidden: debt-the-analyzer-canvas-does-not-scroll. The canvas is a fixed 802px at ROW_H 174, so about 4.6 rows are visible and a card placed past them is drawn outside the window and cannot be pressed; the demo closes such a card over the wire and says why in a comment rather than quietly avoiding the edge of the window. R1649.1.decision_summary: A capability verified only through a bypass is not verified. R1649 shipped a shell whose every control was DEAD TO A REAL MOUSE, and its 118-assertion demo passed, because the demo drives `invoke("point")` / `invoke("send", ...)` and those call the oracle's handlers DIRECTLY -- they never go through the §5.35 input router. The module's own documentation claimed, in as many words, that a real press and a scripted one reach the same code and that no parallel automation surface exists. That claim was false and nothing could see it. The user found it in about a minute by clicking. THE MECHANISM: `forward_pointer_move` resolves the hit target by hit-testing the paint scene for the deepest TAGGED node under the cursor, then looks up an `External` carrying that tag; the shell tags forty-odd nodes as ADDRESSES (R1613: a tag is an address, not a claim of clickability) and there is exactly ONE `External`, the root, so the lookup failed on every move and the router returned without forwarding anything. The fix is one line in the shared `absolute()` helper -- every tagged child is `pointer_transparent`, the root is not -- and it is verified by driving a REAL pointer: a calibrated `xdotool` click on the capture chip toggles capture, on the palette adds a card. The gate that makes it unshippable again is structural rather than behavioural, because the behavioural one needs a live window: a walk of the view scene asserting that every tagged node except the root is pointer-transparent, and that the root is not. The counterfactual that removes the transparency fails it. WHAT IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN FIXED is the class: no gate anywhere else checks router reachability, nobody has counted how many other surfaces tag without transparency, and the only demos that drive a real pointer are the five x11grab ones, which check pixels rather than reachability.

Before the fix: cursor 0,0 and a click changed nothing. After: `hit` resolves shell.appbar.capture, a real click toggles capture True -> False, a real click on the palette moves placed_count 3 -> 4, a real click on the sub bar reports its toast.
