R1650.decision_summary: a painted surface says what a pointer cannot reach: pinion_runtime::pointer_reach plus scene/pointer_reach plus a boot gate every demo pays, and the gate found a second whole app dead to a real mouse on its first run. Declared `none` -- this round builds an instrument and pays a defect with it; claiming an axis for that would be the hand-adjustment these ledgers exist to stop, and the repair it made lands on hello-tile-dashboard, whose own rounds (R1607-R1609) declared `none` for the same reason. THE ROUND EXISTS BECAUSE TWO FACTS WERE BEING ASSERTED AS ONE. `scene/click`, `invoke` and `send` reach a widget's handler BY NAME; a mouse reaches it BY POSITION through the router, which resolves the deepest tagged node under the cursor and looks that tag's primary half up as an External -- and returns SILENTLY when the lookup fails. So a screen can be completely dead to a hand while every scripted assertion about it passes. Measured twice before anything checked it (R1497 lost 100% of the clicks on two header cells; R1649.1 found a whole shell dead behind 118 passing assertions) and a THIRD time by this gate: hello-tile-dashboard had been dead since R1608, whose changelog says 'the model's claim gets a cursor'. Proven with scene/drag -- UNCHANGED under a router-driven drag, MOVED under invoke. THE REPAIR WAS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE: pointer_transparent takes the whole subtree out of the hit test and the grip ring's eight resize cursors are declared inside it, so the answer is the idiom the tree already had -- a COMPOSITE tag (dashboard#card.loss), plus CaptureNormalize::Primary (without it the cursor arrives as a fraction of the grabbed CARD and every drag lands elsewhere) plus decoding the router's composite send payload (without it the input finally arrived and the board still did nothing). THE VERDICT AND THE CENSUS ARE TWO HALVES AND THE SWEEP TAUGHT WHICH IS WHICH: `shadows` reports every tag intercepting a widget's input, which a tagged container legitimately does in its own gaps, and `unreachable` reports a widget whose own centre NO widget answers. The first draft asked whether the widget answered for ITSELF and flagged four containers immediately -- a row over its tree and a cell over its grid are ordinary nesting. Measured over 148 examples that boot with a GPU surface: 14 had a widget nobody can press. Two were repaired here (a label that had grown over its own badge, a status message region that had grown over its bar) and the other 12 are a BUDGET FILE, the ratchet shape R1611 used for 7,999 reference-name occurrences, because a gate that fails everything on day one is a gate somebody switches off. THE WALK IS THE PRIMITIVE 78 TEST FILES HAD BEEN WRITING THEMSELVES: Scene::for_each_node with child_nodes exhaustive over the node-kind census, so a new kind cannot join the tree while every traversal steps over it, and NodeVisit carries the ancestor chain because a path cannot -- a Scroll is path-transparent, so depth is not the segment count. THE GATE'S FIRST SWEEP FOUND A DEFECT IN THE GATE: raising from __enter__ leaks the subprocess, because `with` only calls __exit__ for an __enter__ that RETURNED, and 14 refusals left 14 binaries holding GPU contexts until the next launch died with 'Not enough memory left' instead of its own verdict -- R1570.3's class, reproduced by the thing written to prevent a different one. AND THE REFERENCE CLAIMS GET A METER: tools/reference_surface.py re-derives what this project asserts about the reference toolkit, with the parsed member count PINNED, because an absence proved by search is worth nothing -- a pattern matching nothing and a parse finding nothing look identical. Three claims, re-derived: the transparency attribute exists (so our declaration matches the floor), and of the base widget class's 280 declared members none answers the aggregate reachability question or says whether a press will be acted on. 12 counterfactuals, 12 caught after THREE were findings -- nothing asserted the shadow names the NEAREST widget, nothing could fail when the composite tags were reverted, and the normalisation choice was invisible to cargo and needed a demo-inclusive gate. Also cleared: the two things the push gate demanded of this round -- the catalog axis re-judged 95 to 96, and the measurement is the point (one of the five named absent widget kinds, a key-sequence editor, landed at R1569, the round BEFORE the judgment that called it missing, so that gap has been four kinds for eighty rounds) and hello-analyzer-shell filed on the axis its artifact belongs to.

R1651.decision_summary: The node inspector becomes a widget with a crate home, and the reference tool's screen A is assembled on it. R1650 gave the settings-form MODEL a home and left it with no painter and no consumer; this round supplies both, which is what moves the analysis-tool census row that had scored `gap` since R1646 for want of anywhere for the per-field applies badge to live. changes_bullets: pinion-core::widgets::config_form gains FieldType (six arms, chosen from what one real inspector needs), derived ConfigForm::defects and ConfigForm::verdict where R1650 took the defect list as an argument, ConfigField::hidden / as_custom / with_shape, and the document pair: ConfigForm::document derives a nested deployable configuration from the rows' own dotted paths, ConfigForm::adopt reads one back and NAMES every path it could not place, and the round-trip law document -> form -> document is identity. A path that is a prefix of another is refused as a collision rather than silently dropped, and a blocking value refuses the whole document rather than half-applying.

pinion-core::theme gains the Warning / OnWarning role pair, argued rather than assumed: this project follows Material 3's role set everywhere else and M3 has an error tier and no warning tier, but ConfigDefect's arms differ in exactly one way -- whether the defect blocks -- and a palette with one alarm tone can only paint half of that vocabulary. R1651.1.decision_summary: R1651's own audit found three controls drawn where a press does not reach them, and all three were invisible to R1651's sweep because that sweep's population was WRITTEN OUT BY HAND. The repair is the three defects and the gate that would have caught them: the sweep now derives its probe list from the painted scene, so a control cannot join the screen unprobed.
changes_bullets: The icon rail painted its seats at their WINDOW rectangles inside a container already placed at the rail's own origin, so every seat drew a pane-height below where the hit test looks and a press on one answered its neighbour. R1648's double-offset defect, in the one pane R1651's sweep did not probe.

An option row's chips were laid out by the painter content-hugging with a gap and by the consumer's hit test as an even division of the control, so the second chip of every option row answered for the first. RowBox::options now PUBLISHES where each option landed and both read it -- which is the one-geometry claim R1651 makes, made true on the row where it was false. The chips are placed relative to their own control, because an absolutely-placed child is positioned against its container and passing the form's origin is the same double offset one level down.

A node card's digest lines held the specification table's values verbatim, so editing an endpoint in the inspector left the card showing the old one -- a second, frozen copy of the configuration, which is what this round argues against. The KEYS stay the specification's (which fields are worth showing at a glance is a design decision) and the VALUES are re-read from the form through one digest_path mapping.

R1652.decision_summary: Every debt R1651 and R1651.1 registered is paid, and three of the four repairs are framework additions rather than fixes to one screen: a reactive cell for a model too big to clone, a control per declared field shape, and the measured floor turned from prose back into a file a test reads. The fourth gives a completeness gate the population it had been silent about.
changes_bullets: pinion_core::reactive::Tracked<T> — a reactive cell whose read BORROWS rather than clones. `Signal<T>` requires Clone + Serialize and clones on every read, which is right for a word and wrong for a document, so a screen whose model is a whole graph put it behind a bare RefCell and lost the reactive edge. `Tracked::borrow` subscribes without cloning; `Tracked::borrow_mut` hands back a guard that NOTIFIES ON DROP, and since that guard is the only route to `&mut T`, a mutation that fails to announce itself has no spelling. Deliberately no equality skip (comparing a T this exists for gives back what the clone-free read bought) and no snapshot participation (the Serialize bound is the one it drops) — both stated in the module rather than discovered later.
examples/hello-node-lab moves onto it: the revision signal and all nine hand-bumps are deleted, and the demo passes unchanged, which is what says the repaint survives without them.

pinion_widget_paint::config_form — RowBox::options generalises to RowBox::parts, every affordance inside a control published as a tag suffix and a rectangle, iterated by the painter AND by a consumer's hit test. A boolean gets a checkbox, an integer gets a stepper pair that clamps by the bounds its FieldType declares, a list gets one row per element plus the row that adds one — split by the same FieldType::elements the encoder uses, so the screen and the document cannot disagree about what a comma means. Text keeps the box, and has zero parts, which is the assertion that says so.

docs/reference-form-floor.json — the reference toolkit's form-layout behaviour at 6.11.1, measured by running a three-row form through it and pinned in NEUTRAL vocabulary (policy words are ours; no member, class or product name; ratchet verified). Two tests read it and gate RELATIONS rather than pixels: wrapping makes the form taller, growth widens a control beside and wrapped, beside-unless-it-does-not-fit wraps nothing in a wide box and something in a narrow one, a hidden row shortens the form without changing the row count, and the two absences (one verdict for `not finished` and `out of range`; no automatic label-to-control relation) are recorded as measurements.

tools/demos/r1651_...py — each family prefix the backward direction accepted wholesale now carries a member count, and lab.link's is DERIVED from the specification rather than a constant because its size is a function of the graph.
verification_bullets: cargo test: pinion-core 3364 (6 new for Tracked, including one that walks all THREE routes to `&mut T` and requires each to notify), pinion-widget-paint 839 (2 new for the per-shape controls, 2 for the pinned floor), hello-node-lab 14. cargo clippy on all three clean under -D pedantic.

THE FLOOR TEST FOUND SOMETHING ON ITS FIRST RUN AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT: the beside-growth assertion failed because a 284px pane leaves less room beside a long key than a control's natural width, so both growth policies return the same number and the fixture could not discriminate — R1633's lesson, and the floor's own fixture is 320px against a 91px key for that reason. Widened to 600px, with the cramped case asserted as a stated no-op rather than left unexamined.

The demo passes with 61 derived probes (was 55; the new affordances joined the sweep with no edit to the probe list, which is the property section H was rebuilt for). Its expectation was tightened rather than loosened when a list's element row legitimately covered its control's centre: what must never happen is an answer naming a DIFFERENT row.

A REAL MOUSE over a mapped window drove the new affordances: the checkbox set discovery.multicast to true, the stepper moved 65535 to 65534, and the list's add row went from [] to ['tcp/0.0.0.0:7400'].
tools/reference_names.py --check: ratchet OK with the new pin in the tree. analyzer census selftest PASS, framework owes 9 of 67. phase_b_tally selftest PASS.
carry_forward_bullets: NO NEW DEBT REGISTERED, and that is a claim this round has to be careful about because the last two rounds each said something like it and an audit found three things. What was checked: the four closed files each record what closed them and what residue remains INSIDE the capability rather than as a new file. Two residues are stated and are not debts: `Tracked` does not participate in `Owner::snapshot` (dropping the Serialize bound IS the feature) and does not equality-skip (comparing the T it exists for would give back the clone-free read), both written into the module header. One residue IS external and named where it lives: the pinned floor goes stale silently if the toolkit changes, because re-measurement needs a build of it and the probe cannot live here — but our derivations now fail against the pin, which is the half we control.

debt-the-property-grid-is-an-example-not-a-crate is narrowed a second time: its type-specific-editor half is closed by this round, and what is left is the category tree and the two examples that still hold their own. The shapes FieldType does not yet declare (colour, curve, vector) are recorded as a question about that VOCABULARY rather than about the property grid, because that is where the answer would go.

tools/demos/r1651_...py — each family prefix the backward direction accepted wholesale now carries a member count, and lab.link's is DERIVED from the specification rather than a constant because its size is a function of the graph.
publishable_verification_bullets: cargo test: pinion-core 3364 (6 new for Tracked, including one that walks all THREE routes to `&mut T` and requires each to notify), pinion-widget-paint 839 (2 new for the per-shape controls, 2 for the pinned floor), hello-node-lab 14. cargo clippy on all three clean under -D pedantic.

THE FLOOR TEST FOUND SOMETHING ON ITS FIRST RUN AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT: the beside-growth assertion failed because a 284px pane leaves less room beside a long key than a control's natural width, so both growth policies return the same number and the fixture could not discriminate — R1633's lesson, and the floor's own fixture is 320px against a 91px key for that reason. Widened to 600px, with the cramped case asserted as a stated no-op rather than left unexamined.

The demo passes with 61 derived probes (was 55; the new affordances joined the sweep with no edit to the probe list, which is the property section H was rebuilt for). Its expectation was tightened rather than loosened when a list's element row legitimately covered its control's centre: what must never happen is an answer naming a DIFFERENT row.

A REAL MOUSE over a mapped window drove the new affordances: the checkbox set discovery.multicast to true, the stepper moved 65535 to 65534, and the list's add row went from [] to ['tcp/0.0.0.0:7400'].
tools/reference_names.py --check: ratchet OK with the new pin in the tree. analyzer census selftest PASS, framework owes 9 of 67. phase_b_tally selftest PASS.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: NO NEW DEBT REGISTERED, and that is a claim this round has to be careful about because the last two rounds each said something like it and an audit found three things. What was checked: the four closed files each record what closed them and what residue remains INSIDE the capability rather than as a new file. Two residues are stated and are not debts: `Tracked` does not participate in `Owner::snapshot` (dropping the Serialize bound IS the feature) and does not equality-skip (comparing the T it exists for would give back the clone-free read), both written into the module header. One residue IS external and named where it lives: the pinned floor goes stale silently if the toolkit changes, because re-measurement needs a build of it and the probe cannot live here — but our derivations now fail against the pin, which is the half we control.

debt-the-property-grid-is-an-example-not-a-crate is narrowed a second time: its type-specific-editor half is closed by this round, and what is left is the category tree and the two examples that still hold their own. The shapes FieldType does not yet declare (colour, curve, vector) are recorded as a question about that VOCABULARY rather than about the property grid, because that is where the answer would go.

R1652.1.decision_summary: R1652's own audit found that a list grown past four elements painted its rows straight over the next field, and that the sweep which should have caught it only ever probed the OPENING screen — the one state a specification describes and the one state nobody works in. Both are repaired, and a counterfactual shows the defect is worse than the audit measured: reverted, eleven controls are unreachable and five whole rows are shadowed.
changes_bullets: A control's height is now a function of its SHAPE (`control_height`) rather than a token. R1652 gave every control `style.control_h`, and a list draws one row per element, so a list of six overflowed its own row and was drawn over the field below it. The list's own placement carries a debug assertion that its rows fit the control that was sized for them, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

The regression test asserts over a RANGE of lengths (1..=8) rather than one fixture, because a defect whose trigger is "enough elements" is invisible to any single length — and it asserts the row height STRICTLY INCREASES with the element count, which is the property that separates the fix from a bigger constant.

tools/demos/r1651_...py runs its derived sweep TWICE: on the opening screen, and again after growing a list to seven elements. Growing a list is the cheapest thing that changes a control's SIZE, and size is exactly what a single-state sweep cannot see. The demo asserts the used screen paints MORE controls than the opening one, so a sweep that silently stopped exercising the second state would fail rather than pass quietly.
verification_bullets: COUNTERFACTUAL, run rather than argued: with `control_height` reverted to the token, the unit test panics on its own debug assertion at one element past the boundary AND the demo fails with 11 of 67 painted controls unreachable — `connect.endpoints`, `control.permissions`, `transport.link.tx.batch_size`, both permission chips, both steppers and both add-chips all answer for a list row instead of themselves. So neither gate is one that cannot fail, and the defect shipped in R1652 was larger than the audit that found it measured.

Restored: cargo test pinion-core 3364, pinion-widget-paint 840, hello-node-lab 14; clippy clean under -D pedantic on both changed crates; the demo passes with 61 controls swept on the opening screen and 67 after the list is grown.

A real mouse over a mapped window drives all six checks including the checkbox, the stepper and the list's add row. Its calibration was also made non-flaky: it probes from the window's OWN geometry rather than a fixed screen point, which is why it had failed on one run in three.
carry_forward_bullets: NO NEW DEBT. What the audit that produced this round would have registered is instead FIXED, which is the standing rule; what remains is one generalisation worth stating rather than filing: a sweep over one state is a sweep over one state, and the states that matter are the ones a person reaches by using the screen. This round covers the cheapest such transition (a control that changes size). The transitions it does NOT cover — a node dragged off-screen, a graph with fifty nodes, a form whose every key has been added — are named here so the next round choosing coverage knows what was chosen and what was not.

R1653.decision_summary:
A painted screen says WHERE it painted every mark, and the first comparison of
this project's reference screen against its own specification -- from the paint
rather than from the geometry helper -- found the screen was not painting them
where it thought. The walk now carries the geometry fold, so an untagged mark
(every text run) can be asked where it is; three private copies of that fold
became one recursion; scene/bbox answers both the node's own rectangle and where
a pointer would land on it; and five real defects in the analysis-tool node lab
were found and repaired, four of them invisible to every gate that existed.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: NodeVisit carries the walk's geometry -- offset, clip and
absolute_rect() folding both -- so every painted node reports where it is,
tagged or not. Two lifetimes on NodeVisit, because a visitor that keeps a leaf
past the callback (for_each_text_leaf's two consumers do) cannot be typed
through one.
pinion-core: try_for_each_node adds the early exit the searches needed.
rect_for_tag_absolute, absolute_rects_by_tag and for_each_text_leaf are now one
descent with three accumulators; two private copies of the scroll fold deleted.
pinion-core: the index and the lookup are unified on "the first node carrying a
tag decides, including when it decides nowhere" -- the rule that makes the early
exit sound. They had disagreed on a clipped duplicate while the doc said
otherwise.
pinion-rpc: scene/bbox answers `window` beside `bbox` -- where the node is
painted, offsets folded and clips applied, null when nothing of it is visible.
Adds a `tag` locator and the two-scene basis scene/snapshot takes.
examples/hello-node-lab: src/painted.rs is the integration test -- view() then
compute_layout(), swept over eight states, holding the screen to forward,
backward, reachable, contained, disjoint and clipped.
examples/hello-node-lab: label() and tagged_label() carry a layout style. Every
run in the screen had been flowing.
examples/hello-node-lab: the canvas is a viewport over a world surface
(ScrollAxis::Both), which is what stops a leftward pan underflowing and what
clips content at the pane edge.
examples/hello-node-lab: pins scale with the canvas; three label boxes bounded
so they end where the next begins; the link label's text is its child.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p pinion-core: 3374 passed.
cargo test -p pinion-rpc: 1201 passed (one gate caught a consequence -- the
published window column for scene/bbox -- and the ordering was corrected).
cargo test -p hello-node-lab: 20 passed.
cargo test -p pinion-a11y -p pinion-runtime -p pinion-shell: green.
cargo clippy on the three changed crates with -D pedantic: clean.
tools/demos/r1651_the_node_lab_matches_the_reference.py: PASS, 15 sections, 61
painted controls on the opening screen and 67 after growing a list.
tools/demos/r1484 and r1585 (the other scene/bbox consumers): PASS.
The real render read back as a PNG through PINION_SCREENSHOT, before and after.
5 counterfactuals, 5 caught -- after one was a finding: deleting the grown-list
state left every assertion green, so the floors moved onto the sweep itself.
Measured against the mature toolkit built from source (probe outside the
repository): its scene item's absolute rect ignores an ancestor clip, a fully
clipped child is indistinguishable from a visible one, its widget's absolute
position ignores the scroll area hiding it, visibility is a second call, a text
run inside a control has no geometry API at all, and there is no single-pass
index.
carry_forward_bullets: A text run cannot be told to elide, so a string wider than its box wraps over
what is below it and the integration test -- which measures boxes, not glyphs --
reports the screen as clean. Visible in the render as a smeared card row. There
is no elide anywhere in the tree; the two comments that use the word describe
behaviour no API provides. Registered as its own note rather than carried
silently, and the module doc states the limit at the place the test would
otherwise be believed.

R1653.1.decision_summary:
R1653's own close audit: the world surface it introduced was a fixed pixel
extent, so the range a node position could take SHRANK as the zoom grew, and a
position outside it saturated silently at paint time -- the card appeared in the
corner of the canvas with nothing saying why. A bound belongs where the position
is SET. The surface is now stated in world units and scales with the zoom, so
the range is zoom-independent, and the drag clamps to it, so a node stops at the
edge of the world where the user can see it stop.
changes_bullets: examples/hello-node-lab: WORLD_ORIGIN and WORLD are world units and signed; the
surface's pixel size is derived from them by the zoom.
examples/hello-node-lab: clamp_to_world bounds a dragged node's position, and
the paint-time saturation is now the second half of a stated rule rather than
the only one.

preserved what a pointer reaches.
The render read back as a PNG: unchanged from R1653's.
5 counterfactuals re-run against the moved code, 5 caught.
carry_forward_bullets: None. The bound is stated where a position is set rather than carried.

R1653.2.decision_summary:
R1653's close audit asked the obvious question -- the instrument that found five
defects on one surface reaches exactly that one surface -- and rather than
registering the answer as a guess, asked the second surface on the spot. The
sibling shell is where this class was first measured (R1649 stacked every card's
text down the left edge with 118 wire assertions passing), so it is the one
worth asking first. It passes, which makes the debt "nobody asked" rather than
"there are more defects", and a counterfactual confirms the check can fail.

R1654.decision_summary:
Five defects reported from the running window, and every one of them was
invisible to the tests: the screen ignored the window it was given, its text
escaped its boxes with no way to ask about it, its host frames were rectangles
out of a table rather than groups, its rail icons were two sizes of dot, and a
node could not be dragged above where the graph opened. Four are repairs; the
one that is a capability is the one the report asked for as a question -- why
can the wire not diagnose text leaving its rectangle -- and the answer was that
every read published the box the author PROMISED and none published what the
shaper produced.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: `text_elide` -- one elision policy, the metric supplied by the
caller, because shaped pixels and terminal cells cannot be reconciled and the
decision must not be made twice. `TextOverflow` gains EllipsisStart and
EllipsisMiddle (five arms, censused).
pinion-text: the shaper honours the eliding arms, so every painter inherits
them; styled spans are moved onto the shortened string; `painted_text`,
`ink_size` and `line_count` publish what the entry actually holds.
pinion-rpc: `scene/text_painted` reports every run -- its window rect, what the
scene holds, what the frame drew, the ink extent, the line count, and whether
the ink left the box. `scene/locate` takes the two-scene basis its two siblings
already had.
pinion-widget-paint: the settings form's runs declare an overflow policy.
tools: the boot gate every demo pays refuses a screen whose runs land on each
other, with `docs/text-smear-budget.tsv` as the measured ratchet.
examples/hello-node-lab: panes derived from `use_viewport_size` and the window
made resizable; frames derived from their members, draggable, and joined by a
drop; rail icons drawn as marks; the second clamp on a node drag removed.
verification_bullets: cargo test: 3383 core, 105 text, 1208 rpc, 840 widget-paint, 24 hello-node-lab,
17 hello-analyzer-shell. clippy -D pedantic clean on all seven.
6 counterfactuals, 6 caught.
The running app driven over the wire: resized 1440 -> 1800 and the panes
followed (canvas 844 -> 1204, inspector to 1488, palette unchanged at 230).
Both analyzer demos re-passed unchanged.
The text-smear backlog measured over all 223 example packages: 31 carry 71
overlapping pairs, 9 cannot boot headless and are recorded as unmeasured rather
than clean.
Measured on the reference toolkit (probe outside the repository): four elide
modes live on its METRICS class, its label has no elide property at all (only
its item views do), a label handed a string too wide for it clips while its size
hint still reports the full natural width, and `text()` returns the authored
string -- so nothing there can report what a reader actually saw.
carry_forward_bullets: The smear ratchet's numbers were measured before the settings-form painter
gained its policy in the same round, so a handful are an upper bound on what the
tree does now -- the safe direction for a ratchet, and stated in the file.

R1655.decision_summary:
"Sometimes a node presses and sometimes it does not" — and the model was
innocent. Every point of every card in every state already resolved to that
card; what failed was the ROUTER path. The §5.35 router resolves the deepest
TAGGED node under the cursor and looks that tag up as an `External`; a tag here
is an address, not a widget, so a tagged node that is not pointer-transparent
makes the lookup fail and the router forwards nothing. Two families were opaque:
every wire on the canvas — whose bounding box is most of the canvas — and the
settings form's badges, which are painted by a CRATE and therefore dead in every
consumer of it. Measured by reverting: with the wires opaque the application
never received the cursor at all, reporting 0,0 after a real warp onto the
canvas.
changes_bullets: examples/hello-node-lab: a wire declares itself pointer-transparent; the link
stays selectable through `link_at`, which hit-tests the chord in the app's own
resolver.
pinion-widget-paint: a form badge declares itself pointer-transparent, and the
crate now tests that every tag it writes does — the guarantee belongs where the
node is painted, not in one consumer's suite.
examples/hello-node-lab: three sweeps over the derived population — every card
presses and drags to itself in every state, a press anywhere on a card (a 6x6
grid, ~1,700 points) reaches that card, and every tag but the root is

R1656.decision_summary:
Hand over half a fact and the other half is wrong in a different way at every
consumer. A person reported two things — text painted outside the node cards,
and nodes that stop clicking after a maximise — and both turned out to be that
sentence, in the framework rather than in the screen.

THE INK HALF. A rectangle in a scene is a PROMISE. Every read here reported the
promise and none reported whether it was kept, so the analysis-tool screen
painted seven of its eight cards' last field row three to five pixels below
their own border, at the size it opens in, with four checks watching. Measured
why each was blind: `scene/snapshot` reports promised rectangles and they were
all correct, because what left the box was the INK and the ink is not in the
scene; `scene/text_painted`'s `overflows` compares a run's ink against ITS OWN
box and answered true for 124 of 157 runs (a shaped line box is taller than the
face it holds, so a box authored at the font size overflows by construction) —
a meter that fires on 79% of a screen cannot discriminate; the smear gate groups
runs by their nearest TAGGED ANCESTOR, and the canvas painter emitted each
card's parts as the card's SIBLINGS, so "is this run inside its owner" was being
asked about the canvas, which is big enough to hold anything.

THE POINTER HALF. `External::pointer_move` hands a FRACTION of the widget's rect
and does not hand the rect. A consumer that wants pixels has to find the basis
elsewhere, and there is no reactive scope inside a pointer callback, so the
standard mistake is to multiply by a design constant — and the standard mistake
is exact at the size the app opens in. Solved by two-point calibration rather
than by reading: after a maximise to 2494x1531 the application was told
`app_x = 0.5775 * screen_x` and `app_y = 0.5880 * screen_y`, which are 1440/2494
and 900/1531 to six figures. `External::on_resize` is one of the eight §5.15
contract items and had ZERO call sites in the workspace — R1654's class exactly:
a declared arm with no implementation is worse than an absent one, because a
consumer reads the contract, implements it, and waits forever.

A RULE WAS WRITTEN, MEASURED AND DELETED. Tags here are addresses, so
`lab.node.T-01.id` appears to say it is part of `lab.node.T-01`, and judging a
mark against its longest tag-prefix would have caught the flat painter with no
restructuring. Run against the real screen it produced two findings and BOTH
WERE FALSE: `lab.toolbar.zoom.out` is the button beside the readout
`lab.toolbar.zoom`, not content inside it. A dotted tag expresses grouping, not
containment. So the repair is to stop being a flat painter — to put the relation
back in the scene, where §2 #7 says the description of the screen lives — and
the blindness is asserted as a test rather than papered over.

SIZE WAS NEVER AN AXIS, AND THAT IS WHY FIVE MORE DEFECTS GOT OUT. R1654 wrote
down the reason in its own words — "every check ran the layout at WIN_W x WIN_H,
so the assumption and the defect were the same number" — and left the axis at
one entry. Adding two entries found, on its first run: the toolbar's zoom
readout not painted at all at the declared floor (right-anchored constants
reaching past the pane's own left edge), 22 of 46 controls painted below the
window at that floor, the hint strip 470px wide on a narrower canvas, and 11,472
grid pips painted past the world surface at the minimum zoom on a maximised
window. Eight states times one size is not eight cases; it is one case visited
eight ways.

AND THE GATE FOUND TWO IN A CRATE, which is where the leverage is: the settings
form's key line was `key_px + 7`, one pixel short of the shaper's line box, on
every consumer; and its header badges were painted past the row's right edge
whenever the key was long, because the row's box was right, each badge's box was
right, and only their SUM was wrong. The repair hands the deficit to the flex
pass — badges refuse to shrink, the key may shrink below its content, the shaper
elides it to the width it was actually given — so no number in that file has to
be correct. A first repair that measured the badge strings and subtracted was
still 7px short, because a fallback advance estimate is not a shaped advance.
changes_bullets: pinion-core: `containment` — every painted mark that left the box that owns
it, per edge, with the string a reader loses and whether a clip cut it away.
The metric is a closure for the reason `text_elide`'s is (§2 #6: shaped pixels
and terminal cells cannot be reconciled); the policy is shared.
pinion-core: `containment::line_box` — the height a box needs for one line of
a face, conservative on purpose. The commonest authoring mistake this catches
is a box authored at the FONT SIZE.
pinion-rpc: `scene/containment` publishes it, with `marks` beside the counts
so an empty list on a surface that painted nothing cannot read as coverage.
pinion-rpc: `scene/text_painted` gains `over_w` / `over_h` — the amount and
the axis, because the boolean beside them is true of 79% of a real screen.
pinion-shell: a debug-build paint-time warning, deduplicated per mark, so the
defect is announced on the frame it happens rather than when someone asks.
Release builds do not walk the scene; the read stays available on the wire.
pinion-runtime: `announce_external_sizes` drives `External::on_resize`, a
§5.15 arm with zero call sites until now. The size comes from `rect_for_tag`
on the PAINT scene — the same resolver `capture_rel_coords` divides by — and
the handle from the STATE scene, so the basis and the fraction are one
derivation.
pinion-widget-paint: the form's key line is the shaper's line box, and the
header's key shrinks below its content while the badges refuse to, so a long
path elides instead of pushing them off the row.
examples/hello-node-lab: `CardShape` — the card's box is DERIVED from the rows
it paints and its parts are its CHILDREN, so a row that does not fit is not
expressible and the scene stops lying about the screen.
examples/hello-node-lab: the canvas font scales with the diagram; the world
extent has one derivation; the hint strip is clamped to its pane; the declared
floor is derived from what the chrome needs.
examples/hello-node-lab, hello-analyzer-shell, hello-node-editor,
hello-grid-pointer: the pointer fraction is multiplied by the live surface.
examples/hello-node-lab: the painted sweep runs states x SIZES, holds the
screen to containment measured against the ink, and floors both axes.
tools/rpc_verify.py: a boot gate every surface pays, with a ratchet.
examples/hello-node-lab: a card added from the palette is placed where nothing
already is, and card detail collapses below the zoom at which its face would be
drawn at the legibility floor — the tension every node editor resolves the same
way, because a floored face stops shrinking while the diagram keeps going.
docs/containment-budget.tsv: measured over all 223 example packages — 214
measured, 25 carrying 95 escapes, 9 unmeasured and named rather than omitted.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p pinion-core -p pinion-rpc -p pinion-runtime -p pinion-widget-paint
--features vello: 4,604 pass.
cargo test -p hello-node-lab --release: the painted sweep is green over 8
states x 3 sizes with the containment property on every cell.
cargo clippy on every changed crate and every touched example, --all-targets,
pedantic: clean.
tools/demos/r1656_a_mark_says_the_box_it_left.py: 8,972 marks examined, 0
escapes; the cursor arrives at 700,400 at BOTH the opening size and 2494x1531
(it arrived at 404,235 before); 8 cards selected by pressing where they are
painted on the grown window.
Real mouse, real window, closed-loop aim: 8 of 8 node cards select at the
opening size AND after a real maximise, with the app reporting exactly the
aimed coordinate in all 16 cases. Before the repair the same probe solved the
screen-to-app map as 0.5775x / 0.5880x after the maximise.
Two-point calibration before and after: 1.000000 at both sizes now.
The reference toolkit was BUILT and RUN, not read: its widget aggregate
(`childrenRect`) reports children GEOMETRY (measured: a label given a 60x14
box reports 60x14 there while its text measures 251x17), its scene-graph
aggregate reports boxes, ink is available only one call at a time from a

warns, and a child outside its parent is silently clipped — `visibleRegion`
reports the survivor, not the loss.
8 counterfactuals, and three of them were FINDINGS before they were catches.
Nothing caught an ink metric replaced by the run's own box (the check had no
negative control, so a clean screen and a blind check looked identical);
nothing caught the free-spot search being disabled (the swept states add ONE
node and one node happens to miss); nothing in Rust caught the form's key line
going back to a guess. Each is now a test, and the second of them found that
the round's OWN repair was wrong — `free_spot` searched in window coordinates
against rectangles in world ones, so six added cards landed in a single stack.
The counterfactual driver also refused to start on a red baseline and named two
tests this round had broken while only `r1653*` was being run.
carry_forward_bullets: The containment read is only as honest as the tree: a painter that flattens
its containment gets a CLEAN report. Stated in the module and asserted as a
test rather than worked around with a second channel, because §2 #7 says the
scene is the description of the screen. The tag-prefix rule that would have
covered it was written, measured against the real screen, produced two
findings that were both false, and deleted.
`External::pointer_move` still hands a fraction without its basis. R1656 woke
the channel and moved four consumers onto it; the CONTRACT is unchanged, so a
new consumer can make the same mistake tomorrow and it will be exact at the
opening size. The shape that closes it is a type carrying its own basis across
all six normalised callbacks — 28 implementors.
hello-node-lab's palette and inspector do not scroll, so a list field long
enough puts its last chips below the window whatever the floor is set to.
Counted and ratcheted rather than hidden: marks past the window bottom are
tallied and capped, marks past a pane SIDEWAYS still fail.

R1657.decision_summary:
Bump the vendored SCE pin 8597e692 -> 3fecb424 (74 commits) and consume the
policy that came with it: a pinion-forge diagnostic record now names the build
that emitted it.

WHAT THE BUMP CARRIED THAT PINION HAD TO ANSWER FOR. Upstream added
GENERATOR_COMMIT and made `generator` a REQUIRED field on
schemas/sce-diagnostic.v1.schema.json, with a stated reason that generalises
past SCE: while a wire surface is pre-release, a consumer is told to pin a
specific commit rather than trust the schema version, because a non-additive
shape change may land without a version bump — and a consumer cannot follow
that instruction unless the payload names the commit it came from. On the
failure path there is nothing else to read: a rejected run writes no manifest,
so stdout is empty and the record is all the consumer receives.

pinion-forge's wire module has said since its first round that it MIRRORS that record
shape. That sentence stopped being true at the instant of the bump, with no
file in this tree edited. That is the whole finding: a claim about another
project's shape can go false while nothing here moves, so it cannot be prose.

THE STAMP IS A COMMIT AND NOT THE VERSION. Every pinion crate carries 0.0.1
from the workspace, so the version identifies nothing — two builds a hundred
rounds apart report the same string. crates/pinion-forge/build.rs resolves the
commit the way sce-build's does: follow the gitdir indirection so a worktree or
submodule checkout works, watch HEAD and the symbolic ref and packed-refs so
the embedded value cannot go stale within a session, and report `unknown` when
there is no checkout to read rather than a claim it cannot keep. Scope is the
committed state deliberately — the rerun triggers watch the ref and not the
worktree, so a cleanliness flag computed here would go stale on the next edit,
and a stale "clean" reads exactly like a true one.

THE CENSUS IS THE PATTERN, NOT A LIST. The new gate destructures a real
sce-build diagnostic with no `..`. Exhaustive destructuring means a field added
upstream fails to COMPILE here, so the next required field cannot be absorbed
by silence the way this one was. Every binding is either mirrored on pinion's
record or named as deliberately absent with its reason: `spec` and
`spec_provenance` are SCXML/RFC anchors pinion's closed namespace has no peer
for (RFC 001 section 4 is closed — pinion's codes are not SCE codes), `expected`
and `fix` are SCE's repair-loop payload pinion emits none of, `question_kind`
classifies an authoring question back to the author where pinion's diagnostics
are all refusals. The backward direction is checked too, because the schema is
additionalProperties:false: a key pinion invents leaves the shape.

WHY THE OLD TEST DID NOT CATCH IT. wire_record_has_required_fields hand-listed
the required fields and passed for the whole time `generator` was missing —
the shape this project keeps paying for, where a gate whose population is
hand-written reports a sample as coverage. It now asserts the stamp on the
emitted LINE (the NDJSON path is what a consumer reads, not to_json_value), and
says in place that its completeness is somebody else's job and names whose.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CARRY. The policy pinion just adopted is
honoured on exactly one surface. Measured: pinion-rpc publishes 113 methods and
none of them answers which build the server is; rpc/methods and rpc/schema are
the self-describing surfaces and neither response carries a producer; no crate
but pinion-forge stamps a build at all. That is registered as
debt-only-one-wire-surface-names-its-build rather than closed here, because it
is not the consumption of this bump — SCE's change is to its own diagnostic and

R1657.publishable_decision_summary:
Bump the vendored SCE pin 8597e692 -> 3fecb424 (74 commits) and consume the
policy that came with it: a pinion-forge diagnostic record now names the build
that emitted it.

WHAT THE BUMP CARRIED THAT PINION HAD TO ANSWER FOR. Upstream added
GENERATOR_COMMIT and made `generator` a REQUIRED field on
schemas/sce-diagnostic.v1.schema.json, with a stated reason that generalises
past SCE: while a wire surface is pre-release, a consumer is told to pin a
specific commit rather than trust the schema version, because a non-additive
shape change may land without a version bump — and a consumer cannot follow
that instruction unless the payload names the commit it came from. On the
failure path there is nothing else to read: a rejected run writes no manifest,
so stdout is empty and the record is all the consumer receives.

pinion-forge's wire module has said since its first round that it MIRRORS that record
shape. That sentence stopped being true at the instant of the bump, with no
file in this tree edited. That is the whole finding: a claim about another
project's shape can go false while nothing here moves, so it cannot be prose.

THE STAMP IS A COMMIT AND NOT THE VERSION. Every pinion crate carries 0.0.1
from the workspace, so the version identifies nothing — two builds a hundred
rounds apart report the same string. crates/pinion-forge/build.rs resolves the
commit the way sce-build's does: follow the gitdir indirection so a worktree or
submodule checkout works, watch HEAD and the symbolic ref and packed-refs so
the embedded value cannot go stale within a session, and report `unknown` when
there is no checkout to read rather than a claim it cannot keep. Scope is the
committed state deliberately — the rerun triggers watch the ref and not the
worktree, so a cleanliness flag computed here would go stale on the next edit,
and a stale "clean" reads exactly like a true one.

THE CENSUS IS THE PATTERN, NOT A LIST. The new gate destructures a real
sce-build diagnostic with no `..`. Exhaustive destructuring means a field added

record or named as deliberately absent with its reason: `spec` and

emitted LINE (the NDJSON path is what a consumer reads, not to_json_value), and
says in place that its completeness is somebody else's job and names whose.

R1657.1.decision_summary:
The round's own close audit found a failure mode its new test accepted.

`a_record_names_the_build_that_emitted_it` gates the SHAPE of the stamp — a
short-or-full lowercase hex commit, or the `unknown` a checkout-less build
legitimately reports. That is the schema's own pattern, and it is right. But it
means a resolver that DIED — git absent from the build script's environment, the
rev-parse invocation changed, the env var never emitted — would satisfy it
forever while the stamp identified nothing. The two cases are indistinguishable
to every assertion the round shipped, and the one that matters is silent.

This is the class the previous round named: an implementation exists and nobody
asks whether it is still alive. Registering it as debt would have been the wrong
answer when the test is six lines.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, DELIBERATELY. It does not compare against `git rev-parse
HEAD`. The build script watches HEAD and the values do agree — that was verified
by hand, once, in the built artefact — but a commit landing between the build and
the assertion would turn the test red for a reason that is not a defect, and this
tree's zero-flake rule makes a small race a real cost. Aliveness is the property
worth gating.

BOTH BRANCHES ASSERT. In a checkout the stamp must not be `unknown`; without one
it must be exactly `unknown`, because a build that cannot read a commit has to
say so rather than guess. A guard that silently skips is an assertion that does
not run, and it reads like coverage.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-forge/src/wire.rs: the_resolver_is_alive_in_a_checkout_and_honest_without_one — asks git whether this is a checkout, then requires a named commit in one case and exactly `unknown` in the other
verification_bullets: cargo test -p pinion-forge: 95 pass, 0 fail (94 before); clippy clean; fmt clean

counterfactual 1/1 CAUGHT: make the build script discard git_commit() and always emit `unknown`, which is precisely the dead resolver a checkout-less build is indistinguishable from under the shape assertion alone
carry_forward_bullets: none — the audit finding this pays was the only one, and the round's registered debt is unchanged

R1658.decision_summary:
A keystroke says when it ARRIVED, so a binding stops judging the user's
timeline against its own workload.

WHAT THE CONSUMER ASKED FOR, AND WHY THE REQUEST NAMED THE WRONG TYPE. The
handoff filed this against `pinion_core::event::KeyEvent` — "it carries a key
code and nothing else". Measured: that type has ONE construction site in the
whole tree, its own test, and no dispatch path reaches it. Adding a field to it
would have satisfied the request as written and delivered the consumer nothing.
The gap the report describes is real and its own prose says so correctly two
paragraphs later — "nothing on the dispatch path exposes a time" — and the
dispatch path is `WidgetCore::apply_key` / `apply_key_repeat`, which is where
this landed. A declared type nobody drives is the same class this project keeps
paying for from the other side.

THE DEFECT, IN ONE SENTENCE. The only clock a binding could read was
`Instant::now()` inside its own handler, and that is when this app got round to
the key, not when the key arrived — later by however long the PREVIOUS
keystroke's handler took. Any window judged on it (a repeat window, a chord
timeout, a double-tap) silently shrinks by exactly the amount of work the app
is doing. The consumer measured it: a 500 ms repeat window with a blocking
round trip per keystroke lost two presses out of three under 2x CPU
oversubscription, and the lost presses went through to the terminal underneath
as raw escapes. Their terminal frontend had no such defect because its input
layer hands over the read a key came out of; their GUI frontend could not be
fixed at all. One product, one binding, two frontends behaving differently.

TWO HALVES, AND BOTH ARE NEEDED. `KeyArrival` carries an instant and a batch.
They answer different questions and neither derives the other: keys of one
platform handover share both, but two keys a microsecond apart may still be
separate handovers. A gesture is a statement about the SECOND — three presses
out of one read are one gesture however long the app spends between them —
which is why `arrived_with` is published as a predicate rather than leaving a
consumer to compare ids and become a second author of the rule. A counterfactual
proves the axis: swapping `arrived_with` to compare instants is caught, because
a unit test holds the two halves apart on purpose.

WHERE A DELIVERY BEGINS, PER BACKEND, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CALL ARGUMENT. The
arrival is a property of the loop iteration, not of a dispatch, so it lives on
the shell and each backend says where its handovers begin. The GUI opens one in
winit's `new_events`, which runs before any event of that iteration is
dispatched — that ordering IS the capability, and stamping inside the keyboard
arm instead would date the second key of a burst at after the first key's
handler returned. The terminal asks whether the next event was ALREADY WAITING
when the previous dispatch returned: if it was, the person produced it before
this app finished, so it is the same gesture. Deliberately not "came out of the
same read", because crossterm does not say and "already waiting" is what "same
read" is a proxy for anyway. The RPC drain opens one per drain: keys the agent
handed over together arrived together, and a key from the next request did not.

WHAT IT IS NOT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. It is not when the human pressed
the key. No portable windowing layer offers that — winit exposes no platform
event timestamp — so this is stamped by the runtime as the handover is opened.
That is the whole of what the defect needs, and naming the type `arrival`
rather than `time` is what keeps the claim honest. A side effect worth naming:
carrying it on the event makes a keystroke REPLAYABLE, where a handler reading
`Instant::now()` cannot be replayed at all.

A STRUCT, NOT A FIFTH PARAMETER. `KeyPress` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the next
fact a keystroke carries is a field. This entry point already grew once by
growing a hook — `apply_key` -> `apply_key_repeat` for the auto-repeat flag —
and a hook per fact does not go a third time. The default chain carries a press
down to the 160 `apply_key` impls unchanged, which a counterfactual checks by
severing it.

THE COUNTERFACTUAL FOUND THE REAL HOLE AND IT WAS THE GUI PATH. Making the winit
dispatch stamp a fresh arrival instead of reading the open delivery — the exact
defect, reintroduced — left the whole suite GREEN. Every test written up to that
point drove `CoreShell` or the RPC drain, and neither goes through
`ShellCore::apply_key_inner`. Verifying a capability only through the paths that
bypass the one under repair is this project's standing lesson and it was being
repeated here. Both winit arms now have their own assertion, `apply_key_inner`
and the offer-first `try_apply_key_inner`, because they are two call sites with
two copies of the rule.

ALSO IN THE HANDOFF, AND CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY WORK. Of the four
items the requirements document lists as open, two are already delivered:
`serve_with_exposure` landed at R1469 and is consumed, and a refused invoke has
carried the producer's reason since R1564 — which is IN the pin the consumer is
already on. Their log carried the earlier verdict forward across a pin bump
without re-checking, which is the same staleness class as a debt note nobody
re-measures.

pinion-shell app.rs: ApplicationHandler::new_events opens the delivery once per winit event-loop iteration, before any event of that iteration is dispatched

pinion-shell substrate.rs: both winit dispatch arms read the open delivery instead of stamping at dispatch; the RPC drain opens one delivery per drain; ShellCore::open_key_delivery / key_delivery for the backend

pinion-tui shell.rs: await_terminal_event answers "did we have to wait for this event", which is the terminal's delivery boundary; extracted rather than inlined because the loop was at the too_many_lines ceiling

That reasoning stops holding the moment the burst form above lands, and the debt file says so

R1659.decision_summary:
A consumer that speaks only the JSON-RPC wire no longer links a font-shaping
stack — and the fix is not the one that was asked for, because that one does
not work.

THE REPORT. `pinion-rpc` declares `pinion-text` / `pinion-text-font` /
`pinion-text-unicode`; on Linux the first of those reaches
`yeslogic-fontconfig-sys`, whose build script requires the fontconfig
development headers, so a consumer's CI failed with "The system library
`fontconfig` ... was not found". macOS passes the same commit because fontique
takes Core Text there, which is what made a dependency problem look like a
runner problem. The proposed fix was a `text` feature over those three
dependencies, with the RPC methods that need shaping `#[cfg]`-ed out of the
catalogue when it is off.

TWO MEASUREMENTS CHANGED THE ANSWER, AND BOTH WERE CHEAP.

First, WHICH dependency carries it. `pinion-text-font` depends on
`pinion-text-unicode` and nothing else; `pinion-text-unicode` depends on
nothing. Only `pinion-text` reaches parley. Gating all three would have removed
eleven `font/*` methods and the Unicode normalisation method to solve a problem
none of them cause — the report traced one error to one branch and generalised
to the crates that looked alike.

Second, HOW MANY paths reach it. `cargo tree -p pinion-rpc -i pinion-text`
answers TWO: the declaration in `pinion-rpc` itself, and again through
`pinion-runtime`, which `pinion-rpc` uses at 101 sites and cannot stop using.
So feature-gating the dependencies `pinion-rpc` declares — the fix as proposed —
leaves the font stack linked and the consumer's build broken. The report's own
"not verified" section says it never tried the fix; this is what trying it finds.

WHAT ACTUALLY MOVES. parley's default `system` feature is the whole of it: it
forwards to `fontique/system`, which is what pulls fontconfig. Declining it at
the workspace root and re-enabling it through a `system-fonts` feature that is
ON by default gives an external consumer `default-features = false` and changes
nothing here. Measured both ways against a real external manifest outside this
workspace, because `cargo tree` inside it unifies other members' features and
would have reported the fix as not working: with defaults, fontconfig is
present by both paths; with `default-features = false` it is not in the graph at
all, and the consumer builds.

NO METHOD DISAPPEARS, which is the part worth stating. Every RPC surface that
shapes text compiles and answers in both builds — `rpc/methods` returns the same
catalogue — because what the switch moves is which fonts the stack can FIND, not
which questions it can be asked. A cache told to use only the fonts it was given
(R1573) is the shape that already existed for this. The proposal would have
gated a capability to solve a linking problem, and the linking problem is not
where the capability is.

THE GATE, AND WHY IT IS A GATE. The property is a closure over the dependency
graph — every path must decline, not the visible one — and that is the shape no
reviewer holds in their head and no comment can state; a third path is one
ordinary-looking `Cargo.toml` line away. `tools/wire_only_deps.py` walks
`pinion-rpc`'s path-dependency closure and requires every edge into the text
stack to decline defaults, every crate on the way to offer the switch back and
to offer it by default, and the two halves that give the switch meaning (the
workspace parley declaration, and `pinion-text`'s forward to `parley/system`).
`pre-push` runs its selftest before trusting it.

DESIGNING THE COUNTERFACTUALS FOUND A HOLE IN THAT GATE BEFORE THEY RAN. The
first draft checked that an edge declines defaults and that each crate offers a
switch, but not that the switch NAMES the declined edge — so `pinion-rpc`
forwarding to `pinion-text` and forgetting `pinion-runtime` would have passed
while a default build silently lost system fonts through the second path. That
is the same second path the report missed, arriving a second time from the
opposite direction.

R1660.decision_summary:
Every measurement in this tree shapes against ONE pinned face, so a budget
measured here means the same thing on CI.

THE RED, DIAGNOSED. R1656 built a ratchet on painted INK — `scene/containment`
reports which marks left the box that owns them, every demo pays it at boot
against a per-example budget, and `scene/text_painted` feeds the text-smear
peer. Ink is a function of the shaped face, the face is a function of the
host's font database, and the budgets were measured on one machine. So the
ratchet gave a different verdict on CI: 33 sweep runs red on 8 examples that
pass locally, which is a green local gate saying nothing about CI.

REPRODUCED, NOT ARGUED. Pointing `FONTCONFIG_FILE` at a config exposing only
DejaVu reproduces the CI failure on this machine — `hello-tabbed-chart` 6
escapes to 7, and the marks that move are the chart's tick labels, pure ink
extent. Three hypotheses were killed first and are recorded so nobody re-runs
them: not display geometry (Xvfb at CI's 1600x1200 changes nothing), not a
silently skipped gate (the method answers locally, 273 marks), not run-to-run
flake (6 of 6 identical).

THE CONTROL THAT MISLED ME, because it will mislead the next reader too:
"remove all fonts" is the WRONG control. With no fonts there is no ink, so
nothing overflows and the count is 0 — which reads as "fonts are not the
cause". CI does not have NO fonts; it has DIFFERENT fonts.

R1573 MEASURED THIS EXACT CLASS ONE LAYER DOWN and closed it — 40 of 94 unit
tests read the host — with `LayoutCache::with_own_fonts`. R1656 then built the
demo gate on a host-reading cache, which reopened it one layer up.

THE FIRST FIX WAS MEASURED WRONG, AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S CONTENT. Pinning the
shell's `LayoutCache` to an own-fonts cache made three different hosts agree —
and made `scene/text_painted` report ZERO runs. The screen had no text on it at
all, so `0 escapes` was green for the wrong reason, which is worse than the red
it replaces. An own-fonts cache has no fallback, so a style naming a family the
registered face does not provide resolves to nothing. Reverted.

Replacing the DATABASE instead keeps every fallback path intact and gives it one
thing to find. Measured: 16 of 16 and 63 of 63 runs inked, numbers equal to this
host's own, and identical under a DejaVu-only host and a font-less one.

THE PINNED SET IS EXACTLY ONE FACE, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. Adding the
sibling NanumGothic takes `hello-tabbed-chart` from 6 to 7, and the marks that
move are LATIN tick labels — the app's styles name families neither face
provides, so with two faces fontconfig's ordering decides the fallback and the
ink follows it. With one face there is nothing to decide. Adding a face is
therefore a re-measurement of both budget files, which is why the set is a
named constant rather than a directory.

WHAT THIS ROUND DOES NOT FINISH. The budgets themselves were measured on the
unpinned host and are now stale against the reproducible number:
`hello-endpoint-identity` measures 2 under the pin — agreeing with CI — against
a budget of 1. Re-measuring both files across every surface is the remaining
step and is stated rather than half-done, because a budget raised without a
reproducible measurement behind it is the one use the file itself forbids.

tools/rpc_verify.py: the font-source demos are exempt by that same rule, because they drive FONTCONFIG_FILE themselves and are ABOUT what the host has
verification_bullets: the CI failure is reproduced locally under a DejaVu-only fontconfig (hello-tabbed-chart 6 -> 7 escapes) and disappears under the pin
three hypotheses killed by measurement before the fourth was built: display geometry, a silently-skipped gate, run-to-run flake
the first fix was rejected by measurement rather than by review: an own-fonts LayoutCache made three hosts agree and left the screen with ZERO painted text runs
under the pin, text still shapes: 16/16 and 63/63 runs inked, and the pin is structural (fc-list under it reports exactly one face)
3 of the 8 CI-failing examples now pass locally: r1409_tabbed_chart, r1523_virtual_columns, r1530_headers_asked_for
hello-endpoint-identity now measures 2 deterministically, which AGREES with CI against a stale budget of 1 — the remaining step
carry_forward_bullets: THE ROUND IS NOT FINISHED and CI is still red. Remaining: re-measure docs/containment-budget.tsv and docs/text-smear-budget.tsv across every surface under the pin, then confirm on CI. R1657-R1659 stay unpushed until it is green

the budget files cannot distinguish "no entry" from "measured 0" — hello-audio-device cannot boot on this host (no snd-dummy) so R1656 left it unmeasured and it reads as 0, while CI boots it and measures 1

fontconfig is the Linux font path; macOS and Windows ignore it, so a measurement taken there is still host-dependent. A second platform needs the cache-level pin done properly, which means giving the own-fonts cache a family alias so text still shapes

R1661.decision_summary:
The two ink ratchets get a producer, so their numbers can be re-derived instead
of remembered.

WHY THE BUDGETS WENT STALE, WHICH IS THE POINT. R1656 measured 223 surfaces by
hand, wrote the non-zero rows into `docs/containment-budget.tsv`, and left no
way to do it again. A ratchet whose numbers cannot be re-derived is a ratchet
nobody can re-judge: when the numbers turned out to be host-dependent (R1660),
there was nothing to re-run, and when a surface could not be measured there was
nowhere to say so. Both failures are downstream of the same absence.

`tools/measure_ink_budgets.py` is that derivation. It refuses to run with the
font pin off — `FONTCONFIG_FILE` already set means the numbers would be a fact
about one host again, which is exactly what R1660 removed. Its population is
derived from the tree rather than listed, because a hand-written population
reports a sample as coverage.

THE THIRD STATE. The files could say `<example>\t<count>` and nothing else, so a
surface that could not be measured left no row, and no row reads as `0` — the
strictest budget there is, chosen by nobody. `hello-audio-device` cannot boot
without `snd-dummy`; it was silently budgeted at 0 and CI, which loads that
card, measures 1. The generated files now carry
`<example>\tunmeasured\t<reason>` as a first-class row: it passes the gate and
REPORTS, and the reason travels with it so a host that can measure the surface
is visibly owed a number rather than quietly clean.

WHAT THIS ROUND DOES NOT FINISH, stated rather than implied. The full
re-measurement is running and takes hours; the parsers in `rpc_verify.py` still
read the two-state form; and the pin still has no gate, which is registered as
its own debt because this session already walked into that trap once — an
own-fonts cache that made three hosts agree by painting no text at all.

AND ONE OBSERVATION THE MEASUREMENT ALREADY MADE. `hello-endpoint-identity`
reported 2 escapes through the demo and 1 through this tool, both under the pin.
A number that moves with the pin ON means that surface has a second source of
non-determinism — the font was not its only one. Recorded so the next round
starts from it rather than rediscovering it.

the refusal path is exercised: with FONTCONFIG_FILE set the tool exits rather than producing host-dependent numbers
the full run is in progress at 25 of 223 surfaces when this was committed

R1662.decision_summary: A pane says what no scrolling can reach. Two different things stop a mark being on screen and the tree gave them one answer: the pane scrolled past it (the reader scrolls back) and nothing can bring it into view at all (the pane does not scroll, or its content extent stops short). Measured on a synthetic pane before building anything: the reachable row produced NO containment report, and the unreachable row produced fate "clipped", the same word a two-pixel line-box rounding gets. So `pinion_core::reach` derives the third fact — for every painted mark, the innermost enclosing viewport, its content extent, its range, and either the least-move offset that shows it or how far past the reachable box it sits. The window is that same function with range (0,0), which is what makes "this pane does not scroll" and "this pane scrolls" two values of one derivation rather than two checks that must be kept in step. Published as `scene/scroll_reach`; the reference toolkit was probed out-of-tree and has no equivalent — overflow can only be inferred from a scroll bar maximum, which is also its answer for an area that never set a range.

R1663.decision_summary: A decoded field says which bytes it came from. The analyzer census carried capture.t0.3 -- bidirectional highlight between a field and its bytes -- as a `have`, covered by widgets::hex_dump plus scene/marks. Driven on the wire before building anything, neither surface holds the relation: the dissection External publishes 13 declared paths and NOT ONE names a byte, and the hex External publishes 17 and NOT ONE names a field. That verdict was covering the byte-to-CELL pair, which is a different pair, and it is the error direction R1602 named as the expensive one -- a wrong `have` inflates a number silently where a wrong `absent` self-corrects the moment somebody reaches for it. pinion_core::widgets::field_bytes is the relation: ONE list of FieldSpans, from which forward (extent_of / selection_for, already shaped as the ByteSelection a hex view highlights) and inverse (layers_at, with owner_at DEFINED as its last link rather than computed a second way) are both derived. The marks this tree already had are the right thing for saying why a painted position looks the way it does and cannot carry a dissection, and each gap is asserted against a real MarkSet rather than claimed: one index space, overlap as a paint rule rather than an invariant, two answers where there are three, and no arm for a field with no bytes. So the dissection is the model and the paint marks are derived from it.

R1664.decision_summary: A screen says whether a press can reach anything. `scene/pointer_reach` reported four fields and every one of them is read off the PAINT tree, so a screen whose widgets are registered under names nothing on screen carries reads clean in all four: no tag resolves, so nothing is deliverable; nothing shadows anything, because there is no victim to shadow; nothing is unreachable, because that population is the tags that DID resolve and none did. The only trace was `deliverable: 0`, which is byte-identical to the honest answer a screen with no widgets on it gives. R1663 shipped `hello-packet-view` in exactly that state -- 185 painted tags, an empty shadows list, an empty unreachable list -- the boot gate PRINTED `deliverable=0 inert=30` and passed it, and the defect was found by a person opening the window, pressing things, and reporting that nothing happened. This is the collapse R1661 and R1662 fixed one layer up in the budget files, where "no entry" and "measured zero" were also one value; here it is the gate. The repair walks the same join from the STATE side, where the thing that needs repairing has a name: `externals` pairs every tagged `External` with the shallowest painted tag that routes a press to it, and `is_dead_to_a_pointer` is DERIVED from that list rather than stored beside it. All-and-not-any is the rule, because a single unrouted widget is ordinary -- a model registered for `scene/query` has no surface by design -- while a roster with nothing routed at all is a window in which every press is dropped. An empty roster is not dead either, or "no widgets yet" and "the wiring broke" become one answer again, which is the mistake being undone. AND REPAIRING THE ROUTING LEFT THE SCREEN STILL DEAF, which is the round's second finding: the router then resolved the widget, called `invoke("send", "PointerDown")`, and the screen -- which had named its own action `press` -- returned `UnknownPath`, which `dispatch_send` discards. A press that arrives, is refused, and leaves no trace. Registered as debt rather than closed, because the schema cannot yet judge it: 54 files handle `send` and 17 declare it. The bypass that hid all of this needed no new wire method -- `scene/click {at}` already goes through the §5.35 router and no sweep had ever used it, so `assert_router_press_moves` is a helper and three analyzer demos adopt it with negative controls. Finally the CI sweep's eleven failures, entered as this round's stop-the-line debt and all one shape, a number picked instead of derived: a 24px button holding a 25px line box, a 168px pill holding a 216px label, a third call site reading a scroll-local rect as a window position, and three demos asserting byte-identity of a framebuffer -- which is a claim about the rasteriser, and the software Vulkan CI runs on disagrees with itself by one least-significant bit of coverage. Measured rather than assumed: ten captures of one unchanged screen, GPU byte-identical, lavapipe 2 to 10 bytes apart and every one of them off by exactly 1. So frame equality is now judged on per-channel MAGNITUDE against a tolerance the run measures, which is 0 on a deterministic host and therefore byte-identity unchanged.

verification_bullets: The repair is proved by DRIVING, not by reading. Before it, `scene/click {at}` on a message row left `selected_row` at 6; after it, 6 -> 1. The same target driven with `scene/invoke` moved the screen in BOTH builds, which is exactly why eleven integration tests, a 160-assertion demo and a boot gate all passed on a window where nothing a person pressed did anything.

All eleven of the CI sweep's failures reproduce and pass locally. Four reproduce here directly (r1478_endpoint_identity, todomvc_r665, todomvc_r666, r682_dirty_subtree_cache -- the containment budgets, measured on the empty list and paid by every state with rows in it); r760_fab reproduces with a different sample than CI's, which is itself the finding, because the sample point was a fixed inset rather than a derived one. Three more (r1520_scrolled_paint_cache, r1527_fragment_trace, r1531_glyph_runs_replayed) reproduce only under lavapipe, the software Vulkan the sweep runs on, and the reproduction is what identified them: ten consecutive captures of ONE unchanged screen differ under lavapipe in 2 to 10 bytes of 768,000 and are byte-identical on this host's GPU -- so the assertion was measuring the rasteriser. Every differing byte differs by exactly 1, which is why the replacement predicate is per-channel magnitude and not a count: a count drifts run to run (a floor sampled at 4 rejected a real replay that noised at 6) while a positional error swaps ink for background and moves a channel by tens or hundreds. The repair walks the same join from the STATE side, where the thing that needs repairing has a name: `externals` pairs every tagged `External` with the shallowest painted tag that routes a press to it, and `is_dead_to_a_pointer` is DERIVED from that list rather than stored beside it. THE SCE DELTA HAS NO CONSUMER SURFACE, and that is measured: the diff over `sce-rust-runtime`, the crate this tree links at runtime, is EMPTY across all ten commits, and `sce-build/src` adds no new `pub` item at all. What did change is the diagnostic schema, which gained two codes -- and R1657's lesson is that a claim about another project's shape can become false with nothing changing on this side, so the answer is the test that round built rather than a paragraph: `mirrors_every_field_the_sce_record_carries` destructures a real `sce-build` diagnostic WITHOUT a rest pattern, so an upstream field addition is a compile error, and it passes. THE MNEMOSYNE BUMP IS WHERE THE RISK IS, three hundred rounds of another project's development arriving at once, so it is checked through the gates it moves rather than through its changelog: the hook resolver verifies the new pin under R1507's provenance order and R1508's revision-purity and clean-worktree requirements, `tools/test_hooks.sh` passes 118 assertions against the build it resolved, and `validate-workspace` is green at T1 orphan 0 and T3 reject 0. It is also now running checks the old pin did not have -- citation-gate coverage over 1,019 scanned Rust sources, exclusion integrity over 7,700 excluded files, and the record, VCS and numbering-origin axes -- all at zero findings, which is the honest reading of a jump this size: more is being asked of this workspace than before and it answers. AND THE BUMP MOVED THE CLI THIS PROJECT'S OWN WORKFLOW RUNS: `append-changelog-entry` now takes `--decision-file <path>` where it took `--decision <text>`, which is how this round found out -- the first invocation was refused by name. That is a strict improvement here rather than a cost, because inline text is exactly the shape R1569.1 lost three identifiers to when bash command-substituted the backticks inside a `--decision "..."` argument; a path cannot be substituted. The SEED workaround for that trap is now the tool's only interface. ★AND THE BUMP FOUND A DEFECT IN THE HOOKS THEMSELVES, which is where this round's content actually is. The commit was refused with `cannot produce the pinned build 183a17a` while the submodule was present, at the pin, clean, and its binary rebuilt and answering that revision -- and the same resolver run from a shell returned 0 and chose that very binary. `git commit` exports `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` to its hooks, those variables OUTRANK `-C`, so every `git -C vendor/mnemosyne ...` in the resolver was reading the PARENT repository and the submodule checks were answering about the wrong repo. It survived 150 rounds because the vendored branch had never run inside a hook: an installed build at `$MN_ROOT/<pin>` existed for every pin this tree had used and the resolver prefers it, so moving to a revision with no installed build took the fallback for the first time. A fallback nobody has exercised is a fallback nobody has tested, and this is the branch whose whole purpose is to work when the installed build is absent -- a fresh clone. Fixed by scrubbing the inherited git environment for those three calls, and tested under exactly the environment a hook gets; the two existing cases beside the new ones pass with and without the fix, which is why they could not have caught it.

R1666.decision_summary: The citation gate's own claim gets the resolver it requires, and the pin bump turns out not to be revertible. R1665 verified its Mnemosyne bump through `validate-workspace` and the hook resolver and called that covering the pin; `pre-push` also runs `validate-code-refs`, which is a DIFFERENT command, and it was never run. It refused: the new build carries that project's R1144 rule -- a run stops when citations carry a symbol-level binding and no configured resolver covers them, because `severity_binding` then reads as symbol-level enforcement while the run performs none.
