R1667.decision_summary: The read channel says why it refused, and the matcher stops deciding validity on every family's behalf. `ExternalIntrospect::query` answered `Option<IntrospectValue>`, so the transport turned every `None` into one word: `no such name`, `the family is right and index 999 is not`, `the argument is not an integer`, and `this instance holds no state to read from` reached a client as byte-identical `-32602 UnknownIntrospectPath`. The surface knew which of the four it meant -- its own `parse` and bounds check are what produced the `None` -- and had no way to say so. The write channel never had that problem: `InterveneError` has said UnknownPath / TypeMismatch / ReadOnly / OutOfRange since R51, and R1565 gave the last of those the producer's own sentence. `dispatch::query_error_reason` even carried the comment that documented the gap -- "a READ cannot be refused by a producer: `query` answers `Option`, so every failure here is the transport's own classification". ★TWO ROOTS, BOTH CLOSED, AND THE SHALLOW ONE IS AN INCONSISTENCY THE DOC ALREADY DESCRIBED. `SchemaField::addresses` says it answers "does this field own this path" and "deliberately checks that an argument is present, not that it is well-formed" -- then made exactly one exception, requiring a NON-EMPTY run in each placeholder. Emptiness is a property of the argument, not of the address, so `width.zzz` was owned-and-malformed while `width.` was not owned at all: two malformed probes judged along different axes. The exception was not load-bearing for the parse -- matching is greedy-to-the-next-literal and stays deterministic with empty runs (`cell..2` has exactly one reading) -- so what it actually did was decide, for all 106 declared families at once, that none may have a meaningful empty member, while `SchemaArg` exists precisely so a family can state its own argument's domain. A consumer publishing `find.` as "a search for nothing" was told its own declared family had no such address. ★THE DEEP ONE IS THE SIGNATURE. `query` now answers `Result<IntrospectValue, ReadRefusal>` with four arms -- `UnknownPath`, `NoSuchMember(RefusalReason)`, `QueryTypeMismatch`, `Unavailable(RefusalReason)` -- and `QuerySource::introspect_query` moved with it, because widening only the `QueryOnlyIntrospect` adapter would have forced the adapter to INVENT a reason, which is the same defect wearing the fix's clothes. The two reason-carrying arms ride their own codes (`-32007 NO_SUCH_MEMBER`, `-32008 READ_UNAVAILABLE`) on the rule the other two channels already follow and `rpc/errors` already publishes: `-32602` carries a word from this crate's closed vocabulary, and an application code carries free application text. What a client gains is not detail but opposite INSTRUCTIONS -- `-32602 UnknownIntrospectPath` means stop asking, that name is not on this surface; `-32007` means the name is right, read the family's count path and ask again. ★★THE FOURTH ARM IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A TASTE CALL. `text_field`'s doc has promised since R56.1.f.3 that a client could "distinguish no state bound from no selection", and both were `None`; the test that asserts it is named `r903_find_surface_on_bare_field_is_inert_not_unknown` and the wire answered exactly `UnknownIntrospectPath`. A declared path that this instance cannot answer is neither a bad name nor a bad argument, and folding it into `NoSuchMember` would have rebuilt the collapse this round exists to remove. ★★AND THE MIGRATION IS TYPE-CHECKED, WHICH IS WHAT MADE IT SAFE TO DRIVE MECHANICALLY: `Option<T>` and `Result<T, E>` are different types, so every mis-edit is a compile error rather than a silent behaviour change -- 552 in `pinion-core` alone, each one a site where the old collapse had been invisible to a reader. 134 impls across 112 files, plus the `#[widget]` derive's read-state walk. 36 tests then failed on SEMANTICS, and every one was a place where two facts had shared an answer; each was re-stated on the variant rather than on the sentence, because the variant is the contract a client branches on while the sentence is the surface's own prose.

`pinion-core::external::SchemaField::addresses` — the `arg_len == 0` rejection is deleted: emptiness is well-formedness, and well-formedness is the `query` impl's call
`pinion-rpc::query` — `QueryError::Refused(ReadRefusal)` plus `From<ReadRefusal>`, which keeps a surface's `UnknownPath` on the transport's existing word so no synonym enters the wire vocabulary

`pinion-rpc::dispatch` — `NO_SUCH_MEMBER` (-32007) and `READ_UNAVAILABLE` (-32008), both published in `rpc/errors` with the caller's next move stated; `QueryTypeMismatch` added to the closed -32602 vocabulary
134 `query` impls across 112 files migrated, each stating which of the four refusals it meant; 18 bounds checks now name the range they refused against
`pinion-derive::widget` — the read-state walk matches `Ok(..)`; it folds every refusal alike on purpose, being a paint path rather than a wire one

R1668.decision_summary:
R1668 gave the disabled cascade a reason that is a value, and gave the analysis
tool's screen C the specification and the paint gate its two sibling screens
have had since R1651 and R1663.

The floor was measured by BUILDING AND RUNNING the reference toolkit at 6.11
rather than read: a bool on a widget, a bool on an action, a bool on a quick
item, one flag bit on a model item; assistive technology receives one bit of
fifty-one, whose own source comment records that it used to be called
`unavailable`; `isEnabledTo` answers 1 for both candidate ancestors because it
asks about a segment rather than naming the culprit; and the only slots that
could carry a reason are free-form prose that nothing classifies and nothing
links to the disabled state. On an action that slot defaults to the action's
own label, so an author who writes a reason into it loses the name. The
question that costs most has no answer there: a feature booked for an unshipped
release and a feature this build will never have are the same bool.

`pinion_core::availability::Unavailable` is that reason, on the declaration the
R1554 cascade already inherits: six kinds and one detail whose meaning the kind
fixes, with the recourse DERIVED once rather than restated per site. The
cascade hands the DECLARING node's reason to every node in its region, so a
control deep inside a reserved panel answers without a walk; a node's own reason
beats the region's, because re-enabling the region would leave it inert for that
reason and no other. `scene/disabled` publishes the kind, the detail and the
recourse, both vocabularies pinned in the wire census and proven ON THE WIRE to
be ones their own reader accepts. The accessibility tree lowers the reason to
the node's state description, so a listener hears why rather than "dimmed".

The forcing consumer is screen C, whose reference is emphatic that a later
release's widgets are shown LOCKED rather than hidden. `spec.rs` writes that
screen down as a value -- four widgets this release places, nine it reserves
each naming its requirement, the rail's two locked seats, and the body every
placed card is specified to have -- and `painted.rs` runs the real pipeline over
21 (state, size) cases checking forward, backward, reachable, contained,
disjoint and the round's own reserved law.

The cascade change closed a hole nobody had looked for: the census carried the
declarer's TAG down as its only inheritance, so an untagged declaring container
handed its children nothing and they were omitted -- while the cascade had faded
them and the hit test refused to descend -- and the accessibility assembler
marks a node disabled iff the census names it. Those controls were painted
inert, unreachable by pointer, and announced live.

Seven defects were found by the gates rather than by reading: nine reserved rows
painted their names under the badge; a one-cell card underflowed a column width
to four billion; the byte pane was fixed-width on a card narrower than the pane;
filter chips and stat tiles ran off the card; a decode row lost its KEY and kept
its value, and a map row lost its resource path, both because the identifying
half was allocated last; and the drag preview promised a cell the release did
not take, because `TileGrid::move_to` clamped one way and the shell clamped
another. That last is one fact with two clamps -- R1654's shape -- and it is
closed by giving the grid `landing()` and writing `move_to` in terms of it.

Two counterfactuals PASSED before they caught, and both were findings. The row
clamps were never exercised, because no swept state had ever been small enough;
a shrunk-card state now is. And the row check compared a SET rather than
positions, so reversing a row's four columns passed it -- a value in the wrong
column is exactly what a reproduction claim has to exclude. 14 of 14 caught
after both repairs.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::availability` — `Unavailable` (a kind plus one detail the kind gives meaning to), `UnavailableKind` (6 arms), `Recourse` (5, DERIVED from the kind), and two wire-name arrays derived from the arms so a published vocabulary cannot lag the enum

`pinion-core::style::LayoutStyle` — the disabled declaration is now `unavailable: Option<Unavailable>` with its derivation `resolved_unavailable`, so the reason travels WITH the cascade rather than beside it; `with_disabled(true)` still states the fact without a reason and lands on the `Unstated` arm, which is a thing a census counts rather than a silence

`pinion-core::scene_disabled` — the cascade hands the DECLARING node's reason to every node in its region; a self-declared node keeps its own, because re-enabling the region would leave it inert for that reason; `DisabledNode::reason` joins the census. An untagged declaring container now puts its region in the census, and did not before — the accessibility assembler marks a node disabled iff the census names it, so those controls were painted inert, unreachable by pointer, and announced live

`pinion-rpc::disabled` — `scene/disabled` rows carry `reason`, `detail` and a derived `recourse`, with both closed vocabularies pinned in the wire census through `accepting(..)` and proven on the wire to be ones their own reader accepts

`pinion-a11y` — `AccessNode::unavailable` lowers to the accessibility layer's STATE DESCRIPTION, so a listener hears why rather than "dimmed"; a widget disabled by its own state gets no invented reason, because the scene does not know why it did that

`pinion-core::widgets::tile_grid::landing` — where a tile asked to move would actually land, answered rather than restated; `move_to` is written in terms of it, so a drag preview and the release that follows it cannot disagree

R1668.publishable_decision_summary:
R1668 gave the disabled cascade a reason that is a value, and gave the analysis
tool's screen C the specification and the paint gate its two sibling screens
have had since R1651 and R1663.

The floor was measured by BUILDING AND RUNNING the reference toolkit at 6.11
rather than read: a bool on a widget, a bool on an action, a bool on a quick
item, one flag bit on a model item; assistive technology receives one bit of
fifty-one, whose own source comment records that it used to be called
`unavailable`; `isEnabledTo` answers 1 for both candidate ancestors because it
asks about a segment rather than naming the culprit; and the only slots that
could carry a reason are free-form prose that nothing classifies and nothing
links to the disabled state. On an action that slot defaults to the action's
own label, so an author who writes a reason into it loses the name. The
question that costs most has no answer there: a feature booked for an unshipped
release and a feature this build will never have are the same bool.

`pinion_core::availability::Unavailable` is that reason, on the declaration the
R1554 cascade already inherits: six kinds and one detail whose meaning the kind
fixes, with the recourse DERIVED once rather than restated per site. The
cascade hands the DECLARING node's reason to every node in its region, so a
control deep inside a reserved panel answers without a walk; a node's own reason
beats the region's, because re-enabling the region would leave it inert for that
reason and no other. `scene/disabled` publishes the kind, the detail and the
recourse, both vocabularies pinned in the wire census and proven ON THE WIRE to
be ones their own reader accepts. The accessibility tree lowers the reason to
the node's state description, so a listener hears why rather than "dimmed".

The forcing consumer is screen C, whose reference is emphatic that a later
release's widgets are shown LOCKED rather than hidden. `spec.rs` writes that
screen down as a value -- four widgets this release places, nine it reserves
each naming its requirement, the rail's two locked seats, and the body every
placed card is specified to have -- and `painted.rs` runs the real pipeline over
21 (state, size) cases checking forward, backward, reachable, contained,
disjoint and the round's own reserved law.

The cascade change closed a hole nobody had looked for: the census carried the
declarer's TAG down as its only inheritance, so an untagged declaring container
handed its children nothing and they were omitted -- while the cascade had faded
them and the hit test refused to descend -- and the accessibility assembler
marks a node disabled iff the census names it. Those controls were painted
inert, unreachable by pointer, and announced live.

Seven defects were found by the gates rather than by reading: nine reserved rows
painted their names under the badge; a one-cell card underflowed a column width
to four billion; the byte pane was fixed-width on a card narrower than the pane;
filter chips and stat tiles ran off the card; a decode row lost its KEY and kept
its value, and a map row lost its resource path, both because the identifying
half was allocated last; and the drag preview promised a cell the release did
not take, because `TileGrid::move_to` clamped one way and the shell clamped
another. That last is one fact with two clamps -- R1654's shape -- and it is
closed by giving the grid `landing()` and writing `move_to` in terms of it.

Two counterfactuals PASSED before they caught, and both were findings. The row
clamps were never exercised, because no swept state had ever been small enough;
a shrunk-card state now is. And the row check compared a SET rather than
positions, so reversing a row's four columns passed it -- a value in the wrong
column is exactly what a reproduction claim has to exclude. 14 of 14 caught
after both repairs.

R1669.decision_summary:
R1669 paid the three debts R1668 registered, and paying them found a card that
could not hold its own specification.

★THE SECOND DEBT'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, AND THE ROUND THAT WROTE IT WAS MINE.
It recorded 23 reasonless `with_disabled` declarations. A parse that asks
whether each hit sits inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module answers: production 1,
test fixtures 18, prose 3, and the builder's own definition 1. The raw grep
count had been taken for the population -- the census-over-text failure this
project has recorded four times before, committed this time by the round-close
note itself.

The one real site is the group box, and its reason was knowable and specific:
the panel is inert because the group's own title checkbox is off. That is a
`Precondition` whose recourse derives to `Satisfy` -- the condition is in reach
of the person reading the greyed panel, and it is one tick away. The detail
names it with the mnemonic marker resolved, so the sentence a listener hears is
the word painted in the frame.

The other half of that debt was that nobody counts, and the answer is a boot
gate reading `scene/disabled` on the RUNNING screen rather than a source scan --
because a source scan is what had just been wrong. Its floor is zero for every
surface and its exception list is empty, which is affordable precisely because
the population was one. ★And the gate had no negative control: blinding it
changed nothing, because every surface in the tree is at zero and a gate with
nothing to fire on is a gate nobody has tested.

★★THE CLAMP DEBT IS THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING. A test cannot ask whether a
branch was taken. It can ask whether the OUTCOME that branch exists to produce
was observed -- a body painting fewer rows than the specification gives it --
and whether the other outcome was observed too, so that "always clamped" cannot
pass as coverage either. Asking that over a spec-derived population found two
things on its first run:

  - the filter card's chips have one cell, so their clamped side does not exist,
    and the exemption is DERIVED (a row with fewer than two cells cannot lose
    one and remain a row) rather than named;
  - the identifier-map card's rows were NEVER ONCE seen complete. At one grid
    row its body is 140px and its specified header plus seven rows need 144, so
    the card could not show what the specification says it holds -- at any
    window size, in every state -- while the painter clamped correctly and the
    screen was quietly a row short.

The third debt closed and its counterfactual PASSED, which found a second
self-reference. Screen A's rail seats now carry `Some(requirement)` instead of a
bare bool and are declared through the availability channel, but the painted
gate and the demo BOTH read the booking out of `spec` and compare it to the
screen -- so changing the specification changed both sides and neither noticed.
A check that compares a thing to itself is not a check; the shape is now pinned
where the specification cannot move it.

★And one repair came from outside the debts: growing the filter card made the
containment gate report the sparkline's own line 3px outside its own rect. Its
inset accounted for the marker radius and not for the stroke, which is drawn
centred on a point and hangs outside it -- and a JOIN reaches further still, by
an amount that depends on the angle. Measured: half the stroke took it to 1px
and the full width took it to none.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::style::LayoutStyle::with_availability` — declare availability from an `Option`, the branchless peer of `with_unavailable`; a caller whose widget is conditionally unavailable computes one value instead of branching between two builders, which is where a "live" branch loses a declaration the other branch has

`pinion-widget-paint::group_box` — the one production declaration in the tree that stated no reason now states one: `Precondition("<title> is turned on")`, with the mnemonic marker resolved so the sentence a listener hears is the word painted in the frame

`tools/rpc_verify::_gate_stated_reasons` — a boot gate over `scene/disabled`: every inert region on the opening screen says why. Floor zero for every surface, exception list empty, and measured on the RUNNING screen rather than by a source scan

`tools/test_rpc_verify.py` — that gate's negative control, which a counterfactual proved was missing: a synthetic silent region must fail, a stated one must not, and an exception must make it adoptable

`examples/hello-analyzer-shell/src/painted.rs` — `r1669_the_sweep_reaches_both_sides_of_every_clamp`: for every observable a clamp exists to produce, the sweep must have seen both the clamped form and the full one. Population derived from `spec`; the one-cell exemption derived rather than named
`examples/hello-analyzer-shell/src/spec.rs` — the identifier map and the filter card are two grid rows tall, because at one the map's body is 140px and its own specified content needs 144

`examples/hello-node-lab/src/spec.rs` — the rail's locked seats carry `Some(requirement)` instead of `true`, and the painter declares them through the availability channel; `spec.rail` publishes `reserved_for`
`examples/hello-node-lab/src/tests.rs` — the booking's SHAPE is pinned (`requirement <number>`), which is the half the specification cannot move on its own
`pinion-chart::sparkline` — the geometry insets by the polyline's stroke as well as the marker radius, so a mark's ink stays inside the rect it was handed
verification_bullets: Local: `cargo test` green on pinion-core, pinion-chart, pinion-widget-paint, hello-analyzer-shell, hello-node-lab, hello-group-box and hello-stat-tiles; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all` clean

Four demos re-run against the rebuilt binaries: the group box's, screen A's, screen C's and screen B's, all PASS, with the new `[stated-reason]` line reporting `0 silent` and kinds `['reserved']` on both analyzer screens
`python3 tools/test_rpc_verify.py` — 28 cases, 71 assertions, including the new gate's negative control

Counterfactual 7/7 CAUGHT from a verified-green baseline, under a gate that runs the Rust suites AND the harness tests AND two demos, because three of the seven break something no `cargo test` can see
carry_forward_bullets: The clamp-coverage gate lives in screen C's painted module only. Screens A and B carry clamps of their own and nothing asks the question there -- and asking it on screen C found a real defect on its first run, so the hit rate is known to be high. Registered rather than lifted: one consumer is not three.

The sparkline is now the only chart mark with a rule about its own ink. Every other stroked mark still relies on its consumer's box happening to have room, which is exactly the state the sparkline was in until a card grew.

R1670.decision_summary:
R1670 is a stop-the-line clearance: the demo sweep had been red for two runs and
this round pays off all five of its failures.

★FOUR OF THE FIVE WERE R1667'S OWN. That round split the read channel's
collapsed refusal into four arms carrying two new codes, repaired the 36 Rust
tests that failed on the semantics, and left four demos asserting the old word.
A demo is Python; the sweep runs only in CI; and R1667 pushed on red, so the
signal took a whole round to arrive.

THE HARNESS HAD NO VOCABULARY FOR THE NEW ARMS, which is why nobody reading
those demos could have migrated them. `assert_action_refused` and
`assert_out_of_range` existed for the write channel's two prose-carrying codes;
the read channel's two had no peer, so a demo that wanted to say "the name is
right and the index is not" had no way to say it and went on asserting the
collapsed answer. `assert_no_such_member` and `assert_read_unavailable` are that
peer, with the body lifted at the fourth and fifth copy.

★★THE MIRROR MOVES TO WHERE A ROUND CAN SEE IT. `tools/rpc_verify.py`'s
`PROSE_DATA_CODES` mirrors the catalogue's `data_is_prose`, and the only thing
comparing them lived in a DEMO. This class has now bitten three times — R1564
and R1565 each learned about the drift from a red `main`, and R1667 from a sweep
that had been red the whole time. It is now a `pinion-rpc` unit test that reads
the harness source and compares the sets BY NAME, so a constant renamed with a
stale number cannot pass either. A code added to one side and not the other now
fails a gate every round already runs.

★THE FIFTH WAS OLDER, AND THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S CLAIM WAS TEN OF ELEVEN.
`r760_fab` was failing in the run before this one too, so the round that
reported the sweep's eleven paid off had paid off ten. Its cause is a constant
probing a derived geometry: twelve pixels in from each FAB's left edge, with a
comment saying that was clear of the centred icon. Measured, on the 40px FAB the
flat run of the declared accent is 15px wide and the icon's ink begins at 16 —
three pixels of margin, so whether a glyph's antialiased edge reaches the sample
depends on the rasteriser. It passed on a real GPU and on lavapipe here and
failed on the runner's, twice.

The repair measures instead of guessing: scan the row, take the widest run of
the fill the SCENE declares, assert it is wide enough to be an interior, and
read its centre. ★A FRACTION OF THE WIDTH WAS THE SAME MISTAKE IN THE OTHER
DIRECTION — the extended FAB carries a label across its middle, so it has less
clear interior than the small one despite being six times wider, and this
round's first draft demanded 31px of it and got 19. Two other demos sampled a
constant inset the same way; three consumers is the rule, so the scan is lifted
into the harness and all three adopt it.

★AND THE HELPER'S OWN COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED, TWICE. Removing the width floor
and taking the first run instead of the widest both left every demo green,
because the tree is painted correctly and a helper with nothing to fail on is a
helper nobody has tested. R1669 recorded that exact lesson about a different
gate one round earlier and this round repeated it, which is why the note now
lives in the harness test rather than in a memory file.

Also repaired, found while probing: the two-dimensional out-of-range sentence
read `cell 10000.0 is outside 0..10000.0..3` — one range with three dots in it —
in all three grid surfaces that emit it. The arm carries prose so a client can
act on it, and that sentence is not actionable.
changes_bullets: `tools/rpc_verify.py` — `NO_SUCH_MEMBER` / `READ_UNAVAILABLE` join the harness's code constants, `PROSE_DATA_CODES` and `_PROSE_HELPER`; `assert_no_such_member` / `assert_read_unavailable` are the read channel's peers of `assert_action_refused`, with the shared body lifted at the fourth copy

`pinion-rpc::errors` — `r1670_the_demo_harness_mirrors_this_catalogues_prose_flag`: the mirror that had lived only in a demo now runs in `cargo test`, comparing the sets by NAME so a renamed constant with a stale number cannot pass

`tools/rpc_verify.py::widest_flat_run` / `assert_interior_is` — an interior is a MEASURED run of the fill the scene declares, not a hand-picked pixel; adopted by `r760_fab`, `r735_table_multi` and `r787_file_browser`

`tools/test_rpc_verify.py` — that helper's negative control, which two counterfactuals proved was missing: a wrong fill has no run, a 3px run is not an interior, and the widest run is taken rather than the first

`tools/demos/r1441_brandes_koepf.py`, `r1525_paints_its_model.py`, `r1597_a_frame_holds_what_it_was_given.py` — migrated onto the arm R1667 split out, each asserting the id or the bounds the refusal now names rather than the collapsed variant word
`pinion-core::widgets::{table, grid_sort, row_search}` — the two-dimensional out-of-range sentence names its dimensions separately (`rows 0..N x columns 0..M`) instead of running them together
verification_bullets: All five demos the sweep named reproduce locally before the repair and pass after it; `r760_fab` verified on BOTH rasterisers available here (a real GPU and lavapipe), which is what its failure mode demanded

Local: `cargo test -p pinion-core -p pinion-rpc` green; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all` clean; `python3 tools/test_rpc_verify.py` 29 cases / 77 assertions
Seven demos re-run against rebuilt release binaries: the five the sweep named plus the two that adopted the lifted helper
Counterfactual 6/6 CAUGHT from a verified-green baseline, after the two that PASSED were closed by giving the new helper its own negative control

The full 575-demo sweep was handed to a build machine (32 cores, 110 GB available) rather than run here: this host had 12 GB available against this repository's declared 16 GB floor, at load 10.9. Sent as tracked files plus submodule worktrees, proven identical by `rev-parse HEAD` and `status --short` on both sides, and judged by an exit sentinel
carry_forward_bullets: The mirror now catches a code added on one side and not the other. It does not catch the SECOND half of what R1667 hit: three demos asserting a refusal that has since moved arms. The lifted interior helper has three consumers and there are 61 demos that sample pixels. R1671.decision_summary:
R1671 is three defects a person found by looking at the window, and the reason
every gate this session wrote had missed all three.

★★THE SCREEN DID NOT FILL THE WINDOW. Every rectangle on screen C was authored
against the design constants, so a maximised window got a 1440x900 picture in
the corner. Screens A and B have read the live size since R1654; this one never
did. The sweep already laid the screen out at a maximised size and passed —
because every check compares the screen to ITSELF (is this mark inside its pane,
do these rows overlap), and all of that stays true when the whole screen ignores
the window. R1654 wrote that sentence about screen A; screen C had the sizes in
its sweep and no check that compared the paint to the WINDOW.

★★THEN THE GESTURE DID NOT FOLLOW. With the paint responsive, a person reported
that clicks stopped landing. Measured over the wire at 2494x1531: 20 of 24
probes resolved to the wrong control or to nothing, and a press at a painted
palette row was refused as "outside the 1440x900 shell". The cause is
structural: `window_size` read a channel that lives in the `Owner` scope a view
runs inside, and the `External` invoke path has no such scope, so the two halves
of one screen answered differently about how big it is. The file's own section
header already said "Geometry: ONE source, read by the paint and by the
gesture" — the RECTANGLES were one source and the SIZE they are computed from
was not.

The repair is one fact with two routes: `ShellState::surface`, written by
`External::on_resize`, read by the view as a tracked read (so it re-runs) and by
the invoke path through a `Weak` handle that needs no scope. No copy.

★THE HEADER STRIP SAT ON THE CARD'S OUTLINE. Measured: the card is
(68, 114, 614, 332) with a 1px `Inside` border and the strip was painted at
(68, 148, 614) — exactly the card's x and width, so its fill covered the border
columns. `scene/containment` reported nothing, and that is not a bug in the
report: it compares a mark against its owner's BOX, and a border is ink the box
owns inside that box. CSS has had border box versus content box from the
beginning; nothing here expresses the second one, which is now pinned in the
framework by a test that asserts today's answer and will go red on the round
that fixes it.

All three card bands are inset by the frame now, which is a rule rather than
three decisions — and the second report ("still eating the border") was the
band nobody had thought about, the size-stepper strip.

★★★AND THE ROUND'S OWN COUNTERFACTUALS FOUND THE DEEPEST THING: four of six
PASSED. The Rust sweep cannot see the resize defect at all, because it sets the
shell's size signal directly and so both halves read one value in-process; the
defect lived on the path that has no scope. The frame walk could not be shown to
work either, because with the screen repaired there is nothing crossing for a
weakened walk to miss. A gate that only ever runs against correct code cannot be
shown to work — three times in three rounds now, and this time the answer is
both halves: a WIRE section that resizes and presses, and a CONSTRUCTED crossing
the walk has to find.

`painted.rs::r1671_the_screen_fills_the_window_it_was_given` — the top-level panes' union must equal the window; the check the sweep did not have while it already swept three sizes

`painted.rs::r1671_the_frame_walk_finds_an_untagged_crossing` — that walk's own negative control, on a constructed scene
`r1668_every_painted_control_answers_for_itself` now runs at every size; the skip was the gate agreeing with the bug
`pinion-core::containment::tests::r1671_a_mark_over_its_owners_border_is_called_contained` — the framework gap, pinned where it lives rather than described in prose

Measured over the wire before and after: at 2494x1531, 20 of 24 painted controls resolved to the wrong control or to nothing; after, 3, and those 3 are the same 3 at BOTH sizes and are readouts whose parent card is the right answer

Nothing answers "which painted marks cover which" — `containment` is child-versus-owner, `reach` is mark-versus-window, and `pointer_reach`'s shadows are about the POINTER. R1672.decision_summary:
R1672 is one rule and what happened when three screens were finally asked it:
a box owns the border it strokes inside itself.

★★THE RULE. `containment::escapes` compared a mark against its owner's BOX, and
a border is ink the box owns INSIDE that box, so a child painted at the owner's
full width covered the outline and was reported contained. CSS has had border
box versus content box from the beginning and nothing here expressed the second
one. R1671 pinned that as a test asserting today's WRONG answer, with a doc
saying to rewrite it on the round that gave the channel a content box; this is
that round and the test is the rewrite.

The inset is a `match` over EVERY `BorderPlacement`, not a test for one of them,
and that is not decoration: the first draft asked `is it Inside` and returned
the box otherwise, which is right for `Outside` and WRONG for `Center` — a
centred stroke straddles the edge, so half its width is inside the box, and a
partially covered pixel is covered, so the inside half rounds up. A placement
added later is now a compile error rather than a silent fourth answer.

`content_rect` is PUBLIC because the placement side needs the same answer: a
caller computing the inset itself is a second copy of the rule, free to disagree
with the check that reports it.

★★ABSOLUTE PLACEMENT IGNORES PADDING, and that measurement changed the widget
repair from the one it looked like. The first pass gave `pinion_widget_paint`'s
config-form controls a padding equal to their own frame, re-measured, and found
the two stepper buttons of every integer row STILL standing on the outline: the
padding had moved the value text and nothing else, because a stepper is placed
at a PUBLISHED part rectangle and an absolutely-placed child is positioned
against its parent's border box. So `lay_parts` lays a shape's affordances in
the control's CONTENT rectangle; `control_frame(shape)` says how much that is
(two of six shapes put their parts inside a container that strokes
`control_skin`); `CONTROL_FRAME` is the width `control_skin` builds its border
FROM, so the declaration and the paint are one number by construction; and the
correspondence is asserted over every arm by reading the border width back out
of the painted scene, because a judgement about what a painter does goes wrong
silently and a shape that gained a skin would start painting its own parts over
its own outline with every test still green. In the crate, so every consumer
followed. Screen A's `OUTLINE_ALLOWANCE`, which named the two remaining owners,
is DELETED: an exception mechanism holding the empty set is a place for the next
escape to be filed instead of fixed.

★★★THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED. Screen B holds a
byte-identical copy of the ink metric and never calls the check with it; screen
C has neither. So putting screen B's three scrolling panes back over the
outlines of the panels holding them was caught by NOTHING, while the same break
on screen A was caught immediately. Three mechanical copies of one rule is the
immediate-lift case, and the hazard was never the duplication — it was that a
metric a screen owns but does not use is a vocabulary the screen cannot speak.

`pinion_core::test_fixtures::screen_ink` is that vocabulary: the stand-in (width
font-independent and conservative, height the laid-out line box, because
deciding the vertical against a constant would make the gate a fact about the
host's font database), the off-window split, the assertion — with four negative
controls of its own. All three screens ask now.

★★WHAT THE TWO NEW ASKERS FOUND, none of it visible to anything they already
ran. Screen B: the three panes over their panels' outlines that the previous
pass had repaired blind, now with a gate that would have reported them. Screen
C: five classes of defect, in five different swept states, reported one state at
a time because the gate stops at the first — 32 marks as the screen opens, then
13, then 9 with a card selected, then 1 with the preset menu open, then 25 with
every card shrunk to one cell.

  * Every run placed at an exact rectangle had NO overflow policy, so a label
    longer than its fixed box was painted past it rather than shortened — 32
    marks including four of the app bar's own. Screens A and B set `Ellipsis` on
    every run they place; this is the one screen of three that never did.
  * A code chip's word box was wider than the chip, at two sites, each from a
    separately picked inset. One rule written twice and got wrong twice.
  * A card reserved only its RESTING outline, so the moment it became the
    selected one and swapped its 1px outline for the 2px ring, its header and
    every row of its body stood on the ring's second pixel. The reservation is
    derived from the two widths now, and deliberately CONSTANT rather than a
    function of selection: a content rectangle that changed with the ring would
    move every row in the card when a person selects it.
  * A header too narrow for its own chrome computed a title width with
    `.max(40)` on the end and measured everything after it from that clamped
    number, so a card shrunk to one board cell painted `LIVE` 65px past its own
    frame. R1668's shape — one fact, two clamps, and the second arrives too late
    to be told. It gives way in a STATED order now (identity, then the
    affordance strip dropping from the LEFT so the last-declared control stays
    nearest the edge a hand reaches for, then the ready badge, then the title),
    and a part that does not fit is not painted. The sweep asserts BOTH sides of
    that branch: a give-way that never happens and one that never stops are the
    same to a one-sided check.

★★THE PRESET MENU IS A POPUP, not a child of the bar that opens it. It hung
81px below its parent, which is an escape and is also what a drop-down IS —
anchored, not bounded, which is why the reference toolkit at 6.11 makes a menu a
top-level popup. Moving it is not checkable by itself, and that is the trap this
session kept walking into: the paint and the hit test both read
`preset_item_rect`, so changing that function moves BOTH and no assertion
comparing them can notice. The shape is pinned against something that is not
itself — the chip: the first row hangs under it, the panel lines up with it, and
the menu stays inside the window.

★THE COUNTERFACTUAL DRIVER HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, found by trying to use it.
`--manifest-path` was not known to consume its value, so `cargo test
--manifest-path examples/<x>/Cargo.toml` — which in this repo IS a screen's
whole suite, every example being its own package — was refused as a test-name
filter. A screen's own gate therefore could not be a counterfactual gate at all,
and screens are where three of this round's breaks are visible. Fixed with a
named `VALUE_FLAGS` list, plus two cases in the driver's own tests. The list is
spelled out rather than inferred because a flag missing from it fails CLOSED.

The catalog axis was re-judged 97 -> 98 as the push gate demanded, and the point
goes to the disabled cascade R1668/R1669 closed rather than to this round's own
work: what R1671 and R1672 added is correctness over every bordered widget, not
catalogue breadth. Re-measured rather than recalled: `External::wheel` still has
exactly two widget implementors, and the four absent widget kinds are still
absent (`hello-paged-stream` is Model/View paging, `hello-app-font` loads a face
rather than picking one). Mnemonic adoption was NOT re-counted and is carried
forward as-is, because a number nobody re-derived is not evidence.
changes_bullets: `pinion_core::containment::content_rect` is public and `escapes` judges a mark against the owner's CONTENT rectangle; `border_inset` is a match over every `BorderPlacement`, so `Center` takes half the stroke (rounded up) and a new placement is a compile error

`pinion_core::test_fixtures::screen_ink` holds the ink gate three screens run — `stand_in_ink`, `ink_escapes`, `assert_contained_ink` — lifted from three mechanical copies, two of them in one file, with four negative controls of its own

`pinion_widget_paint::config_form` lays published part rectangles in the control's content box: `control_frame(shape)` names the inset, `CONTROL_FRAME` is the width `control_skin` builds its border from, and the correspondence is asserted over every `FieldType` arm from the painted scene
`pinion_widget_paint::pane::scroll_pane` honours the viewport's ORIGIN, not only its size, so a caller handing a pane its content rectangle gets a body in the right place
screen A: the launch chip's height and its word's seat are derived from the line box and the frame, and `OUTLINE_ALLOWANCE` is deleted — the exception set is empty
screen B: `r1672_every_painted_mark_is_inside_the_box_that_owns_it`, the check this screen held the metric for and never ran

screen C: the same gate plus `label` eliding, `code_chip` seating its word from the chip, `CARD_FRAME` derived from the widest frame a card draws, a header that gives way in a stated order with both sides of the branch asserted, and the preset menu as a top-level popup pinned against the chip that opens it
`tools/counterfactual.py` knows which `cargo test` flags consume their value, so an example package's whole suite is a legal gate; two cases in `tools/test_counterfactual.py`
verification_bullets: counterfactual 15/15 CAUGHT across four plans (5 crate, 2 screen A, 1 screen B, 7 screen C); CF-8 was a FINDING before the repair, and two cases were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing
`cargo test` green on pinion-core, pinion-widget-paint, pinion-rpc, pinion-shell and the four consumer examples (hello-node-lab, hello-packet-view, hello-analyzer-shell, todomvc)
`cargo clippy --all-targets` clean on every changed package under `-D pedantic`; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` clean
`tools/test_counterfactual.py` and `python3 tools/phase_b_tally.py --selftest` pass

R1672.publishable_decision_summary:
R1672 is one rule and what happened when three screens were finally asked it:
a box owns the border it strokes inside itself.

★★THE RULE. `containment::escapes` compared a mark against its owner's BOX, and
a border is ink the box owns INSIDE that box, so a child painted at the owner's
full width covered the outline and was reported contained. CSS has had border
box versus content box from the beginning and nothing here expressed the second
one. R1671 pinned that as a test asserting today's WRONG answer, with a doc
saying to rewrite it on the round that gave the channel a content box; this is
that round and the test is the rewrite.

The inset is a `match` over EVERY `BorderPlacement`, not a test for one of them,
and that is not decoration: the first draft asked `is it Inside` and returned
the box otherwise, which is right for `Outside` and WRONG for `Center` — a
centred stroke straddles the edge, so half its width is inside the box, and a
partially covered pixel is covered, so the inside half rounds up. A placement
added later is now a compile error rather than a silent fourth answer.

`content_rect` is PUBLIC because the placement side needs the same answer: a
caller computing the inset itself is a second copy of the rule, free to disagree
with the check that reports it.

★★ABSOLUTE PLACEMENT IGNORES PADDING, and that measurement changed the widget
repair from the one it looked like. The first pass gave `pinion_widget_paint`'s
config-form controls a padding equal to their own frame, re-measured, and found
the two stepper buttons of every integer row STILL standing on the outline: the
padding had moved the value text and nothing else, because a stepper is placed
at a PUBLISHED part rectangle and an absolutely-placed child is positioned
against its parent's border box. So `lay_parts` lays a shape's affordances in
the control's CONTENT rectangle; `control_frame(shape)` says how much that is
(two of six shapes put their parts inside a container that strokes
`control_skin`); `CONTROL_FRAME` is the width `control_skin` builds its border
FROM, so the declaration and the paint are one number by construction; and the
correspondence is asserted over every arm by reading the border width back out
of the painted scene, because a judgement about what a painter does goes wrong
silently and a shape that gained a skin would start painting its own parts over
its own outline with every test still green. In the crate, so every consumer
followed. Screen A's `OUTLINE_ALLOWANCE`, which named the two remaining owners,
is DELETED: an exception mechanism holding the empty set is a place for the next
escape to be filed instead of fixed.

★★★THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED. Screen B holds a
byte-identical copy of the ink metric and never calls the check with it; screen
C has neither. So putting screen B's three scrolling panes back over the
outlines of the panels holding them was caught by NOTHING, while the same break
on screen A was caught immediately. Three mechanical copies of one rule is the
immediate-lift case, and the hazard was never the duplication — it was that a
metric a screen owns but does not use is a vocabulary the screen cannot speak.

`pinion_core::test_fixtures::screen_ink` is that vocabulary: the stand-in (width
font-independent and conservative, height the laid-out line box, because
deciding the vertical against a constant would make the gate a fact about the
host's font database), the off-window split, the assertion — with four negative
controls of its own. All three screens ask now.

★★WHAT THE TWO NEW ASKERS FOUND, none of it visible to anything they already
ran. Screen B: the three panes over their panels' outlines that the previous
pass had repaired blind, now with a gate that would have reported them. Screen
C: five classes of defect, in five different swept states, reported one state at
a time because the gate stops at the first — 32 marks as the screen opens, then
13, then 9 with a card selected, then 1 with the preset menu open, then 25 with
every card shrunk to one cell.

  * Every run placed at an exact rectangle had NO overflow policy, so a label
    longer than its fixed box was painted past it rather than shortened — 32
    marks including four of the app bar's own. Screens A and B set `Ellipsis` on
    every run they place; this is the one screen of three that never did.
  * A code chip's word box was wider than the chip, at two sites, each from a
    separately picked inset. One rule written twice and got wrong twice.
  * A card reserved only its RESTING outline, so the moment it became the
    selected one and swapped its 1px outline for the 2px ring, its header and
    every row of its body stood on the ring's second pixel. The reservation is
    derived from the two widths now, and deliberately CONSTANT rather than a
    function of selection: a content rectangle that changed with the ring would
    move every row in the card when a person selects it.
  * A header too narrow for its own chrome computed a title width with
    `.max(40)` on the end and measured everything after it from that clamped
    number, so a card shrunk to one board cell painted `LIVE` 65px past its own
    frame. R1668's shape — one fact, two clamps, and the second arrives too late
    to be told. It gives way in a STATED order now (identity, then the
    affordance strip dropping from the LEFT so the last-declared control stays
    nearest the edge a hand reaches for, then the ready badge, then the title),
    and a part that does not fit is not painted. The sweep asserts BOTH sides of
    that branch: a give-way that never happens and one that never stops are the
    same to a one-sided check.

★★THE PRESET MENU IS A POPUP, not a child of the bar that opens it. It hung
81px below its parent, which is an escape and is also what a drop-down IS —
anchored, not bounded, which is why the reference toolkit at 6.11 makes a menu a
top-level popup. Moving it is not checkable by itself, and that is the trap this
session kept walking into: the paint and the hit test both read
`preset_item_rect`, so changing that function moves BOTH and no assertion
comparing them can notice. The shape is pinned against something that is not
itself — the chip: the first row hangs under it, the panel lines up with it, and
the menu stays inside the window.

★THE COUNTERFACTUAL DRIVER HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, found by trying to use it.
`--manifest-path` was not known to consume its value, so `cargo test
--manifest-path examples/<x>/Cargo.toml` — which in this repo IS a screen's
whole suite, every example being its own package — was refused as a test-name
filter. A screen's own gate therefore could not be a counterfactual gate at all,
and screens are where three of this round's breaks are visible. Fixed with a
named `VALUE_FLAGS` list, plus two cases in the driver's own tests. The list is
spelled out rather than inferred because a flag missing from it fails CLOSED.

The catalog axis was re-judged 97 -> 98 as the push gate demanded, and the point
goes to the disabled cascade R1668/R1669 closed rather than to this round's own
work: what R1671 and R1672 added is correctness over every bordered widget, not
catalogue breadth. Re-measured rather than recalled: `External::wheel` still has
exactly two widget implementors, and the four absent widget kinds are still
absent (`hello-paged-stream` is Model/View paging, `hello-app-font` loads a face
rather than picking one). Mnemonic adoption was NOT re-counted and is carried
forward as-is, because a number nobody re-derived is not evidence.
publishable_changes_bullets: `pinion_core::containment::content_rect` is public and `escapes` judges a mark against the owner's CONTENT rectangle; `border_inset` is a match over every `BorderPlacement`, so `Center` takes half the stroke (rounded up) and a new placement is a compile error

`pinion_core::test_fixtures::screen_ink` holds the ink gate three screens run — `stand_in_ink`, `ink_escapes`, `assert_contained_ink` — lifted from three mechanical copies, two of them in one file, with four negative controls of its own

`pinion_widget_paint::config_form` lays published part rectangles in the control's content box: `control_frame(shape)` names the inset, `CONTROL_FRAME` is the width `control_skin` builds its border from, and the correspondence is asserted over every `FieldType` arm from the painted scene
`pinion_widget_paint::pane::scroll_pane` honours the viewport's ORIGIN, not only its size, so a caller handing a pane its content rectangle gets a body in the right place
screen A: the launch chip's height and its word's seat are derived from the line box and the frame, and `OUTLINE_ALLOWANCE` is deleted — the exception set is empty
screen B: `r1672_every_painted_mark_is_inside_the_box_that_owns_it`, the check this screen held the metric for and never ran

screen C: the same gate plus `label` eliding, `code_chip` seating its word from the chip, `CARD_FRAME` derived from the widest frame a card draws, a header that gives way in a stated order with both sides of the branch asserted, and the preset menu as a top-level popup pinned against the chip that opens it
`tools/counterfactual.py` knows which `cargo test` flags consume their value, so an example package's whole suite is a legal gate; two cases in `tools/test_counterfactual.py`
publishable_verification_bullets: counterfactual 15/15 CAUGHT across four plans (5 crate, 2 screen A, 1 screen B, 7 screen C); CF-8 was a FINDING before the repair, and two cases were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing
`cargo test` green on pinion-core, pinion-widget-paint, pinion-rpc, pinion-shell and the four consumer examples (hello-node-lab, hello-packet-view, hello-analyzer-shell, todomvc)
`cargo clippy --all-targets` clean on every changed package under `-D pedantic`; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` clean
`tools/test_counterfactual.py` and `python3 tools/phase_b_tally.py --selftest` pass
the two ink ratchets were regenerated by `tools/measure_ink_budgets.py` under the R1660 font pin — the whole 224-surface census, because the producer refuses a partial run
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: mnemonic adoption on the catalog axis was not re-counted this round and is carried forward at four sites; a count nobody re-derived is not evidence, and the next re-judgment owes it a measurement

R1673.decision_summary:
R1673 pays off the backlog R1672's rule surfaced: 56 marks across seven
surfaces, all one class, plus the three the measurement then found underneath
them.

★★THE LIFT IS THE ROUND'S FIRST MOVE AND ITS COUNT IS THE ARGUMENT.
`containment::content_of(rect, Option<&Border>)` is the arithmetic half of
`content_rect`, for the side that is PLACING children and so has the border
before it has the node. Three screens had written the same `const fn
panel_content` by hand with the inset spelled `1`; the re-measurement then found
seven more surfaces owing the same repair. A rule with ten independent
implementations is ten chances for one of them to disagree with the check that
reports it — and here that check IS the other half, so the placement and the
judgement are now the same arithmetic, asserted as one answer.

★★WHAT THE 56 WERE, AND THAT THEY WERE ONE THING. Measured per surface rather
than assumed: a child laid at its owner's BOX where the owner strokes a border
inside it. `hello-property-grid` 29 (every row), `hello-node-editor` 10 (four
header strips and six ports), `hello-input-chip` 10, `hello-graph-diff` 6,
`hello-data-grid`, `hello-group-box`, `hello-inspector`. Seven repairs, each
derived rather than picked:

  * the property grid, the data grid and the group box RESERVE their frame as
    padding — the instrument that works for a FLOW child, and deliberately not
    the one R1672 needed for the config form's published part rectangles, where
    an absolutely-placed child ignores its parent's padding;
  * the node editor names its two border widths and reserves the WIDER
    constantly, so a card's header and every port keep their place when it is
    selected — the shape screen C's card took at R1672, arrived at again;
  * the inspector's object rows do the same for the cursor ring;
  * the graph-diff node's name is placed by the FLOW inside that reservation,
    because it had been authored as a rect in WINDOW coordinates on a text node
    whose container is already absolutely placed, and a `TextNode`'s rect is its
    box rather than its origin (R1653's lesson, one screen over);
  * the virtual table's load bar stops SHRINKING under its own fill. The track
    and the fill are absolutely placed at one origin so they overlay, and an
    absolutely-placed child does not shrink with its parent — so when the flex
    pass narrowed the cell, the fill kept the width it was sized from. The
    deficit goes to the label beside it (R1656's rule, applied where it was
    written to be applied), so no number in that function has to be right.

★★THE INPUT CHIP'S PADDING WAS TRANSPOSED, and the comment above it had said so
for rounds. `with_padding` takes `(x = left, y = top, w = right, h = bottom)`
and the call passed `(0, PAD, 0, PAD)` under a comment reading "horizontal
padding" — twelve pixels above and below the label and NONE beside it. The
containment rule is what made a stale comment into a failing measurement.

★★THE CHECK MARK IS A RELATION, NOT A TOKEN. `CheckboxStyle::box_size` and
`glyph_size_px` are two independent numbers that decide one thing between them
and nothing compared them, so three consumers put a 16-18px tick in a 14-16px
square where its shaped ink is 20-22 tall. The face is derived now: the declared
size, or the largest whose LINE BOX the square's CONTENT can hold — a ceiling,
so a generous square keeps what it asked for. Two findings came out of writing
it. The first draft INVERTED `line_box` by hand and the sweep caught it on its
first run: at three pixels of content the algebra said nothing fits while a 1px
face's line box is exactly three, so the answer steps down against the function
instead of solving a copy of it. And a square with no room for any tick now
answers NONE rather than a one-pixel mark on its own outline — the arm the sweep
also insists on reaching, because an untested `None` is how R1654's class
starts.

★★★THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING IS AGAIN A COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED, TWICE. With
the group box repaired, removing the frame reservation AND removing the title
band's knowledge of the checkbox it holds both left this crate's whole suite
GREEN: `pinion-widget-paint` had no test that a bordered painter's own content
stays inside its own frame, so only a CONSUMER booting could see it, one screen
at a time — the shape R1655 recorded for this same crate. The repair is that
test, and it uses the framework's own
`test_fixtures::screen_ink::assert_contained_ink`, the one three screens run, so
a widget and the screens holding it are judged by one rule rather than two that
can drift.

★AND IT FOUND A THIRD DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN, in the arm that has no checkbox
at all: the LEGEND overflowed the band by two pixels. Three independent tokens
decided the title band's height between them — `title_height`, the checkbox's
square, and the line box of the legend's face — and nobody had compared any
pair. It is the max of all three now, which is the argument for deriving from a
list rather than from the one member somebody happened to be looking at.

★THE PROPERTY GRID SCROLLS. Its one remaining escape was not a slip and is not
budgeted away: the grid is 1,160px in an 820px window, so 402px of it were
painted where nobody can see them while `scene/pointer_reach` reported fourteen
widgets a person cannot press. A property grid with more rows than window has a
scroll region, and the framework has had one since R55.G.4. Measured after:
containment 0, and `scene/scroll_reach` answers 64 marks reachable by scrolling
with ZERO lost.
changes_bullets: `pinion_core::containment::content_of(rect, Option<&Border>)` is public and `content_rect` is written in terms of it, so the placing half and the judging half are one arithmetic; the three screens' hand-written `panel_content` now call it

`pinion_widget_paint::checkbox` derives the tick's face from the square's content box — a ceiling, stepped down against `line_box` rather than solved by inverting it, and `None` when no tick fits at all

`pinion_widget_paint::group_box` reserves its frame for the content region, derives its title band from the tallest thing in it (token, checkbox, legend line box), and asserts its own containment through `test_fixtures::screen_ink`

seven example painters lay their children in the content box: the property grid, the node editor (both border widths named, the wider reserved constantly), the inspector's cursor ring, the graph-diff node name, the input chip's transposed padding, the data grid's viewport frame
`hello-virtual-table`'s load bar no longer shrinks under its own absolutely-placed fill; the label beside it absorbs the deficit
`hello-property-grid` scrolls: 402px painted below the window and 14 unpressable widgets become 64 marks reachable by scrolling, none lost
`hello-property-grid`'s popup follows the scroll it now sits beside — written the moment the scroll landed, because a row's position had two derivations and only the scene's folds the offset
verification_bullets: the ink ratchet re-measured across all 224 surfaces under the R1660 font pin, by its producer: every one of the seven repaired surfaces reports 0

counterfactual 6/6 CAUGHT on the two crates after TWO were findings (the group box's frame reservation and its title band were both invisible to this crate's whole suite) and three were re-authored because their first form did not compile

`cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` green on pinion-core, pinion-widget-paint and the thirteen consumer examples this round touched; `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo doc --workspace` clean
the three analysis-tool screen demos re-pass unchanged, which is what says the lifted `content_of` did not move a pixel they assert
the ratchet moved 113 -> 30 across the census, eight surfaces to zero, and no surface rose
carry_forward_bullets: the boot ratchet is what guards the seven repaired example painters; only three screens in the tree run the multi-state ink sweep in Rust, which is the coverage gap this round did not close

R1674.decision_summary:
A box declares where its own chrome ends, and every painter in the crate that
strokes a border is asked whether it keeps its own contents inside it.

THE GAP WAS MEASURED. A scratchpad probe built against the reference toolkit at
6.11 and run offscreen reports content margins of `3,23,3,3` for a titled group
box there against a plain framed widget's `2,2,2,2` -- the caption band
INCLUDED -- while `containment::content_rect` subtracted only the border. The
rectangle was parity; the band was a gap the scene had no vocabulary to express.

`style::Chrome` is that vocabulary: an edge, an extent, and a ROLE from a closed
six-arm set, each arm naming a strip something in this tree actually paints. The
role is the half the floor cannot carry, and that is measured rather than
argued: probed there, a custom-painted widget publishes the same inset through a
four-integer margin setter and reading it back gives four integers with the
reason gone, so a caption band and a three pixel border are the same four
numbers; the one place the parts ARE separable is a per-class sub-control enum
belonging to about twenty complex controls, which an application's card header
is not one of. Any painter here declares a band the same way, and
`scene/containment` names what a mark landed on: `Trespass` is `outside` /
`border` / `chrome:<role>`.

THE DECLARATION NEEDED A SECOND HALF. `LayoutStyle::chrome_slot` says a node
OCCUPIES its parent's band. Without it, declaring a caption makes every titled
frame report its own title as an escape; without the declaration, whatever is
drawn up there is exempt and a label that really did land on the caption goes
unreported. A node claiming a role its parent never reserved is judged as
ordinary content rather than exempted, so a typo cannot become a licence.

THE CRATE GATE IS THE BULK AND ITS POPULATION IS PARSED. R1673 measured fifteen
painters calling `with_border` and TWO asking whether their own contents stay
inside it. `frame_gate` is the shared assertion; its census walks this crate's
own syntax trees, because a border STROKED is production code and a gate RUN is
test code and a regex cannot tell them apart. The direction is `strokes -
gated`, so ADDING a bordered painter fails until it asks. No exception list.

ITS FIRST RUN WAS WRONG AND THAT WAS THE FINDING. Six painters failed, every one
a label overflowing right, and the cause was the gate: `screen_ink`'s stand-in
is wider per character than any real face, which is right for a SCREEN whose
boxes are authored constants and wrong for a WIDGET that sizes its box from its
content. The ink now comes from the same `LayoutCache` the layout pass shaped
with, so host font differences move the box and the ink together.

WHAT THE CORRECTED GATE FOUND, none of it visible to anything already running:
the menu popup stretched its rows over its own 1px border in every dropdown in
the tree, and repairing it revealed a SECOND copy of the popup box with the same
defect, which is why the answer is one `popup_box` both builders call; the
devtools highlight drew its ring UNDER the node it highlights while its own doc
comment promised otherwise (`Outside` placement now, since padding would move
what the overlay inspects); the toolbar painted its fifth control 58px past the
bar because CSS's automatic minimum size pins a content-sized flex item at its
min-content width; and six painters declared no overflow policy at all.

THE CHECK MARK IS A PATH, paying a debt R1673 opened while fixing another. It
derived the tick from `line_box`, a RESERVATION generous by ~35% because it
covers a face's ascent, descent and leading -- none of which a shape needs -- so
the M3 tick went 18px to 12px and every checkbox in the tree shrank. A polyline
fits by construction, the size token means what it says again, and the commonest
glyph in the catalog stops asking the host which fonts it has.

THE ANALYZER CARD IS THE CONSUMER. Its header and edit-bar bands are declared
rather than worked out privately, and the first draft was ONE PIXEL OUT: the
placement reserves the wider of two border widths constantly so rows do not

R1675.decision_summary:
The SCE pin moves 60cc4fcb -> 615cb3f6 (19 commits) and the mirror claim it
falsified is repaired.

The consumer surface is ZERO and that is a measurement, not an assumption:
`git diff` over `sce-rust-runtime/` is EMPTY across all nineteen commits, and
the new `pub` count there is 0. The whole delta is build-time — a W3C suite
emitter, per-route backend declarations, symbol-level judgment for three
runtimes, a mutation harness that can study a ctest suite.

WHAT THE BUMP ACTUALLY COST is one field, and R1657 is why it cost anything at
all. Upstream added `Diagnostic::expanded_from`, and `pinion-forge`'s mirror
destructures that record with no `..` precisely so an upstream field addition
lands as a COMPILE ERROR rather than as a claim quietly going false. It did.
This tree changed nothing and its statement "I mirror the SCE v1 record shape"
would have become untrue on its own — which is the thing R1657 wrote down and
this is the first bump to exercise it.

The field is classified NOT MIRRORED, with the reason and the condition that
would reverse it. `expanded_from` names the call site that chose the parameters
when a diagnostic's `location` points at a TEMPLATE row rather than at the
expansion that failed; it is also upstream's signal that the value is synthetic,
which is why no substitution `fix` accompanies it. Pinion has no such case:
every diagnostic here names a row in a real widget chart, and that row contains
the `actual` it complains about, so there is no second coordinate to carry. The
day pinion's forge expands a parameterised chart, this key is what stops a
consumer being handed a location that does not contain what it is told about —
and the destructure is what will bring someone back to it.

Dual-pin discipline held: gitlink, both manifest revisions and the lock move in
this one commit, `tools/pin_sync.py --check-dual-pin` green.
changes_bullets: `vendor/sce` gitlink 60cc4fcb -> 615cb3f6 (19 commits), both `Cargo.toml` revisions, and `Cargo.lock`, in one commit.

verification_bullets: `cargo test --workspace` 12,247 passed / 0 failed on the new pin.
`pinion-forge` 95 tests green, including the shape mirror that failed to compile before the field was classified.
`tools/pin_sync.py --check-dual-pin` green: manifest = lock = vendor/sce at 615cb3f.
Consumer-surface measurement: `git diff` over `sce-rust-runtime/` is empty across the 19 commits and new `pub` items there are 0.

R1676.decision_summary:
The framework answers where a mark can be reached; the harness re-derived that
answer and re-introduced the split the framework exists to close.

THE RED WAS ONE THING AND IT WAS NOT WHERE THE PREVIOUS ROUND LOOKED. Three
data-grid demos failed with an int scrub that stepped zero units. Driven and
measured rather than reasoned about: the Count cell is painted at x=-31 w=100
inside a scroll viewport that starts at x=21, so the centre a demo presses is
TWO PIXELS to the left of anything, the press is silently dropped, and the
release lands on a DIFFERENT cell and focuses it. The value assertion sixty
lines later names neither the press nor the geometry.

THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S REFUTATION WAS WRONG, and the way it was wrong is worth
more than the defect. It removed R1673's 1px frame padding, saw the demo still
FAIL, and recorded "not the cause — do not chase this again". Re-run here: with
the padding gone the demo dies in its BOOT GATE with a containment error, before
it reaches the scrub at all. Two different failures, one verdict, read as one
fact. "Still failing" is not "still failing for the same reason".

Also measured: even before R1673, that press point sat EXACTLY on the viewport's
left edge. The demo had zero pixels of margin and nothing said so.

THE CAUSE IS A MIRROR THAT FOLDS HALF A FACT. `abs_rects_of` in the demo harness
re-derives where every tagged mark is painted — deliberately, because an
independent derivation is what makes a focus-ring assertion a comparison rather
than a tautology (R705.1). It folded each `Scroll`'s OFFSET and not its CLIP.
`NodeVisit::absolute_rect`'s own doc argues at length that reported and visible
have to be ONE fact, because a caller that forgets the second call "asserts
against a rectangle nothing was drawn in" — and this was that caller, for as
long as both existed. It also let a LATER duplicate tag overwrite an earlier one
where the framework keeps the first. Nothing had ever checked that the second
implementation agreed with the first.

THE FLOOR MAKES THE SAME SPLIT, measured offscreen against the mature
retained-mode toolkit at 6.11 rather than argued from documentation. Its item
view, scrolled horizontally to the maximum, answers `x=-232 w=99` for the
leading column against a `0..368` viewport — an intersection of nothing. Its own
point-to-item lookup then AGREES with that rectangle: asked what is at the
centre of a rect lying entirely left of the viewport, it names the cell rather
than refusing, so the two-step is not merely inconvenient, it has an
affirmative wrong answer in it. The honest visible-region call it does have is a
widget member, and an item-view cell is not a widget. There is no enumeration in
either direction.

SO THE ENUMERATION IS THE NEW CAPABILITY. `scene/tag_rects` answers, for every
§5.20 intent tag in the painted tree, its own rectangle and the part of it a
pointer reaches — one round trip, `window: null` when a mark is painted but
wholly clipped away. Carried rather than dropped, because "there is no such
mark" and "it is out of sight" take different repairs and `scene/scroll_reach`
is the method that tells those apart; an enumeration that erased the second
would hand a caller the first. The walk is the one `bbox_of_tag` and
`Scene::absolute_rects_by_tag` already use, so the single lookup and the
enumeration cannot disagree, and the test asserts exactly that over every row.

AND THE TWO QUESTIONS GET TWO NAMES. Restoring the clip to the mirror broke
twenty-six demos, and the sweep is what said so: nearly all of them ask what the
VIEW BUILT — which rows a virtualized grid windowed, which cells it asked the
model for, that the newest transcript entry is painted BELOW the fold — and a
node the renderer then clips away is still one the view built. That is a
different question from "where can a person press", and it had one name.
`unclipped_rects_of` is the second name, both readers come out of one walk so
they cannot disagree about the offsets they share, and `r1445` now uses BOTH:
the visible reader for "pinned means the entry can be seen", the placement
reader for "the newest entry is off the bottom".

THE GATE IS THE PART THAT KEEPS IT TRUE. `_gate_tag_rects_agree` runs at every
demo's boot, compares the harness's whole map against the framework's whole
enumeration, and fails on any disagreement. Full coverage in one round trip, so
it is not a sample.

ONE ASSERTION GOT STRONGER RATHER THAN MOVED. `r1004` claimed "first match
revealed at the top" and asserted that source row 0 was in the band — a claim
about the overdraw, not about what a reader can see. Measured after the jump:
rows 0-2 are painted at y=-20, 16 and 52 above a viewport that starts at 88. The
match IS the topmost visible row, so the assertion now says that.

THE FOURTH RED WAS A FLAKE BY CONSTRUCTION AND ITS CAUSE IS REMOVABLE. R1664
measured that the software rasteriser disagrees with itself by one bit of
coverage and made pixel assertions tolerate it, with the tolerance measured from
a control pair in the same run. Measured here: ten captures of one unchanged
screen, 45 pairs — 3 of 45 byte-identical by default, and 45 of 45 with the tile
count pinned to one. So it is thread interleaving, and it goes away. That
matters twice: a control pair agreeing by luck reports a floor of 0 and then
fails a tested pair that noised by 1, which is exactly what put `r1527` red on
CI and green here; and with a tolerance of 1 a stale fragment differing by one
bit is invisible, so removing the noise gives the assertion its strength back.
The pin is set where the binary is LAUNCHED, not in the CI job, because a repro
on a developer machine has to have the property CI has.

TWO MORE REDS BELONGED TO THE ROUND BEFORE THIS ONE. R1674 added `chrome` to
`BoxFacet` and to the wire and did not move the two demos that restate the key
set independently — which is what those restatements are FOR, and they fired.
The second demand was the sharper one: a facet no binding anywhere can be seen
declaring is a key whose presence on the wire is untested, and neither binding
declared a chrome band, so the demo gained a third one that does.
changes_bullets: `pinion_rpc::locate::tag_rects_of` — every §5.20 intent tag in one pass, each with its own rectangle and the part of it a pointer reaches, first-tag-wins by the same walk `bbox_of_tag` uses.
`scene/tag_rects` publishes it, reading the PAINT tree by default because a view-fn binding's state scene would enumerate a tree of zero rects.
`abs_rects_of` in the demo harness folds each `Scroll`'s clip as well as its offset, and keeps the FIRST match for a duplicate tag — the two ways it had disagreed with the framework.
`unclipped_rects_of` is the second reader: where a mark would be if nothing clipped it, for the callers whose claim is about what the view BUILT.
`_gate_tag_rects_agree` compares the harness's whole map against the framework's whole enumeration at every demo's boot.

`RpcSubprocess` pins the software rasteriser to one tile thread, so a picture is a function of the scene rather than of how the scheduler interleaved the tiles; the `--ignored` GPU pixel job takes the same setting in CI.
Twenty-four demos whose claim is about emission move to `unclipped_rects_of`; `r1445` uses both readers, one per assertion.
`r1004` asserts that the first match is the topmost VISIBLE row, which is what its own sentence always claimed.
`r1514` / `r1516` restate the facet census with `chrome`, and `r1514` gains a third binding that actually declares a chrome band.
verification_bullets: Full local demo sweep, 575 demos: 29 failures before, and every one accounted for — 26 from the mirror's corrected semantics, 2 from R1674's facet addition, 1 environmental (the silent test card is not loaded on this host).
The four CI reds are green: r914 / r915 / r932 pass with the corrected press point, r1527 passes under software Vulkan three runs in a row with a measured self-disagreement of 0.
Rasteriser determinism measured, not assumed: ten captures of one unchanged screen, 45 pairs — 3 byte-identical by default, 45 with one tile thread.

The floor was measured by a probe linked against 6.11 and run offscreen, not read: unclipped per-item rects, a point-to-item lookup that answers for points outside its own viewport, a visible-region call that exists only for widgets, and no enumeration.

Counterfactuals 4/4 CAUGHT — the mirror dropping the clip, a later duplicate tag winning, the enumeration reporting a rectangle where nothing is shown, and the enumeration reading the state tree by default.
`cargo test -p pinion-rpc` green, `cargo clippy -p pinion-rpc --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` green under -D pedantic.
The one demo still failing locally, `r806`, was measured to fail IDENTICALLY at HEAD with none of this round's changes applied: it is the known local x11grab class and passes on CI.
carry_forward_bullets: `r806_focus_ring_corner` fails on this host and passed at HEAD identically, so it is not this round's — it is the documented local x11grab class (a live-pixel demo needing a mapped window) and it is green on CI. Stated rather than silently excluded.
`hello-audio-device` needs a silent test card this host does not have loaded; environmental, and the demo refuses loudly rather than opening an audible default, which is the designed behaviour.

The two facet mirrors are independent restatements on purpose, and nothing tells an author who adds a `BoxFacet` that two demos must move with it. They fired as designed and cost one CI run; the mechanism that would make it cheaper — a tripwire at the enum — would have to not destroy the independence that makes the restatements worth having.
