R1684.publishable_decision_summary:
A form row is where its value is typed, and the specification is driven in a
real window.

The analyzer node screen's settings rows had resolved a press to `field:<key>`
since R1651 — the hit test named it and the wire answered that word — while the
release handler ended in `_ => {}`. A person reported it as "the text box does
nothing", which is exactly what it was: a declared arm with no implementation is
worse than no arm, because the declaration stops the next reader looking.

The rule adopted is the behaviour reference's own, stated beside its inspector:
THE TYPE DECIDES THE CONTROL. A switch flips from anywhere in its control, and
every other shape opens the screen's one text field ON the row that was pressed
— which is what R1683's target parameter was built for. The field MOVES; a form
has as many rows as the document has keys, and a live box per row would be a
focus owner, a keymap and a commit path per key.

Three things followed rather than being aimed at:

* the launch gate gained its gesture. The verdict is derived from the form, so
  closing it means putting a value out of range, and the integer stepper clamps
  at the field's ceiling — correctly. An agent could close that gate and a
  person could not.
* a list ELEMENT became a target of its own, because the affordance that grows
  a list writes a placeholder, and a screen that can add one and never say what
  it is only ever grows invented values.
* the option rows became typable, because a bordered box with dead space
  between its chips is a control that lies — and because typing is the only way
  a person can put an unknown word on an option row and see it reported.

The specification is now driven end to end in a real window: a demo reads the
published operation table and causes all forty-five declared ways from fresh
processes, aims read out of the painted scene, keystrokes through the shell's
own key path. That closes the half of the operation gate the in-process sweep
cannot reach, and it is what caught the two counterfactuals nothing local can.
publishable_changes_bullets: `Editing::Value { node, key, element }` — the one field's third target, and
the first that is a PLACE rather than a thing. `edit_box` answers the row's
control, or a list element's own row, from the geometry the form painter
published; the field is painted last so it stands over what it is editing.
`Hit::Field(key)` gains its release arm (`press_row`): a switch flips, every
other shape opens the field. `act_on_part` gains the numbered `item.<key>.<n>`
arm (`press_element`), which had fallen through a dispatcher that handled only
`add`.
`set_value` — ONE function for the wire's `set_field`, for the affordances
inside a control (`set_and_sync` now delegates) and for a value typed. Before
this there were two, and only one of them said what it had done.
`set_element` splices one element of a list row, leaving its neighbours alone;
emptying it removes it, which is what the form's own splitter already means.
`select_card` — one function for the four sites that moved the selection, so
a box opened over the inspected card's row cannot survive a change of card.
`begin_edit` returns a `Result` and COMMITS an open edit on a different target
before moving. A refused commit refuses the move.
`body_origin` — the inspector's one signed pane-origin. `in_body` clamps it
per rectangle and `inspector_geometry` translates by it, so the form's window
geometry is no longer a second arithmetic that was short by `PANEL_FRAME`.
`NodeLabView::position_caret_for_point` / `select_drag_to_point` +
`field_byte_at` + `edit_field_style` — click-to-caret and drag-select, which
the screen never had; the paint and the hit test now shape through one style.
The wire: `edit` takes `value:<key>` and `value:<key>[<n>]` (`row_target`
parses the spelling `editing.target` reads back) and refuses a row the form
does not hold, an element the row does not have, a number that is not one and
a bracket that never shuts.
`spec::OPERATIONS`: `validate` moves to `gesture: true`, with a driver.
Six gates in `painted.rs`: the centre of every control does something; the
field stands on the seat that was under the cursor, holding what that seat
holds, and applying puts it there; leaving the field applies it and a refusal
refuses the move; picking another card shuts it; a control answers at its
CORNERS; a click resolves to the byte whose caret is painted under it; and the
wire's target grammar with its four refusals.
`tools/demos/r1684_the_specification_is_driven_in_a_window.py` — the whole
published operation table caused in a real shell, both columns, fresh process
per operation, recipes cross-checked against the declaration in both
directions.
publishable_verification_bullets: Local gates, on the crate this round touched:
`cargo test -p hello-node-lab --features pinion-runtime/vello` — 56 passed.
`cargo clippy -p hello-node-lab --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello`
— clean under the workspace pedantic baseline.
`cargo fmt --all --check`.
Every demo that drives this screen, run locally against a release build:
The new demo's own measurement: 30 operations, 20 by action and 25 by gesture,
45 declared ways, every one of them caused something an agent can observe. Four
operations remain absent by declaration (fit the graph to the view, export the
configuration, produce the launch script, go to the first problem).
The gate that opened this round MEASURED the defect before it was fixed: 24 of
45 painted controls did nothing when pressed in the middle, in eight swept
states, and the two causes were both different from the prediction that
motivated the round.
Sixteen counterfactuals, all caught:
Fourteen by the local suite: the dropped `Field` arm; the numbered list-item
arm; the field left in the head of the pane; the field on the row instead of
the element; the element seeded with the whole row; applying an element
writing the whole row; the two coordinate transforms drifting apart again;
an option row going back to dead-in-the-middle; the selection moving with the
field left open; the wire accepting an element a row does not have; leaving
the field throwing typing away; a refused commit letting the field move; the
hit test shaped differently from the paint; and a `gesture: true` with no
driver.
Two only by the demo, which is stated rather than hidden: the screen ceasing
to stand aside inside the open box, and a click that does not move the caret.
Neither can be asked in process — that harness calls the view directly, so
there is no field external and no shell input router.

element-press break was invisible because the placement check derived the
expected seat from the field's own answer (it now also asserts the seat was
under the cursor); the selection break and the refused-commit break had no gate
at all until this round wrote one.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: Nothing is carried that this round could have closed. What is left is stated:
**Four operations remain absent by declaration** — fit the graph to the view,
export the configuration, produce the launch script, go to the first problem.
They are rows of the published table with neither a verb nor a gesture, which
is what makes them countable and what the ratchet holds at four.
**"remove a field" still has a verb and no gesture.** The behaviour reference
draws a delete affordance on every non-derived row; ours has none, so the wire
can take a row out and a person cannot. It is a row of the operation table
rather than a note here, which is the register that gets read.
**The in-process sweep cannot mount the screen's extra externals** — the
standing limit ([[debt-the-in-process-sweep-cannot-mount-a-screens-extra-externals]]),
and this round measured what it costs: two of sixteen counterfactuals are
catchable only by a demo, so those two claims are CI-gated rather than
commit-gated. The demo now exists and catches them; making the local gate able
to ask is the framework-side work that debt names.
**A press inside the open box is answered by the SCREEN, not the field.** That
is now written where it is relied on, and it is why the caret hooks had to be
implemented here rather than inherited. Whether the router should route a
press to the topmost external instead is a framework question this round did
not open.

R1684.1.decision_summary:
The scene walk every text-field binding wrote by hand is lifted, and the audit
that deferred it rested on a premise that is no longer true.

R1684's round-close self-grep — "is what I just wrote the third copy of
something?" — found that it was the FOURTH. Measured: seven bindings compose an
IME caret rectangle the same four lines (look the tag's rect up in the painted
scene, read the theme, call `tf_paint::ime_caret_rect_for`), and four compose a
pointer hit-test the same way over `byte_for_field_point`. Byte-identical apart
from the tag and the style.

R791.1 audited exactly this duplication and recorded a deliberate defer: the
scene walk lives in `pinion_runtime::rect_for_tag`, and `pinion-widget-paint`
does not depend on `pinion-runtime` so it stays backend-agnostic and reusable
from the TUI, which makes the wrapper "irreducibly binding-side".

That is false today, and cheap to check: `rect_for_tag` is a ONE-LINE wrapper
over `Scene::rect_for_tag_absolute`, a method on the scene type
`pinion-widget-paint` already depends on. The dependency the defer was
protecting against was never needed to do the walk there.

So `ime_caret_rect_in_scene` and `byte_for_scene_point` take the scene, and the
eleven call sites lose four lines each. What stays binding-side is the FOCUS
GUARD, which is policy rather than composition — `hello-node-lab` answers "was
this press mine" by geometry where every sibling answers it by tag comparison,
because all of its presses reach one root external.

The general lesson is the one this session keeps paying for: a stated limit
nobody re-checks outlives the thing that made it true. R1681.2 was the same
shape, and so was R1684's discovery that a press does not reach the field's own
external.
changes_bullets: `pinion_widget_paint::text_field::ime_caret_rect_in_scene` and
`byte_for_scene_point` — the existing helpers with the field's rectangle
taken from the painted scene, answering `None` when the tag is not painted.
Eleven call sites rewired: `hello-textfield`, `hello-textarea`,
`hello-find-replace`, `hello-syntax-highlight`, `hello-file-save-dialog`,
`hello-file-manager`, `todomvc` (caret), and `hello-textfield`,
`hello-find-replace`, `hello-syntax-highlight`, `hello-node-lab` (pointer).
The R791.1 note in `pinion-shell` is corrected in place rather than deleted:
it now carries what it claimed, why that was false, and what genuinely does
stay binding-side.
`r1684_1_an_unpainted_field_has_no_caret_and_no_byte` — the `?` on the walk
is the contract, and it had no test in any of the eleven sites.
verification_bullets: Every crate the lift touches, tested and linted together:
`cargo test -p pinion-widget-paint -p hello-textfield -p hello-textarea
-p hello-find-replace -p hello-syntax-highlight -p hello-file-save-dialog
-p hello-file-manager -p todomvc -p hello-node-lab --features
pinion-runtime/vello` — ten suites, all ok.
The same set under `cargo clippy --all-targets`, clean.
`cargo fmt --all --check`.
The demos that drive the two paths this touches, run locally against release
builds: r762 (click-to-caret), r763 (drag select), hello_textfield_compose (the
IME caret rectangle itself), r764 (textarea caret), r790 (save dialog), r791
(file-manager rename), r793 (commit on blur), todomvc_r666, and R1684's own
window demo. All pass.
Two counterfactuals, both caught after the second was written:
Making the walk fall back to a default rectangle instead of answering `None`
PASSED all ten suites on the first run — a field that is not painted would
have reported a caret at the window origin, which is where an IME anchors its
candidate popup. That contract had no test at any of the eleven sites it used
to live at; lifting the code is what made one test enough to cover it.
Dropping the field's origin from the pointer walk is caught by the demos'
byte assertions and by `hello-node-lab`'s caret round-trip gate.
carry_forward_bullets: Nothing carried. Two facts worth stating rather than carrying:
**The focus guard is deliberately NOT lifted**, and the reason is that it is
a policy: which tag a binding owns, and whether a press the router sent
elsewhere should move its caret. `hello-node-lab` answers the second
differently from every sibling — by geometry rather than by tag comparison —
because all of its presses arrive at one root external. A lift that folded
that in would have to encode one answer.
**`ime_caret_rect_for` and `byte_for_field_point` stay public.** A caller that
already has the rectangle (a test, a composite that lays a field out itself)
should not have to put it in a scene first, and the scene-walking pair is
written in terms of them rather than beside them.

R1684.2.decision_summary:
The corner check is asked of every pressable tag, and it immediately found the
same one-pixel defect in the other pane.

R1684 found that the settings form's window geometry was short by the panel
frame, repaired it, and wrote a gate that aims at a control's CORNERS because a
centre absorbs any error smaller than half the control. That gate was scoped to
one tag family — the family the defect had been found in.

A gate that only watches where the last defect was is a gate that finds the last
defect. The screen already declares every pressable tag and what a press on it
must answer (`must_answer`, the population three other checks use), so the
corner check now uses that: 2464 corners across eight swept states.

It reported 243 failures on the first run, and the pattern was the signature
rather than noise — for each palette row the TOP-LEFT corner resolved and the
other three did not, which is exactly what a rectangle shifted by one pixel
looks like. The palette's rectangles are written in window coordinates that
embed the pane's origin and not the outline its scrolling body is drawn inside,
while the paint hands that body `panel_content`. Second instance of one class in
one screen, both invisible for the same reason.

A corner may legitimately be answered by something else — a stepper at the end
of a number row, a pin on a card's edge, the picked link's chrome — so the
excuse is asked of the SCENE rather than assumed: the thing that answered must
itself be painted at that point. An answer naming something that is somewhere
else is the drift this exists to find.
changes_bullets: `in_pane` — the palette's one query transform now carries `PANEL_FRAME`, so
its rows are hit-tested where they are painted. One caller, and the fix is in
the transform rather than in each rectangle.
`r1684_a_control_answers_at_its_edges_not_only_its_middle` — the population is
every tag `must_answer` declares, not one family. A corner answered by
something else is excused only when that something is painted at that point,
which is asked of the scene.
verification_bullets: `cargo test -p hello-node-lab --features pinion-runtime/vello` — 56 passed,
the corner gate now probing 2464 corners in eight states.
`cargo clippy -p hello-node-lab --all-targets` clean; `cargo fmt --all
--check`.
All eight demos that drive this screen, re-run against a release build: the
palette hit test moved by a pixel and r1651 and r1662 are what would have
noticed a regression there.
Two counterfactuals, both caught: dropping the frame term from the palette's
query, and narrowing the corner check back to one tag family.
carry_forward_bullets: Nothing carried.
Stated: the corner check covers this screen's declared pressable tags. Whether
the other thirty-eight surfaces in the tree have the same class is not asked by
anything here, and this round did not measure it — the check is written against
one screen's `must_answer`, which is that screen's own declaration and not a
framework-level one.

R1684.3.decision_summary:
A press lands where the paint put it after a resize — and the reason it did not
is a framework gap this repairs only for one screen.

Reported by a person testing the running window: maximise it and the settings
rows stop selecting. Measured through the wire rather than reasoned about —
after `scene/resize` the paint puts a form control at x≈2339 and `point`
refuses it as "outside the 1440x900 window".

`window_size()` reads the live viewport through `use_viewport_size()`, a hook
that only answers inside an `Owner` scope. The shell paints inside one and
calls this screen's pointer handlers and wire actions OUTSIDE one, so they were
laying every rectangle out against the DESIGN size while the paint used the
live one. The error grows with distance from the origin, which is why the
inspector on the far right dies first and the palette on the left goes on
working — exactly what was reported.

The value now comes from `External::on_resize`, which is §5.15's own lifecycle
arm and which R1656 wired for precisely this class: that round used the
announcement for the CURSOR's basis and left the LAYOUT reading a constant. One
announcement, both readers.

★★ This is a WORKAROUND and is registered as one. The framework hands a widget
its own size through a reactive hook that cannot answer in the callbacks the
framework itself invokes, so every screen that hit-tests its own surface
invents a cache — three of them in this one file (scroll offsets R1662, edit
buffer R1683, window size here). The first two PANIC outside a scope and were
found immediately; this one answered a plausible default and stayed invisible
until somebody resized a window. The mature retained-mode toolkits this project
is judged against have no such split: a widget's own size is plain state there,
answerable in every callback and updated by a resize event.
changes_bullets: `External::on_resize` on this screen's oracle now feeds the LAYOUT as well as
the cursor basis, through `ANNOUNCED_SIZE`; `window_size()` falls back to what
the shell announced instead of the size the screen was designed at.
`r1684_3_a_press_lands_where_the_paint_put_it_after_a_resize` — paints at the
maximised size inside an owner scope, announces it the way the shell does, and
then presses from OUTSIDE the scope, which is where production asks.
verification_bullets: The wire probe that found it, re-run: at 2494x1531 a press at the form
control's painted centre (2339,253) answers `field:id`. Before the fix it was
refused as outside a 1440x900 window.
`cargo test -p hello-node-lab --features pinion-runtime/vello` — 57 passed.
`cargo clippy -p hello-node-lab --all-targets` clean; `cargo fmt --all --check`.
Seven demos that drive this screen, re-run against a release build.
2/2 counterfactuals caught: falling back to the design size off a scope, and
dropping the announcement on the floor.
★ The size axis of the in-process sweep was VOID for the hit test and this is
why nothing saw the defect: those checks run inside `owner.run(...)`, so the
paint and the hit test both resolve the hook and agree by construction. The new
test leaves the scope on purpose.
carry_forward_bullets: One carry, and it is the framework's rather than this screen's:
[[debt-a-widget-cannot-read-its-own-size-outside-a-scope]].
A widget can only read its own surface size through a hook that answers inside
an `Owner` scope, and the shell invokes `External::pointer_press`,
`pointer_move`, `invoke` and `query` outside one — while wrapping
`position_caret_for_point` inside one. That asymmetry is what makes every
self-hit-testing screen keep a hand-written cache.
Two candidate repairs are written down there: run the External dispatch inside
the shell's root owner (symmetry, but the auto-subscribe behaviour of
`Signal::get` has to be measured first), or give the widget its size as plain
state the way the mature retained-mode toolkits do. Neither is chosen here, and the population — how many
screens hit-test their own surface and die on a resize — is unmeasured; R1656's
sibling fix names four candidates.

R1684.4.decision_summary:
A widget can read its own size from anywhere, because the framework now keeps
it — R1684.3's repair was a workaround and this replaces it.

The question a person asked when R1684.3 landed was the right one: should the
framework not do this automatically? It should. A widget could learn its own
surface size two ways and both had a scope attached — `use_viewport_size()`
answers only inside an `Owner` scope, and `External::on_resize` hands the number
over once and then it is the widget's problem to keep. The framework itself
calls `pointer_press`, `pointer_move`, `invoke` and `query` OUTSIDE any owner
scope, so a screen that hit-tests its own surface had to remember the size in a
cache of its own, in every such screen.

`pinion_core::external::surface_size(tag)` is that fact with an owner.
`announce_external_sizes` — the pass that already tells every painted surface
its rectangle (R1656) — records it on the same pass, from the same rectangle, so
the size a widget READS and the size its pointer fractions are fractions OF are
one derivation rather than two. A surface that stops being painted is forgotten,
so a stale size cannot be read back for something that is not on screen.

★ What this does NOT do is close the class. The asymmetry underneath is still
there: the shell wraps `position_caret_for_point` in the root owner scope and
does not wrap the External's own callbacks, so `use_scroll_state` and
`use_text_edit_state` still cannot be called from a pointer handler and two
hand-written caches remain in the screen that prompted this. Those are named in
the debt rather than claimed here; what is fixed is the one that answered a
plausible default instead of panicking, and was therefore invisible until a
person resized a window.

R1684.5.decision_summary:
The statechart engine is bumped, and the reason to check it carefully is what
the seventeen commits contain.

`vendor/sce` tracks upstream `main` and had not moved since 615cb3f. The bump
takes it to 23f1758 — seventeen commits, and four of them are PARALLEL-state
fixes: a transition that exited and entered twice, a nested parallel whose
regions did not all stay live below one level, `currentState` settling on an
atomic state inside a parallel machine, and a `done.state` delivery check across
every backend.

That matters here rather than being upstream's business, because one of this
project's twelve widget statecharts uses a parallel region: `dock_panel.scxml`.
So the verification is aimed at it rather than at the tree in general.

verification_bullets: `cargo test -p pinion-core -p pinion-runtime -p pinion-forge --features
pinion-runtime/vello` — the crates that embed the engine and the one that
emits from it. All ok.
The consumers of the one statechart with a parallel region (`dock_panel`):
`cargo test -p hello-dock-panels -p hello-dock-panels-editor -p
hello-dock-presets -p hello-node-lab`. All ok.
Demos: `r1096_dock_tab_click` and `r1097_dock_pointer_reorganize` drive that
statechart through a real shell; `r1684` re-run because this round's work is
in it. All pass.
The remote builder transfers submodule working trees as well as tracked files
and proves tree equality before running, so these results are against the
bumped engine rather than a stale checkout — checked rather than assumed,
because `git ls-files` does not include submodule contents.
carry_forward_bullets: Nothing carried.
Stated: what was verified is this project's USE of the engine — the crates that
embed it, the one statechart with a parallel region, and the demos that drive
it. Upstream's own suite is upstream's; a bump that broke something this project
does not exercise would not be visible here, and pinning to a branch means the
next bump inherits whatever landed meanwhile.

R1685.decision_summary:
A box can declare that content which does not fit in it is cut there, and the
declaration carries both halves of what that means.

`LayoutStyle::overflow` (CSS `overflow`, two variants: `Visible` and `Hidden`)
is lowered to taffy's own `Style.overflow` AND read by every renderer as the
clip. Before this round the tree could express only the layout half — `min_size
= Px(0)`, which relaxes the same CSS automatic minimum size and is documented
as doing so — while the paint half existed only on `Scene::Scroll`. A region
that had to cut its overflow therefore had to become scrollable, or have its
pixel budget balanced by hand.

The clip also stops being a property of a node KIND. `Scene::clip_window` is
the single reading every consumer takes: the scene walk's fold, both vello
walkers, the terminal cell walker, the PDF projector, the containment
derivation's fate and the reachability derivation's viewport chain. The kind
census keeps the half that is genuinely a kind's — `can_clip_subtree`, "this
kind holds children at all" — asserted against `child_nodes` rather than
restated.

Two variants and not four, each a decision rather than an omission. `Scroll` is
absent because `Scene::Scroll` is the scrolling model and a second one reachable
from a style field would be two answers to one question. CSS's `clip` is absent
because taffy reads it as "cut the ink but keep the content-based minimum",
which is not CSS's own rule, and publishing it would publish an engine quirk as
if it were the cascade. There is one field rather than a per-axis pair because
CSS cannot express a mixed clipping box either: when one axis clips and the
other is `visible`, the visible one computes to `auto` — so the only thing a
per-axis split buys is letting one axis scroll, which is the node's job.

The reachability derivation is why the workaround (a `Scene::Scroll` with a
pinned offset) was refused rather than documented: it reads a viewport's range
off the geometry, so it would have reported every cut mark as "scrollable to
y=152" while nothing in the application could move that offset. A false
REACHABLE is the error that derivation exists to end. The node a screen chooses
is now the declaration — a scroll publishes a range a reader can move, a hidden
box publishes none, and its overflow is `lost`.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::style`: `Overflow` (`Visible` / `Hidden`) + `LayoutStyle::overflow`
+ `with_overflow`, folded into the §5.16 paint-fragment cache key (two nodes
identical but for the clip paint different pixels).
`pinion-core::scene`: `Scene::clips_subtree` / `Scene::clip_window` (the node
half) and `SceneNodeKind::clips_subtree` renamed `can_clip_subtree` (the kind
half). `walk_from` folds the clip from the declaration; the frame shift stays
the scroll's, because a container does not move its children.
`pinion-runtime::layout`: `LayoutStyle::overflow` lowered to taffy
`Style.overflow`, derived from the same `Overflow::clips` predicate the
renderers read so the two halves cannot come apart.
Renderers: the vello walker, the cached vello walker (screen-space damage clip
narrowed too), the terminal cell walker (`cell_clip_of` shared with the scroll
arm) and the PDF projector all clip from `Scene::clip_window`.
`pinion-core::reach`: the viewport chain accepts any clipping node;
`Viewport::origin` records which FRAME the marks are expressed in — zero for a
scroll, the box's own position for a container — and a hidden box's range is
zero by CSS's own rule, so its overflow is `Reach::Lost`.
`pinion-core::containment`: no code change; the fate is read from the walk's
clip, so an overflow container's cut now reports `Clipped`. The scroll
exemption deliberately does NOT extend to it, and the reason is written down.
Wire: `scene/snapshot` publishes `clips` per container; `scene/scroll_reach`
publishes `origin_x` / `origin_y` (with the `ViewportReport` census row).
`pinion-widget-paint::toolbar`: a control declares `Overflow::Hidden` in place
of R1674's and R1680's hand-spelled `min_size: Px(0)`, which also cuts ink the
elide cannot reach because it measures against the box it was given.
`examples/hello-overflow-clip` (new): the consumer report's own shape — fixed
header, yielding body that clips, action bar, tab bar.
`tools/demos/r1685_a_body_yields_and_what_it_cuts_is_gone.py` (new).
`tools/rpc_verify.py`: the python mirror of `absolute_rects_by_tag` narrows at
any node publishing `clips`, not only at a Scroll.
`crates/pinion-shell/tests/backend_parity.rs`: a container fixture on the clip
axis, the kind census asserted against `child_nodes`, and the clip fixtures
rendered inside a frame of CONSTANT size — without which the PDF cell of that
matrix was answering with its page size.
verification_bullets: Local gates, all green: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets
--features pinion-runtime/vello` over every crate whose behaviour moved
(pinion-core, pinion-runtime, pinion-tui, pinion-pdf, pinion-rpc,
pinion-widget-paint, pinion-shell, hello-overflow-clip) — 37 suites — plus
`cargo fmt --all --check`.
New gates:
`reach`: a hidden box loses what a scroll of the SAME geometry only hides
(the two fixtures differ in one word); a hidden box away from the origin
loses nothing it holds; a container that declares nothing is not a viewport.
`scene`: the walk folds a container's clip (a mark past it resolves nowhere,
and is still VISITED); a leaf carries the declaration and clips no subtree;
the pointer never reached the cut half and the paint now agrees.
`style`: the default is CSS's, the predicate answers for both variants, and
the fragment cache key moves with the field.
`layout`: `Overflow::Hidden` produces byte-identical geometry to
`min_size: Px(0)`, with a witness that `Visible` does not.
`containment`: the same overhang is `Clipped` under a declaring container and
`Smeared` under one that declares nothing, and the COUNT is the same — the
declaration changes the fate, never whether it is reported.
`backend_parity`: the container joins the clip axis; all three renderers are
held to it; the fixture must actually declare a clip; the kind census is
asserted against `child_nodes`.
`snapshot`: a container publishes whether it cuts its children.
`toolbar`: a label's ink is cut at its control with ink measured at 40px per
character — no font in the measurement, so the verdict is the same on every
host, which the gate that caught R1680 cannot say.
Demo: `r1685_a_body_yields_and_what_it_cuts_is_gone.py`, 40+ assertions over
five sections against a real shell (declaration on the wire, chrome heights at
three window sizes, containment fates, reachability with the range at zero, and
`scene/locate` landing on the band that is painted there).
Blast radius run and green: every demo whose screen now contains a clipping
container — r692_toolbar, r1206_toolbar_fixed_frame, r989_selection_toolbar,
r799_textarea_format_toolbar, r1449_completer, r990_column_visibility — two of
which FAILED first and found the frame bug in the reachability derivation.
Counterfactuals: 11 of 11 caught (the walk's fold, the declaration gate, the
kind gate, reach's range, the cache key, all three renderers, the taffy
lowering, the toolbar adoption, the wire field). Two more were BROKEN on the
first attempt (they did not compile, so they tested nothing) and were rewritten;
one PASSED and was a finding — the PDF cell of the clip matrix had been vacuous
since R1516 because the projector's page size is derived from scene bounds.
Ink ratchets: `hello-overflow-clip` registered by re-running
`tools/measure_ink_budgets.py --add` (containment 1, smear 0, lost 3), the
numbers derived rather than hand-written. The screen was also LOOKED at, which
changed it: every gate was green while the entries and the body shared a fill,
so the half-cut card was invisible.
carry_forward_bullets: **The paint/gesture split is NOT closed, and this round only narrowed it.**
`Scene::hit_test` gates every descent on the node's own rect, so a child
painted past its parent has never been pressable — measured this round rather
than assumed. Declaring the clip makes the picture agree with that; leaving
`Overflow::Visible` still paints ink no press can reach, which is
`debt-paint-and-gesture-read-two-facts` and is untouched here.
**`Overflow::Clip` is absent by decision.** The day a consumer genuinely wants
"cut the ink, keep the content-based minimum", the enum gains the variant and
`Overflow::clips` gains its second predicate (`zeroes_automatic_minimum`), and
the taffy lowering — which derives from the first predicate today, so the two
halves cannot disagree — becomes two questions. The condition is written at
both sites.
**The population of centred labels with no minimum released is still
uncounted** (`debt-an-overflow-policy-applies-to-the-runs-own-rect`). The
toolbar is repaired at its root and the class is not: any painter that centres
a text child in a box it does not clip can still smear on a host whose font is
wider than this one's. This round makes the repair one word instead of two, it
does not find the sites.
**A hidden box's own content wrapper is reported as an escape.** A container
taller than the body that clips it produces one `Fate::Clipped` row, which is
the honest reading (the reader loses content with nothing saying so) and is
what `hello-overflow-clip`'s containment budget of 1 records. If that turns out
to be noise on a real screen the exemption the scroll has is the shape to
copy — the reason it was NOT copied here is written at that site.

header, yielding body that clips, action bar, tab bar.

R1686.decision_summary:
R1686 — a settings row offers to be taken out, and a layout stops depending on
who is asking.

The analyser screen's operation table has carried `remove a field` as **verb,
no gesture** since R1677: the wire could take a row out of the inspector and
nothing on the screen could. That column exists to make exactly this
impossible to forget, and this round answers it — with the reference tool's own
affordance, a seat at the trailing edge of every row's key line, built into the
form PAINTER rather than into the screen, so the property grid gets it in the
same act.

Making the operation reachable by a person is what forced the rest, and every
piece of it was proven by a failing test before it was made:

1. **The offered set is now DERIVED from the kind's catalogue** rather than
   being a bucket `remove` pushes into. The old shape made the list a record of
   one node's history: a path typed by hand through `add_typed` and then taken
   out came back as a chip, so the form began offering, to every later reader, a
   key somebody once mistyped. Measured on the reference: its offered list is
   `catalogue(role)` minus what is held, and a hand-typed key removed simply
   goes.

2. **A row leaves as it opened.** `remove` reverts the field on the way out.
   A removed row that kept its edit is a ghost — off the screen, nothing showing
   the value, and `add` resurrecting a number nobody can see they still have.

3. **A row put back goes where it opened.** Found by (2)'s own test rather than
   reasoned: the value came back and the form still reported a change, because a
   plain push put the row at the end. Order is what a reader navigates a form by
   and it is half of what `ConfigForm::edited` compares, so a row that came back
   in the wrong place left the form permanently dirty with nothing on screen
   saying why. The reference cannot have this bug — it hides a row with an
   overlay and never touches the definition's order — so here the order is
   derived from the opening key list instead.

4. **★★★★★ `measured_text_extent` answers outside an `Owner` scope.** The seat
   was reachable and correct, and pressing the chip painted for one
   configuration path added another. The cause was one layer under the screen
   and had nothing to do with the seat: the chip row's widths come from the text
   measurer, which answered `None` outside a scope, so a caller fell back to a
   per-character estimate. A shell paints inside the scope and routes a pointer
   outside it — so `form_geometry`, whose own header calls it "the single source
   both the paint and a consumer's hit test read", returned two different
   layouts. Measured: the estimate makes `qos.priority` 99px and the shaper 92px,
   so the hit test fitted one fewer chip per row. Both boxes were "right" and
   only their derivation disagreed.

   The repair is R1684.4's shape one axis over — the scope that HAS the provider
   records it, and a reader outside any scope measures with the same face —
   rather than every screen inventing a cache
   ([[debt-a-widget-cannot-read-its-own-size-outside-a-scope]]).

The round's own counterfactual PASSED once, which is the recorded pattern for a
finding: breaking "the field shuts with the row it was standing on" left every
Rust gate green and only the subprocess demo noticed. `editing` is a plain
signal and needs no external to observe, so the question had no reason to live
only in a subprocess; it is an in-process gate now. 11/11 caught after that.

5. **A FLAKE, and the class audit it forced.** Re-running the screen's demos
   after a refactor, R1685's went red once and passed three times idle: it read
   the opening body height at the tall size. `scene/resize` followed by a fixed
   `tick` is a bet that the render arrives inside that interval, and
   `from=paint` reads the last RENDERED frame — so every read after a lost bet
   answers about the previous window, including the derived reports
   (`scene/containment`, `scene/scroll_reach`).

   [[zero-flake-policy]] asks for the class, not the instance. Audited: of the
   demos that resize, four never waited — and one of them carried a comment
   explaining this exact hazard before taking the bet anyway, which is what a
   rule living in prose looks like. `rpc_verify.resize_and_settle` is the rule
   now, polling the root's own width and height, with a gate over every demo.

   That gate cost three passed counterfactuals of its own before it was worth
   having. It first asked whether a file MENTIONED a settling helper — and
   putting the flaking shape back left it green, because the now-unused import
   still mentioned it. Rewritten to forbid the verb outright, it flagged
   thirteen sites that are already right in a STRONGER way, polling a domain
   outcome rather than the root rectangle; a gate that turns correct code into
   weaker code is not a gate. It is per-function now: a function that sends the
   verb must also wait. And the helper itself had no test — this file exists so
   that what every demo leans on is not the untested part, and `wait_until` had
   one from R1580 while its most load-bearing caller did not.
changes_bullets: `pinion_core::widgets::config_form::ConfigForm` restructured: `addable` (a
mutable bucket) becomes `catalogue` (the kind's offerable keys, invariant:
the constructor's offered list plus the opening rows) plus `parked` (rows
taken out, each already reverted, so `revert` can restore one the catalogue
does not name). `addable()` is derived and now returns `Vec<&ConfigField>`.
`ConfigForm::remove` reverts the field on the way out; `add` restores the
parked row when there is one and otherwise clones the catalogue's; `settle`
clears `parked`; `revert` partitions `fields ∪ parked`; `upsert` places a row
named by `opened_with` at its opening rank rather than pushing it last.
`pinion_widget_paint::config_form`: `RowBox::remove` — the seat that takes a
row away, cut out of the header's trailing edge by `split_off_remove` before
the header goes to the flex pass, moved by `FormGeometry::translated`, painted
by `view_remove_seat` at exactly that rectangle, and published to assistive
technology as a named button by `row_access_nodes`. Its own field rather than
a `parts` entry: `parts` means *inside the control*, and the option painter
and the crate's containment gate both rely on that.
`pinion_core::measured_text_extent` answers outside an `Owner` scope, with the
provider that last measured something; `forget_measuring_provider` clears the
record for a test that wants the headless answer back.
`hello-node-lab`: `Hit::RemoveField` (`remove:<key>` on the wire), resolved
before the header it was cut from; `remove_row` — one function for the seat
and the `remove_field` verb, which shuts the field standing on the row being
taken away, applies it when it was standing on a different one, and re-derives
the card; `spec::OPERATIONS`' `remove a field` declares `gesture: true`.
Gates: the painted-tag census demands a seat per shown row and `must_answer`
maps `lab.form.remove.` to `remove:<key>`; the in-process driver table gains
the gesture; `r1686_taking_a_row_away_shuts_the_field_standing_on_it`.
`tools/demos/r1686_a_row_says_take_me_out.py` (10 sections, >= 30 assertions),
including a gate over EVERY painted add-chip — a press on its centre must
resolve to its own key — which is where the layout disagreement was caught.
`tools/demos/r1684_the_specification_is_driven_in_a_window.py` gains the
recipe its bidirectional check now demands, and
`r1651_the_node_lab_matches_the_reference.py` demands a seat per shown row in
both directions — its BACKWARD census refused the five painted seats before
the forward one was told to expect them.
`rpc_verify.resize_and_settle` — drive a window resize and answer the paint
once the new size has been rendered. `r1685`, `r1662`, `r1656` and `r1649`
went through it; the three that had hand-rolled a fixed tick were a flake
waiting for load.
`test_rpc_verify.py`: `test_resize_and_settle_waits_for_the_frame_that_is_the
_new_size` (the helper, against a renderer that serves the old frame first)
and `test_no_demo_resizes_a_window_and_reads_without_waiting` (every demo, by
AST, per function).
`hello-node-lab`'s `release` sheds its four form arms to `act_on_form` —
the grouping the arms already had, and what kept the function inside the
line budget after the round's arm was added.
`painted.rs`: `press_at` lifted over six copies of the move/press/release
triple found by the round's third-consumer grep.
verification_bullets: Counterfactuals: 11/11 CAUGHT, gate
`cargo test -p pinion-core -p pinion-widget-paint -p pinion-chart -p hello-node-lab`
(baseline verified green first, per the driver's own rule). One PASSED on the
first run and was a finding — see the decision.
Order kept: every model claim was a FAILING test first. `remove` returning a
hand-typed key to the catalogue and an edit surviving a round trip were both
red before the repair, with the offered list and the value printed in the
failure. The row-order defect was found BY that repair's test rather than
predicted.
The layout-agreement defect was found on the RUNNING screen, not by reading:
pressing the chip painted for `control.permissions` added `plugins`. Isolated by
asking the application itself where a press lands (`point`) at every painted
chip's centre — the paint and the hit test disagreed by one chip on the card
whose offered set wraps onto three lines. Arithmetic on the measured rectangles
gave the cause (estimate 99px vs shaped 92px for `qos.priority`), and the repair
was then pinned by a unit test that lays the same form out inside and outside an
owner scope.
Local gates, on the crates whose behaviour moved: `pinion-core`,
`pinion-widget-paint`, `pinion-chart`, `hello-node-lab` — all green.
Demo blast radius MEASURED rather than guessed: `measured_text_extent` has
exactly two callers in the tree (`pinion-chart`'s axis fit and the config-form
painter), so the sweep is every chart demo plus every demo of the one screen
that paints a form, plus the two grid scrub demos that hit-test measured text.
`tools/demos/r1686_a_row_says_take_me_out.py` PASS, and it carries the gate the
defect above escaped: every painted add-chip must resolve a press on its centre
to its own key — every chip, not the one that was wrong (R1684.2's lesson).
The FLAKE was caught by re-running the screen's demos after a refactor, not by
CI: one red, three greens idle. Characterised before it was diagnosed (three
consecutive passes is what made it a flake rather than a break), then the class
was audited across every demo that resizes — four offenders — and closed with a
helper plus a gate. The gate has its own counterfactual plan, 3 of 4 caught; the
fourth is recorded IN the gate rather than left silent, because per-function
scope and file scope cannot be told apart by this tree today and the stricter
one is the one that states the real claim.
`tools/test_rpc_verify.py`: 33 cases, 91 checks, green — run by `pre-push`.
Demos re-run after every later edit, not only after the change they were about:
the nine that touch a resized window or the screen this round changed, 9/9.
Mnemosyne: validate-workspace green before and after; T1 reject 0, orphan_refs
5+0 unchanged.
carry_forward_bullets: None of this round's own. What it opened, it closed:
The seat, the model repairs it forced, and the layout disagreement one layer
under it are all landed and gated, in Rust and in a subprocess demo.
The counterfactual that PASSED is now an in-process gate, and the plan was
re-run to 11/11.
The third-consumer grep found six copies of the move/press/release triple and
lifted them; the drag stays written out because its move happens BETWEEN the
press and the release and that ordering is what it tests.
Two things are STATED LIMITS rather than carry, written here so the next reader
does not have to rediscover that they were considered:
`measured_text_extent`'s record is written by a measurement, so an
out-of-scope call made before anything has measured still answers `None` —
the window between a shell's boot and its first paint. Strictly narrower than
the old behaviour rather than a new gap. Recording at seed time instead would
put a second writer beside this one, and a record that can drift from the
provider is worse than one that arrives a frame late.
The remove seat is drawn on every laid-out row because the form holds the row
and `ConfigForm::remove` therefore succeeds — a derivation, held to by
`r1686_every_row_with_a_seat_is_a_row_the_form_will_remove`. A rule making
some rows unremovable would turn `RowBox::remove` into an `Option`, and the
type change is what would force every consumer to handle it. The reference's
own rule is `!derived`, and this tree has no derived rows to distinguish yet.
External, unchanged: the vello and Mnemosyne-upstream items already on the
permanent list.

gave the cause (estimate 99px vs shaped 92px for `qos.priority`), and the repair

owner scope.

`pinion-widget-paint`, `pinion-chart`, `hello-node-lab` — all green.

exactly two callers in the tree (`pinion-chart`'s axis fit and the config-form
painter), so the sweep is every chart demo plus every demo of the one screen
that paints a form, plus the two grid scrub demos that hit-test measured text.

R1686.1.decision_summary:
R1686.1 — bump the statechart engine to upstream main.

Four commits, and one of them changes what a document this tree writes MEANS:
`datamodel` now selects a language rather than decorating the header, typed so
an unsupported value cannot reach code generation, with W3C SCXML B.1 enforced
per sub-section. Upstream's own message records that twenty documents declared
`null` or `lua` while using value expressions.

Every one of this tree's twelve widget statecharts declares `datamodel="null"`,
so that enforcement is aimed squarely at them. None uses a value expression —
the one `<assign>` this tree contains is a sentence in a comment explaining why
there is none — and the bump is what proves it rather than the grep that
suggested it: `sce-build` and `sce-rust-runtime` recompiled at the new rev and
the generated state machines still build and pass.

The second commit reaches `log` through the runtime so a consumer declares only
SCE, which changes the Rust template every generated machine is emitted from.
That is the one that touches this tree's own output, and it is covered by the
same run.

The other two are upstream's own build and mutation-verdict infrastructure.
changes_bullets: `vendor/sce` gitlink, both `Cargo.toml` revs and `Cargo.lock` move together
to `7e46a5f8` — the triple pin `tools/pin_sync.py --check-dual-pin` enforces.
verification_bullets: `pin_sync.py --check-dual-pin`: green, and it caught the intermediate state —
`git submodule update --remote` moves the WORKTREE and leaves the index at the
old rev, so the gitlink needs staging before the three agree.
`cargo test -p pinion-runtime -p pinion-core` at the new rev: green. Confirmed
from the build log that `sce-build` and `sce-rust-runtime` compiled at
`7e46a5f8` rather than the cached old rev — which is the whole point of the
triple pin, since a manifest left behind builds the previous engine and the run
proves nothing.
Aimed at what upstream moved: the twelve `datamodel="null"` documents this tree
owns, against a release that now enforces W3C B.1 per sub-section.
carry_forward_bullets: None. The statechart-widget demos are running as this lands; a red there is
paid off as its own round, which is the standing rule for a signal that arrives
after the local gates that authorise a push.

R1687.decision_summary:
R1687 — what leaves the screen: the graph says how it is brought up, and the
settings form says what it could not express.

The screen's operation table has carried `export the configuration` and
`produce the launch script` as absent on BOTH channels since R1677 — no verb,
no gesture. They are the last two of the behaviour reference's own "what leaves
the screen" group, and the reference writes them as one group because they are
ONE derivation rendered twice: the launch order, each node's configuration
document, and the rows of its form the document could not carry. Building
either alone means building the derivation and using half of it, and the unused
half is the one that then drifts.

Two substrate pieces carry it, and each was forced by trying to write the
consumer rather than designed in advance.

`Document::launch_order` (pinion-node-graph) — the order falls out of the link
direction by Kahn's walk. The first draft bucketed by "is dialled / dials out"
and justified skipping a topological order with "two peers that dial each other
are a legal mesh, so no such order exists". Both halves were false: `connect`
refuses a cycle outright, so an authored tree is acyclic by construction, and
mutual reachability lives in the OBSERVED layer, which is not authored and not
deployed. With the excuse gone the bucketing was simply wrong — in a chain of
four the middle two share a bucket and a NAME decides their order while the
links demand the reverse. The four words stay as the reported REASON a node
sits where it does, which is what a reader wants and what the order cannot say.
A node switched off is not started and its links go with it, which is two
claims rather than one.

`ConfigForm::compose` (pinion-core) — an asymmetry that had been there since
R1651. The form's READ half is total and says so in its own documentation:
`adopt` places every leaf or NAMES it in `Adopted::unplaceable`, "nothing is
dropped quietly", because a configuration written by a newer target is the
normal case. The WRITE half was all-or-nothing: one unparseable row and
`document()` answers an error instead of the other forty rows, which are fine
and are what somebody asked for. The gap was invisible while the only caller
was a launch gate, because a gate only ever wants the yes-or-no. `compose` is
the total form and `document` is now its narrowing rather than a second walk,
so the pair a caller most needs to trust — "is this shippable" and "what did
not fit" — cannot disagree.

The `unexpressed` population is deliberately smaller than the reference's. It
has two sources — a value that cannot be encoded, and a row that is not a
configuration path at all — and `ConfigField` is declared with the key BEING
the path, verbatim, so there is no second kind of row to fall out. Inventing a
table of run-only keys here would invent the distinction the form was designed
without.

Three defects were found by looking at the running screen and by generalising
the gate that repair earned: a control's own name painted as `ho…`, captions
authored with their own widths so two of three hung outside the button they
name, and the zoom readout painted two pixels inside the `+` button. The
toolbar's declared width was a sentence nobody read and had been wrong since
R1678; it is measured now, on both halves, and the window's floor is asserted
to be their sum. That floor moved 1316 -> 1442, which is a real cost stated
rather than absorbed.
changes_bullets: `pinion-node-graph::deploy` — `Document::launch_order(tree) -> Vec<Placed>`,
the order a graph's nodes have to be started in, derived from the link
direction by Kahn's walk over the reversed edges, deterministic by display
NAME among the ready (an id is minted in authoring order, so ordering by it
would make the plan a fact about the sequence somebody drew the graph in).
`Bringup` (First / Between / Last / Alone) is the reported REASON rather than
the sort key. A disabled node is not started and the links touching it stop
constraining the rest. Total anyway: whatever the walk cannot place goes at
the end in name order rather than being dropped.
`pinion-core::widgets::config_form` — `ConfigForm::compose() -> Composed`,
the total counterpart of `document()`, mirroring `Adopted`: the document
holding every row that could be expressed, plus `Vec<Unexpressed>` naming
each row that could not with `Unexpressible::{Defective, Collides}` and the
value AS THE ROW SHOWS IT. `document()` is re-expressed as the narrowing of
it; `place` answers the taken prefix rather than a `DocumentError`, so
neither caller has an arm for a variant it cannot produce.
`hello-node-lab` — the two operations, on both channels. `deploy::plan` is
the one derivation; `as_document` renders it for an agent and `as_script`
for a person, split per host with the unexpressed rows carried as comments.
Actions `export` / `script` and toolbar seats `lab.toolbar.config` (which
reported the SELECTED card's key count, a different question at a different
scope) and the new `lab.toolbar.script` beside it. Read slot `produced`
holds both artifacts, latched — producing one is an operation, and a slot
that already held the answer would have nothing to witness.
`hello-node-lab` — `seat_caption` derives a toolbar caption from its seat;
the view-reset seat widened 34 -> 48 (its label painted `ho…`); the zoom
readout narrowed 40 -> 36 (it was painted two pixels inside the `+`
button); `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER` 300 -> 426, wrong since R1678 and now
measured by a test on both halves; `MIN_W` 1316 -> 1442 in consequence.
`hello-node-lab` — every pressable toolbar seat gains an access node. The
strip holding the launch control had none at all.
The specification publishes `floor` (`MIN_W` x `MIN_H`); two demos were
carrying their own copy of that number.
`spec::OPERATIONS` — the two rows gain verb and gesture, witnessing
`produced`. `ABSENT_OPERATIONS` 4 -> 2.
verification_bullets: Local gates — the crates whose behaviour changed and the demos the change can
move, both chosen by measurement rather than by rule of thumb.
`cargo test -p pinion-core -p pinion-node-graph -p pinion-widget-paint
-p hello-node-lab` — green. `cargo clippy` over the same four with
`--all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` — green.
Demo blast radius COUNTED rather than guessed: `ConfigForm` has exactly one
example consumer (`hello-node-lab`), and the toolbar's geometry moved, so the
set is every demo that names that screen — nine, all green. Three were red
first and each red was this round's own consequence caught by a gate doing
its job: the tag-family pin (10 -> 11 members), a demo carrying its own copy
of the window floor, and the second copy of the operation roster.
New demo `r1687_what_leaves_the_screen.py`, 49 assertion sites over ten
sections, driving the real application: the declaration on both channels, the
two seats pressed at their CORNERS, the artifacts absent until asked for, the
plan's order checked against the LINKS the screen publishes rather than
against a list written in the demo, one file and exactly one start line per
node, a branch per host, the script's heredoc order equal to the document's
order, a disabled card leaving both artifacts, an unexpressible value carried
into the document, the script and the toast, no toolbar caption cut or
painted outside its seat, and the wire and the seats producing the same plan.
Counterfactuals 8/8 caught, each run against the whole suite rather than one
test:
1. bucket sort instead of Kahn — caught (the four-deep chain).
2. a disabled node's links kept — caught, on the ORDER rather than on a
missing node, which is the half a fixture misses.
3. `compose` drops the rows it can express — caught by the substrate itself
(2 tests) and by the screen.
4. `compose` swallows a defective row silently — caught, BUT NOT BY THIS
ROUND'S OWN SYMMETRY TEST. Because `document` is derived from `compose`,
the bug moved both sides of the biconditional together and they agreed on
the wrong thing; what caught it was R1651's pre-existing test with a
hard-coded expectation. The check now compares the unexpressed rows
against `defects()`, an independent walk, and re-running the same
counterfactual takes it from 2 failures to 3.
5. the old, wrong `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER` — caught.
6. the seat narrowed so its caption is cut — PASSED at first, and that was
the round's sharpest finding: the caption kept its own authored width, so
it hung outside the seat instead of eliding inside it and the check had
nothing to see. Captions are derived from the seat now and the gate asks
both questions; re-run, caught.
7. one seat dropped from the accessibility roster — caught.
8. the script ordered differently from the document — caught in both layers.
The screen was RUN and looked at, on a private display, three times: before
the round (which is how `ho…` was found), after the caption repair, and at
the close.
`python3 tools/phase_b_tally.py` — no STALE, no UNDECLARED; `--selftest`
passes. `mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` — T1 reject 0, no new orphan.
carry_forward_bullets: Two of the reference's operations remain absent on both channels, and they are
this round's own successors rather than carry: fit the graph to the view, and
go to the first problem. `ABSENT_OPERATIONS` is 2 and the ratchet refuses a
growth.
Stated, because a round that discovers a cost should not bury it: the toolbar
is now what dictates this screen's minimum width, and its two clusters fill it
exactly at the floor. The next seat added to either half raises the minimum
window again — a test says so rather than a comment, which is the difference
this round was about. The two absent operations above both want a toolbar seat.
Registered as debt this round:
[[debt-a-caption-is-authored-with-its-own-width]] — the class the passing
counterfactual found. Captions on THIS screen's toolbar are derived from
their seat and gated; nothing checks the same relation on any other screen,
and the check that exists reads `scene/text_painted`, which every screen
already answers. The population was not counted.
Not carry, stated so the next reader does not look for it: the `unexpressed`
population is smaller than the reference's by construction, not by omission —
`ConfigField`'s key IS the configuration path, so there is no second kind of
row to fall out of the document.

R1688.decision_summary:
Where the canvas is pointed: the analyser screen learns to frame the whole
graph and to go to the first thing wrong with it, and the arithmetic behind
both moves into `pinion-node-graph` because two node canvases in this tree had
written it by hand.

These are the LAST two rows of the screen's operation table that were absent on
both channels, so the absence count reaches zero for the first time since the
table was written at R1677. Neither was difficult, and that is the argument for
the column existing rather than an argument against it: a census of what is ON a
screen is blind by construction to what the screen cannot DO — an operation that
is missing paints nothing, so no forward check can see the hole — and eleven
rounds of green sweeps sat over these two.

What is not a screen detail is where the arithmetic went. `hello-node-editor`
frames its graph by folding a union box, dividing the window by it, clamping
into a zoom range and pinning the box centre at the window centre; it anchors a
zoom by unprojecting the cursor at the old scale and re-projecting at the new

R1688.1.decision_summary:
R1687's CI went red on exactly one demo — `r1182_node_edge_autopan.py`, with
`C.3 the node rides the viewport 1:1 (offset 581.0 -> 584.0)` against a
tolerance of 2 — while passing every time locally. Paying that off is this
sub-round, and the rule it follows is the standing one: a red is diagnosed to a
cause, never re-run and forgotten ([[zero-flake-policy]]).

It was not a flaky demo. It was a demo whose instrument could not measure what
it claimed, in front of a real tearing defect.

MEASURED, in this order:

1. The demo's own header said the ride is read "through back-to-back read-only
   queries (no mutation between them, so no tick sneaks in)". False: two
   `query` calls are two RPC round-trips. Reading node-then-viewport instead of
   viewport-then-node moves the computed ride by **27 px** — the artefact IS the
   read order.
2. `scene/set_fps 0` does not stop it. With `pacing_state` confirming `fps: 0`
   and a drag held at the rim: two back-to-back reads move the viewport by 1 px,
   eleven by 135, and **one read + one second of wall clock + one read by 796**.
   The auto-pan advances on REAL time whatever a test does. That contradicts
   what `set_fps` documents, and it is registered as
   [[debt-fps-zero-does-not-freeze-a-not-at-rest-animation]] rather than papered
   over here.
3. Reading the ride from the PAINT instead — one call, so no read order exists —
   showed the node's painted position stable at ~693 px with occasional
   excursions of 4 to 11 px, about one run in six. Those are one tick's pan.
   `AutoPan::tick` wrote the scroll offset and then the dragged nodes' positions
   as **two separate signal writes**, so a frame landing between them painted a
   world that had scrolled and a node that had not yet followed. The rest of
   that editor already knows the rule — `apply_viewport` batches for exactly
   this reason and cites [[signal-batch-atomic-multi-axis-update]] — and this
   tick was the one multi-signal viewport write that did not.

So the repair is two things and a stated limit:

* `AutoPan::tick` is one `batch(...)`. That is a real defect fix: a torn frame
  during an auto-pan is visible to a person, not only to a test.
* The demo reads the ride from the paint, in one call, and its tolerance is
  DERIVED — `zoom / 2 + 1` for the three roundings, plus `AUTOPAN_SPEED * FRAME`
  = 15 px for the one frame of wall-clock pan a snapshot may catch it out of
  step. That second term is a limit of the instrument, written into the file
  with the measurement behind it, and it disappears when the debt above is
  closed.
* The check still has teeth, proven rather than asserted: a follow at half rate
  slides the node off the canvas entirely, and a follow of zero fails B.3.
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-node-editor/src/main.rs` — `AutoPan::tick` wraps its two signal
writes (the scroll offset, and the dragged members' positions) in one
`batch(...)`, with the measurement and the sibling precedent named.
`tools/demos/r1182_node_edge_autopan.py`:
* `painted_x` — the node's painted left edge, from ONE `scene/snapshot` call.
The left edge only: a card held against the rim is clipped there, so its
painted width changes as it rides while its position does not. A missing tag
is a named assertion rather than a `KeyError`, because that is how this
section's own defect arrives when the ride is broken badly enough.
* `ride_slack(zoom)` — the tolerance, derived from the rounding chain and the
auto-pan rate, with both terms written out and the second one attributed to
the framework debt it comes from.
* `settled_x` — the baseline, taken once two consecutive snapshots agree.
`grab_to` returns as soon as the last drag step is sent and the node's follow
lands on the next frame, which was measured 11 px out on one run in ten.
Failing to settle is reported as the ride being broken, by name.
* `assert_pinned` — reads ONCE. The first draft of this repair re-read inside
its own failure message and printed `550 against 550` for a genuine failure,
which is the very defect being repaired, committed by the repair.
* Sections (C) and (I) both use it. (I) carried the identical false "atomic
snapshot" comment and the identical tolerance, and failed on the first re-run
after (C) was fixed — one cause, two sites.

* with the derived slack as well: **15 of 15 green**, then 10 of 10 more after

R1688.1.publishable_decision_summary:
R1687's CI went red on exactly one demo — `r1182_node_edge_autopan.py`, with
`C.3 the node rides the viewport 1:1 (offset 581.0 -> 584.0)` against a
tolerance of 2 — while passing every time locally. Paying that off is this
sub-round, and the rule it follows is the standing one: a red is diagnosed to a
cause, never re-run and forgotten ([[zero-flake-policy]]).

It was not a flaky demo. It was a demo whose instrument could not measure what
it claimed, in front of a real tearing defect.

MEASURED, in this order:

1. The demo's own header said the ride is read "through back-to-back read-only
   queries (no mutation between them, so no tick sneaks in)". False: two
   `query` calls are two RPC round-trips. Reading node-then-viewport instead of
   viewport-then-node moves the computed ride by **27 px** — the artefact IS the
   read order.
2. `scene/set_fps 0` does not stop it. With `pacing_state` confirming `fps: 0`
   and a drag held at the rim: two back-to-back reads move the viewport by 1 px,
   eleven by 135, and **one read + one second of wall clock + one read by 796**.
   The auto-pan advances on REAL time whatever a test does. That contradicts
   what `set_fps` documents, and it is registered as
   [[debt-fps-zero-does-not-freeze-a-not-at-rest-animation]] rather than papered
   over here.
3. Reading the ride from the PAINT instead — one call, so no read order exists —
   showed the node's painted position stable at ~693 px with occasional
   excursions of 4 to 11 px, about one run in six. Those are one tick's pan.
   `AutoPan::tick` wrote the scroll offset and then the dragged nodes' positions
   as **two separate signal writes**, so a frame landing between them painted a
   world that had scrolled and a node that had not yet followed. The rest of
   that editor already knows the rule — `apply_viewport` batches for exactly
   this reason and cites [[signal-batch-atomic-multi-axis-update]] — and this
   tick was the one multi-signal viewport write that did not.

* `AutoPan::tick` is one `batch(...)`. That is a real defect fix: a torn frame
  during an auto-pan is visible to a person, not only to a test.
* The demo reads the ride from the paint, in one call, and its tolerance is
  DERIVED — `zoom / 2 + 1` for the three roundings, plus `AUTOPAN_SPEED * FRAME`
  = 15 px for the one frame of wall-clock pan a snapshot may catch it out of
  step. That second term is a limit of the instrument, written into the file
  with the measurement behind it, and it disappears when the debt above is
  closed.
* The check still has teeth, proven rather than asserted: a follow at half rate
  slides the node off the canvas entirely, and a follow of zero fails B.3.
