two `unspecified` entries. The two `inline` entries did not move for twenty-three
rounds, and the reason recorded beside them was cost: "a refactor of a 16.9k-line
binding".

THE INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG, AND MEASURING IT IS THE ROUND. Asked over the wire,
standing on the dashboard, where this section's surfaces actually are:

    shell.canvas    1096x802 at (52, 98)     <- the page region a screen is given
    shell.subbar    1096x46  at (52, 52)     <- that section's layout bar, ABOVE
    shell.palette    292x848 at (1148, 52)   <- that section's palette, BESIDE

A host paints a section's chrome outside the page region because that is what
chrome is, and a screen judges what it paints. So the recorded route would have
produced a verdict blind to 298,032 px2 of its own section — including the
palette, which is where the reference makes its whole argument about what the
first release contains. The expensive route was also the wrong one, and nobody
had checked because the instruction was written from the type rather than from a
frame.

THE DECISION: A SCREEN AND A VERDICT ARE TWO AXES. `pinion_screen::SectionJudge`
answers one question — how much of a written specification is on the frame — and
grants nothing else: no paint, no hit test, no keys, no accessibility tree. It is
registered per destination through `ScreenRoster::judging`, which refuses a key
the roster does not hold, a key it declares closed, a second judge at one key,
and a key that already has a screen. That last refusal is the one worth having:
two things claiming to answer for one section would make a verdict depend on
which registration a lookup reached first.

The report is not `Option`, unlike `Screen::conformance`. A binding is mounted
for a hundred reasons and judging is not one of them, so a screen may honestly
answer nothing; a judge exists for no other purpose, so registering one IS the
claim that this section is compared with something. A host with nothing to
compare registers nothing and the row still reads `Inline`.

WHAT A JUDGE CANNOT WORK OUT FOR ITSELF, and why the framework tells it. A
mounted screen that is not showing has no recorded frame, so `report_from_paint`
answers away for all of it structurally. A host's inline page has no surface of
its own: its marks are the host's, and the host's store is full of whatever page
it is painting INSTEAD. A judge could notice that by finding none of its own
parts, and that is exactly the escape hatch R1742 refused one level down — "away
because I found nothing" makes every absence an excuse. So `Showing` is handed in
by the roster, taken from the `Journey` once, and it is the same value the row
beside the verdict publishes: the verdict and the label on it cannot disagree.

WHAT THE SECTION IS JUDGED AGAINST. `docs/analyzer-dashboard-spec.json` is new
and is a claim about the behaviour reference in neutral vocabulary: the layout
bar's four parts, the palette panel's heading, its three group headings, its
thirteen entries and two counts, and the four cards the board opens with. It is a
SECOND document for one screen, which is normally this project's defect, and the
seam is evidence rather than screen: `analyzer-board-spec.json` beside it holds
five surfaces two of which are not paint at all (a drop contract is a
declaration; a drop standing is what a router hands a source mid-gesture) and
three of which exist only while a placement is in flight. Those are judged by a
driven sweep that can perform a gesture; this one is judged from the frame, at
any moment, by a running application answering a host. A paint-stamped report
that quietly answered two of its surfaces from a declaration would be the defect
R1758 repaired one level up. The two documents name disjoint surfaces and a test
asserts it.

WRITING THE SPECIFICATION DOWN FOUND THREE THINGS A READER SEES AND NOTHING
COULD NAME. The layout bar draws four things and three were tagged: the placed
count was loose ink, so the only part of that bar which is not a control was the
one no specification could reach. The palette panel's own title and its one-line
hint were loose ink for the same reason. All three are addressed now, which is
what makes two of the five surfaces checkable at all — and the fourth thing was
a reproduction gap: the reference writes which release fills each palette group
into the group's own heading, and this build painted the group and dropped the
release. It is derived from the section's tier now rather than typed beside it,
so a section retiered cannot keep a heading that says otherwise.

THE TWO DIFFERENCES THIS BUILD HAS ARE DECLARED, not deleted. Its palette hint
offers a second way to place a widget (the reference offers one), and its third
group is named for a wider set than the reference's third because it holds two
widgets that act on the system under study rather than report on it. Both are
ledger entries with their reasons, which is the direction this project's rule
about the reference runs: what the reference has and this build lacks is built,
and what this build has beyond it is kept and recorded.

R1762.decision_summary:
R1762 — the last unjudged section answers, and the page it is about is the one
the reference draws.

WHAT FORCED IT. R1738 made the assembled analysis tool count the sections it had
been judged on: four of six unjudged. R1742 made a screen publish a verdict it
already computed; R1747 corrected a reason that had been false for nine rounds
and published a second; R1758 made a verdict say what it was read from; R1761
found the route recorded for the last two was itself wrong and built
`SectionJudge` instead. One entry was left, `settings`, and the reason it could
not ride along with `dashboard` is the whole of this round: A PIN THAT SPECIFIES
ONLY WHAT THE BUILD ALREADY DRAWS IS A DOCUMENT THAT CANNOT FAIL. Measured at
R1761 against the behaviour reference, this build's preferences page was missing
THREE of the reference's TEN rows — a capture-source row and a retention row in
the first group, a payload-format row in the second — had neither the page
heading the reference opens with nor the build strip it closes with, and its
four group headings were loose ink no specification could address. So the page
was built first.

THE FRAMEWORK HALF: A COLLAPSED CHOOSER IS NOT A FORM'S PRIVATE PART. R1732
built the control — a box holding the word in effect, a chevron, and a roster
that appears over everything only while it is open — inside `config_form`,
because a configuration form was the one thing that needed it. Its geometry took
a `RowBox`, its paint took a `ConfigField`, and its roster's tags were composed
from a configuration path; none of that is about choosing. The second consumer
arrived and is not a form, and the three routes open to it were: hand-roll a box
with a word and an arrow (the class R1673 measured, and this shell already
carries one instance in its own preset menu), paint a whole form to get one row
of it, or lift. `pinion_widget_paint::chooser` is the lift: a caller brings the
rectangle, the word, the `Picker` while one is open, and the ROOM the roster
must stay inside — the last of those stays the caller's for R1732's own reason,
that a surface laid into a region it cannot see the bottom of would open a
roster off the end of a scrolled viewport.

WHAT THE PAGE GAINED, all of it the reference's: two value rows whose control is
that chooser (and whose capture-source row writes THE APPLICATION BAR'S source,
which is why the reference puts it on this page), a payload-format chip row, the
page's own heading and the line under it, the build strip it closes with, and an
address for each of the four group headings. Opening a chooser is NOT a write —
the value stays where it is until a word is chosen, which is the rule `Picker`
is built on and the one the floor's own collapsed control breaks by committing
on every arrow press.

★★★★★ AND THE PAGE SCROLLS, WHICH THE GATE FOUND RATHER THAN THE AUTHOR. The
reference's preferences body is `overflow:auto` and this one was not, which held
while the page was four short cards. The moment the reference's own rows were
built, the appearance group landed at y=872 in a region ending at y=900 and the
build strip at y=958 — painted where no press could reach them. Nothing in the
round's own reasoning noticed; `r1695` failed with "the Light segment: expected
light, got dark", which is what a control below the fold looks like from the
outside. The page has its own viewport now, and the hit test folds its offset
through one helper that three hit tests were about to write out separately.

THE PIN, and the two differences it declares. `docs/analyzer-settings-spec.json`
fixes seven surfaces and twenty-eight parts, of which `rows` is the reference's
ten in the reference's order — a row missing, renamed or moved between groups
all read as a difference. Titled by what the frame READS where the reference
fixes the words (the headings, the row titles and their sentences, the booked
rows' verbs, the appearance choices, the payload formats) and by the pin's own
names where a part is a value a session changes or a control that draws no words
at all. Two remainders are declared rather than papered over: the third group's
heading is the shorter half of the reference's, and the last row's sentence is
below the fold at the opening scroll position — which is a fact about the frame
a verdict is read from, and the alternative (an away-condition of *the page
cannot show all ten rows at once*) was refused for R1742's reason.

THE COUNT REACHES ZERO. Measured over the wire: `sections 8, judged 6,
unjudged 0, closed 2`. Every section of this application a reader can arrive at
is compared with a written specification. `docs/analyzer-sections-spec.json`'s
remainder is empty — and it is still asserted as an equality, because empty is a
claim rather than the absence of one.

R1763.decision_summary:
R1763 — leaving a section takes its painted marks with it, so what an
application claims to have reproduced is what a reader can see.

WHAT FORCED IT. `pinion_screen`'s central rule is *the screen the journey is at
is the only one anything reaches*, and leaving a screen already took its
externals, its windows and its accessibility tree with it. Its MARKS were the
one thing it left behind, and since R1742 every verdict in this tree is read
from those. Measured on the assembled analysis tool at R1763, walking every
section once and returning to the first:

    packets  showing=false  25 of 26  away=0  reconciles=true
    keys     showing=false  21 of 21  away=0  reconciles=true
    logs     showing=false  15 of 15  away=0  reconciles=true
    headline                88 of 133 reproduced

Three sections reporting a reproduced specification about frames nobody could
see, and a headline built out of them. R1742 published `showing` beside each row
so a reader could TELL, which was the honest half; this is the other half.

⚠ AND IT STOPPED BEING ONLY A STALE NUMBER AT R1762.
`ApplicationConformance::conforms` is `unjudged == 0 && declared == 0 && every
judged report reconciles`, and R1762 brought the first two to zero. Without this
round an application could report conformance earned entirely by frames that had
left it; what was preventing that was one screen's session-dependent surfaces
happening to be away, which is a coincidence rather than a gate.

★★★★★ THE ENTRY RE-MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE DEBT'S OWN DIAGNOSIS, and the
correction is what made the fix small. The debt file (R1742) said the window
path never forgets: *`forget_painted_regions` exists and the single-surface
fixture path uses it; the window path does not*. Re-measured before writing any
code, that is FALSE and has been since R1737 — `announce_external_sizes` drops a
surface's marks, its announced size and its pointer arrivals the moment it
paints nothing. What is true is narrower and is the whole defect: that loop's
population is the tags in the STATE SCENE, and a screen the journey has left has
no externals there at all, so the loop never reaches it. The forgetting was
already built; what was missing is that nothing told it about a screen that had
gone away.

THE FIX IS THEREFORE THE ROSTER'S, not the window's. `ScreenRoster::latch` runs
once per frame and is already the moment that names the current screen — so it
forgets the marks of every mounted screen the journey is not at. The debt file's
recorded prescription was a per-window store, on the reasoning that "forget
everything this frame did not paint" is wrong when one frame paints one window;
that reasoning is sound and this fix does not need it, because the roster knows
which screens exist and which one is here rather than inferring it from what a
frame happened to contain.

WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH, stated rather than assumed: a screen's own nested
surfaces — a text field that owns focus is an `External` of its own — keep their
marks. Nothing reads them for a verdict; a section's judge reads its ROOT's
store, which is what R1758's ancestry attribution made sufficient.

★★★★★ AND A DEMO WAS PINNING THE DEFECT. R1747 asserted that the row read from
the dashboard is the SAME verdict as the row read while standing in the section,
and called it *R1742's hardest defect, asserted rather than rediscovered*. The
two were equal because the marks stayed — so the assertion was holding the stale
behaviour in place. It now asserts the honest answer: read from elsewhere the
section reproduces nothing, every surface is away, and the SPECIFICATION it is
judged against is unchanged, which is what says only the frame moved.
changes_bullets: FRAMEWORK
`ScreenRoster::latch` forgets the painted marks of every mounted screen the
journey is not at. One loop over the roster's own screens, keyed by
`Screen::tag`, once per frame — the moment that already names the current
screen, so the fact and its consequence are one expression.
Its doc carries the measurement that forced it, why the window path could not
reach it (that loop's population is the state scene's tags, and a screen the
journey has left has none), and what it does not reach (a screen's nested
surfaces keep their marks; nothing reads them for a verdict).
`r1763_leaving_a_screen_forgets_the_marks_it_painted` asks the STORE rather than
a verdict, because a verdict is what this defect reached through — and it
asserts the symmetry, so walking back is covered by the same test.
DEMOS
`r1763_leaving_a_section_takes_its_verdict_with_it.py` is NEW (4 sections, 12
named checks): the headline before a walk, the headline after it, that standing
in a section fills it, and that the host's own pages reach the same honesty by
the other mechanism — their judge is TOLD where the reader is.
`r1747` asserted the DEFECT and is repaired: it required the verdict read from
elsewhere to equal the one read while standing there, which was true only
because the marks stayed. It now asserts that the section reproduces nothing and
every surface is away, AND that the canon it is judged against is unchanged —
which is what says only the frame moved.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE, over the wire, walking every section once and returning:
`packets 25/26 away=0 reconciles=true`, `keys 21/21`, `logs 15/15` — all three
`showing: false` — and a headline of `88 of 133`.
MEASURED AFTER, the same walk: every section a reader is not looking at is away,
reproduces nothing, and does not reconcile; the headline is `26 of 133`, which
is the number it was at BOOT. What the application claims to have reproduced is
now what a reader can see, whatever they walked through to get there.
cargo test — `pinion-screen` 27 + 3 + 1 (one new: the store is asked directly,
and the symmetry with it, so walking back is covered by the same test).
New demo `r1763_leaving_a_section_takes_its_verdict_with_it.py`: 4 sections, 12
named checks, and it drives the walk that produced the measurement above.
Counterfactuals 2/2 CAUGHT: the sign of the comparison (the screen the reader is
ON gives up its marks), and forgetting by a name that addresses no surface. The
first draft of the second did not compile — it removed the loop's only use of
its binding, which is the trap the driver's own header records.
BLAST: every demo that drives any of the five section binaries — 62 — of which
61 pass. The one that does not is `r1684`, and it is not this round's: it drives
`hello-node-lab` STANDALONE, so `ScreenRoster::latch` is never called in it at
all, and its log ends `gpu context init failed: wgpu device request failed:
Parent device is lost` after 54 window launches — the infrastructure class R1758
recorded by name.
🟥 AND A DEMO WAS PINNING THE DEFECT, which is the finding this round would have
missed by running only its own gates: `r1747` asserted that the verdict read
from the dashboard EQUALS the one read while standing in the section. It was
true only because the marks stayed.
carry_forward_bullets: `debt-nothing-forgets-a-surface-that-stopped-painting` is CLOSED for what it was
opened about — a section's verdict outliving the frame it was read from — and
its own recorded diagnosis was corrected on the way (the window path has
forgotten since R1737; what it cannot reach is a screen with no externals in the
state scene). The residue is named rather than folded away: a screen's NESTED
surfaces keep their marks after the reader leaves. Nothing reads them for a
verdict today, which is why this round did not chase them, and the day something
does the population is `Screen::externals` rather than `Screen::tag`.
`ApplicationConformance::conforms` can now only be true about ONE FRAME, which
means it can only be true for an application with one open section. That is the
honest reading of "a verdict is about a frame" and it makes the predicate
unreachable for every multi-section application in this tree — a fact worth
saying out loud rather than discovering later. What a reader of an assembled
application actually wants is a verdict over a JOURNEY: every section judged
while it was showing, and none of it stale. That is a mechanism this round did
not build and did not need; it is the next thing this axis is short of.

R1764.decision_summary:
R1764 — a verdict titled by painted words is a verdict the fold can decide, and
the CI runner decided one.

WHAT FORCED IT. R1762's own gate went red on CI and green on every local run,
including single-threaded:

    `theme` is not what docs/analyzer-settings-spec.json declares:
      `0` is specified as "Dark" and reads "<this part is painted and draws no words>"
      `1` is specified as "Light" and reads "<this part is painted and draws no words>"

THE CAUSE IS THE FOLD, and R1762 had already written half of it down. The
preferences page is taller than its region — that round gave it a viewport for
exactly that reason — so the appearance group, last of four, is cut to a sliver
at the opening scroll position. R1762 declared that for the ROW (its sentence is
below the fold and the pin carries a remainder saying so) and did not notice
that the row's two CHOICES are inside the same sliver. Whether their labels
survive the clip is a fact about where the page happens to be scrolled and how
the host lays a button's label out; here they survived and on the runner they did
not, so the verdict was being decided by the machine.

THE FIX IS WHICH ACCOUNT THE JUDGE READS, not what the pin says. `theme` is
titled from the screen's own table now rather than from the frame's words. The
pin is unchanged — `Dark` and `Light` are what the reference draws and what
`spec::THEMES` holds — so the canon a reader checks against is the same document
it was, and what moved is that the reading no longer depends on a clip.

★★★★★ THE LESSON, and it is the one this project keeps paying for in a new
costume: a sample finds only what it was aimed at. R1762 chose `parts_as_read`
for this surface because the words are the reference's, ran it, and saw them —
on one machine, at one scroll position. The rule the round should have applied
is its own: a part whose words a session can take off the frame is titled by the
table, and only a part that is always on the frame is titled by what it reads.
changes_bullets: `crate::judge::settings_built` reads `theme` with `parts_titled` rather than
`parts_as_read`, from the same table the pin's canon holds.
`docs/analyzer-settings-spec.json` is UNCHANGED: the canon is the words the
reference draws, and this round moved which of the two accounts of those words
is compared against it.
verification_bullets: The red: `gh run view 32493366680` — one job, one step, one test
(`r1762_the_preferences_page_reproduces_its_specification_or_says_why_not`),
100 passed 1 failed.
Reproduced-by-reasoning rather than by re-running: the test is green here at the
default thread count and single-threaded, so the difference is the environment,
and the message names the mechanism — two parts painted, neither reading any
words. Both sit in the sliver the appearance group is cut to at the opening
scroll position, which R1762 had already measured for the row above them
(painted 64px, reachable 28px).
cargo test -p hello-analyzer-shell — 101 passed, 0 failed, at the default thread
count and again with `--test-threads=1`.
Demos: r1738, r1747, r1761, r1762, r1763 all green against the rebuilt binary.
NOT DONE and stated: nothing yet asserts that a surface titled by what it reads
is on the frame at the scroll position the judge runs at. That is the general
form of this defect and it is written into the round's carry rather than
implied.
carry_forward_bullets: The general form of this defect has no gate: a surface titled by what it READS
is one whose verdict a clip can change, and nothing checks that such a surface is
fully on the frame at the scroll position the judge runs at. Four of this page's
seven surfaces are read-titled and three of them happen to be above the fold.
"Happen to" is the whole problem; it is the same sentence R1762's own carry used
about the node lab masking a stale verdict.
The cheap shape is a per-surface assertion inside the page's own gate — for each
read-titled surface, its parts' painted rectangles are inside the page region —
and it is cheap because both numbers are already published (`scene/bbox` answers
`bbox` and `window` and their difference IS the clip).

R1766.decision_summary:
The code this framework actually runs is a tracked artifact now, and the
generator is a verifier.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Every widget's state machine — the thing that decides what a
button does — was produced by the SCE code generator into `OUT_DIR` on every
build and never tracked. Fifteen modules, 9,591 lines, 414 KB, living only
inside a hash-named temporary directory: git could not see them, no diff of
them had ever been read, `git blame` could not attribute a behavioural change
to the pin that brought it, and the only way to read them at all was to build.
This is the same class this repository keeps re-recording — a number with no
recorded evidence is not a measurement (R1519), a prose warning is not a gate
(R1495) — in its sharpest form yet: AN ARTIFACT NOBODY CAN READ IS NOT
REVIEWED. R1765 is what it cost. To answer "did this engine bump change what we
run" that round had to build `pinion-core` twice against two pins and diff two
`OUT_DIR`s by hand, and it closed by registering the absence of a tool to do it.

THE PRESCRIPTION THAT ROUND RECORDED WAS THE WRONG ONE, and this is the round's
first finding. `debt-a-pin-bump-cannot-say-what-its-emit-changed` asked for a
tool that builds twice and diffs — which is a SECOND ACCOUNT of a question git
already answers for tracked files. R1739 refused exactly that shape when it
derived `Sent` from the engine's own discard counter rather than keeping a
second tally. The right move is the one this project states as a rule: do not
fix the rule, make the rule UNNECESSARY. So the debt is closed by removal, not
by automation.

AND THE MECHANISM WAS ALREADY HERE, EXPORTED, UNADOPTED. `vendor/sce` commits
1,114 generated files and gates them with `b9_drift_detection`,
`drift-verify.yml` and `scripts/gates/drift-suites.sh`; and the whole apparatus
is public on the crate this tree ALREADY build-depends on —
`sce_build::forge::drift::{compute_source_hash, compute_template_hash,
render_header, prepend_or_replace_header, parse_embedded_hashes}`, plus
`find_template_dir` and `compile_scxml_lang_typed_with_section`. Measured
before writing anything: 0 of our 15 emitted files carried a drift header.
Upstream solved this and pinion never picked it up. Nothing was invented here
and no upstream work was needed.

THE SHAPE. `crates/pinion-core/generated/` holds the fifteen modules, each
carrying SCE's four-line drift header with `generated-at: 0`. The fifteen
`include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), ...))` sites now name the tracked path.
`build.rs` stopped generating and started REFUSING: it recomputes both digests
on every build and compares them against each file's header, so an edited chart
or a moved SCE pin is reported at `cargo build` rather than at `cargo test`.
`tests/statechart_emit.rs` is the complete half — it regenerates in memory and
byte-compares, and with `PINION_REGEN_STATECHARTS=1` it WRITES instead. The
writer and the judge are one piece of code on purpose, for the same reason the
debt's tool was refused: two of them can disagree.

★TRACKING THE EMIT MADE 67 OF THE GENERATOR'S OWN CITATIONS FALSE, AND AN OLD
GATE CAUGHT IT AT THE COMMIT. This was not foreseen. In a file this workspace
tracks, `§x` is a claim about THIS store, and every section number the
generator writes is a claim about SCE's — `scxml-D`, `synth-5-J-2`. The moment
those files became tracked, `validate-code-refs` read them as pinion citations
and rejected the commit with `section_missing=3`. The gate was RIGHT, and the
first repair reached for was wrong: `[plugins.set_equality_validator]
.scan_exclusions` looks like the tool and is not one — it DECLARES files that
`paths` does not reach so the coverage census can call them chosen rather than
missing, and it does not subtract from the scan. Measured with the exclusion in
place: scanned went 1106 → 1122 and the three violations stood. The repair is at
the IMPORT BOUNDARY instead, beside the inner-attribute strip that was already
there for the same kind of reason — what the generator writes for its own
repository is not valid in ours. The sigil is re-spelled on the way in, the
reference survives, and a new assertion keeps it true. It is confined to comment
lines because a blind replace would reach string literals, and that was measured
before it was written: all 67 sit on lines whose trimmed form starts with `//`.
Only 3 of the 67 had actually rejected — the matcher does not read
`synth-5-J-2` as an id at all — but a rule that fires on the subset the current
matcher happens to recognise is a rule that breaks when the matcher improves.

★THE BOOTSTRAP IS THE PROOF THAT NOTHING MOVED. The regenerated files were
compared against the snapshot R1765 took of the old `build.rs` output: 15 of 15
byte-identical once the four header lines and the added trailing newline are
accounted for. What this framework runs did not change; only where it lives.

★★CROSS-MACHINE REPRODUCIBILITY IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. R1765 closed saying
determinism across machines was likely but unproven. The gate was run on the
32-core build host, whose checkout path, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and cargo git
directory all differ from this one, and the byte comparison passed — which is
what says the artifact carries nothing about where it was produced. A third
machine checks it on every push, because CI runs `cargo test --workspace`.

WHAT THE TEMPLATE HASH BUYS, in this round's own terms: it is R1765's finding
as a one-line answer. That round spent two builds to learn the bump changed
nothing here; `template-hash` is a function of the pinned generator's Rust
templates, so an unchanged value now says it directly, on every build, for free.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-core/generated/` — fifteen tracked `{chart}_sm.rs` modules, each
carrying SCE's four-line drift header with `generated-at: 0`.
`build.rs` no longer generates. It recomputes `source-hash` and `template-hash`
on every build and refuses a tree whose committed emit was produced from other
inputs, naming the regen command in the message.
`tests/statechart_emit.rs` — regenerates in memory and byte-compares; with
`PINION_REGEN_STATECHARTS=1` it writes instead. Four assertions: the bytes
match, every module carries a current header, no module claims a section of
this store, and no module names an absolute path. The chart population is
`SourceSet`'s own walk, so a chart cannot be hashed-but-not-compiled.
The import boundary re-spells the generator's section sigils on comment lines,
beside the inner-attribute strip that was already there for the same reason.
The fifteen `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), ...))` sites now name the tracked
file. The `{chart}_sm.include.rs` shims SCE also wrote are gone — measured
unused by this tree, and all fifteen embedded this machine's absolute path.
`pre-push` gains the byte comparison as a ratchet; `CLAUDE.md` gains the
structure entry and the working-contract rule; `mnemosyne.toml` records what
`scan_exclusions` is, measured, since this round reached for it wrongly.
verification_bullets: COUNTERFACTUALS 5 of 5 CAUGHT, through `tools/counterfactual.py` with the whole
`cargo test -p pinion-core` suite as the gate: a chart edited without
regenerating; a hand-edited emit; an emit whose drift header was removed; an
emit carrying a forged header hash; and an emit re-introducing a section sigil.
The first, third and fourth are what `build.rs` exists for and the second is
what only the byte comparison can see, so the two halves were each shown to
catch what the other cannot.
THE BOOTSTRAP WAS COMPARED, not assumed: the regenerated modules against
R1765's snapshot of the previous `build.rs` output — 15 of 15 byte-identical
once the four header lines and the added trailing newline are accounted for.
Nothing about what this framework runs changed.
CROSS-MACHINE: the gate assertions pass on the 32-core build host, whose
repository path, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and cargo git checkout all differ from
this machine's. That is the measurement R1765 closed without.
`validate-code-refs` rc=0 with `section_missing=0`, from 3 at the first attempt
to stage these files. Workspace clippy (pedantic, `--all-targets`, vello) PASS.
`cargo fmt --all` leaves `generated/` untouched, which is expected — rustfmt
follows `mod` declarations and never enters an `include!`.
`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` EXITS 0 WITH NO TARGET REPORTING FAILED,
and the emit gate's own target reads `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed`.
★THAT SENTENCE IS DELIBERATELY NOT A TOTAL, and the reason is this round's third
finding. Two runs of the same command over the same tree reported 349 targets /
13,279 assertions and 348 / 13,257 — the difference is not the tests but the
EXTRACTION: `RUST_TEST_THREADS` parallelises inside each binary, the lines
interleave, and a regex over `^test result: ok\. N passed` silently loses some.
An earlier attempt to explain the drift by diffing test NAMES failed the same
way, reporting three appearing and two vanishing that this round never touched,
every one of which was present in both logs. So the honest verdict is cargo's
own exit status and the absence of any FAILED line; a workspace-wide count
pulled out of that log with a regex is not a census, and R1765's entry quotes
one taken the same way.
`pre-push` runs the byte comparison as a ratchet; CI runs `cargo test
--workspace` on every push, which is a third machine checking the same bytes.
NOT RUN and stated: the 636-demo sweep (CI's), and any check of the 222 example
renderers, which have the identical defect and are registered as their own debt
rather than fixed here.
carry_forward_bullets: 🟥THE SAME DEFECT IS STILL OPEN ONE LAYER UP, 222 TIMES. Measured this round:
`ls examples/*/build.rs` is 222 and every one of them emits `app.pinion.xml`
through `pinion_forge::compile_file` into `OUT_DIR` and `include!`s the result.
The sentence this round wrote about `pinion-core` holds there verbatim — those
are the binaries 636 demos drive, and what they run cannot be read as source.
Registered as its own debt file rather than carried as prose.
THE DERIVE LIST IS AN INPUT NEITHER HASH SEES. `STATE_EXTRA_DERIVES` /
`EVENT_EXTRA_DERIVES` in the test change the emit, and `source-hash` covers only
the charts while `template-hash` covers only the generator. Changing them
without regenerating is caught by the byte comparison alone — which runs at
`pre-push` and in CI, not at `cargo build`. Stated rather than hidden, and the
same is true of a hand-edited emit and of a generator gone non-deterministic.
THE SIGIL RE-SPELL IS A MUTATION OF UPSTREAM'S TEXT, and that is the honest
name for it. The committed emit is what the pinned generator produces THROUGH
THIS TREE'S IMPORT BOUNDARY, not what a bare `sce-codegen` run writes; the gate
compares against the same boundary, so the claim stays true, but a reader
diffing our file against upstream's raw output will find the sigils and the
stripped inner attributes. Both deviations are now stated in one place.
`libxml2-dev` / `libclang-dev` STAY on the workspace build path. Committing this
crate's emit frees `pinion-core`'s build script, but `pinion-forge` normal-deps
`sce-build` and all 222 examples build-dep `pinion-forge`, so the system
requirement is unchanged. Getting that benefit means the 222-site debt above,
plus possibly severing `pinion-forge`'s `sce-build` dependency — which exists
for diagnostic types in `wire.rs` and has NOT been measured as severable.
The template hash is taken over the generator's **Rust** template directory
because that is the directory the Rust arm is rooted at. R1765's measurement is
the supporting evidence — that bump moved three base-level templates and this
tree's emit did not change by one byte — but the claim rests on the loader's
rooting rather than on an assertion, and nothing here would notice if a future
generator started reading outside it.

(R1495) — in its sharpest form yet: AN ARTIFACT NOBODY CAN READ IS NOT
REVIEWED. R1765 is what it cost. To answer "did this engine bump change what we
run" that round had to build `pinion-core` twice against two pins and diff two
`OUT_DIR`s by hand, and it closed by registering the absence of a tool to do it.

THE PRESCRIPTION THAT ROUND RECORDED WAS THE WRONG ONE, and this is the round's
first finding. `debt-a-pin-bump-cannot-say-what-its-emit-changed` asked for a
tool that builds twice and diffs — which is a SECOND ACCOUNT of a question git
already answers for tracked files. R1739 refused exactly that shape when it
derived `Sent` from the engine's own discard counter rather than keeping a
second tally. The right move is the one this project states as a rule: do not
fix the rule, make the rule UNNECESSARY. So the debt is closed by removal, not
by automation.

AND THE MECHANISM WAS ALREADY HERE, EXPORTED, UNADOPTED. `vendor/sce` commits
1,114 generated files and gates them with `b9_drift_detection`,
`drift-verify.yml` and `scripts/gates/drift-suites.sh`; and the whole apparatus
is public on the crate this tree ALREADY build-depends on —
`sce_build::forge::drift::{compute_source_hash, compute_template_hash,
render_header, prepend_or_replace_header, parse_embedded_hashes}`, plus
`find_template_dir` and `compile_scxml_lang_typed_with_section`. Measured
before writing anything: 0 of our 15 emitted files carried a drift header.
Upstream solved this and pinion never picked it up. Nothing was invented here
and no upstream work was needed.

THE SHAPE. `crates/pinion-core/generated/` holds the fifteen modules, each
carrying SCE's four-line drift header with `generated-at: 0`. The fifteen
`include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), ...))` sites now name the tracked path.
`build.rs` stopped generating and started REFUSING: it recomputes both digests
on every build and compares them against each file's header, so an edited chart
or a moved SCE pin is reported at `cargo build` rather than at `cargo test`.
`tests/statechart_emit.rs` is the complete half — it regenerates in memory and
byte-compares, and with `PINION_REGEN_STATECHARTS=1` it WRITES instead. The
writer and the judge are one piece of code on purpose, for the same reason the
debt's tool was refused: two of them can disagree.

★TRACKING THE EMIT MADE 67 OF THE GENERATOR'S OWN CITATIONS FALSE, AND AN OLD
GATE CAUGHT IT AT THE COMMIT. This was not foreseen. In a file this workspace
tracks, `§x` is a claim about THIS store, and every section number the
generator writes is a claim about SCE's — `scxml-D`, `synth-5-J-2`. The moment
those files became tracked, `validate-code-refs` read them as pinion citations
and rejected the commit with `section_missing=3`. The gate was RIGHT, and the
first repair reached for was wrong: `[plugins.set_equality_validator]
.scan_exclusions` looks like the tool and is not one — it DECLARES files that
`paths` does not reach so the coverage census can call them chosen rather than
missing, and it does not subtract from the scan. Measured with the exclusion in
place: scanned went 1106 → 1122 and the three violations stood. The repair is at
the IMPORT BOUNDARY instead, beside the inner-attribute strip that was already
there for the same kind of reason — what the generator writes for its own
repository is not valid in ours. The sigil is re-spelled on the way in, the
reference survives, and a new assertion keeps it true. It is confined to comment
lines because a blind replace would reach string literals, and that was measured
before it was written: all 67 sit on lines whose trimmed form starts with `//`.
Only 3 of the 67 had actually rejected — the matcher does not read
`synth-5-J-2` as an id at all — but a rule that fires on the subset the current
matcher happens to recognise is a rule that breaks when the matcher improves.

★THE BOOTSTRAP IS THE PROOF THAT NOTHING MOVED. The regenerated files were
compared against the snapshot R1765 took of the old `build.rs` output: 15 of 15
byte-identical once the four header lines and the added trailing newline are
accounted for. What this framework runs did not change; only where it lives.

★★CROSS-MACHINE REPRODUCIBILITY IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. R1765 closed saying
determinism across machines was likely but unproven. The gate was run on the
32-core build host, whose checkout path, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and cargo git
directory all differ from this one, and the byte comparison passed — which is
what says the artifact carries nothing about where it was produced. A third
machine checks it on every push, because CI runs `cargo test --workspace`.

as a one-line answer. That round spent two builds to learn the bump changed
nothing here; `template-hash` is a function of the pinned generator's Rust
templates, so an unchanged value now says it directly, on every build, for free.

R1767.decision_summary:
R1767 — a walk reproduces a specification no single frame can, and the
application publishes the walk.

WHAT WAS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. `ApplicationConformance::conforms` is
`unjudged == 0 && declared == 0 && every judged report reconciles`, and by R1763
all three clauses were finally honest. Together they had also become impossible
to satisfy: one frame paints one section, every other section is away, and an
away surface reconciles nothing (R1742), so an application with two open
sections can never report conformance. Measured at entry by walking all six open
sections of the assembled analysis tool and returning:

    headline  26 of 133 reproduced   conforms=false

which is the boot number, and is R1763's repair working exactly as written. The
honest answer, and no vocabulary for the question a reader actually has.

★★★★★ THE ENTRY RE-MEASUREMENT FOUND A SECOND LAYER THE DEBT DID NOT KNOW
ABOUT, and it is what made this design per-SURFACE rather than per-section.
Standing INSIDE each section rather than reading from outside:

    dashboard 26/28 ok    logs      15/15 ok
    packets   25/26 ok    lab        1/15 FAILS
    keys      21/21 ok    settings  26/28 ok

`lab` fails while the reader is standing in it, and not because the screen is
wrong. Its specification names an enumeration row WITH ITS ROSTER SHUT and the
roster STANDING OVER IT, and those two states exclude each other. The node lab's
own judge wrote it down in prose at R1742 — *this document cannot be fully
judged at any one instant. A reader who wants the whole verdict drives the
session and reads twice* — and nothing anywhere could hold the two readings, so
"reads twice" meant a person comparing two printouts. Twenty-five rounds, and no
census saw it, because a carry that lives in a comment is not a census.

HOW THIS KEEPS "A VERDICT IS ABOUT ONE FRAME" RATHER THAN RELAXING IT, which is
the design question the debt recorded as open. A journey report is not one
verdict about many frames. It is MANY ONE-FRAME VERDICTS, each labelled with the
reading it came from. A `SurfaceVisit` credits only a step at which that surface
was STANDING; an away frame contributes its specification to the denominator and
nothing to the numerator, exactly as one level down. So the walk is part of the
claim, and the report publishes how long it was.

★★★★★ THE DEFINITION OF A STEP WAS WRONG TWICE, and the second was loud enough
to measure. Numbering ARRIVALS cannot do the job at all: opening a roster and
closing it again are two frames of one stop, so a report crediting both to
*stop 4* would say two verdicts came from one frame when the whole point is that
they cannot have. Numbering FRAMES is worse in the other direction — driven end
to end on the running tool, a walk of SEVEN STOPS reported 17,385 STEPS, because
a window repaints whether or not anything changed. An ordinal that counts
wall-clock is not a label a reader can use, and a gate asserting on one would be
asserting how fast the machine is. A step is therefore ONE OBSERVATION THAT SAW
SOMETHING DIFFERENT, and `steps` is DERIVED from the rows rather than carried
beside them, so the recorder's counter cannot name a step the report does not
contain.

AFTER, over one walk of the assembled tool with the lab's session driven both
ways:

    frame verdict   26 of 133   conforms=false   (unchanged, and still true)
    walk  verdict  118 of 133   stood 27 of 27   17 steps at 7 stops
    lab: enum_row credited at step 12, enum_roster at step 13

`stood 27 of 27` is the sentence that could not be said before: every surface
every specification of this application names was on some frame of this walk.

★ AND THE REMAINING FAILURE MOVED FROM STRUCTURAL TO NAMED. The tool still does
not conform, and it now says which surface of which section at which step, which
is a thing somebody can go and fix. Moving ONE variable showed what kind of
thing it is: at 2494x1531 — the size the node lab's own gate paints at, against
the 1096x802 page region this shell gives that section — all three of the lab's
surfaces reconcile and a DIFFERENT section breaks instead. So this tool has no
window size at which it conforms, which is registered as its own debt rather
than repaired here.
changes_bullets: FRAMEWORK
`pinion_screen::journey` is new: `JourneyConformance` over `JourneySection`
over `SurfaceVisit`, with `JourneyStanding` as the per-section arm set. A
surface record keeps two facts apart — the LATEST reading, which is where the
specification's own side comes from, and the last step at which it was
STANDING, which is the only thing ever credited.
`ScreenRoster::journey_conformance` is the reader, and `Walk` (private) is the
recorder. It runs at `latch`, BEFORE R1763's forgetting, because that is the
last instant a departing section's own frame can still be read.
The recorder observes the position the PREVIOUS latch left behind: a latch runs
before the frame it belongs to is painted, so the store holds the last
section's marks, and filing them under the journey's current position would
credit one section with another's paint. A counterfactual holds that ordering.
The section a reader stands on is folded in LIVE at read time from the same
`standing_of`, so a client sees a section's verdict on the frame it arrives at
rather than one frame later. Reading stores nothing; two reads between frames
are equal, and a test asserts it.
`ScreenRoster::standing_of` is an EXTRACTION of the match that was inline in
`conformance`, so there is one definition of what a section says rather than
the three this round would otherwise have written.
`SurfaceStanding::to_json` is lifted to public in `pinion_core::conformance`
and `DocumentReport::surfaces_json` is built out of it, because this round
added a second reader of that row and re-spelling it would have been two
renderings of one verdict.
APPLICATION
The analysis tool publishes `/external/journey` beside `/external/sections`.
Both are published: they are two questions, and reading either as the other is
the mistake both exist to prevent.
GATES
`crates/pinion-screen/tests/journey_conformance.rs` is new — 13 tests over a
fixture application whose shape is the one that made the frame verdict
unreachable: three open sections, one of which specifies two surfaces that
exclude each other. Every fixture surface answers from marks it really
recorded, so the evidence is `paint` for the reason a real screen's is.
`tools/demos/r1767_a_walk_reproduces_what_no_frame_can.py` is new: 8 sections,
47 named checks, identical across two runs.
verification_bullets: MEASURED AT ENTRY, over the wire: walking all six open sections and returning
leaves the frame headline at `26 of 133` with `conforms=false` — the boot
number, and the debt's own recorded figure, reproduced.
MEASURED AT ENTRY, standing inside each section: five of six reconcile and
`lab` does not (`1 of 15`), because two of its three specified surfaces are
ALTERNATIVES. That is the half the debt did not record.
MEASURED AFTER, one walk with the lab's session driven both ways: walk verdict
`118 of 133`, `stood 27 of 27`, 17 steps at 7 stops, `enum_row` credited at
step 12 and `enum_roster` at step 13. The frame verdict is byte-unchanged.
COST, measured rather than assumed: the same binary with the observation behind
an env switch, three sections at ninety frames each. `mean_build_us` WITH
recorder is BELOW THIS INSTRUMENT'S NOISE, which is a different claim from zero
and is the one these numbers support.
COUNTERFACTUALS 7 of 7 CAUGHT: credit an away frame instead of a standing one;
arrive before observing, so one section's marks are filed under another; let an
unvisited section satisfy the walk; accept declaration and refuse paint; take a
step per repaint and none per change; replace a surface's record instead of
folding into it; observe after R1763's forgetting.
The first run reported one BROKEN — an irrefutable `if let` — which is the
driver's own authoring rule (write the break as a WRONG answer, not an absent
one) arriving in a costume its header does not yet list.
cargo test -p pinion-screen: 13 journey + 27 mounted + 3 coverage + doctests.
cargo test --workspace: exit 0, no target reporting FAILED. The blast radius was
COMPUTED by `tools/blast_radius.py`, which answers every workspace package for a
`pinion-core` edit, so the whole suite is the gate rather than a subset.
DEMOS: all 37 that drive this shell, selected by grep rather than memory, pass
on Xvfb :97 — including `r1763`, whose headline this round must not have moved.
NOT RUN and stated: the full 636-demo sweep, which is CI's.
carry_forward_bullets: `debt-a-conformance-can-only-be-true-about-one-frame` is CLOSED. Its recorded
prescription 1 (a journey-level verdict) was right, and the design question it
called open has an answer: the rule is KEPT, because a journey report is many
one-frame verdicts each labelled with the reading it came from.
Its own re-measurement corrected it in one place and widened it in another —
the numbers held, and the problem was per-SURFACE rather than per-section.
NEW: `debt-a-specification-cannot-say-two-surfaces-are-alternatives`. A walk can
now HOLD two mutually exclusive surfaces; a specification still cannot DECLARE
that they are alternatives, so `stood == false` cannot distinguish *the sibling
is standing* from *nobody opened it* from *the screen does not draw it*. The
only place that distinction lives is a screen's hand-written away sentence,
which no gate reads. R1742 named it and it was prose for twenty-five rounds.
NEW: `debt-the-analysis-tool-conforms-at-no-window-size`. Measured this round by
moving one variable: at 1440x900 the node lab's `controls` and `enum_row`
diverge because the inspector is cut; at 2494x1531 those reconcile and
`settings/rows` breaks the other way, its declared remainder paid off by the
wider text fitting. The two failing sets are disjoint and neither size
conforms. Underneath: no specification pin in this tree says which size it was
written against.
STATED rather than folded away: a third size was not tried, so "no size
conforms" is a claim about the two that were measured.

R1770.decision_summary:
R1770 — A VERDICT SAYS WHAT SIZE IT WAS READ AT, AND THE ANALYSIS TOOL
CONFORMS AT A SIZE IT CAN NAME.

The round took `debt-the-analysis-tool-conforms-at-no-window-size`, opened by
R1767 the moment a walk could hold a verdict no frame can. That debt named three
candidate repairs and demanded all three be re-measured before starting. Two of
them were wrong, and the measurement is most of what this round is.

WHAT THE RE-MEASUREMENT FOUND.

(1) The debt recorded the node lab as judged at 1096x802. It is judged at
1388x848. 1096x802 is the shell's page REGION, measured by R1761 for a different
question; the section's own surface is bigger than the page it sits on. A number
one round measured was copied into the next round's file as the number of
something else.

(2) The debt prescribed making the inspector scroll or abbreviate — a FOLD
repair, on the reading that rows fall below the bottom. Driven across eight
window sizes with one binary: the HEIGHT MOVES NOTHING (900 tall and 1531 tall
give identical verdicts) and the width moves everything. Surface 1388 wide gives
`controls` 1 of 5 and `enum_row` 1 of 7; 1548 gives 1 and 3; 1748 gives 5 and 7.
The parts that go are the right-hand ones — the type word, the applies badge,
the remove seat, the pick arrow — and they go because that screen DECLARES it
stops laying out below its comfortable width and clips instead, a number
R1712-R1714 measured three times and corrected twice. Taking the prescription
would have undone a decision three rounds paid for.

(3) What was true was the smallest sentence in the file: no pin says what size
it was written at. Counted: ZERO. And one layer under it, the finding that
governs the round — the node lab's own gate held `CONFORMANCE_SIZE = (2494,
1531)` as a PRIVATE CONSTANT INSIDE ONE TEST MODULE, while the assembled tool
judged the same pin over a fifth of that area. One document, two gates, five
times the area between them, and neither artifact carried the number that told
them apart, because the number was in neither of them.

THE DECISION. A conformance verdict is a fact about a surface extent, and the
vocabulary now says so at three levels. It is the same rule R1752 wrote for a
duration (a number that says how many must say what of) and R1758 wrote for
evidence (a verdict says what it was read from), one turn further.

* `pinion_core::painted::Extent`, recorded BY THE STORE from the surface
  rectangle the recorder already has, so a screen cannot claim to have been read
  at a size it did not paint at — the same one-directional rule `Evidence::Paint`
  carries.
* A pin declares `$at`, the extent its canon was written against, and the
  screen's own gate READS THE SIZE FROM THERE rather than declaring one. Moving
  the pin moves the gate.
* An owed entry declares `at`, the extents it was measured at, and
  `Ledger::judge_at` judges relative to where the verdict was read.

WHY A LIST OF MEASURED SIZES AND NOT A BAND. The obvious shape is *holds at
every extent no taller than H*, and it is a claim about infinitely many sizes
derived from a measurement at one — the error R1656 and R1764 each paid for.
Every extent in an entry's list was stood at and read. It is strict in the safe
direction: at an extent the list does not name the entry excuses nothing, so a
build that still diverges there reports the difference as UNDECLARED and the
gate goes red. Narrowing a list can never hide a divergence.

WHY AN UNSIZED VERDICT IS REFUSED. `Unreconciled::Unsized` is what stops `at`
being an escape hatch: a reader that hands no extent would otherwise find every
sized entry out of force and every declared difference quietly excused — the
most flattering possible reading of *I did not say where I was standing*.

WHY THE NODE LAB'S AWAY IS NOT THE ESCAPE HATCH R1742 REFUSED. That round set
the test: an away condition must be a state the screen is in and can point at,
never a case in which it would fail. This one names a number the screen DECLARES
TO THE FRAMEWORK — the same comfortable width the window system is told — is
read from the HOST's grant so the screen cannot enter the state by drawing
badly, and makes the numbers WORSE: away credits nothing, so at 1440x900 the
tool's headline falls from 118 to 113 of 133 and its stood count from 27 to 24.
Nothing can be flattered by it. The alternative — a ledger entry per clipped
part — was refused because twelve such entries would declare *this build does
not reproduce its specification* as an accepted difference.

THE HEADLINE. Measured over the wire: the assembled analysis tool reports
`conforms=true` at 2494x1531, 129 of 133 reproduced, every one of its 27
surfaces stood in and reconciled. No window produced that before this round, and
the debt's title was exactly that it could not.
changes_bullets: FRAMEWORK — the extent vocabulary.
* `pinion_core::painted::Extent` — a surface size, `Display` as `1096x802` so a
number read off a wire report can be searched for in a pin.
* `PaintedRegions::extent()` / `with_extent()` — the store carries the size the
frame was painted into. `None` is *no frame said*, deliberately not `0x0`.
* `pinion_runtime::record_painted_marks` fills it from the surface rectangle it
already holds, so the windowed path gets it without a caller;
`PaintedRegions::of_scene` takes it from the root it walked, so a fixture
cannot hand in a size the scene does not have.
* `Owed::at` + `Owed::only_at` + `Owed::in_force_at` — the extents an accepted
difference was measured at. Empty means every extent, which is what every
entry written before this round means.
* `Ledger::judge_at` / `reconciles_at`, `SpecDocument::unreconciled_at` — judged
relative to where the verdict was read. `Ledger::judge` is `judge_at(None, …)`
so an existing caller cannot silently pass a sized ledger.
* `Unreconciled::Unsized` — the refusal that keeps `at` from being an escape
hatch.
* `SpecDocument::written_at` from the pin's top-level `$at`;
`DocumentReport::at` / `written_at` / `read_where_written`; `SurfaceStanding::at`.
Both sizes ride on the wire (`at`, `written_at`, `read_where_written`) beside
`evidence`, because they govern how the rest is read.
* `pinion_screen::SurfaceVisit::at`, and the rule below it.
FRAMEWORK — a credit does not survive a resize (found by running).
`SurfaceVisit::record` drops a credited verdict when the next observation was
read at a different extent. Measured: walk the tool maximised where it conforms,
shrink the window where a section declines to be judged, and the walk still
reported `conforms=true` on the strength of frames painted at a size that no
longer exists. R1767's asymmetry is unchanged and its boundary is asserted — an
away frame at the SAME extent still leaves the credit alone, which is the only
thing that lets two mutually exclusive surfaces be credited over one walk.
PINS — six declare `$at`, and each screen's gate reads its size from there.
`analyzer-inspector-spec.json` 2494x1531 · `analyzer-settings-spec.json`,
`analyzer-dashboard-spec.json`, `analyzer-packets-spec.json` 1440x900 ·
`analyzer-keys-spec.json` 1180x760 · `analyzer-logs-spec.json` 1220x760. The
five that do not are not about paint (pointer arrival, press, rail seats, board
drag states, this build's own coverage) and a size would mean nothing on them —
which is why the census that gates this is derived from the RUNNING tool, not
from a glob: every verdict whose evidence is `paint` names both numbers.
The node lab's `CONFORMANCE_SIZE` constant is deleted; `conformance_size()`
reads `$at`. `r1770_the_gate_paints_at_the_size_the_pin_declares` asserts the
recorded extent equals the declared one, because the value goes in as a WINDOW
size and comes out as the extent of a SURFACE and those agree only while the
screen fills its window — measured, in the assembled tool they do not.
PIN — one entry becomes a claim about a size.
`analyzer-settings-spec.json`'s `theme` entry is a fold, and a fold is a
function of how tall the surface is. It now carries `at: [1440x900]`, and the
`why` records what a sizeless ledger did with it.
SCREEN — the node lab declines to be judged below the width it declares.
`judge::built` answers away when the surface it was given is narrower than
`SHRINK.comfortable()`, naming both numbers. `lib::comfortable_size()` exposes
that one declared value to `judge` so the module that says so reads it rather
than restating it.
DEMO — `tools/demos/r1770_a_verdict_says_what_size_it_was_read_at.py`, 48 named
checks over seven sections: the pin census taken from the running tool, every
frame verdict naming its extent, `conforms=true` at 2494x1531, the named away at
1440x900 with both numbers in its sentence and the relation between them
asserted, the headline falling rather than rising, one entry in force at one

CONFORMS AT A SIZE IT CAN NAME.

R1767 the moment a walk could hold a verdict no frame can. That debt named three
candidate repairs and demanded all three be re-measured before starting. Two of
them were wrong, and the measurement is most of what this round is.

WHAT THE RE-MEASUREMENT FOUND.

(1) The debt recorded the node lab as judged at 1096x802. It is judged at
1388x848. 1096x802 is the shell's page REGION, measured by R1761 for a different
question; the section's own surface is bigger than the page it sits on. A number
one round measured was copied into the next round's file as the number of
something else.

(2) The debt prescribed making the inspector scroll or abbreviate — a FOLD
repair, on the reading that rows fall below the bottom. Driven across eight
window sizes with one binary: the HEIGHT MOVES NOTHING (900 tall and 1531 tall
give identical verdicts) and the width moves everything. Surface 1388 wide gives
`controls` 1 of 5 and `enum_row` 1 of 7; 1548 gives 1 and 3; 1748 gives 5 and 7.
The parts that go are the right-hand ones — the type word, the applies badge,
the remove seat, the pick arrow — and they go because that screen DECLARES it
stops laying out below its comfortable width and clips instead, a number
R1712-R1714 measured three times and corrected twice. Taking the prescription
would have undone a decision three rounds paid for.

(3) What was true was the smallest sentence in the file: no pin says what size
it was written at. Counted: ZERO. And one layer under it, the finding that
governs the round — the node lab's own gate held `CONFORMANCE_SIZE = (2494,
1531)` as a PRIVATE CONSTANT INSIDE ONE TEST MODULE, while the assembled tool
judged the same pin over a fifth of that area. One document, two gates, five
times the area between them, and neither artifact carried the number that told
them apart, because the number was in neither of them.

THE DECISION. A conformance verdict is a fact about a surface extent, and the
vocabulary now says so at three levels. It is the same rule R1752 wrote for a
duration (a number that says how many must say what of) and R1758 wrote for
evidence (a verdict says what it was read from), one turn further.

* `pinion_core::painted::Extent`, recorded BY THE STORE from the surface
  rectangle the recorder already has, so a screen cannot claim to have been read
  at a size it did not paint at — the same one-directional rule `Evidence::Paint`
  carries.
* A pin declares `$at`, the extent its canon was written against, and the
  screen's own gate READS THE SIZE FROM THERE rather than declaring one. Moving
  the pin moves the gate.
* An owed entry declares `at`, the extents it was measured at, and
  `Ledger::judge_at` judges relative to where the verdict was read.

WHY A LIST OF MEASURED SIZES AND NOT A BAND. The obvious shape is *holds at
every extent no taller than H*, and it is a claim about infinitely many sizes
derived from a measurement at one — the error R1656 and R1764 each paid for.
Every extent in an entry's list was stood at and read. It is strict in the safe
direction: at an extent the list does not name the entry excuses nothing, so a
build that still diverges there reports the difference as UNDECLARED and the
gate goes red. Narrowing a list can never hide a divergence.

WHY AN UNSIZED VERDICT IS REFUSED. `Unreconciled::Unsized` is what stops `at`
being an escape hatch: a reader that hands no extent would otherwise find every
sized entry out of force and every declared difference quietly excused — the
most flattering possible reading of *I did not say where I was standing*.

the test: an away condition must be a state the screen is in and can point at,
never a case in which it would fail. This one names a number the screen DECLARES

read from the HOST's grant so the screen cannot enter the state by drawing
badly, and makes the numbers WORSE: away credits nothing, so at 1440x900 the
tool's headline falls from 118 to 113 of 133 and its stood count from 27 to 24.

part — was refused because twelve such entries would declare *this build does
not reproduce its specification* as an accepted difference.

R1771.decision_summary:
R1771 — A PROOF THE CENSUS CITES IS A TEST THAT RUNS.

The round took `debt-analyzer-census-verdicts-are-unproven` and re-measured it
first, as this project's rule demands. The debt's own number was stale — it said
20 of 24 `have` verdicts named no proof; measured, it was 18 of 31. But the
re-measurement found something the debt does not mention at all, and that became
the round.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. `docs/analyzer-census.json` carries two kinds of evidence,
and R1648 made them mutually exclusive by verdict: a `have` is proven by a test
(`proven_by`), an `app` by an assembly (`assembled_by`). Since that round, every
path an `assembled_by` names has been checked for existence on every push.
`proven_by` was checked for NOTHING — not existence, not shape. So the field
carrying this file's strongest claim, that a capability was exercised through
the public API, was the one field nothing verified, and the thirteen rows
resting on it were thirteen unexamined strings.

THE SHARPER HALF. The sibling census, `tools/reference_census.py`, has validated
`proven_by` for longer than this one has existed in its current form. So the two
censuses in this tree disagreed about whether a proof needs checking — while
this file's own prose said its answer to *is a `have` true* was "the same as the
reference census's". It was the same sentence and not the same check.

THE DECISION: THE ORACLE IS THE TEST RUNNER, NOT A SEARCH. `--check-proofs`
asks `cargo test -- --list` whether each cited name is a test that can be
SELECTED. A regex over `#[test]` would have been easier and is refused for two
reasons, one of principle and one measured: this census's rule is *prove it with
a test rather than a grep*, and a census that checked its proofs by searching
source text would be breaking that rule in the act of enforcing it; and a search
cannot tell a test that runs from one behind a `cfg` this build does not enable,
which is precisely a proof that does not run.

WHY IT IS NOT MERGED WITH THE SIBLING (obligation 3b). That tool checks the
ADDRESS and states that whether the named test exists is "deliberately only
half", deferred to a per-crate bijection where the COMPILER reads — a sound
design, and stronger where it applies. It does not apply here: this pin's
citations are sentences naming several tests across several crates in three
forms, beside the demo files that drive them, because a capability is rarely one
test. There is no single crate to hold a bijection for such a row. So this file
answers the deferred half by a third route that is also not a text census. The
reason is written into the tool so the next round does not unify them wrongly.

WHAT THE GATE FOUND, IMMEDIATELY. All thirteen pre-existing citations resolve —
a legitimate outcome and the one worth stating plainly. Then, of the eleven
citations this round ADDED, it refused three: `table`, `tree_view` and `tooltip`
were cited under `pinion-core` and live in `pinion-widget-paint`. Three wrong
citations in eleven, caught before they were committed, by a gate written in the
same round — which is the honest measure of how silently the field had been
drifting while nothing read it.
changes_bullets: TOOL — `tools/analyzer_census.py`.
* `proof_names(row)` / `proof_paths(row)` — the peers of `assembly_paths`,
picking citations out of the prose that surrounds them. A token counts when it
is a `::` path or a bare snake_case identifier long enough not to be a word;
the selftest asserts that `end`, `to`, `section` and `D` are not mistaken for
tests, over a string this pin actually carries.
* `check_proofs(rows, known, exists)` — pure in both oracles, the purity its
sibling `check_assemblies` already had, so every rule is testable with no
toolchain and no filesystem.
* `runner_tests(crates)` — the oracle: `cargo test --all-targets -- --list` over
the crates the pin cites, which are DERIVED from the pin rather than listed.
* `proof_oracle(listed)` — three citation forms matched as each is written: a
bare name against a test's tail, a `crate::…::name` past the crate segment,
and a MODULE citation against the tests under it (this pin has one).
* `--check-proofs`, wired into `pre-push` beside `--check-pin`. Kept a separate
mode because it BUILDS: 3.5s warm, and once per clean tree for the cited
crates' test binaries.
SELFTEST — eleven new cases, every one a shape this pin carries. Two are worth
naming: that the prose around a citation is not mistaken for one, and that a
name which is only a SUBSTRING of a real test is REFUSED — the exact failure a
grep-shaped oracle would let through.
PIN — `docs/analyzer-census.json`, eleven rows given proofs: the decode tree and
its collapse driven through the External rather than the transducer; the decode
inspector; the virtualised stream; the throughput series with its stacking; the
share view; the loss timeline's lanes; report tooltips on marks as well as on
widgets; brush-and-zoom read back over the wire; the transport's three states
and its clock; the Okabe-Ito palette, whose test asserts the exact set so the
claim and its proof are one sentence; and label thinning, cited on the REPORT
half rather than the paint half.
**13 of 31 `have` rows named a proof; 24 do now**, and all 57 citations are
answered by the runner. One of the eleven says in its own text what it does NOT
prove — the LRU paging and tail-follow its `covered_by` also claims — rather
than letting the row read as fully exercised.
DOC — the tool's prose said `proven_by` "is empty on most rows today", which
this round made false, and said its standard was "the same as the reference
census's", which was true of the sentence and not of the check. Both corrected,
with the measurement and the two-designs reasoning written where the next reader
of either census will find it.
verification_bullets: RE-MEASURED FIRST, BEFORE ANY CODE.
* The debt said 20 of 24 `have` verdicts name no proof. Measured: 18 of 31.
* `grep -c check_proofs tools/analyzer_census.py` was 0, and `check_assemblies`
runs on every invocation including the `--check-pin` the hook calls. That
asymmetry is what the round is about, and it was read out of the code rather
than assumed from the debt.
* `cargo test -p pinion-core --lib -- --list`: 16s cold-ish, 3,884 tests. All
nine pinion-core citations already in the pin resolve against it.
THE GATE, PROVEN BOTH WAYS.
* Selftest — `python3 tools/analyzer_census.py --selftest` PASS, 0 failures,
with eleven new cases including the substring refusal a grep would pass.
* COUNTERFACTUAL on the live path, not only the injected one: one character
changed in a real citation (`…two_sets` -> `…two_setz`), and
`--check-proofs` exited 1 naming the row and the name. Restored, and the
diff of `docs/analyzer-census.json` confirms only the intended edits remain.
* And unprompted, on this round's own work: three of the eleven citations added
here were REFUSED for naming `pinion-core` where the test lives in
`pinion-widget-paint`. Located by reading the source, corrected, re-run clean.
FINAL STATE.
* `--check-proofs`: 57 citations checked against 6,072 selectable tests, 0
unanswered, exit 0. Warm run 3.5s.
* `--check-pin`: 68 capabilities, pin well-formed.
* `--selftest`: PASS. `tools/reference_census.py --selftest`: all checks passed
(run because this round reasoned about its design and must not have broken it).
* `tools/test_hooks.sh`: 141 passed, 0 failed — run because `pre-push` changed.
* `shellcheck .githooks/pre-push`: clean but for the pre-existing SC1091 info.
* The census report: `24 of 31 have verdict(s) name a proof`, up from 13.
WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. That the twenty-four proofs are SUFFICIENT. The gate
answers *does this citation name a test that runs*, never *does that test
exercise the whole capability* — a judgement no tool makes, and the reason each
citation carries a sentence saying which part it proves. Seven `have` rows still
name no proof and the census prints that ratio on every run.
carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — one, and it is declared by the artifact itself rather than held here.
Seven `have` rows still name no proof: the multi-window tear-off with
always-on-top, the topology map's layout, report export, light/dark parity, the
recovered-topology injection, edge authoring with a direction and a transport
choice, and the auto-discovery switch. The census prints `24 of 31` on every run,
so this remainder is visible to anyone who runs the tool and is not a fact kept
in a memory file. Two of them (parity, export) may not be provable by a unit test
at all and may belong under `assembled_by` on a different verdict — which is a
judgement about the row, not a missing string, and re-judging a verdict is not
something to do in passing at the end of a round that built the checker.
NOT CARRY, stated so it is not mistaken for one:
* The gate does not judge SUFFICIENCY, and cannot. That limit is stated on
`check_proofs`, in the module doc, and in this round's verification.
* The two censuses keep two designs for validating a proof. That is a decision
with its reasoning written into the tool, not an inconsistency left open.
* `--check-proofs` builds, so it is a separate mode from `--check-pin`. On a
clean tree the first push pays for the cited crates' test binaries once. That
is a cost, not a gap, and the hook says so where a reader will meet it.

re-measurement found something the debt does not mention at all, and that became
the round.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. `docs/analyzer-census.json` carries two kinds of evidence,
and R1648 made them mutually exclusive by verdict: a `have` is proven by a test
(`proven_by`), an `app` by an assembly (`assembled_by`). Since that round, every
path an `assembled_by` names has been checked for existence on every push.
`proven_by` was checked for NOTHING — not existence, not shape. So the field
carrying this file's strongest claim, that a capability was exercised through
the public API, was the one field nothing verified, and the thirteen rows
resting on it were thirteen unexamined strings.

THE SHARPER HALF. The sibling census, `tools/reference_census.py`, has validated
`proven_by` for longer than this one has existed in its current form. So the two
censuses in this tree disagreed about whether a proof needs checking — while
this file's own prose said its answer to *is a `have` true* was "the same as the
reference census's". It was the same sentence and not the same check.

THE DECISION: THE ORACLE IS THE TEST RUNNER, NOT A SEARCH. `--check-proofs`
asks `cargo test -- --list` whether each cited name is a test that can be
SELECTED. A regex over `#[test]` would have been easier and is refused for two
reasons, one of principle and one measured: this census's rule is *prove it with
a test rather than a grep*, and a census that checked its proofs by searching
source text would be breaking that rule in the act of enforcing it; and a search
cannot tell a test that runs from one behind a `cfg` this build does not enable,
which is precisely a proof that does not run.

WHY IT IS NOT MERGED WITH THE SIBLING (obligation 3b). That tool checks the
ADDRESS and states that whether the named test exists is "deliberately only
half", deferred to a per-crate bijection where the COMPILER reads — a sound
design, and stronger where it applies. It does not apply here: this pin's
citations are sentences naming several tests across several crates in three
forms, beside the demo files that drive them, because a capability is rarely one
test. There is no single crate to hold a bijection for such a row. So this file
answers the deferred half by a third route that is also not a text census. The
reason is written into the tool so the next round does not unify them wrongly.

WHAT THE GATE FOUND, IMMEDIATELY. All thirteen pre-existing citations resolve —
a legitimate outcome and the one worth stating plainly. Then, of the eleven
citations this round ADDED, it refused three: `table`, `tree_view` and `tooltip`
were cited under `pinion-core` and live in `pinion-widget-paint`. Three wrong
citations in eleven, caught before they were committed, by a gate written in the
same round — which is the honest measure of how silently the field had been
drifting while nothing read it.
publishable_changes_bullets: TOOL — `tools/analyzer_census.py`.
* `proof_names(row)` / `proof_paths(row)` — the peers of `assembly_paths`,
picking citations out of the prose that surrounds them. A token counts when it
is a `::` path or a bare snake_case identifier long enough not to be a word;
the selftest asserts that `end`, `to`, `section` and `D` are not mistaken for
tests, over a string this pin actually carries.
* `check_proofs(rows, known, exists)` — pure in both oracles, the purity its
sibling `check_assemblies` already had, so every rule is testable with no
toolchain and no filesystem.
* `runner_tests(crates)` — the oracle: `cargo test --all-targets -- --list` over
the crates the pin cites, which are DERIVED from the pin rather than listed.
* `proof_oracle(listed)` — three citation forms matched as each is written: a
bare name against a test's tail, a `crate::…::name` past the crate segment,
and a MODULE citation against the tests under it (this pin has one).
* `--check-proofs`, wired into `pre-push` beside `--check-pin`. Kept a separate
mode because it BUILDS: 3.5s warm, and once per clean tree for the cited
crates' test binaries.
SELFTEST — eleven new cases, every one a shape this pin carries. Two are worth
naming: that the prose around a citation is not mistaken for one, and that a
name which is only a SUBSTRING of a real test is REFUSED — the exact failure a
grep-shaped oracle would let through.
PIN — `docs/analyzer-census.json`, eleven rows given proofs: the decode tree and
its collapse driven through the External rather than the transducer; the decode
inspector; the virtualised stream; the throughput series with its stacking; the
share view; the loss timeline's lanes; report tooltips on marks as well as on
widgets; brush-and-zoom read back over the wire; the transport's three states
and its clock; the Okabe-Ito palette, whose test asserts the exact set so the
claim and its proof are one sentence; and label thinning, cited on the REPORT
half rather than the paint half.
**13 of 31 `have` rows named a proof; 24 do now**, and all 57 citations are
answered by the runner. One of the eleven says in its own text what it does NOT
prove — the LRU paging and tail-follow its `covered_by` also claims — rather
than letting the row read as fully exercised.
DOC — the tool's prose said `proven_by` "is empty on most rows today", which
this round made false, and said its standard was "the same as the reference
census's", which was true of the sentence and not of the check. Both corrected,
with the measurement and the two-designs reasoning written where the next reader
of either census will find it.
publishable_verification_bullets: RE-MEASURED FIRST, BEFORE ANY CODE.
* The debt said 20 of 24 `have` verdicts name no proof. Measured: 18 of 31.
* `grep -c check_proofs tools/analyzer_census.py` was 0, and `check_assemblies`
runs on every invocation including the `--check-pin` the hook calls. That
asymmetry is what the round is about, and it was read out of the code rather
than assumed from the debt.
* `cargo test -p pinion-core --lib -- --list`: 16s cold-ish, 3,884 tests. All
nine pinion-core citations already in the pin resolve against it.
THE GATE, PROVEN BOTH WAYS.
* Selftest — `python3 tools/analyzer_census.py --selftest` PASS, 0 failures,
with eleven new cases including the substring refusal a grep would pass.
* COUNTERFACTUAL on the live path, not only the injected one: one character
changed in a real citation (`…two_sets` -> `…two_setz`), and
`--check-proofs` exited 1 naming the row and the name. Restored, and the
diff of `docs/analyzer-census.json` confirms only the intended edits remain.
* And unprompted, on this round's own work: three of the eleven citations added
here were REFUSED for naming `pinion-core` where the test lives in
`pinion-widget-paint`. Located by reading the source, corrected, re-run clean.
FINAL STATE.
* `--check-proofs`: 57 citations checked against 6,072 selectable tests, 0
unanswered, exit 0. Warm run 3.5s.
* `--check-pin`: 68 capabilities, pin well-formed.
* `--selftest`: PASS. `tools/reference_census.py --selftest`: all checks passed
(run because this round reasoned about its design and must not have broken it).
* `tools/test_hooks.sh`: 141 passed, 0 failed — run because `pre-push` changed.
* `shellcheck .githooks/pre-push`: clean but for the pre-existing SC1091 info.
* The census report: `24 of 31 have verdict(s) name a proof`, up from 13.

answers *does this citation name a test that runs*, never *does that test
exercise the whole capability* — a judgement no tool makes, and the reason each
citation carries a sentence saying which part it proves. Seven `have` rows still
name no proof and the census prints that ratio on every run.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — one, and it is declared by the artifact itself rather than held here.
Seven `have` rows still name no proof: the multi-window tear-off with
always-on-top, the topology map's layout, report export, light/dark parity, the
recovered-topology injection, edge authoring with a direction and a transport
choice, and the auto-discovery switch. The census prints `24 of 31` on every run,

in a memory file. Two of them (parity, export) may not be provable by a unit test
at all and may belong under `assembled_by` on a different verdict — which is a
judgement about the row, not a missing string, and re-judging a verdict is not
something to do in passing at the end of a round that built the checker.

* The gate does not judge SUFFICIENCY, and cannot. That limit is stated on
