R1787.decision_summary:
R1787 — A TABULAR EXPORT THAT NAMES EVERY CELL ITS DIALECT COULD NOT CARRY, AND
A CENSUS GAP REASON THAT WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.

The analysis-tool census carried `capture.t1.12` — "marking, bookmarks and
comments, plus exporting a range" — as a gap, on the reason "EXPORTING IS NOT
HERE — measured, no tabular/CSV export derivation exists in any crate".

★★★★★ RE-MEASURED BEFORE THE ROUND WROTE A LINE, THAT REASON WAS WRONG IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS. A derivation existed and had since R1372: `table::rows_to_tsv`, the
shared clipboard-copy codec two grids funnel through. What it lacked was not
existence. It is *structure-preserving over content-faithful* BY DESIGN — a cell
holding a tab or a newline is rewritten with a space so the block's row/column
shape always matches the rectangle it came from — and it made that trade
SILENTLY. A consumer handed the string could not ask whether anything had been
altered, and the codec's own doc deferred the rest: "full spreadsheet-style
quoting is a later enhancement if a delimiter-bearing grid needs faithful
content". So the real gap was FAITHFULNESS AND A REPORT, and a round that had
believed the pin would have built a second copy of something that was there.
That is the standing rule at its ninth case: re-measure the debt's premise,
number, prescription, diagnosis, population AND the query the reason rests on.

THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN RATHER THAN READ. Two probes compiled against the
reference toolkit at 6.11 and executed (scratchpad only, never tracked, per the
confidentiality ratchet):

* asked for a rectangle of four cells *as data*, its item-model layer answers
  TWO BINARY PAYLOADS — `hasText` false, `text()` length 0, and neither the
  header labels nor the cell text recoverable from the bytes;
* its tabular widget, every cell selected and a real copy chord delivered,
  leaves the clipboard holding NO FORMAT AT ALL: `formats` null, text empty.

So the floor for "export this range as text" is nothing, and the bar is set by
what a person needs rather than by a competitor's surface. That is also why the
answer is not "add a CSV writer": a writer alone would reproduce the silence.

WHAT LANDED. `pinion_core::widgets::table_export`:

* `Dialect` says how cells are separated and WHETHER THAT SEPARATION CAN BE
  ESCAPED. The quote is an `Option` and that is the whole design: a dialect with
  one carries any content, a dialect without one is DECLARED lossy rather than
  discovered to be. `is_faithful()` is readable off the dialect before any rows
  exist, so an export menu says so up front. `try_new` refuses three ways of
  spelling a dialect a reader could not invert.
* `write` answers an `Export`: the text, plus one `Loss` per CELL the dialect
  could not carry, addressed by line (`Header` included — a column name can hold
  a delimiter too) and column, naming what was in it.
* `read` is the inverse, and it is what makes "faithful" a LAW rather than a
  claim: for any quoting dialect and any rows, reading back what was written
  yields the rows unchanged. A lossy dialect's output REFUSES to be read
  (`ReadDefect::NotReadable`) instead of guessing which spaces used to be
  delimiters — a round trip that "works on the cells that happened to be plain"
  is the failure mode this module exists to end.
* `rows_to_tsv` and `Table::selected_tsv` now DELEGATE, and `tsv_sanitize` is
  gone. One codec, not two spellings of a lossy transform.

AND IT REACHES A SCREEN, WHICH IS THE HALF A CENSUS ROW CANNOT SEE. `capture.t1.12`
is the CAPTURE VIEWER's row, so closing it on a generic table demo would close a
line while the reference screen gained nothing (R1722's lesson). `hello-packet-view`
composes the derivation: `export_dialects` is readable before exporting, `export`
takes `{dialect, scope}` with each argument's DOMAIN published — the dialect's
values come from a path a client can read, the scope's from a closed vocabulary —
and the answer carries the text, the verdict, the losses and which rows it covered.

★ THE SCOPE VOCABULARY IS DELIBERATELY NOT SHARED. `table_export::Scope` is
`selection | all`, where `selection` means a rectangle of cells. The capture
viewer has no cell rectangle; what a person there is looking at is the set of
rows the FILTER KEPT, so its vocabulary is `shown | all`. The derivation is
shared and the words are not, because putting two different facts under one word
is the defect class this screen's own history is full of.

optional quote, `LineEnd`) with three canonical entries in one `NAMED` roster;
`Headers`, `Scope`, `Carried`, `CarriedSet`, `Line`, `Loss`, `Export`,
`DialectDefect`, `ReadDefect`, `NamedDialect`; `write` / `read` / `dialects_to_wire`.
16 unit tests including the round-trip law on both quoting dialects and on the

CHANGED — `widgets/table.rs`. `rows_to_tsv` is one line over
`table_export::write` in the clipboard dialect (byte-identical output, plus a
report the caller may now ask for); `tsv_sanitize` deleted. New

The demo asserts that honest outcome rather than contriving a cell to break,

2. THE MARKING HALF of `capture.t1.12` — bookmarks and comments — was already

R1788.decision_summary:
R1788 — THE DEPLOYABLE PLAN BECOMES THE FRAMEWORK'S, AND MOVING IT FINDS A
DEFECT THAT HAD BEEN LIVE FOR A HUNDRED ROUNDS.

The analysis-tool census carried `lab.t1.12` — "saving a scenario and exporting
a deployable configuration" — as a gap, on the reason that what was missing is
"the SCENARIO level: a whole graph, its frames and its run plan as one saved
artifact".

★★★★★ RE-MEASURED BEFORE THE ROUND WROTE A LINE, THAT REASON WAS WRONG — the
second census row in two rounds, and the third consecutive round to find a
recorded reason false (R1747, R1787, this). Both halves were built. `Archive`
(R1689) saves the whole document with its camera, its selection and an
application companion, and `Archive::read` answers WHY a file will not open
rather than a bool. `launch_order` (R1687) derives the bring-up order from the
link direction. The node lab has had `save`, `open`, `export the configuration`
and `produce the launch script` since R1687/R1689, all four driven on the wire.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING is the sentence this project's standing rule names:
**the artifact derivation lived in an example.** 371 lines — `Plan`, `Deployed`,
the builder, the document rendering and the script rendering — inside one
binary's `src/`, where no second consumer could reach them. This census asks
what the FRAMEWORK provides, so its `gap` was right and its reason was not.

WHERE IT WENT, AND WHY NOT SOMEWHERE EASIER. `pinion-node-graph` already owns
`launch_order` and is declared pure data — no renderer, no reactive runtime, no
window — while the derivation used `ConfigForm`, which lives in `pinion-core`.
The two crates are siblings and neither depends on the other. Rather than invert
that (a pure-data crate pulling in the scene layer, or the base crate pulling in
a model crate), the plan is **generic over the configuration document** and
takes a boundary type for the rows it could not carry: `Uncarried { key, shown,
why }`, where `why` is already a sentence. The form's reason vocabulary is
rendered once, at the seam, by the consumer that owns it. So the crate gained a
derivation and no dependency, and `serde_json` stays out of its public API the
way its manifest says.

WHAT THE MOVE BOUGHT: `Document::deployment` derives the ORDER itself. While a
screen read `launch_order` and handed the sequence to a builder, the order and
the artifact were a call apart and any caller could pass any sequence — for two
things that are one derivation rendered twice.

★★★★★ AND WHAT THE MOVE FOUND, on the crate's first test run: a plan names each
node's configuration file after the node, the document keyed its `nodes` map by
that name, and **two nodes can share one**. The map kept three of four; the
script wrote two heredocs to one path. Live since R1687.

★★★★★ THE INVARIANT THAT LOOKS LIKE IT COVERS THIS DOES NOT, and that is the
finding rather than the bug. `relabel` maintains *authored names are unique
within a tree, and therefore address exactly one node* — a refusal whose own doc
measured the reference floor for the same rule at 6.11. That is about the
**stored label**. A node with no label still has a name: `display_name` falls
back to its KIND's, and a fallback is not a stored value, so nothing can refuse
a second one. The collision happens WHILE THE INVARIANT HOLDS. Two guards, one
rule, at the two layers where it can be enforced at all — and the example never
saw it because that screen labels every card.

Refused rather than papered over: renaming silently would change what a person
sees on the canvas, dropping one is the floor's behaviour, and export is exactly
the moment somebody can still fix it. Both renderings refuse the same input for
the same reason, because a refusal only one of them made would be the drift this
module exists to prevent.

THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11 ACROSS **TWO PROCESSES**, which is the
population a persistence claim has to be judged over. Handed a value its
settings store cannot encode, the reference reports no error on write, no error
on sync and no error on read; the file keeps the type NAME and no payload; and
reading it back **inside the writing process appears to succeed**, because a
process-wide cache answers instead of the file. Only a second process sees the
value is gone — and the status is still no-error there. The entire signal is one
line on stderr. So the in-process test a developer would write PASSES while the
artifact is broken, which is why `Unplannable` carries the node and why this
round's own probe was re-run across two processes before it was believed.

R1789.decision_summary:
R1789 — AN AUTHORED TRACK OF TIMED ENTRIES, AND THE QUERY A SCRUB CANNOT ANSWER
WITHOUT ONE.

The analysis-tool census asks for `lab.t1.10` — a scenario timeline: warmup,
sequential and concurrent tasks, and killing a node at a given time — and
recorded that a graph which stops a node at eight seconds has NO AUTHORING
SURFACE.

★ THAT REASON HELD. It is the first census reason in four rounds to survive
re-measurement (R1747, R1787 and R1788 each found one false), and the
re-measurement is specific rather than a shrug: `animation` interpolates between
TWO points, `pinion_chart::timeline` reads spans somebody already has,
`TransportClock` is a playhead that knows nothing about what is on it, and this
screen's `run` is a BOOLEAN. Somewhere to put the eight seconds is what was
absent.

THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11. The reference has a keyframe API, so by this
project's rule a consumer for one exists. Measured, not read:

* two keys at one step — the second SILENTLY REPLACES the first;
* a step outside its range — DROPPED, and the only signal is a line on stderr;
* two keys it cannot interpolate between — the value in between is an INVALID
  empty variant, with no reason and no state change;
* which keys did t0 to t1 cross — THERE IS NO SUCH QUERY.

The last one decides the shape. An interpolating keyframe API answers a VALUE at
a time and can say nothing about which discrete entries a step passed, so a
scenario is inexpressible there whatever the value is.

WHAT LANDED. `pinion_core::widgets::track`: a `Track` of timed entries whose
`place` refuses a second entry at one moment (`Misplaced::Taken`) rather than
swallowing it, with `replace` for when replacing IS the intent so the two cannot
be confused; a `Seconds` that is validated once at the boundary, so the two ways
a time can be unusable are refusals given in one place rather than at each of
four verbs; `due(after, upto)` over the HALF-OPEN window a tick advanced
through, and `from_start` for the window that has no lower bound; and a
`Schedule` of named lanes, which is what "sequential and concurrent" needs.

★ The half-open rule is the load-bearing decision and it is asserted rather than
commented: a driver ticks (t, t+dt] repeatedly and each entry has to be
delivered EXACTLY ONCE across the whole run — closed at both ends
double-delivers a boundary, open at both drops it. `duration` is derived from
the last entry rather than declared, so a track and its length cannot disagree;
the floor lets you set a duration shorter than the keys you placed and then
never reaches them.

WHAT IS THE APPLICATION'S. What an entry MEANS. `hello-node-lab::scenario::Act`
is four words — warmup, start, stop, kill — because those are the four things
this tool's reference does to a running graph, and a framework that named them
would be inventing a taxonomy it deliberately does not own (the call lab.t1.8
already records). `Stop` and `Kill` have the same effect and different MEANING,
which is why they are two words: a scenario injecting a fault and one shutting a
node down cleanly are testing different things.

★★ THE CLOCK IS EXPLICIT, which is R1600's division rather than a shortcut.
`advance` takes the seconds and answers what it crossed; `run` does not turn a
clock, a tick does. A wall-clock driver would make every assertion about this
screen depend on how fast the machine is, and would hide the one fact a person
wants — the entries a step passed, in order.

★★★★★ AND DRIVING IT FOUND SOMETHING THE MODEL CANNOT SAY. Two lanes telling one
card opposite things at one moment both run, and which one lasts is decided by
LANE ORDER — stable, stated, and not something the author asked for. That is
REPORTED (`conflicts`) rather than refused, and the difference from R1788's
shared name is when the fact becomes true: a duplicate node name breaks the
artifact the moment it is written, while a scenario is authored one entry at a
time and the second half of a pair somebody is midway through placing is not an
error yet. Refusing it would make the tool refuse the ordinary act of moving an
entry out of the way.
changes_bullets: NEW — `crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/track.rs`. `Seconds` (validated once),
`Key<T>`, `Track<T>` (`place` / `replace` / `shift` / `remove` / `at` / `due` /
`from_start` / `duration`), `Schedule<T>` (`track` / `get` / `lanes` /
`duration` / `due` / `from_start`), `Misplaced` with four named refusals. 12
unit tests, including the exactly-once partition across a whole run.
NEW — `examples/hello-node-lab/src/scenario.rs`. `Act` (the screen's taxonomy),
`Entry`, `schedule` / `unschedule` / `advance` / `conflicts` / `wire`.
CHANGED — `hello-node-lab`. `LabState` gains a `scenario` and a `playhead`; the
wire gains `scenario` (read) and `schedule` / `unschedule` / `advance`, the
first two declared `ArgForm::Object` with the act's domain drawn from the same
roster the read publishes.
LIFTED — `external::ObjectArgs`. Obligation 3b fired: reading a declared object
argument was hand-rolled at R1787's table export, R1787's capture viewer and
this round's scenario, and a workspace grep measured **12** sites spelling
`obj.get("…").and_then(as_str)`. The mechanical half — is this an object, is
this field a usable string, is this field a number — is lifted beside
`ArgForm::Object`, the declaration it reads. The BESPOKE half stays at each call
site: a refusal naming the domain a value should have come from is the surface's
own knowledge, and a generic reader inventing one would publish a worse
sentence. Adopted at all three.
CENSUS — `lab.t1.10` gap -> app, with `assembled_by` naming the screen and the
demo. The framework owes 4 of 68, down from 7 at R1787's entry.
DEMO — `tools/demos/r1789_a_scenario_says_what_a_step_crossed.py`, 44 assertions
over seven sections.
verification_bullets: GATES. Workspace clippy exit 0 — and it caught two of this round's own. One was
a `type_complexity`; the other was a `float_cmp`, and that one was a REAL design
correction rather than a lint appeasement: `conflicts` was grouping by a raw
`f32` when the framework hands back a validated `Seconds` whose `Eq` is a real
equality, so reaching past the type to the number was re-deriving the very thing
it exists to have decided. `cargo doc` exit 0, run here rather than left to CI,
and it caught a redundant explicit link on the first pass — the third round
running in which the CI-only gate found something before publishing.
`cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
TESTS. `pinion-core`, `hello-node-lab`, `hello-packet-view` — the packages the
lift and the scenario can move: 4,149 passed, 0 failed.
DEMO. 44 assertions, PASS. Section F failed on its first run and the failure was
the finding: the playhead was still at 8.5 from the section before, so every
entry below it was behind the window. Rewinding is advancing backwards, it moves
the playhead and UNDOES NOTHING — a script played backwards is not an undo — and
the demo now asserts that rather than working around it.
CENSUS. The framework owes 4 of 68 (5 at this round's entry). `--check-proofs`
resolves every citation against the test runner with 0 unanswered. The gate
caught this round's own `assembled_by`: a path written with brackets around it
is not a path, and it said so.
FLOOR. The keyframe probe was compiled and run against 6.11 before any design
was chosen, and its four answers are quoted in the module header.
carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — two, both stated, and one of them is a user report that outranks them.
1. THE SCENARIO HAS NO PAINT. It is authored and driven over the wire and
reported whole; nothing draws it. That is deliberate for one round — the
census row asks for an authoring SURFACE and the model is what was missing —
but a timeline a person cannot see is half of it.
2. `ObjectArgs` IS ADOPTED AT THREE OF THE TWELVE SITES the grep found. The
other nine are query-result readers rather than invoke-argument readers,
which is a different shape; whether they want the same treatment is a
question this round did not answer and did not pretend to.
★★★★★ AND THE STANDING WORK CHANGES HERE. A reader ran the assembled tool and
reported two defects, both of which are registered and both of which are STILL
OPEN: the shipped 1440-wide window cuts the node lab's inspector, and text is
not centred in the box that holds it. Measured while answering: the lab declares
1625 and its page gets 1388, short by 237 — and 1029 of that 1625 is the TOOLBAR
in a rigid row, so what cuts the inspector is not the inspector. R1781 measured
this and deliberately did not fix it, on the argument that closing it meant
choosing between a window bigger than most laptops, a toolbar overflow
affordance that does not exist, and a screen decision three rounds paid for.
That judgment is overruled by the person looking at the window: an honest report
that a screen does not fit is a measurement, not a deliverable. The next rounds
are those two, in that order, ahead of anything the census would have chosen.

re-measurement (R1747, R1787 and R1788 each found one false), and the
re-measurement is specific rather than a shrug: `animation` interpolates between
TWO points, `pinion_chart::timeline` reads spans somebody already has,
`TransportClock` is a playhead that knows nothing about what is on it, and this
screen's `run` is a BOOLEAN. Somewhere to put the eight seconds is what was
absent.

THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11. The reference has a keyframe API, so by this
project's rule a consumer for one exists. Measured, not read:

* two keys at one step — the second SILENTLY REPLACES the first;
* a step outside its range — DROPPED, and the only signal is a line on stderr;
* two keys it cannot interpolate between — the value in between is an INVALID
  empty variant, with no reason and no state change;
* which keys did t0 to t1 cross — THERE IS NO SUCH QUERY.

The last one decides the shape. An interpolating keyframe API answers a VALUE at
a time and can say nothing about which discrete entries a step passed, so a
scenario is inexpressible there whatever the value is.

WHAT LANDED. `pinion_core::widgets::track`: a `Track` of timed entries whose
`place` refuses a second entry at one moment (`Misplaced::Taken`) rather than
swallowing it, with `replace` for when replacing IS the intent so the two cannot
be confused; a `Seconds` that is validated once at the boundary, so the two ways
a time can be unusable are refusals given in one place rather than at each of
four verbs; `due(after, upto)` over the HALF-OPEN window a tick advanced
through, and `from_start` for the window that has no lower bound; and a
`Schedule` of named lanes, which is what "sequential and concurrent" needs.

★ The half-open rule is the load-bearing decision and it is asserted rather than
commented: a driver ticks (t, t+dt] repeatedly and each entry has to be
delivered EXACTLY ONCE across the whole run — closed at both ends
double-delivers a boundary, open at both drops it. `duration` is derived from
the last entry rather than declared, so a track and its length cannot disagree;
the floor lets you set a duration shorter than the keys you placed and then
never reaches them.

WHAT IS THE APPLICATION'S. What an entry MEANS. `hello-node-lab::scenario::Act`
is four words — warmup, start, stop, kill — because those are the four things
this tool's reference does to a running graph, and a framework that named them
would be inventing a taxonomy it deliberately does not own (the call lab.t1.8
already records). `Stop` and `Kill` have the same effect and different MEANING,
which is why they are two words: a scenario injecting a fault and one shutting a
node down cleanly are testing different things.

★★ THE CLOCK IS EXPLICIT, which is R1600's division rather than a shortcut.
`advance` takes the seconds and answers what it crossed; `run` does not turn a
clock, a tick does. A wall-clock driver would make every assertion about this
screen depend on how fast the machine is, and would hide the one fact a person
wants — the entries a step passed, in order.

★★★★★ AND DRIVING IT FOUND SOMETHING THE MODEL CANNOT SAY. Two lanes telling one
card opposite things at one moment both run, and which one lasts is decided by
LANE ORDER — stable, stated, and not something the author asked for. That is
REPORTED (`conflicts`) rather than refused, and the difference from R1788's
shared name is when the fact becomes true: a duplicate node name breaks the
artifact the moment it is written, while a scenario is authored one entry at a
time and the second half of a pair somebody is midway through placing is not an
error yet. Refusing it would make the tool refuse the ordinary act of moving an
entry out of the way.

R1790.decision_summary:
R1790 — AN ANNOUNCEMENT SAYS HOW MUCH TIME IT HAS LEFT, AND A BASELINE STOPS
GUESSING.

This round pays R1787's CI red. Stop-the-line refused R1789's push, which is the
gate working: one job of that run failed and the failure is mine.

WHAT FAILED, AND WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE HERE. The demo sweep reported one
failure — `r1709_a_resize_is_followed_by_pixels`, on the analysis shell:
`every declared region (1500, 940) does not paint is one the reader can bring
into view: expected [], got ['shell.toast']`. The same demo passes on this
machine in 8 seconds.

★★★★★ ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED. Three demos take a baseline of
what a screen paints at its design size and compare it against a later read at
another size, calling the difference *regions the reader can no longer reach*.
That rule is false for any region with a LIFETIME. The shell says
`Overview loaded` at boot, so `shell.toast` is alive and painted when the
baseline is taken — measured, 214 regions — and 2.6 seconds later it is gone,
213. A toast is not scroll-reachable, so on a slow runner it lands in the
unreachable list. Whether it survives to the comparison is a fact about how much
WALL-CLOCK passed, which is the signature of a check reading a clock it cannot
see. This project does not rerun those.

★★★★★ AND THE ROOT IS ONE LAYER DOWN, IN THE FRAMEWORK. `Saying::left`'s own doc
already argued for the fix — *"published because a screen's own gate may want to
drive time forward deliberately, and a test that guesses the duration is a test
that pins a number this type owns"* — and the fact was reachable only from Rust.
A harness that talks over the wire could not ask, so it guessed. The accessor
was right and the WIRE was missing.

WHAT LANDED. `Saying::to_wire` publishes the sentence AND `left` AND `life`, and
the three screens that hold a `Saying` — the shell, the node lab and the capture
viewer — declare a `saying` slot beside their existing `said`. `said` keeps its
shape and answers WHAT is showing; `saying` answers how long it will be.
`rpc_verify::settled_baseline` advances by exactly what the screen says is left,
until the screen says nothing is, and then reads. No lifetime constant in the
harness, no per-screen exemption table, and nothing that goes stale when a
screen changes its mind about how long it speaks for.

★★★★★ THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE FIX WAS WRONG AND RUNNING IT SAID SO. It took two
reads a step apart and returned when they agreed. A 2.6-second toast looks
perfectly stable across a one-second step, so it returned with the toast still
in — 214 regions unchanged, and settling twice gave different answers. A
predicate that detects CHANGE cannot establish IMPERMANENCE. That is this
session's fourth case of a hypothesis formed by reading and disproved by one
run, and it is why the shipped version asks instead.

AGAINST THE FLOOR. The reference's status bar takes a timeout when it is given a
message and offers no way to ask how much of it is left: a caller can read the
current text and cannot tell a sentence about to vanish from one that just
arrived. Both facts are published here.

★ A SECOND FAILURE WAS MY OWN DOING, and naming it is the honest half. `r1708`
failed locally on a real-drag paint wait — and passed in the same CI run. It
passes here too once the `hello-analyzer-shell` I had launched on the user's
display for them to look at is stopped: a `visible_window=True` demo cannot
share a display with another window of the same application. The failure was the
measurement environment I had created, not the code.
changes_bullets: CHANGED — `crates/pinion-core/src/utterance.rs`. `Saying::to_wire` — the
sentence, `left` and `life` as one value.
CHANGED — `examples/hello-analyzer-shell`, `examples/hello-node-lab`,
`examples/hello-packet-view`. Each declares and answers a `saying` slot beside
its `said`. All three hold a `Saying`; they are also the three screens
`r1709` walks.
CHANGED — `tools/rpc_verify.py`. `settled_baseline` — `declared_and_painted`
taken once the screen has stopped saying things, by ASKING `saying.left` and
advancing past it. A screen with no `saying` slot holds no lifetime, so its
baseline is taken as it stands; a screen whose sentence never runs down raises,
because that is a finding rather than something to wait out.
CHANGED — `tools/demos/r1708_a_drag_is_answered_once.py`,
`r1709_a_resize_is_followed_by_pixels.py`,
`r1710_a_resize_says_what_it_granted.py`. The three sites that take a baseline
and compare it later now take a settled one. The class was audited rather than
guessed: seven demos call `declared_and_painted`, and four of them read it at
one size and use it immediately, which is not exposed.
verification_bullets: THE FIX IS PROVEN BY MEASUREMENT, not by the demo going green — it was already
green here. Probed against the running shell: the raw baseline is 214 regions
and contains `shell.toast`; the settled baseline is 213 and does not; the
difference is exactly `['shell.toast']`, the region CI named; and settling twice
gives the same answer where the first draft gave two.
GATES. Workspace clippy exit 0. `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps
--document-private-items` exit 0. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
TESTS. `pinion-core`, `hello-analyzer-shell`, `hello-node-lab`,
`hello-packet-view` — every package that holds a `Saying` or reads one: 4,254
passed, 0 failed.
DEMOS. Nine: the three that were changed, the four other `declared_and_painted`
callers, `r1719` (the utterance surface) and `tools/test_rpc_verify.py`. 9 of 9
pass. `r1708`'s one failure was the launched-app collision described above and
passes with the display clear — re-run and confirmed, not assumed.
carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — one, and it is the standing work rather than a remainder.
THE TWO USER-REPORTED DEFECTS ARE STILL OPEN and are the next two rounds, in
this order: the shipped 1440-wide window cuts the node lab's inspector, and text
is not centred in the box that holds it.
★★★★★ AND A REVIEW THIS ROUND CHANGED THE FIRST ONE'S AXIS. Asked whether the
node lab's palette and inspector would be better as separate windows, and told
to compose against the reference DCC application's layout, this round read that
application's source rather than answering from memory. Its node editor is ONE
area holding six regions, and the palette and the inspector are regions aligned
LEFT and RIGHT inside it — not windows, and the palette ships hidden. What is
freely arrangeable there is the AREA: split, join, move, swap, close, retype,
and duplicate into a new window, with regions toggled, scaled and flipped
inside it, and named layouts above.
So this project has the window layer and a board layer on one screen, and no
region layer at all: the node lab's four panes are fixed widths in a
hand-written layout, which is precisely why the inspector is cut and why nothing
can be rearranged. The next round is therefore the REGION layer — panels that
collapse, scale and change edge — rather than the toolbar overflow it was going
to be. Registered so the reframing is not lost.

R1791.decision_summary:
R1791 — A ROW THAT RUNS OUT OF ROOM GIVES A GROUP UP AND SAYS WHICH, INSTEAD OF
PAINTING PAST ITS OWN EDGE.

A reader opened the assembled analysis tool and reported that the node lab's
inspector was cut off, and asked whether it should not be impossible to cut it
in any situation. It should. This round is that.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is worse than the report. The shipped window is 1440
wide, the lab's page gets 1388, and the lab declared it needed 1625 — short by
237. Of that 1625, **1029 was the toolbar**, so what cut the inspector was not
the inspector. Then: the right cluster's groups need **607** with their gaps and
get **410** at the lab's own design width, **358** in the shell's page — and
**595 at the 1625 it declared as its minimum**. IT DID NOT FIT AT ITS OWN FLOOR
EITHER. The constant it was checked against, `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER = 609`, was
a **reach** — how far the rightmost seat came in, derived off the rectangles by
R1687 — and a reach is not a sum: it holds only if the two clusters are flush,
with nothing between them.

★ THE SCREEN'S OWN SOURCE HAD WRITTEN THE ANSWER AND COULD NOT TAKE IT: *"what
would take it back is an overflow affordance on the toolbar, which this tree
does not have and which is a round of its own; until then a screen whose chrome
outgrows its window clips"*. R1781 measured the same shortfall and deliberately
did not fix it, naming the three repairs one would have to choose between. A
reader then opened the window and saw the clip, which settles which of the three
was right.

THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11. The reference toolkit has an overflow
affordance, so by this project's rule a consumer for one exists. Ten actions
squeezed from 1200px to 220px: **1 of 10** stays visible; **no member says which
nine went**; and each hidden action's own visibility predicate **still answers
true**. The third is the one that decides the shape — a reader asking what a
toolbar can do right now is told there about controls a person cannot see.

WHAT LANDED. `pinion_core::widgets::overflow` decides a row: items carry a width
and a `WhenTight` (`Keep` / `Move` / `MoveFirst`), and `lay` answers `shown`,
`moved`, whether the control is needed, and `short_by` — how much room the row
still does not have after moving everything it may. The control's own width is
charged **only when something moves**, which is the naive bug (show N, then add
a control that does not fit either). `short_by` is what makes "never cut"
checkable rather than hoped for.

★★★★★ AND THE GATES FOUND THE ROUND'S OWN INCOMPLETENESS, TWICE.

The first draft published WHAT had moved and built no way to reach it:
`lab.toolbar.config` became unpressable, which turns a visual defect into a
functional one and is strictly worse. So the control opens a menu, a moved seat
keeps ITS OWN TAG inside it — a seat MOVES rather than being replaced, which is
what a person experiences and what lets every gate that presses
`lab.toolbar.config` go on pressing the configuration export — and a press is
resolved against the open menu BEFORE the canvas.

The second was found by re-running an OLDER gate. `moved_seats` on the wire was
built from each group's `seats()`, while the in-process predicate
`in_toolbar_overflow` carried a hand-written extra case for `lab.toolbar.zoom` —
the zoom read-out's caption, painted inside the view-reset seat. Two spellings of
one fact, and the WIRE had the incomplete one, so `r1709` read that caption as a
region the reader could not bring into view. Both now derive from one `tags()` =
seats + captions. ⇒ the lesson this project keeps re-learning: **two answers to
one question drift, and the one a demo reads is the one that will be wrong.**
changes_bullets: NEW — `crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/overflow.rs`. `WhenTight`, `Item<T>`,
`Row<T>` (`shown` / `moved` / `needs_affordance` / `short_by` / `fits`),
`Unroomed`, and `lay`. 9 unit tests.
CHANGED — `examples/hello-node-lab`. `ToolGroup` (Zoom / Export / File / Run)
with a derived `width`, its `seats`, the `labels` painted inside them, `tags` =
both, and a `word` the control lists it under; `right_cluster` lays them for the
room the toolbar has; `group_right` and `right_cluster_wants` walk the SHOWN
groups, replacing the hand-derived `*_right` chain; `overflow_rect`,
`overflow_menu_seats`, `toolbar_overflow`, `overflow_control_seat`,
`relocate_if_moved`, `toggle_overflow`, `in_toolbar_overflow` (now derived from
`tags`); `Hit::More`; a `toolbar_open` signal; the paint draws only the groups on
the row; `Hit::in_overflow_menu` resolves the open menu before the canvas.
REMOVED — `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER`, a hand-written 609 that was a reach rather
than a sum. Replaced by `ToolGroup::width` (what each group needs, derived) and
`TOOLBAR_RIGHT_FLOOR` (what the cluster needs at its narrowest), which is what
`MIN_W` now makes room for: **1188**, where it was 1625.
WIRE — `toolbar_overflow` answers six facts: `on_the_row`, `moved`,
`moved_seats`, `open`, `control`, `short_by`.
HARNESS — `rpc_verify.behind_an_overflow` (the tags a screen has moved, asked of
the screen), `press_painted_tag` (opens the control first when it holds the
target), and `widen_until_row_whole` (resize until nothing is held back, and

get **410** at the lab's own design width, **358** in the shell's page — and
**595 at the 1625 it declared as its minimum**. IT DID NOT FIT AT ITS OWN FLOOR
EITHER. The constant it was checked against, `TOOLBAR_RIGHT_CLUSTER = 609`, was
a **reach** — how far the rightmost seat came in, derived off the rectangles by
R1687 — and a reach is not a sum: it holds only if the two clusters are flush,
with nothing between them.

★ THE SCREEN'S OWN SOURCE HAD WRITTEN THE ANSWER AND COULD NOT TAKE IT: *"what
would take it back is an overflow affordance on the toolbar, which this tree

affordance, so by this project's rule a consumer for one exists. Ten actions

one question drift, and the one a demo reads is the one that will be wrong.**

R1792.decision_summary:
R1792 — A BOX HOLDS ITS OWN CAPTION, AND CAN SAY WHERE IT PUT IT.

A reader opened the assembled analysis tool and reported two things: that the
words in the protocol chips were not centred in their rectangles, and that
`discovery off` was aligned oddly. Measured through the paint at the size they
had open, both are worse than "not centred".

★★★★★ THE FIRST IS NOT AN ALIGNMENT DEFECT AT ALL — THE WORD IS OUTSIDE ITS BOX.

    box  lab.palette.protocol.tcp = (69, 587, 36, 18)
    run  "tcp"                    = (76, 591, 32, 12)   +7 by hand, 32 in a 36 box
                                                        => 3px past the RIGHT EDGE

All five chips, each by 3. The `+7` was arithmetic against a rectangle the word
is not inside: the caption is a SIBLING of the tagged container, so nothing in
the tree relates the two. This file's containment sweep asks whether a mark is
inside ITS OWN box — and a caption's own box is itself, so it passed.

★★★★★ AND THE SECOND HAS THE SAME CAUSE ONE LAYER OVER. The switch caption's
width read `PALETTE_W - toggle.x - 48 - PAD`, derived against the PANE while it
is drawn inside the switch's own box — whose right edge is already
`PALETTE_W - PAD`. So the one subtraction landed it EXACTLY FLUSH with that
box's border: measured (117, 657, 154, 13) in a box (69, 647, 202, 58), 48px of
gap on the left and ZERO on the right. Two reports, one class: a caption placed
by arithmetic against a rectangle it is not inside.

⚠ THE DEBT FILE'S OWN DIAGNOSIS WAS FALSE, AND RE-MEASURING IS WHAT FOUND IT.
R1780 had concluded that these labels get text-sized boxes, so centring is the
identity and the defect is a layout choice rather than a framework gap. Measured
now through the paint on five screens: the immediate box is text-sized for **3
of 189** runs in the node lab and **0 of 288** in the capture viewer. The boxes
have room. Following the recorded diagnosis would have closed this as
not-a-defect.

THE POPULATION, because two examples are an anecdote. Across five analyzer
screens at their opening size: **230** caption/box pairs drawn as siblings, **5**
escaping the box they appear in, **166** off-centre by more than 2px — and
**675 of 675** text runs declaring `TextAlign::Start`, which is the DEFAULT. So
no site anywhere had ever expressed an intention, and *off-centre* could not be
told from *deliberately left*.

THE FLOOR, BUILT AND RUN AT 6.11, decided the shape:

  * a caption CANNOT escape its box there — the widget owns its text. Parity to
    match, and this module matches it by DERIVING the rectangle.
  * alignment IS declared and round-trips. Parity to match.
  * a caption that does not fit is drawn anyway with NO REPORT — a label whose
    text advances 171px in a 36px box answers `sizeHint 173` and no error.
  * ★★ NOTHING ANSWERS WHERE THE GLYPHS LANDED. The policy is readable and the
    box is readable; the result is not. The style can recompute a text rectangle
    — from an alignment flag THE CALLER PASSES IN, which is a recomputation from
    an assumption rather than a read.

The last two are the introspection axis this framework exists for, so they are
where it goes past the floor: `Fit::Overflows` names a caption that does not fit
and by how much, and `Placed::run` is the rectangle the node is actually built
with, so a caller and a gate read one fact.
changes_bullets: NEW — `crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/caption.rs`. `Align` (Start / Center /
End, with `offset` and `declared`), `Fit` (`Fits { spare_x, spare_y }` /
`Overflows { over_x, over_y }`), `Caption` (measured size, style, per-axis
alignment, padding, and its own `Silence`), `Placed` (`run`, `fit`), `place`
(the derivation, buildable-free so a gate and a screen read one), `captioned`
(the box WITH its caption as a CHILD), `Pointer` (Target / Transparent),
`CAPTION_SUFFIX`, and `escapes` — the gate predicate. 13 unit tests.
CHANGED — `examples/hello-node-lab`. The five protocol chips go through
`captioned`; the determinism switch's caption width is derived from the switch's
own box (`DISCOVERY_CAPTION_INSET`) instead of from the pane.
GATES — `painted::r1792_no_caption_is_drawn_outside_the_box_it_appears_in` runs
`escapes` over every state the sweep reaches (1,000+ runs judged) and
`painted::r1792_the_switch_caption_is_not_flush_with_its_own_border` reads the
switch from the paint rather than recomputing the formula that was wrong. The
family census subtracts `CAPTION_SUFFIX` by the framework's name for it.
DEMO — `tools/demos/r1792_a_box_holds_its_own_caption.py`, five sections, 14
checks, driven at the size the reader had open. Section E prints the REMAINDER
rather than leaving it to be discovered: how many runs on the frame declare an
alignment at all.
`tools/demos/r1651_the_node_lab_matches_the_reference.py` strips the caption
suffix before its undeclared-elements check — and requires the STRIPPED tag to
be declared, so a caption cannot smuggle in a box the specification never named.
verification_bullets: BOTH REPORTED DEFECTS ARE GONE, MEASURED THROUGH THE WIRE AT THE SIZE THEY WERE
REPORTED AT (1440x900).
2px in on each side, CENTRED, where 3px used to hang off the right edge. All
five, asserted individually.
the border it used to touch, and still left-aligned after the track, which
is the layout this screen chose and this round did not change.
* the population on that frame: **0 of 102** caption/box pairs draw outside the
box a reader sees around them, where the harness measured 5 before.
★★★★★ THE GATE'S FIRST ARMING PRODUCED 40 FINDINGS AND EVERY ONE WAS A FALSE
POSITIVE — which is what taught the predicate. The first draft assigned a run to
the smallest box it OVERLAPPED, so a word clipping the corner of a neighbouring
caption's box was reported as hanging 43px off that box's left edge. Overlap is a
relation between rectangles; *being in a box* is a judgment a person makes about
where the word SITS, and the centre is that judgment written down. With the
centre rule the same sweep over the same states reports the five a reader saw and
nothing else. ⇒ a gate that fires is not yet a gate that is right, and the way to
tell is to read every finding rather than the count.
★★ AND THE GATES CAUGHT TWO OF THIS ROUND'S OWN, both from making the caption a
child:
* the five chip containers became POINTER TARGETS, resolving to no External —
60 dead regions across twelve states, by the screen's own transparency
census. They are a colour key, not controls. `Pointer` is now a required
argument with no default, because neither answer is right for both kinds.
* the family census counting by prefix went from 5 to 10: a caption is PART OF
its box, not a second member of its family. `CAPTION_SUFFIX` is published so
a reader subtracts it by the framework's name rather than spelling the rule
again.
★ THE COORDINATE CONVENTION WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. A child's absolute layout
resolves against its container, so `place` answers in the caller's space and the
node carries a box-relative rectangle. Getting that backwards would double the
offset and put every caption outside its box — the exact defect this module
exists to make unrepresentable — so there is a test that asserts the two
spellings against each other rather than a comment claiming it.
GATES. Workspace clippy exit 0. `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps
--document-private-items` exit 0. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. Four packages:
**5,131 passed, 0 failed**. Eleven demos in the blast radius, all green.
carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — three, stated, and the first is the largest.
★★★★★ 1. ALIGNMENT IS STILL UNDECLARED AT 225 OF 230 SITES. This round gave the
tree a way to SAY where a caption sits and adopted it at five chips. Everywhere
else the default still stands, so `off-centre` and `deliberately left` remain
indistinguishable — 166 runs across five screens are off-centre by more than
2px and not one of them says whether that was meant. The demo prints the
number on every run rather than leaving it to be rediscovered. What closes
this is adoption, screen by screen, and each adoption is cheap: the capability
exists and the gate is already armed.
2. THE ESCAPE GATE RUNS ON ONE SCREEN. `escapes` is the framework's, so a second
screen arms it in one line, and the four other analyzer screens measured 0
escapes today — but *measured today by a probe* is not *gated every push*.
The node lab has it because the node lab is where the report came from.
3. PADDING IS NOT A DECLARED AXIS EITHER, and the switch caption is the case:
its repair is a derivation against the right rectangle, not a declaration that
it keeps room. A caption flush with its border is legitimate for some designs
and wrong for this one, and nothing in the tree can tell them apart — the same
shape as (1), one property over. `Caption::padding` is where that would go.
NOT CARRIED, because measuring it is what corrected it:
`debt-text-is-not-centred-in-the-box-that-holds-it` recorded R1780's diagnosis
that these labels get text-sized boxes and centring is therefore the identity.
Measured through the paint on five screens, the immediate box is text-sized for
3 of 189 runs in the node lab and 0 of 288 in the capture viewer. The diagnosis
is corrected in the file rather than quietly stepped around.

R1793.decision_summary:
R1793 — A HISTOGRAM CHOOSES ITS OWN BINS AND SAYS WHICH RULE CHOSE THEM.

The analysis-tool census records `dashboard.t1.6` — *a latency distribution: a
histogram* — as a gap the FRAMEWORK owes, with the reason "NO BINNING IN THE
CRATE: `Density` (KDE), box and violin exist, and a histogram is assembled by
the application out of `BarChart` bins it computes itself".

RE-MEASURED BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN, that reason is true and precise — and
STRONGER than it says. `Bar::with_bin` has carried a numeric extent since R1395
and `BarChart::select_x_range` cross-filters on it, so a bar can HOLD an
interval; nothing computes one. And `hello-histogram-brush`, the one screen in
this tree named for a histogram, does not bin either: it starts from counts
somebody already aggregated. The step from samples to bins had no consumer at
all.

★★★★★ THE ASYMMETRY THAT DECIDED THE SHAPE, and it is internal rather than a
comparison. This crate already chooses a smoothing width from the data —
`density::Bandwidth` — and the argument written on it is the argument for this
module, word for word: *"It is the one parameter that decides whether a violin
shows two modes or one, so it is declared rather than buried: a chart that
picked silently would be making the reader's conclusion for them."* Bin width
decides exactly that and more brutally. One crate answered the question for the
continuous estimator and left it unanswered for the discrete one.

⚠ NO FLOOR WAS MEASURABLE. The reference toolkit's charting is a separate
module and this install does not carry it, so nothing here compares and no
superiority is claimed on that axis. The comparison this is actually held to is
the internal one, which is stricter.

WHAT LANDED: `BinRule` (Freedman-Diaconis by default, Scott, Sturges, Fixed) in
`Bandwidth`'s own shape — same `Fixed` escape, same `name()` for the wire;
`Binned::of` deriving edges and counts; `BinError` naming what about the samples
made it impossible; `bars()` handing `BarChart` extents the brush already reads.

★★ AND THE HALF A CHART DOES NOT NORMALLY PUBLISH: `Basis` — n, sigma and the
interquartile range. A reader looking at a surprising histogram has two
hypotheses, *the data is like that* and *the binning did that*, and no published
histogram in this tree could tell them apart.
changes_bullets: NEW — `crates/pinion-chart/src/histogram.rs`. `BinRule` (+ `name`), `BinError`
(+ `Display`, `Error`), `Basis`, `Binned` (`of` / `edges` / `counts` / `bins` /
`width` / `rule` / `basis` / `bars`), `MAX_BINS`. Re-exported from the crate
root beside `Bandwidth` and `DensityError`, which are its models. 9 unit tests.
CENSUS — `dashboard.t1.6` moves `gap` -> `have`, with a `proven_by` naming three
tests. The framework now owes 3 of 68, from 4.
DECIDED AND NOT DONE: the consumer. The dashboard's `latency` card is
`Tier::Reserved` (release 2) and promoting it changes which cards the palette
offers in release 1 — a structure the behaviour canon defines, not a round.
R1722's recorded failure was closing a census row that touched no analyzer
screen; the opposite error is reshaping the product to suit a round. So the
promotion is named as R1794's subject rather than taken here.
verification_bullets: THE PROOF IS END TO END AND THROUGH THE PUBLIC API ONLY, which is what the
census's `have` verdict costs: sixteen round-trip times in milliseconds, with
the long tail a latency distribution always has, become a `Binned`, then
`BarChart` bars, then a drawn scene carrying `chart.bar.0` — and brushing the
first bin's own derived extent changes the drawing, so the intervals the
histogram computed are the ones the cross-filter reads.
★★★★★ AND THE RULE IS SHOWN TO BE A DECISION RATHER THAN A DETAIL: twelve
samples with one far outlier bin into MORE bins under Freedman-Diaconis than
under Scott, because one far sample stretches sigma while the interquartile
range barely moves. Same data, two shapes, and a reader can only tell which they
are looking at because the chart says which rule ran.
THE EDGE CASES ARE ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: every sample lands in exactly
one bin under all four rules; the largest sample is IN the top bin rather than
past it (every histogram makes this choice and most make it silently); a rule
whose spread measure degenerates falls back instead of refusing, because the
samples are still binnable and it is the rule that ran out; and no rule can ask
for more bins than `MAX_BINS`, because `n^(-1/3)` against a tiny spread asks for
millions and a chart that allocated them would hang on the data rather than say
anything about it.
★ CLIPPY CAUGHT TWO AND BOTH WERE REAL DESIGN CORRECTIONS, not suppressions: a
float equality became `min >= max`, which on a sorted slice IS "no spread" and
says so without an equality on floats (a margin there would have been WRONG — it
would refuse a genuinely narrow spread); and `width()` now reads the stored
edges rather than recomputing from the span and the count, so the width and the
edges cannot disagree.
GATES: workspace clippy exit 0, `cargo fmt --all` clean, `pinion-chart` full
suite passes, census proof gate 71 citations against 6,157 selectable tests with
0 unanswered.
carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — and the first is now a reader's instruction rather than my choice.
★★★★★ 1. THE CONSUMER, AND THE READER DECIDED IT. Asked whether to promote the
dashboard's `latency` card out of `Tier::Reserved` so this capability has a
screen, the answer was to promote it and build it as R1794. So the next round
reads what the canon puts on that card, bins REAL samples rather than drawing
a placeholder, publishes the rule and the basis on the wire, and gates it.
2. `dashboard.t2.4` (cross-filter every linked view) is still owed and is the
nearer half of this one: bar and line participate, POLAR HAS NO BRUSH LEG AT
ALL. A histogram that cross-filters is worth more beside a polar chart that
also does.
3. `lab.t2.16` (stateful nodes) is owed and is NOT buildable: the census records
it as a deliberate divergence — the only node state is a delay, which is what
buys a tick's reproducibility, and arbitrary state makes a graph's meaning
not a function of the graph. Re-measured this round and still true. It needs
a spec round, and until one happens counting it as buildable work would be
counting a decision as a debt.

R1794.decision_summary:
R1794 — THE WIRE SAYS WHERE THE GLYPHS ARE, NOT JUST WHERE THE BOX IS.

★★★★★ THE ROUND'S SUBJECT IS A DEFECT IN HOW I WORK, AND THE READER NAMED IT.
Shown the assembled tool after R1792, they reported that five chips, three row
seats and a switch caption were still not centred, that a caption was silently
truncated, and that the sidebar clips when the window shrinks. Then:

    "왜 니가 조사 못 하고 나한테 물어봐? 그거 자체가 아키텍처 문제야"

They are right, and the diagnosis is worse than "the framework cannot answer".

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG. R1792 centred RECTANGLES and called it centred text.
The node lab passed `(32, 12)` as `tcp`'s size because 32 was the number the
hand-written code before it used — and **32 was a BOX**. Asked of the wire, the
glyphs advance **15**. So a 32-wide rectangle sat perfectly centred in the
36-wide chip while the shaper laid the glyphs `Start`-aligned at the left of it,
8.5px off centre. The gate was green because it compared rectangles; the reader
was looking at glyphs.

★★★★★ AND THE FRAMEWORK COULD ANSWER ALL ALONG. `scene/text_painted` has
published `ink_w` / `ink_h` (what the shaper produced), `painted` (what was
drawn when it differs from the scene's string) and `over_w` / `over_h` since
R1654. Every gate in this tree reached for `scene/snapshot`, which carries
boxes. So the architectural defect was not a missing capability — it was that
the question nobody asked had no consumer, and a human was the instrument.

THE CAUSE CHAIN, END TO END:

  * `Caption` asked the CALLER for the text's size. The reason written on that
    parameter — *"this crate composes scenes and does not shape text"* — was
    FALSE: `pinion_core::measured_text_extent` shapes, is callable anywhere, and
    exists precisely so a view fn can size text it is about to paint.
  * `seat_w` was a per-character estimate, `len * FONT_SMALL * 7 / 10 + 16`,
    across FIFTEEN call sites. That is the class `measured_text_extent`'s own
    doc names and warns about: *"a caller falls back to its own per-character
    estimate ... Both boxes were 'right' and only their derivation disagreed"*.
    Measured: the estimate makes `delete` 58px; the glyphs are 27.
  * So every seat was a box sized by a guess, holding a caption drawn at the
    left of it, and three separate gates agreed it was fine.

WHAT LANDED. The shaper answers, in both places. And the ANSWER SAYS WHERE IT
CAME FROM: `Sized::{Measured, Stated, Guessed}` on every placement, so an
alignment claim built on an estimate can be refused rather than believed. A
headless caller still lays out deterministically and is told the number is a
guess, which is the arm that used to be silent.
changes_bullets: CHANGED — `pinion_widget_paint::caption`. `Caption::new` takes no size; `place`
asks `measured_text_extent`. `Caption::stating` is the escape for a caller who
genuinely knows better (a test with no provider). `Sized` and `Placed::sized`
publish which of the three answered.
CHANGED — `examples/hello-node-lab`. `seat_w` measures, with the old estimate
kept only for where nothing can shape, and `SEAT_PAD` separated out so the
padding is a decision rather than the slack an estimate happened to leave. The
link chrome's `inner` derives through `caption::place` instead of spanning the
seat's whole inner width. The three node's-life seats (`collapse`, `switch off`,
`delete`) go through `captioned`. The determinism switch ASKS whether its full
sentence fits and paints `discovery_word` when it does not — the sentence is
still what the `AccessNode` announces, so the clause is unpainted rather than
lost.
NEW — `rpc_verify.ink_in_boxes`: for every run, the INK's gaps inside the box a
reader sees it in. ★ It excludes a caption's own box, because a caption's
rectangle IS the ink and judging it against itself answers 0/0 for everything —
that bug was written, measured, and is now what section B of the demo pins.
NEW — `tools/demos/r1794_the_wire_says_where_the_glyphs_are.py`, 36 checks.
GATES — `r1651`'s family roster subtracts `CAPTION_SUFFIX` (a caption is part of
its box, not a member of its family: `lab.inspector` read 18 -> 21 on the first
run). `r1792`'s centring assertion is `abs(left - right) <= 1` rather than exact
equality, because the slack is `box - ink` and a real ink measurement does not
halve — an exact-equality centring check can only survive on invented numbers.
REGISTERED — `debt-below-its-floor-a-screen-clips-where-the-reference-reflows`,
the reader's fourth report. Measured: `scene/resize` clamps at 1440 but a window
manager drag does not, and below the floor this tree CLIPS and offers a pan by
declared policy. The reference DCC reflows instead. That is an axis, not a bug,
and it is too large to half-build here.
verification_bullets: EVERY ONE OF THE READER'S FIRST THREE REPORTS IS CLOSED, AND CLOSED BY THE WIRE
RATHER THAN BY ASKING THEM AGAIN — which is the round's actual deliverable.
seat            ink      left/right   top/bottom
collapse        43x15    23 / 24      2 / 3
switch off      50x15    20 / 20      2 / 3
Truncated runs on the lab's opening frame: 6 -> 5, and
`discovery off · fully specif…` is no longer among them.
★★★★★ THE GATE PASSED VACUOUSLY ONCE AND THE FIX WAS ONE LINE. With the caption
carrying its own tag sized to the ink, `ink_in_boxes` picked THAT as the box and
answered `L0 R0` for every caption in the tree. It looked like a total pass. The
helper now excludes a caption's own box and the numbers above appeared. This is
recorded rather than quietly corrected because it is the same failure shape as
the one the round is about: a check that cannot fail is not a check, and it
reads exactly like a check that passed.
GATES: workspace clippy exit 0 after catching a redundant closure; `cargo doc
--workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` exit 0; `cargo fmt --all` clean;
`hello-node-lab` + `pinion-widget-paint` 1,028 passed 0 failed; twelve demos in
the blast radius all green, two of which had to be corrected first and both
corrections were the gates telling the truth about this round's own change.

R1794.publishable_decision_summary:
R1794 — THE WIRE SAYS WHERE THE GLYPHS ARE, NOT JUST WHERE THE BOX IS.

★★★★★ THE ROUND'S SUBJECT IS A DEFECT IN HOW I WORK, AND THE READER NAMED IT.
Shown the assembled tool after R1792, they reported that five chips, three row
seats and a switch caption were still not centred, that a caption was silently
truncated, and that the sidebar clips when the window shrinks. Then:

    "왜 니가 조사 못 하고 나한테 물어봐? 그거 자체가 아키텍처 문제야"

They are right, and the diagnosis is worse than "the framework cannot answer".

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG. R1792 centred RECTANGLES and called it centred text.
The node lab passed `(32, 12)` as `tcp`'s size because 32 was the number the
hand-written code before it used — and **32 was a BOX**. Asked of the wire, the
glyphs advance **15**. So a 32-wide rectangle sat perfectly centred in the
36-wide chip while the shaper laid the glyphs `Start`-aligned at the left of it,
8.5px off centre. The gate was green because it compared rectangles; the reader
was looking at glyphs.

★★★★★ AND THE FRAMEWORK COULD ANSWER ALL ALONG. `scene/text_painted` has
published `ink_w` / `ink_h` (what the shaper produced), `painted` (what was
drawn when it differs from the scene's string) and `over_w` / `over_h` since
R1654. Every gate in this tree reached for `scene/snapshot`, which carries
boxes. So the architectural defect was not a missing capability — it was that
the question nobody asked had no consumer, and a human was the instrument.

THE CAUSE CHAIN, END TO END:

  * `Caption` asked the CALLER for the text's size. The reason written on that
    parameter — *"this crate composes scenes and does not shape text"* — was
    FALSE: `pinion_core::measured_text_extent` shapes, is callable anywhere, and
    exists precisely so a view fn can size text it is about to paint.
  * `seat_w` was a per-character estimate, `len * FONT_SMALL * 7 / 10 + 16`,
    across FIFTEEN call sites. That is the class `measured_text_extent`'s own
    doc names and warns about: *"a caller falls back to its own per-character
    estimate ... Both boxes were 'right' and only their derivation disagreed"*.
    Measured: the estimate makes `delete` 58px; the glyphs are 27.
  * So every seat was a box sized by a guess, holding a caption drawn at the
    left of it, and three separate gates agreed it was fine.

WHAT LANDED. The shaper answers, in both places. And the ANSWER SAYS WHERE IT
CAME FROM: `Sized::{Measured, Stated, Guessed}` on every placement, so an
alignment claim built on an estimate can be refused rather than believed. A
headless caller still lays out deterministically and is told the number is a
guess, which is the arm that used to be silent.
publishable_changes_bullets: CHANGED — `pinion_widget_paint::caption`. `Caption::new` takes no size; `place`
asks `measured_text_extent`. `Caption::stating` is the escape for a caller who
genuinely knows better (a test with no provider). `Sized` and `Placed::sized`
publish which of the three answered.
CHANGED — `examples/hello-node-lab`. `seat_w` measures, with the old estimate
kept only for where nothing can shape, and `SEAT_PAD` separated out so the
padding is a decision rather than the slack an estimate happened to leave. The
link chrome's `inner` derives through `caption::place` instead of spanning the
seat's whole inner width. The three node's-life seats (`collapse`, `switch off`,
`delete`) go through `captioned`. The determinism switch ASKS whether its full
sentence fits and paints `discovery_word` when it does not — the sentence is
still what the `AccessNode` announces, so the clause is unpainted rather than
lost.
NEW — `rpc_verify.ink_in_boxes`: for every run, the INK's gaps inside the box a
reader sees it in. ★ It excludes a caption's own box, because a caption's
rectangle IS the ink and judging it against itself answers 0/0 for everything —
that bug was written, measured, and is now what section B of the demo pins.
NEW — `tools/demos/r1794_the_wire_says_where_the_glyphs_are.py`, 36 checks.
GATES — `r1651`'s family roster subtracts `CAPTION_SUFFIX` (a caption is part of
its box, not a member of its family: `lab.inspector` read 18 -> 21 on the first
run). `r1792`'s centring assertion is `abs(left - right) <= 1` rather than exact
equality, because the slack is `box - ink` and a real ink measurement does not
halve — an exact-equality centring check can only survive on invented numbers.

R1795.decision_summary:
R1795 — THE RED I PUBLISHED, AND WHY MY BLAST RADIUS WAS A GUESS.

R1791 and R1792 both went out with a failing CI run. `origin/main` stopped at
R1792, and the push carrying R1793 and R1794 was refused by stop-the-line. The
red was not stale — checked first, as the rule requires: BOTH rounds' runs had
failed, in the same job.

★★★★★ THE CAUSE IS ONE SENTENCE AND IT IS MINE. I chose the blast radius by
hand. Every round I wrote down the demos that looked affected, and six of the
645 were not on that list.

And this was already a registered debt —
`debt-nothing-enumerates-which-demo-asserts-which-wire-fact`, open since R1670.
`tools/blast_radius.py` answers which PACKAGES a change can break, from
`cargo metadata`, and its own docstring states this class exactly: *"a lesson
recorded twice and re-broken twice is not a lesson, it is a computation nobody
had written"*. Nothing computes which DEMOS a change can break.

WHAT THE SIX WERE, and every one was a gate telling the truth about R1791/R1792
rather than a regression:

  * `r1684` aimed at `lab.toolbar.config`'s rectangle; the overflow control was
    holding it.
  * `r1688`'s fit-centring tolerance was tuned to one canvas width; R1794
    measured the seat widths, so the cards changed size and the zoom-scaled
    rounding landed differently.
  * `r1691` refused a silent region inside another; a captioned box silences its
    own caption BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the structure R1792 built on purpose.
  * `r1700` counted declared-and-painted tags, and a row that gives a group up
    paints fewer.
  * `r1727` pinned the design surface at 1625, which R1791 brought down to 1440
    — the round's outcome.
  * `r1767` asserted the application still does not conform, which R1791 made
    false.

★ AND ONE OF THEM CARRIED A SECOND DEFECT WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX. `r1727`'s
real-pointer confirmation compared `round(got)` with `round(at)` — two separate
roundings of the same fractional value, through Python's BANKER'S rounding. An
aim at `x.5` rounds DOWN there while the X server had already put the pointer
one pixel up. It surfaced when a node card's width became odd and its centre
landed between pixels. The aim is legitimately fractional — it is a rectangle's
centre — so what had to change is the check admitting that a pointer is not.
changes_bullets: CHANGED — six demos, each to the fact that is true now:
* `r1684` presses through `press_painted_tag`, which opens the overflow
control when it is holding the seat. Third demo to learn it, second to learn
it from CI.
* `r1688` states the same invariant its in-process sibling does — each side
within 1.5px of the ideal half — instead of a tolerance tuned to one canvas.
* `r1691` admits ONE derived exception to "no silence inside a silence": a
caption covered by its OWN box, which is `captioned`'s structure. A pane
silencing something three levels down still fails.
* `r1700` adds back what the overflow control is holding, so the coverage
count is a property of the screen rather than of the window.
* `r1767` asserts per-surface reporting and the node lab's ABSENCE from what
declines, in place of two clauses that said the application cannot conform.
CHANGED — `rpc_verify`'s real-pointer confirmation compares against the pixel
the driver actually asked for, within one, because a fractional aim cannot be
hit by an integral pointer.
REGISTERED — `debt-nothing-enumerates-which-demo-asserts-which-wire-fact` is
widened from "wire fact -> demo" to "any change -> the demos it can break", with
the six as evidence, the measured shape of the fix (a demo names the example it
launches, so an AST walk gives the mapping) and priority raised.
verification_bullets: ALL SIX PASS, and three of them were re-measured rather than relaxed:
* `r1688`: before touching the number, the gutters were measured at three
canvas widths — 3 apart at 844, 1 at 1104, 2 at 1304. It does not grow with
the canvas, so it is each node's position being rounded independently (the
bounding box of rounded rectangles is not the rounded bounding box) and not
a fit that leans. THEN the bound was stated as the invariant.
* `r1700`: the floor's own rule is that a drop is the round's to explain, so
it was explained before it was touched. The node lab answers for 59 at its
design width with two groups moved, and **63** at 1700 and 2000 where
nothing moves — MORE than the committed 61. It did not stop vouching for
part of itself; five of its seats are one press away at the narrow size.
* `r1727`: the pointer failure was diagnosed to banker's rounding rather than
widened. `round(502.5)` is 502 in Python and the X server had used 503.
GATES: workspace clippy exit 0, `cargo fmt --all` clean, and the six demos green
locally. ⚠ `r1767` cannot be judged on this host by wall clock alone — it timed
out on the first local run, which is
`debt-a-deterministic-demo-has-a-wall-clock-bound` — and passed on the re-run;
CI is what settles it.
carry_forward_bullets: CARRY — three, and the first is the round's own subject.
★★★★★ 1. THE COMPUTATION IS STILL NOT WRITTEN. This round repaired the six and
did NOT build the demo blast radius, because the reader asked for the loop to
close. So the next round that changes a screen picks its demos by hand again,
with exactly the same odds. The debt now carries the measured shape: a demo
names the example it launches (`RpcSubprocess("hello-node-lab")`), so an AST
walk over `tools/demos/` yields example -> demos, and `blast_radius.py`
already yields changed paths -> packages. The two compose.
2. THE SWEEP CANNOT BE RUN HERE. `debt-a-deterministic-demo-has-a-wall-clock-
bound` measured 379 of 589 demos timing out on this host, and `r1767` timed
out once during this round before passing. So the local answer has to be a
COMPUTED SUBSET; running everything is not an option that exists.
3. AND THE READER'S REPORTS FROM THIS SESSION THAT ARE STILL OPEN:
`debt-below-its-floor-a-screen-clips-where-the-reference-reflows` (the
sidebar when the window shrinks — an axis, with the reference measured:
`AREAMINX 29`, a vertical minimum of one header, and minima that live on the
AREA rather than on the window) and the alignment adoption at the 225 sites
that still declare nothing.

R1796.decision_summary:
R1796 — THE SCE PIN MOVES 22 COMMITS, AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY BROUGHT IS AN
ORDERING GUARANTEE NOTHING EXERCISED.

`vendor/sce` 87f4b1d8 -> 084dfdbf. ★★★★★ MEASURING BEFORE WRITING CORRECTED THE
FRAMING TWICE, and both corrections matter more than the bump.

FIRST: the regenerated emit is BYTE-IDENTICAL. All fifteen committed
`{chart}_sm.rs` modules came back unchanged, because SCE emits the host-served
path only for a `type` the BUILD declares and this build declared none. So the
bump is inert by construction, not by luck.

SECOND, and this is the one that reversed the round's premise: THE RUST DOOR IS
NOT NEW. `backends/rust/runtime/src/host_processor.rs` existed at the previous
pin — 265 lines then, 297 now. What the 22 commits did was give the SAME door to
the C++, C11, Go, Python and Kotlin engines. Pinion could have opened it before
the bump and did not.

⇒ SO WHAT DID THE BUMP BRING, for a Rust consumer? One widening: a handler
answered with `Option<HostSendResponse>` and now answers with `Vec<…>` — a LIST
of events, in the order the document should see them. SCE's own doc gives the
case: an act can produce two observations a document must see in a particular
order, and the alternatives (re-enter the engine; return one and deliver the
rest next step) either do not port across backends or put the hidden state back
in the host.

An ordering guarantee nothing exercises is an ordering guarantee nobody has
checked. That is what this round consumed.

★ AND THE COUNTERFACTUAL MEASURED SOMETHING BETTER THAN THE PREDICTION. Reversing
the handler's list was predicted to leave the machine in `asking` — never
moving. It rests in `heard_first`: both events reach the external queue in the
handler's order, the state that cannot take `second` DROPS it, and `first` then
moves the machine one step with nothing left to carry it. So an out-of-order
reply does not merely fail to arrive, it costs an event outright, and the
resting state names which one. Sharper than the prediction: an engine that
reordered replies would reach `settled`, and one that delivered them as a SET
would reach `settled` too.
changes_bullets: PIN — `vendor/sce` gitlink, both `Cargo.toml` revs and `Cargo.lock` moved to
084dfdbf in one commit; `tools/pin_sync.py --check-dual-pin` reports
`SCE@084dfdb (manifest = lock = vendor/sce)`.
NEW — `crates/pinion-core/fixtures/host_served_send.scxml`. `asking` sends to
`pinion.fixture.host` and accepts only `first`; `heard_first` accepts only
`second`. The ORDER is therefore asserted by where the document ended up rather
than by inspecting a queue.
NEW — `HOST_PROCESSOR_TYPES` in `tests/statechart_emit.rs`. Not configuration:
SCE decides at compile time whether a `<send type=…>` is a dispatch or an
`error.execution` raise, so this list is the difference between a door and a
wall. Verified in the emit — the new module calls `perform_host_send`.
NEW — `crates/pinion-core/src/host_served.rs`, following the
`self_answering_raise` precedent (a fixture whose purpose is to make an ENGINE
guarantee observable from here). Three tests: the send reaches the host and both
replies arrive in order; reversing the list does not reach `settled`; and a
declared type with NOTHING registered performs nothing, which is SCE's stated
behaviour and is edited in two different files, so nothing else checked that
both halves were present.
CHANGED — `self_answering_raise`'s re-export is `#[cfg(test)]`, which is what it
always was: its one consumer is `crate::resume`'s test module, so a lib build
without `cfg(test)` had nothing using it. Stated rather than suppressed with an
`allow`, because "only the tests drive this chart" is the fact the gate was
reporting.
REGISTERED — `debt-a-host-served-send-is-a-third-escape-hatch`. §3 fixes
`Effect(opaque)` and `External(opaque)` as the ONLY escape hatches, and a
host-served `<send>` whose handler an APPLICATION registers is a third. This
round serves the FRAMEWORK's own type with framework code, which is an internal
path; opening registration to consumers is a spec round, and CLAUDE.md's rule
for exactly this case is to propose one rather than work around. The debt also
records that `debt-dry-run-void-for-invoke-externals` must be answered in the
same round, because a host that really performs an act breaks §2 #3's zero-cost
scenario exploration.
verification_bullets: THE PIN IS SYNCHRONISED IN ALL FOUR PLACES and the gate says so:
`SCE@084dfdb (manifest = lock = vendor/sce)`. ★ It caught the one that is easy
to miss — the gitlink has to be STAGED, not merely checked out, and it reported
"vendor/sce is checked out at 084dfdb but the index records 87f4b1d" until it
was.
THE EMIT IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. Regenerated against the new pin
with nothing else changed: byte-identical, all fifteen modules. Regenerated
again after the fixture and the type declaration: the fifteen move by exactly
ONE LINE each — the `source-hash` header, which hashes the whole SOURCE SET, so
adding a chart moves it for every module. No generated code changed. The
sixteenth module is the new one, and it carries `perform_host_send`, which is
the proof the declaration opened a door rather than leaving a refusal.
GATES: the emit gate run as a COMPARISON (not a regeneration) exit 0, so the
committed bytes are what the pinned generator produces; workspace clippy exit 0;
`pinion-core` + `pinion-runtime` + `pinion-rpc` **5,916 passed, 0 failed**.
★ TWO THINGS THIS ROUND GOT WRONG AND MEASURING FIXED:
* A regeneration was first sent to a BUILD MACHINE. It exited 0 after 871
seconds and wrote the files there; this tree was untouched. A step that
WRITES into the tree cannot be delegated, and the only reason it was caught
is that `git status` was checked instead of the exit code.
* A new fixture cannot be added and consumed in one step: the Rust module
`include!`s a generated file that only the regeneration creates, and the

R1796 — THE SCE PIN MOVES 22 COMMITS, AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY BROUGHT IS AN
ORDERING GUARANTEE NOTHING EXERCISED.

`vendor/sce` 87f4b1d8 -> 084dfdbf. ★★★★★ MEASURING BEFORE WRITING CORRECTED THE
FRAMING TWICE, and both corrections matter more than the bump.

FIRST: the regenerated emit is BYTE-IDENTICAL. All fifteen committed
`{chart}_sm.rs` modules came back unchanged, because SCE emits the host-served
path only for a `type` the BUILD declares and this build declared none. So the
bump is inert by construction, not by luck.

SECOND, and this is the one that reversed the round's premise: THE RUST DOOR IS
NOT NEW. `backends/rust/runtime/src/host_processor.rs` existed at the previous
pin — 265 lines then, 297 now. What the 22 commits did was give the SAME door to
the C++, C11, Go, Python and Kotlin engines. Pinion could have opened it before
the bump and did not.

⇒ SO WHAT DID THE BUMP BRING, for a Rust consumer? One widening: a handler
answered with `Option<HostSendResponse>` and now answers with `Vec<…>` — a LIST
of events, in the order the document should see them. SCE's own doc gives the
case: an act can produce two observations a document must see in a particular
order, and the alternatives (re-enter the engine; return one and deliver the
rest next step) either do not port across backends or put the hidden state back
in the host.

An ordering guarantee nothing exercises is an ordering guarantee nobody has
checked. That is what this round consumed.

★ AND THE COUNTERFACTUAL MEASURED SOMETHING BETTER THAN THE PREDICTION. Reversing
the handler's list was predicted to leave the machine in `asking` — never
moving. It rests in `heard_first`: both events reach the external queue in the
handler's order, the state that cannot take `second` DROPS it, and `first` then
moves the machine one step with nothing left to carry it. So an out-of-order
reply does not merely fail to arrive, it costs an event outright, and the
resting state names which one. Sharper than the prediction: an engine that
reordered replies would reach `settled`, and one that delivered them as a SET
would reach `settled` too.
