R1807.decision_summary:
R1807 pursues north-star condition (2): every `have` verdict in the analysis-tool census naming a test that actually RUNS. The opening re-measurement found the gate one step short of its own purpose.

THE HOLE. R1771 built `--check-proofs` precisely because `proven_by` was checked for nothing at all. It asks whether a CITED test can be selected by the runner, and it never asks whether a row cited anything: `check_proofs` iterates `proof_names(row)`, so a row carrying no field iterates zero times and passes. `check_assemblies` has the identical shape for `assembled_by`. The census therefore REFUSED A ROTTED CITATION AND ADMITTED A CLAIM THAT CITED NOTHING — the stronger claim, checked less — and that fact existed only as a line of prose in the report: "28 of 35 `have` verdict(s) name a proof — the rest are claims, and this says so". A reader can agree with that sentence; no gate can act on it. The rule was written where it could not be enforced, inside the tool built to end exactly that pattern.

THE INSTRUMENT THAT FAILED ME. Attaching the seven proofs began by searching test NAMES, which reported zero tests for `lab.t0.4` (a master auto-discovery switch, off by default). Reading bodies instead, `r1645_a_drawing_known_to_be_incomplete_says_so` opens with `assert_eq!(document.discovery(), Discovery::Off, "off is the default")`. A test that exercises a capability is under no obligation to be NAMED for it, and a name search's "there is none" leads directly to writing a duplicate of a test that already exists.

THE DEFECT UNDER THE SEVENTH. `dashboard.t2.9` claims *light and dark parity*, resting on "the theme system, with every demo asserting both" — a claim with no test behind it. Measured, dark `inverse_primary` on `inverse_surface` reads 3.56 against the light palette's 7.75 for the same pairing, so a snackbar's action label (which is what that role's own documentation says it is) clears WCAG AA in one theme and not the other. The dark palette's constructor meanwhile documents itself as "the accent lightened so the dark surface keeps WCAG AA contrast on every paired role". That sentence was false for over a year, and it was nobody's fault: `contrast_ratio` has existed since R1546 but was built for a chart's ink on a colour ramp and had no table of PALETTE pairings to run over. The instrument was here and the question was never put to it.
changes_bullets: `tools/analyzer_census.py`:

* `check_evidence(rows)` — a row whose verdict PROMISES evidence and carries none. A `have` with no `proven_by` is refused, with no allowlist at all: this round took that backlog to zero in the round that built the rule, and an empty ratchet is the only kind that cannot rot. An `app` with no `assembled_by` is refused unless named in `UNASSEMBLED` (11 rows today).
* The ratchet is tamper-evident in both directions: the tool also refuses a name in `UNASSEMBLED` that no longer needs to be there, so the list can only shrink.
* It runs on EVERY invocation rather than behind `--check-proofs`, because it builds nothing — it reads the pin. The expensive half (does the cited test run?) stays behind the flag.
* Seven new selftest cases, one of which asserts that the two OLDER checks let a bare row through — the property that makes the new rule necessary rather than redundant.
`crates/pinion-core/src/legibility.rs` (new) — ink-over-ground as a value:

* `Pairing { ink, ground, floor }` and `PAIRINGS`, a DECLARED table of 17 pairings. A table rather than `fn ground(self) -> ColorRole` because ink-over-ground is a RELATION, not a map: `OnSurface` is ink on `Surface` and on all four container tiers, and `Accent` is a ground for `OnAccent` while itself being ink on `Surface`. A function would pick one and silently stop checking the rest.

* `Floor::{Text, Boundary}` — WCAG 4.5 and 3.0, named for what the pairing IS. There is deliberately no `Decorative` variant: choosing a standard because it makes a gate pass is rationalisation, so the option is not expressible.

* `parity(light, dark) -> Parity` separates the two ways a palette can be wrong — the themes DISAGREEING about a pairing (the parity defect) from a pairing short of its floor in BOTH (an absolute one they agree about, reported as `short_in_both`). Folding either into the other makes one hide the other. All three sets are filled in one pass, so `Parity::accounted()` equals the table by construction.
`crates/pinion-core/src/theme.rs`:

* Dark `inverse_primary` `#1976D2` -> `#0D47A1` (Material Blue 900, 6.69). Blue 800 measured 4.45 — under the floor, and a value within a rounding error of the threshold makes the next palette tweak a coin toss.
* The dark constructor's doc no longer claims "every paired role"; it says "every paired TEXT role", names the gate that now checks it, and states the boundary pairing it does not cover.
`docs/analyzer-census.json` — the seven unproven `have` rows get citations, six of them naming tests that already existed. `dashboard.t2.9`'s `covered_by` is replaced by what was measured.
verification_bullets: THE GATE WAS WATCHED BITING BEFORE IT WAS SATISFIED. With `check_evidence` in and the citations not yet written, the census exited 1 naming exactly the seven rows — `capture.t2.15`, `lab.t0.3`, `lab.t0.4`, `dashboard.t0.6`, `dashboard.t1.3`, `dashboard.t1.12`, `dashboard.t2.9`. A gate first seen already green is a gate nobody has watched work.
* `python3 tools/analyzer_census.py`: `have` 35 of 35 name a proof (28 before this round), exit 0.

* `python3 tools/analyzer_census.py --check-proofs`: 112 proof citation(s) checked against 7,649 selectable test(s), **0 unanswered** — so every `have` names a proof AND every proof resolves to a test the runner can select. That is north-star condition (2), and it is now a gate rather than a sentence in a report.

* `python3 tools/analyzer_census.py --selftest`: PASS, 0 failures, including the case asserting `check_proofs` and `check_assemblies` BOTH return empty for a bare row — the property that makes the new rule necessary rather than redundant — and the case asserting the ratchet holds only `app` rows, so it cannot excuse a `have`.

THE PARITY GATE, AND ITS COUNTERFACTUAL. `r1807_the_two_palettes_agree_about_every_declared_pairing` passes — but it passes in the round that repaired its subject, and a gate first green beside its own repair could be a tautology. `r1807_the_value_this_round_replaced_would_still_be_caught` puts the pre-R1807 dark `inverse_primary` back and requires the report to NAME `inverse_primary/inverse_surface` with light above the floor and dark below it. Two further non-vacuity guards: every pairing must read differently in the two palettes (so none is a fixture that tests nothing), and a synthetically broken palette must move a pairing out of `clear` into `disagree` carrying both ratios.
* `pinion-core::legibility`: 8 passed, 0 failed.
* `cargo test -p pinion-core -p pinion-node-graph -p pinion-rpc --all-targets`: **5,767 passed, 0 failed** — the palette change broke nothing, including the pinned-palette tests.
* `cargo test -p hello-snackbar -p hello-analyzer-shell --all-targets` (the two examples that paint the changed role): 127 passed, 0 failed.
* `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` (CI's exact flags): exit 0, zero warnings.
* `cargo fmt --all --check`: exit 0.

CLOSING AUDIT CAUGHT A CLAIM I WROTE THIS ROUND. The new module's docs said `contrast_ratio` "has existed since R57"; `contrast.rs` is R1546. Repaired before the commit, and the corrected sentence is sharper than the wrong one — the instrument was built for a chart's ink on a colour ramp, which is WHY nobody had pointed it at the palette.
⚠ NOT VERIFIED: the demo sweep, which CI owns. And the gate answers "is there a running test", never "does that test exercise the whole capability" — the tool says so in its own docstring.
carry_forward_bullets: 🟥 THE REMAINDERS ARE IN OPEN FILES, not inside this round's prose — the debt census cannot see an item that lives only in a closed entry or a code comment.

* `debt-one-outline-role-does-two-jobs-and-clears-neither` — `outline` measures 1.82 light and 1.81 dark against a 3.0 boundary floor, and across 144 call sites it serves as BOTH a component boundary (which WCAG holds to 3:1) and a decorative divider (which has no floor). A mature design system splits those into two roles; this crate has one, so no single floor can be right for it. Splitting touches the palette struct, the wire names in `pinion-rpc`, `ColorRole::all()` and three vocabulary gates, which is why R1807 reports it openly instead of quietly passing it or lowering the standard to fit. The debt records that lowering it is the thing NOT to do.

* `debt-eleven-app-verdicts-name-no-assembly` — the other half of the same hole. Eleven `app` rows name no assembly; proving an `app` verdict needs a composite, so it needs demos, which is a campaign rather than a round. The ratchet stops the number growing and can only shrink.

* `debt-analyzer-census-verdicts-are-unproven` — its FIRST branch is closed by this round and recorded as such; its SECOND is untouched: the plane/tier/verdict classification is still one person's unreviewed reading.
The gate's own stated limit is unchanged and worth repeating: it asks whether a cited test RUNS, never whether that test exercises the whole capability. Sufficiency remains unjudged.
⚠ The axis was not re-judged. `phase_b_tally.py` still reports `dcc` STALE — a demand this round did not answer and did not pretend to.

R1808.decision_summary:
R1808 pursues north-star condition (4): an integration test that walks the three canonical screens past their written specifications. The opening re-measurement found the mechanism already complete, already published, and entirely unasked.

WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE. `ScreenRoster::journey_conformance` has since R1767 recorded each departing frame's verdict, folded the live section in, counted an unvisited section as unreproduced, and refused the application while any section is unanswered. The analysis tool publishes it on the wire (`sections_json`). Measured, every `conforms()` assertion in the tree lived in `pinion-screen`'s own test file over SYNTHETIC fixtures named `inspector`, `stream` and `board` — while the three real screens, each with its own judge, its own specification table and its own per-screen tests, had never once been driven through the walk as ONE application. That is R1794's shape one level up: the framework could answer, and no gate put the question.

WHAT A WALK ACTUALLY NEEDS is two lists, and every caller wrote both by hand — the synthetic test included, at `for key in ["dashboard", "inspector", "stream"]`. The two fail differently, and that difference is the argument for making them derived. Forget a DESTINATION and `conforms()` goes false: the section is still in the report, unvisited and unreproduced. Forget a SURFACE TAG and the section is painted, judged, and reported as reproducing nothing — a defect that reads as belonging to the screen rather than to the harness. One is loud; the other is a wrong answer wearing a plausible face.

THE SECTION THAT COULD NOT PASS. With the walk driving one frame per section, four of five reproduced and the node lab did not, for a reason R1767 had already written down: the lab specifies a value row AND that row's open roster, and the roster IS the row's open state, so the two exclude each other and no frame carries both. A one-frame-per-section walk reports that section as never reproducing its specification and is right to — the fault is the walk's, for looking once.
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-screen/src/tour.rs` (new) — the populations a walk needs, taken off the roster:
* `Tour::itinerary()` — every open destination, in roster order. A section added to the rail joins the walk with nobody editing a list.

* `Tour::surfaces()` — every mounted screen's paint-root tag plus a declared host surface. This is the list that fails quietly when it is short, which is why it is computed rather than spelled at a call site.

* `Tour::walk(arrive, paint)` — two closures, because the ORDER between them is the contract: navigate, then latch, then paint. Latching reads the departing frame out of the paint store, and recording a frame also forgets the surfaces that frame did not paint, so a walk that paints before it latches destroys the evidence it is about to ask for.

* `TourReport` — coverage and reproduction as separate questions (`covered`, `missed`, `strayed`, `conforms`), with a `why()` that names the unreconciled SURFACES of a judged section rather than restating the failure.

`WidgetView::poses()` / `pose(nth)` (pinion-shell, defaulted and additive), through `Screen` and `ScreenRoster::{poses_of, pose}` into `Tour`: a screen declares how many frames its specification needs and puts ITSELF into each, so a host never learns which screen needed it. That is the third population `Tour` takes off the roster.

`NodeLabView` declares two poses and reaches them through the same state its pointer path moves — selecting the card, ADDING the `routing.mode` row (it is an `addable` field, not a default), and opening its roster. The poses refuse loudly when they cannot reach the state.
`examples/hello-analyzer-shell/src/tests.rs` — the consumer: the assembled tool walked past its own specification, with the three canonical keys asserted as a set.
`crates/pinion-screen/tests/journey_conformance.rs` — the fixture inspector gains the same two poses, so the mechanism is exercised in the crate that owns it and not only through the application.
verification_bullets: THE GATE WAS WATCHED FAILING, THREE TIMES, EACH FOR A DIFFERENT AND CORRECT REASON, BEFORE IT WAS GREEN. That sequence is the evidence, because a walk first seen already passing is a walk nobody has seen work:
1. Every section reported as never having painted a frame — the walk painted before it latched and destroyed the evidence.
2. Order fixed: four of five sections reproduced, and `lab` reported `controls (1 of 5)`, `enum_roster` shut and `enum_row` absent — the mutually-exclusive surfaces.
3. Poses added: `pose 1 must open the `routing.mode` roster and it did not` — because `P-01` does not arrive carrying that row.

Then green. The `why()` that made steps 2 and 3 legible was itself a repair: its first draft printed the section's standing sentence and fell back to "did not reproduce its specification" for a judged section, so every section reported the same six words and none of them named a surface.
THE ASSERTIONS:

* `r1808_the_application_reproduces_every_section_over_one_walk` — the assembled analysis tool, every open section, one walk. Screen A is `lab` (mounted), screen B `packets` (mounted), screen C `dashboard` (a page the host paints and judges).
* `r1808_the_walk_covers_the_three_canonical_screens` — the three keys asserted against the visited SET, plus `covered()`, `missed()` and `strayed()`.

* `r1808_the_tour_takes_both_populations_from_the_roster` — the itinerary equals the roster's open destinations, every mounted paint root is in the surface list, and `poses_of` answers 2 for the lab and 1 for a section whose surfaces coexist. Guarded against vacuity: the roster must declare at least three open sections.
COUNTERFACTUALS, in the crate that owns the mechanism:
* `r1808_a_section_that_was_walked_but_not_painted_refuses_the_application` — coverage holds, conformance does not, and the refusal names the section.

* `r1808_without_its_second_pose_the_alternating_section_cannot_reproduce` — the same walk with the fixture pinned to one state reproduces the exact failure the poses exist to remove, so the green above is not green for some other reason.
* `r1808_a_rail_with_no_destination_cannot_be_built` — the empty-itinerary arm is defence in depth rather than a reachable state, and is kept as a test of the refusal instead of deleted.

LOCAL GATES: 807 passed, 0 failed across `pinion-screen`, `pinion-shell`, `hello-node-lab` and `hello-analyzer-shell`. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` (CI's exact flags): exit 0, zero warnings. `cargo fmt --all` applied.

CLOSING AUDIT CAUGHT A CLAIM I WROTE THIS ROUND: a comment on `POSE_CARD` saying the opening graph gives it a `routing.mode` row — which the measurement had disproved an hour earlier, in this same round. Repaired before the commit, and the corrected comment carries the measurement.
⚠ NOT VERIFIED: the demo sweep, which CI owns. And `poses()` is a hand-written count: a screen that grows a third mutually-exclusive surface will go stale — loudly, because the walk fails, but stale.
carry_forward_bullets: 🟥 `poses()` SAYS HOW MANY FRAMES, NEVER WHICH TWO SURFACES ARE ALTERNATIVES. `debt-a-specification-cannot-say-two-surfaces-are-alternatives` stays open and now records this round as a partial advance with the line that still holds: a report cannot tell "away because its alternative is showing" from "away because nobody opened it" — both are one `Built::away` sentence. Closing it properly means the specification carrying, per surface, the state it is specified for, and `poses()` being DERIVED from that instead of written. R1808 built the place for that and did not fill it.

⚠ Two debt files describe that same fact under different names — `debt-a-document-cannot-say-two-surfaces-are-alternatives` (R1742) and `debt-a-specification-cannot-say-two-surfaces-are-alternatives` (R1767). Merging them is its own round, and the standing rule is to ask which one is canonical before deleting either.

The node lab now has two accounts of how to reach its two specified states: this round's `pose`, which moves state, and R1732's gate, which presses at painted coordinates. R1809.decision_summary:
R1809 makes the north star's third condition — *the analysis-tool family of open debts is closed* — a command. It was the only one of the four that was not, and two measured facts explain why it could not become one.

NOTHING SAID WHICH DEBTS ARE IN THE FAMILY. Measured over the memory folder: 317 open `debt-*.md`, with the word `analyzer` appearing in 68 of them — far too loose, because the analysis tool is what this whole tree is about and the word turns up in prose with nothing to do with it. There was no field, no list and no derivation, so "analyzer-family" was a judgement somebody made again each time they were asked.

NOTHING SAID WHETHER A DEBT CAN BE WORKED ON NOW. The north star already excludes two census rows by name — one needs a ratified spec decision, one waits on Phase C — but that exclusion lived in the prompt rather than in the debts, so "are the remaining ones all blocked?" had no denominator and no verdict.

AND COUNTING CLOSED DEBTS CANNOT ANSWER IT. This repository's closing discipline requires a debt to move whatever it did not repay into a NEW open file, so the honest rounds are the ones that keep the number up: R1806 closed one and opened one, R1807 closed one branch and opened two. A condition read as "the count reached zero" punishes the discipline that makes the count trustworthy.

WHERE THE POPULATION LIVES. `git ls-files` matches zero paths under `memory/`: the debts are outside this repository and it cannot version them. That is a fact about the condition, not an obstacle to route around, and it decides two things below — the failure mode when the folder is absent, and why a snapshot is committed.
changes_bullets: `tools/analyzer_debts.py` (new):

* **The population is DERIVED** from what each debt wrote: a `[[wiki-link]]` to one of seven declared roots, or an `analyzer-census.json` row id (`lab.t2.16`, `dashboard.t1.3`, ...). Transitive reachability was measured and rejected — the memory graph's hubs run to 169 in-edges, so everything reaches everything.

* **The roots are declared and therefore checked.** A root that stopped existing would silently SHRINK the family (R1798's class), so the tool refuses one that is not a file, and says which debts have quietly left.

* **The standing is declared** by each debt in its own front matter (`blocked_by:`), from a closed vocabulary drawn from what the debts already said: `buildable`, `campaign`, `unmeasured`, `spec-round`, `phase-c`, `gated-axis`. An unknown word is refused, not guessed at.

* **`campaign` and `unmeasured` do NOT block.** A campaign is buildable work that spans rounds; an unmeasured debt's next step is the measurement. That closes the one way a self-declared field could be abused — relabelling the backlog until the condition is met.

* **It fails OPEN and LOUD** where the memory folder is absent, and **snapshots** the survey into `docs/analyzer-debts.json`, which `--check` refuses to let drift. A reader with no memory folder has the snapshot; a machine with one has both, compared.
`docs/analyzer-debts.json` (new) — the committed snapshot.

The 33 family debts each gained a `blocked_by:` declaration. `debt-one-outline-role-does-two-jobs-and-clears-neither` additionally gained the census row it was born from, without which the survey could not see it.
`.githooks/pre-push` — two steps, split the way the census's three are: the selftest, then the survey.

`tools/test_hooks.sh` — three assertions: the survey is a push gate, its selftest runs before the survey trusts itself, and it passes where no memory folder exists. A step that quietly stops happening is the failure mode that file exists for, and this one reads a folder that is usually absent.
verification_bullets: THE CONDITION IS NOW ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS FALSE. `python3 tools/analyzer_debts.py --check` reports **33 in the family, all declared, 29 not blocked**. That is the point of the round: the condition went from a sentence nobody could evaluate to a number with a list behind it.
The breakdown, which is the report rather than a summary: `buildable` 20, `campaign` 6, `unmeasured` 2 — none of which block — and `spec-round` 2, `phase-c` 1, `gated-axis` 1, which do.
COUNTERFACTUALS, against a fixture memory folder built for them:
* An open family debt with no `blocked_by` is refused BY NAME, with the evidence that put it in the family quoted back ("names lab.t2.16").
* A declared root that no longer exists is refused with the consequence spelled out — "every debt that linked it has quietly left the family" — rather than the family silently shrinking.
* `PINION_MEMORY_DIR` pointing nowhere returns 0 and prints why, so a fresh clone and CI do not refuse a push over a population they cannot see.

SELFTEST: PASS, 0 failures, 16 cases. Two of them are the vocabulary's own guard — that a `campaign` and an `unmeasured` debt are NOT counted as blocked — because that is the property standing between a self-declared field and a relabelled backlog.
HOOK GATES: 182 assertions passed, 0 failed (179 before this round's three). `bash -n` clean on `pre-push`. `analyzer_census.py --selftest` PASS, unchanged.
MEASUREMENTS THIS ROUND RESTS ON, each re-derived here: 317 open debt files; 68 matching the bare word; 169 in-edges on the memory graph's largest hub; zero paths under `memory/` in `git ls-files`.

🟥 THE CLOSING AUDIT FOUND A HOLE IN THE DERIVATION I HAD JUST WRITTEN. `debt-one-outline-role-does-two-jobs-and-clears-neither` was opened at R1807 while proving census row `dashboard.t2.9` and names neither a root nor a row, so the survey that exists to see such debts could not see it. Repaired by making the debt name its origin; the implied rule is now written into the tool as the boundary it cannot see past.
⚠ NOT VERIFIED: whether the 33 standings are RIGHT. The tool checks that a word is in the vocabulary and never that it is the correct word — registered, not glossed over.
carry_forward_bullets: 🟥 THE ROUND CREATED A DEFECT AND REGISTERED IT: `debt-a-debts-standing-is-one-persons-unreviewed-reading`. The 33 standings are one reading, done once, by me. The tool enforces the vocabulary and refuses absence; it asks nothing about correctness. That is the SAME CLASS as the second branch of `debt-analyzer-census-verdicts-are-unproven` — "the plane/tier/verdict classification is one person's unreviewed reading" — now reproduced on the debt side by a round that had that sentence in front of it.

⚠ The four entries to audit first are named there, and the reason is arithmetic: `spec-round` (2), `phase-c` (1) and `gated-axis` (1) are the ONLY ones that leave the denominator, so a single wrong one makes the condition false-as-true. Two of the four are not the two the north star named by hand, which is exactly the pair that needs re-measuring.

The cheapest next step is stated in that debt: make each `blocked_by` name the sentence in its own file that it was read from, the way a census `have` names the test that proves it. That lifts the tool from "is there a declaration" to "does the declaration have evidence".
⚠ The derivation is complete only over debts that NAME their origin, and nothing enforces that at the moment a debt is written — only the audit that found the one case.
29 of 33 are not blocked. Condition (3) is a long way from true, and now says so precisely instead of not saying anything.

R1810.decision_summary:
R1810 audits the input R1809 left unaudited. R1809 turned the north star's third condition into a command; the command's answer rests on 33 `blocked_by` declarations, every one of them a single reading made once, with the tool checking that a word was in the vocabulary and never that it was the right word — the same class as the census's own unreviewed plane/tier/verdict classification, reproduced one field over.

WHY FOUR AND NOT THIRTY-THREE. `buildable`, `campaign` and `unmeasured` all stay in the denominator, so mislabelling one changes nothing the condition can notice — it changes the work order, which is a different question with a different cost. `spec-round`, `phase-c` and `gated-axis` are the only words that REMOVE a debt from the count, so one wrong there is the condition reading true while being false. The audit goes where the arithmetic goes.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND. All four standings survived, and three of them turned out to be answerable by a tool rather than by my reading: `lab.t2.16`'s own census row says *"Needs a spec round, not an implementation"*, `dashboard.t2.12`'s says *"waits on the Phase C renderer"*, and `phase_b_tally.py` marks `osnative` gated. The north star names two exclusions by hand; there are four, and both additions are justified — the list was incomplete, not wrong.

THE FOURTH IS DIFFERENT AND IS NOW SAID TO BE. `debt-two-deliberate-divergences-from-the-behaviour-canon` is blocked by a CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO RATIFIED RULES rather than by a statement: reproducing the canon means a toast that vanishes on a 2.6-second timer and a graph auto-restored from local storage at boot, and each makes every gate that reads them a function of wall-clock or machine state, which the zero-flake policy refuses. Which rule wins is the owner's decision, so `spec-round` is correct — and it is the only one of the four that still needs a person.
changes_bullets: `tools/analyzer_debts.py`:

* **`blocked_because`** — a citation, in one of three forms, each answered by something other than the debt that wrote it: `census:<row>` (must be in the pin AND have verdict `gap`, because a row that is not a gap blocks nothing), `axis:<key>` (the Phase B tally must mark that axis gated), `rule:<memory-file>` (the rule must exist). The census's `have`/`proven_by` shape, one field over.

* **Demanded of the BLOCKED standings only**, and the scoping is the argument rather than a convenience — written into the code beside the rule, so the next reader does not have to reconstruct why coverage is 4 of 33.
* **`census_verdicts()` and `gated_axes()`** read the sibling tools rather than restating what they hold, so the three cannot disagree about which rows are gaps or which axes are gated.
* Nine new selftest cases, including that an unblocked standing needs no citation, that a census citation to a non-gap row is refused, and the record-spanning regex trap below.
The four blocked debts each gained their citation: `census:lab.t2.16`, `census:dashboard.t2.12`, `axis:osnative`, `rule:zero-flake-policy`.

`debt-a-debts-standing-is-one-persons-unreviewed-reading` records the partial repayment and, deliberately, the half that is NOT repaid: the 29 unblocked standings are still one reading. They cannot make the condition wrong — only the work order.
`docs/analyzer-debts.json` carries the citations, so a reader with no memory folder sees not only what is blocked but on what evidence.
verification_bullets: THE GATE WAS WATCHED REFUSING ALL FOUR BEFORE ANY OF THEM CITED. With `check_citations` in and no `blocked_because` written yet, the survey exited 1 naming exactly `debt-a-node-graphs-only-state-is-a-delay`, `debt-a-three-dimensional-surface-waits-on-phase-c`, `debt-two-deliberate-divergences-from-the-behaviour-canon` and `debt-windows-platform-surface-absent` — the four that leave the count, and nothing else. Then all four resolving, and the survey passing.

🟥 THE ROUND'S OWN INSTRUMENT CAUGHT ME BEFORE IT CAUGHT ANYTHING ELSE. `gated_axes` was written as a single `"key": "X" .*? "gated": True` pattern, and `.*?` under DOTALL walks past an ungated axis to the NEXT axis's flag, consuming the axis that flag belonged to. It surfaced as the citation check refusing `axis:osnative` — the gate refusing my own evidence. Re-run against this tally, the bad pattern answers `{api, dcc}` where the truth is `{api, osnative}`: one false positive, one false negative, the third right by luck. The fix reads one record at a time, and the trap is pinned as a selftest case so the shape cannot come back.

SELFTEST: PASS, 0 failures. The nine added cases include the three that make the rule non-vacuous: an UNBLOCKED standing needs no citation (or the scoping argument would be undermined by the code), a census citation to a row whose verdict is not `gap` is refused (a row that is not a gap blocks nothing), and an axis citation resolves only for an axis the tally actually gates.

SNAPSHOT DRIFT REFUSED TWICE, both times correctly: once when the citations changed the snapshot's shape, and once when a debt this round edited gained a census row id in its own prose and so entered the survey's `why` — the second is the drift check catching a change I did not think of.
`bash tools/test_hooks.sh`: 182 passed, 0 failed. `reference_names.py --check`: 0 in 0 files, ratchet OK.
FINAL: `analyzer_debts.py --check` reports 33 in the family, all declared, 29 not blocked. Condition (3) is unchanged and false — this round audited the answer's inputs, not the answer.

🟥 THE CLOSING AUDIT CAUGHT A WORD I WROTE THIS ROUND. The comment recording the regex defect called it "an exact inversion"; re-running the bad pattern shows it was not — one of the three was right. The comment now carries what the pattern actually answered, and the audit's method is the point: it re-ran the thing rather than trusting my sentence about it.
⚠ NOT VERIFIED: the 29 unblocked standings. That is deliberate and argued, not an omission.
carry_forward_bullets: 29 of 33 are still not blocked. Condition (3) is exactly where R1809 left it — this round made the four exclusions answerable, not the condition true.

🟥 THE HALF NOT REPAID, recorded in `debt-a-debts-standing-is-one-persons-unreviewed-reading` rather than glossed: the 29 unblocked standings are still one reading, made once. They cannot make the condition wrong, because none of them leaves the denominator — but they decide the ORDER the remaining work is taken in, and a wrong `campaign` on something that is a single round's work would misdirect several rounds before anybody noticed.

⚠ `blocked_because` covers 4 of 33 by design. The argument for that scoping is written into the tool beside the rule, so a later reader does not mistake the coverage for an oversight and "fix" it by demanding citations from everything — which would bury the four that matter in twenty-nine that do not.

⚠ The fourth citation is the weak one and says so: `rule:zero-flake-policy` names a CONFLICT rather than a statement, and the tool can only check that the rule file exists — never that the conflict is real or that it is unresolved. That one still needs a person, and it is the only one of the four that does.

R51.188.decision_summary: §5.45 R55.E.1 Vello paint adapter clips Scene::Scroll viewport + shifts content by offset
changes_bullets: paint_adapter::to_vello forwards to new to_vello_inner(..., transform: Affine) carrying the cumulative parent transform through the recursion
fill_rect / stroke_rect / paint_text gain transform: Affine parameter; previously each used Affine::IDENTITY (bit-identical for non-scroll callers since IDENTITY * T = T)
Scene::Scroll arm: push_clip_layer(transform, viewport_kurbo) then recurse with child_transform = transform * Affine::translate((viewport.xy - offset.xy)); pop_layer on exit
paint_text composes parent_transform * Affine::translate((t.rect.x, t.rect.y)) for glyph + decoration paints; clip-rect passes parent_transform so scroll-embedded text clips in its parent frame
Public to_vello signature unchanged — all 6 existing call sites (app.rs render + 5 paint_adapter tests) keep working without edits
TUI-side scroll clipping deferred to R51.189 R55.E.2 (carry); cell-grid clipping requires different shape from Vello clip-layer push/pop

R630.decision_summary: feat(core): R630 §5.50 from_css_string modern rgb + hsl coverage
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: extend `Color::from_rgb_function` with W3C CSS Color 4 §8.1 modern space syntax (`rgb(R G B)` / `rgb(R G B / A)`) alongside the existing legacy comma form; the entry point now dispatches on comma presence (`body.contains(',')`) to one of two sibling helpers (`parse_rgb_legacy_body` / `parse_rgb_modern_body`), each calling a shared `parse_rgb_channel_triplet` so the percent/integer homogeneity rule stays in one place

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: `rgba()` and `rgb()` are now true synonyms per CSS Color 4 §8.1 — both accept 3-channel (no alpha) and 4-channel (alpha) legacy forms; pre-R630 the prefix constrained arity, but the spec says they are interchangeable; updated the R624 arity test accordingly and added R630 tests pinning each synonym path

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: add `Color::from_hsl_function(&str) -> Option<Self>` sibling to `from_rgb_function`; supports modern space form (`hsl(H S% L%)` / `hsl(H S% L% / A)`) and legacy comma form (`hsl(H, S%, L%)` / `hsla(H, S%, L%, A)`) with the same dispatch-on-comma pattern; alpha is positional in legacy and `/`-introduced in modern

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: add helper free functions `parse_modern_alpha` (number-or-percent), `parse_hue` (degrees with optional `deg`/`rad`/`turn`/`grad` unit, wraps via `rem_euclid` per CSS Values 4), `parse_unit_percentage` (mandatory `%` suffix per CSS Color 4), `hsl_to_srgb_bytes` (W3C §6.2 canonical conversion with achromatic + lightness-extreme short-circuits), and `hue_to_rgb` (W3C piecewise hue-segment helper); CSS-spec canonical short names `h`/`s`/`l`/`r`/`g`/`b`/`p`/`q`/`t` mirror the algorithm letter-for-letter and ride single fn-level `clippy::many_single_char_names` allow attributes with `reason = "CSS Color 4 §6.2 canonical ..."`

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: `parse_hue` strip-suffix order — `grad` / `turn` BEFORE `rad` / `deg` because `grad` ends with `rad`; a naive longest-first miss would false-positive (`"100grad".strip_suffix("rad") = Some("100g")` → parse fails); documented in source comment

crates/pinion-core/src/style.rs: `Color::from_css_string` dispatcher gains a third arm for `hsl(`/`hsla(`; the doc-comment is updated with the R630 support matrix (modern rgb space + slash alpha + hsl); deferred forms reduce to `oklch()` / `lab()` / `color()` (Level 4 wide-gamut) and named colors

crates/pinion-rpc/src/dispatch_tests.rs: add 2 cross-converter consistency tests — `r631_runtime_owner_unavailable_identifier_is_uniform_across_converters` walks every `RuntimeOwnerUnavailable`-emitting converter and asserts the same `Value::String("RuntimeOwnerUnavailable")` data tag; `r631_not_bound_identifier_is_uniform_across_converters` mirrors for the tag-keyed `NotBound` axis; pre-R631 each handler had its own per-axis wire test (R599 / R600 / R602 / R603 / ...) but no test pinned the *cross-converter* equality, so a rename of one identifier (e.g. `RuntimeOwnerUnavailable` → `RuntimeContextMissing`) would silently break wire consistency for AI agents that pattern-match on the typed name

crates/pinion-rpc/src/dispatch_tests.rs: the test module docstring records the load-bearing property that `RpcError::invalid_params(detail).with_data_string(tag)` overwrites the prose at the `data` slot — only the typed `data_tag` is wire-visible; the R631 tests assert the overwrite IS applied so a future refactor that drops `with_data_string` cannot silently surface the prose as the wire identifier
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace → 3156 / 0 (3145 → 3156, +11 R631 tests; +9 per-converter unit + 2 cross-converter consistency)

R634.decision_summary: feat(cli): R634 §5.7 pinion figma-verify sub-command + Figma REST fetch
changes_bullets: Cargo.toml: add `clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }` and `ureq = { version = "2", features = ["json", "tls"], default-features = false }` to `[workspace.dependencies]`; ureq runs sync at the CLI boundary (no tokio runtime) and uses rustls for portable TLS without a native OpenSSL link
crates/pinion-cli/Cargo.toml: add the new deps + a `[[bin]] name = "pinion"` block so the binary is invoked as `cargo run -p pinion-cli -- ...` (or `pinion ...` once installed)

crates/pinion-cli/src/main.rs: replace the pre-R634 `fn main() {}` stub with a `clap` derive root (`Cli` + `Command` enum) routing to the first sub-command `figma-verify`; future sub-commands land alongside the round that needs them per the [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]] discipline

crates/pinion-cli/src/figma_verify.rs: new module — `FigmaVerifyArgs` (file_key positional + `--output` + `--ids` flags) and `run(&FigmaVerifyArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>` that reads `FIGMA_TOKEN` env var, calls the Figma REST `GET /v1/files/:key` endpoint with optional `?ids=` filter, deserializes to `serde_json::Value`, pretty-prints, and writes to stdout or the `--output` path

Figma authentication contract: token is sourced exclusively from `FIGMA_TOKEN` env var — the CLI never reads from a config file or accepts the token as a flag, so accidental shell-history / git-blame leakage is impossible by construction; the recommended scope is `File content` read-only (figma.com → Settings → Personal access tokens)

Wire shape: `FILE_KEY` is the URL path segment between `/design/` (or `/file/`) and the file name in a Figma URL; the response is the full DocumentNode tree (FRAME / GROUP / RECTANGLE / TEXT / VECTOR / etc. all typed) which R635 will map to `Scene` / `LayoutStyle` / `BoxStyle`
verification_bullets: cargo build -p pinion-cli → clean (ureq 2.12.1 + clap 4.6.1 + transitive rustls / webpki / idna / url — first-time compile only)
cargo test --workspace → 3156 / 0 (unchanged from R633 baseline; the CLI is execution-only, no library code so no unit tests yet — R635 will add JSON → Scene mapping with substrate tests)

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello → clean (initial run surfaced 5 clippy::pedantic lints — doc_markdown / needless_pass_by_value / unnecessary_debug_formatting — all addressed inline)

Smoke: `cargo run -p pinion-cli --quiet -- figma-verify --help` emits the documented usage; `cargo run -p pinion-cli --quiet -- figma-verify FAKEKEY` without `FIGMA_TOKEN` set returns the documented missing-token error message with non-zero exit code
mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace baseline holds; the change does not touch atomic store outside this changelog entry
carry_forward_bullets: R635 §5.7 §5.2 — JSON → Scene mapping pass: `FRAME` → `ContainerNode` + `LayoutStyle` (Figma `layoutMode` AUTO_LAYOUT → `FlexDirection`, `itemSpacing` → gap, `padding{Left,Right,Top,Bottom}` → `LayoutStyle.padding`); `RECTANGLE` → `BoxNode` + `BoxStyle` (`fills[0].color` → `Color`, `cornerRadius` → `BoxStyle.radius` — uniform only until R636+ adds per-corner); `TEXT` → `TextNode` + `TextStyle` (`characters` + `style.fontSize` + `style.fills`); each unsupported Figma feature surfaces a `substrate-gap` log line that feeds the R636+ axis queue

R636+ §5.7 §5.50 — `pinion figma-verify --pixel-diff` mode: take a `scene/screenshot` of the mapped Scene + a Figma `GET /v1/images/:key?nodes=...&format=png` export + compute a per-pixel diff (image dimensions match by design — the Scene is positioned and sized from the same Figma node tree). The diff PNG plus an aggregate similarity score lands in `--output-dir` so the design-parity gap is documentable in PR descriptions

R636.decision_summary: feat(cli): R636 §5.7 pinion figma-fetch-image sub-command + Figma reference PNG verified
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-cli/src/figma_image.rs: new module — `FigmaImageArgs` (file_key + node_id positional + `--output` required + `--scale` (default 1.0) + `--format` (default png)) and `run(&FigmaImageArgs)` that implements the documented two-leg Figma image fetch: (1) `GET /v1/images/:key?ids=:node&format=:format&scale=:scale` returns a per-node S3 URL map, (2) `GET <s3_url>` returns the actual binary PNG bytes; pre-signed URL needs no auth header

crates/pinion-cli/src/main.rs: register the new `figma-fetch-image` sub-command under the `Command` enum + dispatch in `main` next to the R634 `figma-verify` arm; `mod figma_image;` declared above the existing `mod figma_verify;`

Figma response error surfacing — the image-list endpoint reports per-call failures in a top-level `err` JSON field; the CLI propagates the message verbatim so a node-id typo or invisible-node error reaches the user with the exact Figma wording (vs being swallowed under a generic HTTP 200)

First real-world fetch — `cargo run -p pinion-cli --release -- figma-fetch-image qluPDRsuDuPM3deySb0ejR '51553:5180' --output /tmp/figma-btn-ref.png --scale 2` produced a 2946-byte 218×80 RGBA PNG (109×40 native size at scale=2); the image confirms the Material 3 Filled Button visual: fully-rounded purple pill, white `Button` label centered, white leading `+` Material Symbols icon — the trailing-icon slot exists but is empty in this particular variant rendering

Reference image inspection identified the first substrate-gap evidence: the Figma rendering includes a Material Symbols `+` glyph in the leading-icon slot that the R635 hand-write elided to a placeholder (Figma `INSTANCE` node referencing an external glyph component). The pinion-side rendering will visibly differ at the leading-icon position once R635 paint output is captured — first concrete design-parity gap landed in the audit queue

Visual inspection via Read tool surfaces the Material 3 Filled Button: rounded pill, M3 Primary color matching the #675AA4 spec, `Button` label, leading `+` glyph; consistent with the R634-extracted spec at node `51553:5180`

R637+ §5.7 substrate gap (FIRST EVIDENCE landed): Material Symbols icon glyph system. Figma renders the leading `+` from an external Material Symbols font; pinion has no icon-font substrate so the leading-icon slot is currently empty in the R635 binding. Three textbook-canonical options: (a) bundle a Material Symbols subset as a SVG path table, (b) treat Material Symbols as a regular `pinion-text` font and let parley shape the glyph by codepoint, (c) new `pinion-icons` crate with a typed `Icon` enum mapping name → SVG path data. (b) is the smallest delta to existing substrate; defer the architectural pick to R638 once a second Figma binding with icons evidences the same need (Cards / Chips / FABs all use Material Symbols)

R637+ §5.50 substrate gap: pixel-diff library choice — `image` + `imageproc` crates are the canonical Rust pair (image decodes PNG, imageproc has SSIM / per-channel diff). Alternative is to vendor a minimal `pixelmatch`-style algorithm so pinion-cli stays light. Decide once R637 lands the screenshot side

pinion-rpc/src/lib.rs: pub mod simulate + pub use simulate::{simulate, SimulateError, SimulateStep}.
pinion-rpc/src/dispatch_tests.rs: 3 dispatch integration tests (2-step compound snapshot + rollback, empty steps invalid, missing steps param invalid).

Always attempts Owner restore regardless of simulate outcome; Owner restore failure surfaces as SimulateError::RollbackFailed (matches dry_run severity for indeterminate reactive state).

pinion-rpc/src/dispatch.rs: handle_scene_simulate takes runtime_owner: Option<&Owner> param. When Some, routes through simulate_with_owner; when None, falls back to External-only simulate (R646). Bindings that wire DispatchContext::runtime_owner get reactive-layer rollback for free.

Three test cases pinning Owner bridge contract: empty_owner_matches_simulate_output (no-op for unregistered Signals), signal_external_value_restored_via_external_rollback (single tracked Signal mirrors External path), non_idempotent_effect_chain_signal_restored_by_owner_bridge (load-bearing case proving R26 value: independent counter Signal mutated by Effect chain restored to pre-call value).

Test discovery: Effect re-firing during Owner.restore happens when its closure body's .get() subscribes to Signals being restored. Pinned via set_with vs set(get()+1) idiom — set_with reads via inner.value.borrow() without with_current_owner tracking. Documented inline in the test as guidance for future bridge consumers.

R649.decision_summary: R649 §5.23 R27 — Effect side-effect suppression during dry_run/simulate via SimulationGuard thread-local; non-idempotent Effect chains stay idempotent across hypothetical-mutation cycles
changes_bullets: pinion-core/src/reactive/simulation.rs (new): IS_SIMULATING thread-local Cell<bool> + SimulationGuard RAII (Drop restores prior; nesting-safe). is_simulating() query. 3 unit tests pin baseline + flip-on-enter + nested-guard semantics.

pinion-core/src/reactive/effect.rs: Effect::mark_dirty checks is_simulating() between in_run/cancelled checks and weak-self upgrade. Suppresses Effect closure body during simulate scopes; subscription set unaffected (frozen at last rerun), so next post-simulation Signal::set fires the Effect normally.
pinion-core/src/reactive/mod.rs + lib.rs: re-export SimulationGuard + is_simulating at the public surface so pinion-rpc (and future binding-internal dry_run consumers) can compose.
pinion-rpc/src/dry_run.rs: wrap dry_run() body in SimulationGuard::enter(). Single-write External rollback now reactive-safe — no Effect side-effect lands twice.

pinion-rpc/src/simulate.rs: simulate() + simulate_with_owner() both enter SimulationGuard. Nested guard is fine (simulate_with_owner enters first, simulate's inner enter sees prior=true). Owner.restore inside the same scope so Signal value writes during restore don't fire Effects either.

pinion-rpc/src/simulate.rs: new r649_effect_suppressed_during_simulate test — naive `Effect: counter.set(counter.get()+1)` pattern (the R647-era set_with workaround target) is now correct under R649: simulate_with_owner leaves counter at pre-call value, proving R26+R27 compose to give full idempotency.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: 3206 pass / 0 fail (R648 baseline 3202 + 3 simulation primitive tests + 1 effect-suppression dispatch test). All 20 simulate tests + dry_run tests + reactive primitive tests pass with the new guard wired.

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello: 0 errors / 0 warnings. Pre-commit fixed 3 doc_markdown (SCE / dry_run / R641-R648 backticks) + 1 redundant_closure (IS_SIMULATING.with(Cell::get) over closure form).
mnemosyne validate_workspace: T1 orphan 0/0, round-trip 1/1, ledger sync.

R27 §5.23 commitment FULFILLED. dry_run + simulate + simulate_with_owner all suppress Effect side-effects during their hypothetical-mutation scopes. The R26 (Signal value rollback) + R27 (Effect suppression) pair is now spec-complete; non-idempotent Effects (counters, telemetry, network sends) no longer drift across simulate cycles.
Honest LOC: pinion-core +110 (simulation.rs new + Effect.mark_dirty hook + re-exports) + pinion-rpc +12 (3 SimulationGuard::enter() lines + test) = +122 LOC pure capability. No binding code touched.
carry_forward_bullets: R650 candidate: isolated Computed cache (§5.30 R30). Computed values cached during simulate may pollute live cache. Less critical than R27 (cache eviction is benign mostly) but spec commitment open.

§5.8 SCE engine-level dry_run hook still long-term roadmap. v0 External test-and-rollback + R26 + R27 (R647+R649) sufficient for spec compliance; engine hook would replace the per-step intervene approach with state-machine-internal pause/resume.

R647 test workaround (set_with vs set(get()+1)) is no longer load-bearing for simulate_with_owner — both Effect patterns work identically under R649. The R647 test kept the set_with form as defensive guidance; R649 test demonstrates the naive set(get()+1) form succeeds. Either is acceptable in future binding code.

Test fixture pattern carry: long-running Effect that drifts in production may want a manual exit-from-simulation marker (e.g., owner.in_simulate_assert!() inside the Effect closure) so unintended Effect re-fires after the guard are auditable. Not urgent — surface only if a binding hits this debug case.

examples/todomvc/src/main.rs — Signal element type swap: Vec<String> → Vec<TodoItem { id: u64, text: String }>; derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize) on TodoItem (Signal<T> bound); new use_next_todo_id hook (Owner::cache-keyed Rc<Cell<u64>> monotonic counter starting at 1) + allocate_todo_id helper (get + saturating_add(1)); apply_key Enter handler allocates fresh id before push so the resulting tag is stable u64-keyed, not array-indexed.

examples/todomvc/src/main.rs — new TodoDeleteExternal singleton (pub struct + impl External + ExternalIntrospect) registered via WidgetCore::create_extra_externals under DELETE_TAG ("todo_delete"); reuses R51.42 §5.35 composite-tag wire (paint tag "todo_delete#<id>" → InputRouter split → primary External lookup → invoke("send", "<id>:PointerDown")); schema slots {count: int, ids: json, send: string, delete: int}; PointerDown commits delete via Signal::set_with retain, PointerUp/Enter/Leave/Cancel accepted as Bool(false) no-op; direct invoke("delete", Int(id)) path for unit tests + future direct-RPC carry.

examples/todomvc/src/main.rs — build_todos_list rewritten: per-row Container tagged "todo_item#{id}" (stable u64 id, NOT array index) hosts [entry_text, delete_button]; delete_button = 24×24 Container tagged "todo_delete#{id}" with aria_label "Delete" + centred × glyph (DELETE_GLYPH = "\u{00D7}" per [[non-ascii-literal-named-const-escape]], 18px, ColorRole::Error fg); SpaceBetween justify on the row + Center align so the X right-aligns; not in focusable_tags so a click does not steal focus from the textfield.

examples/todomvc/src/main.rs — WidgetA11y::access_node extended to emit per-item ARIA tree: TextInput (textfield) + ListItem per todo (with AccessValue::Text(item.text)) + Button per delete (named "Delete" via paint-side aria_label) + List root with .with_child("todo_item#<id>") references so AT cursor traversal order matches paint order; flat AccessNode vec, builder resolves children to NodeIds.

tools/demos/todomvc_r656.py — RPC self-verification demo with 32 assertions (≥20 target). Drives: focus → type+Enter×3 (alpha/beta/gamma) → snapshot → extract per-item (id, text) tuples from "todo_item#<id>" tags → assert monotonic + unique → scene/click {path: "todo_delete#<id_beta>"} to delete middle via composite-tag wire → assert surviving items keep ORIGINAL ids [id_alpha, id_gamma] (R656 stable-id invariant) → click delete on alpha → gamma alone with original id → click on stale id_beta raises RpcError → add delta+epsilon → assert their ids > id_gamma, never reuse retired id_alpha / id_beta. PASS in 2.67s on the release binary.

changes_bullets: NEW crate `crates/pinion-widget-paint/` (Cargo.toml + src/lib.rs + src/text_field.rs + 7 substrate tests) — sits between pinion-text (LayoutCache + caret_rect substrate) and per-backend shells (pinion-shell GUI / pinion-tui TUI); depends on pinion-core + pinion-text + pinion-a11y only (NOT shell/tui/runtime/rpc — preserves §2 invariant #6 GUI/TUI dual consumption); workspace `Cargo.toml` member added at line 18.

pinion-widget-paint surface (~735 LOC + 7 unit tests): `TextFieldStyle` struct + `m3_filled()` const constructor (9 fields: field_w 360 / field_h 40 / field_pad 8 / field_corner 4 / font_size_px 18 / caret_width 2 / selection_alpha 0xA0 / preedit_bg_alpha 0x40 / preedit_underline_thickness 1) + `Default` impl; `view_field(tag, interaction, caret_byte, theme, style, aria_label) -> Scene` — full ~280 LOC TextField paint composition (caret/selection/preedit overlays + field fill + aria-label) lifted verbatim; `ime_caret_rect_for(tag, interaction, caret_byte, field_rect, theme, style) -> CaretRect` — IME platform bridge caret rect derivation (caller supplies field_rect via pinion_runtime::rect_for_tag so pinion-widget-paint stays free of pinion-runtime dep); `use_text_field_layout_cache()` Owner-cache hook; `parse_text_field_state` / `text_field_state_name` SCXML name lookup; `read_text_field_state(scene, tag)` introspect read helper.

examples/todomvc refactor: Cargo.toml adds pinion-widget-paint dep; main.rs 2672 → 2243 LOC (-429 net) — same delete set as hello-textfield + status_str now calls `tf_paint::text_field_state_name`; binding keeps R655/R656-specific TodoItem + use_next_todo_id + allocate_todo_id + TodoDeleteExternal + build_todos_list + DELETE_GLYPH paint section unchanged; view fn root composition (title + field + status + todos_list) retained.

Carry — LayoutCache key collision avoidance for multi-TextField bindings: today's lifted helper uses one framework-wide cache key. Acceptable for current use; a per-tag namespacing axis lands if a multi-TextField composed app surfaces a cache-collision bug.

crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/scrollbar.rs: ScrollBarInteractionSignal (Signal<u8> wrapper around ScrollBarState; numeric tag bypasses Forge-generated enum's missing Serialize/DeserializeOwned bound) + use_scrollbar_interaction(tag) Owner::cache hook ([[owner-cache-typed-key]] pattern, mirrors use_text_edit_state). ScrollBar.interaction field + ScrollBar::attach_interaction builder; ScrollBarExternal::attach_interaction delegates via std::mem::take. ScrollBar::send mirrors post-transition state into the signal so view-fn paints repaint on every SCXML state-machine edge.

examples/hello-listbox/src/main.rs + examples/todomvc/src/main.rs: both consumers thread the new use_scrollbar_interaction hook through view_vertical_scrollbar (`.get()` auto-subscribe) and create_extra_externals (`.attach_interaction(...)` builder) so hover/drag on the scrollbar thumb repaints in lock-step across the substrate.

R663.decision_summary: R663 §5.49 — scene/double_click primitive substrate (DeferredInput::DoubleClick + shell drain + RPC handler + Python harness + end-to-end smoke).
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-rpc/src/dispatch.rs: DeferredInput::DoubleClick { x, y } variant added; scene/double_click RPC method (handle_scene_double_click) mirrors scene/click selector taxonomy (at xor path). Shared resolve_at_or_path helper unchanged — substrate cleanly composes the second-cycle on top of the existing single-click resolver.

crates/pinion-shell/src/substrate.rs: deferred-input drain arm expands DoubleClick into cursor_moved(MOUSE, x, y) + 2x (mouse_pressed + mouse_released). W3C UIEvent detail:2 convention via two complete press/release cycles at the same coordinate; the receiving InputRouter arc fires identically to a real-mouse double-click (winit MouseInput::Pressed twice within the system double-click window).
tools/rpc_verify.py: tf.double_click(at | path) Python wrapper. Mirror of tf.click() selector taxonomy with the same `exactly one of at / path` invariant.

tools/demos/double_click_r663.py: substrate smoke demo — drives todomvc's existing TodoToggleExternal as the substrate proof. Single-click flips completed 0→1 (sanity); double-click flips 0→1→0 (substrate proof). Both selector forms (at-coord + path) verified. Mutual-exclusion ValueError pinned.

Framework-first ([[r47-class-incident-prevention]]): double-click is industry-precedent input primitive (W3C UIEvent.detail:2, winit MouseInput chain, every desktop toolkit since Smalltalk-80). Lifting it as a substrate before R664 application consumer (todomvc edit-in-place) lands keeps the application-tier strictly substrate-consuming.

At-coord + path selector forms both verified; mutual-exclusion validation raised as expected.
carry_forward_bullets: R664 todomvc edit-in-place — R663 substrate consumer. Per-item double-click on todo_item#<id> text → enter edit mode (use_editing_id Owner::cache + per-item TextEditState via use_text_edit_state(format!("todo_edit#{id}"))); Enter commits new text; Escape cancels. view_field 3rd consumer ROI confirmation (R657 lift validates).

winit-side double-click detection (300ms / 5px threshold) — currently the substrate fires DoubleClick only when the AI client explicitly requests scene/double_click. Native paint-side double-click detection (consecutive MouseInput::Pressed events within the OS double-click window) is a follow-up GUI-backend axis (R670+). The RPC primary path (§2 #2) lands today; native paint parity carries until a paint-side widget cares.

DoubleClick is symmetric with the existing Click selector taxonomy; future Triple+Click etc. would extend DeferredInput rather than mutate this variant (TasteJS convention covers up to detail:2 for double-activate; triple-click for paragraph-select belongs to future text-edit axis).

R664.decision_summary: R664 §5.16 §5.38 §5.39 §5.49 — todomvc edit-in-place + R663 paint-side double-click substrate consumer + focus_request mailbox + AT-action coverage
changes_bullets: pinion-runtime::input::InputRouter — W3C native paint-side double-click detection (300ms / 5px threshold per axis, same target gate). Second consecutive pointer_down on the same hover_target within the window dispatches a synthetic `DoubleClick` named event in addition to `PointerDown`. Unifies the R663 RPC DeferredInput::DoubleClick drain (zero-delta drain trivially fires detection) with native winit MouseInput presses at the framework tier per [[r47-class-incident-prevention]]. 4 unit tests pin the threshold matrix (back-to-back / spatial / cross-target / triple-press reset).

pinion-core::focus_request — programmatic focus-change mailbox (`request(tag)` / `drain()`, thread_local Cell<Option<String>> last-write-wins). New module so widget bodies (External::invoke, reducers, Effect callbacks) can request focus without reaching across the pinion-runtime FocusManager boundary. Mirrors React useImperativeHandle / Solid createRef / Flutter FocusNode.requestFocus shape. 5 unit tests cover the request/drain/clear/overwrite/owned-payload contract.

pinion-shell::ShellCore::handle_tail — drain_focus_request post-dispatch hook applies pending focus requests through FocusManager::focus_set + notify_focus_change so External::on_focus_change observers fire identically to a mouse-driven focus transition. Substrate-side, no application surface change.

examples/todomvc — edit-in-place axis lands end-to-end: use_editing_id reactive Signal<Option<u64>>, TodoEditExternal (5th ExtraExternal under ITEM_TAG) handling `<id>:DoubleClick` via composite-tag wire, TextFieldExternal at EDIT_TF_TAG (6th ExtraExternal) wired through use_text_edit_state/use_caret_blink/use_clipboard, build_todos_list conditional row swap to tf_paint::view_field (3rd consumer of the R657-lifted substrate — view_field ROI confirmed), apply_key_edit handler (Enter commit / Escape cancel / delegate other), commit_edit erase-to-delete (TasteJS canonical), strikethrough TextDecoration on completed item text (2nd consumer of pinion-core TextDecoration substrate). State tuple expanded to (TextFieldState, u32, FilterRadioStates, TextFieldState, u32) to carry editor SCXML state + caret. Multi-text-input apply_composition / apply_middle_click extended for EDIT_TF_TAG target.

examples/todomvc::WidgetA11y::access_child_invoke — extended for 4 composites via per_item_int_action helper (delete / toggle / item-edit) + filter_at_action split. R662 parent_tag substrate reaches 4-of-4 application consumer push (filter / delete / toggle / item). AT-side Click on todo_item enters edit mode (the AT equivalent of double-click).

tools/demos/todomvc_r664.py — 34-assertion AI-first introspection demo: boot steady state → add 3 rows → double-click activates edit → seed text + auto-focus → Backspace + retype + Enter commit → row text updated → Escape cancel → erase-to-delete → strikethrough decoration on completed row → re-entry editor cleanup → selector validation. Drives entirely through scene/double_click + scene/key + scene/snapshot (primary-External-only RPC v0 limit honored via state-snapshot introspect-field walk).

examples/todomvc test battery — 17 new R664 regressions (use_editing_id default / begin_edit activate + stale / view paint swap on/off / commit preserves completed / commit erase-deletes / cancel preserves / focus_request both directions / send DoubleClick wire / send Pointer no-op / focusable_tags / strikethrough decoration / AT Click on item-delete-toggle). Pre-existing tests migrated to 5-tuple State + `r664_create_extra_externals_registers_six_siblings` consolidated count assertion per [[test-name-numeric-count-renaming]].

§1 Vision section — Phase A/B/C/D progression update (Foundation → Professional GUI → Game-engine dual-execution per §2 #4 → AAA editor self-hosted), R663.5 caveats annotating the §2 #4 mode toggle as game-engine entry point rather than GUI diff optimization.
verification_bullets: Workspace: cargo test --workspace = 3328 passed / 0 failed (R663 baseline 3303 + 25 new — 4 InputRouter double-click + 5 focus_request + 17 todomvc R664 - 1 retired duplicate count test).
Workspace: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = clean (pedantic deny baseline preserved).

Visible: cargo run --release -p todomvc — double-click on row text reveals inline editor with seeded text + caret at end, Enter commits + restores main field focus, Escape cancels untouched, completed row text rendered with strikethrough decoration.
AI-first verify: python3 tools/demos/todomvc_r664.py = PASS in 5.72s (34 assertions covering edit entry + commit + cancel + erase-delete + strikethrough + re-entry cleanup).

InputRouter unit tests cover W3C threshold matrix: back-to-back zero-delay → DoubleClick fires; 10px-apart presses → no DoubleClick; cross-target presses → no DoubleClick; triple press → exactly 2 DoubleClick across 4 presses (binary single/double per [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]] until a triple consumer surfaces).

focus_request mailbox unit tests pin the request → drain → clear → overwrite contract; owned-String payload accepted for future dynamic-key consumer; thread_local Cell::take pattern preserves zero-cost steady state.
carry_forward_bullets: scene/query + scene/invoke v0 are primary-External-only (R690+ multi-External addressing carry) — the R664 demo works around via state-scene snapshot introspect-field walk; the R690 lift unifies query/invoke selector with the introspect surface.

scene/double_click at-coord form against Scene::Scroll content uses content-local rect (R51.200 absolute_rect_of carry) — R664 demo skips at-form on rows inside the scroll viewport, uses path-form which the substrate routes correctly.

EDIT_TF_TAG is unconditionally in focusable_tags so the programmatic focus_request succeeds; Tab order visits a ghost stop when no row is editing. Dynamic focusable_tags (per-paint refresh) is a substrate axis deferred until a 2nd consumer of conditional focus-stops surfaces per [[abstraction-needs-second-consumer]].

Per-item TextEditState multi-instance (dynamic Owner::cache key) deferred — single-slot reuse satisfies TasteJS canonical (one row editable at a time). Lift when a 2nd consumer of multi-row simultaneous edit surfaces.
SCE-004 (vendor/sce Forge codegen serde derive) honest carry — external dependency, R664 cannot land directly.

R665.decision_summary: R665 §3 §5.15 — Storage substrate + pinion-platform-storage FileStorage + todomvc External(opaque) persistence cycle (Phase A advance 70%→~80%)
changes_bullets: pinion-core::storage — new module. `Storage` trait (load/save/remove, total surface, bytes-only) + `InMemoryStorage` default impl (`RefCell<BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>>`). Mirror of `Clipboard` / `InMemoryClipboard` (R56.1.e §5.22) substrate-shape: trait + headless default in pinion-core, platform impl in a sibling crate. Re-exported through pinion_core::lib root (`Storage`, `InMemoryStorage`). 9 unit tests cover fresh-default / round-trip / overwrite / empty-bytes / remove / multi-key isolation / dyn polymorphism / binary payloads.

pinion-platform-storage — new workspace crate (16th). `FileStorage::try_new(root)` opens a per-app directory (idempotent `create_dir_all`); `Storage` impl writes via tempfile + flush + sync_all + atomic rename so POSIX `rename(2)` / Windows `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` covers the whole transaction (no torn half-writes). Strict key sanitization (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` 1..=200) so the on-disk filename is a verbatim copy of the key — portable across OSes without escape encoding. `open_app_storage(name)` convenience wrapper composes `dirs::data_dir()` + `try_new` (Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME/<name>/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/<name>/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\<name>\`). 15 unit tests cover round-trip / reopen persistence / atomic-write-no-leftover-tmp / list_keys exclude tempfiles / invalid-key rejection (traversal + separators + null + non-ASCII + whitespace + empty + oversize) / key validator + path helpers / dyn polymorphism / default_app_dir / open_app_storage end-to-end.

examples/todomvc — first consumer of the §3 External(opaque) escape hatch as persistence. `PersistedState { schema_version: u32, todos: Vec<TodoItem>, filter: FilterMode, next_id: u64 }` single-blob shape (atomic-write covers the whole transaction). `use_storage()` Owner::cache hook with `AppStorage(Box<dyn Storage>)` sized newtype (mirror of `AppClipboard`). `use_persistence_boot()` runs ONCE per Owner: (1) pre-resolves all dependent `Owner::cache` slots BEFORE entering the boot slot factory to avoid nested `RefCell::borrow_mut` panic; (2) loads `todomvc.state` from disk + deserializes via serde_json + schema-version-checks + seeds Signals via `pinion_core::reactive::batch`; (3) installs a save `Effect` retained in `PersistenceBootMarker { _save_effect: Effect }` — Effect's Rc<EffectInner> must be held because Owner cleanup queue stores only Weak (R37.5 #2 leak fix), dropping the handle silently GCs the Effect. `PINION_STORAGE_DIR` env var override path for test isolation; default = `pinion-todomvc` app dir. Fallback chain: env-override → app-dir → `InMemoryStorage` (headless CI / sandboxed containers wire up unchanged).
examples/todomvc::Cargo.toml — new dep `pinion-platform-storage`. Workspace Cargo.toml gains `crates/pinion-platform-storage` member entry; transitive `dirs = 5` cargo dep.

tools/demos/todomvc_r665.py — 46-assertion AI-first persistence cycle demo: boot-1 empty storage → 3 rows + toggle + filter cycle → on-disk blob shape validated (schema_version=1, todos array typed, filter='Active', next_id > max id) → atomic write contract (no `.tmp` leftovers) → relaunch process → persisted blob restores ids/text/completion via blob-read (filter-independent, paint tree is filter-dependent) → next_id resumes from persisted value (NOT max+1) → `editing_id` confirmed NOT persisted (transient UI state) → schema mismatch (v999) → defaults restored + blob rewritten → corrupted bytes → defaults restored → delete persistence cycle → filter mode (All/Active/Completed) cycles across relaunches → `PINION_STORAGE_DIR` env override path honoured end-to-end. Uses `tempfile.mkdtemp` for isolation; per-cycle subprocess spawn via `make_subprocess(storage_dir)` env-var injection.

docs/SEED_PROMPT.md — R665 land summary refresh: 직전 5 세션 = R661 → R665 (R660 falls out); 다음 텍스트북 캐논 = R666 (AI-first 12+ step E2E composite path + scene/invoke v1 multi-External addressing) instead of R664; honest 부채 carry update (text-decoration strikethrough R664 청산 ✓ / AT-action wire R664 청산 ✓ / native paint double-click R664 청산 ✓); R665 lessons added (Effect handle retention substrate quirk + nested Owner::cache panic + filter-dependent paint vs blob-read source-of-truth distinction); R666 Phase A 진척 ~85% → ~90% framing.
verification_bullets: Workspace: PINION_STORAGE_DIR=/tmp/pinion-r665-test-isolation cargo test --workspace = 3352 passed / 0 failed (R664 baseline 3328 + 24 new — 9 pinion-core::storage + 15 pinion-platform-storage). Env override required because the default app-dir resolves to the developer's real `$XDG_DATA_HOME/pinion-todomvc/`.

Workspace: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello = clean (pedantic deny baseline preserved across the new pinion-platform-storage crate + the todomvc persistence wiring).

Visible: cargo run --release -p todomvc — exit + relaunch preserves rows + completion flags + filter mode. First launch creates `$XDG_DATA_HOME/pinion-todomvc/todomvc.state` (or `PINION_STORAGE_DIR/todomvc.state`); subsequent launches restore from it.

publishable_changes_bullets: pinion-core::storage — new module. `Storage` trait (load/save/remove, total surface, bytes-only) + `InMemoryStorage` default impl (`RefCell<BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>>`). Mirror of `Clipboard` / `InMemoryClipboard` (R56.1.e §5.22) substrate-shape: trait + headless default in pinion-core, platform impl in a sibling crate. Re-exported through pinion_core::lib root (`Storage`, `InMemoryStorage`). 9 unit tests cover fresh-default / round-trip / overwrite / empty-bytes / remove / multi-key isolation / dyn polymorphism / binary payloads.

pinion-platform-storage — new workspace crate (16th). `FileStorage::try_new(root)` opens a per-app directory (idempotent `create_dir_all`); `Storage` impl writes via tempfile + flush + sync_all + atomic rename so POSIX `rename(2)` / Windows `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` covers the whole transaction (no torn half-writes). Strict key sanitization (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` 1..=200) so the on-disk filename is a verbatim copy of the key — portable across OSes without escape encoding. `open_app_storage(name)` convenience wrapper composes `dirs::data_dir()` + `try_new` (Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME/<name>/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/<name>/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\<name>\`). 15 unit tests cover round-trip / reopen persistence / atomic-write-no-leftover-tmp / list_keys exclude tempfiles / invalid-key rejection (traversal + separators + null + non-ASCII + whitespace + empty + oversize) / key validator + path helpers / dyn polymorphism / default_app_dir / open_app_storage end-to-end.

R670.B.decision_summary: R670.B — Phase B (R700+) first real dogfood. AppShell multi-window refactor (per-WindowSlot cluster lift + per-window winit/accesskit/IME/intrinsic-resize dispatch) + RPC {window: "<id>"} param + WidgetView::view_for_window per-window paint hook + examples/hello-multi-window first multi-window consumer (main Button + inspector state-debug Text mirror via shared ShellCore). Phase B foundation from R670.A trait extension now actually walked + dispatched at runtime.
changes_bullets: Atomic (0) — pinion-shell::AppShell multi-window refactor. New `WindowSlot { render, vello_scene, accesskit, ime_was_composing, last_ime_cursor_area, pending_intrinsic_resize, spec_id }` struct lifts 5 pre-R670.B single-window AppShell fields into a per-window cluster; `AppShell::windows: HashMap<WindowId, WindowSlot<V::Renderer>>` cluster map keyed by winit WindowId, plus `spec_id_to_window_id: HashMap<&'static str, WindowId>` reverse-lookup for RPC scope resolution + `primary_window_id: Option<WindowId>` for default-scope frames. The 15+ existing single-window bindings see bit-identical lifecycle because R670.A's default `V::windows()` returns exactly one WindowSpec (the canonical primary id='main').

Atomic (0) wire — `resumed()` walks `V::windows()` list + delegates to new `resume_spec(spec, cached_window_id, make_primary)` helper which creates one winit Window + GPU renderer + accesskit_winit::Adapter per spec; per-spec `IntrinsicAfterFirstPaint` queue + winit `set_min_inner_size` floor; `make_primary=true` records the spec_id as primary_window_id (RPC frames omitting {window} default-scope here). `suspended()` walks all slots + drops GPU renderers + caches Window arcs. `window_event(window_id, event)` dispatches per-window: `forward_to_accesskit(window_id)` looks up the matching slot's adapter; `Resized` updates the matching slot's renderer; `Ime` updates the matching slot's was_composing; `RedrawRequested` calls `render_window(window_id)`. `render()` split into `render_window(window_id)` + 2 helpers (`emit_accesskit_for_window`, `publish_ime_for_window`) to keep the parent fn under the workspace clippy::too_many_lines=100 ceiling after the per-window cluster lift. `drain_redraw_to_winit` walks every active window slot + calls `Window::request_redraw` (single-window bindings: 1 iteration; multi-window: N iterations).

Atomic (1) — pinion-rpc::DispatchContext gains `window_id: Option<&'a str>` field + `with_window(id)` builder. AppShell::dispatch_rpc parses `params.window` off the JSON-RPC frame via new `parse_rpc_window_id` helper (serde_json sniffer + try/None fallback to default 'main'); `resolve_spec_id` resolves the supplied id against the spec map with primary fallback for unknown ids (AI clients targeting non-existent windows see primary's scene rather than hard error — single-window bindings always have a primary).

Atomic (1) substrate — ShellCore::dispatch_rpc_for_window(request, window_id, resize) per-window variant + private dispatch_rpc_inner shared body (the body holds the original disjoint-field borrow split intact); the per-window variant threads `Some(spec_id)` into the producer closure so `V::view_for_window(spec_id, state, frame)` runs instead of `V::view(state, frame)`. WidgetView::view_for_window(window_id, state, frame) -> Scene trait method with default impl forwarding to Self::view so 15+ single-window bindings stay bit-identical without touching their impls. ShellCore::compute_paint_scene_for_window(window_id, w, h) mirror of compute_paint_scene routing through view_for_window; includes the R51.147 `any_animation_active → redraw_requested` parity bit (the missing parity caused a todomvc_r665 regression mid-refactor; the fix landed by extending compute_paint_scene_for_window to include the same animation-loop heartbeat compute_paint_scene already had).

Atomic (2) — examples/hello-multi-window first multi-window consumer (17th example crate). `V::windows()` returns 2 specs: WindowSpec::new('main', 'hello-multi-window — Main', Fixed{320,200}) + WindowSpec::new('inspector', 'hello-multi-window — Inspector', Fixed{280,140}). `V::view_for_window` switches: 'inspector' → state-debug text rendering `format!("{:?}", state)` of the shared ButtonState + tag 'inspector_state_text'; everything else (canonical 'main' + unknown ids defensively) → main Button view with tag 'main_btn'. Single ShellCore underlies both windows so main's state mutations propagate to inspector on the next paint cycle.

Atomic (2) wire — 6 unit tests in r670_b_multi_window_tests (windows-list-shape, main-view-has-button-tag, inspector-view-has-state-text-tag, inspector-view-reflects-state-value with hoisted walk_for_text helper, unknown-id-falls-back-to-main, default-access-node-empty). `#![allow(clippy::doc_markdown)]` at the binding crate level because example bindings carry doc-comment density that fights the workspace clippy::pedantic floor; substrate crates keep the strict default. New `tools/demos/hello_multi_window_r670b.py` (12+ assertion demo): scene/snapshot {window:'main'} vs {window:'inspector'} content separation; scene/click on main → inspector mirrors Hover; scene/invoke /external/send Disable → inspector mirrors Disabled; scene/invoke Enable → Idle restored; unknown window id falls back to primary.
verification_bullets: 3437 workspace tests pass (was 3431 at R670.A → +6 hello-multi-window r670_b_multi_window_tests). 0 failures across all 61 test suites.
