R897.1.decision_summary: Fix the recurring CI 'No space left on device' link failure (a runner disk-capacity infra issue, not a code flake): reclaim preinstalled runner SDKs inline before the build and strip test-binary debug line-tables, so the windowless test link has headroom and pushes stop needing a manual rerun.
changes_bullets: root cause: the windowless lint-and-test job links every crate + example test binary; the runner's ~14GB free disk ran out at link time ("No space left on device"), failing 2/2 recent pushes (R896.1, R897 attempt#1) — a CI infra capacity issue, NOT a code/test flake
reclaim ~25GB of preinstalled runner SDKs (dotnet/android/ghc/CodeQL/boost) inline before the build in both jobs — inline rm, not an unpinned third-party action (supply-chain surface avoided)
CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 on the test job strips debug line-tables (the bulk of the test-binary link footprint); pass/fail and debug-assertions unchanged
verification_bullets: ci.yml validated as well-formed YAML (python yaml.safe_load; both jobs + step order intact)
effect is observable only on the next CI run (a green attempt#1 with no manual rerun) — disk reclaim cannot be exercised on the dev box
carry_forward_bullets: if the disk pressure recurs despite the reclaim, the next lever is splitting the workspace test job or capping test-link parallelism (-j)

R903.decision_summary: R903 find & replace (cost-no-object textbook; diversify off the R896-R902 node-editor/tree local optimum, R896 lesson). The find session (needle + case/whole-word flags) lives on TextEditState so the editor is self-describing to AI introspection (find_matches RPC reports count/ranges/current); the current match is the selection (browser/VS Code model), so no fragile current-index state. All-match highlight bands reuse selection_rects_for_range with data = find_matches (windowless-verifiable). Replace All is the FIRST consumer of the undo substrate's reserved macro-transaction axis (begin_macro/end_macro -> MacroCommand): N splices fold into one Ctrl+Z. Find/replace mirrors read<->write on TextFieldExternal. Self-grep lift: the {start,end}|Null encoding is now selection_range_to_value SSOT shared by the selection query + find-next/prev. Single-line editor kept (multiline wraps one Scroll, would break caret-count tests); ASCII case-fold (byte-offset exact); keyboard find-bar UI deferred (RPC is the §2 primary path).

R904.decision_summary: R904 syntax highlighting (cost-no-object textbook; 2nd text-depth round after R903 find/replace, completing the code-editor essentials — well under the >3-round-per-axis local-optimum threshold). New pinion-core::syntax: SyntaxPalette (fixed classic scheme) + pure highlight_code(text, keywords, palette, font_size) C-family tokenizer (line comment / string-with-escape / number / keyword), char-aware + byte-offset exact. TextEditState::attach_highlighter makes style_runs() a content-derived read (the R903 find_matches derive pattern) so the SINGLE style_runs() read site feeds paint + caret geometry + hit-test + the scene/style_runs RPC — an AI reads the editor's token colouring directly. The attach_highlighter closure IS the language-agnostic seam (no premature Language trait; the keyword slice covers C-family dialects). Runs bake the field font_size (default size 0 = invisible glyphs). Highlighter and manual styling are mutually-exclusive modes (code editor vs rich text); a Highlighter newtype carries a manual Debug so TextEditState keeps its derive. Self-grep: NO lift — is_word_char (find whole-word) and syntax identifier-char are independent concepts coincidentally \w (coupling = wrong-abstraction); attach_* and derived-accessor are idioms, not duplicated logic.

R905.decision_summary: R905 scene-outliner batch operations (cost-no-object textbook; diversify off the R903-R904 text axis back to the editor/DCC axis with a NEW editing capability — the payoff of R902's multi-selection). delete-selected + rename-selected on the stable-id multi-selection, each ONE undo step. delete-selected removes only the TOP-LEVEL selected subtrees (a selected descendant rides along inside its selected ancestor via collect_top_level dedup), captured granularly (parent+index+subtree, not a whole-tree snapshot) so undo restores the exact shape (redo removes by id, undo reinserts ascending-by-index). rename-selected expands a {n} template numbered in pre-order (or a literal). Both are AI-first invoke ops on the multi-select coordinator (delete_selected/rename_selected return the count, undo/redo a bool) — the §2 RPC primary path. Structural mutation is example-local on the concrete OutlinerNode: TreeNode::children_mut returns a slice (can't resize), so a generic tree structural-edit substrate needs a trait extension (children_vec_mut) deferred to a 2nd consumer. Self-grep NO lift: TreeBatchDelete/Rename are peers of file_browser's single-select delete_selected/rename_selected (different cardinality / model / undo) — coupling = wrong-abstraction; the R903 macro axis was NOT forced (a single multi-target command is cleaner for position-coupled deletes than a macro of N, the hello-node-editor shape).

R906.decision_summary: R906 cost-no-object session-review audit clearance (user '교과서적/SSOT/북극성?' on R903-R905). 3-lens adversarial subagents (SSOT/correctness/scope-deferral) + my own grep+read re-verification, bucketed real / over-reach / genuine-defer. REAL fixed: (A) splice_inner SSOT — R903 added the splice primitive but left 3 pre-existing selection branches (insert/backspace/delete-forward) as copies -> routed through splice_inner (4->1, behaviour-identical). (B) dark-mode defect — R904 baked the classic() light palette unconditionally (illegible on a dark surface); added SyntaxPalette::dark()/for_dark + ThemeProvider::is_dark() (the single resolution SSOT theme() now uses) and the example's highlighter picks by theme.is_dark() (captures the provider Rc + calls is_dark() = pure Signal reads -> reactive in the view AND safe from the Owner-less RPC path). (C) insert_subtree silent push-to-root fallback -> debug_assert (R889 silent-corruption-mask). (E) 3-copy band-box emit (find/selection/preedit) -> push_band SSOT (R903 lifted rect_to_band geometry but not the emit). (F) the outliner had NO keyboard editing -> Delete/Backspace=delete_selected, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y=undo/redo (node-editor precedent; methods existed; was scope-avoidance). (G) begin_macro/end_macro pub but undo/redo unguarded mid-macro -> debug_assert + no-op guard. REJECTED over-reach (verified): is_word_char lift (find search-boundary vs syntax identifier-char = independent concepts coincidentally \w, wrong-abstraction); find_matches.ranges [s,e] vs selection {start,end} (bulk-list pairs vs single W3C range, conventional); replace_all count over-reports no-op replacements (= matches replaced, VS Code convention; a no-op records no undo step, correct). Verdict: cross-round SSOT discipline strong; the gaps were within-round 'added the primitive, did not sweep existing copies' (splice / band) + a dark-mode feature gap + missing editor keys.

R915.decision_summary: Add DragCalibration::traveled_beyond click-vs-drag discriminator; wire into both numeric scrubs so a click focuses the cell and only a past-threshold drag scrubs (completes R914 the canonical DCC way)
changes_bullets: Add DragCalibration::traveled_beyond(basis, threshold_px): the click-vs-drag
discriminator (max cursor travel from press >= threshold), tracked via a new
max_abs_delta on the press anchor (+1 unit test).
Wire it into both numeric scrubs (data-grid + property-grid): is_scrubbing now
means "past the DRAG_CLICK_THRESHOLD_PX dead zone", gating the scrub mutation,
the trailing-click suppression, and the AI `scrubbing` query in one decision.
Result (canonical DCC gesture): a click on a numeric cell now FOCUSES it
(clears the R914 absorption); only a drag past the threshold scrubs.
column-resize + splitter ignore the gate (no click action) — unchanged.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace -j2: all pass (DragCalibration 5 incl traveled_beyond;
data-grid 44; property-grid 45; the R914 click test renamed + flipped to assert
click-focuses; r875 calibration-frame scrubbing assertion updated).
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello: clean.
demos: r915 click-vs-scrub split (34 assert, NEW) + r914 (section H now asserts
click focuses) + r875 (property-grid, unchanged-pass) all PASS (release).
carry_forward_bullets: The threshold gate is opt-in per consumer: scrubs use it (click vs drag);
column-resize / splitter have no click action so they ignore it. Documented on
DragCalibration::traveled_beyond.
Dead-zone jump: crossing the 4px threshold applies travel from the press, so an
int scrub steps by ~round(4/8)=~0/1 at the boundary (negligible, standard).
scrollbar (SCXML-embedded 1-D) + dock + node (2-D) DragCalibration routing still
deferred (R914 carry; shape/architecture reasons, not effort).

R916.decision_summary: Add node-editor Details panel reflecting the single selected node's properties + selection-relative detail.* RPC (read+intervene alias for node.<selected>.*), the editor select->inspect->edit loop
changes_bullets: Add a Details panel (right sidebar) to hello-node-editor: reflects the single
selected node's editable properties (title / x / y / per-port defaults) as
rows, the Unreal "select -> inspect" surface. Placeholder when not exactly one
node is selected.
Add selection-relative `detail.<field>` RPC: a thin alias for
`node.<selected>.<field>` (read + intervene), delegating through one
`selected_node_path` SSOT so the panel's read and write address the same node;
`Null` / UnknownPath when the selection is not exactly one node (R909 pattern).
`detail.*` editing routes through the identical rename / move / set-default
funnels the absolute `node.<id>` path uses (one mutation path, undoable).
Widen the window to TOTAL_W (palette + canvas + panel) and SSOT it with the
root container's size so the flex row never shrinks (canvas stays at its
PALETTE_W offset — the geometry every demo's coordinates assume).

demos: r916 node Details panel (37 assert, NEW) + r838 / r879 / r901 node-editor
all PASS (release); geometry probe confirms canvas back at x=132 (unchanged).
in-panel inline click-to-edit deferred (additive GUI affordance, the R909->R910
sequencing) — editing is the AI-first `intervene detail.*` / card path today.
carry_forward_bullets: In-panel click-to-edit (a row -> inline field in the panel) is deferred: the
panel reflects + edits via `intervene detail.*` / the node card today; the GUI
click-to-edit affordance is the R910-style follow-up (additive, not a blocker).
detail_row paint is panel-local (the property-grid view_row is example-local,
different geometry/model) — per the R909 "cell paint is opinionated" rule, no
cross-example lift until a 3rd identical consumer.
A fixed-size flex row shrinks its sidebars when the window is narrower than the

R926.decision_summary: R926 adds matching-bracket support to the text editor as the third derive-on-read consumer (after find_matches R903 / style_runs R904): TextEditState::matching_bracket() re-derives the (open, close) pair the caret sits adjacent to from the live buffer + caret, read by both the paint outline and the scene/<tag>/external/bracket_match RPC slot so they cannot disagree on the pair. Same-type depth scan over (), [], {} with before-caret adjacency precedence; a baseline matcher (strict cross-type interleave + string/comment skipping deferred to the syntax tokenizer).

byte scan is UTF-8-safe (ASCII bracket bytes never occur inside a multi-byte char)
scene/<tag>/external/bracket_match RPC slot: {open, close} byte pair, or null when no match
view_field frames each matched bracket with an Accent outline box (focus-gated, post-text)
existing hello-syntax-highlight reused as the consumer; new r926_bracket_match.py demo

Migrate hello-lazy-list page cache to ResourceCache (1st consumer); behaviour + 8 tests + demo unchanged
New hello-asset-browser: async source-side sort/filter over a virtualized 10k out-of-memory source
Sort and filter are query params pushed to the source (composite page key sort,filter,page), not client proxies over a materialized Vec
Filtered count is a queried Resource (keyed by filter) that sizes the virtual list; a re-query resets the scroll to the top
Two reactive Effects: count loader (filter dep) and page loader (sort/filter/scroll/count deps, gated on count Ready)

R933.1.decision_summary: R933.1 adversarial 3-reviewer session-review of R933 (correctness / SSOT / doc-honesty), every finding re-verified by my own grep+read. One HIGH correctness defect fixed: fold anchors were not shifted on incremental edits, so an edit before a collapsed block could spring it open or, on a coincidental anchor-byte collision, hide the WRONG block (my 'never wrong content' claim was false). Folds now shift/clip at every text-mutation site and across undo/redo replay, the byte-offset peer of the style-run maintenance. Doc-honesty fixes: removed a fabricated fragment-cache claim, reframed the non-editable example as a read-only RPC fold viewer, softened an unverified VS Code citation; fixed an O(N x lines) per-paint re-derivation in the example. Over-reach rejected after re-verification: match_forward granularity (fold walks forward only) and set_text+undo fold non-restore (correct non-journal semantics).

R943.1.decision_summary: R943.1 adversarial session-review clearance (user-requested 'is it textbook / SSOT / north-star?' audit of R942+R943). Found and fixed 2 real Color-popup consistency bugs: the begin verb (keyboard Enter/F2) only opened Choice popups so a Color cell was keyboard-inert (openable by click only); and access_focus_target always emitted the opt (Choice) composite prefix so an open Color popup advertised a dangling aria-activedescendant the swatch grid never paints. Both stem from generalizing the popup machinery for Color everywhere except these two activation/a11y sites. An adversarial grep of every CellKind gate + every CHOICE_OPT_PREFIX use confirmed these were the only two missed; all other Color gates are consistent. R942 (row_cells, LoaderMarker) re-confirmed local-correct.

access_focus_target uses the kind-correct composite prefix (sw for Color, opt for Choice)

R945.decision_summary: Editor line manipulation: TextEditState::move_lines + duplicate_lines (VS Code Alt+Up/Down move + Shift+Alt copy), N-th consumer of the R938/R939 line-op substrate + a newline-inclusive line_extent_end helper. RPC-primary invoke verbs move-line-up/down + duplicate-line-up/down (keyboard chords deferred — Alt+Arrow overlaps vertical nav). One undo step each; the lone newline relocates exactly when a move crosses the final newline-less line.
changes_bullets: TextEditState gains move_lines(down) + duplicate_lines(down): the move-line (VS Code Alt+Up/Down) and
copy-line (Shift+Alt+Up/Down) commands every code editor has, reusable by every multi-line field
move_lines swaps the current line (or selected block) with the adjacent line as ONE replace_range over
the two-line region, re-sequenced; the lone newline relocates so the buffer keeps exact line structure
even when the move crosses the final, newline-less line (the swapped pair trade which one ends the buffer)
duplicate_lines inserts a copy directly below (one undo step); down chooses caret on the lower copy vs
the upper instance; a last-line block (no trailing newline) gets a separator newline before its copy
caret/selection rides the moved block; a multi-line selection re-covers the moved block
N-th consumer of the R938/R939 line-op substrate (line_starts_in_range) + new line_extent_end helper
(newline-inclusive line end; distinct from syntax.rs line_comment_end which excludes the newline)
line_block_extent lifted as the shared block-finding preamble of move/duplicate (self-grep: byte-
identical 2-consumer mechanical duplicate)
RPC invoke verbs move-line-up/down + duplicate-line-up/down (Null arg -> Bool changed; boundary move
is false; bare field inert) + schema slots; AI-first twins of the chords (RPC-primary, R941 precedent)

toggle routes: with a selection -> merge_style_run; at a collapsed caret -> arm the pending mark
insert overlays the armed mark on the typed span yet leaves it armed (a keystroke run stays styled)
navigation movers (set_caret/move_*/select_*) + wholesale set_text clear the mark; edits preserve it
TextEditCommand gains inserted_runs, the symmetric peer of removed_runs
redo re-overlays run coverage an insert added (clip+shift cannot re-derive it) so a mark survives redo
record_edit captures post-edit coverage; merge concats it across coalesced typing

toolbar_active_style is one SSOT for the view-paint + a11y reflective toggle reads
style_to_value lifts the Option<TextStyle> -> Json/Null encode shared by the two query reads

R964.decision_summary: Bounded slider delegate for the property grid: a ranged Float leaf (Opacity, slot 8, normalised 0..1) clamps to its interval and renders an in-cell slider gauge (Unreal Details factor field). Clamp funnels every writer through set_value (scrub + inline-edit + RPC value.<i>); range introspection via query range.<i> -> lo..hi/none aligned to the data-grid R894 col_range sibling; gauge fill tagged property_grid#gauge<slot> + pointer_transparent, reusing slider.rs colours. Self-grep: 2nd consumer of R894 bounded-numeric-DCC pattern but divergent (Int-column vs Float-slot) so share the stdlib clamp atom only, no forced lift; a11y valuemin/max a shared defer with R894.
changes_bullets: Add the bounded ("ranged") slider delegate to the property grid: a
Float leaf with a fixed [min,max] (Opacity, slot 8, normalised 0..1)
is clamped to its interval and renders an in-cell slider gauge — the
Unreal Details / Blender "factor" field. A thin track + active fill
along the cell's bottom edge shows the value's position in range.
Clamp funnels every writer at one place: scalar_range + clamp_to_range
in set_value (the data-grid set_cell clamp the doc once flagged as
absent), so the scrub, the inline-edit commit, and the RPC value.<i>
intervene all bound the same way.
AI-first range introspection: query range.<i> -> "<lo>..<hi>" / "none",
the same wire as the data-grid R894 col_range.<col> sibling, so one
range format reads across both DCC widgets.
Gauge fill tagged property_grid#gauge<slot> + pointer_transparent: the
rendered fraction (frac * track_width) is introspectable, and a press
falls through to the row's scrub (the R954 overlay stance). Reuses the
slider.rs track/fill colours (no hand-rolled paint).
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace -j2 green (hello-property-grid +3 R964 tests:
pure clamp, range query + intervene clamp both ends, scrub clamp +
un-clamp-on-return; 75 pass).

rects: range "0..1"/"none", out-of-range RPC + live scrub clamp, gauge
fill width == round(frac*230) for 0.1..1.0, reset restores default).
Regression: all 10 hello-property-grid demos PASS (shared set_value /
view_row / schema change; no breakage).
3b self-grep: R964 is the 2nd consumer of the data-grid R894 bounded-
numeric-DCC clamp pattern, but the two diverge (R894 Int-only column-
keyed vs R964 Float-only slot-keyed) -> share only the stdlib clamp
atom, no forced lift; wire aligned to R894 for a future NumericRange.
carry_forward_bullets: a11y valuemin/valuemax/valuenow for the bounded slider leaf is a
shared honest defer: the data-grid R894 sibling also exposes no a11y
range (only the RPC wire), so adding aria-value range is a separate
a11y axis for both, not an R964 regression.
a unified core NumericRange (Int+Float) is the eventual lift home for
R894 + R964 once a 3rd consumer or a kind-unified column/leaf appears;
the RPC wire ("<lo>..<hi>"/"none") is already aligned so the lift is
wire-compatible.
only Opacity is ranged today; widening the range table (more leaves /
Int leaves) is additive once a consumer needs it.

R990.decision_summary: R990 §5.27 §5.38 §5.40 data-grid column hide/show: hello-column-visibility column chooser (reflective toolbar disabled axis 2nd consumer) + binding-level visible-column projection into view_table
changes_bullets: New hello-column-visibility example: data-grid column hide / show, the column
chooser every data grid / asset browser / inspector ships.
Model: a shared Signal<Vec<bool>> (use_visibility), one bit per source column;
the chooser, the view, and the reducer all read it.
Chooser: the R692 ToolbarExternal (primary), one control per column. aria-pressed
AND disabled are both reflective (read from the model each frame): pressed[i] =
visible[i]; the sole remaining visible column's control is disabled (cannot hide
every column) — the 2nd consumer of the R989 reflective toolbar disabled axis.
Grid: the binding projects the visible columns (filtered headers + per-row cells)
into the existing view_table paint; grid_table_nodes announces only the visible
columns (aria-colcount drops as columns hide). No grid-paint change — the
visual<->source column mapping lives in the binding (a 2nd consumer would lift it).

R990.1.decision_summary: R990.1 adversarial session-review clearance of R989+R990: lift read_roving_focus reader (4-site decode), add selected.<i> write symmetry, correct toolbar disabled doc (aria-disabled vs HTML-disabled), full disabled mask in status
changes_bullets: Adversarial session-review clearance of R989 + R990 (2 independent reviewers +
self-grep). Cleared the real findings; rejected the over-flags with evidence.
HIGH: lift `read_roving_focus(intro) -> (usize, bool)` to widgets/toolbar.rs (the
toolbar peer of read_selected / read_open_state). The (focus, focused) decode was
hand-rolled at 4 sites (hello-toolbar / -selection-toolbar x2 / -column-visibility)
= mechanical 3rd+ consumer the self-grep missed; a slot rename would silently break
all four. All four read_state bodies now call the one reader.
MED: SelRowExternal gains intervene("selected.<i>", bool) — the absolute write
mirror of the selected.<i> read (wire-form read/write symmetry; the ListBoxExternal
multi-select admin path). The send wire was the only mutation = relative-toggle only.
MED: corrected the toolbar disabled module doc — it cited "the APG menu/menubar
convention" but this repo's menu SKIPS disabled (non-activatable); rewrote it to cite
the W3C aria-disabled discipline (author-gates) vs HTML-disabled (UA-suppress at the
widget, what button/menu use), documenting the deliberate divergence + why a derived
(reflective) toolbar disabled cannot own the bit without per-frame cross-external sync.
LOW: hello-selection-toolbar status line emits the full disabled mask
(del/clr/all), matching its "full selection state" doc claim.
Rejected (verified defensible): the emit-then-gate disabled discipline is a valid
W3C aria-disabled pattern (not a hack); #[expect(too_many_arguments)] matches the
sibling menu.rs precedent; SelRowExternal is not a ListBoxExternal reimpl (dynamic
shrinking holder vs fixed-N); the column projection / Vec<bool> / serde bound are
correct 1st-consumer calls.
verification_bullets: workspace test 0 failed; clippy 0 (-D pedantic, --all-targets); validate T1=0.
new unit tests: read_roving_focus decodes both slots (toolbar.rs);
selected.<i> absolute idempotent set + OutOfRange/TypeMismatch errors (sel-toolbar).
r989 demo PASS (now 46 assert: added the selected.<i> absolute-write section —
idempotent set, read mirrors write); r990 demo PASS (35); r692 (hello-toolbar) +
r799 (hello-textarea fmt toolbar) regression demos PASS after the read_roving_focus
refactor + the disabled:false ToolbarControl updates.
self-grep: read_roving_focus now the single decoder for all 4 (focus,focused) sites;
reviewers' over-flags (disabled-discipline hack / arg-bundling / ListBox reimpl)
rejected with code+W3C evidence.
carry_forward_bullets: LESSON: in-round self-grep keeps missing mechanical decoder duplication — the
(focus, focused) decode reached 4 sites before an adversarial review caught it.
Add a "wire-decoder reused at N sites?" axis to the self-grep (read_selected /
read_open_state / read_roving_focus are the lifted family); a slot rename test is
the canary. [[verify-seed-claims-audit-first]] vindicated again: my 'clean' was not.
LESSON: when documenting a new widget's disabled (or any a11y) discipline, grep the
SIBLING widgets' actual behavior before citing them as precedent — button absorbs
(statechart), menu skips, this toolbar aria-disables; they are three valid but
DISTINCT disciplines (owned-suppress vs derived-aria-disabled), and the doc must say
which and why, not hand-wave "the APG convention".
the read_roving_focus reader is generic over any external exposing focus:Int +
focused:Bool (the list external reuses it); a future non-toolbar roving widget gets
it for free.

R998.decision_summary: Model-View at-scale campaign slice 3: a declarative per-row style-rule engine (Wireshark/dlt-class row coloring). A rule is a GridFilter predicate -> a RowTint{bg,fg}; rows paint by the first matching rule (Wireshark precedence). The match half REUSES the R997 GridFilter conjunction, so coloring and filtering share the wire vocab. The rule list lives in a reactive RowStyleState (use_row_style SSOT); RowStyleExternal is the AI-first RPC surface (rule mgmt + per-row match.<row>/tint.<row> introspection without pixels). The paint integrates via an additive VirtualTableData.row_style resolver, resolved per source row (coloring survives re-sort), precedence selection > rule > zebra. New hello-grid-row-style reference example + RPC demo.
changes_bullets: New pinion-core widgets::row_style: RowStyleRule{filter: GridFilter, tint:

match_index (first-match precedence, reusing R997 GridFilter::matches) +
use_row_style. The rule predicate IS the R997 GridFilter conjunction, so
coloring and filtering share the wire vocab.
RowStyleExternal: AI-first RPC surface — rule_count / rule.<i> / rules
(query + restore) / add_rule / clear, plus per-row match.<row> / tint.<row>
/ matched_rows via an attached cell source (introspect the coloring without
pixels). Wire: rule "<filter>;<bg-hex>;<fg-hex>", list joined by "|".
pinion-widget-paint table: additive VirtualTableData.row_style resolver
(Option<&dyn Fn(usize)->Option<(Color,Color)>>); row_inputs precedence
selection > rule > zebra; per-SOURCE row so coloring survives a re-sort.

pass row_style: None (byte-identical).

R998.1.decision_summary: Adversarial session-review clearance of R997 + R998 (2 independent reviewers + self-grep). Cleared real defects, rejected over-flags with evidence. HIGH: the grid_sort.rs '## Scope (honest boundaries)' block still said 'Sort only' / 'No undo' though R783/R779/R997 added filter+undo+multi-facet in the same file (the recurring stale-doc failure mode). MED: filter field doc said single-facet; matched_rows did O(N) Signal-clone per row — lifted a pure match_index_in SSOT so matched_rows + the paint resolver read the rule Signal once (the order() read-once pattern). LOW: row_inputs double is_selected, 14-site formatting damage from the R998 perl, |-separator wire doc, clear schema int.
changes_bullets: grid_sort.rs HIGH: module "## Scope (honest boundaries)" said "Sort only" +
"No undo" — both false (R783 filter, R779 undo, R997 multi-facet). Rewrote to
truth (sort + multi-facet conjunction filter; undoable sort, filter off the
stack). MED: `filter` field doc "single-facet" -> multi-facet.
row_style.rs MED: matched_rows did O(N) Signal::get() rule-Vec clones (one per
row). Lifted a pure `match_index_in(&[RowStyleRule], cell)` SSOT (the per-row

flat siblings not one bounding container: Scene::hit_test resolves a full-window container with no child hit as the container ITSELF, which would absorb every center click; thin flat regions let the center fall through to content

Round 1123.1.decision_summary: Round 1123.1: session self-audit clearance (user textbook/SSOT review) — single window-identity resolution restores §2 #7 live-vs-mirror parity, one retain-by-prefix SSOT, per-window-accessor naming, per-window-cache leak fix, inset-height DRY; no architectural must-fix
changes_bullets: A (§2 #7 latent fix): window_chrome_for now returns the resolved canonical spec_id; apply_window_chrome + apply_resize_border key the maximized lookup by THAT spec_id, not by window_id.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_WINDOW) — so the None primary/mirror paint and the Some(id) live paint resolve the SAME window and the maximize/restore glyph + resize-suppression agree (was divergent for any binding whose first window is not named "main", silently breaking the live-vs-mirror parity R1123 claimed)

B (SSOT): clear_highlights now delegates to the shared strip_children_with_prefix; deleted the duplicate is_highlight_child retain-by-prefix (one retain-by-prefix SSOT, two consumers: highlights + R1122 resize border)

C (convention): renamed window_maximized / set_window_maximized to maximized_for_window / set_maximized_for_window to match the per-window accessor family (target_fps_for_window / immediate_subtree_for_window / ...)

D (leak/staleness fix): remove_window now drops maximized_per_window (mine) AND immediate_subtree_per_window (pre-existing R681 omission, same class) — a closed window's entry no longer leaks, and a reused window id (torn-off panels mint runtime ids) no longer inherits stale maximized state / pacing flag

E (DRY): extracted chrome_inset_height(window_id) — the window_chrome_for(window_id).map(|(_, _, style)| style.height_px) inset-height expression was duplicated at both the live + pure-mirror inset sites; one helper now serves both (also keeps compute_paint_scene_internal under the 100-line clippy ceiling)
verification_bullets: new test maximized_glyph_parity_when_primary_window_is_not_named_main: a chromed window id "panel" (not "main"), maximized — the None primary/mirror paint AND the Some("panel") live paint both draw the restore glyph (Path 10 commands) and suppress the resize border; fails pre-fix (None paint keyed "main" -> miss -> maximize glyph) = proves the §2 #7 fix
new test closing_a_window_clears_its_maximized_cache: set maximized on a secondary id, remove_window, assert the entry is gone = proves the leak/staleness fix
chrome fixture macro gained an $id param; added BorderlessPanel("panel") fixture; 3 existing fixtures pass "main"
pinion-overlay 23 tests (highlight delegation intact) + pinion-shell 18 chrome tests green
workspace cargo test green; clippy --all-targets -D pedantic + rustfmt clean
carry_forward_bullets: window_chrome_for is called twice per paint (apply_window_chrome + apply_resize_border each resolve it) = a redundant windows-signal read; kept deliberately for overlay separation-of-concerns + measure-first (no SSOT divergence — both read the same signal); fold into one resolution only if a profile shows it

STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION (not fixed, pre-existing pattern): per-window state is 10 parallel HashMap<String, T> on ShellCore (structure-of-arrays); cohesive but invites the remove_window omission this round caught — a HashMap<String, WindowState> array-of-structures would make cleanup total by construction. A standalone consolidation round, not R1123.1 scope
per-window close (chrome close = event_loop.exit) + resize-cursor-on-hover remain DEFERRED-pending-consumer (unchanged from R1123) — no SECONDARY-window-with-window_chrome-hook consumer yet
session self-audit found NO architectural must-fix; cleared 4 items introduced/surfaced this session — a latent §2 #7 parity bug, an SSOT duplicate, a naming drift, and a per-window-cache leak

Grown rows target their known appended source index (never a visible-position lookup), so a mid-paste re-sort cannot make them chase a moving target.

split_long_edges returns the bends PER EDGE instead of a bare count, which is what makes that route derivable

Round 1443.decision_summary: R1443 — a tangled topology view tidies itself without forgetting its shape: the layered solver gains an exchange step that moves only what a crossing pays for, so a stable drawing has a middle option between keeping every tangle for ever and being redrawn from scratch
changes_bullets: Layering::untangle — the paper's transpose (Gansner et al., TSE 1993): exchange adjacent vertices in a layer
an exchange is accepted ONLY where it strictly reduces the crossing count, so every move is bought by one
strictness is the TERMINATION argument, not a preference: an integer count each accepted exchange decreases
Sugiyama::run_settled — order by the seed, then untangle; a departure from the remembered drawing pays for itself
the two currencies R1442 published are the ones that read the new pass, so three orderings compare on one graph
reduce_crossings becomes the whole of mincross: barycenter pass, then exchange, keeping the BEST order seen
FIX pre-existing: balance rounded with i32::midpoint, which rounds towards zero, so differently each side of 0
a mixed rounding direction loses a unit of the gap the compaction placed between two vertices; floor_midpoint
hello-topology gains Mode::Settled, a policy, and an untangle verb, an action — different in kind, so both exist
the verb never writes the mode signal, so relieving a tangle does not change what the NEXT change will do
status_text names the ordering via Mode::name, the string RPC publishes, instead of a second mapping

Round 1445.decision_summary: R1445 — a scroll pins to the bottom the next layout pass measures: a consumer whose appended extent only the layout knows states the intent instead of inventing a bound, so no false bound is ever published to the readers of that state
changes_bullets: ScrollState::follow_measured_tail — arm a one-shot "take me to the tail the next layout pass measures"
the layout-measured sibling of virtual_list::follow_tail, which needs count x row_pitch to name the bound
a consumer whose extent only taffy/parley know could not name one, and faked it: set_max(0, i32::MAX)
that fake is a bound published to every other reader of the same state, true for exactly nobody
ScrollState::apply_measured_tail_pin(axis) — consume the arming, pin along the node's DECLARED axis
the owning ScrollNode already says which axes scroll, so the tail is read off that, not re-decided
returns whether the offset MOVED, post equality-skip, matching set_max's dirty-bit convention
layout: apply_measured_tail_pins runs LAST, after both bound writers of the frame
so the pin lands on the bound the frame ended with and never needs to know which writer produced it
followers are skipped on the bounds pass's own gate: the pin rides the node that publishes the bound
LIFT (3rd-consumer self-grep): fold_scrolls — the three walks each carried the same traversal
scene/scroll_state publishes following_measured_tail, the standing arming a hidden node keeps
hello-transcript — wrapped-prose transcript; two policies (always reveal / follow only if at the tail)
neither reducer computes an extent; the arming call IS follow_tail's was_following parameter

Round 1446.decision_summary: R1446 - a chart plots the field the user points it at: pinion-chart meets pinion's typed cell model through a ModelMapper, and a cell that holds no number is reported rather than plotted as a zero

the charting crate and the typed cell model had never met; a chart's data was a compile-time fact

ModelMapper: an x Field, N y fields, a first/count record range, and an Orientation

Field::At(i) / Field::Ordinal, named orientation-neutrally so a pivoted block reads the same way

map() invents nothing: an unreadable cell contributes no point and is reported with its TABLE
coordinates and the CellKind actually there, so a consumer names the column instead of drawing a lie
the x field is read ONCE for the record range, not per series, so one bad x cell is counted once
numeric() - Int and Float only; a Bool is a flag, and a numeric string in a text column is text

filter-chip (R753), series-toggle (R1379) and this round each spelled it; the base FILL stays local

Round 1447.decision_summary: R1447 - a terminal frame stops reading the system font list: LayoutCache defers its FontContext to the first shape, so the backend that has no fonts no longer scans for them, and no longer dies on a host that has none
changes_bullets: LayoutCache defers its FontContext to the first call that actually shapes
FontContext::new() enumerates every installed font through the platform font API
measured on this box: LayoutCache::new() 25.5 ms with 635 fonts, essentially all of it that scan
fontique caches nothing across instances - CollectionOptions.system_fonts defaults true
and each Collection::new runs a fresh FcInitLoadConfig, so every cache paid the full scan
the field report's suggested shared-collection fix would NOT have removed it
CollectionOptions.shared governs clone visibility of REGISTERED fonts, not the system scan
the waste was the smaller half; on a host with no matching fonts the scan PANICS
fontique unwraps Err(NoMatch) in backend/fontconfig.rs:685 populating its generic-family map
so eager construction made a font-less host fatal to pinion's font-less backend
measured before the fix: 51 of pinion-tui's 136 unit tests died there
and hello-button-tui exited 101 having painted nothing but the alternate-screen preamble
font_scans() reports how many times a cache enumerated system fonts - a count, not a flag
because the invariant is at most once and a boolean cannot express that
a counterfactual proved it: rebuilding the context per shape passed every flag-based assertion
the public surface is unchanged; a caller that shapes pays the same cost at the same count

and paints a BYTE-IDENTICAL frame under the system's 635-font config - fonts change nothing

without that, every pass would be consistent with the zero-font config quietly finding fonts
CF1 eager construction: bites in all three crates
CF2 rebuild-per-shape: did NOT bite the flag-based tests, which is why font_scans is a count

Round 1451.decision_summary: R1451 - a column carries its width and its place wherever its header is dragged: Qt QHeaderView section state (order x size x visibility) keyed by LOGICAL section in one ColumnLayout, with the whole saveState/restoreState round-trip as typed readable data instead of an opaque QByteArray
changes_bullets: R1450's carry named it: section sizes stayed on the R785 width axis
and were not permuted, so moving a column left its width behind
the defect was a KEYING one - ColumnWidths indexes by SCREEN POSITION
while Qt keys sectionSize / isSectionHidden by the LOGICAL section
new pinion_core::widgets::column_layout::ColumnLayout composes three axes
an embedded ReorderModel owns the permutation (5th consumer)
a shared ColumnWidths owns the sizes, RE-KEYED to logical (3rd consumer)
a hidden flag vector is the one field this module adds
nothing is stored twice: visible_placements is the ONLY walk that applies
hiding and sums cumulative x, and every derived answer reads that walk
SectionPlacement carries (visual, logical, x, size) so a binding's header,
body, insertion line and a11y tree cannot compute four different offsets
hidden sections keep their visual index (Qt's rule), so showing one puts
it back where it was instead of appending it
adds Qt swapSections, logicalIndexAt, sectionPosition, hiddenSectionCount
ColumnLayoutState is saveState as typed data; restore_state is atomic:
length checks, then ReorderModel::set_order which is validate-then-apply,
so a rejected layout writes no size and no flag
composite_tag::parse_pair<A,B> lifted (R1449 debt 3) - the typed two-value
argument codec, now 7 consumers across core and two examples
hello-column-reorder migrated: it holds only the column names and the
keyboard policy now; everything a QHeaderView does is the substrate's
its sections are non-uniform, because on a uniform strip "the width
travelled with the column" and "the widths never moved" paint the same
keyboard gains [ / ] resize and h hide, and the cursor walks PAINTED
sections so it cannot land on one that is not there
hello-column-visibility audited and deliberately NOT migrated: identity
order plus an eager table that takes no per-column widths means the model
would carry two axes nothing reads; R990's stale "a 2nd consumer will lift
this" note is replaced with that finding

changes_bullets: pinion had exactly ONE column sizing policy anywhere: a stored number
so a column could not fill the viewport and could not fit its content,
because there was nowhere to say where a section's size comes from
new SectionResizeMode {Interactive, Fixed, Stretch, ResizeToContents}
per LOGICAL section, like the size it governs, so it travels on a move
the enum answers TWO questions because Qt answers them differently:
stores_size (stored vs derived) and user_resizable (may a GESTURE change

Stretch divides what the other sections LEAVE OVER, not the whole width,
and the remainder is dealt out one pixel each to the leading sections so
the row fills exactly what it was given and the result is deterministic
the division is over the PAINTED sections, so hiding one hands its share
to the others and a hidden Stretch section reports its stored size
ResizeToContents takes a consumer-supplied hint - Qt's own architecture,
where sectionSizeFromContents() asks the model/delegate for a sizeHint
resolution lives INSIDE visible_placements, R1451's single geometry walk,
so positions, the hit test, the strip total and the a11y tree follow the
new sizes with no second rule anywhere
state gains modes; an absent modes field decodes as all-Interactive so a
pre-R1452 snapshot still restores, but a PRESENT malformed one is an
error - a client that misspelled a mode has to be told
use_column_layout lifts the layout to an Owner::cache holder, because the
view fn publishes two inputs the External cannot know: the measured
content hints and the width a Stretch row divides
hello-column-reorder paints its grid in the measured monospace face, so

Round 1453.decision_summary: R1453 - a view function can ask how wide a string will be: QFontMetrics parity as a backend-neutral TextMetrics ProviderSlot, retiring the monospace-only measurement that forced R1452's content hint to be an upper bound
changes_bullets: a view fn could measure exactly ONE thing: the cell of a MONOSPACE face at
a size (MonospaceMetrics, R1003). A proportional face has no cell, so "how
wide is report.pdf in the grid's font" had no answer at all
R1452 worked around it by forcing the grid monospace and multiplying a
character count by the cell - an UPPER BOUND (CellMetric is whole pixels,
so it is the ceiling of the real advance), and only for text you were
willing to make monospace. This round retires both limits
I did NOT build the content-width harvest my own R1452 carry named. The
entry audit found its sink absent: every laid-out-rect feedback path in
the tree hangs off ScrollNode (measured_rows, set_measured_viewport), and
a ColumnLayout is not a scene node the layout pass can reach
and Qt does not solve it that way either - QAbstractItemDelegate::sizeHint
measures text with QFontMetrics, synchronously, in the delegate
new pinion_core::reactive::text_metrics: TextMetrics trait + TextExtent +
NullTextMetrics + the TEXT_METRICS ProviderSlot + measured_text_extent
takes the SAME TextStyle the caller is about to paint with, so the
measurement and the paint cannot disagree about face, size or family
max_width is the wrap bound (Qt boundingRect); None is horizontalAdvance
Inherited verdict, same reasoning as MONOSPACE_METRICS: a per-scope slot
would hand a secondary window a Null provider and every content-fitted
column there would silently fall back, no panic and no log
pinion_text::LayoutCacheTextMetrics is the parley-backed impl, kept
separate from the monospace provider because the two answer different
questions and a merged trait would force every consumer to take both
both axes round UP: a hint that rounded down would clip the last glyph
hello-column-reorder measures its cells in its OWN face again - the
monospace R1452 forced on it is gone - and the hint is now exact

Round 1454.decision_summary: R1454 - measure before deciding: instrument the shaper's miss count, measure the LRU cliff (18.5 us miss vs 118 ns hit, 5.6 ms per 300-string thrashing pass), and bound the per-frame working set with Qt's own QHeaderView::resizeContentsPrecision
changes_bullets: R1453 shipped an honest UNMEASURED carry: measuring every cell each frame
leans on the LayoutCache LRU and nothing had measured how that scales
so this round INSTRUMENTS, MEASURES, then acts on what the number says
LayoutCache::shapes() counts cache MISSES that actually ran the shaper -
a count, not a flag, for the reason R1447 replaced its own bool: the
question is "how many times THIS FRAME", and only a number answers it
measured, release, short labels: a shape MISS costs 18.5 us and a cache
HIT 118 ns - 157x. The cache holds 256 layouts
so a pass over 300 strings that exceeds it re-shapes the whole set every
time: 5.6 ms per frame, a third of a 60fps budget, forever; at 1000
strings the measurement alone is over budget
two tests pin the cliff rather than describing it: a warm set adds zero
shapes, and a set ONE larger than the cache re-shapes in full every pass
the act is Qt's own answer, not an invented one:
QHeaderView::resizeContentsPrecision bounds how many rows a content-fitted
column samples. ColumnLayout gains it with Qt's default of 1000, readable
and writable over the wire, and the consumer honours it
zero clamps to one: measuring nothing would leave a content-fitted column
with no content to fit, and a silently floor-sized column is not an answer
a caller can tell from a bug

sibling `focus_request` carries a LEVEL (final write is the intended
end state, so collapsing is lossless) while a `ModalRequest` carries a
STACK EDIT (push/pop), and `close` then `open` does not collapse to
`open`. The module had inherited its sibling's policy across that
boundary.
Both drain sites apply every queued request in order (§2 #6 GUI/TUI
mirror): `pinion_shell::ShellCore::drain_modal_request` and
`pinion_tui`'s. The focus-observer arc is snapshotted ONCE around the
whole batch, so a handoff reports the single transition the user can
perceive (menu row -> dialog button) and never announces the invoker
the pop transiently restored.
`hello-modal-handoff` (new binding) + `tools/demos/r1456_modal_handoff.py`
(46 assertions): a modal command menu whose destructive row closes
itself and opens a confirm dialog from ONE intent (Qt's menu action ->
QMessageBox::question). The safe row stays a one-request frame as the
regression witness.

gains `SurfaceAction` + `surface_action_scene` (filled-tonal M3
action button on a modal surface). hello-dialog + hello-drawer had
been byte-identical local wrappers since R703; hello-modal-handoff is
the third, so the opinion lands in the substrate and the three drop
their copies. hello-file-dialog / hello-snackbar / hello-undo keep
theirs — they are not this button.
10 example tests had arranged setup AFTER the flush drain, so the
setup's own request now survives into the assertion; the drain moved
below the setup in each. Meaning-preserving: the tests ask "what did
THIS action request".

Round 1457.decision_summary: the measured-tail-pin field report is answered by measurement: the same-frame re-pass already paints the pinned offset, and what remains are four other gaps, registered here
changes_bullets: No code change. This is a review + carry-registration round for the
consumer field report tide filed against R1445 (tide pin 94b7be5c):
"the pin lands, but the frame that would show it never comes".
The report asks WHERE to add "request one redraw when the pin actually
moved the offset". Measured answer: that is ALREADY R1445.
`apply_measured_tail_pins`' dirty bit folds into the frame dirty bit
(`pinion-runtime/src/layout.rs:477`) and the shell re-runs `V::view` +
the layout pass on it (`pinion-shell/src/substrate.rs:4041,4062`), so
the paint carries the pinned offset. `scene/screenshot` reaches the
same re-pass through `render_window` -> `compute_paint_scene_for_window`.
Both remedies the report sketched would have been insufficient AS
WRITTEN: a repaint alone cannot move the viewport, because the painted
offset is the COPY `ScrollNode::from_state` took at view-build time
(`pinion-core/src/scene.rs:2843`), read back by the paint adapter
(`paint_adapter.rs:225`). Only a view re-run moves it — and a second
layout pass does not, because layout is not what writes that field.
The full review is `claudedocs/pinion-review-measured-tail-pin-needs-a-
second-paint.md`. That path is gitignored, so THIS entry, not that
file, is the registration; the substance is repeated here on purpose.
verification_bullets: Substrate probe — written, run once, then REMOVED (no test landed, and
the tree it ran in belonged to another session's round). tide's shape
rebuilt with fixed-height rows so no host font is asserted: a header
row, a `flex_basis:0 / flex_grow:1 / min_size:0` Scroll, and the
conditional "more below" row OUTSIDE the scroll (the row that changes
the viewport height, hence `max`).
Result: after `follow_measured_tail()` the FIRST `compute_paint_scene`
already painted `ScrollNode.offset_y = 300 == max`; the second paint
was identical. Non-vacuous: the pre-pin value is 0, so the defect as
reported would have shown `first=0`. Probe source is kept in the
review doc's appendix.
Store-only round: no `.rs` changed, so no clippy / test / demo claim is
made here. `validate-workspace` before and after: T1 orphan total=0,
T3 reject=0, atomic orphan_refs 5+0 unchanged.
NOT measured, stated so it is not read as proven: the tide binary was
never run from this session, and the present-stage capture path
(`VelloRenderer::capture_rgba8`) was READ, not measured. The capture
hypothesis inside D3 below is a hypothesis, not a finding.
carry_forward_bullets: D1 — the same-frame settle is ONE step. `if scroll_dirty { … }` re-runs
view + layout once and DISCARDS that second pass's dirty bit (`let _`)
in `pinion-shell/src/substrate.rs:4062`, mirrored in the RPC producer
at `:5415`. A consumer whose view depends on offset/max can need two
settle steps (tide paints a "more below" row OUTSIDE the scroll, which
moves the viewport height and therefore `max = content - viewport`);
the intermediate state is what gets painted. Code-read, unmeasured.
D2 — `ScrollState::set_max` clamps the offset when the bound shrinks
but deliberately EXCLUDES that clamp from its dirty bit
(`pinion-core/src/widgets/scroll.rs:267-272, 282-301`). Combined with
D1, a frame can paint the pre-clamp offset. Whoever takes D1/D2: the
regression test must FAIL before the fix and must assert CONVERGENCE
(two consecutive dirty-free passes), not an arbitrary pass budget; a
scene that will not converge must fail loud, never truncate silently —
"stop after one step without saying so" is the defect being repaired.
D3 — what the report's §1 actually measured is still OPEN. The
decisive reading is `scene/scroll_state` (offset / max /
following_measured_tail) taken BEFORE the first `scene/screenshot`:
`offset == max` there means the state was already pinned and the lag
lives in the capture / present path, not in the pin. Asked of tide;
external dependency until they answer.
D4 — doc gap that caused the wrong remedy to be proposed:
`follow_measured_tail` / `apply_measured_tail_pin` speak of "the paint"
without saying the node carries a VIEW-TIME COPY of the offset, so a
careful consumer concludes "repaint once" is the fix. A doc round
should state the copy at the seam the consumer reads.

there. The "in-progress R1455 module" that briefly appeared in
`crates/pinion-shell/src/substrate.rs` was this review's probe, added
and removed from a mnemosyne session; no concurrent R1455 round

Round 1458.decision_summary: a frame runs to a fixed point before it is painted, and a tail pin rides the bound it settled on
changes_bullets: R1457 registered two debts from the tide measured-tail-pin field report as
code-read and unmeasured (D1 one-step settle, D2 silent clamp). Both are now
measured: D1 is real, D2 is refuted.
MEASURED, the number R1457 could not produce: a windowed transcript arms
`follow_measured_tail` and the pin lands 683px SHORT of the tail (2530 asked,
1847 reached) — the same shape as the report's 543/693. The cause is not the
paint. A windowed list only lays out the rows it materialized, so the harvest
measures only those, and the bound the FIRST pass publishes still counts the
un-materialized tail at its estimate. Spending a one-shot arming there froze
the viewport on a provisional bound with nothing left armed to finish the trip.
`pinion_core::widgets::scroll::ScrollState::apply_measured_tail_pin`: the
arming now survives any pass whose pin still MOVED the offset, and is spent by
the first pass with nothing left to move. That is the same fixed point the
caller already iterates to, so it costs no extra pass; one-shot is unchanged in
the sense that matters (a reader who scrolls away after it clears is never
pulled back).
`pinion_runtime::SETTLE_PASS_BUDGET` (4) is one home for both backends.
`pinion-shell`'s window paint + RPC producer and `pinion-tui`'s paint (§2 #6)
replace their hand-rolled single re-pass — whose own dirty bit was DISCARDED —
with a loop to that fixed point. The shell folds the R1012 pane-viewport
publish into the same loop, so one condition means the whole frame settled.
Over budget is never silent: `ShellCore::report_unsettled_frame` logs the
binding bug and requests the frame that continues, instead of leaving a
half-settled picture under `ControlFlow::Wait`. The TUI carries the loop but no
warning, and says why: its diagnostic channel is `log_sink`, which needs `&mut
self`, while `compute_paint_scene` is `&self` by ratified contract.
D2 REFUTED with a test rather than prose
(`r1458_a_shrinking_bound_cannot_clamp_without_reporting_dirt`): every offset
writer clamps against the live bound, so `offset <= max` holds between calls,
and `set_max`'s excluded clamp can only fire when the same call lowered the
bound — which the dirty bit reports. The exclusion is real but unreachable on
its own.
D4 doc gap closed at the seam that produced the report's wrong remedy:
`apply_measured_tail_pin` now states that `ScrollNode::from_state` copies the
offset at VIEW-BUILD time, so repainting reproduces the same picture and only a
view re-run moves the viewport.
`examples/hello-tail-reveal` (new binding) + `tools/demos/r1458_tail_reveal.py`:
hello-transcript's policy on a virtualized list. 60 seeded entries, most never
laid out, so `is_fully_measured` is False at boot — the precondition is asserted
FIRST, because without it the demo would pass on the broken build too.
verification_bullets: Counterfactuals run ONE AT A TIME, each landing on a different half of the fix.
CF-A (arming consumed on the first pass, the pre-R1458 line): the demo FAILS
"reply 1: the viewport sits at the bound: expected 2530, got 1847". CF-1 (shell
loop capped at the old 2 passes): `the_painted_frame_is_the_one_the_chain_settled_on`
FAILS 200 vs 300 while the steady-state control still passes. CF-3 (catch-up
redraw removed): `a_frame_that_cannot_settle_is_bounded_and_asks_for_another`
FAILS on the redraw assert alone.
HONEST COVERAGE SPLIT, stated in the demo's own docstring: capping the RPC
producer's budget leaves `r1458_tail_reveal` green, because every RPC call
incidentally runs a layout pass and the state converges between requests. The
demo pins the arming half; the settle half is pinned by
`crates/pinion-shell/tests/frame_settles_before_paint.rs`, which can observe one
paint's own passes.
Gates: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D pedantic` and `cargo doc
--document-private-items` clean on pinion-core / -runtime / -shell / -tui /
-rpc / hello-tail-reveal. Tests green: core 2734 (+1), runtime 459 (+1), shell
558 (+3). Demo regression on FRESHLY BUILT binaries: the new r1458 demo, plus
r1445_transcript and r1194_measured_list (the two closest incumbents), plus 130
scroll / list / grid / dock / pane demos.
NOT a pass, recorded so it is not read as one: `hello_listbox_scroll_to.py`
failed once inside a back-to-back sweep with "vello error: Couldn't find
suitable device". It then passed 3/3 standalone on this tree AND 3/3 on the
stashed (unpatched) tree, so it is device acquisition under sweep load rather
than a regression — but it was observed, and is not being called green.
carry_forward_bullets: D3 stays OPEN and external: what the report's §1 frame hashes measured is still
unconfirmed for tide's own binary. The decisive reading remains
`scene/scroll_state` taken BEFORE the first `scene/screenshot` — `offset == max`
there means the state was already pinned. This round explains a 543/693-shaped
shortfall (a provisional bound) but does not prove that is what tide hit; their
transcript may not be windowed at all.
`SETTLE_PASS_BUDGET` is 4 because every settling chain known here is at most 3
(the bound, the pane rect, then the pass a refined tail pin brings new rows
into). That is a survey of the chains that exist today, not a proof that none is
longer. A binding that trips `report_unsettled_frame` should be read as evidence
about the budget, not only about the binding.
The pane-viewport publish now runs on every settle pass rather than once per
paint. It is idempotent by Signal equality-skip and 49 dock / pane demos are
green, but a pane Effect with a non-idempotent side effect (a PTY winsize ioctl)
would now observe intermediate rects. No such consumer exists in-tree; sprag is
the one that would.

failed once inside a back-to-back sweep with "vello error: Couldn't find

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: D3 stays OPEN and external: what the report's §1 frame hashes measured is still
unconfirmed for tide's own binary. The decisive reading remains
`scene/scroll_state` taken BEFORE the first `scene/screenshot` — `offset == max`
there means the state was already pinned. This round explains a 543/693-shaped
shortfall (a provisional bound) but does not prove that is what tide hit; their
transcript may not be windowed at all.
`SETTLE_PASS_BUDGET` is 4 because every settling chain known here is at most 3
(the bound, the pane rect, then the pass a refined tail pin brings new rows
into). That is a survey of the chains that exist today, not a proof that none is
longer. A binding that trips `report_unsettled_frame` should be read as evidence
about the budget, not only about the binding.
The pane-viewport publish now runs on every settle pass rather than once per
paint. It is idempotent by Signal equality-skip and 49 dock / pane demos are
green, but a pane Effect with a non-idempotent side effect (a PTY winsize ioctl)
would now observe intermediate rects. No such consumer exists in-tree; sprag is
the one that would.

Round 1459.decision_summary: a frame reports the work it did, not only how long it took: settle passes, whether it settled, and shaper misses
changes_bullets: R1458 left two claims about its own settle loop unmeasured, and R1454 left a
bound that nothing enforced. Both are the same shape of gap: the frame's cost
was measured in microseconds and never in units. `scene/frame_timings` has
carried seven durations since R907 and not one count.
`pinion_runtime::FrameTiming` gains `settle_passes` (view + layout passes this
paint spent), `settled` (did it reach the fixed point, or spend the budget and
give up) and `shape_misses` (text runs handed to the shaper). All three ride
the existing `scene/frame_timings` wire, so a §2 #2 agent reads them where it
already reads the durations.
Why counts and not more durations: `build_us` is the WHOLE settle loop (R1458),
so a 4ms frame that ran one heavy pass and a 4ms frame whose four cheap passes
disagree are the same number and want opposite fixes. This is R1454's own
lesson ("the question is 'how many this frame', so only a number answers")
applied one level up.
`settled` is a bool beside the count, not a value encoded into it: a frame that
converges exactly ON the budget and one that gave up report the same
`settle_passes`, so the count alone cannot tell an agent whether the picture in
front of the user is finished. The only other record of that is R1458's
`tracing::warn!`, which no RPC client can read.
`FrameTiming::with_work` is a builder, not three more parameters on `new`: that
constructor already takes five positional `u64` durations. The three work
fields have three distinct types (`u32` / `bool` / `u64`), so a transposed call
site does not compile.
R1454 carry CLEARED: `LayoutCache::shapes()` (R1454) had zero callers outside
its own tests — the per-frame hook its doc promised ("a profiler can sample it
per frame") was never built. `shape_misses` is that hook. It is a per-paint
DELTA, not the cache's lifetime total: the cache is shared across windows, so
only a delta is attributable to one window's frame.
R1458 carry (c) CLEARED BY MEASUREMENT, not by argument
(`the_pane_publish_lands_on_the_settled_rect_and_says_what_it_did_on_the_way`):
folding the R1012 pane publish into the settle loop DOES let a pane consumer
observe intermediate rects — the "idempotent by Signal equality-skip" claim
covered a republish of the same rect and said nothing about a rect that
genuinely differs between passes. The guarantee that makes it safe, now pinned:
the loop's final pass is a publish, so the LAST value a pane sees is always the
settled scene's rect.
`ShellCore::record_paint_work` folds the work publish and the unsettled report
into one call — they are the same fact read twice (the count an agent reads,
the redraw the user needs), and splitting them is how one gets forgotten at a
future call site.
verification_bullets: The discriminating measurement, two bindings on one wire: `hello-tail-reveal`
(static text) reads EXACTLY 0 shaper misses and 1 settle pass on every idle
repaint, while `hello-frame-profiler` — a HUD whose labels ARE the timings —
reads 3-4 misses on EVERY idle frame, forever. Same shell, same wire; only the
content differs, and until this round nothing could tell you so.
Counterfactuals ONE AT A TIME. CF-A (`shape_misses` reports the cache's
lifetime total instead of the per-paint delta): demo FAILS "static: idle 1
handed the shaper nothing: expected 0, got 21". CF-B (`settle_passes` hard-wired
to 1): the three shell unit tests FAIL (1 vs 4) — and the DEMO PASSED, which is
the finding below.
CF-B EXPOSED A GAP IN MY OWN ASSERTION SET and it was fixed, not excused: the
demo's `settle_passes` assertions were `>= 1`, `<= budget` and `== 1` on idle
frames, every one of which a constant 1 satisfies. Added the cold-start claim
`boot settle_passes > 1` (a first paint re-passes by construction: the layout
writes a scroll bound the view had not read). CF-B then FAILS the demo too.
This is the R1447 rule — if a counterfactual passes every assert, the
assertions are the wrong shape.
The cold-start claim asserts its own PRECONDITION (`frame_count == 1`) rather
than assuming it, so a run where the boot frame has already scrolled past fails
loudly instead of quietly describing some later frame.

carry_forward_bullets: The TUI records no frame timings at all, so its settle loop's passes and its
shaping are unmeasured. `FrameTiming` is shell-recorded (the surface owns the

which no consumer has asked for yet.
`settle_passes` counts the WINDOW PAINT's loop only. The RPC producer runs its
own settle loop (producer parity) and deliberately records nothing, so an
introspection read never manufactures a frame the user never saw — but it also
means work done inside an RPC dispatch is invisible to this wire. That is why
r1458_tail_reveal's append frame reads 1 pass / 0 misses: the click drain's
produce already did the work.
`shape_misses` is a count, and R1454's 18.5us-per-miss is "this machine, this
face". Multiplying them gives a local estimate, not a portable budget. Nothing
in-tree does that multiplication, and no assertion here depends on it.
R1458 carry (b) is now OBSERVABLE but still not PROVEN: `SETTLE_PASS_BUDGET = 4`
remains a survey of the chains that exist. What changed is that a binding
sitting at the budget is now data (`settle_passes == 4 && !settled`) instead of
a log line — so the next evidence about the budget will arrive as a number.
R1458 carry (a) — D3, what tide's frame hashes actually measured — is still
open and still external.

Round 1460.decision_summary: the four R1459 carries are cleared: the TUI records frames, the RPC producer's work is on the wire, and the two remaining ones are decisions, not debts
changes_bullets: R1459 closed with four honest carries. This round clears all four — two by
building the missing thing, two by making the decision the carry was standing
in for. None is deferred.
(a) BUILT — the TUI records frames. Pre-R1460 `scene/frame_timings` existed on
the wire and every `pinion-tui` binding answered `FrameTimingsUnavailable`
forever, which an agent reads as "has not painted yet" rather than "this
backend does not measure": a missing §2 #6 mirror, not a declined one. The
producer measures build + work into a `PendingFrame` (`Cell`, because
`compute_paint_scene` is `&self` by ratified contract) and the `&mut self`
commit hook closes the total span and records. GPU phases read `0`, which is
the honest shape of a terminal frame rather than a gap.
(a.1) `instant_delta_us` lifted from `pinion-shell` into `pinion_runtime::
frame_timing` on its second consumer: two backends rounding the same quantity
their own way is the divergence class, and a sample is comparable across
backends only if the lowering is one function.
(a.2) Found while wiring it — the TUI's RPC scene producer ran exactly ONE
layout pass while its paint (R1458) runs a settle loop, so a TUI
`scene/snapshot` could report a scene the TUI's own paint would never show.
That is the §2 #6 divergence relocated onto the AI path, which is what R1344
built the producer to prevent. It now runs the same loop.
(b) BUILT — `FrameTimingsSnapshot` gains `produce_passes_total` /
`produce_shape_misses_total`, published as the wire's `produce` section. The
scene producer settles exactly as a paint does but records no frame (an
introspection read must never manufacture a picture the user never saw), and
that correct contract left the §2 #2 primary path unable to price its own
calls. Cumulative, never folded into the ring: a produce is not a frame.
(c) DECIDED, at the seam — `shape_misses`' doc now states the policy instead of
leaving it as a note: the COUNT is portable and pinion publishes it; the COST
is not and pinion refuses to. R1454's 18.5us was one machine and one face and
is recorded there as a bound's rationale, not as an API constant. A consumer
needing microseconds measures them on its own host.
(d) DECIDED, at the seam — `SETTLE_PASS_BUDGET`'s doc now says why the "survey,
not a proof" debt cannot be paid: a chain's length is a property of the
BINDING's view-to-layout feedback, which pinion does not author and cannot
bound, so any number here is a policy about when to stop and never a theorem.
What is achievable is that overrunning it is bounded, loud, and DATA
(`settle_passes` + `settled`) — so the next evidence about this constant
arrives as a number from a real binding.
verification_bullets: The TUI mirror is pinned by `r1460_the_tui_records_frames_and_answers_frame_timings`:
nothing before the first paint, exactly one sample after one produce+commit,
work counts present, GPU phases zero, `total >= build`. Its last assertion is
the one that matters for a `Cell` hand-off — a second commit with no produce in
between records NOTHING, because the slot is taken and not cloned, so a frame
cannot be counted twice.
The producer wire is pinned by `r1460_producer_work_is_reported_and_is_not_frames`:
the totals reach the wire, and `frame_count` stays at one FRAME whatever the
producer did. A frame count and a produce count must never be the same number.
`tools/demos/r1460_frame_work.py` (was r1459) gains section (C), and its
CONTROL is the load-bearing half: a `scene/snapshot from: paint` moves NEITHER
counter, because it serializes the stored last-painted scene rather than
producing one. Without that control, "produce work" would mean "any RPC
traffic".
That control exists because the first draft was WRONG and measurement said so:
it asserted a snapshot advances the produce total, and the run reported
`0 -> 0`. Probing found snapshot produces nothing and `scene/click` produces
one pass. The demo was rewritten onto what was measured — and the same probe
retired a suspicion about `compute_paint_scene_pure_internal` running a single
pass, since its real call sites are the post-dispatch finalize and window
restore, exactly where its doc's "runs after the canonical paint" rationale
holds.
Gates: fmt / clippy `-D pedantic` / `cargo doc --document-private-items` clean;
23 test binaries green (core 2734, rpc 941, shell 558 + 7 integration, tui 187).
Demos on freshly built binaries: r1460 (3/3 stable) plus r907 / r925 / r1374 /
r1389 / r1458 / r1445 / r1194, and 9 of the tui/listbox/scroll family.
Clippy rejected the `Cell<Option<(Instant, u64, u32, bool, u64)>>` tuple and was
right for the reason `FrameTiming::with_work` documents — five positional
fields, three of them integers, is a transposition that compiles. It is now a
named `PendingFrame`.
NOT A PASS, and NOT this round's doing: `tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py`
fails its own premise control ("the parley path cannot run font-less"). Verified
PRE-EXISTING by stashing this round's entire diff and re-running on the clean
tree, where it fails identically. R1448 taught pinion to open a window without
fonts, which appears to have invalidated that negative control — but deciding
what the control should be now belongs to whoever owns that claim, not to a
silent edit here.

Round 1461.decision_summary: a red demo is root-caused, not reported: R1448 invalidated r1447's control on purpose, so the control is replaced with one that measures the same fact positively
changes_bullets: A demo that was already failing before this session is root-caused and fixed,
rather than reported as a discovery. `tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py` failed
its own premise control — "the parley path cannot run font-less" — and was
verified PRE-EXISTING by stashing the entire R1460 diff and re-running on the
clean tree, where it failed identically.
ROOT CAUSE: R1448 invalidated that control ON PURPOSE. Its whole point was "a
window opens on a host with no fonts", so the parley failure the control
required stopped happening, and the demo has been asserting pre-R1448 behaviour
ever since. Nothing caught it because the demo sweep does not gate a push.
Fixed by measuring the same fact POSITIVELY through R1448's own typed status
instead of weakening the control: with no fonts reachable,
`LayoutCache::probe_system_fonts()` must answer `SystemFontStatus::Unavailable`
(`r1460_a_zero_font_config_is_font_less_from_inside_the_process`).
`#[ignore]`d, because it asserts a property of the HOST rather than of the code:
on a normal machine (and in CI) fonts exist and the honest answer is
`Available`, so as a plain test it is exactly the host-dependent assertion R1453
calls a flake. The demo runs it with `--ignored` under its own font-less config,
which is where the claim is true and is that test's real coverage.
The measure-arm comparison the control had been built on stays in the demo on
its own terms — it is a claim about the two ARMS, checked under system fonts
where it is true, instead of being pressed into service as a font-environment
detector.

Round 1462.decision_summary: A modal that closes hands focus to the tag its binding named, not to the invoker the substrate remembered: the dispatch tail applies automatic modal policy first and explicit focus intent last, reporting one observable transition.
changes_bullets: `ShellCore::handle_tail` and its terminal mirror now resolve focus at ONE point (`drain_focus_mailboxes`), draining the modal-scope mailbox and the focus-request mailbox together and applying the modal batch BEFORE the request: automatic policy lands first, explicit intent overrides it. Reported live from a downstream consumer (PINION-PR78) — a command-palette row that closes the palette and names where focus belongs always lost to `pop_modal_scope`'s unconditional invoker-restore, landing on the stale invoker or, when the command had removed that node, on `None` (no keyboard focus anywhere).

`drain_modal_request` / `drain_focus_request` became arc-free appliers (`apply_modal_requests` / `apply_focus_request`); the observer arc and the redraw gate moved up to the shared drain. R1456's one-arc rule now spans BOTH mailboxes: the invoker the pop transiently restores is never announced, because applying policy before intent is exactly what creates that transient. The redraw/revision gate widened from "focus moved" to "focus moved OR the modal stack was edited", so a frame that only changes modal depth still schedules a paint.

The field report's own compatibility table was corrected: "open + request on a member is refused today" is false. The R1020 re-derive-on-miss could let that request SUCCEED while the trap was still down, after which `push_modal_scope` snapshotted the dialog's own control as the invoker — so closing the dialog restored focus to a node the dialog took with it. Worse than a refusal, and now covered.

`ModalTailFixture` + `FocusArcRecorder` lifted to `pinion-core::test_fixtures` (a11y / shell / tui impls alongside), so both backends drive the SAME binding. Closes R1456 debt (1): the terminal `drain_modal_request` had ZERO tests; it now has 7, four of them R1456 handoff parity.

New forcing consumer `examples/hello-modal-refocus` + `tools/demos/r1462_modal_refocus.py`: a palette with two rows chosen so the invoker survives one and dies in the other, driving both branches of the report's table over RPC.

verification_bullets: `cargo fmt --all --check` / `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` / `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`: 0 findings.
