Round 1463.decision_summary: A focus request reaches the node a dispatch made paintable in ANY window the binding paints: the R1020 re-derive spans every painted window and folds once, so the same reducer behaves the same in a torn-off pane as in the primary.
changes_bullets: `ShellCore::refresh_focusable_from_view` — the R1020 retry that makes "focus a widget on the frame it appears" work — now re-derives EVERY window the binding has painted, not only `DEFAULT_WINDOW`. A painted window short-circuits `window_focusables` to its harvested cache, so re-deriving the primary alone left a secondary window's enumeration frozen at its last paint: the identical reducer (open an inline editor, name it) landed in the primary and was silently dropped in a torn-off pane, its one-shot `focus_request` consumed by the miss.

The entry audit REFUTED the reason R1462 recorded for this carry. "A brand-new window has never painted so it contributes no tags" is false: R26's `union_focusable_tags` folds declared-but-unpainted windows by deriving them from `view_for_window`, and two tests already pin it. The real gap was the inverse — a window that HAS painted answers from a cache the dispatch just invalidated, and only the primary's cache was being refreshed.

Two extractions with two callers each: `refold_focusables` (the fold + stale-focus-drop + redraw tail of `refresh_window_focusables`) and `derive_window_focusables` (the cache-ignoring half of `window_focusables`). The refresh rewrites every painted window's contribution and folds ONCE — folding per window would hand `update_focusable_tags` an intermediate union in which a pane moving between windows is in neither, dropping a focus that never left the binding.

A counterfactual killed an arm this round had written: "the primary is always re-derived, painted or not, because the boot seed runs before any paint" passed the whole suite when removed, because `union_focusable_tags` always folds the primary and derives it when uncached. The arm was redundant and its doc claim was false; both are gone.

§2 #6 — the terminal mirror needs no equivalent arm and says so: a TUI process owns one alternate screen, so `V::view` IS its whole enumeration. The divergence is in the backends' window models, not in the focus contract.

New forcing consumer `examples/hello-window-refocus` + `tools/demos/r1463_window_refocus.py`: two OS windows, both triggers in the primary, so the two branches share one input path and differ only in which window paints the node the reducer names.
verification_bullets: Measured before fixing: the discriminating pair was written first and the secondary-window half FAILED with `focused: None` while the primary control PASSED — same fixture, same dispatch shape, different window.

`cargo fmt --all --check` / `cargo clippy -p pinion-shell -p pinion-tui -p hello-window-refocus --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` / `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`: 0 findings.

Tests on every touched crate: pinion-shell 196 lib (+3) + 159 dispatch-core + the rest of its integration suites, pinion-tui 145 lib + 19 (doc-only change), hello-window-refocus 4 new. The 3 new shell tests join `r26_undock_focus_follow_tests`, whose 4 pre-existing R25.1/R26 witnesses stay green.

Counterfactuals, applied ONE AT A TIME. CF-1 (primary-only re-derive, the pre-R1463 body): 2 shell tests FAIL — both about the secondary window — while the primary control and all four R26 witnesses PASS; 2 example tests FAIL; the demo FAILS at section (E) with "focus is still on the trigger", the reported symptom. CF-2 (fold per window instead of once): exactly 1 shell test FAILS, `a_pane_moving_between_windows_keeps_its_focus_across_the_refresh`, with `focused: None` — a different half of the fix, and every other assertion passes.

CF-3 (drop the always-refresh-the-primary arm) PASSED all 196 tests. That is recorded as a finding, not waved through: an arm no assertion can see is either untested or unnecessary, and here it was unnecessary. It was deleted rather than propped up with a test written to justify it.

The demo asserts its own premise instead of assuming it: `scene/frame_timings {window: "notes"}` answering (it raises `FrameTimingsUnavailable` until a window paints) is what establishes that the secondary's enumeration is a CACHE. A `{window}`-scoped snapshot cannot establish it — that path re-runs the view and deliberately does not enumerate.

Neighbouring demos on the same focus / multi-window paths, all PASS: r1462_modal_refocus, r1419_window_focus_multi, r1145_undock_tab, r1410_floating_chart, r1327_focused_pane_window_title, r1010_focus_ring.
`validate-workspace`: T1=0, 0 unscanned, 0 stale exclusions.
carry_forward_bullets: Still NOT verified from here: the downstream consumer's live symptom. This round proves the painted-secondary gap in-tree and closes it, and it refutes R1462's stated reason for the carry, but the consumer's own binding was never run — whether their first-pane case is this gap, the declared-but-unpainted path R26 already covers, or a third thing remains theirs to measure.

The cost claim is bounded but unmeasured: one extra view run per PAINTED window, on a focus MISS only. No test or assertion counts view runs, so a future round that makes the re-derive expensive would not be caught by this suite. `LayoutCache::shapes()` (R1454) is the neighbouring counter that could turn it into data.

`use_viewport_size` stays primary-gated, so a secondary window's derivation reads the PRIMARY window's size. A binding that gates focusable nodes on the window size (rather than the per-window pane viewport, which R1021 publishes correctly) derives the wrong set until that window repaints. Pre-existing, documented on `window_focusables` since R26, and not narrowed here.

The derivation order is sorted for reproducibility only. Fold-once makes the order irrelevant to the RESULT, which is why no test pins it — stated so a later round does not read the sort as load-bearing.

Consumer half: scene/click and scene/hover with {path} resolve through the producer, so a path click on a chromed window landed one strip-height high — on the chrome itself for anything in the top rows.

Round 1472.decision_summary: A failed gate must say why it failed: the demo sweep's first CI run in ~100 pushes killed one demo at its 180s budget and reported not one byte of why, so the runner no longer buffers a demo it may kill, names a timeout as a timeout, and the job pre-builds the debug test binaries the one cargo-test demo was compiling inside its own timeout.

tools/sweep_headless.sh: an empty diagnostic is stated as such instead of printing an empty block, so "no output" can never again read as "output lost"
tools/sweep_headless.sh: the budget is one named variable used by both the kill and the message that reports it; a counterfactual caught them disagreeing while this round was being written
.github/workflows/ci.yml: the demo-sweep job pre-builds the debug test binaries (cargo test --workspace --no-run) before running the sweep
.github/workflows/ci.yml: CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 is set at JOB level so the pre-build and the demo's own cargo test share one fingerprint, and for the disk headroom R897.1 needed
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py: records the measurement — 3.63s with the test binaries present, 89.85s without — so the next reader does not re-derive why the job builds them
NO per-demo timeout override: it was written, then deleted when the measurement refuted the premise it was built on
verification_bullets: SCOPE, measured from CI: the first run of demo-sweep in ~100 pushes (R1470 + R1471 unblocked the job it needs) reported 446 PASS / 1 FAIL of 447. The feared backlog of rotted demos did not exist; the single failure is r1447_font_free_tui.py

THE INVISIBILITY, root-caused by reproduction not inference: `out="$(timeout 2 python3 -c 'print(..); sleep(30)')"` captures 0 bytes; the same call with `python3 -u` captures all of it. `timeout` kills the child and Python's block-buffered pipe dies unflushed — which is why CI printed a bare `|` under its only failure
THE FAILURE ITSELF, from the log timestamps: 08:30:11.7168 -> 08:33:11.7268 = 180.010s. Killed by the budget, not by an assertion. Nothing in the job said so

THE CAUSE, measured and it refuted the obvious fix: the demo runs in 3.63s when the debug test binaries exist and 89.85s when it must build them (it is the only one of 447 demos that shells out to `cargo test`; verified by grep). The budget was never too small — the job made one demo compile the workspace inside it

CF on the harness (budget forced to 1s, real sweep, real demo): reports `TIMEOUT (killed at 180s)` and prints 4 lines of demo output where CI had shown none. Restored, and the same demo then PASSes through the harness
CF that caught my own defect: that run showed the message announcing 180s while the kill used 1s — two copies of one number. Now one variable feeds both

PROFILE FINGERPRINT, measured because getting it wrong would have looked fixed while changing nothing: `cargo test -p pinion-text-unicode --lib --no-run` is cached at 0.41s, and the same command with CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 recompiles (24.34s) into a different binary hash. Setting that env on the pre-build step alone would have made the demo rebuild the workspace inside its timeout again
gate: bash -n clean, shellcheck clean, the workflow parses as YAML with the new step in order, and r1447_font_free_tui.py PASSes through the real harness (89.85s cold, 3.63s warm)

tools/sweep_headless.sh: a killed demo is reported as TIMEOUT (killed at Ns) rather than a bare FAIL, and the failure list tags it (timeout); an assertion failure now prints its exit code
tools/sweep_headless.sh: an empty diagnostic is stated as such instead of printing an empty block, so "no output" can never again read as "output lost"
tools/sweep_headless.sh: the budget is one named variable used by both the kill and the message that reports it; a counterfactual caught them disagreeing while this round was being written
.github/workflows/ci.yml: the demo-sweep job pre-builds the debug test binaries (cargo test --workspace --no-run) before running the sweep
.github/workflows/ci.yml: CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 is set at JOB level so the pre-build and the demo's own cargo test share one fingerprint, and for the disk headroom R897.1 needed
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py: records the measurement — 3.63s with the test binaries present, 89.85s without — so the next reader does not re-derive why the job builds them
NO per-demo timeout override: it was written, then deleted when the measurement refuted the premise it was built on
publishable_verification_bullets: SCOPE, measured from CI: the first run of demo-sweep in ~100 pushes (R1470 + R1471 unblocked the job it needs) reported 446 PASS / 1 FAIL of 447. The feared backlog of rotted demos did not exist; the single failure is r1447_font_free_tui.py

THE INVISIBILITY, root-caused by reproduction not inference: `out="$(timeout 2 python3 -c 'print(..); sleep(30)')"` captures 0 bytes; the same call with `python3 -u` captures all of it. `timeout` kills the child and Python's block-buffered pipe dies unflushed — which is why CI printed a bare `|` under its only failure
THE FAILURE ITSELF, from the log timestamps: 08:30:11.7168 -> 08:33:11.7268 = 180.010s. Killed by the budget, not by an assertion. Nothing in the job said so

THE CAUSE, measured and it refuted the obvious fix: the demo runs in 3.63s when the debug test binaries exist and 89.85s when it must build them (it is the only one of 447 demos that shells out to `cargo test`; verified by grep). The budget was never too small — the job made one demo compile the workspace inside it

CF on the harness (budget forced to 1s, real sweep, real demo): reports `TIMEOUT (killed at 180s)` and prints 4 lines of demo output where CI had shown none. Restored, and the same demo then PASSes through the harness
CF that caught my own defect: that run showed the message announcing 180s while the kill used 1s — two copies of one number. Now one variable feeds both

PROFILE FINGERPRINT, measured because getting it wrong would have looked fixed while changing nothing: `cargo test -p pinion-text-unicode --lib --no-run` is cached at 0.41s, and the same command with CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 recompiles (24.34s) into a different binary hash. Setting that env on the pre-build step alone would have made the demo rebuild the workspace inside its timeout again
gate: bash -n clean, shellcheck clean, the workflow parses as YAML with the new step in order, and r1447_font_free_tui.py PASSes through the real harness (89.85s cold, 3.63s warm)

NOT verified here, and it cannot be locally: that the pre-build makes the CI run fit. The demo needs ~4s of its own work against a 180s budget, so the margin is large, but the number that matters comes from the next CI run
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: The five live-pixel / native-drag demos (r706 r707 r786 r794 r787) still SKIP their pixel phase in CI because python3-pil is deliberately not installed (R1333). The sweep now says so in its summary, so the gap is honest rather than hidden, but the coverage is still vacuous and arming it needs those demos hardened first
Whether the pre-build actually lands r1447 inside the budget on a 2-core runner is unmeasured until the next CI run. If it does not, the fix to reach for is the demo's own work, not a larger number

No other demo shells out to `cargo test` today (grep over all 447). Nothing enforces that, so a future demo could reintroduce the same shape; the pre-build now covers it either way, which is why no per-demo budget mechanism was added
The sweep is still not a pre-push gate — the long-standing carry. This round makes its failures legible, which is a prerequisite for gating on it, not a substitute

Round 1473.decision_summary: An application's declared face is what unset text uses: pinion had Qt's addApplicationFont and not its setFont, so hello-vn-tide held a Hangul face in memory while drawing tofu on any host without CJK — LayoutCache now resolves an unset family against a boot-declared default, and the binding declares one.
changes_bullets: pinion-text: LayoutCache::set_default_font_family / default_font_family — the family an unset TextStyle::font_family resolves to (Qt's QApplication::setFont)
pinion-text: the resolution happens at the ONE site that lowers a style to parley properties, so it reaches the base style and every StyleRun alike

pinion-text: setting a DIFFERENT default clears the shape cache, because entries are keyed on the style as written and cannot tell which default shaped them; register_font_data stays non-clearing since registration is purely additive
pinion-core: FontSourceReport gains default_family, so a scene node reporting `font_family: null` has somewhere to say what null renders as
pinion-shell: ShellConfig::with_default_font_family, threaded through new_with_fonts into the same text_cache the layout and paint passes borrow
pinion-narrative: the dialogue line row carries a `vn.line` tag, so an agent can address the prose whose folding is the claim
pinion-narrative: the R1345 flow test measures Korean again, declaring the vendored face the way the binding does — R1471 had to write it in ASCII
examples/hello-vn-tide: declares the repo's NanumGothic and makes it the default, publishes its font state as a tagged row, and its opening narration is long enough to fold
tools/rpc_verify.py: write_fontconfig lifted at its third copy (r1447 / r1448 / r1473 each wrote the same XML over the same two directories)
verification_bullets: THE GAP, read off the code not guessed: pinion had addApplicationFont (R1448) and nothing for QApplication::setFont. cache.rs pushes no FontFamily property when style.font_family is None, so unset meant the platform stack and a shipped face was reachable only by naming it — which vn_scene never did, on any of its all-Korean rows
PREMISE measured with fc-query: the repo's vendored NanumGothic covers ac00-d7a3, so naming it is enough to shape Hangul; no new font is vendored

THE ENVIRONMENT built to match CI, not to be convenient: a fontconfig over a directory holding one Latin-only face. fc-list ':charset=ac00' counts 0 there and 85 on this host. Deliberately NOT a font-less tree, where the application's registered face would be the only one left and could win for the wrong reason

CLAIM (pinion-text, in that environment): registering the face does NOT change what an unset style resolves to (R1471's finding, now a test), and declaring the default does — the same unset style then shapes U+AC00 identically to a style that named the family, while an explicit family still outranks the default

CF-1 (one change): dropping the `.or(default_family)` resolution fails exactly the new scenario with registered=19.2 declared-default=19.2 (the tofu advance), and leaves the font-less and rescan scenarios passing
CLAIM (pinion-narrative): the R1345 flow assertion is Korean again and passes on a host with ZERO Hangul faces as well as on this one — bidirectional, which is what R1471 could not have

CF-2 (one change): removing the default-family call from that test FAILS on the Hangul-less host (all four rows 19px, no fold) and PASSES here — exactly the host-dependent split R1471 measured, reproduced and then removed
CLAIM (over the wire, demo): on the Hangul-less config the binding publishes default=NanumGothic / system=available, and scene/layout reports the narration folding to line_count=2, h=41

CF-3 (the demo's own discriminator, run every time): the same binding with its declaration suppressed reports default=(none) and the same text measures line_count=1, h=22 — same column width, so the difference is the face

OBLIGATION 3b: write_fontconfig was a THIRD mechanical copy and is lifted; the two prior demos now call it and both still pass. font_sources() has two consumers (hello-app-font, hello-vn-tide), so the paint-the-report pattern is NOT lifted yet

gate: cargo fmt --all --check clean, clippy -D pedantic 0 over the five changed crates, cargo doc --workspace --document-private-items 0, pinion-core 2739 / pinion-text 65 + 3 launchers / pinion-narrative 80 / pinion-shell 213 + 161 / hello-vn-tide 3; demos r1473 (new), r1448, r1447, hello_vn_tide all PASS
carry_forward_bullets: The self-hosted §5.37 arm ignores font_family entirely — self_hosted_text_eligible does not consult it, and SelfHostedTextEngine measures with the one system font it loaded. So under PINION_TEXT_ENGINE=1 a named family, and now a declared default, are silently not honoured. Pre-existing and env-opt-in, so out of scope here, but it is a real divergence between the two arms

Only the FAMILY is defaultable. Qt's QApplication::setFont carries a whole font; here every other TextStyle field already has a concrete value from TextStyle::new, so nothing else has an unset state to resolve. Giving them one is a separate design question with no consumer asking

The default is boot-only by construction (ShellConfig), matching R1448's argument that a boot snapshot cannot go stale. A mid-run seam would make FontSourceReport a Signal — the round that adds it decides that, not this one

hello-vn-tide's opening narration was lengthened so a fold is observable over the wire. That is content, and it is load-bearing for the demo; a shorter script would leave the wire unable to tell Hangul from tofu, since both measure the same stretched box

Round 1474.decision_summary: A premise must be about the fixture, not about the developer's machine; and when two explanations are refuted, ship the measurement rather than a third guess — r1473's premise asserted the host could draw Hangul, and r1447's timeout now carries a per-phase clock instead of a fix nobody could justify.
changes_bullets: tools/demos/r1473_app_default_font.py: the premise is about the DEMO'S CONFIG (it has faces, and none cover U+AC00), not about the developer's host having Korean fonts
tools/rpc_verify.py: fc_list_count(fontconfig, pattern) lifted at its third copy; the pattern argument is what lets one helper answer both "any faces" and "faces for this script"
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py + r1448_app_font.py: both now call the lifted counter
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py: every progress line carries elapsed seconds, so the runner that kills this demo reports WHERE the time went
NOT changed: the demo's work. Two explanations for its timeout were measured and refuted, and reducing work on a third guess would have been a change with no evidence behind it
verification_bullets: BOTH failures came from the first CI run after R1472/R1473 (run 30346762987): 441 asserted / 448 run, FAILURES r1447_font_free_tui.py(timeout) r1473_app_default_font.py. r1473 CAUSE, quoted from the log: "premise: this host CAN draw Hangul (0 faces cover U+AC00)". The runner has 53 fonts and no Korean among them. The assertion was about the developer's machine; the claim only ever needed the demo's own config to have faces and no Hangul coverage

r1473 FIXED and re-run: "the demo's config: 1 faces, 0 covering U+AC00 (host: 85 covering it)" — the host count is printed, not asserted, so the demo now passes on a Korean-capable host and a Korean-less one alike

r1447 HYPOTHESIS 1 REFUTED by measurement: cargo feature unification would have meant the job's `cargo test --workspace --no-run` did not warm what `cargo test -p <crate>` builds. Measured: after the workspace pre-build, `cargo test -p pinion-tui --lib --no-run` compiles 0 crates in 0.351s
r1447 HYPOTHESIS 2 REFUTED by measurement: a 2-core runner being simply slower. Measured: `taskset -c 0,1` over the whole demo finishes in 3.61s, against 3.30s unrestricted

r1447 WHAT IS KNOWN, from the preserved log: it reached "pinion-tui: 148 tests pass in both environments" and was killed in the example batteries that follow. Locally that point is t+1.3s. So a runner spent ~180s reaching where this machine spends about a second, and neither refuted explanation covers it

r1447 INSTRUMENTED rather than guessed: each progress line now carries elapsed seconds. Verified locally end to end (t+0.3 premise, t+1.3 the pinion-tui pair, t+2.8 the four batteries, t+4.5 the instrument phase)
gate: python syntax clean on all three touched demos; r1447 PASS 4.50s, r1448 PASS 4.39s, r1473 PASS 2.61s locally. No Rust changed
carry_forward_bullets: r1447 IS STILL EXPECTED TO FAIL in CI, and that is the deliberate state: its cause is unknown, two explanations were refuted, and the round shipped a measurement instead of a guess. The next run's t+ numbers name the phase, and only then is there a fix worth making

The obvious candidate reduction — folding the four example batteries into one `cargo test -p a -p b -p c -p d` — was NOT taken. It would confound the very measurement being shipped, and locally those four cost 0.2s each, so there is no evidence it is where the time is

A demo that asserts about the HOST rather than about its own fixture is a class, not one bug: R1471 fixed one, R1473 shipped another one round later. Nothing enforces the distinction; the cheap check is to ask of every premise whether a CI runner could fail it while the claim still holds

Round 1475.decision_summary: A pre-build warms a fingerprint, not a package name: cargo resolves features per invocation, so the sweep's `cargo test --workspace --no-run` produced pinion-runtime[default,vello] while the one vello-less demo needed pinion-runtime[default] — a superset in name and an empty cache in fact. The job now asks that demo which invocations to replay instead of guessing a command that looks bigger.
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml: the workspace-wide `cargo test --no-run` pre-build is replaced by a replay of the demo's OWN cargo invocations, read from it at job time
.github/workflows/ci.yml: a gate asserts r1447 is still the only demo shelling out to `cargo test` — R1474's carry said nothing enforced that, and the whole warm-cache design rests on it
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py: `CARGO_WARMUP` names every cargo invocation the demo makes, as data with two consumers, so a package added here cannot silently stop being pre-built
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py: `--print-warmup` prints that list rather than executing it — the job owns compiling, the demo owns measuring, and the 180s budget then measures the demo
tools/demos/r1447_font_free_tui.py: the R1472 header comment asserted "the ordinary budget is ample"; one run measured it false, so it is replaced by what survives
NOT changed: the demo's work, again. The measurement says the cost is an unwarmed feature variant, not the demo's own claims, so reducing them would still have no evidence behind it
verification_bullets: CAUSE, read off CI run 30352520291 rather than guessed (R1472's `-u` diagnostics are what made it readable): r1447 printed its FIRST line at t+123.3s, reached the pinion-tui pair at t+174.1s, and was killed at 180s in the example batteries

R1474's INFERENCE REFUTED by those numbers: it read the kill POINT (the example batteries) as the cost. 123.3s of the 180 was spent before the first diagnostic line — inside `ensure_built`, before any battery ran
CONTROL, computed from the same log's per-demo timestamps: neighbours #166-#174 took 1.7-2.7s and the sweep-wide median is 1.7s over 448 demos. The runner was not slow; this demo was
CONTROL, tighter: `r1448_app_font.py` runs immediately after (#171, 2.7s) and makes the same `ensure_built` and `fc-list` calls, so neither of those is the cost

MECHANISM measured with `cargo tree`: `--workspace` resolves pinion-runtime[default,vello] because the GUI examples enable vello, while `-p hello-button-tui` and `-p pinion-tui` resolve pinion-runtime[default]

MECHANISM measured on disk: target/release/.fingerprint holds BOTH units, ["default"] and ["default","vello"], under separate fingerprint hashes. A feature set is part of a unit's identity, so a superset build warms nothing for the subset

WHY R1474 REFUTED THIS SAME HYPOTHESIS AND WAS WRONG: this developer's target dir already contains both variants from months of builds, so `-p pinion-tui --no-run` honestly measured 0 crates. CI's cache holds only what `--workspace` built. A warm dir cannot measure a cold-cache defect

NEGATIVE CONTROL: `-p hello-button` and `-p hello-app-font` resolve [default,vello]. Every demo runs a per-package `cargo build` through `ensure_built`, and the other 447 are fast precisely because their resolution is the one the workspace build already made

SECOND CAUSE REFUTED: the demo alternates FONTCONFIG_FILE between cargo calls, but no build script tracks it (yeslogic-fontconfig-sys declares only RUST_FONTCONFIG_DLOPEN), so it cannot invalidate a fingerprint
THIRD CAUSE REFUTED by reading the harness: the sweep is a sequential `for` loop, so no other demo can be holding the cargo target lock
GUARD COUNTERFACTUAL: with its `grep -v` exclusion removed the detector names r1447, so it is reading the demos rather than passing blindly

gate: python syntax clean, workflow YAML parses, `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean on every demo-sweep run block, all 8 emitted warmup invocations execute as valid cargo commands, r1447 PASS 3.37s locally. No Rust changed

LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: a warm cache cannot be measured on a machine that already has it. Whether the replay actually lands r1447 inside its budget is answered by the next CI run, not by this round
carry_forward_bullets: R1474's host-premise class is NOT cleared. r1447 and r1448 still assert the HOST has fonts, and they are not r1473's shape: there the host was incidental, here the host config IS the second arm of the comparison the demo exists to make

Converting those two to fixtures would put the shaping-dependent cargo tests (pinion-text, the parley arm) against a two-face fixture, and whether they still pass is UNMEASURED. That measurement is the next round's work, not a rename
The vello-less variants are now compiled in the job rather than inside the demo, which lengthens demo-sweep by that compile. Unmeasured on a 2-core runner until the next run

The RELEASE side is warmed only because `--print-warmup` names hello-button-tui. A future vello-less example reached by a different demo would be unwarmed again, and only the `cargo test` half is gated

Round 1478.decision_summary: An RPC endpoint owns a NAME, and only ever binds or unbinds its own: a bind at a live path is refused rather than allowed to displace the incumbent, and teardown releases the name exactly once while it still holds it. The inode guard I first wrote for the second half could not fail — a tmpfs recycles the freed inode straight back to the next bind — so the window is removed by ordering instead of detected.
changes_bullets: crates/pinion-rpc-transport/src/lib.rs: `bind_unless_live` replaces the unconditional pre-bind unlink — bind first, and only on `EADDRINUSE` probe the path with a `connect`; a live owner (serving OR withdrawn) is refused with `AddrInUse`, a stale file is reclaimed as before

crates/pinion-rpc-transport/src/lib.rs: `TransportControl::shutdown` releases the name ONCE and only while the listener is still open (unlink, then signal, then join); the accept thread no longer unlinks at all, and the taken `JoinHandle` is what makes the idempotent second call and the following `Drop` a no-op

examples/hello-endpoint-identity: the reference consumer — it does NOT `expect` its bind, it reports the outcome as scene data on a `role=status` region (`EndpointClaim` = Bound / Contested / Unavailable), so an app that lost its endpoint still answers "which path is contested" over the out-of-band channel

tools/rpc_verify.py: obligation 3b — `SocketClient` (3rd copy: r1393 `SockClient`, r1469 `connect_socket`+`rpc_over_socket`, r1478) and `texts_of` (3 byte-identical copies, one md5) lifted; r1393 and r1469 migrated and re-run
NOT changed: exposure policy, in-flight session semantics, or the stale-reclaim behaviour the old unlink existed for
verification_bullets: DEFECT MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX: the three new integration tests were written first and FAILED on unmodified code (`a_bind_refuses_to_displace_a_live_endpoint`, `a_withdrawn_endpoint_still_owns_its_name`, and the teardown half), while `a_bind_reclaims_a_stale_socket_file` PASSED — the negative control naming the behaviour that had to survive

MY FIRST FIX WAS WRONG AND THE DEMO CAUGHT IT. It carried a `SocketIdentity{dev, ino}` guard so teardown would unlink only its own file. Running the demo failed on `gamma: a NEW socket file`, so the inode was measured directly: four bind/unlink cycles on one tmpfs path returned the SAME `st_ino` every time. A tmpfs hands the freed inode number straight back to the next bind, so the guard could not fail and was no guard at all

SO THE WINDOW IS REMOVED RATHER THAN DETECTED: unlink before signalling the accept loop, while the listener still holds the name, so no successor can be bound at that path yet; and never touch the path again. No inode arithmetic survives in the crate

THE SAME MEASUREMENT DELETED THREE DEMO ASSERTIONS. The demo had asserted inode equality in phases B/C/E as "the name did not change hands"; those would have passed just as happily for a replaced file. They are gone, and the docstring records the measurement and why

CF-1 (the liveness probe never refuses = the pre-R1478 unconditional unlink): exactly 2 unit failures, both R1478 ownership claims; the stale-reclaim control and the whole teardown half PASSED, so the two halves are independent. Demo FAILED at `beta: the bind was REFUSED`, reporting `bound at <alpha's path>` — the takeover, visible

CF-2 (teardown unlinks on every call = the old double unlink): exactly 1 unit failure, the teardown test. `drop_unbinds_the_socket_path` passed — normal teardown is unchanged — and CF-1's two tests passed, so each test has its own teeth

CF-3 (CF-1 plus beta's claim assertions relaxed, so the run reaches the ownership check): FAILED at `beta: clients still reach the INCUMBENT`, `expected 'Instance: alpha', got 'Instance: beta'`. This is the measurement that justifies dropping the inode proxy — the label read back over the socket catches the takeover ON ITS OWN

gate: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; clippy clean on both changed crates with `-D pedantic`; `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` exit 0 (two pub-doc links to the private `bind_unless_live` were rewritten as code spans); pinion-rpc-transport 16 integration + 2 unit + 1 doc, hello-endpoint-identity 3 unit
demos: r1478_endpoint_identity PASS (32 assertion sites, 5 phases, 2 concurrent instances), and both migrated neighbours re-run — r1469_transport_exposure PASS, r1393_conn_lifecycle PASS
carry_forward_bullets: The ORDERING claim in `shutdown` (unlink while the listener is open, so no successor can have bound) is argued from the bind protocol, not measured: the window it closes is sub-scheduler and a ZERO-FLAKE test will not race for it. What IS pinned deterministically is the double-unlink hazard the ordering also removes

Two racing successors reclaiming the SAME stale path can still displace each other (both probe, both find nobody, both unlink, both bind). Inherent to the standard AF_UNIX stale-recovery protocol without a lock file; strictly narrower than the defect fixed here, which struck LIVE endpoints

The liveness probe costs the incumbent one accepted-and-closed connection (an `on_connect`/`on_disconnect` pair with no frames). Documented, and paid only by a bind that was about to displace something; no demo observes it because `hello-endpoint-identity` does not track connections
`text_of` remains duplicated in r1469 and r1478 — two copies, below the 3rd-identical lift trigger, and each demo picks its own "which text counts" rule

Round 1480.decision_summary: An answer an External has already encoded reaches the wire as those bytes. IntrospectValue::Raw carries pre-encoded JSON, and it survives to the socket because the response envelope's payload became a type parameter rather than a hard-wired serde_json::Value — the variant alone would have been a regression, since the compat conversion re-parses what the producer just wrote.
changes_bullets: pinion-core §5.15 — `RawJson`: JSON text a producer already holds. `encode` (one serialization pass, no DOM), `parse` (validates untrusted text and discards the parse), `get`, `to_value`. Equality is TEXTUAL because the bytes are what the type promises to deliver. `IntrospectValue::Raw(RawJson)` + `IntrospectValue::raw()` as the call-shape sibling of R1276's `json()`, + `as_raw()`. Workspace `serde_json` gains the `raw_value` feature.

pinion-rpc §5.7 — `Response

`: the payload is a type parameter because reading and writing a result want different representations of ONE wire shape. A parsed response yields `Value` (the default, so all ~195 reader sites are untouched); a response being written may carry the crate-private `ResultBody { Dom(Value), Raw(RawJson) }`. `serialize` follows.

pinion-rpc §5.12 — dispatch funnel split in two, nested inside one `match`: the outer arms are the methods whose answer may already be encoded (`scene/query`, `scene/invoke` — the two whose answer IS the whole result), the inner match keeps the ~87 that answer with a tree and converts once at its tail. A method joins the outer group by moving its arm, not by re-typing the others. The file diff is ~1477 lines; `git diff -w` is +179/-30 — the remainder is rustfmt re-indenting the inner match.

pinion-rpc §5.15 — `introspect_value_to_body` (top-level: `Raw` rides through as bytes) beside the existing `introspect_value_to_json` (nested: a snapshot node, dry-run step, or intent payload is inside a `Value` the envelope is assembling, and a tree has no splice point part way down, so `Raw` materializes there).

examples/hello-encoded-answer + tools/demos/r1480_encoded_answer.py — a surface serving an 80x24 terminal frame (2,700 B) three ways: `frame` (raw), `frame_via_dom` (the round's control), `encode` (invoke). 33 assertions.

Substrate reuse the mandatory 3b self-grep caught in code I had just written: the query-only `External` skeleton was hand-rolled twice (example + wire fixture) when `query_proxy_external_impl!` is its SSOT, and both hand-rolled `Err(InterveneError::ReadOnly)` for every path when `read_only_or_unknown` is the §2 #7 rule (ReadOnly for a declared field, UnknownPath otherwise). Both routed through the substrate.
verification_bullets: MEASURED, not assumed (release, in-process `dispatch`, 2,700 B payload, 2000 iterations, throwaway harness deleted in-round): raw 2,282-3,711 ns/request vs DOM 9,078-13,770 ns/request. Within-run ratio 3.3-4.5x across 4 runs. Absolute figures move ~30% between runs on this box, so only the within-run ratio is quoted — the same caveat the reporting consumer stated for its own numbers.

CF-1 (envelope re-parses the raw payload — the compat-only shape the handoff itself described as "the benefit disappears"): EXACTLY 2 unit tests fail (query + invoke verbatim), the other 948 pass, and the demo FAILS at (B) showing `['h','rows','w']`. Scope is exact: a producer that does not use the variant is untouched.
CF-2 (nested `Raw` falls through the `non_exhaustive` wildcard to null): EXACTLY 1 unit test + demo (G). Independent of CF-1's half, so the two halves are separately covered.
CF-3 (equality compares values instead of bytes): EXACTLY 1 core test. The textual-equality contract has its own teeth.

A first CF attempt did not compile at all — deleting the `Raw` arm from `introspect_value_to_body` made the variant dead code, which is the type system reporting that the arm has exactly one producer.

The witness is a NEGATIVE made observable: no timing is asserted anywhere. `Value`'s object is a `BTreeMap`, so a tree round-trip sorts keys while serde's derive emits declaration order; the fixture declares `w,h,rows` / `y,dim,text` and the answer's own key order says which path produced it, at both depths. `r1480_a_dom_round_trip_would_have_reordered_it` asserts that premise rather than assuming it — a serde_json built with `preserve_order` would otherwise turn every key-order assertion in this round into a vacuous pass.

Round 1481.decision_summary: A path the read answers, the write may not deny. scene/invoke and scene/intervene gain the paint-scene fallback scene/query has had since R828, so a live immediate-mode driver is actionable rather than read-only by accident — and the borrow seam R828 deferred on dissolves by doing the work inside the borrow instead of returning it.
changes_bullets: pinion-rpc §5.12 — `invoke_shared` / `intervene_shared`: the immediate-mode half of the action and write channels, reachable through a SHARED `&Scene`. R828 gave `scene/query` an immediate-mode branch and deferred these two with a stated reason — they returned a `&mut dyn ExternalIntrospect` that had to outlive resolution, which a `RefCell` borrow cannot do — conditioned on "until a consumer needs it". The seam dissolves the same way the read's did: do the work INSIDE the borrow and return an owned value. `Rc<RefCell<dyn ImmediateMode>>` is interior-mutable, so a shared reference suffices, which is what lets the painted frame answer a write at all.

pinion-rpc §5.7 — `handle_scene_invoke` / `handle_scene_intervene` take `last_paint_scene` and retry on `NoExternalAtPath`, mirroring `handle_scene_query`'s R828 fallback exactly. State-scene authority is preserved the same way: paint is consulted ONLY on that one outcome, so every other verdict returns verbatim.

The fallback is deliberately NOT a wildcard. A retained `ExternalNode` in a painted frame is a `Box` the view fn rebuilds every frame, so a write into it would vanish before the next paint; `*_shared` refuses it. Refusing is the truthful answer for that shape, and a driver's `Rc` — the same one the tick loop holds — is why acting on the other shape is not.

examples/hello-immediate-intent — `BouncingBallDriver` gains a writable `velocity` and a `reset` action returning the bounce count it cleared. The driver already declared `introspect_mut`; the channel existed and was simply unreachable over the wire. Read-only slots now answer through `read_only_or_unknown` so "you cannot write this" reads differently from "this does not exist".

tools/demos/r1481_driver_write_parity.py — 32 assertions, including a sweep over the driver's OWN declared schema asserting that no readable slot is ever refused as absent, so the property cannot drift as slots are added.
verification_bullets: MEASURED on an existing binding before any change: `scene/query ball/external/velocity` answered `-2.5` while `scene/intervene` and `scene/invoke` on that same path answered `NoExternalAtPath` — a claim about the scene's shape the read had just disproved. After: intervene sets `velocity` to a chosen value and the read returns it; `invoke reset` returns the bounce count it cleared.

The FIRST framing was wrong and measurement corrected it. R1480's carry recorded this as a path-SYNTAX asymmetry (`scene/query` resolving `<tag>/external/<field>` where `scene/invoke` did not). A counterfactual that disabled query's paint-scene fallback made the tagged read fail exactly as the write did, proving both paths share one parser and one walker: the real cause is that only the READ consulted the painted frame. The carry note described the symptom with the wrong cause.

CF (remove the paint fallback from `handle_scene_intervene`): all 956 unit tests PASSED and only the demo failed, with the exact pre-R1481 error. That hole was the finding — `invoke_shared` / `intervene_shared` were unit-tested in isolation while nothing covered whether `dispatch` ever reaches them. Four dispatch-level wire tests added; the re-run CF now kills EXACTLY 2 (both intervene-side, matching the CF's scope) out of 960.

`r1481_a_write_the_read_can_answer_is_never_refused_as_absent` states the defect as one assertion: read the path, then write it, and assert the failure — a type mismatch is fine — is never `NoExternalAtPath`.

Gates: cargo fmt --all --check clean; clippy -D pedantic clean on pinion-rpc / hello-immediate-intent; pinion-rpc 960 (+10); demo r1481 PASS (32 assertions) plus the four immediate-mode neighbours r827 / r828 / r829 / r830 and r1480, all PASS.
carry_forward_bullets: The READ side still has the asymmetry's other half unexamined: `scene/query`'s R828 fallback resolves a retained `ExternalNode` in a painted frame too, and that node is a per-frame `Box`, so the value read is whatever the throwaway holds rather than the state scene's. Sound for a driver (shared `Rc`), questionable for a rebuilt node. R1481 did not touch the read; whether that fallback should narrow to drivers the way the write one does is a separate call.

`invoke_immediate_at` and `intervene_immediate_at` are two near-identical borrow-discipline bodies, deliberately mirroring `query`'s inline branch rather than being lifted. The borrow rule is what must not be re-derived, so a third consumer is the lift trigger; two mirrored copies that each read like the read path are the more faithful shape today.

`scene/invoke` on a painted driver is classified `HandlerKind::Mutate` and bumps the scene revision, matching what a state-scene invoke does. Whether a driver mutation SHOULD advance the retained-scene OCC token is a question the immediate-mode axis has not settled; it is bundled with the retained one today.
Round 1481.publishable_decision_summary: A path the read answers, the write may not deny. scene/invoke and scene/intervene gain the paint-scene fallback scene/query has had since R828, so a live immediate-mode driver is actionable rather than read-only by accident — and the borrow seam R828 deferred on dissolves by doing the work inside the borrow instead of returning it.
publishable_changes_bullets: pinion-rpc §5.12 — `invoke_shared` / `intervene_shared`: the immediate-mode half of the action and write channels, reachable through a SHARED `&Scene`. R828 gave `scene/query` an immediate-mode branch and deferred these two with a stated reason — they returned a `&mut dyn ExternalIntrospect` that had to outlive resolution, which a `RefCell` borrow cannot do — conditioned on "until a consumer needs it". The seam dissolves the same way the read's did: do the work INSIDE the borrow and return an owned value. `Rc<RefCell<dyn ImmediateMode>>` is interior-mutable, so a shared reference suffices, which is what lets the painted frame answer a write at all.

pinion-rpc §5.7 — `handle_scene_invoke` / `handle_scene_intervene` take `last_paint_scene` and retry on `NoExternalAtPath`, mirroring `handle_scene_query`'s R828 fallback exactly. State-scene authority is preserved the same way: paint is consulted ONLY on that one outcome, so every other verdict returns verbatim.

The fallback is deliberately NOT a wildcard. A retained `ExternalNode` in a painted frame is a `Box` the view fn rebuilds every frame, so a write into it would vanish before the next paint; `*_shared` refuses it. Refusing is the truthful answer for that shape, and a driver's `Rc` — the same one the tick loop holds — is why acting on the other shape is not.

examples/hello-immediate-intent — `BouncingBallDriver` gains a writable `velocity` and a `reset` action returning the bounce count it cleared. The driver already declared `introspect_mut`; the channel existed and was simply unreachable over the wire. Read-only slots now answer through `read_only_or_unknown` so "you cannot write this" reads differently from "this does not exist".

tools/demos/r1481_driver_write_parity.py — 32 assertions, including a sweep over the driver's OWN declared schema asserting that no readable slot is ever refused as absent, so the property cannot drift as slots are added.
publishable_verification_bullets: MEASURED on an existing binding before any change: `scene/query ball/external/velocity` answered `-2.5` while `scene/intervene` and `scene/invoke` on that same path answered `NoExternalAtPath` — a claim about the scene's shape the read had just disproved. After: intervene sets `velocity` to a chosen value and the read returns it; `invoke reset` returns the bounce count it cleared.

The FIRST framing was wrong and measurement corrected it. R1480's carry recorded this as a path-SYNTAX asymmetry (`scene/query` resolving `<tag>/external/<field>` where `scene/invoke` did not). A counterfactual that disabled query's paint-scene fallback made the tagged read fail exactly as the write did, proving both paths share one parser and one walker: the real cause is that only the READ consulted the painted frame. The carry note described the symptom with the wrong cause.

CF (remove the paint fallback from `handle_scene_intervene`): all 956 unit tests PASSED and only the demo failed, with the exact pre-R1481 error. That hole was the finding — `invoke_shared` / `intervene_shared` were unit-tested in isolation while nothing covered whether `dispatch` ever reaches them. Four dispatch-level wire tests added; the re-run CF now kills EXACTLY 2 (both intervene-side, matching the CF's scope) out of 960.

`r1481_a_write_the_read_can_answer_is_never_refused_as_absent` states the defect as one assertion: read the path, then write it, and assert the failure — a type mismatch is fine — is never `NoExternalAtPath`.

Gates: cargo fmt --all --check clean; clippy -D pedantic clean on pinion-rpc / hello-immediate-intent; pinion-rpc 960 (+10); demo r1481 PASS (32 assertions) plus the four immediate-mode neighbours r827 / r828 / r829 / r830 and r1480, all PASS.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: The READ side still has the asymmetry's other half unexamined: `scene/query`'s R828 fallback resolves a retained `ExternalNode` in a painted frame too, and that node is a per-frame `Box`, so the value read is whatever the throwaway holds rather than the state scene's. Sound for a driver (shared `Rc`), questionable for a rebuilt node. R1481 did not touch the read; whether that fallback should narrow to drivers the way the write one does is a separate call.

`invoke_immediate_at` and `intervene_immediate_at` are two near-identical borrow-discipline bodies, deliberately mirroring `query`'s inline branch rather than being lifted. The borrow rule is what must not be re-derived, so a third consumer is the lift trigger; two mirrored copies that each read like the read path are the more faithful shape today.

`scene/invoke` on a painted driver is classified `HandlerKind::Mutate` and bumps the scene revision, matching what a state-scene invoke does. Whether a driver mutation SHOULD advance the retained-scene OCC token is a question the immediate-mode axis has not settled; it is bundled with the retained one today.

Round 1482.decision_summary: A scene/query answer says which surface produced it — the state scene, a live immediate-mode driver in the painted frame, or a per-frame node whose value is as of that frame — disclosed atomically with the value via opt-in params.with_origin, because a provenance fetched by a second call may describe a frame the value never came from.
changes_bullets: `pinion-rpc` `query.rs`: new `SceneSource{State,Paint}` + `AnswerOrigin{State,PaintDriver,PaintFrame}`; `query_from` returns `(value, origin)` from the SAME walk `query` performs, and `query` becomes its origin-dropping projection so the two cannot drift.
`AnswerOrigin::of(source, driver)` is the single site combining the scene the dispatcher chose with the node kind the walker found; `to_wire` is the single enum-to-word mapping.

`dispatch.rs` `handle_scene_query`: opt-in `params.with_origin` wraps the answer as `{"value","origin"}`; absent or `false` leaves the ratified §5.12 shape (result IS the value) byte-identical for ~287 call sites.
The wrap is encoded through `RawJson::encode`, so R1480's pre-encoded answers ride verbatim one level down instead of being undone by the envelope.

New `hello-answer-origin` example: one binding exposing all three origins at once (state-scene model / live `ImmediateModeNode` driver / per-frame retained `ExternalNode`), plus `tools/demos/r1482_answer_origin.py` (32 assertion statements).
`tools/rpc_verify.py`: `query(path, with_origin=False)` mirrors the new wire param so demos do not hand-roll the envelope.
verification_bullets: Defect reproduced at HEAD before any edit: one dispatcher, three byte-identical frames — `result:7` (state scene), `result:0` (per-frame copy), `result:99` (live driver). The caller could not tell which contract it held.

CF-1 (collapse PaintDriver into PaintFrame = the plain "which scene" disclosure): exactly 4 unit failures, all driver-distinction claims; the other 968 passed. Demo failed at `★C: expected 'paint_driver', got 'paint_frame'`.
CF-2 (`with_origin` ignored): exactly 5 unit failures, all disclosure claims; every bare-shape assertion passed, so the two halves are independent. Demo failed at the envelope check.
CF-3 (wrap rebuilds a DOM instead of splicing raw): did not compile — the type system reported `OriginatedAnswer` has exactly one producer; with an allow, exactly 1 unit failure (the raw witness).
CF-D3 (paint consulted before state): demo failed at `★H: expected 'state', got 'paint_frame'`, so state-scene authority has teeth.
My own raw-path assertion first read `parse_response`'s `Value` — a `BTreeMap` round-trip, the very rebuild it exists to detect. Rewritten against the wire text.

The example's state-scene fixture first wrapped the primary in a `Container`; measured against the running app (`scene/snapshot from=state` reports a bare `{"type":"External","tag":"model"}`) and corrected to mirror production.

Gates: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, clippy `-D pedantic` 0, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` 0, pinion-rpc 972 (+12), hello-answer-origin 6 (new). Demos PASS: r1482 (new), r1481, r1480, r828, r827, r829, r830, r1468.

Obligation 3b: the example's `line` helper is the 2nd identical copy (md5-compared against hello-encoded-answer), not the 3rd, so no lift; the `External` skeleton and read-only rule route through the existing `query_proxy_external_impl!` / `read_only_or_unknown` substrate rather than being re-typed.
carry_forward_bullets: The disclosure is opt-in, so a caller that never asks still cannot tell which surface answered. That is a stated limit, not a claim of completeness: making it unconditional would change the result shape for ~287 call sites and is the reason the ratified §5.12 shape was preserved.
Errors carry no origin. `UnknownIntrospectPath` from the painted frame and from the state scene read identically; only successful answers disclose.
`scene/invoke` does not disclose. Its fallback is driver-only (R1481), so a successful fallback invoke is always `paint_driver` — derivable, but not stated on the wire.

Round 1483.decision_summary: One name reaches one surface in both compositions: a binding's primary External answers to its own tag whether compose_root left it at the scene root or wrapped it beside extras, closing a stable-address gap that a reactive external set could open and close at runtime.
changes_bullets: `pinion-rpc` `resolve.rs`: new `lookup_addressed` / `lookup_addressed_mut` — `Scene::lookup_path_ref/_mut` plus a root-name alias, guarded by the private `names_the_root`.
All five external-path resolution sites now route through it: `introspect_at`, `introspect_mut_at`, and the immediate-mode branches of `query`, `invoke`, `intervene`.

The alias is a FALLBACK, so a descendant that matches still wins and every path resolving before this round keeps its meaning; it consumes exactly one segment, so a root's tag cannot become a silent path prefix.

New demo `tools/demos/r1483_stable_tag_address.py` (31 assertion statements) drives one binding of each composition — `hello-answer-origin` (bare root) and `hello-listbox` (wrapped) — over a real wire.
verification_bullets: Root cause re-framed by measurement, not carried forward as written: R1482's carry called this a path-resolution defect. `Scene::lookup_path_ref` in fact round-trips with its own producer — `hit_test` emits the root's path as the EMPTY chain — so the walker is correct. The defect is that `CoreShell::compose_root` makes the primary External the root when the binding has no extras and a child when it has some, while giving it `WidgetCore::tag()` in both cases.

Measured on one tag naming one logical surface: extras=0 gives `/model/external/count = NoExternalAtPath`, extras=1 gives `Ok(1)`. Since R688 made the external set a reactive projection of state, `reconcile_externals` re-composes at runtime, so a working address could stop working when an unrelated extra appeared or went away.

CF-1 (alias removed = pre-R1483): exactly 5 failures, all new claims; the guards (precedence, one-segment, untagged root, bare shorthand) all passed, which is their job. Demo failed with `NoExternalAtPath`.

CF-2 (precedence inverted so the root shadows a descendant) FIRST PASSED ALL 982 TESTS. The precedence guard held one child, so both orderings descended to the same external and the assertion could not tell them apart. Refixtured with a decoy ahead of the named child so the two orderings answer 1 vs 7; CF-2 rerun then killed exactly 1 — the guard.
CF-3 (alias on the read but not the write, the R1481 divergence class): exactly 2 failures, both channel-parity claims.

Round 1485.decision_summary: A refusal says which surface refused: scene/query's with_origin opt-in now covers the failure channel, so the three surfaces that answer differently and refused identically are distinguishable, and a refusal that reached no surface names none.
changes_bullets: `query_from` now returns `Result<_, QueryRefusal>` — a refusal plus the surface that produced it — where its error arm previously had nowhere to carry one; `query` keeps `QueryError` by projecting the refusal.

`refused_by` is `Some` exactly when the walk reached an introspect surface (`UnknownIntrospectPath`, `IntrospectionOptedOut`) and `None` for refusals that named no node (`NoExternalAtPath`, `UnsupportedPath`, `Path`). Each stage attaches the origin where that stage knows what it reached, rather than a classifier re-deriving it from the variant.
`params.with_origin` now covers the failure channel: `error.data` widens from the bare word to `{reason, origin?}`, with `origin` ABSENT (not null) when no surface was reached.

New `query_error_reason` is the one place a `QueryError` becomes its wire word, shared by the bare and disclosing renderings; `query_error_to_rpc` fell out as dead once every query refusal routed through `refusal_to_rpc`.

New demo `tools/demos/r1485_refusal_origin.py` (46 assertion statements) drives `hello-answer-origin`; two new unit tests in that example pin the refusal origins and that a refusal points at the `$schema` lacking the slot.

Substrate lift (obligation 3b): `rpc_error_data` added to `tools/rpc_verify.py` as the capture peer of `assert_rpc_error`, migrating four hand-rolled sites (three inside `r1386_snapshot_path_error.py`, one new).
ZERO-FLAKE fix in `r1481_driver_write_parity.py`: two assertions compared a signed `velocity` a wall bounce may legitimately negate; both now assert the magnitude, which `tick` provably preserves.
verification_bullets: Measured on the running `hello-answer-origin` binding BEFORE any edit: three different surfaces refusing for three different reasons produced the byte-identical `data:"UnknownIntrospectPath"` (`/external/nope` = the state model, `/sim/external/nope` = a live driver, `/probe/external/nope` = a per-frame node), and `with_origin:true` was accepted and then silently ignored on the failure channel — the with/without blocks were identical.

Round 1486.decision_summary: The push gate now bounds the build cache it creates: target/'s size is reported on every push and oldest artifacts are reclaimed past a budget, after the build gates so the sweep cannot remove what they just built.
changes_bullets: New `.githooks/lib/target-budget.sh` — `enforce_target_budget` reports `target/`'s size on every push and, when it exceeds a budget, reclaims oldest artifacts via `cargo sweep --maxsize`.

Wired into `.githooks/pre-push` as step 4, deliberately AFTER the clippy and rustdoc gates: those gates build the workspace, so their artifacts are the newest in the tree and an oldest-first sweep cannot remove them. Run before, it would delete artifacts the very next command rebuilds.
The size line prints unconditionally, over budget or not — that number is the fact whose absence let the growth run unseen.
Default budget 100 GiB, overridable with `PINION_TARGET_BUDGET_GB`; a non-integer value is rejected loudly rather than silently reverting to the default.
Never fails the push: a missing `cargo-sweep`, an unmeasurable tree, or a failed sweep all report and continue, because the commit being published is not what is unsafe.
`CLAUDE.md` gains a "Build-cache budget" subsection under the hooks section — the durable tracked home, since `docs/SEED_PROMPT.md` is gitignored.
verification_bullets: Measured 2026-07-29 before any change: `target/` was 198 GiB (debug 191 GiB) and the filesystem was 100% full with 8.1 GiB free. `cargo sweep --time 1` reclaimed 165.37 GiB, and an incremental `cargo check -p pinion-rpc --all-targets` still finished in 2.3s afterwards — essentially all of it was dead weight.

The defect was invisibility, not the absence of a deleter: nothing in the repo had ever reported the size, so ~800 rounds of growth went unseen until a different session hit the full disk and asked whether cleaning was safe.
Size budget chosen over `--time N` days because what ran out was space, not age: a week-based sweep reclaims nothing during a heavy week and deletes useful artifacts during a quiet one.
`--maxsize` semantics verified both ways by dry-run before wiring: `--maxsize 200GB` on a 69 GiB tree reported "would clean: nothing"; `--maxsize 40GB` reported 36.63 GiB.

Every branch executed, not just the no-op one: under budget (prints the number, acts not), non-integer budget "80GB" and "0" (both rejected, default not silently substituted), missing `target/` (silent rc=0), and OVER budget for real — budget 60 GiB against a 67 GiB tree reclaimed 18.00 GiB and reported "target/ now 50 GiB".

The design's load-bearing claim measured directly: immediately after that 18 GiB sweep, `cargo check -p pinion-rpc --all-targets` finished in 3.7s, so the artifacts the gates had just built survived an oldest-first sweep.

The stated overshoot limit reproduced on a second data point: `--maxsize 60GB` landed at 50 GiB, as `--maxsize 40GB` had landed near 32 — `cargo sweep` converts a size budget into a timestamp cutoff, so it trims coarsely.
`du -sb` cost measured at 0.12s on a 69 GiB tree, so the unconditional report is free. `shellcheck -x` clean (0 findings) on `pre-push`, `lib/target-budget.sh` and `commit-msg`; `bash -n` clean.
carry_forward_bullets: Not a lock. A concurrently building session's artifacts are the newest in the tree, so oldest-first will not reach them, but nothing here coordinates with another process — the hazard the session that first reported the full disk correctly raised.
`cargo sweep` trims at timestamp granularity and so overshoots the budget (measured twice). Safe for this purpose — it only ever means a little more rebuilding — but it is not a precise trim.

Only pinion is bounded. Measured the same day: sprag 88G, watching-zenoh 87G, hda4-diag 62G, the-tide-that-counts 45G, scxml-core-engine 44G, mnemosyne 36G — over 360G of very likely the same accumulation. The cross-repo rule forbids a pinion session from running cargo in any of them, so each needs the same treatment from its own session.
The budget is enforced at push time only. A session that builds heavily without pushing is unbounded until its next push; a round that never pushes never reports.

Round 1487.decision_summary: The write channel says which surface it reached: scene/invoke and scene/intervene now honour with_origin on both channels, and a painted retained node is refused by name instead of by denying it exists.
changes_bullets: `scene/invoke` and `scene/intervene` now honour `params.with_origin` on BOTH channels: a success answers `{value, origin}` and a refusal widens `error.data` to `{reason, origin?}`, in the vocabulary and envelope `scene/query` has used since R1482.

New `invoke_from` / `invoke_shared_from` / `intervene_from` / `intervene_shared_from` return the surface beside the outcome; `invoke` / `intervene` / `*_shared` survive unchanged as the origin-dropping projections.

The shared-borrow (painted-frame) walk now LOOKS before refusing: a retained `External` at the address yields the new `RetainedNodeNotWritable` named by its surface, where it previously reported `NoExternalAtPath` about an address `scene/query` resolves and names `paint_frame`.
New `resolve::external_node_at` is the existence half of `introspect_at`, written in terms of it, so the read and the write channels cannot answer "is there a surface here" two different ways.

New `crates/pinion-rpc/src/origin.rs` owns `SceneSource` / `AnswerOrigin` / the generic `Refusal<E>` (`QueryRefusal` is now `Refusal<QueryError>`); its home in the read module was an accident of which round needed it first.

Substrate lifts (obligation 3b): `Refusal::from_resolve` replaces the resolve-stage classification hand-written in query / invoke / intervene; `refusal_to_rpc` became generic over the error type with the per-method vocabulary passed in, so three methods share one disclosing-refusal renderer; `originated_body` and `wants_origin` are one site each.
`tools/rpc_verify.py` gains `assert_disclosed` (lifted at its third demo, migrating r1482 and r1485) and `with_origin` kwargs on the `invoke` / `intervene` wrappers.
New demo `tools/demos/r1487_write_origin.py` (48 assertion statements plus loops) drives `hello-answer-origin`, whose three surfaces each gained a declared, run-counting action.
verification_bullets: Measured on the running bindings BEFORE any edit: `with_origin:true` was accepted and silently ignored by `scene/invoke` on both channels, and two reached surfaces refused byte-identically (`/external/nope` state model and `/sim/external/nope` live driver both `UnknownInvokePath`).

The sharper measured defect: `invoke` / `intervene` on `/probe/external/*` answered `NoExternalAtPath` while `scene/query` answered the same address and named it `paint_frame` — the wire denying an external the read had just resolved.

R1481 wrote that rule and applied it to one of the two painted node kinds: `dispatch_tests.rs` asserts "the read just proved an external is there" for a driver, and four lines later asserted `NoExternalAtPath` for a per-frame node. R1485's own demo pinned the false word too.
Changing the walk broke exactly 3 of 1014 pinion-rpc tests, and all three were the ones asserting that word; every other test passed untouched.
CF-1 (write channel never discloses = pre-R1487): exactly 3 unit failures, all new wire claims; the demo names it ("asked the wire to disclose the origin and got the bare answer instead: 105").
CF-2 (`refused_by` always None): 13 failures, 8 of them PRE-EXISTING R1485 tests, so the write disclosure rides the mechanism the read channel already guards.
CF-3 (revert to denying a per-frame node exists): exactly 6 — the 3 R1481 tests updated here plus 3 new ones — and the demo names the claim that moved.
CF-4 (disclose unconditionally): 11 failures, 8 PRE-EXISTING, so the ratified bare shape is guarded by tests older than this round.
CF-5 (claim a surface at every missed address): exactly 3, all "nothing reached names nothing" guards, plus the demo's absence assertions.

CF-1, CF-2 and CF-3 each first killed the demo WITHOUT naming the defect (AttributeError / KeyError); that is why `assert_disclosed` was lifted and why the refusal-origin claim is stated as a group before any origin is read.

Gates: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, clippy `-D pedantic` 0, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items` 0, pinion-rpc 1014 (+14), hello-answer-origin 10 (+2). Demos PASS: r1487 (new), r1482, r1485, r1481, r1483, r1484, r1480, r828, hello-no-primary.
carry_forward_bullets: WIRE WORD CHANGE: a write to a retained `External` reachable only through the painted frame now reports `RetainedNodeNotWritable` instead of `NoExternalAtPath`. The refusal itself is R1481's and unchanged; only the false claim about the scene is gone. In-repo consumers updated: r1482 and r1485 demos plus three unit tests. The full demo sweep runs in CI.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE for opt-in callers: `with_origin:true` on `scene/invoke` / `scene/intervene` changes the success result shape and the `error.data` type. Both were previously ignored, so no caller can have depended on them; the bare form is byte-identical.

`retained_refusal` is duplicated in `invoke.rs` and `intervene.rs` — 8 lines each, differing only in which enum's `RetainedNodeNotWritable` they name, which no `From` impl can supply. Two consumers; the lift trigger is a third write channel.

`invoke_shared_from` / `intervene_shared_from` take a `SceneSource` that production only ever passes `Paint`, mirroring `query_from`. A caller that passed `State` would get a coherent origin but a `RetainedNodeNotWritable` reason naming a route it did not take.
An unreached refusal still does not report WHERE the walk looked — unchanged from R1485, and still with no consumer asking.
`scene/rewind`, `scene/dry_run` and `scene/simulate` have no paint fallback and so no origin to report; if one ever gains a fallback it inherits this round's shape rather than inventing another.

Round 1488.decision_summary: Dead-toolchain artifacts are dropped unconditionally before the build cache is measured: that removal is provably free, so gating it on a size budget would carry dead weight whenever the tree happens to fit.
changes_bullets: `enforce_target_budget` now calls a new `sweep_uninstalled_toolchains` first: `cargo sweep --installed` drops artifacts built by a toolchain rustup no longer has.

Unconditional, unlike the size sweep — a toolchain that is not installed cannot build anything, so nothing it produced can ever be reused and removing it costs no rebuild. Budget-gating a free removal would carry dead weight whenever the tree is under budget.
Runs BEFORE the size is measured, so dead-toolchain bytes are not counted toward a budget the workspace is not actually using.
Silent when it reclaims nothing, which is this repo's normal outcome; only a non-empty reclaim prints.
`CLAUDE.md` records the step and, more importantly, why it reclaims nothing here today.
verification_bullets: Measured before implementing: `cargo sweep --installed --dry-run` reports "Would clean: nothing" on the 50 GiB tree. The reason is structural, not incidental — `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `channel = "1.88.0"`, an exact version rather than `stable`, so every build in the project's history used one rustc which is still installed. There has never been a toolchain rotation, so there is no rotation debris: the 198 GiB R1486 addressed was entirely SAME-toolchain accretion.

Kept anyway on a measured cost of 0.33s (`du -sb` on the same tree is 0.18s) and a foreseen trigger: `rust-toolchain.toml` states that bumping past 1.88 is expected on a workspace-dep trigger, and at that moment the tree can hold two toolchains' artifacts while still under budget, so the size sweep would not fire and the dead half would be carried indefinitely.

Four paths executed. Real no-reclaim: silent. Reclaim: verified against a PATH stub reproducing cargo-sweep's observed output shape — prints one line, suppressing the tool's installed-toolchain list. Full function: unchanged budget behaviour ("target/ is 51 GiB (budget 100 GiB)"). Missing `cargo-sweep`: silent rc=0.

The reclaim test caught a defect in the first draft: a real `cargo sweep` prints `Cleaned nothing` rather than staying silent when there is nothing to reclaim, which a DRY RUN never shows (it prints `Would clean: nothing` instead). The filter had been written against dry-run output and would have printed a meaningless line on every push, diluting the size report. Fixed and re-verified.

Also measured and REJECTED this round: the `--stamp` / `--file` build-aware flow. After a fully warm `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features pinion-runtime/vello` plus `cargo doc --workspace` that rebuilt nothing, `--file` would remove 26.16 GiB of 50 GiB, including all 2539 `target/release` entries (5.0 GiB of demo example binaries the next round rebuilds). Its precision is relative to the build set bracketed by the stamp, and this repo's push gate runs only one of the several configurations a round cycles through — the same fact `ci.yml` already records from R1475 ("cargo resolves features per invocation ... a superset is not a warm cache").
`shellcheck -x` clean on `lib/target-budget.sh` and `pre-push`.
carry_forward_bullets: Reclaims nothing until `rust-toolchain.toml`'s pin moves. That is a measured statement about today, not a claim that the step is inert: the pin is documented as movable on a workspace-dep trigger.

Everything R1486 carried still holds — not a lock against a concurrent build, timestamp-granularity overshoot in the size sweep, push-time enforcement only, and pinion alone being bounded while sibling repos hold 360G+ of very likely the same accretion.

Round 1489.decision_summary: The build cache is bounded by construction, not by a push-time sweep: every project's target/ moved onto a fixed-size compressed volume, and the hook that measures it was repaired to follow the symlink it would otherwise have read as zero.
changes_bullets: `.githooks/lib/target-budget.sh` now measures with `du -sbL`: R1489 made every project's `target/` a symlink onto a compressed volume, and without `-L` the gate measured the LINK (29 bytes) and reported `0 GiB`, so it could never fire again.
The hook's header and `CLAUDE.md` now say the hook is the trend line, not the bound — the hard ceiling is the fixed-size volume, and a daily user timer sweeps every project rather than only this one.

`CLAUDE.md` records the corrected root cause: the size is a per-target floor (~148 MiB independent of the example's own code) multiplied by the target structure, not the push gate's clippy/doc as R1486 stated.

Machine-level (outside the repo, recorded here because it changes what `target/` IS): `~/.buildcache.btrfs` 100 GiB btrfs image, `compress=zstd:1`, `nofail` fstab entry, every project's `target/` symlinked into it; `buildcache-sweep.timer` user timer with linger enabled.
verification_bullets: Per-target size is independent of the example's own source: `hello-checkbox` 298 LOC = 148.3 MiB, `hello-button` 446 LOC = 148.0 MiB, `todomvc` 5,518 LOC = 154.3 MiB, `hello-node-editor` 8,998 LOC = 155.0 MiB. The binary is the framework re-linked, not the example.
`.debug_*` is 82.6 MiB of that 148.3 MiB (56%); `strip --strip-debug` gives 65.6 MiB and `--strip-all` 45.0 MiB.

Multiplier measured from `cargo metadata`: 198 bin + 25 lib + 26 test + 2 bench targets, and 190 of 197 examples carry `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. One example's test executable built directly: 54.1 MiB. So ~200 MiB per example, ~40 GiB per complete workspace build.
R1486's stated cause is refuted by measurement: clippy/doc produce `.rmeta` 2.75 GiB + `.rlib` 5.55 GiB + doc 0.26 GiB and never link, while `target/debug` top level is 26.79 GiB of linked binaries.

Compression measured as ground truth via image growth (not `du`, which does not report btrfs compression): 457.6 MiB of real binaries grew the image by 118.8 MiB = 3.85x. Standalone zstd-1 on one binary was 4.46x at 570 MB/s, faster than the NVMe write it replaces.
Machine-wide result: 118 GiB of `target/` across six repos became 37 GiB; root free went 288 GiB to 367 GiB.
Build behaviour unchanged on the compressed volume: `cargo check -p pinion-rpc --all-targets` 0.17s warm (0.16s before), 2.84s after touching a source file, `cargo test -p pinion-rpc` 1014 passed.
The fstab entry was verified by actually unmounting and running `mount -a`, then rebuilding — not by inspection. `nofail` means a missing image cannot block boot.
The timer was verified by running the service once (`37 GiB used of 100 GiB, within budget`) rather than by registering it and assuming.
The hook fix was verified by running `enforce_target_budget` before and after: 29 bytes vs 51 GiB.
carry_forward_bullets: NOT DONE, measured and deliberate: `[profile.dev] split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` would stop ~400 binaries each embedding a private copy of the framework's DWARF. It composes with compression rather than overlapping it (zstd is per-file, so 400 copies still cost 400 times). Untried here because it wants a full-rebuild measurement; the compression landed first because it needed no build-config change at all.

The budget number in the hook is apparent bytes while the volume stores compressed, so the two units differ by ~3.9x. A future round that wants one number should read the volume's own usage, not `du`.
The loopback image adds a device layer; measured build timings were unchanged, but no throughput benchmark was run. A dedicated partition is the eventual form.
`cargo sweep --installed` still reclaims nothing (R1488's finding stands): `rust-toolchain.toml` pins an exact 1.88.0, so no toolchain has ever rotated.

Round 1490.decision_summary: Dev executables stop carrying a private copy of the framework's DWARF: the debug info was always in the rlibs and only the linker's copying is removed, which measurement shows costs nothing and saves on both size and build time.
changes_bullets: `[profile.dev] split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` — dev executables now carry a skeleton pointing at the rlib-resident DWARF instead of a private copy of it. `Cargo.toml` records the measured pair beside the setting.
`CLAUDE.md`'s build-cache section records the measurement and the one caveat (a dev binary is debuggable only while its `target/` is intact).
verification_bullets: Controlled pair: the same 20 examples (40 executables: one bin plus one `#[cfg(test)]` test binary each) built cold into two EMPTY target dirs on the same compressed volume, differing only in `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_SPLIT_DEBUGINFO`. Cargo.toml was untouched during the experiment so it left no trace in the tree.
Tree total 5.96 -> 4.97 GiB (-16.7%), hardlink-aware (cargo hardlinks top-level binaries into deps/, and a naive per-file sum double-counts them by 3 GiB).
Per executable 101.6 -> 74.6 MiB (-26.6%). The whole tree delta (-0.99 GiB) is accounted for by the executable delta (-1.06 GiB); everything else moved +0.07 GiB.
rlib 1.06 GiB / 346 files and rmeta 0.44 GiB / 346 files were IDENTICAL in both trees. That is the proof the DWARF was not dropped: it was always in the rlibs, and only the linker's copying stopped.
Section-level: `.debug_str` 26.2 -> 1.6 MiB and `.debug_info` 9.9 -> 1.4 MiB left the binary while `.debug_line` (25.4 MiB) stayed and a `.debug_addr` skeleton (3.7 MiB) appeared.
No capability lost: `addr2line -e <binary> -f -C <addr>` resolves the SAME file:line in both builds.
On disk, measured with `compsize` (not `du`, which does not report btrfs compression): 1.6 -> 1.4 GiB, 28% -> 29% of apparent.
Build time fell as well: `cargo build` 105s -> 91s (-13%), plus `cargo test --no-run` 133s -> 119s (-11%) — there is less for the linker to copy.
Applied to the real workspace and re-measured: `hello-badge` 137.4 -> 107.8 MiB with `.debug_*` 72.1 -> 42.5 MiB, matching the experiment; `cargo test -p pinion-rpc` 1014 passed.
Release is unaffected by construction: a release binary carries 0.0 MiB of `.debug_*` (measured), so `dev` is the only profile this setting reaches.
carry_forward_bullets: The saving scales with executable COUNT, so the workspace-wide figure is an extrapolation, not a measurement: 27 MiB per executable across ~394 of them is roughly 10 GiB apparent (~2 GiB on disk after compression). Only the 20-example pair was measured directly.

A dev binary is debuggable only while its `target/` is intact. That is what a build cache is, and nothing here ships dev binaries — but a workflow that copied one elsewhere to debug would now need the rlibs too.

Compression and this setting compose rather than overlap (zstd is per-file, so N copies still cost N times), but the on-disk gain is the smaller of the two: compression already squeezes each duplicate.
Not tried: `debug = "line-tables-only"`, which would drop type and variable DWARF outright. It was not measured because this round found a change that costs nothing, and that one does not.
