Round 1491.decision_summary: R1491 - a header says which section it is sorted by: the Qt QHeaderView sort indicator becomes logical-keyed header state, so one strip is movable AND clickable and the arrow travels with its column instead of staying on a position
changes_bullets: ColumnLayout owns the sort indicator: sort_indicator (logical, ascending) + sort_indicator_shown, Qt's sortIndicatorSection / sortIndicatorOrder / setSortIndicatorShown.
ColumnLayoutState carries both, so the peer of QHeaderView::saveState() no longer drops a field saveState() carries; absent decodes as the older shape (the R1452 modes rule).
release_section commits the drop and reports the clicked LOGICAL section only when the permutation came out unchanged - Qt's rule for a header that is both movable and clickable.

grid_sort_parse lifts the grid_sort_str grammar as a STRICT parse; grid_sort_from_str is now that function with its two failure cases folded together, so the leniency is a documented weakening rather than a second parser.

Wire: query sort_indicator / sort_indicator_section / sort_indicator_order / sort_indicator_shown; intervene both writable slots; invoke set_sort_indicator / cycle_sort_indicator / clear_sort_indicator, each returning the state it reached.

hello-column-reorder is the forcing consumer: the same colhdr#<visual> strip is now movable AND clickable, paints the arrow through the col_sort_dir / sort_glyph SSOTs, carries aria-sort, and projects the body row order from the indicator via grid_order_by.
verification_bullets: pinion-core 2761 tests pass (+41 for this round); hello-column-reorder 27 pass (+7).
tools/demos/r1491_header_sort_indicator.py PASS - 49 assertions over the real wire, including a click expressed as scene/drag with both endpoints on one section.
Blast radius: r1450 / r1451 / r1452 / r1453 all PASS; r1451 pinned the whole state object by equality and was updated, which is what a whole-object assertion is for.
Counterfactual 1 (a drag also counts as a click): 3 witnesses - 1 core unit, 1 demo unit, demo assertion 17.
Counterfactual 2 (the click answers the position, not the column): 3 witnesses - 1 core unit, 1 demo unit, demo assertion 22.
Counterfactual 3 (the paint asks the glyph question by visual index): 2 witnesses - 1 demo unit, demo assertion 19.
Counterfactual 4 (no strict grammar parse): 3 witnesses - 2 core units, demo assertion 42.
Counterfactual 5 (the restore does not range-check the indicator): 2 witnesses - 1 core unit, demo assertion 47.
Gates: cargo fmt --all --check clean, clippy -D pedantic 0, cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items 0.
carry_forward_bullets: The demo's data has no bare-number column, so cell_cmp's numeric branch never fires there; assertion 25 asserts the string order it actually produces and the direction bit is discriminated separately by assertion 26.

GridSortExternal::intervene("sort") stays lenient on a malformed payload (the R778 contract, with existing consumers). Only ColumnLayout's two doors are strict; unifying them is a separate blast-radius decision.

A click cycles through cycle_col_sort's three states (ascending, descending, unsorted); Qt's QHeaderView cycles two. The three-state cycle is pinion's established grid vocabulary and the header now shares it rather than forking.

The header does not sort anything itself - a consumer connects the indicator to its model, as Qt connects sortIndicatorChanged to sortByColumn. hello-column-reorder projects the rows; a model-backed grid would drive its proxy.

Still open from the Qt QHeaderView surface: defaultSectionSize / minimumSectionSize / maximumSectionSize, cascadingSectionResizes, firstSectionMovable, and an explicit sectionsClickable flag (the click policy is the binding's today).

setDefaultSectionSize applies the new default to every SHOWN section and spares the hidden ones, which is Qt's rule and already this module's: a hidden section keeps its size, so a bulk resize a user cannot see is one they cannot undo.

The default is clamped where it is READ, not where it is written, so a bound moved afterwards carries it along and there is no second write path to forget. The raw value survives, so widening the bounds brings back the size asked for.

section_sizes is the effective logical-keyed plural: the number the header paints. sizes stays the stored plural a restore replays. section_size(logical) now reads section_sizes rather than repeating the walk, so the singular and the plural cannot answer differently.

ColumnLayoutState carries default_section_size, min_section_size and max_section_size - three fields Qt's saveState carries and R1492 added to the header without adding here. A restore replays the rule, not only its result.

Round 1494.decision_summary: R1494 - a resize is paid for by the sections after it: Qt QHeaderView's cascadingSectionResizes lands as a per-header rule with the undo memory that makes a cascade a drag rather than a destruction, on an interactive resize entry point distinct from the programmatic one
changes_bullets: ColumnLayout gains Qt's cascadingSectionResizes: readable, writable, carried by saveState, and false by default as in Qt.

interactive_resize_section is the entry point the property governs, distinct from resize_section. That split is Qt's: the property applies to interactive resizing and resizeSection() never cascades. With cascading off the two are the same call.

With it on, growing a section takes the space from the sections AFTER it, in visual order, each down to the floor; shrinking it hands that space back, most-recently-squeezed first, never past what each held before it paid.

The cascade remembers what every follower held before it paid, because a cascade that cannot be undone is not a drag. Qt keeps the same memory and clears it when the drag ends; this widget has no drag session, so the anchor stands in for one.

Only Interactive, visible sections pay: a Fixed section is fixed against a neighbour's drag as much as its own, a Stretch or ResizeToContents section derives its size and has no stored width to give, a hidden section is painted nowhere.
The followers pay as far as they can. When they are all at the floor the section still grows and visible_total reports the row actually painted, rather than refusing a resize with nothing to say why.
The gesture ends on a different anchor, on any programmatic resize, on a bulk default write, and when the rule itself is withdrawn - each of those can make a remembered size a lie.

hello-column-reorder's [ / ] gesture now calls interactive_resize_section. It was gated like an interactive resize (it refuses a Fixed section) while writing like a programmatic one. This binding has no pointer grabber, so the keyboard is its interactive resize.
The readout names the rule ("cascade on" / "cascade off"), because the same keystroke does two visibly different things depending on it.
section_and_size extracted: the two resize arms differ only in which method they call, so one parser decides for both whether a payload is Rejected or TypeMismatch.
query_parametric split out: the scalar and per-section halves answer different shapes of question and only one of them grows when a per-section fact is added.

Round 1495.decision_summary: R1495 - the push gate knows what the last push did: stop-the-line becomes a mechanical refusal to publish onto a red base, and the hook libraries get the first tests any of them have had
changes_bullets: pre-push refuses to publish onto a base whose last COMPLETED CI run failed (.githooks/lib/ci-status.sh). Stop-the-line is a ratified rule whose only enforcement was a sentence in docs/SEED_PROMPT.md - a gitignored file, read by whoever remembers to.

It reads CI's verdict; it never reproduces it. One gh call, no build. Running the full suite or the demo sweep locally is against a standing instruction, so the gate does the one thing that instruction leaves room for.

Fails open on a missing gh, no network, or no auth - infrastructure absence is not evidence of breakage - but always prints, because the failure mode it prevents is a check that silently stopped happening.

PINION_PUSH_ON_RED=1 publishes anyway, loudly. A stop-the-line rule with no way to push the fix stops the line permanently. The override is armed by the exact value only, so a stray 0 in a shell profile cannot disarm it.
Any completed conclusion other than success is red - cancelled, timed_out, startup_failure and action_required are not verdicts to build on unexamined.

tools/test_hooks.sh: the first tests any githook library has had. pre-push runs it before trusting the libs it decides with; it takes milliseconds, so the gate proves itself every time rather than being trusted because it used to work.
commit-msg-lint.sh gets coverage for the two rules that actually rejected commits this session: a subject over 72 bytes, and an indented continuation line.
CLAUDE.md records the gate, the fail-open choice, the override, and the gh-version constraint.

Counterfactual 3 (an empty listing claims green): 2 witnesses.
Counterfactual 4 (the override is armed by any value): 1 witness.
Counterfactual 5 (fail closed when gh is absent): 1 witness.
Counterfactual 6 (reintroduce the --branch flag the real gh lacks): 2 witnesses - and this one only kills AFTER the stub was hardened, which is the finding below.

carry_forward_bullets: The round's own gate was broken when first written, and its own tests certified it. gh 2.4.0 has no `gh run list --branch`; it answers usage text with exit 0 and no rows, which the caller cannot tell from "no runs yet", so the gate would have fail-opened on every push forever. It was caught by running the function against the real repo rather than the stub. The stub had accepted any arguments, so it was more permissive than the thing it stood in for, and a stub more permissive than reality tests the stub rather than the caller. The stub now rejects flags it was not taught, and CF-6 confirms the original defect now dies.
target-budget.sh is still untested. It needs a filesystem fixture (a target/ of a known size) rather than a text fixture, which is a different harness shape; recorded rather than half-built.

The gate reads the LAST COMPLETED run, so a push made while the previous run is still in flight inherits the verdict before it. That is the honest answer - an in-progress run has judged nothing - but it means two pushes in quick succession can both land before the first is judged. publishable_changes_bullets: pre-push refuses to publish onto a base whose last COMPLETED CI run failed (.githooks/lib/ci-status.sh). Stop-the-line is a ratified rule whose only enforcement was a sentence in docs/SEED_PROMPT.md - a gitignored file, read by whoever remembers to.

It reads CI's verdict; it never reproduces it. One gh call, no build. Running the full suite or the demo sweep locally is against a standing instruction, so the gate does the one thing that instruction leaves room for.

Fails open on a missing gh, no network, or no auth - infrastructure absence is not evidence of breakage - but always prints, because the failure mode it prevents is a check that silently stopped happening.

PINION_PUSH_ON_RED=1 publishes anyway, loudly. A stop-the-line rule with no way to push the fix stops the line permanently. The override is armed by the exact value only, so a stray 0 in a shell profile cannot disarm it.
Any completed conclusion other than success is red - cancelled, timed_out, startup_failure and action_required are not verdicts to build on unexamined.

tools/test_hooks.sh: the first tests any githook library has had. pre-push runs it before trusting the libs it decides with; it takes milliseconds, so the gate proves itself every time rather than being trusted because it used to work.
commit-msg-lint.sh gets coverage for the two rules that actually rejected commits this session: a subject over 72 bytes, and an indented continuation line.
CLAUDE.md records the gate, the fail-open choice, the override, and the gh-version constraint.

Round 1496.decision_summary: R1496 - a header says who may touch it: Qt QHeaderView's sectionsMovable and sectionsClickable land as header state that saveState carries, and the click stops being a by-product of a drag so the two permissions can be independent
changes_bullets: ColumnLayout gains Qt's sectionsMovable and sectionsClickable: readable, writable, carried by saveState, and false by default as in Qt, where a view opts in (setSectionsMovable / setSortingEnabled).
The two are independent, which is the reason both exist rather than one: a header may be sortable and pinned - the commoner shape - or reorderable and inert.
begin_section_drag is the movable-gated arm. A header that is not movable returns no payload, so the router opens no session: nothing previews a drop it would refuse to commit.

The programmatic move ignores the rule. Qt's moveSection() reorders a header the user cannot drag, and so do move_section and swap_sections here - the same split R1494 drew between resize_section and interactive_resize_section.
The click moves off the drop commit and onto the router's release. R1491's release_section derived it from the permutation; end_section_drag replaces it and only commits.

handle_send decodes the pointer edges: PointerDown records the pressed visual, PointerUp reports the clicked logical section when the release was on the same one, PointerLeave and PointerCancel end the press without activating it.

The press is remembered on the layout as well as on the reorder model. The model's copy is consumed by the drag - drag_release clears it before the router dispatches the release - so it cannot answer which section was pressed.
ColumnLayoutState carries the two permissions and resize_contents_precision, all three of which QHeaderViewPrivate::write() serialises.

That reverses R1454, which held the sampling bound was "what a consumer MEASURES, not what the header IS". R1454 had already abandoned that line once, making the field a Signal because the bound is an input to a painted result; the same argument saves it.

An absent permission decodes as true, not as Qt's false: the only fallback in this decoder that is not a Qt default. A pre-R1496 header had no such rule and was unconditionally movable and clickable, so true is what an older snapshot describes.

use_column_layout_with is the general form of use_column_layout, for a header that needs configuring at construction. A view fn cannot declare a permission: it runs every pass and would overwrite what the user or an agent had since written.

hello-column-reorder declares both permissions in one shared factory. R1491 put set_sort_indicator_shown in the External alone, so the header's rules depended on whether the External or the view fn reached Owner::cache first.
The readout names what the header allows, for the R1492 reason the bounds are painted: a gesture that does nothing looks like a broken widget unless the rule that refused it is on screen.
bool_rule lifted beside px_bound on its third writer, so a flag cannot accept 1 on one path and refuse it on another.
27 demo scripts called run_demo without propagating its return, so they exited 0 whatever they asserted and the CI sweep counted them green. A test that cannot fail is not a test.

Round 1497.decision_summary: A pointer target is a node that can receive the event: pointer resolution climbs past tagged decoration to the widget behind it (Qt WA_TransparentForMouseEvents / CSS pointer-events:none parity), because a tag is a name and only an External is a target.
changes_bullets: Pointer resolution answers the deepest node that can RECEIVE the event: resolve_pointer_tag walks the hit path deepest-first and returns the first tag whose primary half resolves to an External, falling back to the deepest tag when none does (window chrome).

refresh_hover, cursor_over_tag and resolve_drop_point's fallback all read that one answer, so hover cannot arm a tag the dispatch discards and a capture release cannot read off-target over the widget's own label.

Retired the router's private find_external_by_tag / tag_matches / widget_flag_walk walks for pinion_core::Scene::find_external_with_tag, whose own doc had called itself a mirror of them since R55.D.5; the R1497 predicate would have been a fourth copy.
The core walk descends Scroll.content, so an External the state scene wraps in a Scene::Scroll is now addressable by every dispatch site.
DragCaptureExternal's four bool opt-in flags became one OptIns set (clippy::struct_excessive_bools was right: they were never independent).

Round 1498.decision_summary: A row fills the viewport it was given: the last PAINTED section absorbs the leftover width (Qt QHeaderView::stretchLastSection), which is a header rule keyed by position and therefore not the Stretch mode that is keyed to a column.
changes_bullets: The last painted section absorbs the leftover viewport width — Qt's QHeaderView::stretchLastSection, off by default as in Qt, readable, writable, and carried by saveState().

Implemented as Qt's documented override rather than a second sizing pass: the last visible section's effective resize mode becomes Stretch, so the division that already exists gives it what the others leave over.

The rule is keyed by POSITION, not by column, which is why Stretch on the last column is not a spelling of it: hiding that column dropped the fill entirely and moving it painted the fill wherever the column went.

effective_resize_mode / effective_resize_modes join resize_mode / resize_modes on the wire — the same stored-versus-applied pair sizes and section_sizes already form, because a rule that overrides a mode makes the two differ.
R1494's cascade now asks the effective mode: a filled section derives its width, so squeezing its stored size would move no pixels while the cascade counted the debt as paid.
The binding's [ / ] gesture is gated on the effective mode too, and its readout names the applied modes with the set ones beside them, the shape it already used for sizes.
Nothing is written to any section, so withdrawing the rule restores the previous width by construction; Qt needs a lastSectionSize memory only because Qt writes the stretched width into the section.

Split the scalar-rule writes out of ColumnLayout::intervene (clippy 100-line, extracted rather than allowed) on the axis query_parametric uses: only that half grows when Qt's next header property arrives.
verification_bullets: Measured over the real wire before any change: stretch_last_section absent (UnknownIntrospectPath), visible_total 570 against an available_width of 640 — 70 pixels no rule claimed.
The Stretch-mode contrast measured in the same session: 4:stretch filled to 170, hiding it dropped visible_total to 470, and moving it to the front painted the 170-wide fill at x=0.

Round 1500.decision_summary: A test that reads ambient state is testing the environment, not the code: the hook suite takes its PINION_PUSH_ON_RED posture as a mandatory argument, because inheriting it let the documented stop-the-line escape hatch fail the very test that guards the rule it escapes.
changes_bullets: with_stub takes the PINION_PUSH_ON_RED posture as a MANDATORY first argument ("-" unsets it), so every case states the environment it asserts about and none can inherit one.

Two assertions on the override's stderr: a red base under an armed override still names the failing run, and still names the rule that let the push through — the exit code alone cannot tell "published because green" from "published because overridden".
The shellcheck source= directives use SCRIPTDIR, so `shellcheck -x` resolves both hook libraries from any working directory.
verification_bullets: The defect was found by using the escape hatch for its documented purpose: `PINION_PUSH_ON_RED=1 git push`, publishing R1499's fix for the red base R1497 left. pre-push runs the hook tests before trusting its own libraries, the exported value reached them, and "a red base refuses" got 0 instead of 1 — so the push was refused, for the wrong reason, by the test guarding the rule the override exists to escape.
Verified across four caller environments (unset, =1, =0, =yes): 24 assertions pass in all of them, where before the suite passed only when PINION_PUSH_ON_RED was absent.

4 counterfactuals one at a time: harness inherits the environment again = 1 failure under =1 and none when clean (the exact R1495 shape, invisible to a clean run); posture argument ignored = 1; the override's message goes silent = 2; CWD-relative source= restored = shellcheck exits 1.
shellcheck -x clean from the repo root, from tools/, and from /tmp — R1495 recorded the file as clean while SC1091 hid both libraries from the linter, so neither was ever checked through it.
No Rust changed; pinion's build and test gates are untouched by this round.
carry_forward_bullets: A gate whose documented escape hatch cannot be used has no escape hatch, and the way this one broke is that the hatch disarmed the test guarding the rule it escapes. Any future hook test that reads process state has the same exposure; the mandatory-posture argument is the shape that prevents it here.
R1498 and R1499 were still unpushed when this round opened, because this defect is what refused them.

Round 1501.decision_summary: A surface declares what it answers: the header's schema moved to the module that answers it and is composed by its consumer, because three rounds in a row added a path upstream and left the hand-copied list downstream behind, leaving five surfaces the wire answered and $schema denied.
changes_bullets: ColumnLayout::SCHEMA_FIELDS declares every path the layout answers, composed with ReorderModel::SCHEMA_FIELDS rather than restating it; hello-column-reorder composes that in turn and no longer hand-copies ~40 names.
ColumnLayout::query is gated on the declaration, so an arm no field addresses is unreachable and the round that adds one fails its own tests instead of shipping a path $schema denies.
SchemaField::concat lifts the const-fn composition hello-audio-device had written by hand; that binding now calls it, which is what a third caller of a mechanical wiring pattern earns.
Every section-keyed parametric family answers through one range check against the declared IndexOf(count) domain; five of the nine used to answer a plausible value for a column that does not exist.
logical_index_at.<x> is declared parametric with a typed argument bounded by visible_total, where it was a scalar whose path spelled a placeholder.

ColumnLayout answers count, so the domain its families declare is one this surface publishes; intervene's fall-through routes through read_only_or_unknown, so an unwritable read is ReadOnly rather than nonexistent.
verification_bullets: Measured over the real wire before the round, against hello-column-reorder: $schema declared 50 fields while stretch_last_section, effective_resize_modes, effective_resize_mode.<logical> (R1498), resize_contents_precision (R1496) and reset_default_section_size (R1493) all answered and none was declared. After: 55 fields, all five present, and a walk of the whole declaration reads every non-action path over the wire.

Measured on a 3-section header before the round: section_size.3 = 0, section_hidden.3 = false, resize_mode.3 and effective_resize_mode.3 = "interactive", content_width.3 = 0. The other four families already answered null, so the module knew the rule and five accessors' unwrap_or_default broke it on the way out. After: all nine answer null outside the domain, in-range reads unchanged.
Extending the R1353.1 dynamic audit to the layout found the resize_mode case on its first run; the layout was unreachable from that audit while its declaration lived in an example.

7 counterfactuals, one at a time, after proving the runner reports failure: a declared field deleted = 3 dead (2 are R1498's own tests, so the declaration is load-bearing across rounds); the query gate removed = 0 dead, honestly recorded, because the gate is preventive and CF-1 is what shows it is wired; the domain guard dropped = 2 including the R1353.1 audit; the family re-declared a scalar = 4 including two older suites; the refusal-origin fall-through dropped = 1 plus the demo; concat dropping its second operand = 17, of which 14 are older suites from R1450 through R1498; the count slot removed = 3 including the audit.
cargo fmt, workspace clippy with -D pedantic, and cargo doc are clean. pinion-core 2817 tests (+6), hello-column-reorder 39, hello-audio-device 8. Demo r1501_declared_surface is new at 51 assertions.

13 affected demos re-run and passing: r1450, r1451, r1452, r1491, r1492, r1493, r1494, r1496, r1497, r1498, r1501, r1347, r990. hello_audio_device cannot boot on this host because snd-dummy is not loaded; verified environmental by reverting this round's change to that binding and reproducing the identical refusal.
carry_forward_bullets: The gate is per-widget. ColumnLayout cannot grow an undeclared path; every other External in the tree still can, and IntrospectSchema.fields is still a hand-written literal at ~104 sites. What would generalise this is the per-crate audit R1353.1's own doc asks for, which now has one worked example instead of none.

SchemaField still does not separate a readable value from an invoke channel, so the declaration lists both and the tests name the 15 actions to skip them. That list is the one place in this round a path can be added without the declaration noticing.

The label in hello-column-reorder's section_cell is inset 12px, not centred; R1499's comment said centred and the paint says otherwise. Corrected in place. The real discriminator for the R1497 defect is label width against section width, which is why it could not be inferred from the tree.

Round 1502.decision_summary: The tool that gates every commit is pinned by the workspace it gates: mnemosyne.toml names the revision, the PATH binary delegates to it, and a concurrent reinstall can no longer change what pinion's hooks measure mid-session.
changes_bullets: mnemosyne.toml declares [tool].pin, so every gate on this workspace re-execs the build at $MN_ROOT/<pin>/bin instead of whatever a machine-global install happens to be.
Pinned at d02c12f (Mnemosyne R839), the newest revision whose findings pinion can act on; the comment records why R840 is held behind and what unblocks the bump.
verification_bullets: Measured 2026-07-30: the PATH binary was reinstalled at 13:26:41 by a concurrent Mnemosyne checkout, and commit eb340571 — which had just passed pre-commit — was refused by pre-push three minutes later. One gate, one tree, two answers, and nothing in the repo said which was pinion's.

The refusal is R840 ("an exclusion is a claim, now checked"). Reproduced at the PARENT commit 7f65e51b, which is already pushed and whose CI run 30505489473 is fully green, so the finding is pre-existing and unattributable to the round that hit it.

All four cited sections are SCE's own spec numbering inside vendor/sce, not this store's: 5.5, 5.10, 6.2, 6.4. Neither remedy the gate names is available — scan_exclusions already documents that scanning vendor/ would measure a document pinion does not own, and binding the citations would record a relationship that does not exist. The axis has no severity knob (the config carries nine severity_* keys and none covers it).

Delegation verified by running it: the PATH build 5bbf4d17 prints "switching to the pinned build at /home/coin/.local/mn/d02c12f/bin/mnemosyne-cli", and validate-workspace then reports the same T1=0 / entries=1479 pinion has had all along. validate-workspace and validate-code-refs both exit 0 through the pin.

The pin window is bounded at both ends and was found rather than guessed: R832 introduced the delegation this file relies on, R840 introduced the failing axis, so R839 is the newest revision that both understands [tool].pin and leaves pinion actionable.
carry_forward_bullets: The four citations are still swallowed; the pin makes the result attributable and stable, it does not make the finding go away. When upstream distinguishes a citation into another document's numbering from one into this store's, bump the pin and delete that paragraph from mnemosyne.toml.

Only two pin roots exist on this machine (d02c12f, 27396a9). A fresh clone has none, and the hooks do not install one — they will delegate to a path that is not there. The install line is in the mnemosyne.toml comment, which is where someone hitting it will be looking.

CI never runs mnemosyne-cli at all (zero references in .github/workflows), so this pin governs local hooks only. Whether CI should run the same pinned gate is a separate question this round does not answer.

Reproduced through the real hook path with the PATH binary and pin delegation, no MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP.

The first before/after was INVALID and was redone: 27396a9 silently re-exec'd to the pin and reported the pin's clean result as its own. A revision comparison needs MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP=1, or the old pin answers for the revision under test.

R858's "exactly four false positives" is upstream's own four, not pinion's. pinion's four were still live at 0c82ad73, measured. Trusting that commit message would have bumped the pin onto a red gate on the strength of a coincidence in the number.

The R867 advisory silences 5969 section-tokens under vendor/sce and upstream states nobody has read inside them. Closed structurally for pinion rather than by sampling: vendor/ holds exactly one entry, sce, at index mode 160000 — a clean submodule of scxml-core-engine — and this workspace never commits into it, so no silenced token can be pinion's own citation.

R863 verified by A/B in a throwaway workspace carrying a pin plus an unknown key, because the first draft of this round called that unverifiable without editing mnemosyne.toml, which was a false constraint: the pre-R863 build dies on the unknown key with NO hand-off, and be4c164 prints the hand-off and delegates, the delegate then dying on the key. The failure moved from before the hand-off to after it, which is the claim.

FIVE CLAIMS OF THE REPORT WERE CORRECTED by upstream's reply, which measured this tree read-only: the pin path IS verified (R832's loop guard re-checks after exec, and R861 moved that check before the hand-off), so the report's central argument against the pin mechanism was false; recommendation (C)1 is structurally dead code, since only a build that already knows the key could carry a message about it; (B) was refused because a permanent ignore region turns a loud refusal into silent non-enforcement, not on cost; two of the four swallowed ids are W3C SCXML citations expressible by prefix, so only two ever needed the file's location as their signal; and asking for a severity knob was the wrong ask, because what was imprecise was attribution, not severity.
The delegation note's doubled "this build this build", reported as a minor observation, is also fixed at be4c164.
carry_forward_bullets: THE SUBMODULE IS STILL OWED, and this round's first draft dropped it on a false reading. R863 fixes only an unknown key stopping the hand-off; it does nothing when the PATH binary predates the key entirely, which is exactly what blocked this repo twice today. Two failure modes stay open under a pinned PATH — a build below R832, and a fresh clone with no pin root — and only vendoring closes both. Upstream reached the same conclusion independently while measuring this tree.

The reasoning that dropped it was also wrong about cause: an actively developed tool makes the PATH binary churn MORE, including backwards, so upstream's same-day responsiveness raises this risk rather than lowering it.

Four pin roots now exist under ~/.local/mn (27396a9, d02c12f, 0c82ad7, be4c164) at roughly 42 MB each. Only be4c164 is referenced; the other three are inert and are kept because a future bump can then be measured without a rebuild.
CI still never runs mnemosyne-cli at all, so this pin governs local hooks only. Whether CI should run the same pinned gate is the question R1502 left open and this round does not answer either.

Backtick suppression in the citation gate is per LINE, so a code span wrapping across two lines leaves the inner text unprotected — upstream hit this in their own source while quoting this report's examples. Nothing in this tree trips it today (validate-code-refs rc=0), but a section example written into a scanned doc comment will.

Round 1504.decision_summary: The header says where its labels sit: Qt's defaultAlignment becomes header state and the per-section exception stays the model's, as Qt splits them — and the declaration learns to say which of its paths are read and which are called, so the sixteenth hand-listed action name was never written.
changes_bullets: ColumnLayout answers Qt's QHeaderView::defaultAlignment, plus the per-section exception Qt keeps in the model: default_alignment (header scalar, in saveState), alignments, section_alignment.<logical> and its override, and set_section_alignment whose value half is a spelling or the literal `default` that hands a section back to the rule.

TextAlign::as_wire / from_wire lifted to pinion-core, this round being the third consumer; the RPC writer and the TextField decoder are redefined on top, and the lifted match is exhaustive so a new variant is a compile error rather than the "Unknown" string one copy emitted and the silent Start the other chose.

SchemaField declares its channel (SchemaChannel::Read / Invoke) and $schema carries it, which clears R1501's carry (b): the fifteen action names a test held by hand were about to become sixteen, and both the unit gate and r1501_declared_surface now read the split off the declaration.
The header label is painted into a box that spans its section instead of a bare extent pinned 12px in, which is what an alignment has to align within.
verification_bullets: Six counterfactuals, injected one at a time, all fatal: effective alignment collapsing to the header rule (3 core + 2 demo-unit + script), absent decoding as the construction default (2 + script), a lenient write channel (2 + script), a restore keeping stale exceptions (2 + script), the label box collapsed (script), and the action declared as a readable path (2 + script).

CF-5 first died on an unused-variable lint rather than on behaviour, which proves nothing about the rule; it was re-injected so the box collapsed while the value stayed consumed, and then it killed the geometry assertions on their own merit.

Measured before writing the assertions rather than assumed: a label node's rect is its BOX, so the three alignments produce byte-identical trees. The rule is therefore asserted on the surface that owns it, and the tree is asserted for the box. Stated in the script instead of worked around.
gates: fmt / clippy -D pedantic / cargo doc all clean, pinion-core 2822 (+5), pinion-rpc 1014, hello-column-reorder 41 (+2), r1504 demo 43 assertions.

Thirteen demo scripts over the real wire, all green. Three needed updating and each names why: r1501 now reads the channel it used to hand-list, r1496 asserted the readout by position, and r1497's witness INVERTED — its measured asymmetry (labels 3 and 4 cover their cell centres, 0-2 do not) is now uniform, so R1499's pointer_transparent is load-bearing in all five sections rather than two.

A REGRESSION THIS ROUND CAUSED, found by running the peers and attributed by stashing: r1453 read the header label's rect as its glyph EXTENT to derive an exact content hint, a premise the box breaks. It now asserts exactness where the body drives the hint and bounds where the header does, and says which is which.
The clippy line budget was met by lifting the arm body to a method, not by an allow, the split R1494 made for section_and_size.
carry_forward_bullets: The header's glyph extent is no longer readable from the paint tree, which cost r1453 two exact assertions. Nothing in this round needed it, but a consumer that wants "how wide is this label really" has no path today; the answer would be a measurement surface, not a wider rect.

No live-pixel guard was added, so nothing proves the three alignments PAINT differently — the scene tree cannot show it by construction, and only a pixel readback can. This is the round's weakest link and the visual-widget precedent (R706/R707.3) says a guard belongs here.

SchemaField::action exists and is used by this widget and the embedded ReorderModel only. R1501's carry (a) is untouched: roughly 104 hand-written schema literals across the workspace still declare invoke channels as readable paths, and the per-crate audit its doc asks for has one more worked example now, not a sweep.

TextAlign's wire spelling is capitalised while this module's SectionResizeMode spelling is lower case. The type owns its spelling and TextAlign's had two live consumers before this round, so the inconsistency is declared rather than resolved.
Justify is reachable over the wire and skipped by the demo's cycle, because a header label is one line and the variant is a multi-line rule.

Round 1505.decision_summary: The declared alignment reaches the glyphs: the rule R1504 proved at the surface that owns it is now proved at the node it built and at the pixels it moves — measured by breaking the paint side and watching R1504's own demo pass.
changes_bullets: A demo asserts the middle link of surface -> label node -> glyphs: every colhdr_label node's style.text_align is read from the paint scene and matched against what the header reports, through the rule changing, a per-section exception, a column move, a restore that drops the exception, a sorted section, and a hidden one. The scene has carried text_align on every Text node since R55.G.10 and no assertion anywhere had ever read it.

A headless pixel guard asserts the last link: the same node shape a header label is built from is rendered through the production to_vello walk under Start / Center / End, and the ink must SLIDE — ordered, anchored to the box edges, and the same width each time, so a re-shape or a soft wrap is not mistaken for an alignment.
The guard registers its own font instead of discovering one, because a guard that leans on whatever the host has installed measures the host.

A test pins the consequence R1504 did not record: self_hosted_text_eligible has always required Start, so moving ColumnLayout's default to Center took every header label off the S5.37 arm and onto parley. The condition was documented from R1068 and never asserted; the sibling test covers hard breaks, styled runs and decoration and stops short of it.
verification_bullets: The decisive measurement: with the label's with_align dropped so every header paints flush left, R1504's own demo PASSES. Its whole paint side can be removed and the round that added it reports green. The gap was real and larger than the honest weakness it recorded, which named only the missing pixel guard.
CF-5 (the label node never receives the alignment) kills the new demo at its second assertion, naming the link it exists to prove.

CF-1 (layout.align never called) and CF-2 (the box width never handed to the shaper) each kill the pixel guard on the ordering assertion; CF-3 (aligning within half the box) survives ordering and dies on the anchoring assertion, which is why both are there.
CF-1 first died on an unused-import lint, which discriminates nothing; it was re-injected consuming both values so only the behaviour changed, the trap R1501 recorded.
CF-4 (the eligibility predicate relaxed to admit alignments) kills the arm test.
CF-1 was re-run after the guard moved onto glyph_gutters, because a refactor can silently weaken a guard.

The 3rd-consumer self-grep caught this round hand-rolling a scan glyph_gutters already performs in the same module; the guard was moved onto it and the duplicated lit-pixel count dropped rather than kept as a second measurement.
gates: fmt / clippy -D pedantic / cargo doc clean, pinion-runtime 577, pinion-shell all targets green, r1505 demo 35 assertions over the real wire, r1504 demo still green.
carry_forward_bullets: The pixel guard renders a faithful reconstruction of the label node, not the widget's own, because pinion-shell cannot depend on an example. The composition is sound only because the demo asserts the real node's fields; a binding that changed its label's box or overflow would leave the guard measuring a shape production no longer paints.
The guard is headless, so nothing yet proves alignment survives the live window path. The x11grab demos are the precedent for that and this round did not add one.

The demo mirrors the binding's label arithmetic (cell border, inset, sort-glyph width) as constants. Those numbers live in the example and a change there would make the slack premise assert against a stale formula rather than fail loudly.
R1504's carry that a label's glyph extent is not readable from the paint tree is untouched and is why the slack premise is asserted from layout arithmetic rather than measured ink.

The S5.37 arm now declines every header label. That is correct, since parley is the reference, but the arm's coverage of production text shrank and nothing tracks what fraction of painted leaves it still serves.

Round 1506.decision_summary: A guard that renders a copy of the thing under test is testing the copy: the header section paint is lifted so the pixel guard calls what the binding calls, the live window becomes a witness, and the demo stops mirroring geometry that already has a home.
changes_bullets: pinion-widget-paint::column_header lifts the QHeaderView section paint out of hello-column-reorder: ColumnHeaderStyle owns the geometry (section gap, symmetric label inset, the arrow's reserved end, the label-box arithmetic), HeaderSection is what the caller's model supplies, and header_label_node / view_header_cell are what both the binding and the tests now call. The binding keeps only the projection from its own state onto HeaderSection.

R1505's pixel guard renders that production leaf instead of a reconstruction, asserts against the LABEL BOX rather than the render target (so Start begins at the inset, not at zero), and installs its fixture font as the cache's default family because a production label names none.

tools/demos/r1506_alignment_live_pixels.py is the live-window witness R1505 lacked: three x11grab frames, one per alignment, whose difference localizes the label band without hunting the window, and the ink centroid inside it must slide rightward. It asks the X server for the screen size rather than hardcoding 1920x1080 as the sibling x11grab demos do.

crates/pinion-shell/tests/self_hosted_arm_coverage.rs measures what R1504 silently changed: with the header rule at Center the S5.37 arm paints none of the five labels, at Start it paints all five, and a sorted strip is MIXED because the arrow declares no alignment.

r1505_alignment_reaches_glyphs.py no longer mirrors any of the binding's label geometry. It measures the insets off the painted tree and asserts the invariants instead: symmetric insets, a box that tracks its SECTION rather than its string (equal-width sections with different labels get equal boxes; a resized section moves its box by the same delta), and an arrow that starts after the label box ends.
verification_bullets: CF-6 / CF-7, one at a time: with label_style no longer passing section.align through, the pixel guard FAILS and the live demo FAILS. Before the lift neither could have — the guard set the alignment on its own reconstructed node, so a binding that stopped declaring it left the guard green. That is the class the lift closes, measured rather than argued.

The live demo's first draft reported that same counterfactual as a SKIP with exit 0. It waited for a frame to differ from the previous alignment's, which conflates "the repaint has not landed" with "the repaint landed and moved nothing". Rewritten to settle on frame STABILITY, with a separate liveness premise (hiding a column must move screen pixels) that decides SKIP-vs-FAIL before any alignment is measured. Re-measured: the counterfactual now exits 1 with the right diagnosis.
That first reading of the exit code was itself wrong — `| tail` masked it and reported exit 0 for a failing run, the pipe-masks-exit-code trap this workspace already had a lesson for.
CF re-run after the clippy line-budget split, because a refactor can silently weaken a guard.

Verified on a live window: ink centroid slides 278.4 -> 299.7 -> 325.1 over a 46.7px sweep, liveness probe 9540 px. NOT on the host's own display, where the window presents black to x11grab and the demo SKIPs — the pre-existing r706 demo SKIPs there for the same reason, so this is the host, not the demo. Run on a private Xvfb display with lavapipe, which is CI's recipe.
The lift is behaviour-preserving by measurement: all 41 hello-column-reorder unit tests and all 14 of its demos pass unchanged.
The clippy line budget was met by extracting the render half into a helper plus a type alias, not by an allow.
gates: fmt / clippy -D pedantic / cargo doc clean, pinion-widget-paint 724 (+4), pinion-shell all targets green plus 3 new census tests, hello-column-reorder 41.
carry_forward_bullets: The live demo asserts an AGGREGATE centroid over the whole strip, not per section. A change that slid four labels right and one left could average out. Per-section geometry is asserted deterministically in the sibling demo and the headless guard; splitting the live assertion per section needs the screen-space section bounds, which means mapping window coordinates onto the capture.

The live demo is the sixth x11grab demo and therefore CI-row: it cannot run in a normal local sweep without a mapped window, and on a host whose windows present black it SKIPs. The SKIP path is exercised; the PASS path is verified only under Xvfb + lavapipe.
The arm-coverage census covers one widget. Nothing yet reports the arm's share across the workspace's painted text, which is the question the module docs actually pose.

ColumnHeaderStyle's defaults are hello-column-reorder's measured numbers. A second consumer with a different type scale would want them theme-derived rather than constant, and would be the signal for that.

It measures the insets off the painted tree and asserts the invariants instead: symmetric insets, a box that tracks its SECTION rather than its string (equal-width sections with different labels get equal boxes; a resized section moves its box by the same delta), and an arrow that starts after the label box ends.
publishable_verification_bullets: CF-6 / CF-7, one at a time: with label_style no longer passing section.align through, the pixel guard FAILS and the live demo FAILS. Before the lift neither could have — the guard set the alignment on its own reconstructed node, so a binding that stopped declaring it left the guard green. That is the class the lift closes, measured rather than argued.

The live demo's first draft reported that same counterfactual as a SKIP with exit 0. It waited for a frame to differ from the previous alignment's, which conflates "the repaint has not landed" with "the repaint landed and moved nothing". Rewritten to settle on frame STABILITY, with a separate liveness premise (hiding a column must move screen pixels) that decides SKIP-vs-FAIL before any alignment is measured. Re-measured: the counterfactual now exits 1 with the right diagnosis.
That first reading of the exit code was itself wrong — `| tail` masked it and reported exit 0 for a failing run, the pipe-masks-exit-code trap this workspace already had a lesson for.
CF re-run after the clippy line-budget split, because a refactor can silently weaken a guard.

Verified on a live window: ink centroid slides 278.4 -> 299.7 -> 325.1 over a 46.7px sweep, liveness probe 9540 px. NOT on the host's own display, where the window presents black to x11grab and the demo SKIPs — the pre-existing r706 demo SKIPs there for the same reason, so this is the host, not the demo. Run on a private Xvfb display with lavapipe, which is CI's recipe.
The lift is behaviour-preserving by measurement: all 41 hello-column-reorder unit tests and all 14 of its demos pass unchanged.
The clippy line budget was met by extracting the render half into a helper plus a type alias, not by an allow.
gates: fmt / clippy -D pedantic / cargo doc clean, pinion-widget-paint 724 (+4), pinion-shell all targets green plus 3 new census tests, hello-column-reorder 41.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: The live demo asserts an AGGREGATE centroid over the whole strip, not per section. A change that slid four labels right and one left could average out. Per-section geometry is asserted deterministically in the sibling demo and the headless guard; splitting the live assertion per section needs the screen-space section bounds, which means mapping window coordinates onto the capture.

The live demo is the sixth x11grab demo and therefore CI-row: it cannot run in a normal local sweep without a mapped window, and on a host whose windows present black it SKIPs. The SKIP path is exercised; the PASS path is verified only under Xvfb + lavapipe.
The arm-coverage census covers one widget. Nothing yet reports the arm's share across the workspace's painted text, which is the question the module docs actually pose.

ColumnHeaderStyle's defaults are hello-column-reorder's measured numbers. A second consumer with a different type scale would want them theme-derived rather than constant, and would be the signal for that.

Round 1507.decision_summary: The caller resolves the pin, and checks it: the gate tool is vendored at the declared revision and verified by its own --version, so neither a stale PATH binary nor a fresh clone can decide what this workspace's gates measure.
changes_bullets: vendor/mnemosyne is a submodule pinned to the revision mnemosyne.toml [tool].pin names, so the tool that gates every commit and push here can be produced from a checkout of this repository and nothing else.

.githooks/lib/mnemosyne-tool.sh resolves that pin in the CALLER rather than asking the PATH binary to re-exec the pinned build itself. Order: the installed pin under $MN_ROOT, else the vendored source built with this workspace's own toolchain, else a loud refusal naming both remedies. It never falls back to PATH.

The resolved build's revision is CHECKED, not read off the directory name: mnemosyne-cli --version reports the revision and the pin must be a prefix of it. A directory called be4c164 is a label someone typed; the binary inside it is the fact.
Both hooks use the resolver for validate-workspace and validate-code-refs, and log which source answered.
tools/test_hooks.sh grows 19 assertions over the resolver: the table-scoped pin reader, the revision check, and the refusal-rather-than-PATH behaviour.
verification_bullets: The stated entry gate, measured before any design was committed to: Mnemosyne builds under pinion's pinned rustc 1.88.0 with --locked in 1m16s, despite its own rust-toolchain.toml naming 1.94.1 — its declared rust-version is 1.88 and that is the honest number. No second toolchain is needed.

And the mechanism that makes that true was measured rather than assumed: rustup resolves rust-toolchain.toml from the WORKING DIRECTORY, not from --manifest-path. Probed both ways (1.88.0 in the outer root, 1.94.1 inside the submodule directory), then confirmed the vendored build runs under toolchains/1.88.0 when invoked from the root, which is where the hooks run.

The fresh-clone guarantee verified end to end with MN_ROOT pointed at an empty directory: the resolver built vendor/mnemosyne in 55.87s, reported revision be4c1647 matching the pin, and validate-workspace over this workspace returned rc=0 with T1=0 and zero citations swallowed.

Four counterfactuals, injected one at a time. Trusting the path instead of checking --version kills 3 assertions; a pin reader that ignores which table it is in kills 2; a silent PATH fall-back kills 3.

The fourth killed NOTHING at first. Deleting the submodule-revision check left every assertion green, because the fake submodule's build fails anyway — the test was measuring a broken Cargo.toml, not the guard. Reshaped to assert the REASON (the refusal must name the revision mismatch, which it can only do before attempting a build), and re-measured: the counterfactual now kills it.

R868's VCS-derived foreign-subtree logic absorbed the second submodule with nothing declared: the advisory reports {vendor/sce: 5969, vendor/mnemosyne: 525} and still zero citations swallowed. That is upstream's design choice paying off over the declaration this consumer originally proposed.

An inline clearance found on the way: R1500 made tools/test_hooks.sh's `shellcheck source=` directives SCRIPTDIR-relative but left the three hooks' own directives CWD-relative, so `shellcheck -x` from the repo root — where every gate here runs — followed none of them. Fixed in all three; shellcheck -x is now clean over the hooks and all four libraries.
gates: shellcheck -x clean, tools/test_hooks.sh 41 passed, validate-workspace rc=0, validate-code-refs rc=0, submodule clean with its own /target ignored.

Measured after the first draft of this round was already committed, by reading its own output: the resolver set MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP for every invocation, so the tool printed on every commit that the pin "is NOT enforced" and results "are not attributable to that revision" — the opposite of what the resolver had just verified. Probed both branches without it: the installed pin and the vendored build each recognise themselves as the pin and do not delegate, the vendored one even with MN_ROOT pointing at an empty directory (rc=0, no warning). The suppression bought nothing, so it now covers the revision PROBE only, where it is load-bearing: a binary allowed to hand off would report its delegate's revision and the check would prove nothing. Mnemosyne's own enforcement stays in place behind this one, so the pin is checked twice.

Two further counterfactuals for that boundary, using a fake CLI that reports a matching revision only when it was allowed to skip: restoring the suppression in the run path kills the assertion, and removing it from the probe kills the other.
carry_forward_bullets: The installed-pin branch trusts a build whose --version matches the pin to BE that revision's build. Verifying more would mean rebuilding it, which is the cost the branch exists to avoid.
vendor/mnemosyne/target/ is the submodule's directory and target-budget.sh measures only this workspace's target/, so the vendored build's ~1 GiB is unswept and unreported.

A fresh clone that skips `git submodule update --init` and has no installed pin cannot commit. That is intended — a gate whose tool has unknown provenance is not a gate — but it is a new way for a first-time clone to be blocked, and the message is the only thing that makes it recoverable.

Nothing yet checks that the pin and the submodule revision agree at rest; the resolver notices only when it has to build. A drifted pair with an installed pin present would go unmentioned until the day that install disappears.

The pin is now checked twice — once by this resolver, once by the tool itself. That is deliberate belt-and-braces, but it means a future Mnemosyne that changed its self-recognition could start delegating under the resolver without anything here noticing until it failed.

Round 1508.decision_summary: The pin is checked where it can actually be wrong: a dirty build is not the revision it names, a build that would delegate elsewhere is not the one checked, and the two pins are one decision verified at rest rather than only when a build is needed.
changes_bullets: The revision must be a revision: pure hex with the pin as a prefix. R1507 matched it as a bare prefix, so `be4c1647-dirty` — Mnemosyne's stamp for a build made from modified sources — passed as the pin. Measured before the fix: `be4c1647`, `be4c1647-dirty` and `be4c164-dirty` were all accepted.

The build must report the same revision whether or not it is allowed to delegate. The probe has to suppress delegation to describe the binary rather than a delegate, which makes it blind to a build that hands off elsewhere when left alone — the assumption R1507 leaned on with nothing checking it. Asking twice costs one exec.

The declared pin and the recorded gitlink are checked on EVERY run, before a source is chosen. R1507 checked the submodule only inside the vendored branch, so a workspace whose installed pin resolved never looked at it and the two could drift apart indefinitely.

A vendored build requires a clean submodule worktree. Upstream's stamp derives `-dirty` from git metadata and its own docs say an unstaged edit moves neither HEAD nor the index, adding that if a locally built binary ever has to be trusted AS a pin then something must watch the worktree instead. R1507 made a locally built binary exactly that; this is that input, and the consumer is the one who can supply it.

A never-checked-out submodule is initialised automatically, turning a fresh clone's hard block into a wait. Never one that already exists: `submodule update` force-checks-out the gitlink and would discard local work there.
`target-budget.sh` reports `vendor/mnemosyne/target/` on every push (measured 326 MiB), reported rather than swept because another repository's tree is not this budget's to reclaim.
verification_bullets: The entry audit found ⓐ was not the deliberate trade-off R1507 recorded but a hole, and upstream had already written down the case: "if a locally built binary ever has to be trusted AS a pin, this needs an input that watches the worktree rather than git's metadata". R1507 had done precisely that.

Five counterfactuals, injected one at a time. A bare prefix match kills 2 assertions; asking only the suppressed probe kills 2; tolerating a dirty vendored worktree kills 2; auto-initialising an existing checkout kills 2.

Two of the five killed NOTHING at first, both for the same reason, and both were fixed rather than accepted. Removing the at-rest dual-pin check left every assertion green because they all called the function directly and nothing asserted that the resolver CALLS it — so a test was added that drifts the gitlink while a VALID installed pin is present, which is exactly the situation R1507 left unchecked. And the dirty-worktree outcome assertion passed either way because the fixture's build fails regardless; it now asserts the reason.
That is the third appearance of one shape — an outcome asserted in a fixture that would fail anyway — after R1507's own CF-4. It is now named in the test file rather than left to be rediscovered.

Verified against the live tree, not only fakes: appending a line inside vendor/mnemosyne makes the vendored branch refuse and name the reason; setting the pin to a revision this machine HAS installed still refuses, because the gitlink check runs first.
gates: shellcheck -x clean over both hooks and all four libraries, tools/test_hooks.sh 58 passed, validate-workspace and validate-code-refs rc=0.
carry_forward_bullets: An installed MN_ROOT build made from an unstaged edit of the pinned revision still passes: the stamp cannot see it and the source it was built from is no longer there to inspect. Closed for the vendored build, where the worktree is present; not closable for an installed one without rebuilding it, which is the cost that branch exists to avoid.
The auto-init is announced but not bounded: a first clone pays an unannounced network fetch of the submodule's history before the ~1 minute build it does announce.
`vendor/mnemosyne/target/` is reported and never reclaimed. One release binary is not the accretion the budget exists for, but nothing will ever shrink it either.

The delegation cross-check compares two `--version` answers. A build that delegated to a DIFFERENT build of the same revision would agree on both and pass, which is the correct outcome by revision but not by provenance.

Round 1509.decision_summary: A check that cannot fail is not a check: R1508 asked about delegation on the one command that never delegates, so the question is now put to a command that does — and the build whose provenance this repo can actually verify is the one it uses.
changes_bullets: Delegation is probed on a command that actually delegates. R1508 asked by comparing `--version` with and without MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP; the probe is now `query --list-sections` and the assertion is that the tool's own `switching to the pinned build` announcement is absent.

The already-built vendored binary is preferred over the installed pin. Its provenance is the one this repo can check — the source is present and its worktree verified — and once the build exists preferring it costs nothing. The installed pin's role narrows to avoiding the FIRST build.
The worktree-clean condition is lifted to `mnemosyne_vendored_worktree_clean` and gates the reuse as well as the build, so the second caller cannot trust what the first refused to make.

The vendored build cache is bounded, not merely reported: over 2 GiB it is reclaimed whole, because one pinned revision has nothing worth keeping selectively and the resolver rebuilds it in about a minute.
The auto-init announcement says it clones history over the network (~200 MiB), which R1508 did while announcing only the checkout.
verification_bullets: The entry audit found that R1508's own delegation check CANNOT FAIL. Measured: `--version` is answered before the pin logic, so this machine's PATH build — revision a886cd0f, nothing like the pin — reports a886cd0f both suppressed and unsuppressed and prints no hand-off note for `--version` at all. `query` and `validate-workspace` do print it. So the check only ever discriminated against a synthetic fake modelling behaviour the tool does not have, which is the "a check that cannot fail is not a check" class (R1478) — introduced one round after citing that very lesson.
The probe's cost was measured before choosing it: 39 ms, against gates that already take minutes.

Four counterfactuals, injected one at a time: never probing delegation kills 2 assertions; removing the vendored-first preference kills 2; letting the reuse skip the worktree check kills 1; reporting the cache without reclaiming it kills 1.

The third counterfactual's first injection broke the file's syntax and produced 19 failures, which measures nothing about discrimination. Re-injected cleanly, it kills exactly the one assertion it should.

Four R1508 tests broke on this round's changes, all for one reason worth keeping: the fakes answered only `--version`, so they were no longer models of a thing that now runs a real command. They were taught the command surface rather than the check being loosened — and the `delegating` fake was rewritten to announce a hand-off, which is what the tool does, instead of changing its `--version` under suppression, which it does not.
Two behaviours had no assertion at all when introduced and now do: which source wins when both are available, and that a dirty worktree disqualifies the vendored binary it would otherwise reuse.
The over-budget cache path is exercised with a sparse file, because `du -sbL` measures apparent bytes — so a 3 GiB assertion costs no disk.
gates: shellcheck -x clean over both hooks and all four libraries, tools/test_hooks.sh 66 passed, validate-workspace and validate-code-refs rc=0.
carry_forward_bullets: The delegation probe matches upstream's wording. If that message changes it fails OPEN — it stops detecting hand-offs rather than refusing everything. Only the matcher's own behaviour is testable here; that the real tool still prints that string is not.

An installed build made from an unstaged edit of the pinned revision still passes, and cannot be told apart without rebuilding it. The exposure is now one clone's first commit rather than every run, since the vendored binary takes over afterwards.
The probe adds one 39 ms command to every hook run, and it reads the store — so it is doing real work whose only purpose is to observe whether a hand-off happened.
Nothing verifies that the reclaimed vendored cache is actually rebuilt on the next run; the two halves are tested separately.

Round 1510.decision_summary: The header dresses the sections the selection reaches: Qt QHeaderView::highlightSections, where the header owns the rule and the view owns the selection. The rule is saved state; the per-logical-section coverage is a consumer-published input like content_widths and is not. Qt's two paintSection predicates become one three-state SectionSelection, and its two style flags reach two properties of the label — weight and colour — leaving the section fill to the drag and the keyboard cursor. carry_forward_bullets: (a) THE WEIGHT HAS NO PIXEL WITNESS, and cannot have one from this repo: the two
bundled font fixtures are Regular-only and committing a production font is
disallowed, while resolving the face through the host is the host-dependence
R1473/R1500 forbid. Measured both ways (174/174 pinned, 161->251 host). The
weight is asserted on the node and at the §5.37 arm only.
(b) CONTAINER BORDERS NEVER PAINT — the runtime's `Scene::Container` arm fills
and shadows but never strokes `BoxStyle::border`, so 45 container-attached
declarations are silently dropped (`button.rs` focus ring, `tooltip.rs`,
`menu.rs`, `checkbox.rs`, `listbox.rs`, `table.rs`, ~14 examples). Found by this
round's pixel guard reading 0. Its own round: the fix changes pixels in ~30 files
at once and needs the full demo sweep.
(c) THE EXAMPLE'S SELECTION IS NAMED, NOT DERIVED. `s` sets a section's coverage
directly; a real grid derives none/partial/full by comparing selected rows in a
column against its row count, which is what Qt's header does with the selection
model. This binding has no cell cursor, so the demo exercises the publish path
and not a derivation.
(d) NOTHING STRUCTURALLY FORCES A CONSUMER THROUGH THE GATE. `highlights` is the
rule-gated row and `selections` is not; a binding that painted from the second
would bypass the rule. This one reads `highlights`, and only review enforces
that.
(e) THE §5.37 ARM DECLINES MORE TEXT NOW. Every bold or italic leaf leaves it, on
top of every aligned one (R1504). Correct — the arm cannot pen those faces — but
the share of production text it still serves is measured for ONE widget only
(`self_hosted_arm_coverage.rs`), which is the R1506 carry this round did not
widen.
(f) THE R806 CANARIES STILL HAVE NO CI COVERAGE OF THEIR UPSTREAM HALF. They now
run in CI and skip it loudly under lavapipe rather than being excluded by name,
which is strictly more information, but the flood assertion itself can only be
exercised on a hardware adapter and CI has none. `adapter_floods_top_tile` reads
the adapter CLASS rather than probing for the flood, so a hardware adapter on
which upstream fixed the bug is the one case it reports correctly and a CPU
adapter on which the flood appeared would be misread.
(g) THE FRESHNESS DEFENCE IS OPT-IN. `expect_rebuild=True` has to be passed by a
caller who knows the source just changed; nothing detects that on its own, and
the demo harness's own `ensure_build` path does not pass it (it is the
no-change case, where `fresh` is the correct answer). Cargo's content-hash
freshness (`-Z checksum-freshness`) would remove the need entirely and is
nightly-only against this workspace's pinned stable toolchain.

Round 1511.decision_summary: The renderer honours the border the scene declares — one painter for a styled rect, so a Container and a Box cannot disagree
changes_bullets: paint_adapter: lift `paint_box_decoration` (shadows -> background -> border) and route all FIVE styled-rect sites through it — `Scene::Box` and `Scene::Container` in `to_vello_inner`, the same pair in `to_vello_cached_inner`, and the cacheable-container fast path. Before R1511 the four arms open-coded the sequence and only the two `Box` ones stroked a border, so a border declared on a `Scene::Container` reached the TUI walker and the PDF projector but never the GUI.

The census: 91 `with_border` sites, 45 of them on containers. Audited one by one for what the fix makes visible. Round 1512.decision_summary: The renderers are compared where they can diverge — one backend-neutral property, three cells, each with teeth
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-shell/tests/backend_parity.rs` — the cross-renderer contract test R1511 recorded as absent. The three renderers emit incomparable artifacts (a vello `Encoding`, a ratatui cell `Buffer`, a PDF content stream), so the asserted property is backend-neutral: for every renderer and every node type, rendering a scene WITH a declared border must differ from rendering it WITHOUT. R1511's defect is exactly one cell of that matrix — vello x Container — having been equal.

Determinism is asserted first and is load-bearing: each probe renders the same scene twice and requires the bytes to match, because an inequality between two renders is evidence only if the renderer is stable for a fixed scene.

A second test says what each renderer does in its OWN vocabulary (one extra vello path, four box-drawing corners, a longer PDF stream), so a failure names the missing artifact instead of reporting that two blobs matched. Deliberately the weakest specific claims — tighter geometry belongs in each renderer's own suite, and duplicating it here would make this file a competing source of truth for three backends.

`pinion-shell` is the home because it is the cheapest crate that can see all three: it already enables `pinion-runtime/vello` unconditionally, so the GPU-free `to_vello` walk needs no new wgpu dependency anywhere, and it already hosts the cross-cutting render proofs. `pinion-tui` + `pinion-pdf` join as dev-dependencies; neither is a cycle. A crate whose only purpose is cross-renderer conformance is the alternative, and one contract item does not justify it — the second one landing here is the signal.
verification_bullets: Three counterfactuals, one per renderer, all dead and each naming its own cell: drop the border from vello's Container arm = 2 kills, "vello ignores the border declared on a Scene::Container"; disable the TUI walker's border draw = 2, "the TUI walk draws all four box-drawing corners"; disable the PDF stroke = 2, "the PDF projector emits more content". So no cell is decorative.

The R1511 carry item (d) was MEASURED rather than assumed, and the measurement changed what should be done about it. `access_node` takes the shell's live `focused` parameter and compares `focused == Some(TAG)`; it never reads the focus half of the binding's own state tuple. So that half is not merely unused by the view — it is a dead per-frame computation, `read_button_focused` walking the scene once per button.

Removing it is safe: with the focus half deleted from `hello-dialog`'s state, `r694_focus_ring` and `r693_dialog` both pass, AND — the load-bearing check, because those demos read the RPC produce mirror rather than the live window — `scene/frame_timings.frame_count` still advances on a focus change with nothing forcing a paint (41 -> 49 with the half removed, 42 -> 50 with it present). The shell repaints on focus of its own accord.

But a blanket removal would be WRONG, which is the second thing the measurement found: `hello-combobox` reads `state.trigger_focused` to choose a border colour. At least one binding genuinely consumes the value, so the removal is per-file with verification, not a sweep. The probe was reverted; no binding changed this round.

Round 1514.decision_summary: The comparison sees everything the renderer emits, and the table is the census the type publishes
changes_bullets: The R1512 parity matrix compared two of its three renderers through a LOSSY reduction. vello was serialized as path geometry alone (`n_paths`, `n_path_segments`, `path_data`) and the TUI as `cell.symbol()` — neither carried a single colour. Measured before touching anything: six cells were false negatives. `fill` reads as IGNORED by vello and by the TUI, whose own doc says it paints a fill as the cell `bg`; `gradient` reads as IGNORED by vello, whose `fill_box_bg` paints it in both arms. Only the PDF stream, serialized whole, was right — the control that showed the other two were instruments, not evidence.

Both reductions now carry the whole artifact: every vello encoding stream (`path_tags` / `draw_tags` / `draw_data` / `transforms` / `styles` and the counters, not just path data) and the whole ratatui cell (symbol AND fg / bg / modifier). The matrix goes from 18 cells to 30 and all pass.

A precondition is asserted before any verdict is read, beside determinism: each reduction must distinguish a change that moves NO geometry. It uses a `TextStyle` colour — a change no row in the table needs to be right about — so the guard cannot be satisfied by the same path the rows exercise. This is the check whose absence let R1512 ship.

Non-observation splits in two. `Ignores` = the medium cannot carry it, a contract. `Gap` = the medium CAN and this renderer does not, a debt with a name. Both assert the same byte-equality; the difference is what the reader is told. R1512 recorded "the PDF projector paints fill + border only" as though it were a property of PDF, while the projector's own doc files gradients and shadows under "Deferred ... additive when a consumer arrives".

Round 1515.decision_summary: A probe must be located relative to the feature it asserts about, or it measures the rasteriser
changes_bullets: `r1511_container_border.py` was the ONE failure in the R1513 sweep (469 of 470 passed, so R1511's ~30-file pixel change is otherwise clear). It failed its FIRST CI run at "a checked box is FILLED — the centre carries ink", having passed locally in the round that wrote it.

Root cause is a property of the widget, not the runner: the M3 checkmark is drawn in `on-primary`, which is near-white — the SAME side of the demo's `INK` threshold as the page — so a checked box is not a solid block of ink. The glyph carves a page-coloured trail through the fill, and measured on a real capture that trail runs within ONE pixel of the centre column.

The two states were never close: the interior is 0.0000 inked when hollow and 0.9568 when filled. R1511 reached for the one measurement with a one-pixel margin when the one with total margin was available.

The interior claims are now AREA measures (`interior_ink`), applied in all three places that had point probes — hollow, filled, and hollow-again after the round trip. The hollow side gets stronger too: three sampled points become all 324 interior pixels.

The failure message reports the measured fraction and says what each end means, so a future failure discriminates by itself: ~0.00 is a hollow box (the click never landed, or the fill was dropped) and ~0.96 is a filled one.

A second assertion pins that `filled < 1.0` — the glyph must be there. Demanding a perfectly solid interior would forbid the checkmark, and the two bounds together say "filled AND checked" rather than merely "not page".
verification_bullets: The CI failure was reproduced WITHOUT CI, on a real capture: shifting the probe by two pixels flips the old single-pixel assertion from PASS to FAIL while the interior fraction is unchanged at 0.9568 for every offset from -3 to +3. That is the whole defect, measured.

What was ruled out first, by measurement rather than by argument: the adapter (forced lavapipe locally — PASS), the display (Xvfb :98 + hidden window, 6 runs — PASS), a timing race (20 runs including 8 under full 32-core load — PASS), and a stale frame (`capture_window_screenshot` calls `render_window` synchronously, so the screenshot re-renders rather than reading a presented frame).

CF-1, the click withheld: FAILS with `got 0.0000 (threshold 0.8)` and the message names the right cause — "the box is still HOLLOW: the click did not land, or the fill was dropped". So the area measure still catches the failure a point probe was there to catch.

Class audit, as [[zero-flake-policy]] requires: every other demo using `png_pixel` / `is_ink` either scans a REGION in a loop or compares against a known colour with a tolerance over a flat fill. `r1511` was the only one asserting a lone interior point in a filled area that another near-page feature crosses.

Which pixel moved in CI is NOT established and is recorded as such — a font-driven layout shift and a different rasterisation phase are both consistent with the evidence. The fix is invariant to all of them, which is why it did not need to be settled.
carry_forward_bullets: The CI-vs-local divergence itself is unexplained at the mechanism level. Everything reproducible locally was reproduced and none of it failed; only the assertion's fragility is proven. If the demo fails again the reported fraction will say which side it is on, which is the check this round could add and the diagnosis it could not.
The 6 live-pixel demos CI skips for want of Pillow (`r706`, `r707`, `r786`, `r787`, `r794`, `r1506`) are still vacuous there, unchanged by this round.

changes_bullets: `pinion_core::scene::SceneNodeKind` — the census of `Scene` variants,

header names the `Mesh` / `Camera` / `Light` variants meant to land in
Phase C) and no other crate can enumerate or exhaustively match it. Two
compile links, the `BoxFacet` (R1514) prescription one axis over: a new

crate, and the census variant it forces fails every downstream `match`.

and `clips_subtree()`.
`Scene::box_style() -> Option<&BoxStyle>` — the accessor behind "what did
this node declare visually", exhaustive where the variant list is knowable.

focus-ring corner-radius walk in `pinion-overlay` (production — a rounded
node of a future kind would have been ringed square), a `MatchBoxStyle`
trait in `pinion-runtime`'s test module whose comment called itself
one-off, and the backend-parity matrix about to grow the third.

Container }` with a doc comment claiming it was complete; `clip` joins as a
