Round 1517.decision_summary: The accessibility tree's focus flag has one source, and the gate that says so found three bindings that had another
changes_bullets: `read_button_focused` doc — the canon. pinion answers "is this focused" on
three channels and they are not interchangeable: this per-External boolean
("am *I* focused", for a composite painting its own ring, on the paint's
cadence), the `focused: Option<&str>` argument of `access_node` /
`access_focus_target` / `apply_key` (the shell's live tag — the canonical
source for the a11y tree), and `focus_state::focused()` (R1327's reactive
binding-wide tag, for display state derived from focus). R1513 registered this
as a two-source ambiguity; there were three, and the third — the seam R1513
called a design change still to be made — had existed since R1327.
`hello-property-grid` — the asset dialog's two action buttons took their AT
focus flag from `read_state`, walking the painted scene. Removed: the paint
discarded those halves, so the walk existed only to answer a question the
shell already answers. Its roving tree cursor is now gated on the grid owning
shell focus, matching what its own `access_focus_target` already did.
`hello-data-grid` — `access_node` ignored the shell argument (`_focused`)
and flagged the cell at the roving cursor unconditionally; the cursor and the
open popup's option cursor are both gated now.
`hello-inspector` — the object and property cursors were gated on the
binding's INTERNAL pane region only, not on the binding owning shell focus.
`rpc_verify.access_node_by_tag` + `access_focus_flags` — obligation-3b lift:
five demos carried a byte-identical private node lookup (r979-r983). The
access tree is a flat list, so it is a scan, not `find_by_tag`'s descent —
its own name rather than a flag on that one.
`tools/demos/r1517_at_focus_one_source.py` — the gate, over five bindings.
verification_bullets: The entry hypothesis was refuted twice by measurement before anything was
written. "The snapshot source goes stale across frames" — measured over the
wire: a read dispatch cannot mutate focus, so the producer's snapshot and the
manager's tag are the same instant; and re-opening the modal showed no sticky
residue either. What was left was not a reachable wrong answer but a second
derivation, fresh by an ordering coincidence the a11y builder does not control.
The invariant's SHAPE was measured, not guessed. The first draft asserted
"the flagged set == the focus/get tag"; four bindings x 7 samples showed that
is false for a roving composite, which flags a DESCENDANT (`data_grid#0_0`
under the `data_grid` stop). The shipped predicate is "every flagged tag is
accounted for by the manager's tag" — itself or `{stop}#...`. Written before
measuring, it would have reported correct behaviour as a failure.
The gate then failed on its first run, against bindings this round had not
touched. `hello-data-grid` and `hello-inspector` each flagged a node at boot
with `focus/get` = null. `hello-property-grid`, after the cursor moved and
Tab left the grid, reported TWO tags claiming focus at once while its own
`access_focus_target` correctly named only the search box — a tree
contradicting its own focus target. All three violate the WAI-ARIA
precondition that `aria-activedescendant` holds only while the composite owns
focus; the workspace's own overwhelming convention
(`group_focused && i == active`) was already correct, and these three were
the exceptions.
Four `hello-inspector` tests encoded the old behaviour: they called
`access_node(state, None)` and expected a focus flag, leaving "the inspector
has focus" an unstated premise. Now passed as `Some(INSPECTOR_TAG)`.
Counterfactuals, one at a time, all fatal: CF-1 (data-grid cell gate reverted)
= boot flag; CF-2 (property-grid cursor gate reverted) = the two-claim case,
naming both tags; CF-3 (inspector gate reverted) = boot flag; CF-4 (the
round's own subject re-sourced wrongly) = the dialog case. CF-4's first
attempt died at COMPILE (unused argument), which measures nothing about the
demo, so it was rewritten to consume the argument and source from it wrongly.
CF-5 = the unit guard, which fails before the fix and after re-injection.
Gates green: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D pedantic` on the four
changed crates, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets`. hello-property-grid 82 (+1),
hello-inspector 78, hello-data-grid 144, pinion-widget-paint 724.
Demos: `r1517_at_focus_one_source.py` PASS, 126 assertions over 20 focus
stops (counted by the demo itself, not claimed by its docstring). The 21
demos of the three changed bindings that touch `scene/access` or focus all
PASS, including the five whose helper was lifted.
carry_forward_bullets: The gate walks five bindings. A binding it does not walk can still source an
AT focus flag from anywhere — this is a runtime census over a chosen list, not
a structural impossibility, and no type prevents an `access_node` from
ignoring its `focused` argument while emitting a flag. The grep that found
these three (emits a flag AND ignores the argument) is repeatable but is a
grep. Closing it structurally would mean the a11y builders taking focus as a
value only the shell can mint, which is a larger design change than this
round.
`hello-inspector`'s two remaining `access_node(state, None)` test calls are
left alone: they assert roles and values, not focus, so `None` is honest
there.
The `focus_state::focused()` channel — the third one this round names as
canon for its own question — has NO production consumer in the workspace
(measured): only a `pinion-shell` test fixture calls it, and the two examples
that mention it do so in prose. So the channel a binding should use to derive
display state from focus is documented and tested but undogfooded, and nothing
forces such a binding to use it rather than caching an `apply_key` argument,
which is the staleness R1327 was written to prevent.

Round 1518.decision_summary: The AT focus target and the tree's per-node focus flag are one answer, stamped where both are known
changes_bullets: `pinion_a11y::build_access_tree` — the assembler every embedder shares (the
AccessKit emit, the `scene/access` dump, the TUI shell) now STAMPS each node's
`AccessState::focused` from the `AccessFocus` it just read: the bearer is the
focused composite's `active_descendant` when it names one, else the focus tag,
and nothing when no target exists. A binding can no longer claim focus the
shell did not grant, drop one it did, or put it on a node other than the one
the AT was told about — for all 186 `access_node` implementations at once,
whether or not a demo walks them.
`AccessFocus::addressing(parent, Option<child>)` — obligation-3b lift at the
4th identical `map_or_else(atomic, composite)` site (`grouped_focus_target`,
the dock tab strip, the inspector cursor, the property grid's tree cursor).
Mechanical wiring, no policy: a roving cursor that MAY rest on a descendant.
`pinion_widget_paint::dock_tablist_focus_target` — the focus-target half of
`dock_tablist_access_nodes`, which shipped without one. A focused strip now
names its active tab; both consumers (`hello-tabbed-chart`,
`hello-dock-panels-editor`) adopt it.
`hello-data-grid` — reports the 2-D roving cursor's gridcell as the active
descendant, through the same `cell_tag` its nodes are built with. Its doc
claimed the cell's own `focused` flag "marks the cell active descendant"; that
flag is not lowered to AccessKit at all, so the claim was false.
`hello-inspector` — gains `access_focus_target` plus an
`access_cursor_tag` state method, naming whichever region's cursor is
live (the object row or the property row). Also `PROP_PREFIX` /
`prop_tag`, a 3-site lift of the `prop_<i>` spelling the paint, the a11y
node and the AT-action parse each spelled out.
`hello-model-chart` — delegates to `radio_composite::composite_focus_target`,
the substrate its sibling radio bindings already use.
`tools/demos/r1518_at_focus_one_answer.py` — the end-to-end gate, 14 bindings.
`tools/demos/r1517_at_focus_one_source.py` (D) — "stale" now means a claim the
reopened stop does not ACCOUNT FOR, not merely one that is not the stop.
verification_bullets: The canon was measured, not chosen. The entry hypothesis — the bearer is
`active_descendant ?? focus_tag` — was REFUTED on first measurement: 12 of 70
samples disagreed. Widening to every example (188 measured, 940 observations:
boot plus four `focus/next` stops) put a number on it: 144 disagreed with the
target the same tree published. 130 MISSING (a focus target no node echoed),
11 MOVED (a roving cell flagged for the AI while the AT heard only the
container), 3 OVERCLAIM (a flag with no focus anywhere, at boot). The
disagreements were not noise — they were three distinct defect shapes, and
`hello-tree-view` at a stop showed what the correct shape looks like.
What made the direction decidable was reading the lowering: `lower_access_node`
carries `checked` / `mixed` / `disabled` and NO focus. The per-node flag never
reaches a screen reader; it is the wire's spelling of what `AccessFocus` tells
AccessKit. So it is derivable, and the sharpest defect was that the AI mirror
was RICHER than the AT truth — `hello-data-grid` named `data_grid#0_0` for an
AI client and told a screen reader only "Asset table".
After: the same census twice — 907/28 and 905/30 OK/MISSING, OVERCLAIM and
MOVED both ZERO. The 28-30 residue is a different axis (below).
Counterfactuals, one at a time, all fatal. CF-1 (stamp removed) killed all five
unit guards and the demo at its first binding, with the pre-fix symptom
verbatim. CF-6 (bearer ignores `active_descendant`) killed exactly the two
composite guards and left the other three passing. CF-2/3/4/5 (each repaired
binding stops reporting its cursor) each killed section (C) — and NOT (A)/(B),
because the stamp keeps the wire self-consistent either way, which is why (C)
exists. CF-3's first attempt died at COMPILE (unused argument), measuring
nothing, so it was rewritten to consume the cursor and discard it.
Gates green: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D pedantic` on the 8 changed
crates, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`, and
the tests of the changed crates AND the assembler's consumers — pinion-shell
1016, pinion-tui, pinion-rpc — because "touched crate" means the crate whose
behaviour changed, consumers included.
Demos: `r1518_at_focus_one_answer.py` PASS, 164 assertions over 56 focus stops
in 14 bindings (counted by the demo, not claimed by its docstring);
`r1517_at_focus_one_source.py` PASS 130; and r705 focus-ring placement,
The focus ring moved, measured: `resolve_focus_ring_tag` reads the same
`active_descendant`, so the shell overlay now frames the cursor cell rather
than the whole container for the four repaired bindings — which is what R705's
doc says the ring is for. Of the four, only `hello-inspector`'s row paints its
own border as well.
carry_forward_bullets: A focus stop absent from its own AT tree is the residue the stamp exposed and
cannot fix: 28-30 observations over 8 bindings where the target names a tag the
tree does not contain, so AccessKit collapses focus onto the window root and a
screen-reader user hears nothing about the control. Two are deliberate
(`settings-panel` "AT-invisible for v1", `hello-window-focus-multi`'s empty
`WidgetA11y`); the rest have a populated tree with a stop missing from it. The
demo REPORTS these rather than absorbing them, but does not assert them.
The 78 binding-side `focused:` computations are now non-authoritative — the
stamp overwrites them. Sealing `AccessState::focused` so a binding cannot spell
it at all is the structural end state, and it is a multi-round migration: 78
set sites across 66 files and 267 assertions across 80 files, most of which
call `access_node` directly and would need re-pointing at the assembler.
`hello-inspector` moves from the "overlay rings the container" side of
debt-toolbar-double-indicator to the "overlay rings the same item the item
rings" side: its object row paints a white 2px cursor border AND is now framed
by the shell ring. That is the registered styling debt (current-item is not
focus — Qt separates them), not a reporting one; reporting the descendant is
the correct AT behaviour.
Observed and unexplained, recorded rather than resolved: two SIGSEGVs at boot
(one per census run, ~1 in 187) in a throwaway 187-process measurement harness,
on a DIFFERENT example each time (`hello-dock-panels`, then `hello-no-primary`)
and never reproducible — 101 targeted boots of both, including the full walk,
were clean. No mechanism links it to this round (safe Rust, bounded loop). The
pre-change run saw none in 188, which at n=1 does not distinguish a rate change
from chance. CI's sanctioned sweep is the check.

Round 1519.decision_summary: Phase B is re-tallied, and the tally becomes a tool whose judgments carry the evidence they were made against
changes_bullets: `tools/phase_b_tally.py` (new) — the Phase B progress tally, as a tool. It does
NOT compute the percentage: "how complete is the DCC axis against Qt" is a
judgment, and a script emitting a number for it would be inventing precision.
It counts the evidence each axis rests on, holds each judgment NEXT TO the
evidence snapshot it was made against plus the round it was made in, and
reports STALE when today's evidence has drifted past 25% of that snapshot. So
the number stays human and its staleness becomes mechanical.
It also reports what it cannot classify, and what it deliberately excludes and
why — an axis-less body of work is exactly how the dataviz campaign became
invisible.
It derives the value order (LEVERAGE = weight x remaining, buildable axes only)
rather than trusting a hand-written list.
`--selftest` checks its own logic, including that the staleness detector can
actually fire and that no input is silently dropped.

Round 1520.decision_summary: The paint-fragment cache survives a scroll: fragments are transform-free
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-runtime/src/paint_adapter.rs` — the §5.16 fragment cache takes
its fast path at ANY inherited transform, not only `Affine::IDENTITY`. A
fragment is always encoded at `IDENTITY` and the inherited transform is
supplied to `vello::Scene::append`, which pre-multiplies every transform in
the appended encoding (glyph runs included). That closes the R682+1 carry
R682's own doc registered.
`paint_hash` becomes a COMPLETE cache key rather than one that is merely safe
under a side condition: the stored fragment cannot contain a transform, so two
placements of the same content share one entry by construction.
The walk now carries three facts about where a subtree lands, which used to be
one because they were the same value. `transform` is the ENCODING frame and
resets to `IDENTITY` inside a cached fragment. `placement` is the SCREEN frame
and never resets. `clip` is the accumulated clip in screen space, narrowed at
each `Scene::Scroll` by its viewport.
`last_damage_region` is computed from `placement` intersected with `clip`, so
it publishes where a missed container's pixels actually are. `screen_bounds`
maps a rect's four corners through an affine and clamps into the unsigned
`Rect` space; `intersection` is its local peer.
`crates/pinion-shell/src/headless_screenshot.rs` — a lavapipe pixel guard that
the cached scrolled placement is byte-identical to the uncached reference walk,
on the first paint AND on the cache-hit replay.
`tools/demos/r1520_scrolled_paint_cache.py` (new) — the wire proof over
`scene/cache_stats`, driving `hello-virtual-list`.
verification_bullets: The round was chosen by `tools/phase_b_tally.py`: pro-tool performance is the
derived LEVERAGE leader (weight 9 x remaining 50), and its stated gap was "no
measured hot-path optimisation". This is one.
Measured first, on an idle box. The entry hypothesis was wrong: a first harness
said the encode walk costs 3.7us/node, which turned out to be TEXT SHAPING, not
walk overhead (boxes 110ns/node vs texts 6264ns/node). Correcting that is what
found the real defect.
One paint of 4,681 unchanged nodes: 22us bare, 1,360us wrapped in a `Scroll` at
a non-zero offset, and IDENTICAL warm or cold — the cache was inoperative. After:
42us. Reported as the scroll/bare RATIO measured inside one binary, 61.8x -> 1.83x,
because that ratio is immune to machine noise while the absolute numbers are not.
The cliff's SHAPE is what made it worth closing: caching worked at offset 0 and
died at the first scrolled pixel, so it was absent from exactly the frames a
pro-tool workload spends its time in.
The equivalence is structural, and was checked rather than assumed: the ONLY use
of the inherited transform in the whole paint adapter that was not a left
composition was the identity gate itself, so `T * (IDENTITY * local) == T * local`
holds at every paint site.
Wire counterfactual on `hello-virtual-list`, measured both ways: cacheable
fragments 4 -> 36, per scrolled frame 1 hit / 2 misses -> 19 hits / 6 misses.
FOUR. The entire binding offered four cacheable containers because everything
inside the list lived under a scroll translation.
Three gates, deliberately not redundant, each with its own counterfactual.
Dropping the transform at placement leaves ALL SIX runtime counter tests GREEN
and fails the pixel guard by 7,105 bytes. Restoring the identity gate fails three
counter tests. Dropping the clip fails exactly the two damage tests. No gate
covers another's failure mode.
The clip was very nearly shipped as a carry, and the carry was wrong. Letting the
cache into scrolled subtrees put a scrolled container's own rect into
`last_damage_region`, and a virtual list's content container is as tall as the
data set: the wire reported a 320,000px-tall region inside a 460px window. The
stated excuse — that tightening it "wants a partial-blit consumer to design
against" — does not survive contact: a clipped container paints nothing outside
its clip, so the intersection is unconditionally correct and strictly tighter,
with no policy for any consumer to choose. It is 460 on the wire now.
Local: 585 pinion-runtime + 16 pinion-shell suites, 29 lavapipe `--ignored` pixel
tests, clippy/fmt/doc clean, and every demo that reads `scene/cache_stats`
(r682 / r681 / r827 / r831 / r889) plus three scrolled-pixel demos.
carry_forward_bullets: The first scrolled frame after an idle frame still misses broadly: R682's
mark-and-sweep evicts everything the root-hit walk did not consult, so an idle
frame leaves only the root fragment and there is nothing to re-place at the new
offset. Reuse is a steady-state property, which the demo asserts as one. This is
R682's eviction policy, not something R1520 introduced, and changing it changes
the memory bound R682 chose deliberately ("no LRU heuristic, no fixed cap" —
boundedness derived FROM mark-and-sweep). A retention policy that survives an
idle frame is a real axis with a real trade-off; registered rather than
hand-waved.
`last_damage_region` still reports a missed container's whole clipped rect
rather than the sub-area whose pixels moved. Over-coverage is the safe direction
(under-coverage is a stale-pixel bug) and this is R682's granularity, unchanged.

Round 1521.decision_summary: The shape cache grows into its working set, on proof rather than a guess
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-text/src/cache.rs` — the §5.36 shape cache's capacity ADAPTS
to its working set instead of standing at a fixed 256. It grows only on
proof it was too small: a miss on a key this cache itself evicted, the
ghost list of 2Q / ARC. A key that returns after eviction witnesses a
working set that did not fit; a key that never returns is a scan, and a
scan grows nothing.
The ghost list is sized to `MAX_CAPACITY`, NOT to the capacity. Sized to
the capacity (the 2Q/ARC convention, and this round's first attempt) it
detects a working set only up to about 2x the capacity: beyond that a
cycle's own evictions push the earlier evidence out before the cycle comes
round to supply it. At 256 vs 1,200 — the case that motivated the round —
it never fires at all. Ghosts are `u64` hashes, not keys.
`grow` clears the ghost list. Without that, one round of evidence is spent
one evicted key at a time: a 300-leaf scene arrives at pass two with 44
ghosts and grows five times on them, landing at 8,192 for a set that fits
`with_max_capacity(initial, max)` is new and makes a hard bound
expressible; `max == initial` pins the capacity and reproduces the old
behaviour exactly. The cliff is now something a caller opts into, not
something every caller inherits from a constant.
`crates/pinion-core/src/text_cache_stats.rs` (new) — `TextCacheStats`, the
snapshot type, in the parley-free crate so `pinion-rpc` can hold a typed
slot without depending on `pinion-text`. Same split as `SystemFontStatus`.
`crates/pinion-rpc/src/text_cache_stats.rs` (new) + dispatch + registry —
`scene/text_cache_stats`, per-SHELL rather than per-window because one
`LayoutCache` serves every window.
`tools/demos/r1521_shape_cache_working_set.py` (new) — the wire proof over
two Model/View-at-scale bindings.
verification_bullets: The round was chosen by `tools/phase_b_tally.py`: pro-tool performance is
the derived LEVERAGE leader (weight 9 x remaining 50).
Measured first, in the paint walk, release. Steady-state cost of one paint
of N text leaves through a shell-sized cache, before -> after: 256 leaves
1200 leaves 27.4 -> 1.59 ms. A 17% content increase (256 -> 300) multiplied
the per-frame cost by TEN and never recovered, because LRU on a cycle
longer than its capacity has a 0% hit rate, not a degraded one.
1,200 leaves is a 30-column data grid with 40 visible rows and cost 1.6x
the whole 60fps budget on shaping alone.
Growth is proportionate: each case settles on the smallest power of two
above its working set (300 -> 512, 1200 -> 2048, 3000 -> 4096), within
`growths + 1` frames, bounded at five from the default.
Entries measured at ~3.1 KB (RSS delta over 20,000), so the 8,192 ceiling
is ~26 MB. A fresh cache costs 33 kB for the ceiling-sized ghost map; every
per-call constructor in the tree is a documented one-shot.
WIRE COUNTERFACTUAL, both columns measured on real bindings rather than
argued. Cumulative `shapes` after each scroll sweep, capacity pinned at 256
shapes per sweep, forever, against +0. Sweep 1 is IDENTICAL on
`hello-virtual-list` — cold content costs the same either way and the whole
change is in the steady state.
No shipped binding exceeds 256 on a boot frame — the widest,
`hello-grid-frozen-col`, shapes 198. The cliff is reached by USE, not by
opening the app, so a boot-frame census would have reported everything
healthy. Scrolling a large list down and back up is what crosses it.
The demo fails on the pre-R1521 build, and at the right assertion. Its
first draft asserted the precondition over `entries > 256`, which cannot be
satisfied when the capacity is pinned at 256 — it failed there for the
wrong reason and hid whether the real claims were reachable. Restated over
distinct strings shaped in one sweep, which is capacity-independent.
Local: 29 suites green across pinion-core / -text / -rpc / -shell / -tui
(`--no-fail-fast`), clippy / fmt / rustdoc clean, and every demo that reads
a cache counter (r1521, r1520, r682, r889, r827, r907).
carry_forward_bullets: A working set larger than `MAX_CAPACITY` still thrashes, and deliberately
does not grow toward the ceiling — the ghost list is ceiling-sized, so such
a set produces no witness. That is correct rather than a gap (it fits at no
permitted capacity, so growing would spend memory to change nothing), but
it means 8,192 is a real bound and a scene past it has no recourse inside
the cache. `at_ceiling` on the wire is how a consumer learns it is there.
The hit path still allocates: `layout_with_runs` builds an owned
`LayoutKey` (a `String`, a `Vec`) and probes the map twice — `contains`
then `get` — on every call including hits. Measured at 118 ns against the
2.6 us the paint walk spends per text node, so it is not this round's
defect and was left alone rather than folded in. The two-lookup shape is
the classic NLL borrow limitation, not an oversight.
The `LayoutKey` still includes `fg_color`, which is paint metadata and not
a shape determinant, so a colour cross-fade re-shapes every frame. R587
registered this and its Rule-of-Three gate is unchanged by R1521 — but the
gate's stated reason ("the working set that would suffer is bounded") is
now weaker, since the capacity no longer bounds anything.

Round 1523.decision_summary: The data grid windows its columns, not just its rows
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/column_widths.rs` — `visible_columns(widths,
offset_x, viewport_w, overscan)` + `columns_width_before`, plus the reactive
`ColumnWidths::visible_columns` binding. NOT a second implementation: the
arithmetic IS `compute_visible_range_variable` over a `RowOffsets` prefix sum of
the column widths. A grid's two axes are the same one-dimensional problem, which
is why Qt serves both orientations from one `QHeaderView` parameterised by
`Qt::Orientation`; re-deriving it would be the divergence-is-a-bug class.
`crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/table.rs` — `view_virtual_table` windows the
column axis for the header band and for every data row. R859 already rendered a
contiguous column range with an absolute `col_base` (for freezing); this round
chooses that range from the measured horizontal viewport. `ColumnPad` is the
width of the columns left out, rendered as one empty box per side — TanStack
Table's `virtualPaddingLeft` / `virtualPaddingRight`. Chosen over
absolutely-positioning each cell (the row axis' technique) so the eager
`view_table` and the windowed grid keep ONE row builder, and so the row's
natural width stays correct without a second sizer to keep in step. The frozen
pane never windows: a pinned column is on screen at every offset by definition.
`crates/pinion-a11y` — `aria-colcount` on the grid and `aria-colindex` on every
columnheader / gridcell (`AccessNode::column_count` / `column_index`, the
AccessKit lowering, and the new `windowed_grid_nodes_wide`). The row axis has
conveyed "which of how many" since R775 through setsize/posinset; windowing the
column axis without its extent pair would leave a 200-column table announced as
five columns wide — less readable than before it scaled.
`crates/pinion-rpc/src/access.rs` — the same pair on the wire. That serializer
hand-writes every field, so a new `AccessNode` field is absent from the RPC
surface until someone adds a line — and the RPC access tree is the primary path
an AI agent reads a11y through (invariant #2), so the round's claim would have
had no verifiable surface at all.
`crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/spacer.rs` (new) — obligation-3b lift on the
third consumer: `datepicker::blank_cell`, `tree_view`'s depth indent and this
round's column pad were the same fixed-size untagged empty box. The lifted home
owns the one decision worth centralising, which `tree_view`'s comment had
recorded alone: a spacer is UNTAGGED, or it becomes a phantom node in the a11y
tree, the hit router and every `scene/snapshot`.
`examples/hello-virtual-columns` (new) + `tools/demos/r1523_virtual_columns.py`
(new, 43 assertions) — a 200-column x 10,000-row grid, the widest in the tree by
20x. `tools/rpc_verify.py` gains `indexed_tags` (obligation-3b: five demos
carried a byte-identical private copy and this round would have added the sixth
and seventh).
verification_bullets: The round was chosen by `tools/phase_b_tally.py`: Model/View at scale is the
derived LEVERAGE leader (weight 16 x remaining 25).
Measured, same function and both configurations: one row of the 200-column grid
builds 200 cells un-windowed and 5 windowed
(`r1523_windowing_is_a_40x_reduction_in_cells`). Over the RPC surface the whole
grid holds 91 cells + 7 headers at boot where un-windowed it would hold 2,600 +
The columns are deliberately UNEQUAL (a five-width cycle) in every fixture, and
the demo carries an independent Python prefix-sum oracle. A uniform-pitch
derivation was checked as a counterfactual rather than assumed away: it fails at
offset 599, where the reported first column's span does not contain the offset.
The defect had two records in the tree and both failed before this round.
`hello-grid-hscroll`'s own view fn said "no column virtualization at 8 columns",
and r784's demo ASSERTED that an off-screen column was still in the tree — it
died with `KeyError('ghs_ch7')` on the first run after the fix. r784 / r785 /
r786 are re-aimed at absence-from-the-tree, which is the stronger witness; r786

Round 1524.decision_summary: The data grid asks for the cells it paints
changes_bullets: `crates/pinion-widget-paint/src/table.rs` — `view_virtual_table`'s data
contract becomes per-cell: `cell: impl FnMut(CellIndex) -> String` replaces
`build_cells: impl FnMut(usize) -> Vec<String>`. This is the Model/View
contract of every framework with a virtualized grid — Qt
`QAbstractItemModel::data(QModelIndex)`, Flutter `TableView.builder`'s
`cellBuilder(TableVicinity)` — and `CellIndex` is a struct for the reason both
of theirs are: the two coordinates share a type, so a positional pair accepts
them swapped, and the named `col` field can state the property a windowed grid
makes load-bearing (it is ABSOLUTE, whatever the window or the frozen split).
`render_unsplit` asks for the `span` columns only; `render_frozen`'s panes ask
for `0..frozen_cols` and for the window within `frozen_cols..` respectively.
The split had been the worst case: the per-row builder ran once per pane, so
each pane rebuilt the whole row and every column was produced twice.
`pane_texts` replaces R1523's `clamped` at the same three call sites. A
per-cell contract cannot express a short row, so the "a cell beyond the
returned length renders blank" rule it existed to enforce becomes `cell`
returning an empty `String` and there is no length to reconcile.
`materialize_cells(rows, cols, cell)` — obligation-3b lift. Six bindings seed a
`GridSortState` / `RowSearchState` with the whole matrix (a model sorts and
filters rows the viewport never exposed), and each had derived it from its own
per-cell function with an identical nested map. Deriving it in one place means
a binding cannot seed its model from a formula that has drifted from the one
its cells are painted with.
`examples/hello-virtual-columns` — the per-frame request count is published
into the scene at `vcol_status`. The round changes who builds what, not what
is painted, so the painted scene alone cannot witness it; the count reaches
`scene/snapshot` with no pixels and no profiler (invariant #7), the readout
pattern `hello-grid-multi-select` already uses for selection cardinality.
All 12 `view_virtual_table` consumers migrated: each `fn row_cells(id) ->
Vec<String>` becomes `fn cell_text(CellIndex) -> String`, a `match c.col`.
`tools/demos/r1524_cells_asked_for.py` (new, 38 assertions).
verification_bullets: The round was chosen by `tools/phase_b_tally.py`: Model/View at scale is the
derived LEVERAGE leader (400), and R1523 registered this as its own first

Measured, and by cross-checking two independent observables rather than one
instrumented number: `asked` (the consumer's request count, published in the
scene) against the data cells actually in the paint tree. Their EQUALITY is
what the round claims, and it rejects a regression in both directions — a
return to full-row asking raises `asked` while the painted count stands still,
and a window bug lowers it below the painted count. An upper bound would pass
the second.
Counterfactual, applied one at a time and reverted. Restoring pre-R1524 asking
in `render_unsplit`: the unit gate reports asked 2400 vs painted 84 and the
demo reports asked 2200 vs painted 77 (they differ because the status band
costs the demo one windowed row) — 28.6x either way. Restoring the frozen

The address is verified, not only the count: `cell_text` renders `r{row}c{col}`

tag it is painted under, so a consumer answering for a transposed or
off-by-one address would fail there while every count still matched.
The painted scene is unchanged: `pinion-widget-paint`'s 736 pre-existing tests
pass untouched, and the R1523 demo — which asserts the column window, the
header lockstep and every cell's exact x-position against an independent
Python prefix-sum oracle — still passes against the same binding.

Round 1525.decision_summary: The data grid paints the model it orders
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-grid-{sort,row-style,filter,multifilter,header-menu,search}` —
the view now asks the MODEL for its cells (`|c| m.cell(c.row, c.col)
.to_string()`) instead of the `cell_text` formula. Those six hold a
`GridSortState` / `RowSearchState` whose comparator, filter predicate and
search all read `cell(row, col)` directly, so before this round the string the
user read was not the string the ordering was computed from. `cell_text`'s
remaining job is seeding the model once.
`GridSortState::cell` / `RowSearchState::cell` had **zero view consumers**
before this round (measured: read only by the sort comparator, the filter
predicate and `search_matches`, all inside their own modules) — the accessor
the model offers for its data, which nothing that painted it used.
`crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/grid_sort.rs`,
`crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/row_search.rs` — both externals answer
`cell.<row>.<col>`, the wire form `TableExternal` has always answered for the
eager table, with the parametric schema field so the slot is discoverable
rather than folklore. Without it the round's claim has no RPC-side witness:
`scene/snapshot` gives the painted text and nothing independent to compare it
against. (R1523 added its a11y column pair to `access.rs` for exactly this
reason — RPC is invariant #2's primary path.)
`RowSearchExternal` also gains `cols`, which its new `cell.<col>` schema
argument cites as the column bound; it had no column-count slot, so declaring
the bound without it would have left a dangling schema reference.
`tools/demos/r1525_paints_its_model.py` (new, 28 assertions statically, ~55
executed).
verification_bullets: The discriminating evidence is a **divergently-seeded model**, which is what
makes a defect that nothing currently fails against reachable at all.
`use_grid_sort` / `use_row_search` cache on their key, so pre-seeding the
binding's own key hands it a model whose text the formula cannot produce.
`hello-grid-sort`: counterfactual paints `Alpha0000` where the model says
`MODEL-0-0`. Both premises are asserted rather than assumed (the pre-seed
reached the key; the formula cannot produce the model's text).
`hello-grid-search` states the sharper form: the cursor must land on text that
CONTAINS the query it was matched on. The search decides matches from the
model, so a formula-painted grid can highlight a row whose visible text does
not contain the query. Counterfactual: `got Some("Alpha0000")` for a row the
model matched on "Delta".
**My first draft of that test could not fail.** Seeding matches as
`MODEL-Delta-{r}` left the formula's own Delta rows containing "Delta" too, so
both sources satisfied `contains("Delta")` and the counterfactual passed. The
match set is now INVERTED relative to the formula's, so the cursor lands on a
row whose model text contains the query and whose formula text cannot. A test
that passes against the defect is not evidence, and this is the recurring
finding: the assertion's shape fails before the fix does.
Honest limit on the RPC demo: it CANNOT discriminate the paint-source change.
Over RPC both sources agree by construction (the model is seeded from the
formula), and divergent seeding is not reachable from outside the process. What
the demo does prove is the new wire surface (present, bounded, declared with
both coordinates) and end-to-end agreement of painted text with the model's own
copy across unsorted, sorted and filtered states — including that a sort's
painted column reads ascending when walked through `source_at.<pos>`, so order
and text are checked against the same model. The paint-source discrimination is
the unit tests' job, and it is done there.
Absence vs present-but-empty is pinned on both sides, because the two
conventions differ deliberately: `cell.<row>.<col>` past its bound is ABSENT
(an address that does not exist), `source_at.<pos>` past the view is Null (a
real position with no source). Asserted in the demo and in both unit tests.
Local: pinion-core 2848, pinion-rpc 1019 (which carries the gate that scans
every parametric declaration against its `strip_prefix`), the six bindings'
own tests, and 9 demos (r1525, r778, r779, r783, r986, r988, r997, r998,
r1004) each checked by exit code. fmt / clippy (pedantic) clean.
carry_forward_bullets: `tools/phase_b_tally.py` registers this round at +0% on Model/View for the
second consecutive round, for the reason R1524 recorded: the axis' evidence is
an example-name census and neither a contract round nor a data-path round
creates an example. The generalisation is now argued by two same-shaped cases
on this axis plus two on perf, and the treatment is the axis-EVIDENCE model,
not any one axis' patterns. Adding a `demo-body` probe pattern that happens to
match this round's demo would repeat precisely the error R1522 diagnosed —
patterns that name the rounds that already exist.
The `|c| m.cell(c.row, c.col).to_string()` closure now appears at six call
sites and was deliberately NOT lifted. A generic helper needs a `CellSource`
trait, which would have to live in `pinion-core` beside the two states (the
paint crate cannot own a trait core types implement), to save a one-line
closure — and the precedent against it is in the same argument list: the
`is_selected` predicate is a per-binding one-liner at all twelve call sites and
is correctly not lifted either. The closure is the call site's expression of
the contract, not wiring duplication.
Two legitimate cell-source shapes now coexist and the contract serves both: a
MODEL (these six — the app sorts, filters or searches the whole set, so it
must hold it) and a pure FORMULA (`hello-virtual-columns` — 200 x 10,000 cells
that nothing orders, where materialising 2M strings to paint ~80 would be
absurd). Which is right is an application property, not a framework one. This
is worth stating because R1524's carry framed the eager matrix as a cost to
remove; for a model-backed grid it is the store, and only the second PAINT path
was the defect.
`hello-virtual-columns`, `hello-virtual-table`, `hello-grid-nav`,
`hello-grid-frozen-col`, `hello-grid-hscroll` and `hello-grid-multi-select`
keep formula cell sources and hold no model, so they are untouched and
correctly so. `hello-grid-multi-select` is the one to re-examine if it ever
gains a sort or filter axis.

publishable_changes_bullets: `examples/hello-grid-{sort,row-style,filter,multifilter,header-menu,search}` —
the view now asks the MODEL for its cells (`|c| m.cell(c.row, c.col)
.to_string()`) instead of the `cell_text` formula. Those six hold a
`GridSortState` / `RowSearchState` whose comparator, filter predicate and
search all read `cell(row, col)` directly, so before this round the string the
user read was not the string the ordering was computed from. `cell_text`'s
remaining job is seeding the model once.
`GridSortState::cell` / `RowSearchState::cell` had **zero view consumers**
before this round (measured: read only by the sort comparator, the filter
predicate and `search_matches`, all inside their own modules) — the accessor
the model offers for its data, which nothing that painted it used.
`crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/grid_sort.rs`,
`crates/pinion-core/src/widgets/row_search.rs` — both externals answer
`cell.<row>.<col>`, the wire form `TableExternal` has always answered for the
eager table, with the parametric schema field so the slot is discoverable
rather than folklore. Without it the round's claim has no RPC-side witness:
`scene/snapshot` gives the painted text and nothing independent to compare it
against. (R1523 added its a11y column pair to `access.rs` for exactly this
reason — RPC is invariant #2's primary path.)
`RowSearchExternal` also gains `cols`, which its new `cell.<col>` schema
argument cites as the column bound; it had no column-count slot, so declaring
the bound without it would have left a dangling schema reference.
`tools/demos/r1525_paints_its_model.py` (new, 28 assertions statically, ~55
executed).
publishable_verification_bullets: The discriminating evidence is a **divergently-seeded model**, which is what
makes a defect that nothing currently fails against reachable at all.
`use_grid_sort` / `use_row_search` cache on their key, so pre-seeding the
binding's own key hands it a model whose text the formula cannot produce.
`hello-grid-sort`: counterfactual paints `Alpha0000` where the model says
`MODEL-0-0`. Both premises are asserted rather than assumed (the pre-seed
reached the key; the formula cannot produce the model's text).
`hello-grid-search` states the sharper form: the cursor must land on text that
CONTAINS the query it was matched on. The search decides matches from the
model, so a formula-painted grid can highlight a row whose visible text does
not contain the query. Counterfactual: `got Some("Alpha0000")` for a row the
model matched on "Delta".
**My first draft of that test could not fail.** Seeding matches as
`MODEL-Delta-{r}` left the formula's own Delta rows containing "Delta" too, so
both sources satisfied `contains("Delta")` and the counterfactual passed. The
match set is now INVERTED relative to the formula's, so the cursor lands on a
row whose model text contains the query and whose formula text cannot. A test
that passes against the defect is not evidence, and this is the recurring
finding: the assertion's shape fails before the fix does.
Honest limit on the RPC demo: it CANNOT discriminate the paint-source change.
Over RPC both sources agree by construction (the model is seeded from the
formula), and divergent seeding is not reachable from outside the process. What
the demo does prove is the new wire surface (present, bounded, declared with
both coordinates) and end-to-end agreement of painted text with the model's own
copy across unsorted, sorted and filtered states — including that a sort's
painted column reads ascending when walked through `source_at.<pos>`, so order
and text are checked against the same model. The paint-source discrimination is
the unit tests' job, and it is done there.
Absence vs present-but-empty is pinned on both sides, because the two
conventions differ deliberately: `cell.<row>.<col>` past its bound is ABSENT
(an address that does not exist), `source_at.<pos>` past the view is Null (a
real position with no source). Asserted in the demo and in both unit tests.

every parametric declaration against its `strip_prefix`), the six bindings'
own tests, and 9 demos (r1525, r778, r779, r783, r986, r988, r997, r998,

second consecutive round, for the reason R1524 recorded: the axis' evidence is

creates an example. The generalisation is now argued by two same-shaped cases
on this axis plus two on perf, and the treatment is the axis-EVIDENCE model,

changes_bullets: `docs/phase-b-rounds.tsv` (new) — the round ledger. One row per round:
round<TAB>axis<TAB>note, where axis is an AXES key or `none`. Rows at or below
R1519 are rejected: the tally was born in R1519 and assigning axes to the 1500
rounds before it would be inventing history rather than recording it. `none` is
legal and must carry a reason, the same rule NOT_PHASE_B entries follow.
Seeded with the six rounds since the floor: R1520/R1521 perf, R1522 none,
R1523/R1524/R1525 modelview, R1526 none.
`tools/phase_b_tally.py` — a third evidence kind, `round-axis`, a CENSUS whose
universe is the rounds git knows and whose text is what the ledger declared for
each. The count moves when work LANDS rather than when an artifact is CREATED,
which is the property every kind before it lacked: R1523, R1524 and R1525 each
closed a named Model/View gap by editing `hello-grid-*` examples the axis
already owned, so its evidence moved +0%, +0%, +0%. R1522 had fixed the same
blindness on perf by adding a `demo-body` probe, which worked only because an
optimisation happens to leave a new demo behind — the cardinality assumption
underneath was untouched and resurfaced on the next axis three rounds later.
Git, not the ledger, enumerates which rounds exist. If the ledger were also the
census a forgotten declaration would be invisible rather than reported, which is
the false-negative direction R1522's asymmetry says must never go silent. A
round with no row is reported UNDECLARED; a row naming a round with no commit is
reported DECLARED AHEAD (the round in progress at commit time, a mistyped number
by push time).
`patterns_for` derives the round-axis pattern structurally — an axis's key IS
its pattern — instead of the eight hand-written copies the (kind, patterns) form
would otherwise need. An axis that cannot register depth work is now
unwriteable rather than merely discouraged.
Evidence snapshots are per kind. R1522 summed perf's 4 examples and 7 demos into
one `11`, which buries a kind that moves inside a kind that does not: against 37
examples one depth round is +2.7%, so nine would be needed to cross the 25%
threshold that a count of rounds crosses at once. `evidence_snapshot` is now a
dict keyed by kind, drift is computed per kind, and an axis is STALE if any of
its kinds has drifted.
`parse_ledger` is strict — a malformed row, an unknown axis key, a round at or
below the floor, and an exclusion with no reason each raise. A skipped row is a
declared round counted as undeclared, or worse a round credited to an axis a
typo named.
Model/View at scale re-judged **75% -> 80%**, forced by this round's own change
taking its declared rounds 0 -> 3, with `judged_at` and both snapshots moved in
the same edit for the reason R1522 recorded. Not higher: header data is still
per-slice (the binding takes `headers: &[&str]` for all 200 columns where Qt's
`headerData` is per-section) and `cell` returns a String with no role dimension.
`--selftest` gains the property whose absence made this round necessary, stated
so it holds for work that has not happened: an artifact count cannot see a round
that only modified an artifact, a declared round registers on its axis having
created nothing, and every axis draws on both a creation kind and the round
kind. Also asserted: no axis key contains another (round-axis matches by
substring, so the two agree only while that holds), the ledger's four rejection
cases, and that the subject parse takes one round per commit — a subject citing
another round declares only its own, and a round that landed as two commits is
one round.
`.githooks/lib/phase-b-tally.sh` — the push grep carries UNDECLARED and
DECLARED, the two findings this round adds. The ledger's whole defence against a
forgotten declaration is that the omission is spoken at every push.
`tools/test_hooks.sh` 76 -> 78 assertions, covering both new lines through the
hook rather than only in the tool.
`CLAUDE.md` — Phase B 69% -> 70% all axes, 75% -> 76% buildable; tree at R1526
27 crates / 198 examples / 479 demos; true north ~27% -> ~28%. The derived
LEVERAGE order changes for the second time and is recorded as such: perf 360
returns to first, Model/View drops to third at 320. The working contract gains
the per-round obligation to append a ledger row, because `docs/SEED_PROMPT.md`
where round obligations otherwise live is gitignored and a fresh clone does not
have it.
verification_bullets: `python3 tools/phase_b_tally.py --selftest` PASS (0 failures).
`bash tools/test_hooks.sh` 78 passed, 0 failed.
No Rust changed, so no cargo gate applies to this round.
Four counterfactuals, run one at a time in memory against the real tree:
CF-1, the state this round found — Model/View judged at R1519 with three depth
rounds landed since: `rd 0 -> 3`, STALE, exit 1.
CF-2, the same tree and the same three rounds with evidence counted the R1522
way (artifacts only): `ex 36 -> 37 (+3%)`, not stale, exit 0. This is what was
actually reported at R1525 and it is the defect exactly.
CF-3, a round that lands with no ledger row: reported as UNDECLARED naming the
round, not silently absent.
CF-4, the next depth round on the axis just judged: `rd 3 -> 4 (+33%)` fires,
`ex 37 -> 38 (+3%)` does not. Per-kind snapshots are what make that possible;
summed they are 40 against 36, +11%, and silent.
Reverting only the hook's grep change fails exactly the two new assertions in
tools/test_hooks.sh and nothing else.
Two alternative designs were measured and rejected before this one was written.
Attributing rounds to axes from git paths: R1511 and R1513 each touched ~40
examples spanning six axes, so a sweep round registers on every axis at once,
and unlike a false positive in a count — which appears in both snapshot and
today and cancels — that noise accumulates in a rate. Total example bytes: it
moves (Model/View 982K -> 1022K, +4.1% over the three rounds) but makes
verbosity read as progress, which the R661 LOC baseline exists to prevent.
`git log --format=%s --no-merges` over 1921 round-tagged commits measured 0.12s,
so the census costs the reporter nothing it should not pay.

unchanged.

per-section. Named in the new Model/View judgment as one of the two reasons it
is 80 and not higher.
`cell` returns a String with no role dimension — Qt's Display / Edit /
Decoration / ToolTip roles have no counterpart. The second reason for 80.
The ledger is appended by hand. Its natural long-term home is a field on the
atomic changelog entry every round already writes, which would remove the extra
step entirely; that is a Mnemosyne schema change and therefore an upstream
carry, not something this repo can do. Until then the census is the defence: a
missing row is reported, it is not assumed absent.
A round could declare an axis it did not advance and nothing checks it. The cost
is a re-judgment that finds nothing, which is the safe direction, so no check
was added — recorded so the omission is deliberate rather than unnoticed.
The ledger does not close [[debt-a11y-invisible-to-tally]] and slightly sharpens
it: a round advancing accessibility can now only declare `none`, because there
is no a11y axis to name. That makes the gap legible — a run of `none` rounds all

axis-set question is a judgment R1519 made and this round deliberately did not
re-open.

any axis whose last judgment predates work done before the floor. Every axis

Round 1527.decision_summary: The §5.16 paint cache's mark phase gets a trace step: a fragment is live if the walk consulted it or a live fragment subsumes it. R682 stated the bound correctly — the set of cacheable Containers actually painted in the most recent frame — and implemented a proxy for it, the set the walker consulted. Those coincide only while the cache is missing: a hit ends the walk, so everything under it is painted and never consulted, and the sweep read that silence as death. The divergence was therefore worst exactly where the cache worked best, and it collapsed the live set in a single idle frame. Containment is the edge a mark-and-sweep needs to follow, so no policy changes: no grace frames, no cap, and the short-circuit stays.
changes_bullets: FragmentCache gains containment edges (`subsumes`) recorded at install time and a worklist trace in `end_paint`: a fragment is live if the walk consulted it OR a live fragment subsumes it. The mark phase had no trace step, so a hit that short-circuited the walk read its own descendants as dead.

`mark_painted` / `enter_subtree` attribute each consulted fragment to the innermost open miss-encode, which makes "nearest cacheable descendant" fall out of the stack rather than being computed; the pop-then-mark order in `insert_miss` is what puts a container in its PARENT's frame.

`run_demo` (tools/rpc_verify.py) now raises SystemExit instead of returning a status. An AST census over 474 demos found exactly 2 that dropped the value — r1520 and r1521, the cost-counter demos of the two prior perf rounds — making them incapable of failing the sweep, which judges by exit code.
r1520_scrolled_paint_cache section (C) asserted `entries == 1` after an idle frame, pinning the defect as expected behaviour; section (D) explained the consequence away in a comment. Both corrected.
New demo r1527_fragment_trace on hello-grid-nav (31 assertions, sections A-G) with a negative control (a dataset jump must re-encode) and a pixel witness (a retained fragment is not a stale one).
verification_bullets: Measured on hello-grid-nav, both ways (the "before" column is a real run with the trace removed, not an estimate): entries after one idle frame 1 -> 83; one ArrowDown 1 hit/83 misses -> 20 hits/10 misses.
Unit measurement, 1200 rows at one cacheable container each: changing ONE row cost 17.1 ms at 0 hits, against 1.4 ms at 1199 hits after the trace (12.2x); a second change 9.8 ms -> 1.3 ms.

Measure-first rejected the round's first hypothesis: the LayoutCache hit path allocates an owned key per lookup, but it is 83 ns/lookup = 9% of the walk, not the dominant term. Breakdown at 1200 leaves: vello encode 54%, glyph-run walk 37%, cache lookup 9%.

Three counterfactuals, one at a time, each rebuilt and run: remove the trace step (all 4 unit guards fail, printing the defect as `(0, 41)` vs `(39, 2)`); never sweep the edge map (exactly the memory-bound guard fails, 42 vs 5); mark before popping the frame (all 4 fail). The demo fails on the reverted build at section C, and section D fails independently when C is neutralised.
Sections F and G are negative controls and pass BOTH ways by design — they guard over-retention and staleness, which the pre-R1527 code also did not have.

Local gates: pinion-runtime 589 tests, pinion-shell 391, pinion-rpc 1019, all pass; clippy -D pedantic clean; cargo fmt --check clean; cargo doc --workspace clean (two public-doc links to the private `subsumes` field lowered to code spans). Demos r1520 / r1521 / r1527 pass with exit 0; r1527 run 5x consecutively, no flake.
Self-grep: mark-and-sweep-without-trace has exactly one site in the tree. ImageCache has no eviction at all; LayoutCache and ResourceCache are LRU. No lift.
carry_forward_bullets: The vello encode (54%) and the parley glyph-run walk (37%) remain the paint walk's dominant terms on a cache MISS; this round removed the reason misses were happening, not the cost of one. 1200 leaves still cost ~1.06 ms uncached.

`subsumes` holds a Vec per fragment even for the leaf containers that subsume nothing. Measured cost is 8 bytes per edge against the encoded scenes it keeps alive, so it was not worth a niche representation, but it is an empty allocation per leaf fragment.

The trace runs every `end_paint` over the whole live set even when nothing was evicted. O(live entries) with no early exit; at 83 fragments this is invisible, at a 10k-fragment scene it is not measured.

`last_damage_region` could not be asserted on a keystroke frame: it describes the LAST frame and `paint_after` returns once paint_count advanced, which a 30fps idle tick can carry past. The counters aggregate correctly across that; this field does not. A demo helper that lands exactly one frame is the real fix.
R1520's registered debt named three candidate fixes, all of which change what R682 chose. None was taken, and the debt file must now be closed rather than left reading as open.

Round 1528.decision_summary: The value axis can be logarithmic (Qt QLogValueAxis). pinion-chart had ELEVEN chart types and ONE mapping, LinearScale, so a latency series over 0.1ms..1000ms put everything below 100ms on the baseline. The log scale IS the linear scale, over the log-transformed domain (d3's transformLog), which is why it inherits the degenerate-domain and descending-range handling already proved there rather than restating that arithmetic. Two layers follow: LinearScale is the arithmetic (total, affine) and ValueScale is the AXIS (Qt's QAbstractAxis distinction), whose map returns Option because a log axis has no pixel for zero. That partiality is the design and not an inconvenience - a sample the axis cannot place draws no mark and is REPORTED by LineChart::off_scale, which is the Mapped::unreadable stance applied to the axis instead of to the input.
changes_bullets: scale.rs: LogScale (a LinearScale over the log-transformed domain, configurable base, total construction with a reported fallback) + ValueScale{Linear,Log}, whose map returns Option<f32>; axis_defines is the one definedness rule, reachable instance-free by charts that know their axis kind before a plot resolves.

ticks.rs: log_ticks (decades, whole-decade stride when they outnumber the labels), log_minor_ticks (2..base subdivisions, capped at 6 decades), nice_log_domain (decade snapping with an exponent-dust guard: ln(1000)/ln(10) is 2.9999999999999996), format_log_tick (SI above 1000, exponent below 1e-3, faithful digits between).

TickFormat replaces the scalar tick step at the label sites. A linear axis has ONE gap, so a scalar determined every label's decimals; a log axis has none, so the scalar is not a lossy summary of that tick set but a wrong one. It survived because on a linear axis the two agree - the R1439 derivation-by-coincidence, one layer up.

plot.rs: LogAxes{x,y} mirrors Rescale; CartesianPlot carries a ValueScale on both axes; a log axis auto-domains off Bounds::positive_x/y, which come out of the SAME bounds scan rather than a second one. resolve_focus now inverts through the axis instead of interpolating the domain linearly, and nearest_point_in takes a keep predicate so a series whose nearest sample is off-scale still contributes its nearest drawn one.

examples/hello-log-chart (new, 6 tests) + tools/demos/r1528_log_axis.py (37 assertion sites): three latency percentiles across four decades, one click between linear and log, and a caption rendered from LineChart::off_scale rather than from a restated rule.
verification_bullets: Measured on the example, read off the painted scene: p50's polyline spans under 10px on the linear axis and over 4x that on the log axis - the same series, the same plot. Decade gridline gaps are equal within 1px and the y labels are 0.1/1/10/100/1k/10k.

The demo's discriminator is the LABELS, not the spacing: gridlines are evenly spaced on BOTH axes, so asserting even spacing alone would pass on a linear axis and prove nothing. Both facts are read together.
The x-axis labels are captured on both scales and required to be identical, so a change that logged both axes would fail rather than look like a success.
Off-scale is asserted as a property of the AXIS: the zero sample contributes 11 of 12 polyline vertices under log and 12 under linear, and the caption reports it in one case and not the other.

Measurement corrected the round's own counterfactual. The predicted failure of the scalar step on a log tick set was label collapse to 0; a log axis's gaps GROW, so the scalar is the smallest of them and the real failure is over-specification (1.000, 10.000, 100.000). Both directions are pinned now, including the strided case where the low decades do round to zero.

Local gates: pinion-chart 251 tests + 2 doc-tests and hello-log-chart 6 tests pass, 18 of them new r1528 units; clippy -D pedantic clean on both; cargo fmt --check clean; cargo doc --workspace clean (six public-doc links to private items lowered to code spans). Every pre-existing pinion-chart test passes unchanged, which is what makes this a generalisation rather than a rewrite.
Consumer regression: the eight chart example crates' tests pass, and demos hello_chart_r1354, r1377_scatter_scrub and r1391_brush_filter pass unchanged.

Self-grep (obligation 3b): LogAxes, tick_pixels, axis_format, minor_gridlines and off_scale_points are each one definition with two to four call sites, written shared rather than lifted afterwards. mul_alpha moved from line.rs to draw.rs at its second consumer, beside the MUTED_ALPHA it is applied to.
carry_forward_bullets: The bar chart is deliberately excluded: a bar encodes magnitude by length from a zero baseline and a log axis has no zero. Qt permits a log bar chart; the length encoding is what makes it a lie. Recorded at the call site.

A dropped interior sample makes the polyline join its surviving neighbours, so it reads as interpolation rather than as a gap. This follows the crate's existing stance for unreadable model cells verbatim - a true gap needs a gap-aware Series, which still does not exist. One rule for one class, and this is the second consumer asking for that machinery.

The Steps struct is duplicated in line.rs and scatter.rs (two consumers, identical shape). Its field TYPE changed identically in both this round, which is the signal, but the crate's own stated rule defers a two-consumer split; a third numeric-x chart settles it.

text_of now has four demo-local spellings across three shapes (r1448, the identical r1469 and r1478, and this round's). No three are byte-identical - they differ in Optional-versus-assert error behaviour - so no lift is owed, but the mechanical core is shared and the class is worth watching.

A log axis snapping outward to whole decades can reserve a mostly empty decade: the 1600ms spike opens 1k..10k. This is the same trade nice_ticks already makes for round labels, and it is stated in the demo rather than tuned away by picking friendlier data.

Round 1531.decision_summary: The paint replays a glyph draw list it does not rebuild. The §5.36 cache held what parley SHAPED, not what a painter DRAWS, and those differ: putting a shaped layout on screen means walking lines/items/GlyphRun and running positioned_glyphs(), which accumulates every glyph's pen advance. That walk is a pure function of the layout, and it ran on every paint of every text leaf. Measured at 1200 leaves it cost 1489 us a frame against 480 us for encoding a pre-derived list — 3.1x, on exactly the frames a §5.16 fragment-cache miss produces and a §5.36 shape-cache hit hides. The list now lives in the entry that already owns the layout, which is the canonical shape: Skia's SkTextBlob, Qt's QGlyphRun.
changes_bullets: `pinion_text::glyph_run::PositionedRun` is the draw list a painter replays: font, size, brush, layout-absolute glyphs, and each decoration resolved (font-metric fallback applied, parley's baseline-upward offset flipped into screen space). Renderer-agnostic by construction — `pinion-text` names no rasteriser.

`LayoutCache` entries become `CachedLayout { layout, runs: Option<..> }` and gain `positioned_runs()`. Same key, same entry, same eviction as the layout: the draw list is the second half of one derivation, not a second cache. Derivation is LAZY because this cache has callers that shape to MEASURE and never paint (text metrics, caret geometry, the TUI cell-grid measure arm).

`paint_text` and `draw_cell_glyph` replay the list instead of walking `lines() -> items() -> GlyphRun -> positioned_glyphs()` on every paint. Production census: zero glyph-run walks remain outside the derivation itself.

New counter `LayoutCache::run_builds()`, carried by `TextCacheStats` and published on `scene/text_cache_stats`. Nothing else distinguishes a replayed draw list from one rebuilt identically — same pixels, 3.1x apart in cost, and `shapes` is still across exactly those frames by construction.

Round 1532.decision_summary: A column declares how its cells are painted. GridModel::cell answers with a String, so every column of every pinion grid was a label: a size column could not be a bar, a visibility column could not be a mark, a swatch column could not be a swatch. That is the extension point of every Model/View framework — Qt's QStyledItemDelegate, whose documented purpose is precisely a column that is not text — and a DCC/IDE grid is mostly made of such columns. The gap was already being paid for: hello-property-grid draws a gauge inside a cell by not using the grid's cell path at all, building its own row tree instead, which is what a missing extension point looks like from the consumer side.
changes_bullets: `VirtualTableData::delegate` is Qt `setItemDelegateForColumn`: a lookup from column to `CellPainter`, resolved once per painted COLUMN (a column's delegate cannot vary by row, so resolving per cell repeats one answer once per row — the per-section discipline R1530 gave the header axis).

`CellRender` carries what Qt hands a delegate as `(painter, option, index)`, minus the painter: §2 #1 forbids an opaque paint callback, so a painter RETURNS a `Scene`. That is what keeps a custom column as introspectable through `scene/snapshot` as a text one, and is why the demo asserts everything it asserts with no pixels.

The built-in `text_cell_painter` is reached through the same call a custom painter is, so an undelegated column is not a second path that can drift from the delegated one; it is also public, so a painter that only decorates the default composes with it.

`hello-virtual-table` gains a delegated `Load` column painted as a gauge. It still paints the model's own string beside the bar — a bar encodes in pixels, and a delegate that dropped the label would take the column out of §2 #7 introspection and away from a screen reader (Qt's `QProgressBar::text` for the same reason).

New demo r1532_cell_delegate (69 assertions, sections A-F) with a negative control (the undelegated columns must be unchanged) and a virtualization pass (scrolling re-paints delegated cells for the new window, with no leftovers).
verification_bullets: Three counterfactuals, one at a time, each rebuilt and run. Ignore the delegate: the two paint tests fail. Make the lookup claim every column: the paint test and the per-column-resolution test fail, and the demo fails at its negative control. Drop `CellRender::tag` from the binding's painter: the demo fails at section B.

The third counterfactual found a discrimination gap and it was closed rather than recorded: every unit test in `hello-virtual-table` passed with the tag deleted, so the contract's one rule for a painter was guarded only by the demo. `r1532_the_delegated_cell_keeps_its_hit_tag` now fails there, alone.

Measured on the binding: one tagged cell per column per windowed row for all four columns; the delegated column's cells carry the gauge geometry and the other three carry none; the delegate lookup runs once per painted column against `rows x cols` painted cells.

Local gates: pinion-widget-paint 749 tests, hello-virtual-table 8, all pass; clippy -D pedantic clean on both; cargo fmt clean; workspace check clean. Demos r1532, r1523, r1524 and r1530 (the other grid-contract rounds) pass.
`data_row` crossed the argument budget as the seam went in; `painters` and the `Theme` they need moved onto `RowPane`, the bundle this file already uses for exactly that reason.
Doc-to-code ratio on the round's added Rust: 0.48x, inside the R661 1.5x baseline.
carry_forward_bullets: The eager `view_table` exposes no delegate on its own surface, so the tree holds two cell-paint contracts — the shape R1530 left on the header axis, recorded rather than fixed.
The delegate covers PAINT only. Qt's `QStyledItemDelegate` also owns editing (`createEditor` / `setEditorData` / `setModelData`), and every editable grid here still hand-rolls its own edit latch.

The framework ships one painter, the text default. Qt's default additionally renders `Qt::CheckStateRole` and `Qt::DecorationRole`, which belongs with the role dimension the Model/View axis still lacks rather than with this seam.
Six example bindings build cell subtrees outside the grid's cell path (`hello-property-grid`'s `ranged_slider_cell` is the clearest); none was migrated, so the seam has one consumer.

`VirtualTableData` is now invariant in its lifetime because the delegate names it in a `Fn` return type. `GridRender` took a second lifetime parameter to absorb that; any future caller holding a `VirtualTableData` across differing borrows will meet the same constraint.

Round 1533.decision_summary: A value widget answers the wheel. External::wheel has been the router's stage-1 offer since R877 — on every wheel event the framework asks the widget under the cursor first, and only then falls through to the enclosing Scene::Scroll — and a census of the whole repo found ONE implementor: hello-node-editor's canvas, which zooms. Every widget in the catalog declined, so a wheel over a slider, a spin box or a number field did what a wheel over blank wallpaper does, it scrolled whatever was behind it. Qt implements wheelEvent on precisely these widgets (QAbstractSlider, QAbstractSpinBox), which is why every volume slider, zoom slider and DCC parameter field on a desktop answers a wheel without being clicked first. The hook was not missing. The widgets were not using it.
changes_bullets: `WheelStepper` (pinion-core `event.rs`, beside `WheelDelta` and `LINE_HEIGHT_PX`) banks sub-notch pixels: Qt's `offset_accumulated` / `wheelDeltaRemainder`, one home. A continuous consumer — the node canvas' zoom exponent — can divide a pixel delta and be done; a stepped one cannot, because a trackpad reporting 0.4px an event rounds to zero forever and the widget never moves.

The type also states the three-way consume verdict both widgets follow. Banked (under one notch): consume, so the page behind cannot jitter between the notches of a slow trackpad. Stepped: consume. Saturated: DECLINE and drop the carry, so the wheel this widget cannot spend reaches the scroll container behind it.

`SliderExternal::wheel` is Qt `QAbstractSlider::wheelEvent`: one notch is one snap `step` on a discrete slider (so it walks its own stops) or one `CONTINUOUS_WHEEL_STEP` on a continuous one. 5% is what every slider binding here already spells in its arrow-key map, which preserves Qt's real invariant — one `singleStep` drives the wheel and the arrows alike.

A notch emits `value_changing` AND `value_committed`. A notch is atomic (there is no press to release), so if the commit channel stayed silent every consumer that persists or seeks on commit only — hello-scrubber, settings-panel — would watch the thumb move and do nothing. Qt's wheel likewise emits `valueChanged`, not just `sliderMoved`.

`SpinButtonExternal::wheel` is the same rule in domain units (Qt `QAbstractSpinBox::wheelEvent`). Two deliberate divergences from Qt, both toward the slider's rule: no `Ctrl`-times-ten step, and no always-accept — Qt's spin box eats the page scroll of any form containing a field pinned at its bound.

Qt's `wheelScrollLines` multiplier (three single-steps a notch) is deliberately not carried over: it exists because a QSlider's step is 1 of a 0..99 range, whereas a step here is a normalised fraction the binding chose. hello-slider-discrete has six stops, and three a notch is not a slider.

`SliderExternal::set_value` returns `bool` now, mirroring the `Slider::set_value` it wraps. The wheel needs the gate-by-effect answer to tell a step from a saturated push; every existing call site is a statement.
New demo r1533_wheel_steps_value (42 assertions, sections A-H) over four bindings, no pixels: hello-slider, hello-slider-discrete, hello-spinbutton, and hello-range-slider as the negative control.
verification_bullets: Nine unit counterfactuals and two demo counterfactuals, one at a time, each reverted before the next. Sign flipped: 9 tests fail. Banked verdict declines: 3. Saturation consumes (Qt's spin-box rule): 4. No commit intent: 2. `round` for `trunc`: 8. No direction-flip reset: 2. Spin-button sign / saturation: 6 and 2.

The saturation-reset counterfactual found a discrimination gap TWICE and both were closed, not recorded. First pass: the test reversed direction to recover, and `feed`'s own sign-flip reset drops the carry on a reversal, so deleting the saturation reset changed nothing. Second pass: recovering in the same direction, the chosen fractions summed EXACTLY onto the notch boundary and binary rounding decided the trunc — the counterfactual passed by luck. With 0.3 of a notch instead of 0.2 it fails, alone.

Demo counterfactuals rebuilt the release binaries and re-ran: making the slider decline every wheel fails at section B; replacing the accumulator with a per-event truncation fails at section D, which is the assertion that carry exists for.

Measured end to end through the real router, not the widget in isolation: hello-slider 0.0 to 0.05 on one notch, hello-spinbutton 3.0 to 4.0, and the AccessKit node's `value.float.value` tracks the wheel so a screen reader reads the number a sighted user sees.

The wheel does not disturb either statechart: the slider reads Hover (the cursor is over it), never Dragging, and both spin-button steppers stay Idle — a phantom pressed arrow is what routing a wheel through the stepper channel would paint.

Local gates: pinion-core 2870 tests, pinion-widget-paint 749, eight slider/spin/scrubber/settings consumer examples, all pass. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D pedantic` clean. Demo r1533 passes in 8.2s.
Doc-to-code ratio on the round's added Rust: 0.55x, inside the R661 1.5x baseline.
carry_forward_bullets: The router keeps its own pixel remainder (`wheel_remainders`, plus the middle-pan copy) and was left alone: same shape, different unit boundary — it rounds toward whole scroll pixels where this truncates toward whole notches. Unifying them needs a unit parameter and a rounding mode, which is a forced abstraction at two consumers, so it is recorded rather than built.

No modifier arm on either widget. Qt's slider pages on Ctrl/Shift and its spin box multiplies by ten; a slider here has no page-step property to answer with, and one rule on both beats a modifier that means something on one widget and nothing on the other.
Only the vertical wheel axis is read. A horizontal wheel or trackpad axis over a horizontal track is a refinement the same hook absorbs.

Qt has `wheelEvent` on `QComboBox` and `QTabBar` too, and neither combobox (`virtual_select`) nor the tab bar answers a wheel here. That is index arithmetic rather than value arithmetic, and it is the third consumer that would decide whether the verdict belongs in `WheelStepper` as a combinator.
The range slider is deliberately without a wheel and is this round's negative control: Qt has no two-thumb slider, so there is no `wheelEvent` to mirror and no answer to which thumb a notch moves.

Browsers gate a number field's wheel on FOCUS (Chrome and Firefox both), Qt does not, and this round follows Qt. A focus gate would be the first production consumer of `focus_state::focused()`, which is the open half of [[debt-a11y-focus-flag-unforced]].
A banked sub-notch consumes, so the shell requests a repaint for a frame that paints identically. The cost was not measured; the fragment cache (R1520/R1527) is what makes it plausibly free.
