Browsers gate a number field's wheel on FOCUS (Chrome and Firefox both), Qt does not, and this round follows Qt. A focus gate would be the first production consumer of `focus_state::focused()`, which is the open half of [[debt-a11y-focus-flag-unforced]].
A banked sub-notch consumes, so the shell requests a repaint for a frame that paints identically. The cost was not measured; the fragment cache (R1520/R1527) is what makes it plausibly free.

Round 1534.decision_summary: A plot can be zoomed and panned. A window over the data has existed since the R1357 brush — a Brush resolves a (low, high) fraction pair onto the data extent and the consumer re-domains the chart with it — but a brush is an OVERVIEW STRIP: a second widget below the plot, dragged by two thumbs. Nothing could zoom or pan the plot ITSELF, which is where QtCharts puts it (QChart::zoomIn / scroll / zoomReset) and where d3 puts it (d3.zoom on the plot area, then transform.rescaleX). The difference is not only which pixels take the gesture. A strip cannot zoom ABOUT A POINT, and that is the whole feel of a wheel zoom: the minute of the incident under the reader's cursor keeps its pixel while four hours spread around it. Two thumbs cannot express keep this fixed.
changes_bullets: `PlotWindow` (pinion-chart `window.rs`) owns the normalised window and the arithmetic a gesture needs: `zoom_about(anchor, factor)` holds the data under the cursor still, `pan_by(fraction)` slides by a share of what is VISIBLE (a pan comes from pixels, so a tenth of the plot must be a tenth of the window at every zoom), `reset()` is `zoomReset`.

Every operation answers whether the window MOVED, and that is what makes the wheel handler correct: a gesture the window cannot spend — at the 25x magnification ceiling, already flush against the extent — is handed back rather than swallowed. R1533's consume verdict, on a second kind of consumer.

The representation is the brush's, not a parallel one. `map_window` is now the single statement of what a window fraction MEANS, called by both `PlotWindow::domain` and `Brush::domain`; `Brush::DEFAULT_MIN_SPAN` is defined as `PlotWindow::DEFAULT_MIN_SPAN`. A plot disagreeing with its own overview strip would be a visible bug and there is no second copy to drift.

`plot_area` is public: the axis's own pixel span, which was `pub(crate)` while `hello-chart` and `hello-autoscale-y` each carried the identical margin arithmetic to align their brush strips. Both migrated; this round's wheel target would have been the third copy. `draw::plot_rect` is now derived from it, so the overlay covers exactly the drawn axis.

`hello-time-chart` gains a `PlotZoomExternal` laid over `plot_area` — NOT over the chart rect, because `x_rel` is the zoom's anchor and an anchor measured across the y-label gutter pivots about an instant the cursor is not on.

The wheel vocabulary is deliberately `hello-node-editor`'s (R877): `Ctrl`+wheel zooms about the cursor, `Shift`+wheel pans, a horizontal wheel axis pans (R1533 left `dx` unread on the value widgets; here it has an obvious meaning), and a plain vertical wheel is DECLINED so a chart in a scrolling dashboard never steals the page scroll.

An unzoomed window does not re-domain the chart, and `Escape` resets but only CONSUMES the key when there was a zoom to reset — a binding that swallowed Escape on an unzoomed plot would shadow whatever else the app wants it for.

New demo r1534_plot_zoom (58 assertions, sections A-H) plus four `hello-time-chart` tests. No pixels: the window is read through `/plot/external/{low,high,span}` and the axis through the painted tick labels.
verification_bullets: Five unit counterfactuals and three demo counterfactuals, one at a time, each reverted before the next. Anchor ignored: 2 tests fail. No extent clamp: 2. Pan extent-relative: 2. No magnification ceiling: 3. Pan unclamped: 4. Target on the chart rect: the demo fails at the geometry premise. Plain wheel zooms: fails at the pan premise. Always re-domain: fails at the numeric no-regression assertion.

The clamp counterfactual found a VACUOUS test and it was closed, not recorded: deleting the `[0, 1 - span]` clamp in `zoom_about` changed nothing, because from a full window the arithmetic cannot leave the extent (`high = pivot + (1 - anchor) * new_span <= 1` whenever the window started at `0..1`). The clamp only earns its place zooming OUT from an edge-flush window, which no test covered; `r1534_zooming_out_from_an_edge_stays_inside_the_extent` now does, on both edges.

The re-domain counterfactual found the round's own stated rationale to be unverified AND mis-attributed. It said pinning the raw extent would nice-round the axis into a different one; measured, the TIME axis is indifferent (this window starts on a nice boundary, so `nice_time_domain` returns what it was given) and the NUMERIC axis draws 9 gridlines derived against 7 pinned. The claim moved to where it bites, in the demo and in `r1534_an_unzoomed_plot_is_the_chart_it_was_before`.

A third vacuous assertion was caught while writing the demo: an anchor at fraction 1.0 puts the cursor one pixel PAST the rect, so the wheel missed the target entirely and the window stayed `0..1` — and `high == 1.0` is also its unmoved value, so "flush right" passed for a gesture that never happened. Replaced by a zoom-out from an edge, where both the span change and the clamp are asserted.

Measured end to end through the real router: one `Ctrl`+wheel notch takes the window to `0.1..0.9` (span `1 / 1.25`), four notches to `0.2952..0.7048` (`1.25^-4`), `Shift`+wheel pans by `0.15` of the visible span, a plain wheel moves nothing, `Escape` restores `0..1`.

Local gates: pinion-chart 289 tests plus all 64 packages that depend on it, hello-time-chart 10, all pass. `clippy -D pedantic` clean on the four changed crates; `cargo fmt` clean. Demos r1534, r1529 (the axis this deepens), r1354 and r1397 (the two migrated brush strips) all pass.
Doc-to-code ratio on the round's added Rust: 1.42x total, inside the R661 1.5x baseline.
carry_forward_bullets: No DRAG pan and no rubber-band zoom. QtCharts has both (`QChartView::setRubberBand`, and a drag pan). An `External` has no pointer-down / pointer-up hook, so a press-drag needs either the raw-pointer-button seam or a slider-style statechart — a design choice this round did not have to make, and should not make by accident.
The window is x-only. QtCharts zooms a RECT, so a y-axis window (and the diagonal drag that selects one) is absent; `hello-autoscale-y` fits y to the x-window, which is a different thing.

The zoom is invisible to a screen reader. The status line is a text node like the caption, so an AT user gets no announcement that the plot is windowed — where the brush at least carries a range-slider role. An a11y round, not a paint one.

One consumer. The brush consumers (`hello-chart`, `hello-autoscale-y`, `hello-scatter`, `hello-linked-brush`) were not given plot zoom, so the two ways of windowing an axis do not yet appear together on one plot — which is where the interesting question is (does a wheel move the strip's thumbs?).
`hello-scatter` aligns its strip to the full rect on purpose (a scatter draws no axis margins) and was left alone, so `plot_area` has three call sites and one deliberate non-caller.

`Ctrl` is undiscoverable without the status line, and Qt's own chart examples zoom on a plain wheel. Plain-wheel zoom is what steals a dashboard's page scroll, so the status line IS the answer here — but a first-time reader still has to read it.

The 25x ceiling is shared with the brush and configurable through `with_min_span`, which no consumer sets. d3's `scaleExtent` is per-consumer for a reason; the first chart with a different data density will want it.

Round 1535.decision_summary: A cell is asked for its decoration role. GridModel had no role dimension — cell and header each returned a String, so the only thing a grid could say about a cell was what it spelled; R1530 named that as Model/View's largest remaining gap and R1532 named the same thing from the paint side. Roles are typed accessors rather than Qt's one data(index, role) returning QVariant, because an untyped hole every caller unwraps is a worse contract in Rust and R1530 already chose this shape when it split headerData out as GridModel::header. Decoration is asked per CELL, which is the axis its value varies on and precisely what R1532's per-column delegate cannot express.
changes_bullets: GridModel gains a third typed accessor `decoration` (Qt `data(index, Qt::DecorationRole)`), asked once per painted cell beside the display role; `no_decoration` is the accessor for a grid with no marked column.
`CellDecoration::Swatch(Color)` — an enum because `Qt::DecorationRole` is a variant type (QColor | QPixmap | QIcon), so the arms pinion cannot paint yet are absent rather than misrepresented.
`text_cell_painter` (Qt `QStyledItemDelegate`) now paints decoration + display, gated so an undecorated cell emits the pre-R1535 node exactly — no swatch, no gap spacer.
`pane_texts` + the new decoration fetch merged into `pane_cells`, which asks both roles against ONE column span so a misaligned mark is unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.
`CellRender` carries the fetched decoration, so a custom delegate places the model's mark instead of re-asking; `TableStyle` gains `decoration_px` / `decoration_gap_px`.
`hello-virtual-table` is the consumer: its `Status` column answers with a colour keyed to the ROW, the axis R1532's per-column delegate cannot express, in the same grid that has a delegated column.
verification_bullets: 7 in-crate tests + 1 example test + `tools/demos/r1535_cell_decoration.py` (36 assertion statements, sections A-G); pinion-widget-paint 756 tests, all 12 grid example crates, 9 grid demos green.
6 counterfactuals run one at a time: per-column resolution, unwired frozen pane, unconditional gap, non-transparent swatch, painter ignoring `None`, relative-instead-of-absolute column span.
CF-6 (relative column span) passed every test as first written — a scrolled-unsplit-grid test was added for it, and the same counterfactual then failed only that test.

Three probes in this round identified a node kind by a property another kind now shares: the in-crate swatch locator read the gap spacer as a mark, and `count_bar_tracks` + the R1532 demo read a swatch as a gauge bar (`BAR_H` == `decoration_px` == 10). All three retightened.

The "unchanged grid" claim was a comparison between two grids that share one painter, so making the gap unconditional passed it; restated as an absolute node-shape assertion, which the same counterfactual then failed.
carry_forward_bullets: The role dimension is opened, not complete: `EditRole` (belongs with the delegate's absent editing half) and `ToolTipRole` (needs a per-cell hover path) are still unanswerable, and the header axis has no role dimension at all.
`CellDecoration` has one arm. The `QIcon` arm is reachable — `Scene::Image` exists and the shell caches sources — and was left out because it would ship a variant no consumer paints.

The decoration is invisible to assistive technology: the accessible name is still the display text, so a decoration-only column would be silent. Qt is silent here too, so this is a stated limit rather than a divergence, but a colour-only status column is a real DCC shape.
One consumer. The mark has never met `row_style` (a per-ROW Foreground/Background role that lives on `VirtualTableData`, not on `GridModel`) — the two role homes are now visibly inconsistent.
`decoration_px` and `hello-virtual-table`'s `BAR_H` are both 10 by coincidence, which is what made three probes ambiguous at once; nothing prevents the next such collision.
The eager `view_table` answers no decoration role (`decorations: &[]`), so the tree still holds two cell-paint surfaces — the shape R1530 left on the header axis and R1532 on the delegate axis.

Round 1536.decision_summary: A decoration states what it means, and the name walk enters a scroll. Qt's decoration role is appearance only — what a mark MEANS is a separate role its item view does not wire to the decoration, so a colour-only status column is an empty cell to a Qt screen-reader user. Here the two travel in one answer and cannot drift. Wiring it and then ASKING the running app what the AT tree said found two stacked defects underneath: the name derivation's walker did not descend a ScrollNode (so no virtualized list, grid or tree could name anything), and the grid marked each cell's own label presentational (a role meant for glyphs a walk must skip past). Qt names its cells; pinion did not. Qt is the floor, not the target.
changes_bullets: `CellDecoration::Swatch` carries a `meaning` beside its `color` — empty is the DECORATIVE answer (HTML `alt=""`, correct when the mark restates the cell's text), non-empty joins the cell's accessible name ahead of the label.

The mark is ADDRESSABLE: `GridTag::cell_decoration` (the `'_'` presentational family, so it never enters the click-router namespace) — R1535 left it anonymous on the reasoning that a tag would shadow the cell, which `pinion_overlay`'s tagged pointer-transparent focus ring disproves.

`find_container_by_tag` descends `Scene::Scroll` — the transparency `rect_for_tag_with_offset` and `lookup_path_ref` already had. Without it nothing painted inside a `ScrollNode` could be named at all.

The grid's cell label is no longer `TextRole::Presentational`: that role is for decoration glyphs a name walk must skip past, and a data cell has no other label — meanwhile `pinion_a11y::tree_view` documented the opposite contract in words.
The mark keeps its declared size in a tight cell (`min_size`); the flex pass was shrinking a 10px swatch to 6px against its sibling label.
`hello-virtual-table` gains a mark-only `Flag` column, so one grid now carries plain text, a decorative mark, a meaningful mark and a delegated gauge.
verification_bullets: Measured on the running app, before -> after: `hello-virtual-table` 0 of 75 `gridcell`s named -> 75 of 75. The reach is not the grid's: `hello-virtual-list` 1/16 -> 16/16, `hello-listbox` 1/13 -> 13/13, `hello-file-browser` 1/6 -> 6/6, `hello-lazy-list` -> 17/17.

The a11y regression hid for ~760 rounds because the BOUNDS walker descends a scroll: the AT tree was structurally correct and pointed at the right pixels while announcing nothing, so no structural assertion could see it.

`enrich_names_from_scene` indexes the scene ONCE instead of searching it per node — `O(nodes x scene)` to `O(scene + nodes)`. Making the walk succeed is what made the quadratic term real.

`CellDecoration::Icon { source, meaning }` — Qt's `QIcon` arm, drawn `Fit::Contain` at the same square with the same address / shrink / hit rules, shared through `decoration_layout`.
`TableData::decoration` — the EAGER `view_table` answers the role too, so the tree no longer holds two cell-paint contracts that disagree about whether it exists.
`hello-table` consumes the icon arm: two theme-coloured discs registered under R1404 `memory://` sources, no vendored asset; the mark is decorative because it restates its own cell's label.
verification_bullets: Every R1536 carry is closed; none was deferred. The round ends with carry 0 except nothing — there is no external dependency left open here.

Round 1537.decision_summary: The frame states what the GPU took: pinion owns the wgpu device so it can ask for TIMESTAMP_QUERY, and brackets each frame with two timestamp queries. Recorded as an upstream blocker, it was ours — vello::Renderer::new takes a device the caller owns.
changes_bullets: New leaf crate `pinion-gpu`: `GpuContext` owns the wgpu instance / adapter / device / queue and `GpuSurface` the swapchain plus the intermediate storage target and blitter, replacing `vello::util::RenderContext`, whose private `new_device` fixes the feature set so no device it returns can carry `TIMESTAMP_QUERY`. The device is asked for the intersection of what the adapter offers with `CLEAR_TEXTURE | PIPELINE_CACHE` (vello's own request, kept identical) plus `TIMESTAMP_QUERY | TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_ENCODERS`; an adapter without them still boots and reports no GPU time.

`pinion_gpu::FrameTimer` brackets one frame's GPU work with two timestamp queries, resolves them and reads the result back WITHOUT blocking the frame that wrote it. The opening stamp is submitted in its own near-empty command buffer because it must be ordered before the rasterizer's internal submit and `render_to_texture` records into no caller encoder; the closing stamp rides the blit encoder. A frame whose predecessor is still in flight is SKIPPED, never blended.

`GpuFrameClock` is three states, not `Option<u64>`: `Unsupported` (this machine never will) / `Pending` (nothing new since you last asked) / `Measured(us)`. `clock()` takes `&mut self` and CONSUMES the reading, so each measurement is stamped onto exactly one frame sample — reporting the persisting level instead put the same number on every sample in the ring, which made `mean_gpu_us` a mean of one value repeated and made `gpu_sample_count` count frames.

The forge `backend="vello"` template is built on the owned device, gains `gpu_clock()` / `gpu_timing_counts()` and a `Gpu(GpuError)` error arm; every timing site is gated on the timer existing, so a host that cannot measure creates no encoder and submits no extra command buffer. 192 example manifests gain the dep.

`pinion_runtime::FrameTiming::gpu_us: Option<u64>` (builder `with_gpu`), and the window fold gains `mean_gpu_us` / `max_gpu_us` / `gpu_sample_count` / `gpu_timing_supported` / `gpu_dropped_total`. The mean divides by the TIMED sample count, not the frame count. `scene/frame_timings` publishes all of it, omitting the three durations rather than zeroing them.

The `scene/screenshot` capture path is timed by the same clock. It is a real rasterize + blit, and it is the only paint an agent driving the window over RPC gets — this is the first change to exercise `vello_capture`'s stated mirror-not-lift obligation.
verification_bullets: Adapter probe (built, read, deleted): `TIMESTAMP_QUERY` + `TIMESTAMP_QUERY_INSIDE_ENCODERS` present on all three adapters this project builds against — NVIDIA RTX 4070/Vulkan, llvmpipe/Vulkan (what CI uses), NVIDIA/GL. The round's premise is measured, not assumed.

`tools/demos/r1537_gpu_frame_clock.py` PASS on two bindings: `gpu_us` present and > 0, values distinct across frames, `gpu_sample_count == frame_count - 1` exactly on every driven frame, `gpu_dropped_total == 0`, the CPU partition `total >= build+encode+acquire+render` still exact, and every GPU aggregate omitted rather than zeroed before the first sample.

Five counterfactuals, one at a time, each restored and the restore VERIFIED: (1) close the span before the blit -> template order guard fails; (2) ungate the timing cost -> the `pays_nothing` guard fails; (3) divide the GPU mean by `window_len` -> `r1537_gpu_mean_is_over_timed_samples_not_over_frames` fails; (4) report a constant 1234us -> the demo's not-a-constant assertion fails; (5) never map the staging buffer -> the per-frame sample-count assertion fails.

Counterfactual (5) is also how the consumed-reading defect was found: an incomplete restore left the capture path unmapped, and with the level being re-stamped every frame the wire still looked healthy at one real measurement per 14 frames. Only one sample had ever landed.

Local gates green: clippy `-D pedantic` and tests on pinion-gpu / pinion-runtime / pinion-rpc / pinion-forge / pinion-shell, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`.
No regression in the four existing frame-timing demos (r907, r925, r1460, r1389), all PASS.
carry_forward_bullets: The GPU span covers rasterize + blit, not present. What the compositor does after `present()` is outside any queue timestamp pinion can write, so a frame's true screen latency is still unmeasured. External: it needs a presentation-timestamp extension wgpu does not expose.

No large-scene 60fps END-TO-END measurement. This round makes the GPU number exist; the perf axis's other named gap — a scale-invariance claim over a large scene — is untouched, and a wall-clock assertion would collide with the zero-flake rule, so it needs deterministic counters.

The extra command buffer per timed frame is unmeasured. It is one near-empty submit, gated on timing being possible, but this round did not price it — and the axis's own standing rule is that an unmeasured cost is a cost nobody revisits.

`FrameTimer::dropped` counts a failed staging map without unmapping, because `unmap` on a never-mapped buffer raises a wgpu validation error. If that path is ever hit repeatedly the buffer state is untested — no host has produced one, so the recovery is reasoned rather than observed.
`GpuSurface` is per-`GpuContext` with one adapter. A discrete/integrated split or a second X screen needs a second context, which multi-window would want; nothing in-tree exercises it.

The three-state clock is consumed by exactly one caller. `FrameTimer::last_gpu_us` (the persisting level) now has no production consumer, kept because it is what a HUD would read; a second consumer would settle whether it earns its place.

Round 1537.1.decision_summary: The R1537 carry list is closed rather than carried: the unpriced cost is measured and bounded, seven accessors with no consumer are removed, and the sample-discard branch is made testable without a GPU.
changes_bullets: Carry ⓒ (the extra command buffer was unpriced) CLOSED by measurement. Interleaved with/without pairs, 60 steady-state frames each, timer disabled at construction: median `render_us` without = 634 / 629 / 668 µs, with = 634 / 726 / 674 µs. The between-configuration difference (~34µs median) is smaller than the within-configuration spread (39µs without, 92µs with), so the extra submit is NOT resolvable in `render_us` at n=60 on this host — bounded under ~5% of the CPU submit phase rather than shown to be zero.

Carry ⓕ (accessors with no consumer) CLOSED by removal. A census found seven: `FrameTimer::last_gpu_us` / `samples` / `period_ns`, `GpuContext::adapter` / `gpu_timing`, `GpuSurface::target_texture` / `can_copy_from_surface`. `last_gpu_us` was the worst of them — a persisting *level* beside the consumed `fresh` reading, two stored sources for one question, and the windowed level a caller actually wants is the ring fold (`mean_gpu_us` / `max_gpu_us`). `GpuContext` no longer stores whether the timestamp request succeeded either; `FrameTimer::new` reads it back off the device, so there is one source rather than two that can disagree.

The emitted renderer's `gpu_timing_counts() -> (u64, u64)` becomes `gpu_dropped_samples() -> u64`. Its one consumer read `.1` and discarded `.0`, which is an accessor with no consumer wearing a tuple.

Carry ⓓ (the discard branch was reasoned, not tested) CLOSED for the half that can be: `span_us_from(start, end, period_ns)` is now a free function, so the branch that DISCARDS an out-of-order tick pair is testable without a GPU. The map-failure half stays reasoned — no host has produced one.
verification_bullets: Counterfactual: replace the discard with `wrapping_sub` — the naive form, which would report ~18 million seconds of GPU time as a hitch — and `r1537_out_of_order_ticks_are_discarded_not_reported` fails. Restored, and the restore verified by grep rather than assumed.

`pinion-gpu` unit tests 2 -> 5; the new three cover the discard, integral-microsecond truncation (`Some(0)` for a sub-microsecond frame is a MEASUREMENT, not an absence), and that a device's `timestampPeriod` actually scales the span.

The map-failure path deliberately does not `unmap` (an `unmap` on a never-mapped buffer raises a wgpu validation error, i.e. a second fault reported for a non-existent problem). No host has produced a failure, so that recovery is reasoned rather than observed — and `gpu_dropped_total` is what would make it visible.

Round 1538.decision_summary: The frame states how much of the scene it walked: scene/frame_timings gains a node census, so 60fps-at-scale becomes a complexity claim asserted with deterministic counters instead of a wall clock that reads the host.
changes_bullets: `pinion_runtime::LayoutPass { scroll_dirty, nodes }` replaces the bare `bool` the layout entries returned. `nodes` is taffy's own `total_node_count()` for the pass's tree plus every nested scroll pass's — read from the tree, never walked, because a profiler that traverses the scene to size the scene is the cost it exists to find. `build` stops at a `Scene::Scroll`, so the scrolled half has no outer equivalent and is exactly where a large scene lives.

`FragmentCache` counts the nodes the encode walk ENTERS, per paint, published by `end_paint`. A cacheable container that hits returns before descending, so the count describes the walk and not the tree — which is what `scene/cache_stats`' hit rate cannot state: replaying two enormous fragments and replaying two tiny ones are both 100%.

`FrameTiming` gains `scene_nodes` / `layout_nodes` / `encode_nodes` (builder `with_census`) and the window fold gains `max_scene_nodes` / `max_layout_nodes` / `max_encode_nodes`. Maxima, not means: the guarded property is an upper bound, and one frame that built the whole model averages away. `scene_nodes` is the LAST settle pass's count (the tree that reached the screen); `layout_nodes` is the sum over passes (what was paid for).

`PaintWork` replaces the `(u32, bool, u64)` tuple the paint producer handed the surface — R1538 would have made it three same-typed `u32`s written positionally at a distance, the transposition R1459 refused. All four view producers now state their size: `ProduceWork` and `MirrorWork` gain `nodes`, so an agent can price the work its OWN call caused, where `passes_total` counts loop iterations and is the same number for a 40-node scene and a 40,000-node one.

New example `hello-scene-scale`: one binding whose model steps 1e2 to 1e6 at runtime and whose list is virtualized or EAGER on demand. The eager arm is a deliberate negative control — a scale guard that can only measure the passing case cannot fail, and a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate (R1527). Its cap refuses rather than clamps, because a guard reading a clamped value cannot tell a bound from a lie.

`end_paint`'s two exits each carried their own copy of the per-paint publish, so R1538 hoisted the pair ahead of the early return before adding a third to it. `post_layout_write_backs` is lifted out of `compute_layout_inner`, whose whole content is the ORDER of three writes that was previously stated only by their adjacency inside a hundred-line body.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1538_scene_scale.py` PASS: the painted tree is IDENTICAL across a 10,000x model growth (63 nodes at every rung of 1e2..1e6), identical again at the far end of a million-row scroll, and the eager arm's grows one node per row. 29 assertion sites, several inside loops; not one names a microsecond, a frame rate or a machine.

Measured rather than adjusted: the top of a list has no rows above it to overscan into, and a row-aligned offset needs one fewer partial row than a misaligned one. Round 1539.decision_summary: The wire states the shape of what it answers: every serialized type declares its key set, nesting, absence and nullability, published by rpc/schema and gated against the types it describes.
changes_bullets: `pinion_rpc::wire_census` — `WIRE_TYPES`, a census of all 82 types this crate serializes: per type a `WireShape` (object / string enum / internally-tagged union / scalar union), per field the wire name, the JSON type, whether the key may be ABSENT, whether it may be `null`, and `of` — a `$ref` naming the censused type nested there. References, not inline shapes, so `LayoutNode.children` can name `LayoutNode` without the const cycle inlining would need.

`optional` and `nullable` are separate columns because they are separate contracts. `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]` omits the KEY; a bare `Option<T>` keeps the key and writes `null`. Both are `Option<T>` in Rust and look identical there — the first census conflated them and was wrong about twelve fields until the gate compared it against the source.

New method `rpc/schema` publishes the census, so an agent discovers the SHAPE of what it will be answered with and not only the names of methods. The census describes ITSELF (§2 #7): `WireType`, `WireField`, `WireShape`, `WireTy`, `RpcSchema` are all in it, so the reply that lists the shapes has a listed shape.

`crates/pinion-rpc/tests/wire_census_matches_types.rs` parses this crate's own source and asserts the census matches it — set-equality on the type names AND per-type equality of the field lists. The same edit that took CI red now fails in `pinion-rpc`'s unit gate, in the round that makes it.

On failure the gate NAMES the demos that assert on the changed field names, ranked by how many they name. The local gate runs the demos a round TOUCHED; the ones a wire change breaks are exactly the ones it did not.
`tools/demos/r1465_mirror_work.py` expects five mirror fields and three produce fields — the R1538 addition it was still red on.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1539_wire_states_its_shape.py` PASS: 32 assertion sites, several over the whole 82-type census (281 field checks). Six live methods are validated against their declared type recursively, exercising all four shape kinds.

Six counterfactuals, one at a time, each restored and every restore verified: (1) a field added to `FrameTimingsMirror` exactly as R1538 added `nodes_total`; (2) a new `Serialize` type absent from the census; (3) `optional` claimed where the source says `nullable`; (4) a wrong JSON type; (5) a dangling `of` reference; (6) a type dropped from the census.
Counterfactual (1) is the round's central claim: the gate fails, and the FIRST demo it names is `r1465_mirror_work.py` — the one that took CI red 44 minutes into the R1538 sweep.

Counterfactual (3) fails in BOTH gates independently: the unit test reports `string|null` against `string?`, and the demo reports the live `focus/get` answering `null` under a declaration that forbids it. The two checks are not one check twice.
Counterfactual (2) was proved by the round's own work rather than staged: adding `RpcSchema` made the completeness gate fail until the census was extended.

The gate found three defects in its own first draft — a `Response` type the bootstrap generator's regex missed, multi-line `#[serde(...)]` attributes read as one line, and one-line struct variants read as a single field. The parser was rewritten character-driven.

Local gates green on both crates whose behaviour changed: `cargo test -p pinion-rpc` (1026 + 4), `cargo test -p pinion-shell` (428), `cargo clippy -p pinion-rpc --all-targets -D pedantic`, `cargo fmt --all --check`. Demos affected by the new catalog entry run and pass: r1465, r1539, r1089, r1419.
`tools/phase_b_tally.py --selftest` PASS; the new demo is registered in `NOT_EVIDENCE` because it calls `cache_stats` to check a shape, not to measure a cost.
carry_forward_bullets: Which method answers with which type is NOT declared. This is the one place Qt 6.11 is still ahead — `QMetaMethod::returnMetaType()` binds a return type to a method. It is withheld rather than shipped partial: the census holds 28 `*Outcome` types against 91 routed methods, so a `response` column would read `null` for most of the surface, and an agent reads a null return type as "answers with nothing" rather than "not described yet". Giving those handlers response types is the named next slice.

The census covers `pinion-rpc` only. `scene/snapshot` and `scene/access` answer with trees built in `pinion-core` and `pinion-a11y`, and the gate's source parse does not reach them. It is a stated boundary, not an oversight — but the same class of defect can still land there unseen.

The gate is source-text, the trade `catalog_matches_dispatch_match_arms` already makes. It is loud rather than lenient — an unmodelled `#[serde]` attribute panics — but a `flatten` or a custom `serialize_with` would need the parser taught before it could be used.

The census is hand-written and the gate proves it TRUE, not that it was written deliberately. A round that adds a field and pastes the gate's expectation satisfies both. The demo-consumer list is what makes that a decision rather than a reflex, and nothing forces it to be read.

Round 1540.decision_summary: A text run states its underline form and colour: the GUI adopts the SGR 4:x vocabulary the terminal has spoken since R1399, so a diagnostic undercurl is drawable on screen and not only in a cell grid.
changes_bullets: `UnderlineStyle` moves from `term_grid` to `style`, the general text-style home, and is re-exported so its 61 existing sites are undisturbed. A run and a cell are the same question asked of two backends; SGR 4:x is one ENCODING of the vocabulary, and it stays with the terminal writer that speaks it.

`TextDecoration.underline` becomes that enum instead of a `bool`, and gains `underline_color: Option<Color>` (Qt `setUnderlineColor`, SGR 58). One field, not two: a bool beside a style would be two sources for one fact. `with_underline(bool)` keeps Qt's `setFontUnderline` meaning — on selects `Single`, off clears whatever form was there — so every pre-R1540 caller reads unchanged.

`paint_decorations` calls `paint_underline`, the painter the cell grid has used since R1399. Both now place a form identically, which is what lets a GUI and a TUI rendering of one document agree. The strikethrough stays on the plain primitive: it has exactly one form in both SGR (9) and Qt, so it borrows no axis it cannot use.

The form is resolved per run by byte offset in `positioned_runs`, mirroring parley's own last-push-wins overlap rule — parley carries the underline's brush and metrics but has no notion of an undercurl. `PositionedRun.underline` becomes `Option<RunUnderline>` so the form and the rule travel together and cannot disagree about whether there is an underline.

`hello-richtext` carries the two canonical diagnostic marks: a blue dotted rule under purple text, a red undercurl under saddle-brown italic. The colours are unlike the text they sit under, because that is the contract a separate colour axis exists for.
verification_bullets: `crates/pinion-shell` `r1540_glyph_run_underline_draws_its_form` — a pixel witness, font-independent by construction: same text, size, position and font across every render, each DIFFERENCED against an unstyled baseline so only the underline's own ink is measured and no glyph enters an assertion. `None` adds zero ink (the negative control), `Double` inks past `Single`, `Dotted`/`Dashed` ink less with the dashed duty cycle higher, `Curly`'s crest rises above a straight rule, and a red squiggle inks red and not green.

`tools/demos/r1540_underline_states_its_form.py` PASS: 29 assertion sites (39 with loops expanded) over the live wire. Neither mark is `single` — a bool could already express a plain rule, so a demo showing only one could not tell this round from the last.

Five counterfactuals, one at a time, each restored and every restore verified: (1) the painter flattened back to one rule; (2) parley never handed the underline's own brush; (3) the wire spelling capitalized; (4) the overlap precedence inverted to first-wins; (5) the serde spelling unification removed.

Counterfactual (4) closed a hole the first draft had: nothing exercised OVERLAPPING style runs, so the mirror of parley's overlap rule was stated and unasserted. The new unit test asserts the AGREEMENT OF TWO INDEPENDENT OBSERVATIONS — parley picks the winning span's brush by its own rule, pinion picks its form by the mirror — so a drifted mirror shows up as one span's form under the other's colour.

A demo census over the changed wire form found `r967_textarea_toggle_format.py`, which asserted `underline == False`. Running it surfaced a REAL pre-existing defect this round would otherwise have shipped.

Local gates green on every crate whose behaviour changed: tests + clippy `-D pedantic` on pinion-core, pinion-text, pinion-runtime, pinion-rpc, pinion-tui, pinion-shell and hello-richtext, plus `cargo fmt --all --check`. Every demo that reads a decoration was run: r1540, r713, r967, r1399, r974, r1403, todomvc r664/r665/r666.
carry_forward_bullets: The mark is invisible to assistive technology. A red undercurl says "error" to a sighted reader and nothing at all to a screen reader, which is the defect R1536 named for grid decorations. Qt is in the same position — `QTextCharFormat`'s underline style is presentation-only — so this is Qt-parity rather than below it, but it is the axis's largest remaining gap and there is no per-run a11y surface in the tree to hang it on yet.

Qt's `DashDotLine` / `DashDotDotLine` are deliberately not adopted. They exist because they are `Qt::PenStyle` arms, they have no SGR encoding, and adopting them would make one document render differently by backend for a mark no editor draws. The capability (multiple distinguishable forms including a wave) is present; the shape was chosen, which is what [[qt-is-the-floor-not-the-target]] permits.

The ratatui TUI arm still collapses every form to one `UNDERLINED` modifier. That is ratatui's vocabulary, not ours — the SGR forms reach a real terminal through the cell-grid arm — but it means the same document has three fidelities (GUI, cell grid, ratatui) and only two of them are guarded.

Round 1541.decision_summary: A cold connection is admitted on readiness, not on a 50 ms timer: the RPC endpoint's accept loop waits on the listener, so a per-invocation consumer no longer pays a poll interval it has nothing to amortise over.
changes_bullets: `pinion-rpc-transport`'s accept loop no longer sleeps a fixed 50 ms per `WouldBlock`. It waits on `poll(2)` over two fds — the listener, and the read half of an out-of-band `UnixStream::pair` wake channel — with an unbounded timeout, so an arrival is admitted the instant the kernel has it and an idle endpoint makes no syscalls at all.

The wake channel is deliberately NOT the socket path. A self-connect wake (the alternative the old docstring named) has to reach the endpoint through its own name, so it must happen before the unlink — which puts an unbounded `connect` inside `Drop` and re-opens the successor window R1478 closed. Out-of-band, the R1478 ordering is untouched: unlink first, while the listener is still open.

The signal is the wake channel's CLOSE, not a byte written into it. A first draft wrote a byte and then dropped the half, which is two mechanisms for one signal; closing an fd cannot fail, and a failed wake would leave the loop parked with `shutdown`'s join waiting on it forever.

`TransportControl::accept_wakeups` publishes how many times the loop returned from its wait. That is what makes "the wait is demand-driven" assertable as a COUNT rather than as a duration: an idle endpoint reads 0 however long it idles, one arrival reads 1, an idle lifetime plus a shutdown reads 1. Qt's `QLocalServer` publishes no equivalent — the wait lives inside `QSocketNotifier` where a consumer cannot see it.

The per-connection writer sends one frame in one write. `writeln!` on an unbuffered socket issued the payload and the terminator as two syscalls — measured by `strace`, not inferred — costing the client an extra readable event per response. `write_replies` takes its sink by generic so the call COUNT is observable; a `BufWriter` would not fix it, because a response past its capacity bypasses the buffer and leaves the terminator for a second write.

`rustix` (safe `poll(2)` wrapper, already transitive via async-io and calloop) joins the workspace. `libc::poll` needs `unsafe`, which `workspace.lints` forbids outright, and `polling::Poller::add` is itself an `unsafe fn`; two fds and one socketpair need no readiness framework.
verification_bullets: Measured before and after on the same box by the same file (`tests/accept_wakes_on_arrival.rs`): cold connect-request-response median 50,141 us (min 49,955 / max 50,366) polled, 36 us (min 32 / max 250) waiting on readiness — 1,393x. The narrow band is the signature of a timer, and it matches the sprag consumer's independent 50,188 us (p10 50.021 / p90 50.332) to three digits on a different machine.

Six guards, five of them machine-independent counts rather than durations: an idle endpoint wakes 0 times, a withdrawn one also 0, one arrival is exactly 1, three arrivals are 1-2-3 checked as each lands, and an endpoint that only ever shuts down wakes exactly once. The sixth bounds the cold median with two-sided margin (~690x below, 2x above the defect's fastest sample).

Five counterfactuals, one at a time, each restored and every restore verified by md5: (1) the pre-R1541 sleep-poll wait; (2) shutdown sets the flag but never delivers it; (3) the listener left blocking; (4) the framing back to `writeln!`; (5) the two poll slots read from each other's index.

Counterfactual (1) exposed a REAL HOLE and the tests were rewritten before it passed: `one_arrival_is_one_wakeup` and `three_arrivals_are_three_wakeups` PASSED on the defective loop, because on a 50 ms timer the client spends its whole round-trip waiting out exactly one interval, so the count reads 1 there too. Bracketing each arrival with idle periods states the property the bare count cannot. All six now fail under (1).

`tools/demos/r1541_cold_connection_costs_nothing.py` PASS: 31 assertion sites over the live `AF_UNIX` wire against a real app, and it FAILS on the defective transport at 48.671 ms with 20 of 21 connections over budget.

The demo's first draft would have shipped a 1.5x margin while claiming ~100x. Comparing cold round-trips against warm ones does NOT isolate the accept path: measured, the difference was 16.6 ms with the accept path already fixed, because `hello-conn-lifecycle` repaints on `on_connect` and a request dispatched while that repaint is in flight lands one vsync later. The baseline is now the SECOND request on the same fresh connection — both pay the app's cadence, only the first can pay an admission — measured at -0.09/-0.10/+0.02 ms over three runs with a worst single sample of 0.71 ms.

Local gates green on every crate whose behaviour changed and every demo that drives this transport: `cargo test`/`clippy -D pedantic` on pinion-rpc-transport and pinion-shell, clippy on hello-conn-lifecycle and hello-endpoint-identity, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and demos r1541, r1469, r1393, r1478.
carry_forward_bullets: `accept_wakeups` is a Rust-level counter and reaches no RPC method, so an agent cannot read it. This is a scope statement rather than an omission: PR-47 puts the transport's LIFETIME with the consumer, `pinion-shell` never holds a `TransportControl` (verified — it names the type only in a doc comment), so the framework has nothing to publish it from. A framework-side transport registry would be a new design axis, and the module header explicitly rejects one.

A cold round-trip against `hello-conn-lifecycle` still measures ~16.6 ms, and none of it is the transport: the app repaints its connection list on `on_connect`, and an RPC dispatched while that repaint is in flight lands after the next present. The demo's baseline proves this by paying the same price with no admission in it. Whether the shell should dispatch RPC ahead of a vsync-blocked present is a separate axis (R1361.1 already recorded that `render_us` carries vsync backpressure).

The accept loop's drain admits everything queued before returning to the wait, and that is deliberately NOT asserted. It is not load-bearing for correctness — a level-triggered wait simply returns again for the next connection — and how many of a burst have landed by the time the drain runs is a timing question no zero-flake test can pin.

The wake-readiness branch in the accept loop is unreachable through the public API (`Drop` runs `shutdown`, which stores the flag before it closes the channel). It exists so a level-triggered fd that stayed ready cannot spin a core, i.e. the impossible state exits rather than being assumed away — but it is a branch no test can reach.

`ERROR_BACKOFF` still parks 50 ms after a failed wait or a non-`WouldBlock` accept error. Descriptor exhaustion is the realistic cause and no test exercises it, so the endpoint's behaviour under `EMFILE` is reasoned about rather than measured.

Round 1542.decision_summary: A grid states the winsize its PRODUCER was given: rect goes back to meaning the paint extent alone, so a pane sized by an authority other than the layout can finally say what it holds.
changes_bullets: `TextGridNode` gains `winsize: Option<(u16, u16)>` plus `with_winsize` / `winsize()`. `cols()` / `rows()` answer the declaration when there is one and derive from `rect` when there is not — so every existing binding is bit-identical, the struct being `#[non_exhaustive]` already.

One `rect` was meaning two things: the PAINT EXTENT (R1028 fills all of it so a sub-cell margin cannot leak the parent surface) and the WINSIZE. They agree only while the layout is what sizes the producer. sprag is a multiplexer where it is not — a daemon tiles a session in CELLS, a display client lays those panes out in PIXELS, and one boundary quantised twice sat permanently at 38 painted vs 37 buffered. Shrinking the rect trades R1028 away; leaving it mute trades the fact away. R1542 splits them.

The wire gains `winsize_source` (`"layout"` / `"producer"`) on `TextGridSnapshot`. R-80.2 asked the R974.1 interpretation rule to gain a conditional, and a conditional a client cannot evaluate is not a rule: the AUTHORITY is not recoverable from the values, because a declaration equal to the derivation is byte-identical to none. This is the same move R974.1 made when it stopped clients inferring the projection size from `grid_rows` lengths.

**Both painters now clamp to the node's winsize**, closing a §2 #6 divergence the round exposed. The TUI arm has clamped since R995; the Vello arm leaned on its `rect` clip, which is equivalent ONLY while the winsize is the derivation. It stopped being equivalent twice over: a rect whose width is not a whole number of cells left the GUI painting a sliver of one more column than the TUI showed, and a declared winsize can be narrower on purpose. The grid cursor is bounded by what was painted for the same reason.

`hello-textgrid` grows `htg_tiled` — the sprag case at demo scale (rect spans 8 cells, producer holds 7). Its paint extent is DERIVED from the span constant rather than written beside it, because the round's whole claim is that the two are different facts.
verification_bullets: Five contract tests in `pinion-core`: an undeclared grid derives (the pre-R1542 default, pinned because every binding in the tree is that case); a declared one answers the declaration; declaring does not touch `rect` AND the derivation is still computable from it; a declaration EQUAL to the derivation is still a declaration; and a declaration survives the next layout pass writing `rect`.

`pinion-shell` `r1542_declared_winsize_leaves_the_sub_grid_margin_to_the_gutter_fill` — the report's acceptance criterion, in pixels. The buffer DELIVERS 4 columns and the producer was told to hold 3, with a rect spanning all four, so only the declaration excludes the last one. It must read palette default bg: red means the painter drew a column the node does not hold, white means the gutter fill stopped covering the rect (what shrinking the rect would have produced).

`pinion-tui` `r1542_declared_winsize_bounds_what_the_tui_paints` — the §2 #6 sibling on the same buffer shape. R1542 changed no code in that arm; it changed what `n.cols()` answers, and the guard is what makes that a property rather than a coincidence.

`pinion-rpc`: the declared winsize reaches the snapshot with its authority; the authority is reported even when the VALUES agree (the case no client could infer); and `r1542_the_text_grid_wire_states_its_exact_key_set`.

`tools/demos/r1542_grid_states_its_winsize.py` PASS, 44 assertion sites over the live wire. Its strongest arm is a controlled pair: `htg_cursor_blink` has a pixel-identical rect and the same cell metric, so two nodes with IDENTICAL geometry report different `cols` — which is the whole claim in one comparison. Eleven other grids in the same snapshot report `"layout"` and derive `cols` from their rects, so the field is shown to discriminate rather than to be a constant.

Five counterfactuals, one at a time, each restored and every restore md5-verified: (1) `cols()` ignores the declaration; (2) the Vello painter drops the clamp — the pixel guard reads (255,0,0) where it wants black; (3) the TUI painter drops it; (4) `winsize_source` is a constant; (5) the wire key is dropped.

Local gates green on every crate whose behaviour changed — tests + clippy `-D pedantic` on pinion-core, pinion-rpc, pinion-runtime, pinion-tui, pinion-shell and hello-textgrid, plus `cargo fmt --all --check`. All 31 `#[ignore]d` headless pixel guards pass, including all 14 grid ones, so the paint clamp regressed nothing. Every demo that reads the TextGrid wire was run: r1542, r972, r973, r974, r976, r977, r978, r1008, r1399, r1403, r1424, r1425, r1427.
carry_forward_bullets: **R1539's census gate cannot see this change, and that is a finding about R1539 rather than about R1542.** Its scope statement is "every value this crate serializes"; its discriminator is `#[derive(Serialize)]`. `TextGridSnapshot` derives none — it is hand-built into a `serde_json::Map` by `text_grid_snapshot_fields`, and MEASURED, 51 such hand-serializer functions live in `dispatch.rs`. So a key was added to a published response and every gate in the tree stayed green: the second instance of exactly the failure R1539 was built to prevent (R1538 was the first). What is closed here is R1542's own exposure — the type this round changed now has the exact-key-set assertion the derived types get for free, in a unit test and again over the wire. Teaching the census a second discriminator is a campaign the size of R1539 itself and is the named next slice of the §7 axis.

The TUI backend does not fill a grid's rect with the palette default background at all — R1028 is a Vello-arm contract. The sub-grid margin therefore reads as whatever the parent drew there rather than as terminal background. Pre-existing and arguably right for a character-cell backend (there is no surface to leak), but it means the two arms agree about which cells are the grid and not about what the margin looks like.

A declared winsize is not validated against the rect. A producer may declare a grid wider than its paint extent, and the Vello arm then clips the overflow while the TUI arm draws past the node — the mirror image of the divergence this round closed, in a direction no consumer has asked for. Rejecting it would need a policy (clamp? error? paint anyway?) that no consumer has forced, and inventing one blind is how the wrong one gets frozen.

The winsize is per-node with no reactive seam: a producer re-declares by rebuilding the node in its view-fn, which is how `with_cells` already works. Nothing here is a regression, but a consumer whose daemon changes a pane's size at high frequency will rebuild the node each time.

`pinion-rpc`: the declared winsize reaches the snapshot with its authority; the authority is reported even when the VALUES agree (the case no client could infer); and `r1542_the_text_grid_wire_states_its_exact_key_set`.

`tools/demos/r1542_grid_states_its_winsize.py` PASS, 44 assertion sites over the live wire. Its strongest arm is a controlled pair: `htg_cursor_blink` has a pixel-identical rect and the same cell metric, so two nodes with IDENTICAL geometry report different `cols` — which is the whole claim in one comparison. Eleven other grids in the same snapshot report `"layout"` and derive `cols` from their rects, so the field is shown to discriminate rather than to be a constant.

Five counterfactuals, one at a time, each restored and every restore md5-verified: (1) `cols()` ignores the declaration; (2) the Vello painter drops the clamp — the pixel guard reads (255,0,0) where it wants black; (3) the TUI painter drops it; (4) `winsize_source` is a constant; (5) the wire key is dropped.

Local gates green on every crate whose behaviour changed — tests + clippy `-D pedantic` on pinion-core, pinion-rpc, pinion-runtime, pinion-tui, pinion-shell and hello-textgrid, plus `cargo fmt --all --check`. All 31 `#[ignore]d` headless pixel guards pass, including all 14 grid ones, so the paint clamp regressed nothing. Every demo that reads the TextGrid wire was run: r1542, r972, r973, r974, r976, r977, r978, r1008, r1399, r1403, r1424, r1425, r1427.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: **R1539's census gate cannot see this change, and that is a finding about R1539 rather than about R1542.** Its scope statement is "every value this crate serializes"; its discriminator is `#[derive(Serialize)]`. `TextGridSnapshot` derives none — it is hand-built into a `serde_json::Map` by `text_grid_snapshot_fields`, and MEASURED, 51 such hand-serializer functions live in `dispatch.rs`. So a key was added to a published response and every gate in the tree stayed green: the second instance of exactly the failure R1539 was built to prevent (R1538 was the first). What is closed here is R1542's own exposure — the type this round changed now has the exact-key-set assertion the derived types get for free, in a unit test and again over the wire. Teaching the census a second discriminator is a campaign the size of R1539 itself and is the named next slice of the §7 axis.

The TUI backend does not fill a grid's rect with the palette default background at all — R1028 is a Vello-arm contract. The sub-grid margin therefore reads as whatever the parent drew there rather than as terminal background. Pre-existing and arguably right for a character-cell backend (there is no surface to leak), but it means the two arms agree about which cells are the grid and not about what the margin looks like.

A declared winsize is not validated against the rect. A producer may declare a grid wider than its paint extent, and the Vello arm then clips the overflow while the TUI arm draws past the node — the mirror image of the divergence this round closed, in a direction no consumer has asked for. Rejecting it would need a policy (clamp? error? paint anyway?) that no consumer has forced, and inventing one blind is how the wrong one gets frozen.

The winsize is per-node with no reactive seam: a producer re-declares by rebuilding the node in its view-fn, which is how `with_cells` already works. Nothing here is a regression, but a consumer whose daemon changes a pane's size at high frequency will rebuild the node each time.

Round 1543.decision_summary: A label declares its mnemonic (Qt `&File`): one declaration on the painted TextNode from which the underline ink, the Alt+char binding, and the AT accesskey are all derived, plus `scene/mnemonics` — an accelerator map with static conflict reporting that Qt keeps private in QShortcutMap.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::mnemonic` — `Mnemonic` / `MnemonicLabel::parse` (Qt's `&` / `&&` vocabulary, character for character) / `MnemonicBinding` / `scene_mnemonics`, the paint-scene-derived accelerator map with case-insensitive folding by full Unicode lowercase mapping and static ambiguity.

`TextNode.mnemonic` is the sole authority; `TextNode::mnemonic_styled` / `with_mnemonic` / `with_mnemonic_buddy` lower the discoverable underline into a `StyleRun` over exactly the marked character, so both the Vello and the TUI painters draw it through the styled-run path they already had (R713 + R1540) with no per-backend paint code.

`CoreShell::dispatch_mnemonic{,_for_window}` resolves Alt+char against the painted scene, focuses the target (falling back to a composite's owner), and fires `KeyboardActivate`; ambiguous keys cycle in paint order through a per-(window, key) cursor keyed by target tag. Both shells call it — the GUI ahead of `keybinding`/`apply_key`, the TUI ahead of the same pair — so the two backends cannot diverge on what Alt+F does.

`pinion_core::widgets::aria::send_keyboard_activate` lifted out of `apply_aria_activate` (2nd consumer): composite-aware via the R742.4 `#` SSOT + the R51.42 `:` SSOT, so `menu#t0` sends `t0:KeyboardActivate` exactly as the router addresses a click. `MenuBar::activate_title` adds the WAI-ARIA §3.5 keyboard open (first item highlighted, unlike the pointer open), and the menu's send wire accepts `KeyboardActivate` on titles and items.

`AccessNode.access_key` -> `accesskit::Node::set_access_key` (UIA `AccessKey`, deliberately NOT `keyboard_shortcut`), stamped by `enrich_access_keys_from_scene` at the `build_access_tree` chokepoint, and mirrored on the `scene/access` wire as `accesskey`.

`scene/mnemonics` publishes the whole map (key / accel / target / label / index / ambiguous) with both new types registered in the R1539 `WIRE_TYPES` census. Consumers: `hello-menu-app` titles + items, `settings-panel`'s `QLabel::setBuddy` form row.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1543_label_declares_its_mnemonic.py` — 60+ executed assertions over `hello-menu-app`: the published map's exact key set and every field, the `&` absent from pixels and from the AT, `accesskey` agreeing with the map on the same tag, Alt+F opening a COMPOSITE tag, the map growing with the open dropdown and shrinking when it closes with no registration anywhere, Alt+S emitting the same `menu.command` intent a click emits, and two negative controls (an undeclared Alt+key, and the same character without Alt).

Backend parity observed, not inferred (§2 #6): `pinion-text` drives the real shaper and asserts ONE glyph underlined at a non-zero x; `pinion-tui` asserts the marked cell carries `UNDERLINED` and the other three do not.

7 counterfactuals, one at a time, every restore md5-verified: drop the Alt gate (demo J fails), keep the `&` in the display string (demo B), drop the accesskey stamp (demo C), underline the whole label (pinion-text AND pinion-tui), disable cycling (CoreShell), stop descending into `Scene::Scroll` (core), reject item activation (demo F).

Gates: `cargo test` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -D pedantic` green on all 8 changed crates + both changed examples; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; the R1539 census gate green with the two new wire types. Round 1544.decision_summary: A cell states whether it can be edited: the delegate's editing half (Qt createEditor / setEditorData / setModelData), the model's EditRole fused with ItemIsEditable, and the view's latch + trigger gate — with a refused write keeping the editor open, which Qt's void setModelData cannot express.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::cell_value::CellEdit` — a cell's `Qt::EditRole` answer, fused with `flags() & Qt::ItemIsEditable`: `None` IS "not editable", so producing an editor for a read-only cell is unrepresentable rather than a check the view must remember. `From<&CellValue>` seeds it from `edit_text()`, whose documented inverse is `CellKind::parse`.

`pinion-core::model_index` — `CellIndex` moved down from `pinion_widget_paint::table` (re-exported there, so no path changed) beside `CellValue`, the model's other half, plus `GridExtent`. Forced: the editing latch is state, state substrates live in this crate, and a module cannot name a type defined above it.

`pinion-core::widgets::grid_edit` — `GridEditState` (the latch, Qt's `QAbstractItemView` half), `EditTrigger` / `EditTriggers` (Qt `EditTriggers`, persisted as its wire NAMES so a new arm cannot reinterpret a stored bitmask), `EndEditHint`, `use_grid_edit`. `commit_with` propagates the model's verdict; `advance` walks the MODEL extent row-major with wrap, bounded by the cell count.

`pinion-widget-paint::table` — `GridModel::edit` (the fourth role), `no_edit`, `GridEditing` / `CellEditRender` / `CellEditorPainter` / `text_cell_editor`. An open editor replaces exactly one cell through the same `data_row` call the display painter is reached by; the column's editor delegate is resolved once per painted row, never per cell.

`pinion-a11y` — `AccessState::read_only` (WAI-ARIA `aria-readonly`, accesskit `set_read_only`), absent from the tree until now, and `mark_grid_editability`, which marks the NON-editable windowed cells from the same `edit` role the editors open from. Also mirrored on the `scene/access` wire, where `mixed` had been missing since R1229 too.

`VirtualSelectExternal::on_cell_gesture` — the view-level hook a cell click drives beyond selection, offered BEFORE the selection transition so Qt's `SelectedClicked` ("already selected") is still answerable. `hello-grid-nav` becomes the editable Model/View grid at scale: a current CELL, three columns whose edit role differs three ways, and an editor delegate on the bounded one.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1544_cell_states_whether_it_edits.py` — 40 assertions over `hello-grid-nav`: the read-only column is `aria-readonly` on the wire while its editable neighbours stay silent; F2 / a printable key / a double-click each open an editor through their own Qt trigger; the editor replaces exactly one cell and its neighbours keep the display painter; the delegate's range hint is painted where the built-in editor paints none; a refused commit keeps the editor open holding the typed text, and correcting it in place commits; Escape leaves the model unchanged; Tab advances past the read-only column and Shift+Tab walks back.

Unit: 16 in `pinion-core::widgets::grid_edit` (trigger wire round-trip driven by the census, serde-as-names, seed selected whole, refusal keeps the buffer, advance skips / wraps / terminates on a fully read-only model), 2 in `pinion-a11y::virtual_grid` (only non-editable cells marked; absent cells skipped, no node invented), 7 in `hello-grid-nav` (editor replaces one cell, the delegate paints, the read-only column answers no role, refusal, committed value painted, a11y, Tab skip).

8 counterfactuals, one at a time, every restore md5-verified: the a11y pass claims every cell editable (demo A fails); a refused commit closes anyway, i.e. Qt's `void setModelData` (demo E); the cell never swaps in the editor (demo B); the editor delegate is never consulted (demo D); advance ignores editability (demo G); begin does not select the seed, so type-to-replace appends (demo B'); `read_only` never reaches the wire (demo A); the cell-gesture observer never fires (demo B'').

Gates: `cargo test` green on `pinion-core` / `pinion-a11y` / `pinion-widget-paint` / `pinion-rpc` / `hello-grid-nav` / `hello-virtual-table`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D pedantic` clean; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. carry_forward_bullets: Qt's `openPersistentEditor` (N simultaneously open editors) is not implemented. It is a property of the VIEW, not of the delegate this round closes, and it needs N independent text-edit states while `use_text_edit_state` is keyed by `&'static str`. Recorded as a remaining item of the DCC axis, not built on speculation about its shape.

The `EditRole` seam has ONE consumer. Six bindings still hand-roll a cell edit latch (`hello-data-grid`, `hello-property-grid`, `hello-inspector`, `hello-node-editor`, plus the two rename editors), and none of them uses the grid's cell path at all — migrating them is per-binding domain work, not the seam.

Round 1545.decision_summary: A category is an axis KIND: Categories / CategoryScale as the fourth AxisKind arm (Qt QBarCategoryAxis), the bar chart's private slot metric replaced by it, a numeric-x chart able to swap it in — with the band published and a window resolved from names before it can reach a chart, neither of which Qt's axis can do.
changes_bullets: `pinion-chart::scale` — `Categories` (Qt `QBarCategoryAxis::categories`, shared so a clone is a refcount bump), `CategoryScale`, `CategoryWindow`, `CategoryLookup`, and the fourth `AxisKind` / `ValueScale` arm. The kind is the first that is not a scalar, so `AxisKind` drops `Copy`: a categorical axis's labels are DATA, not derivable from a value the way a number, a magnitude or an instant is, and keeping `Copy` would have meant keeping the names outside the thing that decides how a tick is labelled.

`CategoryScale::band` — the pixel span a category occupies. Qt has no such accessor: a bar's rect is computed inside the private `QBarSeriesPrivate` painter, so a Qt application cannot ask where category 3 is drawn. That absence is exactly why `bar.rs` carried three copies of `left + i * slot` — bar box, label, click surface — under a doc calling itself "the ONE definition of where bar `i` sits".

`CategoryScale::visible` / `BarChart::visible_categories` — which slots a live window is showing. `QBarCategoryAxis` reports `count()` (all of them) and the min/max NAMES it was set to, never what is on screen; since R1534 that window moves under a wheel, so the question has a per-frame answer.

`Categories::window(from, to)` returns `Result<CategoryWindow, CategoryLookup>`, naming an unknown or ambiguous endpoint. Qt's `setRange(QString, QString)` returns `void`: a typo leaves the axis silently unwindowed and a duplicated name resolves to the first match with nothing said.

`pinion-chart::plot` — the category arms of `kind_extent` / `axis_domain` / `axis_scale` / `axis_ticks` / `axis_format`, so a categorical axis resolves, ticks and labels through the machinery the other three kinds already shared. Its extent is its list, not its data: `x_extent` measures nothing for it.

`BarChart` — its x IS this axis now. `BarGeom.x: CategoryScale` replaces the private slot metric, the three `left + i * slot` copies collapse to one `band` call, the label text comes from `TickFormat::Category`, the inspect hit-test is `CategoryScale::nearest`, and `BarChart::x_window` narrows bars, labels, click surfaces and hit-test together because all four derive from the axis.

`LineChart::x_category` / `y_category` and the `ScatterChart` twins — the swap the round exists for: a numeric-x chart takes the categorical axis exactly as it takes the log and time ones. A sample naming no slot has no pixel and is reported by `off_scale`.

Round 1546.decision_summary: A text run states its BACKGROUND: TextStyle::bg_color (Qt QTextCharFormat::setBackground) resolved into painted bands from the shaped layout through the same selection_rects the selection band uses, reaching the Vello rasteriser and the terminal cell from one declaration — with the painted extent and its WCAG contrast published by scene/text_backgrounds, neither of which Qt exposes.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core::style::TextStyle::bg_color: Option<Color>` + `with_bg_color` / `without_bg_color` (Qt `QTextCharFormat::setBackground`, CSS inline `background-color`, Flutter `TextStyle.background`). `None` is the UNSET brush, not a transparent one, so "does this run declare a background" is a type question rather than an alpha comparison. Run-level, so a syntax highlighter / diff view / search layer declares it exactly as it declares a colour.

`pinion-text::glyph_run::TextBackground` + `backgrounds()` — the band derivation. Cut by BYTE, not by parley run: a parley run splits on font fallback and bidi level, neither of which a background cares about, so one declared highlight can arrive as three runs and three abutting f32 rects is three chances of a hairline seam. The byte space is segmented at every declaration boundary, each segment takes its effective `bg_color`, adjacent segments agreeing are merged, and each survivor is measured by `selection_rects_for_range` — parley's own per-line range geometry, and the function the TextField's selection, find-match and preedit bands already call. A highlight and a selection over the same bytes are therefore one function called twice, not two derivations that happen to match.

`pinion-core::scene::effective_style_at` — the "last run covering this byte, else the base" walk, lifted when the background became its THIRD copy (the TUI cell painter, R1540's underline-form resolution, and this). Last-match is not a preference: parley resolves overlaps last-push-wins, so a consumer resolving first-match would take a byte's decoration from one run and its ink from another.

Both backends from the one declaration. Vello fills the bands before the glyphs (Qt's own `QTextLayout::draw` orders it the same way and for the same reason); `pinion-tui` sets `cell.set_bg`, closing a section 2 #6 gap open since the section 5.41 grid arm — `TermCell` carried `fg` AND `bg` while a `Scene::Text` run could speak only the foreground, so one document was paintable with a highlight in a terminal and not as text. The section 5.37 self-hosted arm DECLINES a leaf declaring a background rather than dropping it silently.

`scene/text_backgrounds` — where each band was PAINTED (window-absolute, scroll offsets folded the way `rect_for_tag_absolute` folds them), plus the WCAG 2.x contrast of the run's own foreground against it. Both past Qt 6.11: the rect Qt fills for a format range is computed inside the private `QTextLayout::draw` and never stored, so a Qt application re-derives it from `cursorToX` — a second implementation free to disagree with the painter's; and Qt will paint any brush behind any pen and say nothing, while "no highlight in this application drops below 4.5:1" is here one call. `contrast` is withheld (null, with the reason) for a translucent background, because WCAG is defined on rendered colours and the backdrop is an arbitrary painted subtree.

The WCAG trio (`relative_luminance` / `contrast_ratio` / `readable_ink`) moved from `pinion-chart::color_scale` to `pinion-core::contrast` — the crate that owns `Color` — now that a consumer exists on each side of the dependency edge; `pinion-chart` re-exports, so its callers are unchanged. `background_builds` joins `run_builds` on `TextCacheStats` and `scene/text_cache_stats`: the two derivations are separately lazy, so one counter could not say which a caller is watching.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1546_run_background.py` — 43 assertions over `hello-richtext-background`: the declaration and the painted consequence are read from two different surfaces and cross-checked (the band is registered against the node's rect from `scene/snapshot`, and is a fraction of it rather than the box recoloured); the Toggle drives the contrast from 16:1 to 1.3:1 while the geometry does not move a pixel; the hole-punch is two bands with a real gap; text declaring nothing contributes none; `rpc/schema` describes the three new types and its key set is compared against the live response's.

Unit: 7 in `pinion-text` (one declaration is one band across a shaping boundary — with the split asserted to be real; a run with no background punches a hole; overlapping declarations agree with the SHAPER on the winner, checked as two independent observations; a wrapped declaration is one band per row; the band registers with the caret's line box; derived once and replayed; undeclared text has none), 10 in `pinion-rpc`, 2 in `pinion-tui` (the terminal cell, and the lift checked against the pre-lift body kept as an oracle), 1 in `pinion-runtime` (the section 5.37 decline, both arms), 5 in the example, 5 in `pinion-core::contrast`.

Live-pixel guard `r1546_a_declared_run_background_reaches_pixels` (ignored by default, CI `gpu-tests`): the fill is probed AT THE COORDINATES the wire publishes, the glyphs are asserted still legible on it (the band goes behind), the page past the range is bare, and the same text without the declaration reads page at that very pixel.

Counterfactuals, one at a time, md5-restored. Six discriminated: last-match to first-match (failed in two independent places), the adjacent-span merge removed, the TUI arm removed, the translucent withholding removed, the scroll fold removed, and the Vello fill removed. TWO passed and both were findings rather than noise: the section 5.37 decline was unasserted (a test was added, and it now fails without the guard), and the Vello fill was unasserted by all 614 runtime + 1044 rpc + shell tests, which is what the pixel guard above exists for.

A seventh counterfactual passed and is a genuine EQUIVALENCE, not a gap: skipping leaves that declare no background is cost-only — the published answer is identical either way, and only `background_builds` would differ. Following R1545, the reason is written at the code rather than pinned by an assertion an unrelated scene edit would break.

Round 1547.decision_summary: A header section is asked for its role. `GridModel` had four accessors, three addressing a cell and one addressing a section, and the section could answer exactly one question: what the column is called. Qt reaches both axes through one role enum and `QHeaderView::paintSection` consumes `Qt::DecorationRole` into `QStyleOptionHeader::icon`, so a Qt grid can put a key, type, filter or lock glyph in a column header; nothing here could mark a column at all. R1547 opens the section axis's role dimension with the role R1535 opened the cell axis with, answered with the same type and drawn by the same painter. Two things past Qt 6.11: the mark's meaning reaches assistive technology (Qt's `QAccessibleTableHeaderCell::text(Name)` answers from `DisplayRole` alone, so a Qt header whose distinguishing information IS its glyph announces only the column's name), and the `columnheader` is named by what is PAINTED — the a11y builders no longer receive labels at all, so no second source is left to disagree with the pixels, where Qt derives that name from the model on a path independent of `paintSection`. Reaching for the second found the reason it was reachable: the builders' hand-stamped name would have silently won over the derivation, which is the same write-path/read-path split R1536 found on the cell axis.
changes_bullets: `GridModel::header_decoration` (Qt `headerData(section, Qt::Horizontal, Qt::DecorationRole)`), asked once per PAINTED section like `header` beside it; `no_header_decoration` is the section-axis peer of `no_decoration`

`CellDecoration` renamed `Decoration`: a role is not axis-specific (Qt reaches both axes through one role and one `QVariant`), and two types would be two contracts that must agree about what a mark is
`HeaderSection` binds a section's two role answers where they are asked, so a header band cannot paint a section with its neighbour's mark; `header_texts` becomes `header_sections`

`decoration_node` lifts the arm `match` out of both paint sites (obligation 3b) — `Decoration::meaning`'s own doc records that a read-site match is how an arm gets forgotten, and R1547 was about to write a second one
`GridTag::header_decoration` -> `"{tag}_hdeco{col}"`, its own prefix because `"{tag}_deco0_{col}"` is a real CELL address and the namespace must stay unique
`TableData::header_decoration` gives the eager `view_table` the same role, so the tree does not hold two header contracts that disagree about whether it exists
a marked header's `meaning` joins the `columnheader`'s accessible name ahead of the label (R1536's rule on the section axis); empty stays the decorative answer

the a11y `columnheader` is named from the PAINT: `GridColumns` holds counts not labels, and all six `windowed_grid_nodes*` builders take a column count — closing R1536's stated gap that five of six took every label

`hello-virtual-table` answers the meaningful ("Primary key" on `Index`) and decorative (a legend swatch on `Status`) arms; `hello-virtual-columns` answers it over 200 columns and publishes the per-frame ask count at `vcol_hdstatus`

the widget-paint test helper `cell_access_name` now CALLS `enrich_names_from_scene` instead of restating its precedence — the R1536 mirror answered `None` for a header cell because it looked only at direct children
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1547_section_states_its_role.py` — 46 assertions over two apps: the mark painted at its own address on the answered sections and only those, a section mark is not a cell mark, meaningful announced / decorative silent, every `columnheader` named and named by the painted label, the role asked once per painted section over 200 columns, and all of it surviving a horizontal scroll

Round 1547.publishable_decision_summary: A header section is asked for its role. `GridModel` had four accessors, three addressing a cell and one addressing a section, and the section could answer exactly one question: what the column is called. Qt reaches both axes through one role enum and `QHeaderView::paintSection` consumes `Qt::DecorationRole` into `QStyleOptionHeader::icon`, so a Qt grid can put a key, type, filter or lock glyph in a column header; nothing here could mark a column at all. R1547 opens the section axis's role dimension with the role R1535 opened the cell axis with, answered with the same type and drawn by the same painter. Two things past Qt 6.11: the mark's meaning reaches assistive technology (Qt's `QAccessibleTableHeaderCell::text(Name)` answers from `DisplayRole` alone, so a Qt header whose distinguishing information IS its glyph announces only the column's name), and the `columnheader` is named by what is PAINTED — the a11y builders no longer receive labels at all, so no second source is left to disagree with the pixels, where Qt derives that name from the model on a path independent of `paintSection`. Reaching for the second found the reason it was reachable: the builders' hand-stamped name would have silently won over the derivation, which is the same write-path/read-path split R1536 found on the cell axis.
