Round 1548.decision_summary: A row is asked for its header. Qt spells both section axes with one virtual — headerData(section, orientation, role) — and a QTableView shows the vertical one by default; pinion had no vertical axis at all. A column could be asked what it was called and what mark it carried; a ROW could be asked nothing — no row numbers, no pin, no lock, no breakpoint gutter, the whole left-hand band a professional table, editor or profiler has. R1548 adds it as a TYPE rather than a second pair of accessors: HeaderAxis<L, D> holds the two roles a section answers, GridModel::columns and GridModel::rows are both one, so the two axes answer the same role set by construction and one lifted painter draws either. Two things past Qt 6.11, both read over the wire: an unanswered axis is a DECLARATION and not a blank strip (Qt's orientation is a runtime argument, so the commonest QAbstractTableModel bug there — handle Qt::Horizontal, fall through returning QVariant() — paints sections that still occupy their width and is reported by nothing; here no_row_header() is written down, the band is not painted, the model is asked ZERO times a frame, and painted-iff-answered is structural because there is no second show-the-header flag to disagree with the first), and the mark's MEANING reaches assistive technology (QAccessibleTableHeaderCell::text(Name) answers from Qt::DisplayRole on BOTH orientations, so a Qt row header whose distinguishing information is its glyph announces only the row's number). The rowheader's name is derived from the painted band, so this axis is born with no second source — R1547.1 had to migrate hand-stamped names on the other axis; this one never had them.
changes_bullets: HeaderAxis<L, D> makes a section axis a TYPE: Qt's orientation promoted from a runtime argument to the field the axis is stored in, so a role added to sections is added to both axes or to neither
GridModel::rows (Qt headerData(section, Qt::Vertical, ...)) asked once per PAINTED row with the row's DATA index, so a mark and a number travel with their row across a sort

no_row_header() is the written statement that a grid has no vertical axis; painted-iff-answered is structural — the band's width is a TableStyle dimension, not a second presence flag that could contradict the model

GridTag::row_header / row_header_decoration / header_corner, each with its own prefix so no address can be read as another axis's; row is a usize because the string id space is the tree-grid's and a QTreeView has no vertical header
section_content lifts the mark-and-label composition out of header_cell (obligation 3b, at the second consumer) so both axes' bands share one painter, one gap constant and one accessible-name rule
SectionRoles::ask states one-address-every-role once; ask_sections is its contiguous-span form, and the row band uses the same function over the windowed rows in sort order
TableData::row_headers gives the EAGER view_table the same axis through the same type, so the tree does not hold two contracts — the R1547.1 lesson, applied inside the round that opens the axis

attach_row_headers is a composing PASS over built nodes (the R1544 mark_grid_editability shape), so the axis reaches every grid topology — identity, sorted, frozen, column-windowed, single- and multi-select — instead of the one builder a flag would have grown

consumers: hello-virtual-table (both roles + a pinned mark no cell states), hello-virtual-columns (per-frame ask count at vcol_rhstatus), hello-grid-sort (the number is the row's identity under a permutation), hello-table (the eager surface, icon arm)

Round 1549.decision_summary: A held press repeats — the press-and-hold auto-repeat Qt has had since Qt 1 (`QAbstractButton::setAutoRepeat`, `QAbstractSpinBox` arrows on by default) and pinion had nowhere: censused, the single `auto_repeat` hit in the tree was keyboard-repeat SUPPRESSION (R1071), so holding a spin arrow stepped exactly once however long it was held. A widget DECLARES a cadence and the router supplies the clock; a fire re-dispatches the widget's own PointerUp+PointerDown arc, so a repeat is a click by the same derivation and no widget needed a new SCXML transition to become repeatable. Past Qt 6.11 in three ways, all read over the wire: (1) the hold is DRIVABLE AS DATA — Qt's is a QBasicTimer on the event loop, so a test sleeps and no client can express "hold this for 900 ms"; here it rides the same clock `scene/tick` drives, and the demo asserts exact fire counts with no tolerance; (2) the RUN IS PUBLISHED — `scene/auto_repeat` answers target, repeating, cadence, fires so far and seconds to the next, where Qt's only public fact is a static per-widget property and the run itself lives in a private timer observable only through its side effects; the census is PREDICTIVE, and the demo ticks exactly `next_fire_in_secs` then asserts the repeat landed; (3) a HELD ARROW AT ITS BOUND STOPS — `QAbstractSpinBox` keeps its 10 Hz timer running against a value pinned at `maximum()` for as long as the user holds, here the widget answers None, which also releases the frame loop. And the structural claim: armed-ness is re-ASKED of the widget every frame rather than stored, and the run lives IN the R876 press record, created and destroyed by the two statements that already opened and closed a press — so Qt's runaway-timer bug class (a missed release / hide / disable leaving the timer firing) has nowhere to live.
changes_bullets: `AutoRepeat` (pinion-core §5.35): delay + interval + a closed-form accel ramp with a floor; Qt AUTO_REPEAT_DELAY/INTERVAL as the defaults, `QAbstractSpinBox::setAccelerated` as a curve rather than a bool. Every constructor clamps so no declaration can produce a zero interval, which is what bounds the router's catch-up loop

`External::auto_repeat() -> Option<AutoRepeat>` (§5.15/§5.38): the widget is ASKED every frame, so armed-ness is read off its own statechart and never stored. Consumers: `ButtonExternal` (opt-in, `QPushButton` default off), `SpinButtonExternal` and `PaginationExternal` (on by default, as Qt's spin arrows are)

`InputRouter::tick_auto_repeat` (§5.35): the run lives IN the R876 press record (`DragLatch` widened to `PressRecord`), created by `pointer_down` and removed by `pointer_up`, so a repeat outliving its press is unrepresentable. A fire re-dispatches the widget's own `PointerUp`+`PointerDown` arc, so a repeat IS a click by the same derivation

Clock: the paint's wall-clock delta (frozen while `set_fps 0`) and `scene/tick`'s injected delta drive ONE driver through the same substep splitter. The router's armed answer feeds the shell's redraw gate — the `Tickable::is_at_rest` peer for a gesture outside the animation registry
`scene/auto_repeat` (§5.12/§5.7): every in-flight press as data — target, repeating, declared cadence, fires so far, seconds to the next. Total (no `*Unavailable`): "nothing held" is `{"holds": []}`
verification_bullets: pinion-core 2945 unit tests green, incl. 8 `AutoRepeat` cadence tests (Qt-constant pin, ramp-to-floor, no-zero-interval over 6 malformed declarations, deceleration refused, published-vs-stepped schedule agreement) and 14 widget declaration tests across button/spin/pagination

pinion-runtime 627 green, incl. 13 router tests driven end-to-end through a REAL `ButtonExternal`/`SpinButtonExternal` (nothing stubbed): exact delay-then-interval cadence, undeclared button never repeats over 10s held, release ends it with no un-arm path, one large tick == 63 small frames, frozen and NaN deltas fire nothing yet still report armed, a quiet answer rewinds the ramp, catch-up stops at the bound it reaches mid-tick

A widget DECLARES a cadence and the router supplies the clock; a fire re-dispatches the widget's own PointerUp+PointerDown arc, so a repeat is a click by the same derivation and no widget needed a new SCXML transition to become repeatable. Past Qt 6.11 in three ways, all read over the wire: (1) the hold is DRIVABLE AS DATA — Qt's is a QBasicTimer on the event loop, so a test sleeps and no client can express "hold this for 900 ms"; here it rides the same clock `scene/tick` drives, and the demo asserts exact fire counts with no tolerance; (2) the RUN IS PUBLISHED — `scene/auto_repeat` answers target, repeating, cadence, fires so far and seconds to the next, where Qt's only public fact is a static per-widget property and the run itself lives in a private timer observable only through its side effects; the census is PREDICTIVE, and the demo ticks exactly `next_fire_in_secs` then asserts the repeat landed; (3) a HELD ARROW AT ITS BOUND STOPS — `QAbstractSpinBox` keeps its 10 Hz timer running against a value pinned at `maximum()` for as long as the user holds, here the widget answers None, which also releases the frame loop. Round 1549.2.decision_summary: The held press repeats in a terminal too — §2 #6 closed by the round's own closing audit. R1549 landed press-and-hold auto-repeat on the Vello path only: the advance lived in `compute_paint_scene_internal` and the census in the pinion-shell dispatch context, so a widget that repeated in a window was inert in a terminal, and `scene/auto_repeat` there answered an empty list however many presses were in flight. §2 #6 (one scene, two render dispatch paths) is a HARD invariant, and this is the exact shape R1460 recorded when `scene/frame_timings` existed on the wire while every TUI binding replied `Unavailable` forever — a mirror that was MISSING, not declined. Nothing about the backend justified it: a terminal reports mouse press and release edges (SGR mouse mode) just as a window does, so a hold is as expressible there. The deeper finding is about the harness rather than the code: this could not have been caught by any existing test, because every test fixture's button declared NO cadence, so a backend that never ticks a hold and one that ticks it correctly are observationally identical. A capability landed as an opt-in declaration is invisible to a fixture set in which nothing opts in — so the fixture is part of the seam, and `RepeatingButtonFixture` is now the negative-control's positive twin.

Round 1549.3.decision_summary: The GUI's live paint-clock arm had no coverage, and the round's own demo is why. Measured: with that arm DELETED OUTRIGHT — the wall-clock advance inside `compute_paint_scene_internal`, the path a real mouse in a real window takes — the entire pinion-shell suite passed AND `r1549_held_press_repeats.py` passed all 58 assertions. The demo calls `scene/set_fps 0` to make its fire counts exact, and a paused window is precisely the case where that arm contributes zero; so the demo exercises only the injected `scene/tick` arm, by construction. This is [[r1506-guard-renders-production]] in a new dress: not a guard drawing a copy of its target, but a guard whose own precondition for being deterministic is the thing that steers it away from the production path. Determinism and coverage pulled in opposite directions and I noticed only the first. It is also the SECOND time in one round that a capability landed on one arm and the guard landed on another — R1549.2 was Vello-vs-TUI, this is injected-vs-live — which says the failure is not carelessness about backends but a habit of testing where testing is easy. The fix asserts on `held_secs`, the accumulator every armed frame advances before any threshold applies, so the guard runs the real paint with a real clock and still needs no sleep and no tolerance.

Round 1549.4.decision_summary: The same hole, a third time, on the mirror of what R1549.3 just fixed — and this time the fix is structural rather than another test. Asked whether the debt was registered, the audit ran the R1549.3 counterfactual against the TUI: deleting the run loop's `core.tick_auto_repeat(dt)` kept every pinion-tui test green, because R1549.2's guard called `tick_auto_repeat` DIRECTLY and so never exercised the wiring that calls it. Three instances in one round — Vello-vs-TUI (R1549.2), injected-vs-live (R1549.3), method-vs-wiring (here) — is not three oversights; it is one habit, testing at whatever seam is easiest to reach, and a fourth test written the same way would have the same blind spot. So the response is to remove the degree of freedom instead: `begin_frame` measures the frame's delta AND advances the held press, `measure_frame_dt` goes private, and `commit_paint` loses its `dt` parameter and opens the frame itself. The paint needs a delta; the only producer of one advances the hold. "Painted a frame without advancing its hold" is no longer a sequence the module can express — the same move R1548 made for the header axis and R1549 for the press record, now applied to the place my own guards kept failing to reach.

`commit_paint` takes `&mut ShellCoreTui` and opens the frame itself; its `dt` parameter is gone. "Painted a frame without advancing its hold" stopped being a sequence the module can express — the same fuse-two-statements move as R1548's header axis and R1549's press record

Round 1551.decision_summary: R1551 a paragraph states its own block format
changes_bullets: pinion-core: `style::BlockFormat` — the block (paragraph) format, Qt `QTextBlockFormat`: left/right indent, space above/below, heading level. Typed and exhaustive where Qt's is a `QVariant` property bag, and every length is CSS px where Qt mixes `indent()` (indent-width units) with `leftMargin()` (pixels) in one class

pinion-core: `style::TextIndent` — CSS `text-indent` with both keywords (`hanging`, `each-line`) Qt's bare `qreal textIndent` has no spelling for; joins `text_align` as a paragraph-level field of `TextStyle`, so every shaping caller reaches it through the `&TextStyle` it already passes

pinion-core: `TextNode::block` + `with_block`, the ONE lowering site — the format's four lengths become the node's `LayoutStyle::margin`, so the ordinary flex pass indents a paragraph with no document-specific layout code, on both backends. The declaration is kept beside the box it produced because a margin cannot be read back as a block format
pinion-core: `Scene::for_each_text_leaf` — the scroll-offset fold over text leaves, lifted at its second consumer (`scene/text_backgrounds` had spelled it, `scene/text_blocks` was about to)
pinion-core: `composite_tag::DocumentTag` — the document/paragraph paint-tag SSOT, in the `'_'` presentational family

pinion-text: `shape` calls parley `Layout::set_text_indent` before breaking, because the indent is a BREAKING input — an indented line has less room, so where it breaks depends on it. parley's `IndentOptions` carry the same two CSS keywords, so this is a rename and not a re-derivation
pinion-text: `line_boxes` + `TextLineBox` — parley's own per-line metrics, published so the shaped result is checkable

pinion-text-unicode: `wrap_paragraph_with_line_budget` + `LineContext` — the breaker asks for each line's budget instead of taking one for the paragraph, and reports the two flags CSS selects on (`is_block_start` / `is_scope_start`) because only the breaker knows which lines those are. `wrap_paragraph_with_measure` is now its constant-budget case

pinion-tui: `CellTextLayout::place` + `CellLine` + `GapPad` — the cell backend honours BOTH paragraph-level fields: `text-indent` (including a negative one, which widens the node clip so an outdent is drawn rather than erased) and `text-align`, which reached the terminal for the first time. Justify distributes leftover cells across inter-word gaps; `wrap` survives as the `TextStyle::new()` case of `place`

pinion-a11y: `AriaRole::Heading` + `attach_block_headings` — a declared heading level becomes a WAI-ARIA `heading` with `aria-level`, named by the PAINTED text, riding the `build_access_tree` chokepoint so it reaches every binding

pinion-rpc: `scene/text_blocks` — each paragraph's declaration BESIDE where its shaped lines landed, plus `block` on `scene/snapshot`'s text nodes and `text_indent` in its style object; four new wire-census types

pinion-widget-paint: `document::{TextBlock, view_document}` — a document is a column of block nodes, so it composes with the rest of the tree; `QTextDocumentLayout` is a private second layout engine that cannot
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1551_block_format.py` — 45 assertion sites over a real binding: the declared format as scene data, the shaped line boxes beside it, the first-line indent landing at the declared px with no other line moving, the hanging mirror from the same amount, the quote's indents cross-checked against `scene/snapshot`'s independent rect, a negative control (an ordinary label is not a paragraph), the heading outline over `scene/access`, and the R1539 census covering the new types

Round 1553.decision_summary: R1553 a datum can be a distribution
changes_bullets: pinion-chart: `distribution` — `Distribution`, the crate's first datum that is NOT a point. Every value it could plot resolved to one position; this one occupies a span of the value axis and carries interior landmarks, so ONE datum emits a box, a median, two whiskers, two caps and a mark per outlier

pinion-chart: `QuantileMethod` — Tukey's hinges, Hyndman & Fan type 7, type 6. They disagree at small n, so which one built a box is part of what the box MEANS; it lives in `DistributionSource::Samples` beside the count and the fence. Qt's QBoxSet is five doubles and QtCharts computes none of them, shipping a findMedian() helper in its own EXAMPLE

pinion-chart: Tukey's k*IQR fence limits each whisker and every sample beyond it becomes its own addressable mark. QBoxSet has five slots and no per-outlier geometry, so a Qt box plot cannot draw one at any setting, and that fence is the defining half of the form

pinion-chart: `Distribution::notch` — McGill, Tukey and Larsen 1978, median +- 1.58*IQR/sqrt(n). It answers None for a pre-computed summary because the statistic is a function of a sample count a summary never carried, so such a box keeps its plain rectangle in the same chart

pinion-chart: `from_summary` is Qt's own contract with the ordering CHECKED, naming the first landmark that goes backwards. QBoxSet::setValue accepts an upper quartile below the lower one and paints an inverted box in silence

pinion-chart: `boxplot` — `BoxPlotChart` over R1545's category axis and a full `ValueScale`, so `y_log` is R1528's axis rather than a second one. A log value axis is legitimate here where the bar chart is denied it: a box encodes five POSITIONS, not a length from zero
pinion-chart: `BoxPlotChart::off_scale` — a landmark the axis cannot place draws nothing and is REPORTED by kind, R1528's stance applied to a datum with extent rather than to a point
pinion-chart: `draw::polygon_node` — the closed-path primitive taking both PathStyle arms, so a box is ONE node kind whether or not it grew a waist
pinion-chart: `scene_probe` — obligation-3b lift. Eight copies of the test `find` walker in three spellings and three of `tags`, all semantically identical; this round wrote the eighth and the third
examples/hello-boxplot: the forcing consumer — five endpoints' RAW latencies, a quantile-method radio group, a notch toggle and a log-axis toggle
verification_bullets: tools/demos/r1553_distribution_datum.py — 57 assertion sites over a real binding: the mark cardinalities, the parts checked against EACH OTHER, the definition deciding an outlier, the whisker stopping at the fence, the notch read as both a command count and a narrowed median, and the log axis dropping two marks and reporting them

Ten counterfactuals, one at a time, each FAILING on an assertion: fence inert / one quantile definition / notch without n / box never notches / domain ignores outliers / off_scale silent / inverted summary accepted / median not inset / binding pins the method / caption drops the report

The counterfactual driver was itself wrong twice, both recorded lessons this round re-walked: a piped gate masked cargo's exit code so all ten first read as DEAD, and a uniqueness assertion placed outside the try block left one patch in the tree
Two of the ten first failed to COMPILE, which proves nothing; the driver now refuses a counterfactual whose gate did not fail on an assertion
cargo test green on pinion-chart (328) and hello-boxplot (8); clippy pedantic clean on both; cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items clean
carry_forward_bullets: Four of the five series types R1519 named remain: polar, candlestick, spline, 3D-surface. Candlestick is the cheapest now, being the same interval geometry over open/high/low/close, and is deliberately left as the SECOND consumer that would decide whether the interval mark lifts
The pre-computed `from_summary` arm has no forcing consumer: hello-boxplot derives all five of its distributions, so Qt's own contract is exercised by unit tests only

A box has no per-mark a11y. The scrub readout names the whole summary and its provenance, which is past Qt since QtCharts implements no accessibility interface at all, but an individual outlier is painted geometry with no accessible relationship
The notch is deliberately NOT clamped to the box: a small sample with a wide IQR yields a bowtie, which is what R draws and warns about. Folding it in would hide the case a reader most needs to see

Round 1554.decision_summary: R1554 a container states that its subtree is inert
changes_bullets: pinion-core: `LayoutStyle::disabled` — the first INHERITED interaction declaration on the layout sidecar. Its four peers (pointer_transparent R705, focusable R1020, drop_target R1080, cursor R1196) each describe the node carrying them and nothing else; Qt's QWidget::setEnabled is the one that reaches a whole subtree, which is why a checkable QGroupBox was inexpressible and no group container existed in this tree at all

pinion-core: `scene_disabled::resolve_disabled` — the cascade. It writes the derived half in BOTH directions on every produced paint scene, so nothing survives a frame to go stale. Qt's QWidgetPrivate::setEnabled_helper writes WA_Disabled into every descendant and must walk them back, keeping N copies of one fact in step by procedure

pinion-core: the ink fades by the M3 DISABLED token toward the nearest opaque backdrop — the same token and direction a self-disabled widget's state layer uses, which is why the token moved DOWN from pinion-widget-paint this round rather than being restated. Resolving to concrete channels rather than reducing alpha is what carries the fade into the terminal, where a TermCell has no alpha at all

pinion-core: the two descending walks read the DECLARATION at every level, so they are correct on a scene the cascade has not run over. collect_focusable_tags does not descend; hit_test treats the region as OPAQUE rather than transparent — the press stops there and never falls through to a peer painted beneath, which is Qt's propagate-to-parent

pinion-runtime: the cascade rides `settle_to_fixed_point`, the one loop all five paint-scene producers in both backends already pass through. Its generic scene parameter became concrete Scene to do it; a producer cannot forget the cascade because there is nowhere left to forget it

pinion-a11y: `stamp_inherited_disabled` at the R1518 chokepoint, WIDENING rather than replacing. Disabledness has two independent sources — the scene's regions and the widget's own state enum — so neither can deny the other, which is also Qt's WA_ForceDisabled rule

pinion-rpc: `scene/disabled` publishes the CAUSE. Qt's isEnabled() is a bool, isEnabledTo() needs the caller to have already guessed the ancestor, WA_ForceDisabled names nobody, and no Qt call enumerates a window's disabled set at all

pinion-rpc: focus/set answers `tag_disabled` handing back the region to act on, where QWidget::setFocus() on a disabled widget returns void and does nothing — the caller cannot tell a refusal from a success, let alone learn why

pinion-widget-paint: `view_group_box` — Qt QGroupBox with title, alignment, flat and the checkable gate. Its title sits ABOVE the frame rather than interrupting it: an overlapping title welds paint z-order to Tab order and they disagree, which the binding's own test caught
examples/hello-group-box: the forcing consumer — a gate checkbox and two members, with no disabled bookkeeping, no Tab-order list and no aria-disabled plumbing anywhere in it

examples/settings-panel FIX: its six notification checkboxes were seeded on slot "value", which CheckboxExternal rejects (a checkbox names its bool "checked"; ToggleExternal names its "value"). None had ever hydrated from its persisted signal, and `let _ =` on the Result kept that silent
verification_bullets: tools/demos/r1554_container_states_its_subtree.py — 49 assertion sites over a real binding: the Tab order shrinking with no list in the binding, the named refusal, the press landing on the region, aria-disabled on members that never claimed it, the exact faded ink re-derived from the M3 spec inside the demo itself, and the whole tree returning byte-for-byte when the gate is restored

Sixteen counterfactuals, one at a time, each FAILING on an assertion: focus walk / hit_test / cascade never clears / no transition gate / transparent ink materialised / backdrop frozen / outermost declarer / style runs unfaded / a11y stamp replaces / a11y stamp absent / settle loop not cascading / re-passed frame not cascaded / terminal never sees the fade / group gates itself / title after the frame / generic refusal
One counterfactual first read DEAD because it did not compile, which proves nothing; the driver requires an assertion failure, and its byte-restore revert is asserted rather than a git checkout

Four node kinds carry content the fade cannot reach — Image, External, ImmediateModeNode, TextGrid. Qt cannot grey a QOpenGLWidget either, so it is PUBLISHED as each row's ink rather than left to be discovered from a screenshot

pinion-core: the two descending walks read the DECLARATION at every level, so they are correct on a scene the cascade has not run over. collect_focusable_tags does not descend; hit_test treats the region as OPAQUE rather than transparent — the press stops there and never falls through to a peer painted beneath, which is Qt's propagate-to-parent

pinion-runtime: the cascade rides `settle_to_fixed_point`, the one loop all five paint-scene producers in both backends already pass through. Its generic scene parameter became concrete Scene to do it; a producer cannot forget the cascade because there is nowhere left to forget it

pinion-a11y: `stamp_inherited_disabled` at the R1518 chokepoint, WIDENING rather than replacing. Disabledness has two independent sources — the scene's regions and the widget's own state enum — so neither can deny the other, which is also Qt's WA_ForceDisabled rule

pinion-rpc: `scene/disabled` publishes the CAUSE. Qt's isEnabled() is a bool, isEnabledTo() needs the caller to have already guessed the ancestor, WA_ForceDisabled names nobody, and no Qt call enumerates a window's disabled set at all

pinion-rpc: focus/set answers `tag_disabled` handing back the region to act on, where QWidget::setFocus() on a disabled widget returns void and does nothing — the caller cannot tell a refusal from a success, let alone learn why

pinion-widget-paint: `view_group_box` — Qt QGroupBox with title, alignment, flat and the checkable gate. Its title sits ABOVE the frame rather than interrupting it: an overlapping title welds paint z-order to Tab order and they disagree, which the binding's own test caught
examples/hello-group-box: the forcing consumer — a gate checkbox and two members, with no disabled bookkeeping, no Tab-order list and no aria-disabled plumbing anywhere in it

examples/settings-panel FIX: its six notification checkboxes were seeded on slot "value", which CheckboxExternal rejects (a checkbox names its bool "checked"; ToggleExternal names its "value"). None had ever hydrated from its persisted signal, and `let _ =` on the Result kept that silent
publishable_verification_bullets: tools/demos/r1554_container_states_its_subtree.py — 49 assertion sites over a real binding: the Tab order shrinking with no list in the binding, the named refusal, the press landing on the region, aria-disabled on members that never claimed it, the exact faded ink re-derived from the M3 spec inside the demo itself, and the whole tree returning byte-for-byte when the gate is restored

Sixteen counterfactuals, one at a time, each FAILING on an assertion: focus walk / hit_test / cascade never clears / no transition gate / transparent ink materialised / backdrop frozen / outermost declarer / style runs unfaded / a11y stamp replaces / a11y stamp absent / settle loop not cascading / re-passed frame not cascaded / terminal never sees the fade / group gates itself / title after the frame / generic refusal
One counterfactual first read DEAD because it did not compile, which proves nothing; the driver requires an assertion failure, and its byte-restore revert is asserted rather than a git checkout

cargo test green on pinion-core, pinion-runtime, pinion-a11y, pinion-widget-paint, pinion-rpc, pinion-tui, pinion-shell, hello-group-box and settings-panel; clippy pedantic clean on all nine; cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items clean; the three settings-panel demos still pass with the seeding fix
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: The cascade has ONE consumer. Every other catalog widget expresses disabledness only through its own state enum, so a form cannot gate a section without a group box

Four node kinds carry content the fade cannot reach — Image, External, ImmediateModeNode, TextGrid. Qt cannot grey a QOpenGLWidget either, so it is PUBLISHED as each row's ink rather than left to be discovered from a screenshot

LayoutStyle now carries five bools and the struct_excessive_bools lint is allowed with a stated reason. The encodings that would satisfy it need a fifth enum variant for "declared, cascade has not run" whose distinction a reader must carry for no gain
The five remaining absent widget kinds this axis names — QDial, QStackedWidget/QWizard, QKeySequenceEdit, QFontComboBox, QMessageBox/QInputDialog — each appear in this tree only inside a doc comment

Round 1555.decision_summary: A cell editor is chosen by its datum's kind — Qt QItemEditorFactory, the half of Qt's editing decomposition the tree did not have. R1532 and R1544 built the per-column override (setItemDelegateForColumn); the registry from a value's TYPE to an editor did not exist, so one inline text field was the built-in for all six CellKinds — and for Bool and Choice that field refuses every keystroke and parses to nothing, so the seam opened an editor that could not be typed into and whose commit could never produce a value. CellKind::editor_form is the registry and EditorForm its answer, a pure function where createEditor instantiates a QWidget; five forms ship, scene/cell_editors publishes the whole mapping (Qt's creatorMap is private and cannot be enumerated), and the a11y role is derived from the form rather than from whichever widget a factory happened to construct. Reaching for it forced the model half: CellEdit now carries the datum, because a Choice's options are part of its value's identity. Every commit outcome is named — malformed apart from refused — where Qt's commitData discards setData's verdict.

selector / swatch) + `CellKind::ALL` + `CellKind::editor_form` — Qt
`QItemEditorFactory::createEditor(QMetaType::Type, parent)` as a pure
function, exhaustive over the six kinds. `CellKind::is_text_editable` is
now DERIVED from the form (it had been a second copy of the same

for the form that has it; `select` bounds-checks against the datum's own
option list.

`pinion-rpc`: `scene/cell_editors` publishes the factory census (kind,
form, buffer_is_text, inline_text, accepts_keystrokes, role) + its
`WIRE_TYPES` entries and dispatch arm.

with R1544's stated blocker CORRECTED: `Owner::cache` has taken
`impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>` since R685.C exactly so runtime ids
allocate without `Box::leak`, so a runtime-keyed text-edit state was
always possible. Only `use_text_edit_state`'s own signature is

declaration read from the widget's own state, and a step arrow is a
sub-region of one External covering every cell — so repeating it needs a

which duplicates the router press record R1549 put the run inside on
purpose. The same shape R1549 recorded for scrollbar arrows.

reading stands: each is per-binding domain work, not seam work.

Round 1556.decision_summary: R1556 §5.16 — the frame states the work it DREW, not just the nodes it walked. R1538 gave this axis its node census and stated the scale claim with it, but a count prices every node at one: a Container is one node and a Text leaf holding four thousand glyphs is one node, so two frames can report a byte-identical census and hand the GPU two orders of magnitude of different work — the guard R1538 built to bound per-frame work could not see the difference it existed for. DrawWork counts what was drawn in the units a 2D vector renderer is charged in (draw commands, paths, path segments, clip layers, glyph runs, glyphs), read off the scene that was SUBMITTED, so a subtree the fragment cache replayed counts exactly like one encoded this frame and no drawn work can escape the count. Qt's floor is QQuick3DRenderStats (drawCallCount / drawVertexCount / renderPassCount); four things past it: it covers the 2D pipeline, where a QWidget or a Qt Quick 2D scene has no draw-work census of any kind and Qt Quick's batch counts exist only as QSG_RENDERER_DEBUG stderr text behind an env var; the counts are the encoded streams' own lengths rather than a renderer's separate tally, so the number cannot disagree with the work; text is in it, and no Qt surface publishes a per-frame glyph count anywhere; and it BOUNDS a claim rather than decorating a HUD — hello-scene-scale asserts five of six units flat across a 10,000x model with an eager negative control, while the sixth moves by exactly the digits the header displays. path_segments and glyphs are disjoint, because vello resolves glyph outlines to paths downstream of the encoding, so a frame's vector cost and its text cost are readable apart instead of summed.
changes_bullets: `pinion-runtime` `frame_timing`: new `DrawWork` (draws / paths /
path_segments / layers / glyph_runs / glyphs) + `DrawWork::max_of`;
`FrameTiming::draw` with `with_draw_census`; `FrameTimingsSnapshot::max_draw`
folded per field (max, not mean — the guarded property is an upper bound).
`pinion-runtime` `paint_adapter`: `draw_work_of(&vello::Scene)` reads the
census off `Scene::encoding()`. `layers` is derived exactly as
`(n_clips + n_open_clips) / CLIP_ENTRIES_PER_LAYER`, the one modelled
quantity, pinned by `r1556_a_layer_costs_two_clip_entries` against vello
itself (R1550's model-drift class made loud instead of silent).
`pinion-shell` `app`: the census is taken off `render_target` — the exact
scene submitted to the renderer — and rides `FrameClose` into the sample.
`pinion-rpc`: `FrameTimingsDraw` under `last.draw` and `window.max_draw`,
projected by destructuring so a new `DrawWork` field cannot be silently
dropped; registered in the R1539 `rpc/schema` census.
`pinion-tui`: no draw census, asserted rather than implied — a cell grid has
no paths, segments, layers or glyphs, and a cell is a different quantity.
`hello-scene-scale`: second size axis `label_chars` (`LABEL_LADDER`
24 -> 1,536, `MAX_LABEL_CHARS` refused not clamped) + a third header region,
so the harness can hold every node count fixed while the drawn work moves.

carry_forward_bullets: Present latency is still unmeasured: the GPU span covers rasterize + blit,
and what happens after `present()` needs a presentation-timestamp extension
wgpu does not expose. External, unchanged from R1537.
A count still has no cost shipped with it, deliberately: what a glyph or a
segment costs moves with the GPU, the driver and the resolution, so
`gpu_us / path_segments` is a measurement the reading host makes.
The census is per FRAME, not per subtree. "Which subtree is expensive" needs
the encoder sampled around each node and self-cost separated from children's
— a flame graph, and the axis's next named slice rather than a gap this
round papers over.
Images are counted only inside `draws`, not broken out: `vello_encoding`'s
`Patch` is not re-exported through `vello`, so matching `Patch::Image` would
need a second version-pinned dependency beside `vello` itself.
R1550's two modelled arenas (`hash_table_bytes` / `lru_table_bytes`) are
still unpinned. This round pins its OWN model against vello and shows the
shape the fix takes; applying it to hashbrown and lru is that carry's round.

Round 1557.decision_summary: R1557 §5.16 §5.18 — the frame states WHICH SUBTREE drew it. R1556 gave this axis the frame's draw census, and it is one number per frame: it says how much and never where, so two frames each costing four thousand glyphs somewhere different read identically while wanting opposite fixes. scene/draw_profile is the other half and the shape of every profiler's central artifact — a tree mirroring the painted scene, each node carrying an inclusive cost (itself and its subtree) and an exclusive one (itself alone). The attribution is a DIFFERENCE of censuses of the encoded scene, one before a subtree is walked and one after, so a subtree the fragment cache replayed lands in it exactly as a freshly-encoded one does and nothing a node draws escapes its own row; own is then total minus the children's totals, arithmetic rather than a second measurement. Qt's floor is QSG_RENDERER_DEBUG=render, an env var that dumps scene-graph batches to stderr with raw QSGGeometryNode pointers, and on the widget stack there is no per-item draw accounting at all. Four things past it: it is queryable rather than printed; a node's identity is the address scene/locate produces and Scene::lookup_path_ref consumes, so which subtree is expensive and act on that subtree are one string; it is deterministic rather than sampled, so the same scene profiles identically on every host and a CI guard can assert on it; and text is attributed, which no Qt surface reports per item. The profile re-encodes into a COLD fragment cache, which makes the root's total equal to frame_timings' last.draw a CHECK rather than an assumption — the first out-of-crate test of the cache's own replay invariant.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core` `Scene::path_segment_at` — the tag-or-index path segment
rule, lifted from three byte-identical copies (hit_test x2,
collect_intersections) when the profiler became the fourth site.
`pinion-runtime` `draw_profile` (new): `DrawProfileNode` (segment / kind /

`pinion-runtime` `frame_timing`: `DrawWork::since` (exact for `layers`
because the derived numerator is always even) and `DrawWork::plus`.
`pinion-runtime` `paint_adapter`: the six walk-invariant parameters bundle
into `PaintSession` (11 args -> 7, `too_many_arguments` allow dropped),
`to_vello_cached_inner` becomes the profiler bracket and delegates every
arm to a new `encode_node`, so enter/leave pairing is structural. New
public entry `to_vello_cached_profiled`; unprofiled paints pay one
`Option` test per node.
`pinion-shell`: `ShellCore::draw_profile_for_window` re-encodes the
retained paint scene into a scratch `FragmentCache` (cold, so every node
is decomposed) with the live shape and image caches; `AppShell` gates it
on the method, as `arena_footprints` is gated.
`pinion-rpc` `draw_profile` (new): `scene/draw_profile` with `depth`,
`heaviest_by` and `limit`; `Unit` is the six-field census; `locate`'s
`format_path` lifted to `pub(crate)` so one formatter renders every
address. Registered in `methods` and the R1539 `rpc/schema` census.

painted scene, and there is no way to ask for one subtree's profile
directly. `depth` prunes the reply, not the measurement.
A profile row's address has no general reader. `scene/query` and
`scene/invoke` resolve the same vocabulary but only to reach an
`External`; `scene/snapshot` takes a window selector with no scene tail;
`scene/layout` addresses its own nodes by bare index and its `path` filter
is an accepted-and-ignored R47.7.x carry that predates this round.
Whether a subtree was REPLAYED or re-encoded is not published per node.
The scratch cache makes every node a miss by construction, so the encode
axis stays where it is: `encode_nodes` and `scene/cache_stats`, per frame.
`DrawProfileNode::own_sum` has no in-tree production consumer — it is the
balance identity an in-process consumer verifies, and the wire's own check
sums the rows in the demo instead.
`scene/locate` answers `OutOfBounds` for every point in this binding
(pre-existing; the hit-test root has no area), so the cross-surface
address check goes through `scene/query` rather than through the method
that PRODUCES these paths.

Round 1560.decision_summary: R1560 §5.36 §5.40 §5.12 §5.21 — a cell is addressed by its place in the flow. Everything else a table has can be written by hand: a border is a stroke, a padding is an inset, a column width is a length. The ADDRESS cannot, because it is not a property of the cell — it is where the cell lands once every earlier cell's spans have taken their slots, so inserting one cell re-addresses every cell after it and a rowspan reaches into a row nobody has written yet. R1559 named QTextTable first among what was left of the document model, and this is it: a CellSpec declares MEMBERSHIP and REACH and never an address, place_cells derives the allocation by HTML's own slot rule, and view_document lowers each address onto a real CSS Grid — the layout kind pinion did not have, added here with its forcing consumer because a column of flex rows measures each row alone and cannot express a rowspan at all. Six things past Qt 6.11, all read over the wire. (1) The address is DERIVED, not maintained: Qt's insertRows/insertColumns make the caller own the rectangular grid and mergeCells the merges, so the geometry has a second copy to disagree with. (2) A span that does not fit is CLAMPED AND NAMED: mergeCells returns void and silently does nothing on a rectangle that is not a merge candidate, so afterwards the ask and the result are indistinguishable; here declared_column_span sits beside column_span with clamped naming the difference — and the clamp is to the FREE RUN, not the row's width, which is what makes 'no two cells share a slot' a property of the derivation rather than a hope. (3) A table may be RAGGED: Qt's grid is always full, so the slots nobody filled are a state QTextTable cannot be in; TableRun::slack reports them. (4) HEADER COLUMNS: Qt has headerRowCount and no column peer, and its purpose is pagination; here both bands are declared once and header-ness is DERIVED FROM THE ADDRESS, so a cell that moves into a band becomes a header with nothing restated. (5) It reaches ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY: table / row / cell with aria-rowindex / aria-colindex / aria-rowspan and the columnheader / rowheader bands, where a QTextTable reaches no accessibility interface at all — QAccessibleTextInterface has no method that reports block structure, and QAccessibleTableInterface belongs to the item VIEWS — so to a screen reader a Qt document's table is an undifferentiated run of paragraphs whose merges silently shift every following cell. (6) The structure is ENUMERABLE: scene/text_tables answers what tables are on screen, what shape they are, and where each cell was PAINTED, where Qt requires walking the frame tree qobject_cast-ing each child, in-process. The addressing rides the painted node, so the grid area on screen, the aria-colindex an AT hears and the census an agent reads are one allocation with no second source.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core` `style`: `Display::Grid`, `GridTrack` (CSS `<track-size>`:
auto / px / percent / fr / min-content / max-content = Qt `QTextLength`
plus CSS's two intrinsic keywords), `GridPlacement` (`<line> / span <n>`),
and `LayoutStyle`'s four grid fields. `LayoutStyle` loses `Copy`: a track
list IS a list, and the blast radius was MEASURED at one call site before
the cost was paid.
`pinion-runtime` `layout`: the taffy lowering — `to_taffy_track` is CSS's
own minmax pairs, `to_taffy_placement` the start/span translation. An empty
template lowers to taffy's default, so every pre-R1560 tree is unchanged.
`pinion-core` `text_table` (new): `TableFormat` (Qt `QTextTableFormat` plus
the header-COLUMN band Qt has no property for), `CellSpec` (authored
membership, reach and continuation), `CellPlacement` / `TableRun` /
`GridSlot`. `place_cells` is the derivation: HTML's own slot allocation,
with the span clamped to the FREE RUN so no two cells can share a slot.
`pinion-core` `TextNode::cell` (boxed) + `DocumentTag::table` / `table_row`
/ `cell`.
`pinion-widget-paint` `document`: `TextBlock::in_cell`; `view_document`
segments the block sequence, folds each segment's lists PER SEGMENT (so a
list in a cell starts at 1) and rebuilds each table run as a grid holding
a row band per row and a box per cell at its derived address.
`pinion-a11y`: `AriaRole::Table` / `Cell` (the axis `Grid`'s own doc
predicted), `AccessNode` row_count / row_index / row_span / column_span,
`table` (new) wired into `build_access_tree`. `NodeIndex` lifts the
find-or-create four passes were each doing linearly — R1559's own note.
`pinion-rpc` `text_tables` (new): `scene/text_tables`. `scene/access` and
`scene/snapshot` carry the same axis; `wire_census` gains four types.
`examples/hello-richtext-cells`; `tools/demos/r1560_table_addressing.py`;
`docs/phase-b-rounds.tsv` 1560; `tools/phase_b_tally.py` `-table`.

`pinion-rpc` 1115 + wire-census 4, `pinion-a11y` 278, `pinion-widget-paint`,
`pinion-runtime`, `pinion-shell`, `pinion-tui`, three example crates.
0 failures. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all
--check` and `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items`
all clean.
`r1560_table_addressing.py` PASS, 70 assertions. Neighbours re-run and
PASS: `r1559_list_numbering.py` (the list fold was restructured beneath
it), `r1551_block_format.py`, `r1546_run_background.py`,
`r1539_wire_states_its_shape.py` (the census gained four types).
Nine counterfactuals, one at a time, each reverted by md5-verified copy and
rebuilt: clamp ignores occupancy / cursor does not step over a held slot /
painted column line taken from the row / the assembler never calls the pass
/ header-ness read off the format / the wire echoes the granted span as the
declared one / a continuation opens its own cell / every slot reported
covered / a merged cell announces span 1. Eight discriminated at the WIRE.
Three formulations were themselves findings: two failed to COMPILE (the
compiler caught them, which is not an assertion catching them), and the
first clamp counterfactual PASSED — the binding had no cell whose free run
was shorter than its row's remainder, so the demo could not tell the two
clamps apart. The scene was changed until it could.
`hello-richtext-cells` paints the same scene through the TERMINAL backend
and the day column begins in one cell column on both rows — a table is an
ordinary grid container, so `pinion-tui` needed no table code (§2 #6).
carry_forward_bullets: Stated gaps, not carry. NESTED TABLES are absent: Qt has them, and the
honest way in is the general `QTextFrame` containment axis rather than a
second ad-hoc level counter beside the list one — two nesting mechanisms
that must agree. `minmax()` / `fit-content()` track sizing, and CSS's
`grid-auto-flow`, are unbuilt (every cell here is placed explicitly, by
design, so auto-flow never runs). `setMarkdown` / `toHtml` remain the rest
of the document model.
A row every column of which is covered from above gets no `row` node, since
no cell names it. Its extent is still announced, by the spanning cell's
`aria-rowspan` and the table's `aria-rowcount`.

`#[cfg(test)]` scene walkers to the count R1556 registered and R1559 grew;
the cause is unchanged — `pinion_core::Scene` has no general traversal
primitive.

linear `find` per item (R1559's own note) — lifted to `NodeIndex`, which
`attach_block_headings` now uses too; and `tools/phase_b_tally.py` counted
`hello-combobox-editable` as Model/View evidence because "editable"
CONTAINS "table", a substring census with no word boundary crediting an
axis with a combobox for as long as the pattern has existed.

Round 1560.1.decision_summary: R1560.1 §5.12 §5.16 — the census resolves its boxes from one traversal. R1560 asked whether it had registered all of its own debt, and the census it had just written answered no: collect_tables resolved each cell's painted box with Scene::rect_for_tag_absolute, which walks the whole scene per call, so a table's census was O(cells x scene). MEASURED before anything was changed — one 5,000-cell table took 1.17s to answer, on a per-request read path. The first fix was the wrong one, and measuring is the only reason that is known: the obvious defect was the linear per-cell lookup into the rows already collected (the shape R1559 recorded and R1560 had itself lifted to NodeIndex an hour earlier, then repeated here), and indexing it moved 1.17s to 0.84s. An isolating probe then showed the rect resolution alone accounted for 0.92s of a 0.92s census — the whole cost was the term that had not been suspected. Scene::absolute_rects_by_tag collects every tagged node's window-absolute rect in one walk, folding scroll offsets and clips arm for arm with the single lookup, and an equivalence test asserts the two agree tag for tag over a scrolled, clipped scene — including on the tags neither answers for — so the index cannot drift into being a second implementation. It is R1536's finding on the accessible-name pass, one surface over: making a lookup SUCCEED is what makes its quadratic term real. scene/text_lists carried the identical shape from R1559 and is fixed by the same helper rather than left as a measured, known defect next to its own repair.

window-absolute rect from ONE traversal — the indexed peer of
`rect_for_tag_absolute`, folding scroll offsets and clips arm for arm.

for tag over a scrolled, clipped scene, so the index is not a second
implementation free to drift.
`pinion-rpc` `text_tables` / `text_lists` resolve their boxes through it.
The table census also indexes its own rows by tag, the `NodeIndex` shape.

Round 1561.decision_summary: R1561 §5.27 §5.40 §5.38 §5.12 — a selection is a set of RUNS, not a set of rows. "Rows 0 through 999 999" is ONE fact, and holding it as a million facts makes the cost of storing it, comparing it, and — on a framework whose §2 #7 invariant is that the scene is queryable as data — SAYING it proportional to the model rather than to the statement. `VirtualSelect` held a `BTreeSet<usize>`, so on the shipped 10 000-row `hello-multi-select` a Ctrl+A allocated ten thousand nodes and `query("selection")` answered with 58 890 bytes of JSON in 10.9 ms — measured before anything changed — for a fact whose statement is `[[0, 9999]]`, eleven bytes. On the 1 000 000-row model this axis is NAMED for, the same call is ~5.9 MB and ~1.1 s, per read, forever. `IndexRuns` keeps its runs sorted, disjoint AND non-adjacent, so `{0..=4, 5..=9}` is not a value the type can hold because it IS `{0..=9}`; that canonicality is load-bearing rather than tidy, because `VirtualSelect` reports whether an interaction changed anything by COMPARING selections, and a representation that could spell one selection two ways would report a change that did not happen. The invariant also survives the wire: deserialization canonicalises, so a restored session or a malformed `intervene` payload cannot reach a state the constructors refuse to build. Qt's selection is already range-based — `QItemSelection` is a `QList<QItemSelectionRange>` — so the IDEA is Qt's floor rather than this round's invention; four things are past it, and each falls out of the canonical invariant rather than being an extra feature. (1) THE COUNT IS ANSWERABLE: `QItemSelectionModel` has `hasSelection()` and no count accessor at all, so "how many rows are selected" is `selectedRows().size()` — one `QModelIndex` per selected row, built and thrown away to read a length; `selection_count` sums run lengths. (2) THE EXTREMES ARE O(1): `selectedIndexes()` is documented to return a list that "contains no duplicates, and is not sorted", so the first selected row — the target of every scroll-to-selection — costs a scan. (3) EQUALITY IS SET EQUALITY: only `QItemSelection::merge` is documented to guarantee non-overlapping ranges, which is why `selectedIndexes()` must promise de-duplication, so two Qt selections covering the same rows can differ as values depending on the order the `select()` calls arrived in. (4) MATERIALISING IS A WRITTEN DECISION: `iter` is the only accessor that costs the selection's size and it is named, where `indexes()` is how a Qt consumer reads a selection at all. Reaching for the wire form found the same defect one layer up: the a11y builders took a `&BTreeSet<usize>` that every binding rebuilt each frame purely so `contains` could be asked about the ~20 rows in the window — a third representation of a fact the model and the paint projection each already held — and they now take the membership QUESTION, so neither binding mentions `BTreeSet` any more. The demo's decisive assertion is a BOUND ON THE PAYLOAD rather than a clock (a whole-model selection answers in at most 64 bytes, which no per-row encoding satisfies at any speed), with negative controls beside it so the run count is a measurement and not a constant.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core` `index_runs` (new): `Run` (inclusive, `first <= last`, so an
empty run is unrepresentable) and `IndexRuns` — sorted, disjoint AND
non-adjacent, so `{0..=4, 5..=9}` is not a value the type can hold because
it IS `{0..=9}`. Canonical is load-bearing, not tidy: `VirtualSelect`
reports whether an interaction changed anything by COMPARING selections.
`insert_run` / `insert` / `remove` (splits) / `contains` (binary search) /
`len` (rows, O(runs)) / `run_count` / `first` / `last` / `clamped_below`.
`iter` is the ONLY materialising accessor and is named so a call site that
pays the model's size is greppable.
serde is `[[first, last], …]` via `From<Vec<(usize, usize)>>`, which
CANONICALISES — so a hand-written snapshot, a restored session or a
malformed `intervene` payload cannot reach a state the constructors refuse
to build. The invariant survives the wire, not just the methods.
`pinion-core` `virtual_select`: `VirtualSelect::selection` is an
`IndexRuns`; `select_all` and `extend_to` are O(1) in the model's size;
`set_selection` clamps per RUN; new `selected_count` (Qt's missing
`QItemSelectionModel::count()`). The `selection` wire slot carries runs,
`selection_count` is a new read-only derived slot, and `intervene` decodes
through the model's own serde rather than a hand-rolled walk — so a
malformed payload is REFUSED whole where the pre-R1561 filter applied the
integers it recognised and said nothing about the rest.
`selection_to_value` / `read_selection` (the R743.1 encode/decode pair)
both speak runs; `read_selection` returns `IndexRuns`, so a binding paints
with `contains` per RENDERED row instead of projecting every selected index.
`pinion-a11y` `virtual_grid` / `virtual_list`: `GridSelection::Multi` and
both `*_multiselected` builders take `&dyn Fn(usize) -> bool` — the
membership QUESTION (Qt's `isSelected`) — not a `&BTreeSet<usize>` every
caller built over the window each frame. That set was a third
representation of a fact the model and the paint projection each held.
`examples/hello-multi-select` / `hello-grid-multi-select`: `from_runs`
fills the Copy bitmap with one `fill` per run and takes its total from
`IndexRuns::len`; the status bar shows the RUN COUNT beside the row count,
so the number the cost is in is on the glass. Neither binding mentions
`BTreeSet` any more.
`examples/hello-inspector`: one selection type throughout — the
coordinator, the four domain derivations, the paint projection's
`from_parts`, and `intervene`, which now decodes runs through the model.
`tools/rpc_verify.py`: `selection_rows` / `runs_of`, the demo-side decoder
and its inverse, lifted once for the seven demos that read this slot.
`tools/demos/r1561_selection_runs.py` (new, 47 assertions);
`docs/phase-b-rounds.tsv` 1561 modelview.
verification_bullets: MEASURED BEFORE, then after, same box, same probe, same steady state, on
the shipped `hello-multi-select` (10 000 rows). Before:
`invoke("select_all")` = 10 000 integers, 58 890 bytes, 15.8 ms;
`query("selection")` = the same 58 890 bytes, 1.2 ms warm. After: `[[0,
9999]]`, 11 bytes, 1.0 ms and 0.3 ms. The fact those 58 890 bytes stated is
11 bytes long. On the 1 000 000-row model this axis is named for the old
pair is ~5.9 MB and ~1.1 s, per read.
`tools/demos/r1561_selection_runs.py` — 47 assertions over the wire. The
decisive one is a BOUND ON THE PAYLOAD, not a clock: a whole-model
selection must answer in <= 64 bytes, which no per-row encoding satisfies
at any speed. Zero-flake by construction.
FIVE COUNTERFACTUALS, one at a time, each reverted and the revert verified
by md5, all caught over the wire: (1) abutting runs do not merge — caught
at "putting the row back MERGES the two runs"; (2) `selected_count` reports
`run_count` instead of rows — caught at "every row is selected, and the
count says so"; (3) `clamped_below` drops a straddling run instead of
trimming it — caught at "the part of the run the model has is kept"; (4)
`intervene` accepts a malformed payload instead of refusing it — caught at
"an array of bare indices is not an array of runs"; (5) the binding's
on-screen run count is a constant — caught at "punching a hole shows two
runs on the glass".
NEGATIVE CONTROLS inside the demo itself, so the run count is a
measurement rather than a constant: three apart rows really are three runs,
three adjacent rows are one, and a hole splits a whole-model run in two
while the ROW count moves by exactly one.

Six pre-existing demos re-run green after the wire form changed:
MEASURED AND FOUND NOT OURS: any RPC request following a mutating `invoke`
on these bindings stalls ~1 s (424-1000 ms). Reproduced identically at HEAD
in a separate git worktree, so it predates this round; independent of the
selection's size (a one-row `select` and a `clear` stall the same); and
independent of what the follow-up asks (`query("anchor")`, `scene/tick` and
`scene/snapshot` all stall). Registered, not fixed — it is the event-loop
wake path, a round of its own.
carry_forward_bullets: STATED LIMIT, not a gap: a binding's Copy paint projection still
materialises. `WidgetCore::State` is `Copy` and an `IndexRuns` owns a
`Vec`, so `hello-multi-select` / `hello-grid-multi-select` keep a
`[bool; N]` bitmap. It is now filled per RUN and counted by `IndexRuns`,
and the framework's own answer for state that is not `Copy` already exists
(shared state resolved in the view fn — `use_scroll_state`,
`use_column_layout_with`, and `hello-inspector` for this very model). No
binding needed it here; a million-row multi-select would.
STATED LIMIT: `IndexRuns` has one consumer. The other index sets in the
tree were censused and are correctly NOT consumers — `text_edit` folds and
`group_order` collapsed groups are sparse by nature, and `TreeSelect` /
the node editor key on stable ids, where runs mean nothing.
STATED LIMIT: the runs are one-dimensional. Qt's `QItemSelectionRange`
spans rows AND columns; the selection this framework windows is the row
axis, and a second dimension nothing selects on would be a field every
consumer filled in with "all columns". The capability is Qt's floor, the
shape is chosen.
NEXT GAP on this axis, unchanged by this round: the section axis answers
two of Qt's roles on both axes; the ROW axis has no interaction at all
(`QHeaderView` section click selects the row) — and this round is what
makes that expressible, since "select this row" from a header band is a
run; the band's width is stated rather than `ResizeToContents`;
`virtual_grid.rs` has two row emitters; a binding states its row window
twice (paint + a11y).
PRE-EXISTING, NOT OURS, NOW MEASURED: any RPC request following a mutating
`invoke` stalls ~1 s (424-1000 ms), reproduced identically at HEAD in a
separate worktree. Independent of the selection's size and of what the
follow-up asks, so it is the event-loop wake path rather than anything in
this axis. Whether it is headless-only (`PINION_HIDDEN_WINDOW`) is
UNRESOLVED and deliberately not guessed at. A round of its own, and a large
one: every automation and AI interaction with these bindings pays it.

Round 1562.decision_summary: R1562 §5.27 §5.40 §5.35 §5.38 — a header section selects the LINE through it. R1548 gave the grid its vertical band and R1547 gave a section its roles, so a row could be asked what it was called and what mark it carried; nothing could be DONE to it. Pressing the band did nothing, and the only way to select a row was to land on one of its cells — the part of a row least likely to be on screen, because the band is pinned against the horizontal scroll and the cells are not. That is the whole of Qt QHeaderView's interaction, missing. R1562 makes a section an ADDRESS: `GridSendKey::RowHeader { row }` (`"r<row>"`) and `Corner` (`"c"`), and — the line the round turns on — `row()` answers `Some(row)` for a row header, so a band press reaches the very `select` / `toggle` / `extend_to` transition a CELL press reaches. Qt gets the same behaviour from a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION: `QHeaderView::mousePressEvent` -> `QAbstractItemView::selectRow`, beside `QAbstractItemView::mousePressEvent` -> `selectionCommand(index, event)`. Here there is one, so no chord can mean one thing in the band and another in the body, and the demo asserts that state-for-state across all three chords rather than trusting it. It rests directly on R1561: a Shift-press spanning 897 rows is ONE run in eleven bytes, which is why the band's reach is free rather than proportional to what it selects. FIVE THINGS PAST Qt 6.11, all read over the wire. (1) THE CORNER IS TRI-STATE: `QTableView::setCornerButtonEnabled(true)` is documented as "clicking on the corner button of the table view selects all cells in the view" — one-way, with no state — so a Qt user who select-alls by mistake clears by clicking a cell, which also selects that cell; here the corner shows how much of the model is selected (`SelectionExtent`, O(1) off R1561's runs where Qt's equivalent is `selectedRows().size() == rowCount()`) and takes it back. (2) IT IS NAMED: `QTableCornerButton` is a private `QAbstractButton` with no text, and `QTableView` exposes no accessor for it, so there is no supported way to name it — a screen-reader user meets an unnamed button whose state is not reported because it has none; here it is a `columnheader` holding a named `checkbox` carrying `aria-checked` and its `mixed` leg, HTML's own shape. (3) THE SECTION SHOWS THE SELECTION BY DERIVATION: Qt's `QHeaderView::highlightSections` is a view flag that DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so a Qt band is silent about the selection unless someone turns it on and is then a second statement free to disagree with the rows; here the fill comes from the same predicate the strip beside it is filled from. (4) THE CONTROL IS A VERB: `invoke("toggle_all")` drives it headlessly (§2 #2), where Qt has no such method at all. (5) THE BAND IS WINDOWED AND SO IS ITS COST: selecting all 10 000 rows draws no extra section. Reaching for the corner forced the band to be NAMED as a thing — `RowHeaderAxis` holds the section axis AND the corner, because a corner is not a role (the horizontal axis has none) and because that is where Qt puts it too, on `QTableView` rather than on `headerData`. Naming the band is what lets the corner reach the virtualized and the eager surface from `row_header_column`, the one place they already share, so the two cannot end up with different answers about whether a corner acts. The eager surface gets the press too, through the same model verbs its cell press drives, because a band that paints on one surface and is inert on the other is the exact defect R1547.1 and R1536 each already paid for.

Round 1563.decision_summary: R1563 §5.27 §5.40 §5.38 §5.35 — a selection has TWO AXES. R1561 made a selection a set of runs over ROWS; R1562 made the vertical band's section select the row through it, and named the mirror it could not build: a COLUMN header cannot select its column, because there was no column axis to select on. "Column 3" was not a statement the windowed coordinator could hold at any price. Qt is two-dimensional throughout — `QItemSelectionModel` selects `QModelIndex`es and `QItemSelectionRange` is a rectangle — so the CAPABILITY is Qt's floor; the SHAPE is chosen here, and it is forced by one fact a rectangle list cannot accommodate. A set of cells has NO UNIQUE MINIMAL DECOMPOSITION into rectangles: a cross — row 0 entirely plus column 0 entirely — is two rectangles two different ways, both minimal, and R1561 made canonicality load-bearing because it is what lets the model report whether an interaction CHANGED anything. So `CellSelection` is not a rectangle list. A selection is a function from a row to the set of columns selected in it, and this holds that function GROUPED BY ITS VALUE: one band per distinct `ColumnSpan`, carrying the rows that have it, which is unique by construction because each row's column set is one value. THE AXES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT SYMMETRIC, and the asymmetry is the model's: the ROW axis is the one this framework windows, so a selection stated over rows must not silently claim rows that stream in later; the COLUMN axis is the schema, so adding a metadata column must not demote a selected record. `ColumnSpan::All` therefore carries no column count. FOUR THINGS PAST Qt 6.11, all read over the wire. (1) A RECORD OUTLIVES THE SCHEMA: a Qt full row is `QItemSelectionRange(index(r, 0), index(r, columnCount() - 1))`, bound to the width at the moment of selection, so inserting a column leaves the range covering every column BUT the new one — the row is silently no longer fully selected and `QItemSelectionModel::selectedRows()`, documented to return rows "where all columns are selected", stops returning it. Here that row is `"all"` and stays whole; the demo reads the two spellings side by side as DIFFERENT VALUES over identical painted cells. (2) EQUALITY IS SET EQUALITY IN TWO DIMENSIONS: `QItemSelection` is a `QList<QItemSelectionRange>` that permits overlap — which is why `selectedIndexes()` must promise de-duplication — so two Qt selections covering the same cells can differ as values by the order the `select()` calls arrived in. (3) THE HEADER SELECTION IS A DECLARATION: Qt reaches column selection through `sectionPressed` while `sectionClicked` drives `sortByColumn`, and nothing says which a given header has, so a header can silently have both; `SectionPress` is one value, defaulting to `Inert` so no sortable header starts selecting. (4) IT REACHES ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY ON BOTH AXES: Qt has `QAccessibleTableCell::isSelected()` and `QAccessibleTableHeaderCell` has NO selection state of any kind, so a fully selected Qt column announces exactly as an unselected one. Reaching for the column axis found a duplication one level up: `SelectionBehavior` already existed on the EAGER `Table` (R954, two arms), and "what does a press select" is one concept Qt spells once — so it moved to `cell_selection`, gained Qt's third arm `SelectColumns`, and is re-exported where R954 named it. The paint's selection argument became the QUESTION rather than a row predicate (`GridSelection`, the R1536 seam widened), with a blanket impl over `Fn(usize) -> bool` so all ~20 row-select consumers keep both their spelling and their exact behaviour — and the band's fill became TRI-STATE, a state unreachable before this round and one Qt's `highlightSections` bool cannot express at all.

Round 1563.publishable_decision_summary: R1563 §5.27 §5.40 §5.38 §5.35 — a selection has TWO AXES. R1561 made a selection a set of runs over ROWS; R1562 made the vertical band's section select the row through it, and named the mirror it could not build: a COLUMN header cannot select its column, because there was no column axis to select on. "Column 3" was not a statement the windowed coordinator could hold at any price. Qt is two-dimensional throughout — `QItemSelectionModel` selects `QModelIndex`es and `QItemSelectionRange` is a rectangle — so the CAPABILITY is Qt's floor; the SHAPE is chosen here, and it is forced by one fact a rectangle list cannot accommodate. A set of cells has NO UNIQUE MINIMAL DECOMPOSITION into rectangles: a cross — row 0 entirely plus column 0 entirely — is two rectangles two different ways, both minimal, and R1561 made canonicality load-bearing because it is what lets the model report whether an interaction CHANGED anything. So `CellSelection` is not a rectangle list. A selection is a function from a row to the set of columns selected in it, and this holds that function GROUPED BY ITS VALUE: one band per distinct `ColumnSpan`, carrying the rows that have it, which is unique by construction because each row's column set is one value. THE AXES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT SYMMETRIC, and the asymmetry is the model's: the ROW axis is the one this framework windows, so a selection stated over rows must not silently claim rows that stream in later; the COLUMN axis is the schema, so adding a metadata column must not demote a selected record. `ColumnSpan::All` therefore carries no column count. FOUR THINGS PAST Qt 6.11, all read over the wire. (1) A RECORD OUTLIVES THE SCHEMA: a Qt full row is `QItemSelectionRange(index(r, 0), index(r, columnCount() - 1))`, bound to the width at the moment of selection, so inserting a column leaves the range covering every column BUT the new one — the row is silently no longer fully selected and `QItemSelectionModel::selectedRows()`, documented to return rows "where all columns are selected", stops returning it. Here that row is `"all"` and stays whole; the demo reads the two spellings side by side as DIFFERENT VALUES over identical painted cells. (2) EQUALITY IS SET EQUALITY IN TWO DIMENSIONS: `QItemSelection` is a `QList<QItemSelectionRange>` that permits overlap — which is why `selectedIndexes()` must promise de-duplication — so two Qt selections covering the same cells can differ as values by the order the `select()` calls arrived in. (3) THE HEADER SELECTION IS A DECLARATION: Qt reaches column selection through `sectionPressed` while `sectionClicked` drives `sortByColumn`, and nothing says which a given header has, so a header can silently have both; `SectionPress` is one value, defaulting to `Inert` so no sortable header starts selecting. (4) IT REACHES ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY ON BOTH AXES: Qt has `QAccessibleTableCell::isSelected()` and `QAccessibleTableHeaderCell` has NO selection state of any kind, so a fully selected Qt column announces exactly as an unselected one. Reaching for the column axis found a duplication one level up: `SelectionBehavior` already existed on the EAGER `Table` (R954, two arms), and "what does a press select" is one concept Qt spells once — so it moved to `cell_selection`, gained Qt's third arm `SelectColumns`, and is re-exported where R954 named it. The paint's selection argument became the QUESTION rather than a row predicate (`GridSelection`, the R1536 seam widened), with a blanket impl over `Fn(usize) -> bool` so all ~20 row-select consumers keep both their spelling and their exact behaviour — and the band's fill became TRI-STATE, a state unreachable before this round and one Qt's `highlightSections` bool cannot express at all.

Round 1563.1.decision_summary: R1563.1 §5.27 §5.40 — the debt census answers the question, and it found a defect. Asked whether R1563's debt was all registered, the honest procedure is to RUN a census rather than to recall one (R1561.1's lesson, applied). Four findings. Three are stated limits and are recorded as such. The fourth is a real defect and is repaid here: the binding's paint snapshot answered "is this column selected anywhere" — the question that decides whether a header section shows as involved — by scanning the whole projected model, once per PAINTED section. That is O(model x window) every frame, on the very axis whose claim is that per-frame work is bounded by what is visible, and R1563 shipped it with a comment CALLING it bounded by the window. It is now the union of the bands' own column masks, taken while projecting them, which is O(bands): eight byte-tests where the shipped 10 000-row model was paying about sixty thousand. The round also finds why nothing caught it — the column band's `Partial` arm, the only reason the scan existed, had NO TEST. R1563's tests covered the row band's `Partial` and the column band's `All` and stopped there. The new test asserts both the painted result and that the O(bands) union equals the O(model) scan it replaced, for every column, so the optimisation cannot silently change the answer. Two counterfactuals were written before one held: the first two did not compile, and a counterfactual the compiler catches proves nothing about the assertion (R1558).
changes_bullets: `examples/hello-column-select`: `CellSnapshot::touched` — per-column "selected in ANY row", taken as the union of the bands' own column masks while projecting them, so it costs O(bands). It was `self.rows.iter().any(...)` per painted section: O(model x window) EVERY FRAME, on the axis whose whole claim is that per-frame work is bounded by what is visible. On the shipped 10 000-row model that is ~60 000 byte-tests a frame for a fact the bands answer in eight.

`examples/hello-column-select`: `r1563_1_a_partly_covered_column_is_involved_not_selected` — the assertion that arm never had. R1563's tests covered the ROW band's `Partial` and the COLUMN band's `All`; the column band's `Partial`, which is the only reason the scan existed, had no test at all. It also pins the derivation against the scan it replaced, for every column.

Round 1564.decision_summary: R1564 §5.15 §5.12 §2 #2 §2 #7 (PINION-PR82) — a refused invoke STATES WHY. `InvokeError::Rejected` was a payload-free variant, so a producer that knew exactly why it was refusing had nowhere to say it; the variant's own doc had already conceded the point by listing "preconditions unmet, statechart in a forbidding state, etc." — a SET, not a reason. The cost was measured downstream rather than argued: over sprag's fifteen reachable CLI failure paths, SIX print a list of causes joined by `or`, not because the consumer is lazy but because the daemon's handler knew which one it was and the wire had no slot for the answer. `report_agent` refuses in exactly two places, "no detector installed" and "no pane with that id", demanding completely different operator actions; they arrived fused, as the string `InvokeRejected`. Qt has NO CHANNEL AT ALL here — `QMetaObject::invokeMethod` answers `bool`, `QAction::trigger()` answers `void` — so nothing in this round is parity and the shape is chosen. THE TWO HALVES ARE ONE CHANGE, which is the round's load-bearing argument. Carrying the producer's sentence in `error.data` ALONE would make the wire LESS machine-readable, not more: `data` was previously always a word this framework authored, so a consumer could match one to classify, and free application prose in the same slot takes that away. So a refusal arrives under `ACTION_REFUSED` (-32005), a code distinct from `-32602 Invalid params` — which is the wrong category anyway for a call whose parameters were FINE, the path having resolved and the argument type having matched before the surface declined on a fact about its own state. A consumer branches on the CODE and PRINTS the sentence; it never matches the sentence. This also removes a live collision PINION-PR82 flagged: sprag reads `-32602` as "no such session", safe today only because a READ cannot carry an action refusal — "safe by accident" being a state worth spending a code on. The reason is REQUIRED by the type, and that is deliberate: an optional reason is a reason nobody supplies, the same argument `ArgDomain::Open`'s doc makes about a domain that must never be a default. The price is a sweep of all 277 in-tree construction sites, and the sweep is where the round found its evidence. `pinion-widget-paint`'s dock wrote `Err(_) => Err(Rejected)` while `TopologyError` carried a full `Display` sentence for every arm — the reason existed, was recorded into an internal outcome log, and was DISCARDED at the wire, under a comment explaining that the log was the SSOT. `pinion-audio` had a comment conceding an unknown clip and a full command ring were the same value ("both are 'could not play now'") when one will never succeed and the other is the one to retry. `menu.rs` had two refusals distinguished only by a test COMMENT. Reaching for the sentence also opened a fact the tree had and could not reach: the sce codegen emits `EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS`, `from_name` tests membership against it, and nothing could ASK what it contained — so a refused `send` could say a name was wrong and not what would have been right. `drivable_names` is derived from that same const, so the vocabulary a refusal advertises and the vocabulary the surface accepts cannot drift; a refused `send` now names both what arrived and the closed set it failed to join.
