Round 1565.decision_summary: R1565 §5.15 §5.12 §2 #2 §2 #7 (PINION-PR82) — the WRITE channel states its range, and the codes become enumerable. R1564 gave `invoke` its reason and left two things its own audit named: `InterveneError` carried none, and the code R1564 allocated was discoverable only by reading pinion's source. This closes both, plus the two shape defects R1564 left in its own work. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN, not a gap left in it. Only `OutOfRange` gains a payload, because it is the only arm of `InterveneError` whose meaning its variant does not determine — a client holding it knows its value was wrong and not what a right one would be. `ReadOnly`, `TypeMismatch` and `UnknownPath` are each fully determined by their variant: there is one way for a path to be undeclared, one way for a `String` to arrive where an `Int` belongs, one way for a slot to be unwritable. The honest test of that claim is PINION-PR82's own complaint — a producer knowing WHICH of several facts and unable to say — and for a read-only slot there is only one fact. THE CODE IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. Unlike a refused action, an out-of-range write really IS a bad parameter, so `-32602` was the right CATEGORY; what makes it wrong now is the PAYLOAD. `rpc/errors` publishes the rule that `-32602` carries a word from this crate's closed vocabulary while every application-defined code carries free application text, and leaving an out-of-range sentence under `-32602` would falsify that rule for every method at once. That publication is itself the second closure: R1089 made the method names askable and R1539 made the response shapes askable, and R1564 moved the whole classifying job onto `error.code` while leaving the codes readable only in source — which would have replaced one undiscoverable contract with another. `data_is_prose` is the field that matters: it tells a client whether the payload it is holding may be matched or only shown. THE SWEEP FOUND THE SAME DEFECT BELOW THE WIRE, twice. `wire::resolve_index` — one helper, eight surfaces — already held the bound it checked against and threw it away, and `table` carried two open-coded copies of that helper which reaching for a sentence made visible: three copies of a bound cannot disagree while they all answer one payload-free variant, and three copies composing a sentence can. Larger: `ColumnLayout::restore_state` refuses for FIVE distinct reasons, each already explained by a comment beside its guard, and every one left by the same `bool` — Qt's `restoreState()` has exactly that shape, which is why this one did. It now returns a `Result` whose sentence rides straight out through `intervene`, and writing that sentence is what exposed the ordering: a demo needle failed because the restore refuses at a guard the demo's own comment placed later. R1564.1 also corrects two things R1564 got wrong in its own hands. Its fix for a passing counterfactual PARSED the advertised vocabulary back out of the refusal message, which closed the hole and opened a smaller one — a drifted format answers with an empty list, and an empty list satisfies a membership test vacuously; the property never needed the message, because `require_event` composes the sentence FROM `drivable_names` and asking that function is asking the source rather than its rendering. And the `#[non_exhaustive]` wildcard that R1564 made honest at RUNTIME is now caught at COMPILE time, by an exhaustive match inside the defining crate where the attribute does not apply — the gate the transport's mandatory `_` arm cannot have.
changes_bullets: `pinion-core` `external`: `InterveneError::OutOfRange(RefusalReason)` + `out_of_range()` / `reason()`. The ONE arm of this enum whose meaning its variant does not determine — a client holding it knew its value was wrong and not what a right one would be. `ReadOnly` / `TypeMismatch` / `UnknownPath` deliberately stay bare: each is fully determined by its variant, so a sentence would restate it. The honest test of that split is PINION-PR82's own complaint — a producer knowing WHICH of several facts; for a read-only slot there is one fact, for an out-of-range value as many as there are slots.

`pinion-core` `widgets::wire`: `resolve_index` states the range, for eight surfaces from one place. It already held the bound, which is why the sentence belongs there; `what` names the thing indexed in each surface's own vocabulary. The two failures are told apart on purpose — an index past the end names the extent, a NEGATIVE one cannot be an index at all, and saying "0..3" about `-1` invites the reading that some other negative would have worked.

`pinion-core` `column_layout`: `restore_state` returns `Result` instead of `bool`. It refuses for FIVE distinct reasons, each already explained by a comment beside its guard, and every one left by the same `false` — PINION-PR82's complaint one level below the wire. Found by writing the sentence: a demo needle failed and showed the restore refusing at a guard the demo's own comment said ran later.

`pinion-core` `column_layout` / `column_widths`: `row_len` / `px_ceiling` / `pixel_width` — a whole-row write states BOTH counts (the header's extent is the fact a client is missing; "wrong length" alone leaves it guessing which number to change), and a pixel bound states the ceiling.

`pinion-core` `table`: `resolve_row_intervene` / `resolve_col_intervene` were open-coded copies of `wire::resolve_index` and now route through it. Reaching for the sentence is what made that visible — three copies of a bound could not disagree while they all answered one payload-free variant.

`pinion-rpc` `intervene`: `InterveneError::OutOfRange(RefusalReason)` forwards it verbatim, and `UnmappedSurfaceError` takes the `#[non_exhaustive]` wildcard. That wildcard used to absorb `TypeMismatch`, so a variant added upstream would have been reported as "your value was the wrong TYPE" — a specific and probably false statement about the caller's payload.

`pinion-rpc` `dispatch`: `VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` (-32006). FORCED by the reason rather than chosen: unlike a refused action, an out-of-range write really IS a bad parameter, so `-32602` was the right CATEGORY — what makes it wrong is the PAYLOAD, now free application text, against a published rule that `-32602` carries a closed vocabulary.

`pinion-rpc` `errors` (new, R1564.1): `rpc/errors` publishes every code with `data_is_prose` — the fact that decides whether a client may MATCH the payload or only show it. R1089 made the names askable and R1539 the shapes; moving the classifying job onto `error.code` without this would have replaced one undiscoverable contract with another. A source-scan test asserts every code this crate emits is published.

`pinion-core` `widget_core` (R1564.1): `advertised_vocabulary` DELETED. R1564's fix for a passing counterfactual parsed the list back out of the refusal message, which closed the hole and opened a smaller one — a drifted format answers with an empty list, and an empty list satisfies a membership test vacuously. The property needs no message: `require_event` composes the sentence FROM `drivable_names`, so asking that function is asking the source rather than its rendering.

`pinion-core` `widget_core` (R1564.1): an exhaustive match on `InvokeError` inside the DEFINING crate, where `#[non_exhaustive]` does not apply — the compile-time gate `pinion-rpc`'s mandatory `_` arm cannot have.

`pinion-core` `test_fixtures`: `assert_out_of_range_saying`, separate from `assert_refused_saying` rather than generic over the error type — a helper taking "any error with a reason" would read as though `ReadOnly` might grow one.
`tools/rpc_verify.py`: `assert_out_of_range` + `VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE`, replacing `data="OutOfRange"` at 9 demo sites.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1564_refusal_states_why.py` extended — 10 phases, PASS. The write channel states its range under its own code; a READ-ONLY slot keeps the pre-R1565 word under -32602 (without which the new code would be unfalsifiable); `rpc/errors` publishes both prose-carrying codes and the rule that decides matchability; the catalogue is reachable through `rpc/methods`.

It now returns a `Result` whose sentence rides straight out through `intervene`, and writing that sentence is what exposed the ordering: a demo needle failed because the restore refuses at a guard the demo's own comment placed later. R1564.1 also corrects two things R1564 got wrong in its own hands. Its fix for a passing counterfactual PARSED the advertised vocabulary back out of the refusal message, which closed the hole and opened a smaller one — a drifted format answers with an empty list, and an empty list satisfies a membership test vacuously; the property never needed the message, because `require_event` composes the sentence FROM `drivable_names` and asking that function is asking the source rather than its rendering. Round 1566.decision_summary: R1566 §5.12 §5.15 §2 #2 §2 #7 — a refusal never says a DECLARED path is unknown. Three verbs address one surface and each answered "no such path" when it did not recognise a name, which is frequently something the surface itself contradicts: a name one channel does not know may be published on another. The trait says so out loud — `InterveneError::UnknownPath`'s doc reads "path is not declared in the schema" — and no impl can honour it, because an impl knows only that its own match fell through. R1353 WROTE THE FIX DOWN and left it opt-in: `read_only_or_unknown`'s doc says "every read-only External needs exactly this rule", and 2 surfaces route through it against 97 that implement `intervene`. R1566 makes it structural instead. The wire refusal is derived from the surface's own `$schema` at a place the compiler will not let a dispatch site skip: the infallible `From` conversion is gone, replaced by one that cannot be called without the declaration. query on a declared ACTION answers PathIsAnAction; intervene on a declared SLOT answers ReadOnly; intervene on a declared ACTION answers PathIsAnAction; invoke on a declared SLOT answers PathIsAReadSlot. PAST QT 6.11 DECISIVELY: Qt fuses every one of these into a value carrying no reason — `setProperty()` and `invokeMethod()` answer a bare bool, and `property()` answers an invalid QVariant, the same value it answers for a name in no meta-object at all. THE MEASUREMENT IS THE ROUND. Deriving the refusal made `SchemaChannel` load-bearing and it had never been read by anything: R1504 added it, `Read` was the silent default, nothing branched on it. Probed at R1566: 116 of 288 declared scalar fields across nine bindings — 40% — were actions declared as readable slots, plus 102 inside the framework itself, 0 of them dual. Nobody was lying; a declaration with no consumer is a declaration nothing keeps true, and R1563 had already found and fixed exactly this in ONE widget with a hand-written gate. THE SHARP EDGE WAS FOUND BY A DEMO, NOT BY REASONING: `SchemaChannel::Read` means "readable", not "read-only", so every writable slot is declared that way too. The write channel therefore re-judges only a SCALAR path, where "the impl did not recognise it" entails "the impl does not write it"; for a family the impl recognised the SHAPE and rejected the ARGUMENT, and `voice.999.gain` under a writable `voice.<id>.gain` was reported read-only until `hello-audio-engine` caught it. Adding three words to a vocabulary R1565 called closed and never published forced the last piece: `data_vocabulary` now publishes it, gated in both directions, and enumerating it corrected R1565's claim — two focus refusals put the word in `error.message` and the caller's own tag in `error.data`, so the honest statement is "a word this crate owns, or an echo of what the caller supplied — never free application prose". A SECOND FINDING came out of the wide re-run and is registered UNFIXED on purpose: `r1182_node_edge_autopan` is flaky at HEAD (control worktree, 1 in 6, untouched by this round), because it reads an invariant offset through two separate requests while every request nudges the very auto-pan it is measuring, and the pan then clamps against the world bound. Four fixes were tried and each measured worse; the honest one needs an atomic multi-path read or a pausable clock, neither of which this framework has, so the demo is left exactly as CI has it rather than shipped half-fixed.
changes_bullets: `pinion-rpc` `intervene` / `invoke`: the infallible `From<TraitXError>` conversions are GONE, replaced by `from_declined(err, schema, path)`. That is the whole structural move: an `err.into()` had no access to the declaration, so the only thing it could do with the trait's `UnknownPath` was repeat it — and the trait documents that variant as "path is not declared in the schema", which no impl can honour because an impl knows only that its own `match` fell through. Taking the schema by value makes the judgement unskippable rather than remembered, and the compiler enumerated the sites.
`pinion-rpc` `intervene`: `InterveneError::PathIsAnAction`. A write addressed at a declared ACTION now names the channel instead of denying the path exists.

`pinion-rpc` `invoke`: `InvokeError::PathIsAReadSlot`. The mirror, and deliberately NOT mirrored in the other direction: a name declared an action that the impl then does not recognise is a surface whose declaration and dispatch disagree, and `UnknownInvokePath` reports that honestly where a friendlier word would hide it.

`pinion-rpc` `query`: `QueryError::PathIsAnAction`, applied ONLY to the cross-channel case. A declared readable FAMILY whose index addresses nothing is genuinely unknown, so overriding there would trade one false statement for its mirror image.
`pinion-rpc` `resolve`: `declared_channel` — the one question every "no such path" refusal must ask before it is allowed to say that.

THE SHARP EDGE, found by `hello-audio-engine` and not by reasoning: `SchemaChannel::Read` means "readable", NOT "read-only" — every writable slot is declared that way too. So the write channel re-judges only a SCALAR declared path, where "the impl did not recognise it" does entail "the impl does not write it". For a parametric family it does not: the impl recognised the SHAPE and rejected the ARGUMENT, and `voice.999.gain` under a writable `voice.<id>.gain` would have been reported read-only. Nothing is lost — `read_only_or_unknown` has answered that case at the impl since R1353, where the difference is knowable.

`examples/`: 116 more, across 8 bindings. `hello-data-grid` alone published `add_row`, `paste` and `reset_all` as readable fields; `hello-topology` published `untangle`, which the R1443 demo's own docstring calls "a verb".

`pinion-rpc` `errors`: `ErrorEntry::data_vocabulary` — every word `-32602`'s payload may hold, published. This round ADDS three, and R1564's own argument applies to them: a contract a client can only learn by reading pinion's source is no contract.

Enumerating it CORRECTED the claim R1565 published. `-32602`'s payload is not uniformly a vocabulary word: two focus refusals put the word in `error.message` and the caller's own tag in `error.data`, and a window-prefix failure appends the offending id. The entry now says "a word this crate owns, or an echo of what the caller supplied — never free application prose".

`tools/rpc_verify.py`: `assert_declared_channels_are_true` — the reusable gate that walks a whole surface. Side-effect free by construction: `query` only, because probing the write directions would fire the very actions it inspects.
`tools/rpc_verify.py`: `call` lifted at the EIGHTH byte-identical copy (seven demos each wrote it out); the seven now import it.
verification_bullets: `tools/demos/r1566_refusal_names_the_channel.py` (new) — 11 phases, PASS. All four cross-channel refusals over the wire; the surface's own verdicts untouched, R1565's sentence included; R1487 provenance composes; the whole-surface gate on two bindings; the parametric sharp edge asserted against a family that IS writable; and the three new words read back out of `rpc/errors`.

ONE FINDING, fixed in-round and by a demo rather than by reading: the first form of the write-channel rule reported a writable parametric family as read-only. The restriction to scalars is the fix, and it is asserted in both a unit and the wire demo.

A SECOND FINDING, pre-existing, root-caused and NOT fixed: `r1182_node_edge_autopan` is flaky. Proven pre-existing by a control worktree at HEAD (1 fail in 6, untouched by this round; 3 in 5 under load), so this round neither caused it nor hid it. Root cause measured rather than guessed, in three steps. (1) Its "back-to-back reads = atomic snapshot" comment names TWO separate requests, so a frame lands between them and an invariant offset reads back 568 / 580 / 581. (2) The auto-pan advances on the shell's own frames and EVERY RPC request gives the loop time to run — 12 plain queries with no tick moved the viewport +167 where a `tick(0.05)` moved it +69 — so a read is a nudge, not a free observation. (3) The pan CLAMPS against the world bound (~1408, where a further tick moves it +0), after which the node stops riding and C.3 fails for a reason unrelated to riding. Phase B spends most of that budget before phase C starts, so the demo has been passing on luck.

Four fixes were tried and every one measured WORSE, which is why none shipped: a validated read (viewport / node / viewport again, accepted only when the two viewport reads agree) removes the tear and is 10/10 alone but its retries burn the budget — one first read retried 28 times while the pan ran 86 -> 1250; a warm-up drain makes four trials byte-identical but still failed once under sweep load; `wait_until` convergence fails deterministically because polling reaches the clamp; sampling until two unclamped observations gets NONE, because phase B already clamped the node. The honest fix needs something the framework does not have — an atomic multi-path read, or a pausable clock — so it is a round, not a patch, and `r1182` is left exactly as CI has it rather than shipped half-fixed.
carry_forward_bullets: The framework's declaration gate is still PER WIDGET. R1563 wrote one for `VirtualSelectExternal` by hand; this round found 102 sites the shape never reached, and closed them by census rather than by a gate that cannot be escaped. A generic Rust-side gate needs an instance of every External, which the tree has no registry for.

The 116 corrected declarations cover the 9 bindings probed; ~99 more schema-declaring bindings were not probed, because each needs its own release binary. The reusable gate now exists, so adopting it is one line per demo.

`SchemaChannel` still cannot say a slot is WRITABLE. Qt's `QMetaProperty::isWritable()` can, so this is below Qt: an agent must attempt a write to find out. Declaring it means auditing every writable slot in ~1240 declarations, and publishing it before that audit would ship a fact that is wrong for most of the surface.

All four of R1539's gaps still stand (no method->type binding, no version negotiation / deprecation / compatibility policy / freeze, no per-method error taxonomy, census covers `pinion-rpc` only), and so does R1552's (no per-subscription filter). The vocabulary published here is per CODE; per METHOD is R1539's item and is what a client actually wants.
`rpc/errors` remains a hand-maintained catalog (R1565's own carry). The vocabulary half is now gated in both directions by a source scan; the `meaning` prose is not.

Two framework absences are underneath, and both are round-sized: the wire has no MULTI-PATH ATOMIC READ, so a client wanting two facts about a moving scene from one frame cannot ask for them and every such consumer reads a torn pair; and there is no way to PAUSE the clock from the wire, so a headless client cannot observe an animation without perturbing it — every request it makes advances the thing it is measuring.

Round 1567.decision_summary: R1567 §5.38 §2 #1 §2 #7 — a candle is NOT a distribution, and the reason is the round. R1553 gave this crate its first datum with extent and recorded in `lib.rs` that a candlestick would be its SECOND CONSUMER, "the same interval geometry over open / high / low / close". Building one showed that wrong. A `Distribution`'s five landmarks are TOTALLY ORDERED by construction — derivation cannot invert the box and `from_summary` rejects one — while a candle has four landmarks and only THREE order relations among them: the low is below both middle values and the high above both, and `open` and `close` are not ordered against each other at all. That absence is not a weaker invariant, it IS the datum: which of the two is larger is the fact a candlestick chart exists to show, and two sessions with the same four numbers, the same extent and the same body mean opposite things. A type whose invariant is "non-decreasing" cannot hold it. What the two really share is the PAINT — a band across a slot with landmarks mapped through the value axis — and that is where the sharing now is. PAST QT 6.11, six things, every one read over the wire. (1) The relations are CHECKED and the refusal names the slot; `QCandlestickSet` is five qreals with void setters, so a transposed high and low, or an open outside the extremes, paints whatever geometry it implies. (2) The direction is a VALUE with three arms; Qt has `increasingColor` / `decreasingColor` as paint properties on the SERIES, no accessor on the set, and a documented strict `close > open` — so a DOJI, the session that closed where it opened and the single most-read signal in the form, is silently painted as a losing one. (3) The direction is encoded TWICE: also as the body's fill, hollow for a rise and solid for a fall, the traditional Japanese form which predates colour, so it survives a colour-blind reader and a grayscale print where Qt's hue-only encoding does not. (4) THE DEFAULT HUES WERE CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT AND THE MEASUREMENT IS A FINDING: the conventional mid-green / mid-red pair measures 1.11:1, all but ISOLUMINANT, which is precisely why the traditional finance palette fails a deuteranope so completely — strip the hue and nothing is left. The shipped pair is separated in luminance and `direction_contrast` publishes the ratio. (5) ONE DATUM, TWO READINGS OF THE X-AXIS: a candle carries its own instant, so equal ordinal sessions (the weekend invisible, how price action is read) or real UTC time (the weekend a three-day gap) is a property of the CHART. Qt reaches the two by attaching two axis objects and handing the category one a QStringList supplied SEPARATELY from the sets' timestamps — two descriptions of when the sessions were, with nothing checking they agree — while here the slot names are DERIVED from the instants and the sessions sorted by them once, so the readings cannot disagree, and one CategoryWindow narrows both. (6) A slot the log price axis cannot place is REPORTED rather than pinned to a domain floor. THE COMPARISON ALSO FOUND DEBT IN ITS SIBLING: `Distribution`'s fields were `pub` while its doc claimed the landmarks were "non-decreasing by construction", so the rejection in `from_summary` was defeatable by assignment; made private with accessors, and the claim is now true. THREE OBLIGATION-3b LIFTS landed at their thresholds, one of which the code had NAMED IN ADVANCE — `line.rs` said its numeric x-label loop was "deferred from the R1377 lift until a third numeric-x consumer arrives", and the elapsed reading is that consumer. THE COUNTERFACTUAL PASS FOUND THREE GAPS, all in code this round wrote or lifted, and one of them is the round's sharpest lesson: asserting WHICH sessions a window draws cannot see a window that failed to reach an axis's DOMAIN, because the survivors are still drawn — just in the wrong pixels.
changes_bullets: `pinion-chart` `candle`: `Candle` — instant + open / high / low / close, with the invariant that IS the datum: `low <= min(open, close)` and `max(open, close) <= high`, and NOTHING between open and close. Private fields, `new` the only way in, because a `pub` field would let a caller reach the state the constructor refuses.

THE CORRECTION. `lib.rs` said a candlestick would be `Distribution`'s SECOND CONSUMER, "the same interval geometry". Building one showed it wrong: a distribution's five landmarks are totally ordered by construction, and folding a candle into them discards which of the two middle values is larger — the whole content. Two sessions with the same four numbers, the same extent and the same body mean opposite things. What the two really share is the PAINT, and that is where the sharing now is.

`Direction` — three arms, where Qt has two paint properties on the SERIES and no accessor on the set at all. Qt's documented rule uses a strict `close > open`, so a DOJI — the session that closed where it opened, the single most-read signal in the form — is silently painted as a losing one.

`Direction::body_fill` / `BodyFill` — the direction's SECOND, hue-independent encoding: a rising body is hollow and a falling one solid, the traditional Japanese form, which predates colour. `alpha()` is 0 or 255 rather than two shades, because a shade is a hue distinction under another name and dies in the same grayscale pipeline.

The default hues were chosen BY MEASUREMENT and the measurement is the finding: the conventional mid-green / mid-red pair measures 1.11:1 — all but isoluminant, which is exactly why the traditional finance palette fails a deuteranope. The shipped pair is separated in LUMINANCE (a light green against a deep red) and clears WCAG 2.2 1.4.11's 3:1, published by `CandlestickChart::direction_contrast`.

`pinion-chart` `candlestick`: `SessionAxis` — ONE datum, two readings of the x-axis. Ordinal slots (Qt `QBarCategoryAxis`; the weekend is invisible, which is how price action is read) or real UTC time (Qt `QDateTimeAxis`; the weekend is a gap). Qt reaches the two by attaching two axis objects and handing the category one a `QStringList` supplied SEPARATELY from the sets' timestamps — two descriptions of when the sessions were, with nothing checking they agree or are even the same length. Here the slot names are DERIVED from the instants and the sessions sorted by them once at construction.

One `CategoryWindow` narrows BOTH readings, from the same index pair; Qt needs two calls against two axis objects in two vocabularies (`setRange(QString, QString)` vs `setRange(QDateTime, QDateTime)`), with nothing relating them.

The elapsed reading's body pitch is the MINIMUM adjacent gap, not a mean. Qt clamps a mean-derived column between `minimumColumnWidth` and `maximumColumnWidth`, which overlaps wherever the data is irregular — and session data is irregular by construction, a half-day before a holiday being a real bar.
`CandlestickChart::off_scale` — a slot a logarithmic price axis cannot place draws nothing and is REPORTED by slot, R1528's stance carried to a datum with four of them.

OBLIGATION 3b, three lifts, each at the count the project works to. `draw::category_label_node` at the THIRD byte-identical copy (bar R1374, box plot R1553, candlestick). `draw::x_tick_labels` at its third, where `line.rs`'s own comment had NAMED the threshold in advance: "deferred from the R1377 lift until a third numeric-x consumer arrives". `scene_probe::text_of` at the FIFTH (donut / bar / timeline / treemap).

INLINE DEBT, uncovered by the comparison: `Distribution`'s fields were `pub` while its doc claimed the landmarks were "non-decreasing by construction" — a rejection defeatable by assignment. Made private with accessors; the claim is now true.

Round 1568.decision_summary: R1568 §5.38 §2 #1 §2 #7 — the crate's first NON-CARTESIAN coordinate system, and what makes it one is not the trigonometry. Every chart in `pinion-chart` rested on an assumption nobody had examined: a value maps to a pixel on ONE axis, x horizontally and y vertically, and the two compose by sitting at right angles. `ValueScale` is that assumption's type — `f64 -> f32`, a single number on a single line — and four axis KINDS (linear, log, time, category) all fit inside it precisely because each is still a map onto one line. A polar plot does not fit: its two axes are an angle and a radius, and a point's screen position is a function of BOTH together. THE ONE NEW FACT IS PERIODICITY. On a line, 0 and 360 are two places; on a circle drawn over a 0..360 period they are the SAME place, and the entire round falls out of that. A value outside the period is PLACED rather than dropped — 370 on a compass is 10 — and is reported as WRAPPED, which only an axis that placed it can say. A series CLOSES ON ITSELF, the segment from the last sample back to the first being the axis's doing. The tick at the period's end is the tick at its start, so a closed axis emits ONE of them. PAST QT 6.11, five things, all read over the wire, and every one has a locatable cause: Qt's angular axis is an ordinary `QValueAxis` — the same class a cartesian x-axis uses — so periodicity is modelled NOWHERE. A value outside the range behaves there exactly as it does on a cartesian axis (not drawn); closing a radar loop is the caller's job, done by appending the first point again, which puts a duplicate in the data the model does not contain; `QPolarChart` is always a full circle, so a SECTOR — a gauge over half a turn, an ordinary professional form — is inexpressible; the origin is fixed at 12 o'clock and the winding at clockwise with no accessor, so a mathematician's polar plot cannot be drawn at all; and the angular axis is AUTO-SCALED like any other, so a wind rose whose samples happen to span 10..350 silently gets a period of 340 and every bearing means something different. Here the period is a REQUIRED constructor argument — the opposite of what every cartesian builder in this crate does — because a period is a fact about the QUANTITY (a compass has 360 degrees, a week has 7 days) and no sample reveals it. THE SHAPE THAT MAKES IT COHERE: `closes()` is DERIVED from the sweep rather than declared beside it, so an axis wraps iff its sweep closes the circle. That is not tidiness — wrapping a sector would fold data onto the gap it deliberately leaves, so the wrap, the loop close and the seam tick are three consequences reading ONE answer instead of three flags that can disagree. THE ROUND ALSO LIFTED AN OPTION CHIP at its third byte-identical copy, and the lift produced its own finding: all three bindings had chosen the same label size independently, so the size is a TOKEN rather than a parameter — which also took the wrapper under clippy's argument ceiling, a constraint that pointed at the right design rather than at an allow. TWO FINDINGS IN THE ROUND'S OWN TESTS, both fixed: the seam-tick assertion was first anchored on a period whose nice ticks never land on its endpoint, so it passed whether or not the de-duplication existed; and the demo indexed rings from zero when `chart.ring.0` correctly does not exist, the innermost radial tick being the centre. THREE COUNTERFACTUALS came back as non-verdicts and all three were HARNESS defects — two would not compile, and one read as a PASS because the driver ran `cargo test --lib`, which silently excludes every test in a bin-only example package.
changes_bullets: `pinion-chart` `polar`: `AngularScale` — a value interval mapped onto a sweep of angle, and the crate's first scale that is not a `ValueScale`. Angles are radians clockwise from 12 o'clock, which is the frame `crate::draw`'s arc builder already draws in, so a grid ring and a data point are placed by ONE convention rather than two that must agree.

THE ONE NEW FACT: the axis is **periodic**. `fraction` wraps a value into the period, so `370` on a compass is `10` — placed, not dropped — and `wrapped()` reports that it needed wrapping, which only an axis that placed it can say.

`closes()` is **derived from the sweep**, not declared beside it: an axis wraps iff its sweep closes the circle. Wrapping a sector would fold data onto the gap it deliberately leaves, so a bearing outside a sector's period is genuinely off-scale where the same bearing on a full turn is merely on the other side. One answer feeds all three consequences — the wrap, the loop close, and the seam tick.
`Winding` + `with_origin` + `with_sweep`: the three things `QPolarChart` hard-codes (12 o'clock, clockwise, full circle) are declarations. `mathematical()` is the convention Qt cannot draw at all.

`PolarPlot` is the counterpart of `CartesianPlot` and could not BE one: the radial axis is an ordinary `ValueScale` over `0 .. radius` — so a logarithmic radius is R1528's, not a second implementation — while the angular one is an `AngularScale`, and a point's pixel is a function of both together rather than one per screen dimension.

Round 1568.publishable_decision_summary: R1568 §5.38 §2 #1 §2 #7 — the crate's first NON-CARTESIAN coordinate system, and what makes it one is not the trigonometry. Every chart in `pinion-chart` rested on an assumption nobody had examined: a value maps to a pixel on ONE axis, x horizontally and y vertically, and the two compose by sitting at right angles. `ValueScale` is that assumption's type — `f64 -> f32`, a single number on a single line — and four axis KINDS (linear, log, time, category) all fit inside it precisely because each is still a map onto one line. A polar plot does not fit: its two axes are an angle and a radius, and a point's screen position is a function of BOTH together. THE ONE NEW FACT IS PERIODICITY. On a line, 0 and 360 are two places; on a circle drawn over a 0..360 period they are the SAME place, and the entire round falls out of that. A value outside the period is PLACED rather than dropped — 370 on a compass is 10 — and is reported as WRAPPED, which only an axis that placed it can say. A series CLOSES ON ITSELF, the segment from the last sample back to the first being the axis's doing. The tick at the period's end is the tick at its start, so a closed axis emits ONE of them. PAST QT 6.11, five things, all read over the wire, and every one has a locatable cause: Qt's angular axis is an ordinary `QValueAxis` — the same class a cartesian x-axis uses — so periodicity is modelled NOWHERE. A value outside the range behaves there exactly as it does on a cartesian axis (not drawn); closing a radar loop is the caller's job, done by appending the first point again, which puts a duplicate in the data the model does not contain; `QPolarChart` is always a full circle, so a SECTOR — a gauge over half a turn, an ordinary professional form — is inexpressible; the origin is fixed at 12 o'clock and the winding at clockwise with no accessor, so a mathematician's polar plot cannot be drawn at all; and the angular axis is AUTO-SCALED like any other, so a wind rose whose samples happen to span 10..350 silently gets a period of 340 and every bearing means something different. Here the period is a REQUIRED constructor argument — the opposite of what every cartesian builder in this crate does — because a period is a fact about the QUANTITY (a compass has 360 degrees, a week has 7 days) and no sample reveals it. THE SHAPE THAT MAKES IT COHERE: `closes()` is DERIVED from the sweep rather than declared beside it, so an axis wraps iff its sweep closes the circle. That is not tidiness — wrapping a sector would fold data onto the gap it deliberately leaves, so the wrap, the loop close and the seam tick are three consequences reading ONE answer instead of three flags that can disagree. Round 1597.decision_summary: A frame holds what it was GIVEN, not what it covers. hello-node-editor finishes moving onto pinion-node-graph and debt-two-node-graph-models closes: the tree carried TWO node models and two frame implementations from R1577 until now, and a census for `struct GraphNode` / `struct Edge` is 0. The migration is the round and what it FOUND is the value. Membership was a rectangle re-tested on every read, so widening a comment frame silently adopted nodes and shrinking it abandoned them -- what the frame SAID it held changed with nobody having edited it. It is Node::parent now (R1589, Blender's bNode::parent), and the two gestures that were missing came with it: `attach` / `detach` are NODE_OT_attach / NODE_OT_detach, two census operators whose model layer had landed at R1589 with nothing to reach it, and each ANSWERS the nodes whose frame changed where Blender's operators report only whether the operator ran. Containment reads from both ends and both depths -- frame.<id>.contains one level, .contents transitively, node.<id>.parent -- where Blender exposes node.parent to Python and has NO accessor for a frame's children at all, so its own UI walks every node comparing pointers. `dissolvable` widened from a shape test (exactly one wire in and one out) to LOSSLESSNESS, and dissolve_severs.<id> names the wires a dissolve would cut, which node_internal_relink deletes and returns void for. A cycle can no longer be AUTHORED: connect refuses the closing wire and names the path, where the editor's own gate blocked only a direct self-loop. And a snapshot undo no longer re-issues an id -- Document::advance_ids_from is the crate capability the migration forced out, because restoring a value restores its mint counters and an agent addressing by id would have been talking about a different node.

The example goes 9,186 -> 8,537 lines with the duplicate gone.

Frame membership is a FACT (Node::parent, R1589) where the editor re-derived it from the rectangle on every read, so widening a comment frame silently adopted nodes and shrinking it abandoned them. A resize now changes the box and nothing else.

`attach` / `detach` verbs, which are NODE_OT_attach / NODE_OT_detach -- two census operators whose model layer landed at R1589 with no gesture to reach it. Each ANSWERS the nodes whose frame changed; Blender's report only whether the operator ran. A drag that ends over a frame attaches, as Blender does out of its transform.

Containment reads from both ends and both depths: frame.<id>.contains (one level), frame.<id>.contents (transitive), node.<id>.parent. Blender exposes node.parent to Python and has NO accessor for a frame's children at all.
`dissolvable` widened from a shape test to LOSSLESSNESS (Rewired::lossless), and dissolve_severs.<id> names the wires a dissolve would cut -- node_internal_relink deletes them and returns void.

pinion-node-graph::layout: Extent / Layered / Organic / Placement / Quality. The adapter read four things and only two belong to an application; R1442 lifted the SOLVER at its second consumer and left this behind. Fixes a live defect -- a fixed column pitch charged every column a full card.
Document::advance_ids_from, so a snapshot undo never re-issues an id an agent may hold. Restoring a value restores its mint counters, which is Blender's node_undosys shape too.
Violation::MistypedPortValue: set_port_value refused a value its port could not hold and validate did not, so a peer's document could carry one and the node evaluated to nothing with no explanation.
Sugiyama::run states its determinism in its public doc; the projection had inherited a canonicalising sort whose written reason was false.
PERSISTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 7 -> 8 (the blob is a Document now). Found by the closing audit, and the prohibition that should have caught it is prose with no gate -- registered as its own debt.

tools/demos/r1597_a_frame_holds_what_it_was_given.py PASS -- seven sections over the live RPC surface driving every changed wire contract.

Counterfactuals: six. CF-5 (membership re-derived from the rectangle) fails section B exactly; CF-6 (undo restores its snapshot verbatim) fails section G exactly; CF-1 (fixed column pitch) and CF-2 (frames arranged) each fail their crate tests.

CF-3 and CF-4 both PASSED and that is the round's finding. CF-3 removed the projection's canonicalising sort and nothing failed, because no fixture had a cycle; adding one still did not fail, which exposed the sort's written reason as false. CF-4 removed the SOLVER's own sort and still nothing failed, because a 3-node 2-cycle is degenerate -- no vertex has two successors whose visit order decides anything -- so the discriminating shape was derived (a feeds b and c; b and c loop), and CF-4 then fails.

Also found by running rather than reasoning: a resting value belongs only on a SOURCE's output. The first draft declared one on every port, and R1594's rule then made a node on a cycle evaluate to a plausible grey instead of the null R1260's debugger reads use to localise it.
The example's `add_edge` was reporting true for a wire the crate had refused; caught by a test whose premise had become unreachable.

Registered separately: debt-persisted-schema-bump-is-prose-only -- the closing audit found PERSISTED_SCHEMA_VERSION still at 7 while the serialized shape had changed completely (bumped to 8 here), and the prohibition that should have caught it is prose in a gitignored file with no gate behind it. The honest fix is probably widening the R1539 rpc/schema source-parse gate to cover binding persistence types rather than a new mechanism, which is unmeasured.

Round 1598.decision_summary: A node changes what it IS, not which node it is. Document::set_kind is Blender's NODE_OT_swap_node, and the shape is the whole divergence: there the operator CREATES A NEW NODE AND DELETES THE OLD ONE, so the swapped node's identity dies and every reference to it dies with it -- a selection, a saved layout, an undo record, an agent holding the id. Here the body changes in place, so the NodeId, the position, the label, the appearance, the bypass and the place in the frame forest all survive, which is what makes a swap an EDIT rather than a replace-and-hope. The hard part is not the body: a kind DECLARES its ports (R1594), so changing the kind changes the signature underneath every link and every authored value on the node, and each has to be re-examined. ONE derivation decides what survives -- by NAME, then by POSITION, never against the type relation (R1593's conversion, the same one a link is judged by) -- and it is injective by construction, which is why a swap can neither over-feed an input nor close a cycle and answers no ConnectError at all: links only ever move between ports of the same node, so the node-to-node edge set can lose members and never gain one. Everything that does not survive is NAMED: Swapped carries the ports carried (and whether by name rather than by position), the ports dropped, the links severed and the authored values discarded.
changes_bullets: PAST BLENDER on the rule as well as the report. Blender picks between by-name and by-index from a hard-coded pair of node-type sets (transfer_by_index = both_math_nodes or both_switch_nodes, two literal lists in a Python file), so a wire between two kinds nobody put in those lists is dropped even when the ports line up perfectly; doing both, in order, needs no table -- a name match is the author saying "this is the same port" and position is the honest fallback when nobody said anything. And Blender reports NONE of what it costs: three swallowed exceptions (except IndexError: pass, except KeyError: pass, except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError): pass) plus a silent tree.links.remove for a link that turned out invalid, so "the swap worked" and "the swap worked and cost you two wires" are the same outcome there.

EditError::NotAKind refuses a frame, a group instance or an interface node BY NAME: a body this crate owns is not the application's to overwrite, and a frame with a signature would be linkable. Document::remap_node_ports lives in model.rs because that is the module that mutates a tree's link list, and keeping it there is what makes "no link can be half-moved" a property of the code rather than a convention.

A census finding: NODE_OT_swap_node is implemented in PYTHON (scripts/startup/bl_operators/node.py), not C++. The campaign census had counted it from source/blender/editors/space_node/*.cc, where it appears only as a string inside a WM_operatortype_find lookup -- the R1587.1 class a third time, a name-matching census attributing an operator to a module that merely mentions it.

Round 1598.1.decision_summary: The closing audit of R1598, which found three things and fixed all three. First: `Swapped::discarded`'s doc said "with what they were" and the field was a bare `Vec<PortRef>` -- a doc promising what the type does not do, which is the class this project keeps recording as "a documented prescription is also audit material". It carries the value now (`Vec<(PortRef, K::Value)>`), and that is the better answer anyway: the swap has already happened, so "port in1 lost something" leaves a caller nothing to show or to put back while "port in1 lost 0.5" does. Second: the port correspondence was below the reference on one case. Blender scans for the FIRST COMPATIBLE socket when the old node is a `NodeReroute`, and this had only name-then-position, so a lone port whose type fits a port that is not at its own index was dropped where Blender keeps it. A third pass adds it, gated on the side having exactly ONE port -- a lone port has no position worth preserving and no name that means anything beside a name it is the only one of, so "wherever it fits" is honest rather than a guess. Blender gates the same behaviour on `bl_idname == "NodeReroute"`, so there it is one node TYPE's privilege; here it falls out of the arity and every single-port kind gets it. Third: `r1598_a_lone_port_lands_wherever_it_fits`'s own second half admitted in a comment that the taxonomy had no shape to test it with, so it asserted nothing about the pass it was named for; `Op::Stamp` ((Count: Number, Body: Text) -> Text) is that shape, and the test now drives it.
changes_bullets: Swapped::discarded carries the value, not just the address. The wire form is `in1=#010203` rather than `in1`.
A third correspondence pass for a side with exactly one port: the first port that will take it. Derived from the ARITY where Blender gates it on a node type.
Op::Stamp in the crate's test taxonomy -- (Count: Number, Body: Text) -> Text, the shape that makes the lone-port pass falsifiable.

Round 1598.2.decision_summary: Seven pre-existing demos asserted the contracts R1597 changed, and the stop-the-line push gate caught it -- which is the round's finding about process, not about the node graph. R1597 fixed the unit tests and did not compute the blast radius over the DEMOS, even though every one of those seven drives the node editor and the round changed what four of its verbs mean. The lesson R1582 already wrote down ("a gate, not prose") was followed for the crates a round touches and not for the demos a round's CONTRACT changes, which is a different axis: `cargo test -p <changed>` cannot see a Python script asserting over the wire.
changes_bullets: r1227_node_comment_frames / r1234_node_frame_move_resize: a frame is a node, so it mints from the node counter -- every hardcoded frame id becomes the id `add_frame` answered. r1234 additionally states the new membership contract: a resize changes the box and NOT what the frame holds, and `attach` is the act that joins, which is the exact opposite of what it asserted before.

r1236_node_dissolve: `dissolvable` widened from a shape test to losslessness. A Multiply is now lossless (its output routes from input 0) and a SOURCE is the lossy one; the demo reads `dissolve_severs`, then runs the dissolve and asserts exactly the named wire went.

r1255_node_eval / r1260_node_debugger_reads: a cycle can no longer be AUTHORED, and r1260 records the stronger fact -- it cannot be LOADED either, because `set_graph` runs validate. So this editor can never hold a cyclic graph, where before it accepted the wire and detected the cycle afterwards. The localisation itself is proven where a peer's document can be constructed: the crate's tests and the example's.

r1258_node_set_graph_validation: three of the violations it drove are now unrepresentable (a per-node port list, a duplicate id, a counter behind its ids), so the demo asserts their ABSENCE from the blob and drives two a peer can still send -- a dangling endpoint and a node claiming a parent that is not there, the second of which the editor's own checker never had.

Round 1599.decision_summary: The graph says WHEN, not only what. A node graph has two kinds of edge and this crate had one: a value link says what a node is built out of, a control link says what runs next, and they are not variations on each other -- they obey OPPOSITE laws. Port::flow is the one declaration (Flow::Value{ty,default} | Flow::Control), and the way it was introduced is the method: the field's TYPE changed rather than gaining a neighbour, so the COMPILER enumerated all 36 sites that had to decide about control, instead of a grep doing it. That choice is the round's own defence against the failure debt-blender-census-by-field-name records four times over, and it is also why a control port has no type and no resting value structurally rather than by convention -- there is no field in Flow::Control to put one in, where Unreal spells exec-ness as the STRING "exec" occupying the pin's type slot. The laws INVERT by flow, in one 2x2 derivation replacing four hard-coded checks: a value input takes one producer and a control output takes one successor (a value has one def and many uses; a control transfer has one successor and many predecessors -- SSA's duality, and why a CFG has join points where a dataflow graph has fan-out); and a cycle through value links is a contradiction while a cycle through control links is a LOOP, so connect refuses the first and ACCEPTS the second, validate calls it no violation, and Document::control_loops names its members statically. Document::run then derives the execution order from the control plane while data is pulled through the value plane exactly as before, on a stack, so a fork runs each arm TO COMPLETION before the next.
changes_bullets: NodeKind::control is one provided method and its default is a BEHAVIOUR rather than a silence -- fall through every control output in port order -- which is what R1594's audit ("a third extension point would be worth resisting") is answered with: a node with one control output writes nothing, and a node with SEVERAL writes nothing either, because that is already a sequence. Unreal needs a UK2Node_ExecutionSequence class plus an FKCHandler_ExecutionSequence compile handler for the same behaviour, and that handler finds its own output pins by testing whether each pin NAME starts with the string "Then", under the standing admission //@TODO: Sort the pins by the number appended to the pin! -- so there the order control leaves a Sequence by is the order the pins happen to sit in the array, and the node's own author noted it is not the order the user reads off the screen. Here the order IS the port order, because that is the only order a signature has, and renaming a port cannot change it.

PAST UNREAL 5.8.1, measured against ~/UnrealEngine rather than remembered. Exec-ness is a string comparison written out 40 times outside the IsExecPin helper that exists for it, so a site that forgets is not a compile error. A control loop COMPILES there -- FKismetCompilerContext::PinIsImportantForDependancies returns PinCategory != PC_Exec, commented "the execution wires do not form data dependencies, they are only important for final scheduling and that is handled thru gotos" -- and a runaway one is discovered at RUN time, in a shipped build, by counting to GMaximumScriptLoopIterations and raising EBlueprintExceptionType::InfiniteLoop; here the loop's members are named before anything runs. Its DATA cycle report is per NODE (every node on the cycle and every node downstream of it) under its own //@TODO: Probably want to determine the actual pin that caused the cycle. And CONNECT_RESPONSE_BREAK_OTHERS displaces a link while TryCreateConnection answers a bare bool, so what it broke is gone; Connected::displaced names it, which is what makes either replacement undoable.

crossing() is the ONE question every derivation asks about a pair of ports, unifying the flow check with R1593's directed type relation -- control into control is Direct with nothing asked of the taxonomy, value into value defers, and the two never mix. It was FOUND by a counterfactual that passed: removing the mixed arm from crossing left connect's refusal intact, because connect had been stating the mixed-flow rule itself. That is one rule with two statements, so connect now derives its refusal from crossing and only NAMES which of the two it was, with the unreachable fourth case asserted rather than reasoned. The same unification is what makes bypass carry control through a bypassed node for free (R1586's rule was already "the identity as far as the signature allows", and the signature now includes the flow) and what makes a swap carry a control wire across (R1598's correspondence takes PORTS now, not their types, because a control port has none to hand it). Violation::OverfedInput becomes Violation::Overlinked{socket, side}, named for the rule rather than for the one side that used to be its only case.

Closes debt-persisted-schema-bump-is-prose-only, and this round is the one that would have fallen into it: Port's serialized shape changed, so every document holding a group definition changed with it. pinion_core::test_fixtures::assert_persisted_shape holds an append-only (version, digest) ledger whose four assertions leave no way out -- today's digest must equal the last entry's, the last entry's version must equal the live constant, no version may repeat, and no digest may repeat -- so changing a shape can only go green again by appending a pair whose version nobody has used, which IS the bump. The digest is FNV-1a rather than DefaultHasher, which is explicitly not stable across releases and would have rotted silently. The gate has its own counterfactual proving each of the four goes red, and the round then found two more copies of the version living as literals (a unit test and tools/demos/r1227_node_comment_frames.py, the latter caught by the demo blast radius rather than by any crate test) and removed both.

Round 1599.publishable_decision_summary: The graph says WHEN, not only what. A node graph has two kinds of edge and this crate had one: a value link says what a node is built out of, a control link says what runs next, and they are not variations on each other -- they obey OPPOSITE laws. Port::flow is the one declaration (Flow::Value{ty,default} | Flow::Control), and the way it was introduced is the method: the field's TYPE changed rather than gaining a neighbour, so the COMPILER enumerated all 36 sites that had to decide about control, instead of a grep doing it. That choice is the round's own defence against the failure debt-blender-census-by-field-name records four times over, and it is also why a control port has no type and no resting value structurally rather than by convention -- there is no field in Flow::Control to put one in, where Unreal spells exec-ness as the STRING "exec" occupying the pin's type slot. The laws INVERT by flow, in one 2x2 derivation replacing four hard-coded checks: a value input takes one producer and a control output takes one successor (a value has one def and many uses; a control transfer has one successor and many predecessors -- SSA's duality, and why a CFG has join points where a dataflow graph has fan-out); and a cycle through value links is a contradiction while a cycle through control links is a LOOP, so connect refuses the first and ACCEPTS the second, validate calls it no violation, and Document::control_loops names its members statically. Document::run then derives the execution order from the control plane while data is pulled through the value plane exactly as before, on a stack, so a fork runs each arm TO COMPLETION before the next.
publishable_changes_bullets: NodeKind::control is one provided method and its default is a BEHAVIOUR rather than a silence -- fall through every control output in port order -- which is what R1594's audit ("a third extension point would be worth resisting") is answered with: a node with one control output writes nothing, and a node with SEVERAL writes nothing either, because that is already a sequence. Unreal needs a UK2Node_ExecutionSequence class plus an FKCHandler_ExecutionSequence compile handler for the same behaviour, and that handler finds its own output pins by testing whether each pin NAME starts with the string "Then", under the standing admission //@TODO: Sort the pins by the number appended to the pin! -- so there the order control leaves a Sequence by is the order the pins happen to sit in the array, and the node's own author noted it is not the order the user reads off the screen. Here the order IS the port order, because that is the only order a signature has, and renaming a port cannot change it.

PAST UNREAL 5.8.1, measured against ~/UnrealEngine rather than remembered. Exec-ness is a string comparison written out 40 times outside the IsExecPin helper that exists for it, so a site that forgets is not a compile error. A control loop COMPILES there -- FKismetCompilerContext::PinIsImportantForDependancies returns PinCategory != PC_Exec, commented "the execution wires do not form data dependencies, they are only important for final scheduling and that is handled thru gotos" -- and a runaway one is discovered at RUN time, in a shipped build, by counting to GMaximumScriptLoopIterations and raising EBlueprintExceptionType::InfiniteLoop; here the loop's members are named before anything runs. Its DATA cycle report is per NODE (every node on the cycle and every node downstream of it) under its own //@TODO: Probably want to determine the actual pin that caused the cycle. And CONNECT_RESPONSE_BREAK_OTHERS displaces a link while TryCreateConnection answers a bare bool, so what it broke is gone; Connected::displaced names it, which is what makes either replacement undoable.

crossing() is the ONE question every derivation asks about a pair of ports, unifying the flow check with R1593's directed type relation -- control into control is Direct with nothing asked of the taxonomy, value into value defers, and the two never mix. It was FOUND by a counterfactual that passed: removing the mixed arm from crossing left connect's refusal intact, because connect had been stating the mixed-flow rule itself. That is one rule with two statements, so connect now derives its refusal from crossing and only NAMES which of the two it was, with the unreachable fourth case asserted rather than reasoned. The same unification is what makes bypass carry control through a bypassed node for free (R1586's rule was already "the identity as far as the signature allows", and the signature now includes the flow) and what makes a swap carry a control wire across (R1598's correspondence takes PORTS now, not their types, because a control port has none to hand it). Violation::OverfedInput becomes Violation::Overlinked{socket, side}, named for the rule rather than for the one side that used to be its only case.

The digest is FNV-1a rather than DefaultHasher, which is explicitly not stable across releases and would have rotted silently. Round 1600.decision_summary: a graph that REMEMBERS, per instance: NodeBody::Delay plus Machine / tick / settle, and Document::run finally descends into a group instance. These are the two halves R1599 named as remaining and they are ONE subject, because the INSTANCE is the address both need. R1599 made a control loop authorable and recorded why it could not yet mean anything: NodeKind::evaluate is a pure function of the resolved inputs, so a node that ran twice computed the same thing twice. What a second pass needs is a value one step behind (SSA phi at a loop header, Lustre pre, Simulink unit delay), and this crate owns it rather than the taxonomy for a STRUCTURAL reason an application cannot argue with: evaluate(and self, inputs) has nowhere to put a register, so a taxonomy trying to supply one would have to reach outside itself and one that forgot would have no loops at all. Everything follows from two facts. (1) A delay output this step is not a function of its input this step, so it CUTS the dependency graph, which IS Lustre causality ("every cycle must be broken by a pre") reached as ONE predicate (cuts_dependency) that connect, cycle_nodes, data_path_between and validate all read, so they cannot disagree about which cycles are legal; set_bypassed refuses to bypass a delay a cycle runs through and names the path, because a bypassed delay is a plain wire and that is the same illegal state reached by taking the cut away instead of adding the wire, and validate reports it for a document that arrived from a file. (2) The register belongs to an INSTANCE, the same key the evaluator memo has used since R1577, and that is exactly why control can descend now: entering a group means resolving its interior against THIS instance inputs, which R1599 recorded as the mechanical blocker (Evaluator per-instance descent was private and had to be SHARED, not duplicated). Descent is a call stack with a return address per level; a group instance takes no turn of its own, and entering one shows as the first Step inside it whose Step::instance names it. SIMULTANEITY IS ENFORCED BY THE BORROW CHECKER rather than by convention: tick holds the machine by mutable reference and the evaluator borrows it immutably, so no register can be written while another is being read. Two mutually-delayed registers therefore SWAP, where a sequential update gives both the same value, asserted against the rejected design ACTUALLY RUNNING (built from the real evaluator plus Machine::force) rather than described. Past Blender 6.x at 8cf50599: its Repeat Zone UNROLLS (geometry_nodes_repeat_zone.cc, "the graph is built with as many body copies as there are iterations. Since this graph depends on the number of iterations, it cannot be reused in general"), so the count must be known before the graph is built, a data-dependent exit is inexpressible, and memory scales with iterations, where fifty iterations here leave the graph the same size and cost one register; and its simulation state is keyed by a flattened bNestedNodeRef id persisted in the .blend, a side table that must be kept in step with the tree and one of whose fields its own comment describes as unused half the time, where the address here is derived by the walk that needs it and stored nowhere. Past Unreal 5.8.1: state there is a Blueprint VARIABLE written by an execution wire, so which value a read sees depends on where control went and the graph meaning is not a function of the graph; and a macro instance is not an instance at all, since FKismetCompilerContext expands one via FEdGraphUtilities::CloneGraph so N uses are N copies before anything runs. That is why FindMacroCycle has to exist there, and its defect matters: it RETURNS on its first macro-instance child instead of continuing the loop, so a cycle reachable only through the second child is never looked for. Held as a test helper and asserted to MISS a cycle Document::containment finds and names. Counterfactuals: 12, all caught after two repairs, and both repairs are findings. CF-2 PASSED first time and that is the round own discovery: every fixture wired its feedback delay-first, where the walk own cut already answers, so connect check that the NEW link adds a dependency at all was untested; a consumer-first fixture is now r1600_a_wire_leaving_a_delay_can_never_close_a_cycle. Then rustfmt reflowed that same line and the driver reported NOT-APPLIED rather than PASS, which is exactly the R1594 failure the property exists to catch. The Machine wire form was decided by a FAILING TEST rather than by reading the derive: a BTreeMap keyed by (Instance, NodeId) is not expressible as JSON at all, so registers travel as ROWS carrying their own address, which is the Node wire-form argument one level down. 237 crate tests, 10 binding tests, one RPC demo with 44 assertions.
changes_bullets: NodeBody::Delay(K::Type) is the fifth structural body, and the reason this crate owns it is structural rather than stylistic: NodeKind::evaluate takes a shared self and returns values, which is the purity that makes Document::evaluate safe after an arbitrary edit, so there is nowhere in the trait to put a register. Its signature is DERIVED from the type it holds (one in, one out, both that type), so a delay cannot narrow or widen what passes through it; its INITIAL value is R1594's per-node authored value on its own output port, which is Lustre's arrow and needed no new mechanism at all; and set_kind refuses it by name (EditError::NotAKind, widened) because taking a cut out of the data plane is not a rename. Document::delays enumerates them, where Blender's simulation cache is a private Map on the modifier with no accessor that walks it.

Machine holds one value per delay per Instance plus the tick count, and holds NO reference to a document, so a scenario is saveable, restorable, comparable and sendable. Document::tick advances every register at ONE instant and reports what moved (Committed carries before and after, so Tick::changed answers "is this a fixed point" for the whole machine rather than per node); Document::settle runs to that fixed point or to a stated budget, where the last tick still moving IS "did not converge". A tick is also the AUTHORITY on which registers exist: anything the walk did not reach is dropped and NAMED (Tick::dropped), so a machine cannot grow across an editing session, and that is withheld when the walk was truncated because an incomplete walk is not evidence of absence. Machine::force is the debugger's verb, named for stepping outside the tick discipline rather than for setting a value.

Document::run descends into a group instance and RunError::ControlEntersGroup is gone. The tunnel is derived rather than declared: a group's control ports are interface ports whose flow is Control, so entering at the instance's control input i continues at the definition's inside-input node output i, and reaching the inside-output node at input i resumes in the caller at the instance's output i. The walk is a call stack, each level holding the Descent it reads through and the return address it came in by; Descent and Evaluator::enter are the shared per-instance derivation R1599 named as the blocker, made public rather than duplicated. Step gains an instance, so two runs through one definition are two sets of steps; Run::visited, visits_in and entered are the readings that need it, and the flattened Run::visits is kept and DOCUMENTED as flattening, with a test asserting that it collides ids across trees. Two refusals are new and both are named rather than silent: EntryIsAnInstance (control enters a group by a port, so a run beginning there arrived by none) and GroupHasNoEntry (a tunnel with nothing on the far side, which a silent halt would have made look like a finished run).

hello-node-flow is the composition and it now needs both halves: its loop exits only when a register carries the elapsed count past a limit authored on the node that reads it, and arm 1 -- a group instance control descends into -- is reachable only once arm 0 completes. The wire gains ticks, registers, delays, trace_instances, entered, at_fixed_point and ticks_to_finish, plus tick, settle, force and rewind. ticks_to_finish answers "how many more ticks until this scenario halts" WITHOUT taking them, by ticking a copy, which is a capability of the machine being a value. The composite address on the wire is instance-at-node, and the separator was added because reading the wire showed instance /0:10 followed by node 6 printing as /0:106, which is also what instance /0:106 would print.
verification_bullets: 237 pinion-node-graph tests green, of which 219 predate this round and none changed their expectations except the one R1599 wrote for the refusal this round removes, which now asserts the descent instead. Plus 10 hello-node-flow, 255 hello-node-editor, 16 hello-node-groups, and the crate doc test. cargo fmt clean; clippy pedantic-deny clean on all four; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items clean.

tools/demos/r1600_a_graph_remembers_per_instance.py PASS, 44 assertions over the live wire in seven sections: the register enumerable and its derived signature, the group interface carrying control, the cycle legal through the register and REFUSED around it with the path named, four runs leaving the clock where it was against one tick moving it, the trace changing with no edit at all, halting and converging asserted as different questions, the descent with its three steps inside and the flattened reading colliding with a root node of the same id, forcing a register and the scenario jumping to its end with zero ticks, and a refused bypass leaving both the document and the machine alone.

Counterfactuals: 12, 12/12 caught, and TWO of them were findings about the verification rather than the code. CF-2 PASSED because every fixture in the crate wired its feedback delay-first, where the dependency walk's own cut already answers, so connect's separate check that the NEW link adds a dependency was untested; the consumer-first fixture is now r1600_a_wire_leaving_a_delay_can_never_close_a_cycle. Then cargo fmt reflowed that very line and the re-run reported NOT-APPLIED rather than PASS, which is exactly the R1594 failure mode. The blast radius was computed rather than remembered (tools/blast_radius.py names four packages) and running it with --all-targets found two example test targets that a plain workspace build had not: the R1600 arm made two matches in hello-node-groups non-exhaustive.
carry_forward_bullets: A run does not advance the clock and a tick does, so a control loop spins within one instant and the world moves between instants. That is Simulink's own division of labour between a step's sorted execution order and its unit delays, and it is what keeps a tick's outcome a function of the document and the registers rather than of the walk -- but it means a loop cannot count WITHIN one run, and a scenario that iterates does so by alternating run and tick. The alternative (a register advancing when control passes through its scope, which is SCADE's rule for a pre inside a state) would make the state a function of the control walk and is deliberately not taken.

Simultaneity has no one-line counterfactual, and that is the strongest available form of the claim rather than a gap: tick holds the machine mutably and the evaluator borrows it immutably, so a sequential update is not an edit away, it is a restructure. It is asserted instead against the rejected design ACTUALLY RUNNING, built from the real evaluator plus Machine::force. Also stated: mutable node state beyond a delay is deliberately absent (the whole point of the limit), a definition instantiated in a diamond has one register per instance which is correct and can be exponential in pathological nesting, and the campaign's operator census still leaves find_node and insert_offset plus three application gestures.

A tick is also the AUTHORITY on which registers exist: anything the walk did not reach is dropped and NAMED (Tick::dropped), so a machine cannot grow across an editing session, and that is withheld when the walk was truncated because an incomplete walk is not evidence of absence. Machine::force is the debugger's verb, named for stepping outside the tick discipline rather than for setting a value.

Document::run descends into a group instance and RunError::ControlEntersGroup is gone. The tunnel is derived rather than declared: a group's control ports are interface ports whose flow is Control, so entering at the instance's control input i continues at the definition's inside-input node output i, and reaching the inside-output node at input i resumes in the caller at the instance's output i. The walk is a call stack, each level holding the Descent it reads through and the return address it came in by; Descent and Evaluator::enter are the shared per-instance derivation R1599 named as the blocker, made public rather than duplicated. Step gains an instance, so two runs through one definition are two sets of steps; Run::visited, visits_in and entered are the readings that need it, and the flattened Run::visits is kept and DOCUMENTED as flattening, with a test asserting that it collides ids across trees. Two refusals are new and both are named rather than silent: EntryIsAnInstance (control enters a group by a port, so a run beginning there arrived by none) and GroupHasNoEntry (a tunnel with nothing on the far side, which a silent halt would have made look like a finished run).

hello-node-flow is the composition and it now needs both halves: its loop exits only when a register carries the elapsed count past a limit authored on the node that reads it, and arm 1 -- a group instance control descends into -- is reachable only once arm 0 completes. The wire gains ticks, registers, delays, trace_instances, entered, at_fixed_point and ticks_to_finish, plus tick, settle, force and rewind. ticks_to_finish answers "how many more ticks until this scenario halts" WITHOUT taking them, by ticking a copy, which is a capability of the machine being a value. The composite address on the wire is instance-at-node, and the separator was added because reading the wire showed instance /0:10 followed by node 6 printing as /0:106, which is also what instance /0:106 would print.

Round 1601.decision_summary: The reference census is a TOOL, and it withdrew its own number. MEASURED: Blender registers node operators FOUR ways -- ot->idname 75, WM_operatortype_append_macro 11, Python core under scripts/startup 27, Python addon 23, total 136 -- and the old census saw one of them. It MISSED 25 core operators, every Python one, including the ENTIRE ZONE FAMILY (add_zone, add_simulation_zone, add_repeat_zone, add_foreach_geometry_element_zone, add_closure_zone, swap_zone) and six interface_item_* operators; the zone family is the reference's own state-and-loop mechanism, which is precisely R1600's subject, and it was reading as zero. Round 1601.1.decision_summary: Forcing a register is checked by the thing that knows the document. R1600 shipped Machine::force with a doc claiming that a mistyped forced value would be reported by Document::validate in exactly the way an authored one is. That is FALSE and the audit for this round's close found it: validate reads a DOCUMENT, and a forced value lives in a Machine that deliberately holds no reference to one, so nothing could report it. The fix is not to correct the sentence but to move the operation: a machine cannot know that a node is a delay or what type that delay holds, and the document can, so the check lives on the document. Document::force answers ForceError::NoSuchInstance / NoSuchNode / NotARegister / WrongType, and the type leg is R1594's own gate, so a taxonomy that declines to classify its values is not held to a rule it cannot state. It also closes a smaller hole R1600's own Descent doc had asserted away: an Instance is public, so a caller CAN build a path the document does not have, and Document::tree_of is the one place a hand-built path is now checked. The consumer's hand-rolled 'is this a register' guard goes with it -- a second statement of a rule the framework now owns.

The type gate is R1594's own, so a taxonomy that declines to classify its values is not held to a rule it cannot state.

Document::tree_of is the one place an Instance built by hand is checked against the document. An Instance is public (root / inside), so a caller can assemble a path the document does not have; a Descent's instance is built by the walk and cannot be wrong, and R1600's Descent doc had claimed that property for instances generally.
hello-node-flow drops its hand-rolled "is this node a register" check, which was a second statement of a rule the framework now owns.
