Round 1602.decision_summary: A census verdict is PROVEN BY A TEST. R1601 made the reference census a tool, and what a tool of that shape proves is COMPLETENESS -- no upstream operator is silently absorbed into a percentage. It proves nothing whatever about whether a verdict is TRUE, and the 214 judgements in docs/reference-census.json were one session's hand reading. The two error directions are not symmetric, which is what makes that dangerous: a wrong `absent` puts a fake item on the gap list and the next round discovers it by trying to close it, so it self-corrects; a wrong `have` INFLATES THE COVERAGE NUMBER AND NOBODY TRIPS OVER IT. That is exactly the direction R1601 itself had to correct, 93% down to 78%. So every `have` row now carries `proven_by`, addressed <crate>::<test>, and 67 proofs land: 61 in crates/pinion-node-graph/tests/reference_census.rs and 3 in crates/pinion-core/tests/reference_census.rs -- the region-select trio, whose capability R1590 measured as belonging to the painted surface rather than to a node model, which is why a proof is addressed by CRATE rather than by a bare name. Each proof reaches the capability through the PUBLIC API only, the position an application is in, and asserts an outcome that would differ if the capability were missing; measured by isolation, each of four broken mechanisms fails exactly the census proofs resting on it and no others. THE CHECK IS TWO HALVES THAT NEED EACH OTHER: reference_census.py --check-pin resolves the address to a census file that exists, which is a question about paths, so no Rust is parsed and the census-over-text failure this whole tool exists to stop is not reintroduced; and each crate's own census file asserts a BIJECTION between the pin rows addressed to it and the proofs it holds, where the compiler is the one reading. Together, a `have` cannot be added without a test, a proof cannot be deleted or renamed without the pin noticing, and a verdict that leaves the numerator may not keep its evidence. The verdicts most worth doubting were named in the debt and they were the COMPOSITION claims -- "call expose again", "there is nothing to sync", "disconnect covers break-node-links" -- because a composition is a HYPOTHESIS UNTIL IT IS RUN, which R1571 already learned by building R1555's written prescription and finding it harmful. All of them hold, and writing them out produced two facts the pin could not have stated: a Socket names a port INDEX and takes its side from which end of the Link it sits on, so "break this pin's links" must choose an end and a filter that ignores the end matches twice; and Unreal's HideNoConnectionNoDefaultPins is a filter over the published hidden set crossed with the signature's declared defaults, not a second appearance flag, so the crate supplies the parts and the narrower rule is the application's. THE SHAPE OF THE BINDING WAS CHOSEN BY A COUNTERFACTUAL, not by reasoning. The first draft stored a bare fn() pointer beside each row, and CF-2 -- rename a proof -- was NOT CAUGHT: the bijection compared operator names on both sides and the derived name against the pin, so the function's own identifier was never in the comparison at all, and `proven_by` was free to name a test that no longer existed. The fix is a generic proof() helper whose type parameter is the function's ITEM type, so type_name_of_val answers with its path: the identifier is written once, at the call site, and the string it is checked against comes from the compiler. This closes axis 1 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed. Axis 2 -- the Unreal census is ONE header, so 39% is a lower bound -- stays open and is R1603, and the finding this round adds to it is that the second source is not more of the same unit: UEdGraphSchema's virtuals are the axis an OPERATOR census is structurally blind to, and R1593's implicit conversion and R1594's per-socket default value are both on it, both read as zero, and both were prerequisites.

The verdicts most worth doubting were named in the debt and they were the COMPOSITION claims -- "call expose again", "there is nothing to sync", "disconnect covers break-node-links" -- because a composition is a HYPOTHESIS UNTIL IT IS RUN, which R1571 already learned by building R1555's written prescription and finding it harmful. All of them hold, and writing them out produced two facts the pin could not have stated: a Socket names a port INDEX and takes its side from which end of the Link it sits on, so "break this pin's links" must choose an end and a filter that ignores the end matches twice; and Unreal's HideNoConnectionNoDefaultPins is a filter over the published hidden set crossed with the signature's declared defaults, not a second appearance flag, so the crate supplies the parts and the narrower rule is the application's. THE SHAPE OF THE BINDING WAS CHOSEN BY A COUNTERFACTUAL, not by reasoning. The first draft stored a bare fn() pointer beside each row, and CF-2 -- rename a proof -- was NOT CAUGHT: the bijection compared operator names on both sides and the derived name against the pin, so the function's own identifier was never in the comparison at all, and `proven_by` was free to name a test that no longer existed. The fix is a generic proof() helper whose type parameter is the function's ITEM type, so type_name_of_val answers with its path: the identifier is written once, at the call site, and the string it is checked against comes from the compiler. This closes axis 1 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed. Axis 2 -- the Unreal census is ONE header, so 39% is a lower bound -- stays open and is R1603, and the finding this round adds to it is that the second source is not more of the same unit: UEdGraphSchema's virtuals are the axis an OPERATOR census is structurally blind to, and R1593's implicit conversion and R1594's per-socket default value are both on it, both read as zero, and both were prerequisites.

Round 1603.decision_summary: The census grows the surface it was BLIND to, on both references. R1601 measured what Blender and Unreal let a user INVOKE and R1602 made each of those verdicts cost a test, and both rested on an assumption neither examined: that a reference has one list of things it can do. It does not, and the evidence was already in this campaign's own history. R1593 (a link may CONVERT) and R1594 (a value is authored on a SOCKET) each closed something a node substrate cannot host a material or a Blueprint graph without -- prerequisites rather than polish -- and both are UEdGraphSchema virtuals in Unreal (CreateAutomaticConversionNodeAndConnections, TrySetDefaultValue) and bNodeType / bNodeTreeType callbacks in Blender. Neither is an operator. So the operator census read both as ZERO, and every completion judged on top of it was overstated by exactly the amount nobody could see. That is not incompleteness, it is BLINDNESS: an incomplete census undercounts within an axis it can see, and this one could not see the axis. tools/reference_census.py now enumerates a HOOK surface on both trees -- Blender's bNodeType 20 + bNodeTreeType 7 + bNodeSocketType 7 out of BKE_node.hh, brace-counted rather than regex-scoped because a struct's extent is a nesting question and a regex answering one is how a census acquires a hole; Unreal's UEdGraphNode 82 + UEdGraphSchema 115 -- and coverage is reported PER SURFACE, because a single denominator would let a fat surface hide a starved one, which is the same error as counting a macro. 231 new rows are judged. Blender 54/72 = 75% (operator 78%, hook 62%); Unreal 60/149 = 40% (command 39%, hook 40%). R1601 had named its 78 a floor and it was: the widened Unreal number lands beside it rather than below it, which is worth recording because the fear was that it would fall. Every have on the new surface is PROVEN under R1602's rule: 35 new proofs, taking crates/pinion-node-graph/tests/reference_census.rs to 98 tests, each exercising the capability through the PUBLIC API alone. THE BIJECTION BECAME A WEAKER RELATION ON PURPOSE, and that is a finding rather than a concession. One pinion mechanism often answers SEVERAL reference rows: Blender's bNodeTreeType::localize and Unreal's UEdGraphSchema::DuplicateGraph are one Document::fork_definition; NODE_OT_delete and SafeDeleteNodeFromGraph are one remove_node; TrySetDefaultValue and TrySetDefaultText are one set_port_value, because the value is the taxonomy's own and needs no per-type setter. So a proof now has exactly one OWNER -- the row its name derives from, checked against the name the compiler reads off the function -- and may be CITED by any number of other rows, and the fan-out is asserted to be non-zero. That turns "the reference writes it three times and this derives it once" from a sentence R1589 wrote by hand into a measurement the test suite maintains. One new verdict arm, host-framework, for the 20 rows that are UObject or DNA/RNA lifecycle rather than node-system decisions; every out-of-denominator class still states its reason and the selftest asserts the set. THE JUDGING RULE WAS STATED BEFORE IT WAS APPLIED, and it follows from R1602's asymmetry: when unsure, prefer absent, because a wrong absent is self-correcting (the next round finds it by trying to close it) and a wrong have inflates the number in silence. What the new surface NAMES that no operator list could reach: a KIND cannot contribute a rule to Document::validate, so the standing check is the crate's alone; a node has no WARNING state a kind attaches to itself; a port has no description beside its name; there is no per-graph refusal of a node kind, because a Document is one tree kind; there are no CONTAINER socket types; and there is no relinking of an existing wire's end. Counterfactuals 5 of 5 caught, the sharpest being a surface DROPPED from the census: the tool reports its own pinned rows as GONE rather than quietly shrinking the denominator, which is the property that makes a census safe to extend. This closes axis 2 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed, and with it the whole debt.

Round 1603.1.decision_summary: The two demos R1600 and R1601.1 left red are repaired, and CI is the thing that found it. R1600 changed hello-node-flow's SEED -- a register, a second task and a group, so drain moved into a definition and every node id after branch shifted -- and updated its own demo without updating r1599's, which mirrors the same fixture. R1601.1 then moved the force check from Machine to Document, so ForceError names the tree, and updated the example and the example's tests without updating r1600's demo. Both are the same failure: a demo asserts over the WIRE, so what broke it was a fixture's node ids and a framework's sentence, and neither is a thing the compiler or a crate-level blast radius can see. Every expectation here was RE-DERIVED by probing the live binary rather than read off the source -- the demo's own header says it mirrors the seed rather than importing it, precisely so a change to the fixture is caught, and reading the fixture back out to fix it would have thrown that away. Two claims moved rather than being renumbered. The join in section G was asserted on Branch.False, which is now the loop wire, so re-wiring it DISPLACES (a control output takes one successor) instead of joining; the free control output in the new seed is Task settle's, and joining that onto Finish's already-fed control input demonstrates the same rule -- measured, Finish then runs more than once down different paths. And section E's set_reading now converts the condition node itself, which SEVERS the wire that fed it, because a Reading has no inputs: that is set_kind reporting what did not survive rather than dropping it, so the round asserts the severed wire as a fact of its own and resets before F. The recurrence is recorded on debt-local-gate-misses-example-tests, whose own text already said "the crates a round touched" means "the crates whose BEHAVIOUR changed, consumers included" and did not say that a demo is one of those consumers. The gate's unit is a package and a demo is not a package; the mapping that would close it is the binary name each demo opens with RpcSubprocess, taken with a parser rather than a substring.

Round 1604.decision_summary: The Advanced DCC axis is re-judged DOWN, 98 -> 86, and it is the largest single move this table has had and the second downward one. The tool demanded it (round-axis 18 -> 23 = +28%, past the band) and it absorbs five rounds: R1599, R1600, R1601, R1602, R1603. TWO FORCES, POINTING OPPOSITE WAYS. Up: the item every judgment in this series has named as the cap is CLOSED. "Execution semantics -- control flow, iteration, side effects, time -- are inexpressible in evaluate(inputs) -> outputs, so the control plane is at zero" was the stated reason not to reach 99, three judgments running. R1599 gave a port a FLOW, so a graph has two kinds of edge whose laws invert, a control cycle is a LOOP rather than a contradiction, and Document::run derives an execution order from the control plane; R1600 gave it MEMORY -- NodeBody::Delay, a machine addressed by INSTANCE, tick and settle -- so a loop can compute something different on its second pass. That cap is gone. Down, and it dominates: for the first time this axis has a MEASURED, test-backed figure for its node-graph third, and it is far below what the 98 rested on, which was a hand census claiming 93%. R1601 made that census a tool and WITHDREW the number for a measured 78%. R1602 made every have verdict name a TEST that exercises the capability through the public API, so a verdict can no longer be a hand claim, and the shape of that binding was itself chosen by a counterfactual. R1603 then found the census was BLIND rather than incomplete -- R1593's implicit conversion and R1594's per-socket default value are UEdGraphSchema virtuals and bNodeType callbacks, not operators, so an operator census read two PREREQUISITES as zero -- and censused the hook surface on both references, reporting per surface because one denominator lets a fat surface hide a starved one. Measured: Blender 54/72 = 75% (operator 78, hook 62), Unreal 60/149 = 40% (command 39, hook 40). THE NODE-GRAPH FIGURE. This axis's own name is two references' worth of scope -- "visual scripting / material graph" -- so Blender at 75 and Unreal at 40 at equal weight give 57.5. Two stated biases push that up and neither is a measurement, so they buy a little and not a lot: R1603's judging rule was "when unsure prefer absent", which biases the number LOW by construction, and the absences CLUSTER, since Unreal's 89 are about eight distinct capabilities counted many times (alignment 11, variadic ports 6, struct pins 5, breakpoints 5, watches 2, relinking 3, per-node permissions 6, colour 5). Node graph lands at 62. The METHOD is unchanged on purpose -- the three families averaged, as every judgment in this series has done -- because changing the method and the inputs in one re-judgment would make the move unreadable: property grid ~98 and data grid ~98, neither having had a round since R1571, and node graph 97 -> 62, which averages 86. THE DROP IS NOT A REGRESSION. Nothing this axis had was lost. Three rounds built a meter and this is its first full reading, which is precisely the lesson R1519 built this table to record -- a completion nobody checked against a reference is not a measurement -- and precisely what R1577 recorded when the first census moved this same axis down. The consequence for the campaign is the point: DCC goes from LAST at 60 leverage to FIRST at 280, the widest any axis has carried here and three times the next, so the derived order now sends every round to the axis whose number just fell. The ledger row is declared `none` rather than `dcc`: a re-judgment advances no axis, and declaring the one it judged would let an axis credit itself for having been looked at.

Round 1604.1.decision_summary: The R1604 judgment record carries an addendum, because the figures it was judged against moved two commits later and the durable copy of them did not say so. R1605 widened both censuses and the correction was recorded in docs/SEED_PROMPT.md, which is .gitignore'd — a fresh clone does not have it, so the next demanded re-judgment would have read tools/phase_b_tally.py, found "Blender 54/72 = 75%", and computed from a number that is no longer true. That is the drift class this table was built to stop, one level in: the evidence_snapshot mechanism watches example and round COUNTS and has no opinion about a census figure quoted in prose beside them. It is an ADDENDUM and deliberately not a rewrite. R1604's paragraph is left standing because what a snapshot is for is saying what was known at the time; falsifying it to match today would destroy the only record of what the judgment actually rested on. THE TWO HALVES MOVED DIFFERENTLY and that is the part worth carrying. Unreal did NOT move -- 40% before and after, command 39% before and after, 20/51 -> 45/113 -- so reading eight command lists instead of one found that the generic canvas was REPRESENTATIVE, which is a result rather than the absence of one. Blender DID: 75% -> 71%, operator 78 -> 73, because the census had been reading C++ as text and a FIFTH registration mechanism was invisible to it -- NOD_socket_items_ops.hh registers 69 operator ids through four templates whose idnames live as static constexpr StringRefNull in a per-accessor struct, so no registration site writes ot->idname at all. Live 170 -> 246. The completion is NOT changed on that account. The tool did not demand a re-judgment (round-axis 23 -> 24 = +4%, inside the band), and moving a number on evidence the staleness check has not flagged is precisely the hand-adjustment this table exists to stop -- the discipline only means something when it also forbids the moves that would feel responsible. The inputs are recorded so the next demanded look starts from Blender 71 / Unreal 40. ★ And the direction is now a pattern worth naming rather than three coincidences: R1601, R1603 and R1605 each widened this measurement and each time the coverage FELL. Every widening so far has found more reference than it found pinion, which is the honest expectation to carry into the next one.

R1605 widened both censuses and the correction was recorded in docs/SEED_PROMPT.md, which is .gitignore'd — a fresh clone does not have it, so the next demanded re-judgment would have read tools/phase_b_tally.py, found "Blender 54/72 = 75%", and computed from a number that is no longer true. That is the drift class this table was built to stop, one level in: the evidence_snapshot mechanism watches example and round COUNTS and has no opinion about a census figure quoted in prose beside them. It is an ADDENDUM and deliberately not a rewrite. R1604's paragraph is left standing because what a snapshot is for is saying what was known at the time; falsifying it to match today would destroy the only record of what the judgment actually rested on. THE TWO HALVES MOVED DIFFERENTLY and that is the part worth carrying. Unreal did NOT move -- 40% before and after, command 39% before and after, 20/51 -> 45/113 -- so reading eight command lists instead of one found that the generic canvas was REPRESENTATIVE, which is a result rather than the absence of one. Blender DID: 75% -> 71%, operator 78 -> 73, because the census had been reading C++ as text and a FIFTH registration mechanism was invisible to it -- NOD_socket_items_ops.hh registers 69 operator ids through four templates whose idnames live as static constexpr StringRefNull in a per-accessor struct, so no registration site writes ot->idname at all. Live 170 -> 246. The completion is NOT changed on that account. The tool did not demand a re-judgment (round-axis 23 -> 24 = +4%, inside the band), and moving a number on evidence the staleness check has not flagged is precisely the hand-adjustment this table exists to stop -- the discipline only means something when it also forbids the moves that would feel responsible. The inputs are recorded so the next demanded look starts from Blender 71 / Unreal 40. ★ And the direction is now a pattern worth naming rather than three coincidences: R1601, R1603 and R1605 each widened this measurement and each time the coverage FELL. Every widening so far has found more reference than it found pinion, which is the honest expectation to carry into the next one.

Round 1605.decision_summary:
R1605 — the census reads every list a graph editor binds, and stops reading C++ as text.

Closes debt-census-surfaces-are-still-incomplete, all three axes.

AXIS 1 — the debt said three Unreal command lists were missing, and the real
answer was EIGHT, because the unit is the TCommands CLASS rather than the
header: BlueprintEditorCommands.h holds three classes and only one of them is
the graph's, BehaviorTreeEditorCommands.h holds three, and R1603's single list
happened to be one class per file so the difference was invisible. 152 rows
judged across the Blueprint, material, animation, sound-cue, sound-class and
three behaviour-tree lists. Scope is now DECLARED rather than assumed: every
TCommands class under Engine/Source/Editor (90) is either read by
UNREAL_COMMAND_CLASSES or excluded BY NAME in UNREAL_COMMANDS_OUT with a
reason, and one in neither is a finding — so the next list Epic adds cannot sit
quietly outside the denominator, which is the failure this round exists to stop
repeating. THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING: 20/51 = 39% became
45/113 = 39%, Unreal held at 40% overall, so the generic canvas was
representative of the whole — while the per-editor split is not (MaterialEditor
58, BlueprintEditor 38, BehaviorTreeDebugger 22, AnimGraph 16), which is why
coverage is now reported per MECHANISM under each surface as well as per
surface.

AXIS 2 — measured rather than argued, and the tool re-derives it every run. Of
36 GetNodeContextMenuActions overrides, 17 register a command from a TCommands
list, so they are the SAME unit as axis 1 and are in the denominator now that
the per-editor lists are read; 16 build an FUIAction on the spot, and those
entries have no name anywhere — no id, no binding, nothing to key a row on — so
they cannot be a census unit at all, and what they expose (add a pin, remove a
pin, convert this node) is already named on the command lists.

AXIS 3 — the hook verdicts stay with self-correction, per R1602's asymmetry,
except that two were settled by reading the call site: SoundCue's ToggleSolo
and ToggleMute reach the audio debugger's ToggleSoloSoundCue on the ASSET, so
they are app-content rather than the node bypass their names suggest.

THE BLENDER HALF IS THE LARGER CORRECTION, and it came from the user asking
whether reading C++ as text is good enough. It is not, and the way to answer
was to make the census account for EVERY NODE_OT_ token rather than find the
ones it knew how to find. That surfaced four things at once. (1) A FIFTH
registration mechanism: NOD_socket_items_ops.hh registers 69 operator ids
through four templates whose idnames live as static constexpr StringRefNull
members of a per-accessor operator_idnames struct, in source/blender/nodes
rather than editors/space_node, so NO registration site writes ot->idname at
all — and Blender's own comment beside the maker says the string is spelled out
"so that it is more searchable", meaning the reference anticipated a text
census and this one still missed it, because it accepted exactly one spelling.
(2) A receiver that is not called ot: NODE_OT_new_compositor_sequencer_node_group
writes operator_type->idname, which is debt-blender-census-by-field-name — a
census keyed on a VARIABLE name — recurring inside the tool built to end it.
(3) An id spelled __func__, which no text scan can read without knowing what
the compiler substitutes. (4) A registration FUNCTION whose symbol is not an
operator id at all: NODE_OT_collapse_toggle sets idname to
"NODE_OT_hide_toggle", so counting the symbol would have invented an operator.
Blender's live census goes 170 -> 246 and its coverage 75% -> 71% (operator 78%
-> 73%). The completeness claim is now COMPUTED: every token is an id, a
template constant, a registration function's symbol, or a string naming a
Python operator, and one in none of those is a finding — currently zero.
Comments are blanked before matching, newlines preserved so a brace count and a
line regex are unaffected.

A new verdict, instance, is composition in the other direction. R1601 added
composition because one macro registers under its own name and IS several
operators, so counting it as a gap invents one; instance is the mirror, because
69 ids that are four behaviours instantiated for twenty-three of Blender's own
node types would put ONE capability in the denominator sixty-nine times. Each
instance row names the row that carries the verdict, and that verdict is
absent: the capability is variadic ports — a node whose socket list is authored
per node rather than fixed by its kind — which is the same gap Unreal spells
AddOptionPin and RemoveOptionPin.

One new proof: unreal_material_editor_matertial_paste_here. Fragment stores
every node's position relative to the selection's centroid, so insert(at)
places the FRAGMENT and carries the relative layout untouched — a distinction
one node cannot show and three can, which is why the existing single-node paste
proof could not tell an anchor from a per-node override. Past Unreal 5.8: the
anchor is a value on the fragment (Fragment::origin), where Unreal's clipboard
is a text blob holding absolute positions and the averaging that turns it into
a paste location lives inside FBlueprintEditor::PasteNodesHere. The other 25
new have rows CITE proofs the generic canvas already owned, and that fan-out is
the measurement: eight editor-specific lists, 152 commands, and every
capability among them that this crate answers is answered by a mechanism
already named.

Counterfactuals 12/12 caught, and CF-6 earned its keep twice. It first PASSED
against an edit that was a no-op, because \s already spans a newline; fixing
the edit to genuinely forbid one showed that the scope check could not see a
class the parser STOPS RECOGNISING, since its input is the parser's own output
— a check fed by the parser cannot audit the parser. A second, deliberately
dumber reading of the base clause, which does not know the class's name, is now
the audit.

Round 1605.1.decision_summary:
R1605.1 — and Python has two string quotes.

The closing audit asked whether every debt this round produced was registered,
and found a DEFECT instead, in the same class as the four the round is about: a
census that accepts exactly one spelling. PY_IDNAME matched only double-quoted
literals, and node_wrangler writes bl_idname = 'node.nw_swap_links', so SIX
Blender operators were invisible. All six are addon operators, so the coverage
number does not move — but that is luck rather than a bound, because an operator
under scripts/startup/ written with single quotes would have left the DENOMINATOR
silently short, which is the direction that inflates. Blender's live census goes
246 -> 252 and the six are judged addon.

It also opened the Python side's own residue, which the C++ side had closed and
Python had not: a bl_idname whose value is not a quoted literal is unreadable by
ANY text census, because the name exists only after the module is imported.
blender_computed_idnames counts them and the report prints the number — 14 at the
pinned revision, all of them keying sets, addon preferences and key
configurations, no node operator among them. That is a fact about today's tree
rather than a property of the mechanism, so it is measured rather than assumed,
and debt-python-idname-can-be-computed records that nobody is yet watching it
grow.

Two counterfactuals, both CAUGHT: narrowing the quote class, and making every
value count as a literal so the residue reads zero.

The audit also registered debt-census-instance-owner-is-prose: R1605's new
`instance` verdict points at the row that carries the judgement IN PROSE, so if
that row is renamed or removed, 69 rows stay out of the denominator with nothing
judging them — one capability disappearing in silence, the same direction as a
wrong `have`. The fix is the same shape proven_by already uses (a field, checked
by --check-pin for existence and verdict), and it lands naturally with
debt-census-covered-by-is-unverified-prose's own prescription.

Round 1606.decision_summary: The geometry of a byte dump is a value. This is the analyzer-tool audit's plane-A gap, registered as debt-hex-view-is-an-example-not-a-crate three messages before it was built: a protocol inspector's window has two hard pieces and only one of them was in a crate. The detail tree is row_dissect, whose module doc calls itself Wireshark's packet-detail pane; the DUMP lived entirely inside examples/hello-hex-dump, so an application that wanted one had to copy 1,477 lines. Copying a renderer is a nuisance; copying a GEOMETRY is a fork, because the invariants go with it and then drift, and this project has already paid that exact bill once -- debt-two-node-graph-models, where the example held its own node model until R1597 closed it and only then discovered that frame membership had been a rectangle re-tested on every read. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A TYPE. A byte appears in two disjoint places, its two hex digits and its one ascii glyph, so a dump needs byte->cell to paint and cell->byte to hit-test, and the two must not be able to disagree. Before this module they were three hand-written functions that agreed by inspection, beside five hand-computed column constants -- ASCII_BAR_L = 60, ASCII_START = 61, ASCII_BAR_R = 77, TOTAL_COLS = 78, HEX_START = 10 -- that a person had derived once, on paper, from a 16-byte row split into two groups of 8. Widen the row and every one of those numbers is wrong with nothing to say so. HexLayout is now the declaration (bytes per row, bytes per group, offset digits, gutter) and every column is derived from it; region_at is the ONLY place that reads a cell, and hex_cell / ascii_cell are checked against it by a round-trip property over eight layouts including a group that does not divide the row, a row narrower than a group, and a short final row. Totality is asserted too: every cell inside the grid classifies, and each byte is claimed exactly three times. The test that the derivations reproduce all five paper constants EXACTLY is what makes the lift faithful rather than merely compiling. TWO THINGS PAST WHAT A HEX VIEW NORMALLY DOES, and Qt is not a floor here because it has no hex view at all -- no widget, no geometry -- so the existence is not parity with anything and the shape is chosen. A cell that is not a byte says WHAT it is: Region names the offset field, the gutter bars and the padding apart from each other, where the old hit-test answered Option<usize>, so "you clicked the offset column" and "you clicked the gap between the two groups" were the same value and an editor wanting to select a row by its offset had nothing to read. And a hex cell names its NIBBLE, which is the difference between overtyping one digit and overtyping the byte -- the thing a hex editor is for -- rather than rounding both digits to the byte. THE MIGRATION CAUGHT A WIRE CHANGE MADE WITHOUT MEANING TO. ByteSelection::hex was written to join pairs with a space, and the existing consumer's published contract is "0000002c" with no separator; the example's own tests went red on it. The resolution is not a different default but a PARAMETER: a clipboard payload meant to be pasted into code and a status readout want different separators, and a crate that picks one is making a presentation decision on behalf of every consumer. The signature records why it is shaped that way. It also re-confirmed the class this project keeps paying for -- cargo check compiles the bin and not the test target, so the stale constants left in the example's test module were invisible until the tests were actually run, which is debt-local-gate-misses-example-tests one more time.

Round 1607.decision_summary: A dashboard's tiles are a value, and the layout it needs already existed. THE FINDING IS WHAT THIS ROUND DID NOT BUILD. debt-no-tile-grid-dashboard-substrate asked for one thing before any code: measure whether R1560's CSS Grid already holds a Grafana-class dashboard, rather than adding a second layout kind on the strength of an argument. It does, and pinion-runtime's tile_dashboard_measurement is that measurement as a TEST -- a full-width header, two halves and a two-row-tall card placed on twelve Fr(1.0) tracks resolve to exactly the pixels a twelve-column dashboard wants at 1200 wide, and a second case asserts the property a splitter tree cannot have: widening one card leaves the other rows' columns alone, because grid tracks are sized once ACROSS the container while a column of flex rows measures each row on its own. So the layout is not the gap and no new one was written. What was missing is the half a layout engine has no opinion about -- which tile is where, the rule that keeps two of them off one slot, and what a drag does to the tiles it lands on. THE INVARIANT IS THE TYPE. TileGrid holds tiles that do not overlap; every operation either keeps that true or is refused by name, and violations() exists for a grid that arrived from a file and has promised nothing, which is Document::validate's own argument one domain over. The difficulty is not rejection: a drag onto an occupied slot does not fail, it DISPLACES, so the interesting part is a reflow that terminates and is deterministic. Both properties come from one rule -- a displaced tile only ever moves down, and only to just below the lowest tile it collided with -- so rows increase monotonically over a finite set and the walk cannot cycle; the settle bound in the loop is a backstop for a caller who handed us a grid already in violation, not part of the argument. TWO THINGS PAST GRAFANA, which pushes displaced panels down silently, as a side effect of its drag. A move REPORTS what it displaced: Reflow names every tile that moved and the row it came from, which is what an undo record, a "your layout changed" notice and an agent driving the board over the wire all need and none of which Grafana can answer. And compaction is a VERB rather than a consequence: Grafana floats tiles up to close gaps after every drag, so a gesture moves tiles the user never touched and its inverse is not a gesture; compact() is a separate call, is idempotent, and names what it moved. A FAILING TEST THAT THE IMPLEMENTATION WON. The first draft of the displacement test expected a drag to push a tile in a column it does not share, and the reflow correctly left it where it was. The effect is LOCAL, which the module doc claimed and which is now a thing a test asserts rather than a thing a comment says -- and the assertion records that the expectation was the wrong half. DELIBERATE INCOMPLETENESS, NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. There is no consumer and therefore no demo, so this round does not satisfy the standing per-round visible-deliverable obligation, and it says so instead of letting a unit test stand in for one. The debt keeps its gesture axis open: what closes it is a binding that wires a pointer drag and an RPC verb to move_to / resize / compact, which is also what would tell us whether the reflow's locality feels right under a real cursor. The model is the half that could be built correctly without one; the gesture is not.

Round 1608.decision_summary: The tile dashboard gets its gesture, and the model's claim gets a cursor. R1607 built TileGrid, measured that R1560's CSS Grid already holds a Grafana-class dashboard, and then stopped without a consumer -- writing in its own changelog that a consumer was the only thing that could tell us whether the reflow's LOCALITY holds under a real pointer. It does. Three layers meet in examples/hello-tile-dashboard and only one is new: the layout is R1560's grid, the arrangement is R1607's model, and the gesture is this file. A press latches the card under the cursor AND the cell the grab happened at relative to that card; each move snaps the cursor to a cell and subtracts the grab offset; the release lets go. THE GRAB OFFSET IS THE WHOLE TRICK. Snapping the cursor's cell and moving the card's top-left there makes a card jump under the pointer the moment it is grabbed anywhere but its corner, which is exactly the difference between a drag and a teleport, and it is the kind of thing no amount of model testing surfaces. THE MODEL CANNOT TRAVEL THROUGH WidgetCore::State, because State is Copy and an arrangement is a Vec. The canonical shape for a model this size is hello-node-groups': the state lives in an Owner::cache'd signal that the external mutates and the view reads. That is not a workaround -- it is what makes the painter and the wire read ONE arrangement instead of two copies that could disagree, which is the same argument R1607 used for putting the zero-based-to-CSS conversion in exactly one place. Every gesture is a verb over the wire (move_to / resize / compact / remove) and the whole board is one JSON read (layout), so an agent rearranges the dashboard with no pixel; every slot is read-only, and a read-only refusal is told apart from an unknown path, which is R1566's rule rather than this binding's invention. Past Grafana on the wire as well as in the model: last_reflow names what a gesture displaced INCLUDING the transitive case, a card pushed by a card that was itself pushed. FOUR OF THIS ROUND'S ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT EVERY TIME, which is the round's real content rather than an embarrassment to bury. `alarms` is eight columns wide in a grid of twelve, so it cannot move at all and the drag fixture had to be a narrower card -- the model's clamp was correct and the test's choice of card was not. The displacement list was longer than expected, because the reflow is transitive. A 6x2 resize came out clean, correctly, because the rows it grew into were empty by then. And a card that shares no column with the dragged one is not touched at all: that is the locality the model's doc claimed, that R1607 could not test, and that the demo now asserts over the wire. The visible-deliverable obligation R1607 recorded itself as breaking is met here: a real binding, a real window, and a demo with forty assertions over ten sections that reads the painted board out of scene/snapshot rather than assuming it.

Round 1609.decision_summary: A tile board is editable without a pointer, and an edge is a HANDLE. This closes both axes of the debt R1608's own close audit registered: a resize existed only as a wire verb with no handle to grab, and there was NO KEYBOARD CHANNEL AT ALL, so the assistive-technology nodes R1608 added let a screen-reader user read the arrangement and never change it. They close TOGETHER because they are one derivation. set_edge puts one side of a card on a grid line and holds the opposite side still; a handle drag calls it once per edge in the handle, a Grow or Shrink chord calls it once with a one-cell step. One private function, four public entry points, so a corner drag and a keyboard chord cannot disagree about what moving a side means. Qt's floor here is real and was read rather than assumed: QMdiSubWindow has keyboard move AND resize. Five things are chosen differently, each measured against qtbase 6.11.1. NO MODE: Qt's keyboard editing lives behind isInInteractiveMode, entered only from the system menu, because _q_enterInteractiveMode begins by casting q->sender() to a QAction and returns unless it is MoveAction or ResizeAction -- so switching from moving to resizing costs a menu round trip and one arrow key means different things depending on state the user cannot see. TileNudge is twelve flat values and the chord says which. NOTHING WARPS THE POINTER: Qt computes each arrow as mapFromGlobal(cursor().pos() + delta) and then calls cursor().setPos(...) to drag the mouse along, with the whole keyPressEvent body inside #ifndef QT_NO_CURSOR -- so a cursor-less build has no keyboard layout editing at all, and every other build jumps the user's physical pointer across the screen. A nudge here is arithmetic on cells. AN EDIT CAN BE TAKEN BACK: Qt stores oldGeometry on entering interactive mode and never reads it back, because Key_Escape, Key_Return and Key_Enter all fall to one leaveInteractiveMode() arm, so Escape COMMITS. And even restoring the rectangle would not be enough, which is the more interesting half: a move displaces OTHER cards, so TileEdit holds the whole arrangement and Escape puts the board back. A SESSION'S REFLOW IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A SUM: four chords that walk a card down past another push that card once, from row 1 to row 5, where adding the per-chord reflows reports four displacements of a card that moved a single time. Reflow::between derives it from the two arrangements. ARROW NAVIGATION IS TOTAL, AND THE INVARIANT IS WHY: negate Tile::overlaps and what is left is exactly "separated on some axis in some direction", so every other card lies beyond one of the four edges and TileGrid::neighbour can reach all of them. QMdiArea cannot make that claim because its subwindows may overlap, which is precisely why its navigation is activateNextSubWindow, a walk down a QList in creation order with no notion of direction at all. On the pointer side, Qt's initOperationMap hand-writes nine rows pairing a private Operation value with a ChangeFlag mask and a cursor, and the enum, the map and the cached regions are all private, so no caller can enumerate a subwindow's handles or ask which cursor one wants. TileHandle::ALL is the enumeration, and both the edges a handle moves and the cursor it asks for are DERIVED, the diagonal's slope included: two start edges or two end edges lie on the nwse diagonal, one of each on nesw. That derivation forced CursorHint's two diagonal arms, and the finding there is the debt-window-has-no-level-declaration shape a third time -- the R1189 window-chrome path has mapped ResizeDirection::NorthWest to CursorIcon::NwseResize for some 420 rounds, so the capability was proven in-tree and only the scene-node VOCABULARY could not name it. A test now asserts a card's grip and a window's south-east corner resolve to one icon rather than agreeing by coincidence. THE ANNOUNCEMENT NEEDED A NEW CHANNEL, and it is a framework addition with this board as its forcing consumer. pinion-a11y gains AccessLive, the WAI-ARIA aria-live axis, because the cards an edit displaces are by definition not the one the user is on, so no per-card value can carry the fact. Qt 6.8 added QAccessibleAnnouncementEvent and, measured over qtbase, NO WIDGET FIRES ONE: the only references outside qaccessible.h and .cpp are the platform adapters that deliver it and qtestaccessible.h, while qmdisubwindow.cpp, qmdiarea.cpp and qsizegrip.cpp contain no accessibility notification of any kind -- so a Qt MDI window that moves or resizes is silent to a screen reader even though QAccessibleMdiSubWindow::state() advertises movable and sizeable. A DECLARED region rather than a fired event is also the only shape section 2 invariant 7 can report: an event leaves no trace, so scene/access could not publish it and a test could only observe it by intercepting a callback. Three arms where Qt's politeness has two, and the extra one is not padding -- an event has no "off" because not firing it is off, while a declared region nests, so Off is how a subtree opts out of a live ancestor. THREE OF THE ROUND'S ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT, which is where its content is. A Grow then a Shrink restores the CARD and not the BOARD, because the reflow only moves tiles down and floating them home is compact's separate verb -- so an inverse gesture is not an undo, and that is the argument for TileEdit stated as a test instead of a paragraph. The corner test's first fixture grew both axes and its three routes agreed, because a rectangle reached by two outward steps contains every intermediate; the hazard needs one edge going each way. And the difference-not-a-sum fixture first walked its card UP, which collides once, so it measured 1 against 1 and could not tell the two answers apart. A FOURTH defect was found by a test rather than by reasoning, and it is an interaction one: handles are painted only on the selected card and the first draft hit-tested them on EVERY card, so a press near any card's edge resized it with nothing on screen saying it would. The paint and the gesture now read one fact, and selecting first then grabbing second is what every real board does anyway.

Round 1609.1.decision_summary: The close audit found a defect in R1609's own paint, and it is the class this round had already named twice. The grip ring was eight absolutely-positioned nodes whose insets were computed from two stated constants, CARD_INNER_W 40 and CARD_INNER_H, and a card's resolved width is a LAYOUT-PASS OUTPUT -- so any inset a view function can state is a guess that happens to fit one card size. On the seed board the twelve-column header's right-hand grips would have floated somewhere in its middle. The framework cannot express it that way either: LayoutStyle::absolute_position anchors left and top only, and CSS's `right: 0` has no analogue here, so stating the inset was not a shortcut but the only thing the vocabulary allowed. THE FIX IS A GRID, and it makes the ring say exactly what it means in one place: an overlay pinned at (0,0) with Auto size, so it resolves to the card's content rect, carrying three tracks per axis -- the outer two a grip thick, the middle Fr(1.0). Each grip's cell is DERIVED from the same TileHandle::horizontal / vertical pair its cursor already comes from, mapping a near edge to line 1, no edge to 2 and a far edge to 3. So the ring is correct at every card size with no arithmetic that can be wrong, it is ONE node rather than eight positioned ones, and R1560's CSS Grid is now used twice inside one round -- the board's own layout is the other. Two constants went away and one stayed, HANDLE_PX, which is the only pixel the ring states. THE TEST COULD NOT SEE THE DEFECT, which is the second finding. It asserted every grip's tag and every grip's cursor and said nothing about where a grip IS, so it passed against both the broken and the fixed paint. It now asserts each grip's grid cell, that the eight cells are distinct, that the middle cell is not a grip, and -- after a counterfactual came back BROKEN rather than caught -- the track KINDS, because replacing all three tracks with Px(HANDLE_PX) kept every placement assertion true while squeezing the card's content into eight pixels. A broken counterfactual is normally just a plan to fix; this one pointed at a real coverage gap on the way.

Round 1609.2.decision_summary: A grip's SIZE is the hit-test band, and the audit that found this was prompted by the user asking whether every new debt had been registered. The answer to that question was three debts; on the way to writing them, a third instance of the round's own defect class turned up. The painted grip was a fixed eight pixels thick and the hit-test band was a quarter of the card, which is TWO NUMBERS DESCRIBING ONE THING, and they disagree at every card size except the one where a quarter happens to be eight pixels: on a wide card a strip resizes with nothing drawn under it, and on a narrow one part of the painted grip does not resize. Fractional grid tracks make the ring BE the band by construction -- HANDLE_BAND for the two outer tracks and a derived HANDLE_CORE for the middle -- on both axes and at every card size, and HANDLE_PX is gone. The test now asserts the tracks against the very constant TileHandle::at is called with, plus that the three cover the card exactly and that the interior is non-empty. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE ROUND that what is DRAWN and what RESPONDS were derived from different facts: R1609 hit-tested handles on cards that painted none, R1609.1 placed grips at a pixel inset off a stated width while a card's width is a layout-pass output, and this is the unit split. One was found by a test and two by audit, and every one of them passed a test that asserted only one side. That is now a registered class debt of its own, because the general form is real and unguarded -- an External receives pointer_move in its own fractions and computes its own hit regions, so every binding that does so can split the same way, and the framework's Scene::hit_test / hit_test_shape path is not what they use. Two more debts registered by the same audit: LayoutStyle::absolute_position anchors left and top only, with no CSS right/bottom analogue, which is what pushed R1609.1 into stating a width in the first place -- the vocabulary's hole moved a person toward the wrong answer; and AccessLive has exactly one consumer, while the tree already holds the widgets the channel is FOR (snackbar, status bar, progress), so this is not a missing-consumer defer but a coverage gap, and a declared region can be gated where a fired event could not.

Round 1610.decision_summary:
A window declares its LEVEL, and says what became of it. This closes debt-window-has-no-level-declaration, which was the last open analyzer-tool debt: plane C asks for a torn-off readout that stays above the application being watched, and the CAPABILITY was already proven in this tree, because the shell's own drag-preview window has hard-coded an always-on-top level since R1147. Only the vocabulary was missing, which is the shape R1609 had just met for the third time in CursorHint. Declared osnative on R1576's precedent: this is the same WindowSpec axis, and what that axis is gated on is Mac and Windows NATIVE SURFACES, which a window-manager stacking request buildable and testable on Linux is not.

A NOTE ON HOW THIS ENTRY IS WRITTEN. The user directed today that reference-project names must not appear in anything pushed. The comparisons below were read from a reference implementation and are recorded here as the reasoning WITHOUT the citation; the citation lives in the local memory topic, which is outside the repository. That split is the point rather than a compromise: a pushed artifact should carry why a design is shaped the way it is, and a design reason survives losing its source. What does not survive is the ability to re-verify, so the source is kept where it can be read again.

THE SHAPE IS CHOSEN AGAINST THE CONVENTIONAL DESKTOP-TOOLKIT ENCODING IN FIVE PLACES, each read rather than assumed. A LEVEL IS ONE VALUE WITH THREE ARMS: the usual encoding is a pair of independent bits in a window-flags word, one for stay-above and one for stay-below, so on-top-AND-on-bottom is a value a program can build -- and a value a program can build is a value some layer has to resolve. Measured across three platform backends of one reference implementation, they resolve it three DIFFERENT ways. One sets both stacking hints on a mapped window with no exclusion at all, while the path taken at show time is if-above-else-if-below, so the same pair means one thing at map time and another on a live change. One warns that the window cannot be on top and on bottom at once, and takes top. And one never reads the stay-below bit anywhere in its backend, so the declaration does nothing at all, silently. Here the contradiction is not representable and no platform gets to arbitrate it.

THE OUTCOME IS PUBLISHED BESIDE THE DECLARATION, and that is the point of the axis. A window-flags accessor returns the value the program STORED, so on that third backend a program sets stay-below, reads it back as set, and is wrong. A declaration whose fate is unreportable is a declaration a program can be silently wrong about -- and this is not the platform lacking the capability, because that platform does have levels below normal and the window backend used here drives one. LevelOutcome names applied, unsupported and unknown against the backend ACTUALLY RUNNING, which the window backend answers from the live event loop rather than from a build target, because one Linux binary runs on either of the two windowing systems whose support differs. Three arms rather than a bool, because "this backend cannot" and "nobody here has measured this backend" are different facts, and collapsing them means inventing a failure or claiming a success.

THE ERROR DIRECTION IS CHOSEN. WindowingBackend::outcome is a MODEL of the window backend, not a query: no windowing system reports that it ignored something, and the backend exposes no getter for a window's level. So the table can go stale, and it is arranged to fail in the self-correcting direction. A backend that gains support is over-reported as unsupported, which the next person to reach for it notices; the reverse, claiming applied for a backend that drops it, is the silent lie described above and nobody would ever notice it. That is R1602's asymmetry applied to a vendored-behaviour model, and the residual is registered rather than left implicit.

CHANGING IT COSTS ONE CALL. When the level lives inside a window-flags word, changing it reparents and therefore HIDES the window -- the caller has to show it again -- and on one platform backend the native window is destroyed and recreated, because a changed stacking bit is recorded as a recreation reason and the next show rebuilds the window. That costs the native handle, the mapped state and a visible flash. Here it is one live call. That is also why the axis has to be reconcilable rather than create-time: a level is a thing the USER toggles, so a create-time-only level would not be the feature at all.

AND THE LEVELS ARE ENUMERABLE. WindowLevel::ALL and the wire's level_names make a level picker buildable from the wire alone, where two bits inside a flags word carrying twenty unrelated hints carry no enumeration of themselves and the exclusivity rule lives in the platform backends rather than in the type.

TWO LIFTS THE ROUND WAS FORCED INTO RATHER THAN CHOSE. window_axis_changes: the level pass would have been the THIRD hand-written copy of one same-id walk, beside title (R1319) and decorations (R1320), and three mechanical copies of a rule is precisely the R727 and R732 third-consumer mandate. The three are now one derivation with a projection, and getting the ADD case right in one copy and wrong in another is no longer possible. window_placement_moves is deliberately NOT expressed through it: a resolution against the live monitor topology is not a field comparison, and it has an add that CAN require an apply. A shape that only looks similar is not the same rule. Then scene/window_declare: scene/windows publishes five axes and exactly ONE of them, position, could be written back, so title, decorations and display were readable and writable by nobody. Adding a per-field scene/window_level would have been the second step toward one method per field. The read is one method over the whole declaration, so the write is one method over the whole declaration, and scene/window_move is re-expressed as the position-only patch it always was, driven through the same closure -- two closures writing one signal is two places for the same axis to acquire different semantics, and R1088's "an explicit AI reposition PINS the window" would have been true of one and not the other. Absent, null and a value are three distinct messages, which is what makes going BACK to a window-manager-placed window expressible at all; the same argument R1576 made on the binding side when with_placement(None) was added because the builders could only ever add. strategy is deliberately absent from the patch: it is create-time intent with no reconcile pass, so a write wire that accepted it would silently do nothing.

INLINE CLEARANCE, AND THE ROUND'S SECOND FINDING. Publishing the new NoAxisDeclared refusal was impossible without touching R1566's vocabulary gate, and the gate turned out to see TWO of the FOUR shapes this dispatcher emits a word in. It was built around WireFault::params and Cow::Borrowed, which is how path.rs and query.rs spell it; the dispatcher's own refusals are spelled as a bare literal handed to invalid_params, and as the let-variant-match block thirteen error types share. EIGHTEEN words reached the wire that a client could only learn by reading pinion's source -- ClosureUnavailable, InputInjectionUnavailable from 24 call sites, InvalidSize, OutOfBounds, SnapshotFailed, RenderBackendUnavailable and the rest -- inside the gate built to make exactly that impossible. The scan now walks the variant blocks STRUCTURALLY, which a line-local rule cannot do, because the arrow-quote-Word spelling is also how a dozen VALUE enums write their wire names: measured, a line-local rule collects sixteen of them as refusals. Requiring the block's function to actually reach invalid_params(variant) is also what correctly EXCLUDES apply_error_to_rpc, which shares the shape and builds an OBJECT payload. Vocabulary 17 to 35 with no new refusal written. This is R1605's lesson a second time: make every emission account for itself, rather than finding the ones you already know how to find. What remains unaccounted is registered -- three named constants and six expression arguments are prose by reading and not by a gate.

THREE COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED AND TWO OF THEM WERE REAL. Deleting the signal write from the example's level verb, and making a placement preset reset the level, both left the example suite green: every test there exercised a PURE function, and the state object's own verbs were reached only by the demo, which does not run under cargo test. Signal::new needs no Owner scope and the display handle is constructible, so the state object was always a value a test could hold and there was never a reason for the gap; three tests now cover it and both counterfactuals are caught. The third, CF-16, is a DEGENERATE mutation rather than a finding, and saying so is the honest reading: removing the guard that starts a block at let-variant-match selects the same set on today's source, because the block END guard and the reaches-invalid_params guard already do. CF-14, CF-15 and CF-19 prove those three guards load-bearing -- dropping any of them fails -- so the fourth is defensive rather than dead, and it stays.

The vocabulary scan is better and still not complete. The real answer is R1605's and it is a round rather than a patch: make every invalid_params call site classify or FAIL, which reaches the limit of a text scan at the constant and wants a parser -- the conclusion debt-param-census-blind-to-variable-keys already came to.

The user's directive that reference-project names must not appear in anything pushed is met for everything this round wrote, and NOT met for the tree: 4,438 mentions remain across crates, examples and tools, plus the docs and this ledger's own history. Registered as debt-reference-project-names-in-pushed-artifacts with the census, the regex (which must require a lower-case letter after the leading capital, or every all-caps word is a false positive), and the order to do it in -- a ratchet gate FIRST so the count cannot grow, then the human-facing judgment documents, then the crates. It is not a mechanical substitution: those sentences carry the reason a type is shaped the way it is, so each has to be re-stated without its citation, which is what this round did to its own and what makes it slow.

Publishing the new NoAxisDeclared refusal was impossible without touching R1566's vocabulary gate, and the gate turned out to see TWO of the FOUR shapes this dispatcher emits a word in. Round 1610.1.decision_summary:
Three things the GATES found after R1610's own reasoning was done, and each of them corrected a design rather than a slip. Recorded as a follow-up entry because R1610 is frozen; nothing in it is falsified, which is itself the first finding.

ONE: A THREE-WAY PATCH IS ONE VALUE WITH THREE ARMS, AND THE LINT SAID SO. The draft of scene/window_declare spelled its two nullable axes as Option<Option<T>> with a serde double-option, the idiomatic trick for absent-versus-null-versus-value, and clippy::option_option refused it under this workspace's -D pedantic with a message that names the answer rather than merely objecting: "consider using Option<T> instead of Option<Option<T>> or a custom enum if you need to distinguish all 3 cases". WHAT MAKES IT WORTH RECORDING IS THE INCONSISTENCY IT CAUGHT: R1610's whole argument for WindowLevel is that a level must be ONE value with three arms rather than two independent bits, because a two-flag encoding makes a contradictory value representable and then some layer has to resolve it -- and the same round was writing its patch as two stacked Options, where a reader of Some(None) has to know which layer means what. One round cannot make that argument in its type and contradict it in its wire params. Patch<T> is Untouched / Clear / Set(T); apply_to is the ONE place the three arms are matched, so no consumer can treat Untouched as Clear, which is the defect the nesting invited and which the shell's closure had already hand-written as an if-let that happened to be right. Only the two NULLABLE axes carry it -- title, decorations and level stay plain Options, because those axes have no cleared state, so the difference between the axes now lives in the types rather than in a comment.

TWO: THE WIRE CENSUS ENFORCED A RULE THIS CRATE STATES ABOUT ITSELF. DeclaredWindow first carried the domain types directly -- pinion_core's WindowLevel and LevelOutcome -- and wire_census_matches_types failed, because it parses THIS crate's sources and a field typed with another crate's vocabulary publishes as `any`. That is not a tooling inconvenience, it is the rule DeclaredWindow's own doc already states ("this crate owns only the wire shape") and the rule R1576 followed when it made `display` a String rather than a DisplayId and projected Anchored into a flat, locally-owned AnchoredOutcome. So level becomes the wire spelling and level_outcome becomes LevelOutcomeWire, flattened to kind / declared / backend on AnchoredOutcome's precedent, because all three outcomes carry the same two facts beside their kind and a client branches on kind either way. WindowDeclareParams.level follows: a String parsed by WindowLevel::from_wire, refused as UnknownLevel BEFORE the closure runs so a bad spelling cannot half-apply a patch whose other axes are good. The cost is real and named: serde's own unknown-variant error used to enumerate the valid spellings for free, and a bare String does not, so the refusal is a vocabulary word and the enumeration lives where the rest of the wire's vocabulary lives.

The census also had to be taught one structural fact, and the shape of that teaching matters. Patch<T> has hand-written Serialize and Deserialize -- that is where the three states live -- so no derive scan can see it and every field using one published as `any`, telling an agent nothing about the very axis whose three-ness the type exists for. The parser now unwraps Patch<T> as optional-and-nullable-T. That is a STRUCTURAL fact about a LOCAL type, deliberately not a hand-kept table of foreign type names to wire types, which is the maintained-list failure this project keeps paying for.

THREE: LIFTING HALF A DUPLICATION LEAVES THE OTHER HALF, AND A LINE CAP IS WHAT SAID SO. R1610 lifted the DIFF half of the three live-axis passes into window_axis_changes and left the APPLY half as three hand-written copies of "look the spec id up, reach the live window, set the value, trace it" -- and clippy's too-many-lines fired at 103 of 100 on reconcile_windows, which is the design signal this project treats it as rather than a number to raise. apply_axis_pass is the mirror of window_axis_changes, and the lookup it now states once is the subtle part: the apply reaches a Suspended(Some) window through its cached arc and skips only a Suspended(None) slot, which resume_spec rebuilds from the current spec. Three copies of that rule were three chances for one to skip a window shape the others reach. The pair is the general lesson: when a duplication has a produce half and a consume half, lifting one and not the other leaves the count at three on the side nobody looked at.

AND THE FIRST FINDING, WHICH IS ABOUT THE LEDGER ITSELF: none of this falsifies a word of R1610, because that entry described the CONTRACT ("absent, null and a value are three distinct messages") and never the encoding. A ledger that cannot be amended rewards stating what a thing guarantees rather than how it is spelled, and this is the first time that has been tested here.

Round 1613.decision_summary:
R1613 — a byte dump paints from the map that hit-tests it, and a byte says which named runs lit it.

The analyzer-tool audit's plane A had one gap left, and it was an asymmetry R1606 created rather than a hole it left: the detail tree's paint was already a crate (view_virtual_tree) and the dump's was 55 lines inside hello-hex-dump, so an application that depended on one got a picture and an application that depended on the other got a map and homework. pinion_widget_paint::hex_dump::view_hex_dump closes it, and the move is not a relocation.

The painter asks region_at what each cell IS and glyph_at what it SHOWS — the same two questions a pointer asks — so a cell that draws a byte is a cell that selects that byte, by construction rather than by two functions agreeing. That is the general form of debt-paint-and-gesture-read-two-facts, demonstrated on a real widget: the hit region is derived FROM the paint's own source.

Making that affordable forced region_at into closed form. A scan of the row's bytes is fine for a pointer, which asks about one cell, and quadratic for a painter, which asks about all of them; every group of hex digits occupies a fixed stride, so the group is a division and the byte inside it is another. The closed form is held to the scan it replaced by an exhaustive cell-for-cell property over every layout shape, plus a wall-clock ceiling at 2^24 bytes a row where the two costs are four orders of magnitude apart.

THE OFFSET COLUMN WAS BROKEN AND NOTHING COULD SEE IT. The example formatted the row offset to a fixed EIGHT hex digits and then truncated to offset_digits, so every declared width below eight printed the leading zeros of an eight-digit number — 0000 on every row, including the rows not at offset zero. The layout has carried a with_offset_digits builder since R1606 and the one width nobody exercised was any width but the default. glyph_at derives the digit from its place value instead.

MARKS ARE NAMED, NOT COLOURED. MarkSet is a declaration-ordered list of named byte runs carrying no colour at all; names_at(byte) answers WHY a byte is lit with the whole stack that decided it, innermost last, and overlap resolves LAST-wins for every visual channel alike. The reference is a mature toolkit's list of range decorations over a text layout, and the two differences are the whole point. There a decoration is (start, length, format), so a run has no identity apart from how it looks and by the time anyone asks only the colour is left — two runs resolving to the same ink are indistinguishable. And its draw loop resolves overlap in TWO opposite directions at once: a later range's background overpaints an earlier one, while a later range's foreground is suppressed wherever an earlier one already drew text. Background last-wins, foreground first-wins, in the same loop, documented nowhere and queryable not at all. One direction, stated, with the stack readable, is the choice here.

CellRole exists so that a new region cannot go unpainted. Region stays non_exhaustive because the hit-test's vocabulary grows; role() collapses it to a painter's question inside the module, where the match IS exhaustive; and CellRole is deliberately not non_exhaustive, so a new role fails to compile in every painter rather than falling into a wildcard arm. That is debt-node-body-arm-is-weaker-than-a-type, answered structurally instead of by census.

Thirteen counterfactuals, thirteen caught — but ONE PASSED FIRST, and it was the round's own doing. The paint crate had restated the printable-byte rule that the geometry already owns; narrowing it to drop the space broke nothing, because no fixture held a space and the assertion had been written against the same predicate it was testing. The fix was not a better fixture. It was deleting the second copy: the painter now asks whether the glyph IS the byte, which cannot drift from a rule it does not restate. The fixture gained a space as well, so the next such copy has something to fail on.

pinion-core widgets::hex_dump: CellRole + Region::role() — the painter's closed question, collapsed inside the module where the match over the non_exhaustive Region is exhaustive.
pinion-core widgets::hex_dump: Mark + MarkSet — named byte runs, no colour; at / names_at / top_at / get, declaration order, last-wins.
pinion-widget-paint hex_dump: view_hex_dump + HexPalette + MarkInk + ink_at. The application declares names and colours; the crate walks the grid.

marks_at names the field run in its arguments because the field belongs to a sibling external, not to the dump's oracle. The seam is stated rather than hidden, but a scene that could report the marks it painted would not need the caller to supply half the question.

Background last-wins, foreground first-wins, in the same loop, documented nowhere and queryable not at all. One direction, stated, with the stack readable, is the choice here.

Region stays non_exhaustive because the hit-test's vocabulary grows; role() collapses it to a painter's question inside the module, where the match IS exhaustive; and CellRole is deliberately not non_exhaustive, so a new role fails to compile in every painter rather than falling into a wildcard arm. That is debt-node-body-arm-is-weaker-than-a-type, answered structurally instead of by census.

Thirteen counterfactuals, thirteen caught — but ONE PASSED FIRST, and it was the round's own doing. The paint crate had restated the printable-byte rule that the geometry already owns; narrowing it to drop the space broke nothing, because no fixture held a space and the assertion had been written against the same predicate it was testing. The fix was not a better fixture. It was deleting the second copy: the painter now asks whether the glyph IS the byte, which cannot drift from a rule it does not restate. The fixture gained a space as well, so the next such copy has something to fail on.

Round 1614.decision_summary:
R1614 — the reference names reach zero, and the ones that stay say what they are.

The standing directive (2026-08-09) is that the names of the projects this one is judged against must not appear in what we publish. R1611 built the gate and R1612 cleared 7,999 occurrences down to 766. This round takes 766 to 0, and the interesting part is not the count: it is that every step was a derivation the first pass had already found and then declined to apply, plus one category where zero turns out to be the wrong target.

THE ID FAMILIES ARE DERIVATIONS TOO. The migration tool reported the operator ids, the DCC's C structs and the engine's classes and left them for "a round of their own", on the grounds that the "strip the prefix, de-camel it" rule that works on a toolkit class does not apply unchanged. It applies with one substitution each. An operator id is a vendor prefix plus a capability, so the capability is what is left — and that is not a new spelling, it is the SAME one `tools/reference_census.py`'s `public_id` already derives, so the prose and the proof tables agree by construction instead of by care. A C struct is `b` plus its own generic noun exactly as a toolkit class is `Q` plus one. An engine class is a type-prefix letter, a subsystem word and a name, where the subsystem word is the vendor's spelling of a generic thing: a graph, a node, that language's compiler, a visual script.

A DOC LINK IS REMOVED, NOT REWORDED. The first pass refused every line holding a URL and was right to — substituting inside a host name produced `doc.the-toolkit.io` — but refusing it left the citation in place, which is the thing the directive is about. So the definition line goes whole, the label it defined loses its brackets so no rustdoc link is left dangling, and the name inside the label is then an ordinary symbol the class pass can read. Only a TRAILING blank comment line is dropped with it: the blank before a definition that SURVIVES is load-bearing, because a link reference glued to the paragraph above it stops being a definition at all. That rule was not reasoned out. It arrived as two broken rustdoc links at the commit gate.

THE REST WAS ASSERTION LABELS, AND THE ANSWER IS A JUDGE, NOT A CLASSIFIER. The tool's refusal to touch a string literal is sound in general — a literal may be a payload an assertion compares against. But what was left after the comment pass was almost entirely labels: the third argument of `assert_eq`, the sentence in an `expect`, a demo's title. No classifier can tell a label from a payload, and none is needed, because a rewritten payload fails its own test and a rewritten demo string fails its own demo. So `--in-strings` is opt-in per file and the caller runs those tests. It caught its own error on the first run: a local variable named `qt`, for a quit sink, became `let the toolkit =`, and the compiler said so before anything else did.

THE WRAPPER HAD BEEN MEASURING THE WRONG LINE ALL ALONG. The re-flow hides a code span behind a placeholder so the wrapper cannot split it, and the placeholder was three characters standing in for eighteen — so every paragraph holding a span came out over the margin by the difference. Nothing failed. No lint measures a comment, so the only witness a rewritten comment has is a reader, and the pass that rewrote four thousand lines of prose had none.

AND ZERO IS NOT ZERO EVERYWHERE. The design-parity workflow's host name, token header and environment variable are not a citation of a project this one is judged against. They are an ADDRESS, and renaming any of them stops the feature working. So everything that WAS ours to name was renamed to the role it plays — `pinion design-verify` / `design-fetch-image` / `design-diff`, the `design_*` modules, `examples/design-button-m3` — and the three constants were gathered into one small module, `crates/pinion-cli/src/design_api.rs`, so that the gate's exclusion could be that one file rather than a whole subsystem. The prose in the modules around it stays counted, so a citation cannot regrow behind the exclusion. `.gitignore` is excluded for the same shape of reason and is the narrowest entry in the list: an ignore pattern IS the literal directory an editor creates, and a file of path patterns holds no prose for anything to regrow in.

What is lost, everywhere, is the ability to look a symbol up. That is what the round's memory notes are for, and R1613 started paying that back: the evidence for one interface comparison now lives in a memory note with its file, its symbol and its line.

Round 1614.1.decision_summary:
R1614.1 — the census reads its own pin again, and the node-coverage numbers come back.

R1612 renamed the reference census's committed pin — its tree names and its operator ids — into a spelling that does not name a vendor, and taught `emit` to write them that way. It did not teach `report` to read them that way. So `pin.get(tree)` looked up a live tree name in a file keyed by public ones and missed every time.

The consequence was silent in the worst direction. Coverage printed **nothing at all**: the denominator was zero, so the line that reports it was skipped rather than printing `0/0`, and a number that is absent does not look wrong. Meanwhile all 679 judged operators came back as unmeasured, which reads as "the reference grew" rather than "the reader broke". And `--check-pin`, which reads the pin directly and never touches a live tree, went on reporting 679 judged and 0 problems — so the tool passed its own check while its headline output said nothing.

**Two readers of one census, one taught.** That is the shape R1612.3 recorded a week ago about the wire census, and R1611 before it. This one is inside the tool that recorded the class.

The fix is two lines: resolve the tree through the public-name table, and map each live id through the same `public_id` the writer uses, before the lookup.

THE NUMBERS ARE BACK AND THEY MOVED. The DCC reads 54/76 = 71% where the last recorded audit said 54/72 = 75% — four operators appeared in the reference, so the denominator grew while the numerator did not. The engine reads 85/211 = 40%, unchanged in rate. 301 live operators are unjudged, and that is the real state the node-coverage campaign works against; the broken reader had been calling it 679.

AND THE ROUND'S FIRST TEST WAS THE WRONG TEST. It asserted the **pin's** shape — that its keys are public — and a counterfactual that restored the broken lookup **passed** it, because the artifact was never what broke. A test of an artifact is not a test of its reader. Replaced with one that runs `report` over a synthetic tree and a synthetic pin and asserts the coverage line it prints; both halves of the fix now have a counterfactual that catches them.

tools/reference_census.py: the unregistered-name check maps through public_id too, so a sixth registration mechanism is still reported.

tools/reference_census.py selftest: report() is run over a synthetic tree and pin and its coverage line asserted, replacing a check that asserted the pin's shape and could not tell the fixed reader from the broken one.
verification_bullets: the live census now prints coverage again: the DCC 54/76 = 71 percent, the engine 85/211 = 40, with 301 operators unjudged.
reference census --selftest: all checks passed; --check-pin unchanged at 679 judged, 0 problems.
