Round 1615.decision_summary:
R1615 — the scene says why it painted, and a run says what it is.

R1613 gave a byte dump named marks and an oracle to ask them of. Its own close audit registered what that oracle could not do: the field run belongs to a SIBLING external — the overview brush — so the caller had to query one oracle, feed the answer into another, and reproduce the framework's composition rule on its own side. debt-scene-cannot-say-which-marks-it-painted named the general form: whenever a widget's appearance is decided by more than one external, the COMPOSED fact belongs to no single oracle, and the view is the only place that can publish it.

THE CENSUS THE DEBT DEMANDED, AND IT SAID "DO NOT ESTIMATE". tools/assembled_state.py: 73 multi-external bindings, 11 of which read more than one external, 1 of which publishes the assembly. The population is mechanical — create_extra_externals is the only substrate for a sibling external — and the verdict is a source scan whose reading range is stated. Its own selftest caught the scan short twice. A direct find_external_with_tag scan misses hello-hex-dump ENTIRELY, the very binding the debt is about, because it reads its brush through a typed reader one crate over; and the check that the typed-reader list is not silently short first answered 5 by counting four rustdoc mentions and a free function that takes the tag as a parameter. Sixteen bindings hold tag arguments the scan cannot resolve to a constant, and they are REPORTED rather than dropped.

THE ANSWER IS A CHANNEL ON THE NODE, NOT A BETTER ORACLE. pinion_core::marks lifts Mark / MarkSet out of widgets::hex_dump — a named run is not a hex concept — and gives a set a required DOMAIN, because a dump's runs are over bytes of the inspected buffer while the cells showing them are three times as many, so a client that assumed cells would read a plausible wrong answer rather than an error. TextGridNode carries an Option<MarkSet>; StyleRun carries an Option<name>; Scene::marks_for_tag answers over both, and scene/marks puts it on the wire.

A SECOND CONSUMER, AND IT IS THE LEGIBLE ONE. highlight_code has always classified a token as keyword / string / comment / number and then kept only a colour — and the colour is not even a stable name for the class, because SyntaxPalette::classic and ::dark paint the same class two different inks. A run now names its class, so the ink and the reason for it are ONE declaration that cannot drift apart, and "why is this word blue" is answerable from the wire.

PAST THE REFERENCE IN THREE PLACES, each read from the reference's own source. Its range decoration IS its format, so two runs that resolve to the same ink are indistinguishable once drawn — a name can be smuggled through the format type's open integer-keyed user-property space, but nothing in that framework declares one, so no reader can expect it and no surface reports it. The decoration list is handed over whole, so "which runs cover offset N" is every caller's own loop. And its runs are always over characters, where a stated domain lets a grid index something else entirely.

FOUR OUTCOMES, NOT TWO. published / silent / no-channel / no-such-tag, and the no-channel arm carries WHICH kind of nothing — uniform, structural or opaque — so an agent learns from the wire that a Box has nothing to attribute rather than that a widget forgot to. SceneNodeKind::marks_channel is exhaustive, so a node kind added later has to say which it is instead of defaulting into silence.

THREE FINDINGS FROM 20 COUNTERFACTUALS, and the first is the sharpest. The census test compared the declaration to the declaration — match kind.marks_channel() { other => assert_eq!(answer, NoChannel(other)) } — so retagging Container as Opaque PASSED. The expected channel is now DERIVED from behaviour three other matches already implement: does find_with_tag descend it, does find_external_with_tag or find_immediate_with_tag resolve it, does it carry a tag at all. Second: nothing asserted that the field's text node carries field_text_tag, so deleting the tag left the whole Rust suite green with only a demo to notice. Third: Some(empty) versus None on TextGridNode::marks — a terminal emulator that never attributes its cells against a dump with nothing selected this frame — was documented as two facts and tested only one layer up, on MarksLookup, which is not the layer that can get it wrong.

A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND BY A DEMO AND IS NOW UNIT-GATED. Tagging the field's text node made it a candidate hit-target for the input router, and every interior click stopped positioning the caret. The current-line band's own comment had predicted it three lines below, saying the band works today only because the untagged text node paints on top and shadows it. Round 1616.decision_summary:
R1616 — the wire says what a level may be.

R1610 gave a window a declared level and refused a wrong spelling by name. What it could not do was say what a right spelling looks like. `rpc/errors` published the refusal word `UnknownLevel`; `rpc/schema` published the key as `string?`; and the only enumeration of the valid values anywhere in the tree was `level_names` on one binding's own external — an application surface, which another binding need not have and which is no framework contract at all. An agent was left to guess a spelling, be refused, and guess again.

That is R1566's defect one field over, and R1610 is the round that fixed R1566's gate. Knowing that matching is safe is worthless without knowing what to match.

THE PROJECTION WAS RIGHT AND INCOMPLETE. R1610.1 made the field a `String` for two reasons that still hold: this crate owns the wire shape, and the level axis must be parsed BEFORE any other axis in the same message is applied — a typed enum would abort the whole frame at deserialization, so a bad level and a good title in one patch could not be refused as a unit. Its own carry named the cost: the earlier `Option<WindowLevel>` draft got serde's unknown-variant error, which lists the valid values, and the projection threw that away. This round pays that cost back without undoing the projection.

VALUES IS THE VALUE HALF OF OF. `of` names a censused TYPE, and only a typed Rust field can carry one, because the census gate compares its declaration against the parsed source. A key deliberately typed `String` therefore has no way to reference an enum — the closed set it accepts had nowhere to live. `WireField::values` is that place, and the census describes its own new key, so an agent learns the slot exists the same way it learns every other.

THE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER RETYPED. `LEVEL_WIRE_NAMES` is a `const` computed in a `while` loop from `WindowLevel::ALL`, so its length is the domain census's length by construction. A hand list would have been this debt's own shape one layer down: a second copy of a closed set, going stale in silence.

THE PUBLISHED SET AND THE ACCEPTED SET ARE PROVEN TO BE ONE SET. That is the only thing that makes publishing worth anything, and it is where the round's assertion is: every published spelling is driven through the real `window_declare` parse path and must land; a non-member must be refused by name; and the negative control asserts the non-member is genuinely outside the set. The check lives with the axis because only the axis knows its parse path. What is general lives in the census gate — a `values` declaration must sit on a string-bearing key, be non-empty, and hold distinct non-empty spellings, and at least one field must declare one, because a census slot nothing fills is a promise to a client nobody keeps.

AND THE REFUSAL LEADS SOMEWHERE NOW. The `-32602` entry says that a word naming a closed value set does not carry the set, and that `rpc/schema` does, by the name of the slot. A word that leads to pinion's source is the loop this surface exists to end.

FIVE COUNTERFACTUALS, AND THE ONE THAT PASSED WAS THE FIXTURE'S FAULT. It deleted the tail of the sentence and left the `rpc/schema` pointer standing, so the gate was right and the counterfactual was wrong. Worth recording because a passed counterfactual is normally a finding, and this project's own rule — ask first whether the fixture separates the counterfactual from the truth — applied to the counterfactual itself.

Round 1617.decision_summary:
R1617 — a window says whose answer it is.

Two questions look like one. "Where was this window asked to go" is the declaration, and R1576 answered it with `anchored`. "Where is this window" is a different fact: a window-manager-placed window declares nothing at all and is still somewhere, and a window the user drags has moved without any declaration changing. That second question has two answerers, and until this round only one of them was ever consulted. Registered by R1576's own close audit as debt-display-home-not-cross-checked; the analyzer-tool audit's plane-C pair closes with it.

THE TWO ANSWERS CAN DIFFER WITHOUT EITHER BEING WRONG, AND THAT IS MEASURED. This framework derives a home from the window's live rectangle — the display holding the largest share. Read from the window backend's own four desktop implementations rather than assumed, there are FOUR rules: two resolve by largest intersection, one caches an answer refreshed only inside a synthetic configure path when the scale factor changes, and one reports the first compositor output the surface entered, which is not geometric at all. One of them answers with the FIRST ENUMERATED monitor for a window that is on no monitor, where this framework answers nowhere. So this is a REPORT and not a gate: a gate would have to invent a rule that overrides a platform's own. The debt wrote down that observation "seems right but the judgment is unverified" — this is the verification.

SILENCE IS NOT AGREEMENT. The backend's accessor is an option, so `platform_silent` is its own arm rather than being folded into `agreed`. Folding them would report a cross-check that never happened as one that concurred. `DisplayHome` is five arms over the product of two options, `between` is its only constructor, and its published vocabulary is proved by DRIVING that constructor over every combination and asserting set equality with the published list — a stronger claim than R1616's const-derived-from-a-census can make, because it pins what the code can EMIT rather than what the type declares.

PAST THE TOOLKIT BY READING ITS SOURCE, NOT BY ASSERTION. It has both answers too and hides one. Its geometric resolver is declared in a private header so an application cannot call it; it decides by CENTRE POINT, so a window nine tenths on the right panel whose centre is on the left resolves left, with a fallback that keeps the LAST intersecting sibling it iterated; and it is consulted only when the application itself moves the window, short-circuiting whenever the current screen already contains the centre. A user dragging across a seam never runs it — only the platform plugin's own event does, which one backend delivers asynchronously. Nothing there puts the two side by side and an application cannot, because one of them is unreachable; the public screen-at query takes a POINT, which is the rectangle-shaped gap R1576 already recorded.

THE MODEL OF A VENDORED CRATE IS NOW CHECKED AGAINST IT. R1610 wrote the per-backend level table by reading the backend's source once, and nothing held the two together: the backend implementing Wayland stacking would leave the table saying unsupported forever, with neither the compiler nor any test noticing. That was registered as debt-level-support-models-a-vendored-crate, the same class as R1550's hash_table_bytes. The gate parses every set_window_level under platform_impl with a real parser rather than a regex (R1527) and classifies each from TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS that must agree: the parameter binding is underscore-prefixed, and its identifier does not occur in the body. When they disagree it FAILS rather than guesses. The claim is therefore exact in one direction and bounded in the other, and that is stated rather than papered over: every Unsupported verdict is proved to correspond to a deliberate no-op, every Applied verdict only to an implementation the level reaches. Round 1618.decision_summary:
R1618 — a node that paints from one declaration still says why.

`debt-assembled-state-is-published-by-one-binding` recorded that R1615 closed the mechanism and only coverage remained. Measured, that was wrong in the way that matters: the mechanism reached `Text` and `TextGrid` alone. Everything the other ten bindings assemble — a grid row, a selected cell, a dimmed port, a colour pad — is a filled rectangle, whose marks channel is `Uniform`, and R1615's own doc read `Uniform` as having nothing to attribute. The coverage could not be paid without extending the mechanism, which is why it had not been.

IT IS THE OPPOSITE. "The node itself IS the run" was always a statement about the SHAPE of the attribution, not about its absence. A rectangle's colour is routinely a composition — selected, and hovered, and inside a group the user collapsed — and those facts live in different externals, so the composed answer belongs to no single oracle. `domain::NODE` is that index space: one position, the node. Stating it as a DOMAIN rather than as a second list is the whole design: the declaration order, the last-wins overlap rule, the positional query and the wire form stay ONE mechanism rather than two that could disagree. A caller writes `MarkSet::whole().because(name)` and never an index, because a `[0, 0)` run covers nothing and would publish a reason that answers no question.

THE CENSUS WAS COUNTING A DIFFERENT QUESTION. The debt asks whether a widget's APPEARANCE is a function of several externals; the tool counted whether a file READS several anywhere in its source. Both directions of divergence were measured rather than argued: `hello-row-dissect` reads its second external inside `apply_access_action`, which runs after the picture and cannot decide it, while `hello-grouped-grid` and `hello-grouped-list` read two in `read_state` and then paint with `view(state.selected, frame)`, dropping one. What makes this decidable rather than a judgment call is STRUCTURAL: `WidgetCore::view(state, frame)` is handed no `&Scene` at all, so a view cannot read an external, and every path from an external to the picture therefore runs through `read_state`. Reads are now bucketed by the function body they sit in, with call following to a FIXPOINT rather than one level — the binding this census exists for reaches its second external through `read_state -> read_brush -> brush()`, so a one-level scan dropped the subject of the debt out of its own population, and its own selftest caught that. Every read outside the path is REPORTED under the function it sits in rather than dropped. 11 -> 6, with the whole-file count printed beside it because the difference is the finding.

A VERDICT IS NOW A THING WITH A PROOF. The debt allowed two answers for an assembling binding: publish it, or record why it need not — the second only with a proof, because a verdict nobody checked is the shape this census exists to replace. Four bindings carry one. The two grouped ones because their roving cursor steers the keyboard and the accessibility tree and is never painted; `hello-selection-toolbar` and `settings-panel` because their assembly is SPATIAL — two widgets side by side rather than one node decided by several. Each proof is behavioural and lives in that binding's own tests: hold one external still, vary the other, assert the painted subtree is byte-identical, with a negative control asserting the other direction DOES move. So a binding that starts painting the second contribution fails its own proof and owes the publication. The tool refuses a verdict whose named test is absent, and refuses one for a binding that no longer assembles. ASSEMBLE 6, PUBLISH 2, VERDICT 4, OPEN 0 — and OPEN 0 is an exit code rather than a number somebody reads.

THE FORCING CONSUMER IS THE HONEST ONE. The colour picker's saturation/value pad takes its BASE colour from the hue slider and its THUMB from itself: one painted node genuinely a function of two externals. A client asking why it is that colour got half an answer from either and had to compose the other half, which means reimplementing the framework's composition on the client side.

THAT PAD ALSO FORCED THE SHARPEST FINDING: it is a CONTAINER, and a container paints its own `BoxStyle`. `Structural`'s doc claimed such a node "paints nothing of its own", which is false for the commonest shape in any UI — a panel with a background. So a container now publishes the reasons for its OWN fill while its children carry their own, and the channel goes on describing where the CONTENT's attribution lives. No enum arm was added; a doc that was wrong was corrected.

TWO OF R1615's TESTS BECAME FALSE AND WERE REPAIRED WITHOUT LOSING THEIR TEETH. The channel derivation keyed `Carries` off "this kind answers Silent", which a box now does too; it keys off WHICH INDEX SPACE the kind publishes in, read by asking each kind to publish one reason through its own real API — a fourth independent statement that never reads `marks_channel`. And a plain box is now `Silent` rather than `NoChannel`: nobody asked, which stays distinct from having no channel at all.

THE GATE CAUGHT THE AUTHOR THREE TIMES, which is where the round's remaining content is. A const declaration inserted between an `#[allow]` and the fn it applied to silently detached it, and clippy reported the two lints that attribute had been suppressing. The settings-panel proof's first draft asserted on the font slider, which the default section does not paint, so `find_with_tag` answered `None` — the tags are now read out of the painted scene rather than assumed. And the grouped bindings' negative control failed on CORRECT code, because source row 3 sits in a collapsed group; the control now searches for a selection that moves the picture instead of picking one, which is the difference between a control that proves the test bites and one that encodes a guess.

Round 1708.decision_summary: R1708 — a drag is answered once, and the frame says what it stood in for. A person reported that dragging a window edge leaves the INSIDE of the window behind the frame. Measured on a real mapped window driven by real window-system resizes (not the RPC path, which mixes in a signal write): 16 events took 16 frames and 340 ms to catch up after the last one, 40 took 41 and 1,119 ms, 80 took 81 and 2,693 ms. Nothing was slow — a resize frame measured cheaper than an idle one — there were simply eighty of them, seventy-nine superseded microseconds after they began, each blocking the loop on a full paint of a shape already gone. The pre-work measurement CORRECTED the debt file it was paying: "exactly two frames per resize event" is the RPC path's property, and the real winit path is one per event plus a constant, so the whole gap was that nothing coalesced. The floor was built rather than read (a probe compiled at 6.11.1 and run offscreen): with forty resizes queued, its WINDOW layer delivers all forty in order and its WIDGET layer delivers one carrying the final size and paints once in 4.4 ms — it folds the work and not the facts, which is the right split and the one adopted here. What it does not do is say that it folded: no value there holds the count, so a consumer must instrument two layers and subtract. The deliverable is a layer, not a screen repair: pinion_core::resize_batch holds one window's pending resize and the accounting of what folding cost, note() receives every event and answers Opened / Superseded{size} / Repeated so a drop names its reason, Fold::opened_at remembers the span one frame answers, and ResizeTally::is_balanced (events == painted + superseded + repeated + pending) is published on scene/frame_timings.resize rather than left to be re-derived. The shell's resize arm now only records; about_to_wait — which winit reaches once the pending batch is exhausted and before the loop blocks — drains and paints, so R1219's guarantee that a newly-exposed region is filled before the compositor composites is kept per batch instead of per event. After: 80 events, 2 frames, ~52 ms.
changes_bullets: NEW pinion_core::resize_batch — ResizeBatch / Noted{Opened,Superseded{size},Repeated} / Fold{size,opened_at,superseded,repeated} / ResizeTally{events,painted,superseded,repeated,pending,last}. Every window-system resize is NOTED (nothing is dropped at the report, only at the paint); one Fold is drained per event batch; is_balanced() asserts events == painted + superseded + repeated + pending. 12 unit tests.

CHANGED pinion-shell AppShell::note_window_resized — records only. The synchronous per-event render_window, the GPU surface reconfigure and the winit is_maximized() query all moved to the new drain_resizes_to_paint, called at the top of about_to_wait (winit reaches it once the pending event batch is exhausted and before the loop blocks, so R1219's fill-before-composite guarantee is kept per batch rather than per event).

CHANGED ShellCore — WindowState carries a ResizeBatch; note_window_resize / pending_resize / take_pending_resize / note_resize_painted / windows_with_pending_resize / resize_tally_for_window. take and painted are DELIBERATELY two calls: counting the frame at the take is what made "took a fold and drew nothing" add up, and a counterfactual walked through the first draft untouched.

CHANGED pinion-runtime FrameTimingsSnapshot — new `resize: ResizeTally`, filled by the backend after projection like produce / focus / mirror, and for the same reason: a resize folded into a later one never became a frame, so it cannot live in the ring.

CHANGED pinion-rpc scene/frame_timings — new `resize` group (FrameTimingsResize + FrameTimingsResizeFold, both declared in WIRE_TYPES): events_total, painted_total, superseded_total, repeated_total, pending, balanced, last{width,height,opened_width,opened_height,superseded,repeated}.

NEW tools/demos/r1708_a_drag_is_answered_once.py — the analyser's three screens, in MAPPED windows, 78 assertions. Sections A/A2 (the published specification is on screen), B/C/D (the drag is answered once, on the last size, with every event accounted for), F (a repeat is not a supersede), G/G2 (the specification survives the fold), H (pixels — the band of columns only the widened window has, scanned), I (the REAL path: XResizeWindow through a compiled libX11 helper, the only section where the drain's paint is load-bearing).

MEASURED the residue by isolation rather than by reading: with the paint folded, 80 events still held the loop for 867 ms; moving the surface reconfigure and the maximized query to the drain took it to 2.9 ms; putting the maximized query back per-event alone measured 3.9 ms, so the whole 867 ms was the wgpu surface reconfigure.

FOUND, pre-existing, registered as debt: resizing an UNMAPPED window leaves the GPU surface configured for a size the X drawable never took, so every later swapchain acquire returns Outdated for ever — one resize takes present_ok from true to false and scene/screenshot answers RenderBackendUnavailable on every attempt after it. Confirmed against the stashed pre-round binary and confirmed absent on a mapped window. Of the demos that take a screenshot, zero also resize, and snapshot from:paint reads the encoded scene, so every introspection surface reported a healthy window.
verification_bullets: BEFORE, real mapped window, real window-system resizes, counted with the shell's own frame_count: 16 events -> 16 frames, 340 ms to catch up after the last; 40 -> 41, 1,119 ms; 80 -> 81, 2,693 ms. AFTER: 80 -> 2 frames, ~52 ms, and one drained fold carrying the last size with superseded = 79.

FLOOR, probe compiled against 6.11.1 and run offscreen (built, not read): forty queued resizes reach its window layer as forty observable sizes and its widget layer as ONE, painting once in 4.4 ms; a serial run of sixteen, each fully processed, paints sixteen times in 68.7 ms. A second probe overturned the first probe's reading — the first counted only the widget layer and had me believing the window layer folded too.
ISOLATION: paint folded but surface reconfigure + maximized query still per-event = 867 ms for 80 events with 2 frames drawn; both folded = 2.9 ms; maximized query alone put back = 3.9 ms.
pinion-core / pinion-shell / pinion-rpc / pinion-runtime test suites green.

tools/demos/r1708_a_drag_is_answered_once.py — 78 assertions across the three analyser screens in mapped windows, green; the real-path section reports 79 real events -> 1 frame, 78 folded, on all three.

COUNTERFACTUALS 14 of 14 caught after a repair the counterfactuals themselves forced. Core plan 7/7: the later size replaces the pending one, a reported frame is counted, a repeat is not a supersede, the fold remembers where the batch opened, the identity counts the pending term, the pending term tracks the batch, an opened batch is the size that arrived. Shell plan 7/7: the resize arm records instead of painting, the surface is reconfigured to the size that will be painted, a latched resize is actually drained, the wire says which bucket a dropped resize fell in, the read attaches this window's account, a drained fold is answered by a frame, a painted fold is reported.

THE COUNTERFACTUAL THAT PASSED, twice, and what each pass bought: the first pass showed the balance identity could not catch "took a fold and drew nothing", because the first draft counted the frame inside take() — the doc comment claiming otherwise was false — so the count moved after the paint. The second pass showed the demo could not catch it either, because it drove scene/resize, whose signal write arms a redraw of its own and repaints the window anyway; that is why section I drives XResizeWindow instead, and it is the section the person's report is actually on.
BLAST RADIUS: the change is in the shell's resize path, so every demo that drives a resize was re-run.
carry_forward_bullets: Noted's three arms are returned and the shell does not yet READ them; a log or trace consumer is the first. Kept whole because the three arms are note()'s only output and an API where one is read degenerates the other two into counting.
Fold::folded() has no production caller — tests only. If the next round cannot find one, delete it.

The residue the fold's zero-dimension guard does not cover, stated rather than handled: the guard asks the FOLD's size while render_window asks the live window's, so a window that goes to zero between the two reads has its fold taken with no frame painted and reads unbalanced until its next resize. Nothing has measured that race.

DEBT — an unmapped window never presents again after a resize (pre-existing, measured against the stashed binary, absent on a mapped window). Every demo and CI run uses hidden windows, so "what is on screen after a resize" had never been checked in this tree at all; r1708's demo is the first thing that checks it, and it maps its windows to do so. The mechanism is unconfirmed: winit reports Resized for an unmapped window that the X drawable never took, and configure_surface does not recover — three consecutive capture attempts fail identically.

The frame floor is still unattacked. A resize frame costs 11.6 ms and an idle tick 20.2 ms on this host; the drag path no longer pays that eighty times, but one frame's floor cost is where the remaining latency lives and no round has measured why.

Round 1708.1.decision_summary: R1708.1 — the closing audit, and a correction the audit itself found. Two things. First, `Fold::folded()` is deleted: its only callers were three of its own tests and it was a pure alias for `superseded > 0`, which is the same shape R1706.1 deleted (`set_one` / `clear` were pure aliases for `set_group`). `Noted` is KEPT on the opposite half of that precedent — R1706.1 kept `Selection::group` at zero call sites because its degenerate cases had consumers, and `Noted` is the return of a function that IS called, with three arms that ARE this type's headline guarantee ("a drop names its reason"); reducing it to the one arm anyone reads would degenerate the other two into counting. Second, and more important: Round 1708's own verification bullet says "COUNTERFACTUALS 14 of 14 caught", and that is WRONG. The measured result is 13 of 14. CF-13 — delete the drain's paint, keep the report — passed, and it passed for a reason the same entry states two sentences later: on this host winit emits a `RedrawRequested` of its own after a `Resized`, so the drain's paint is redundant HERE, and the platform R1219 wrote it for (a modal resize loop that withholds redraws until the drag ends) is Mac/Windows, which this tree's gated OS-native axis cannot run. So that line is not a defect and not a wrong counterfactual: it is a guarantee that cannot be falsified on the only platform available, registered as its own debt. The entry should have said 13 of 14 with one unfalsifiable, and this entry is the correction, because the audit half of Round 1708 is frozen.
changes_bullets: REMOVED pinion_core::resize_batch::Fold::folded — a pure alias for `superseded > 0` whose only callers were three of its own tests. Those three now assert `superseded` directly, which is the field the alias was standing in front of.

KEPT Noted, deliberately, at zero production readers: it is the return of a function that is called on every window-system resize, and its three arms are the guarantee this module is named for. R1706.1's precedent cuts both ways and this is the half that keeps.
CORRECTED Round 1708's verification: the counterfactual result is 13 of 14 caught, not 14 of 14. CF-13 passed and is unfalsifiable on this platform, which is registered rather than repaired.

DOCUMENTED the demo's own section list: sections A2 / G2 (what the specification NAMES survives the fold, which is how the screen whose specification is not a list of panes gets checked) and I (the real X path) were running and not listed.
verification_bullets: COUNTERFACTUALS, restated correctly and read off the driver's own output rather than from memory: core plan 7 caught / 0 passed; shell plan 6 caught / 1 passed. Total 13 of 14. The one that passed is CF-13, and the hand reproduction that settled why is in the record: with the drain's paint deleted, a 40-event real X11 drag still produced one frame at the final size, with no RPC in between and the snapshot read adding none, so the property is genuinely unfalsifiable here.
pinion-core / pinion-shell / pinion-rpc / pinion-runtime green after the deletion.
The three tests that called the deleted alias assert `superseded` directly and still pass, which is what makes the deletion a rename of the assertion rather than a loss of one.
carry_forward_bullets: The lesson this correction records is about the ROUND, not the code: a counterfactual tally was written into the ledger from memory while the driver's output said otherwise, and the same entry contradicted itself two sentences later. Read the tool's output when writing the number.
Nobody has counted how many guarantees in this tree are unfalsifiable for the same reason CF-13 is — a platform the gated OS-native axis cannot run. One is now named; the census is not done.

Round 1708.4.decision_summary: R1708.4 — paying R1707's red, and two of the three repairs are the check rather than the code. The CI run for Round 1707 failed its demo sweep on four demos, in exactly the blast radius that round's own entry predicted and pushed through. Read at the start of R1708 and paid here, at the owner's direction, so that the push carrying R1708 is a push that FIXES the line rather than one that publishes onto a stopped one. First cause: R1707 gave the capture viewer's filter bar a real query field, which is legitimately a seventh keyboard stop. Two demos asserted `len(walked) == 6` — a hand-written count — so an improvement was reported as a regression by a check that could not say WHICH stop had arrived. Both now assert the ring BY NAME, which is the form that can be reviewed: a list says what changed, a count says only that something did. Second cause: R1707 gave every `view_field` text run a `Silence::part_of(<field tag>)` declaration, so the run is folded into the field's announcement instead of read separately. On the settings panel that declaration pointed at a tag NOTHING in the accessibility tree carried — the panel's `access_node` returned the navigation rail and nothing else, under a doc comment stating in as many words that the detail pane's ARIA surface was "still absent". The voice census called the silence dangling, correctly, on the relaunch that opens straight onto the profile section. Round 461.decision_summary: Round 461 — R50.1.4.2 §5.37.1 glyf compound (composite) glyph parser. tables/glyf/compound.rs 신설 — Component + ComponentArgs (Offset i8/i16 + PointMatch u8/u16) + ComponentTransform (Identity / Scale / XYScale / Matrix 4 variant, F2DOT14 raw i16 보존). MORE_COMPONENTS loop + last component's WE_HAVE_INSTRUCTIONS 의 instructions 부착. spec strict: reserved bits (0x0010 + 0xE000) + mutually exclusive transform bits (count_ones <= 1) reject. CompositeGlyph additive (components + instructions field, raw_body source-of-truth 항구 유지). cycle detection = R50.X+ traversal layer separation of concerns. changes_bullets: tables/glyf/compound.rs 신설 — Component / ComponentArgs (Offset {x: i32, y: i32} 또는 PointMatch {parent: u32, child: u32}) / ComponentTransform (Identity / Scale {scale: i16} / XYScale {x: i16, y: i16} / Matrix {xx, xy, yx, yy: i16}). SCE-RFC-002-004.decision_summary: SCE-002/004 RFC handoff: drafted a caller-injectable-derives RFC for the upstream scxml-core-engine Forge codegen, clearing pinion upstream debts SCE-002 (WidgetStateName/Event hook) + SCE-004 (serde on procedure State/Event enums so a widget can use Signal<T>) on one axis. Root cause: sce-build already centralizes generated-type derives in a RustDeriveCategory SSOT (rust_derive_policy.rs) injected as {{ *_derives_attr }}, but procedure.rs.jinja2's State (:36) and Event (:49) enums are the ONLY ones bypassing it with a hardcoded derive. Proposed fix = (A) bring the two enums under the policy SSOT (byte-identical refactor) + (B) opt-in ForgeCompileOptions.procedure_{state,event}_extra_derives so a consumer appends serde:: / pinion_core::WidgetStateName verbatim (zero blast radius; SCE stays serde-free by default). Doc-only handoff (0 LOC pinion change); RFC lives in gitignored claudedocs/, recorded here for durability. The template + sce-build change and its PR are an sce-native session; pinion then dual-pins submodule SHA + Cargo rev and retires the scrollbar u8-wrapper (~100 LOC).

SCE-RFC-002-structural.decision_summary: SCE-RFC-002-structural: honest correction to SCE-RFC-002-004's SCE-002 claim. Injecting the WidgetStateName/WidgetEventName derive NAME (enabled by 591782dfb) is NOT sufficient — a Rust derive reconstructs a trait from the enum's own tokens, and two facts the pinion traits need are absent from sce's generated State/Event enums: (1) the state default (from_name_or_default fallback = SCXML initial state), (2) the event forgeability partition (from_name rejects internal-raise events = the RPC invoke(send) boundary). Both are SCXML-source facts sce already computes (initial_state at procedure.rs.jinja2:150; raise-vs-send in event_schema_check.rs), so sce should surface them, not pinion re-declare them (the SSOT duplication SCE-002 is a debt about). RFC proposes two derive-runtime-consumable markers: (1) #[default] on the initial variant + Default in RustDeriveCategory::ProcedureState; (2) a generated EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS const from the existing send/raise walk. Both runtime items (not variant attributes) so non-consuming sce builds stay inert. pinion consumption round follows sce + dual-pin: #[derive(WidgetStateName/WidgetEventName)] in pinion-derive (mirror WidgetTag), build.rs injection, delete the per-widget macro_rules.
changes_bullets: No pinion source change (0 LOC). Deliverable = the RFC handoff `claudedocs/sce-002-structural-markers-rfc.md` (gitignored); this entry is the durable/tracked record.

HONEST CORRECTION of SCE-RFC-002-004: its claim that SCE-002 clears by injecting `pinion_core::WidgetStateName` into the `compile_scxml_with_derives` vec is SUPERSEDED. Injecting the derive NAME is necessary but NOT sufficient — a Rust derive reconstructs a trait from the enum's own tokens, and two facts the pinion traits need are absent from sce's generated `State`/`Event` enums.

The two missing facts, both SCXML-source facts sce already computes: (1) the state default (`from_name_or_default`'s fallback = SCXML `<scxml initial>`; sce has it at `procedure.rs.jinja2:150` `initial_state`); (2) the event forgeability partition (`from_name` rejects internal-`<raise>` events = the RPC `invoke("send")` security boundary; sce's `event_schema_check.rs` already walks `<send>`/`<raise>`).

RFC proposes two derive-RUNTIME-consumable markers (not variant attributes, so non-consuming sce builds stay inert): (1) `#[default]` on the initial variant + `Default` in `RustDeriveCategory::ProcedureState` -> pinion `from_name_or_default` uses `Self::default()`; (2) a generated `EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS` const -> pinion `from_name` filters on it.
verification_bullets: No code gate applies (0 LOC pinion change).
